119/// One outgoing data packet on its way to the wire.
120type EgressItem = (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut);
121
122/// The result of asking the PIX egress gate for permission to send one packet.
123///
124/// `Left` is the answer the gate could give synchronously — a permit, or a refusal because the
125/// Session is being torn down. `Right` is the parked case, and the only one that allocates.
126type EgressPermit = futures::future::Either<
127    std::future::Ready<Result<EgressItem, std::io::Error>>,
128    futures::future::BoxFuture<'static, Result<EgressItem, std::io::Error>>,
129>;
130
131/// Passes one outgoing data packet through a Session's PIX egress gate, if it has one.
132///
133/// Returns a future rather than awaiting so this can sit in a `Sink::with` without the combinator
134/// having to box anything in the common case. The gate answers synchronously whenever service is
135/// available — a relaxed load and a compare-exchange — and only the exhausted-budget path allocates,
136/// which is a path that is about to block regardless.
137///
138/// A Session that negotiated no PIX passes through with no gate at all, so an un-supervised Session
139/// pays one `Option` check per packet and nothing else.
140///
141/// Nothing is measured on the admitted arm, deliberately. That arm is the steady state at the
142/// Session's full packet rate, and what an operator wants from it — how much was served, and on
143/// whose money — is already counted inside the gate's own compare-exchange and flushed once per
144/// supervisor turn by [`PixSessionTelemetry`](crate::supervision::telemetry::PixSessionTelemetry).
145/// Only the refused arm, which is about to allocate a boxed future and block, does any telemetry
146/// work of its own.
147///
148/// A packet the gate never admits gives back the SURB its sender counted for it (see
149/// [`count_return_packet_surb`]), since it never reaches the routing resolution that would have taken
150/// one. That covers a packet a closed gate refuses, a park the gate's poisoning fails, and a parked
151/// future dropped with the Session's sink.
152fn acquire_egress_permit(
153    gate: Option<Arc<ServiceGate>>,
154    routing: DestinationRouting,
155    mut data: ApplicationDataOut,
156) -> EgressPermit {
157    let Some(gate) = gate else {
158        return futures::future::Either::Left(std::future::ready(Ok((routing, data))));
159    };
160
161    match gate.try_acquire_sync() {
162        Ok(GateVerdict::Admitted) => futures::future::Either::Left(std::future::ready(Ok((routing, data)))),
163        // Forwarded rather than reconstructed: the gate now names its own error, so both of its
164        // entry points report the same one and neither caller has to know what a refusal means.
165        Err(closed) => {
166            record_gate_closed();
167            data.surb_refund.give_back();
168            futures::future::Either::Left(std::future::ready(Err(std::io::Error::other(closed))))
169        }
170        // Budget exhausted: park until the supervisor funds the front, restores a successor's
171        // allowance, reports front-cycle progress, or gives up on the Session entirely.
172        //
173        // The episode is opened *here*, at the refusal, and moved into the future, so its clock
174        // covers the whole park and its `Drop` closes it however the park ends — resumed, failed,
175        // or cancelled. Opened outside the `async move` rather than inside it because the refusal
176        // has already happened by the time this returns: a future that is constructed and never
177        // polled is still a packet the gate turned away, and starting the clock at first poll
178        // would under-report every stall by however long the caller took to await it.
179        //
180        // One episode per park rather than per refused packet: this sink is serial, so the next
181        // packet is not offered until this future resolves, and a caller cannot open a second
182        // episode by retrying harder.
183        //
184        // The packet's refund is taken off it here and moved in with the episode, for the same
185        // reason: only `Drop` sees every way a park can end without an admission.
186        Ok(GateVerdict::Blocked(reason)) => {
187            let episode = PixGateBlockEpisode::begin(reason);
188            let refund = ParkedSurbRefund(std::mem::take(&mut data.surb_refund));
189            futures::future::Either::Right(Box::pin(async move {
190                let _episode = episode;
191                match gate.acquire().await {
192                    Ok(()) => {
193                        data.surb_refund = refund.admit();
194                        Ok((routing, data))
195                    }
196                    // `refund` gives the SURB back as the future ends.
197                    Err(closed) => Err(std::io::Error::other(closed)),
198                }
199            }))
200        }
201    }
202}

204/// [`acquire_egress_permit`] for a packet of the slot `instance`, which is refused once the instance
205/// is superseded.
206///
207/// Checked twice by the callers' design: before the packet is counted (the caller's own
208/// `instance.is_superseded()` test, ahead of any accounting), and here once the gate has admitted a
209/// *parked* packet. A writer parked on the gate while its slot is torn down is woken by the gate's
210/// poisoning with an error, but a permit granted in the same breath must not slip through either. The
211/// synchronous admission has no suspension between the caller's check and the permit, so it needs no
212/// second look. A cut packet gives back the SURB its sender counted.
213///
214/// One cost is left, and accepted as bounded: a writer parked on the gate that the gate then admits
215/// has been counted as served by the gate (its served counter, and its predeposit allowance while
216/// unfunded), though its packet is cut and no progress follows. Across a takeover the gate is kept,
217/// so the old plane's parked writer costs the new one a single unit of its served-without-progress
218/// ceiling. A sink drives one send at a time, so a plane has at most one such writer, once per
219/// takeover, against a ceiling of thousands of packets (`max_served_without_progress`). A gate
220/// operation that undid the count would have to do so across a mode change and a progress snapshot
221/// without ever being able to over-credit, which is a worse trade than one packet.
222fn acquire_egress_permit_for(
223    instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>,
224    gate: Option<Arc<ServiceGate>>,
225    routing: DestinationRouting,
226    data: ApplicationDataOut,
227) -> EgressPermit {
228    match acquire_egress_permit(gate, routing, data) {
229        parked @ futures::future::Either::Left(_) => parked,
230        futures::future::Either::Right(parked) => {
231            let instance = instance.clone();
232            futures::future::Either::Right(Box::pin(async move {
233                let (routing, data) = match parked.await {
234                    Ok(admitted) => admitted,
235                    // A teardown poisons the gate; the writer still learns it was superseded.
236                    Err(_) if instance.is_superseded() => return Err(superseded_write_error()),
237                    Err(error) => return Err(error),
238                };
239                if instance.is_superseded() {
240                    data.surb_refund.give_back();
241                    return Err(superseded_write_error());
242                }
243                Ok((routing, data))
244            }))
245        }
246    }
247}

249/// The SURB refund of a packet parked at the PIX egress gate, given back unless the gate admits the
250/// packet.
251///
252/// A park ends without an admission in two ways, and `Drop` sees both: the gate is poisoned, which
253/// fails the park, or the Session's sink is dropped with the parked future in it, polled or not. An
254/// admitted packet takes its refund back with [`admit`](Self::admit), for routing resolution to give
255/// back if the packet starves there.
256struct ParkedSurbRefund(SurbRefund);
257
258impl ParkedSurbRefund {
259    /// The gate admitted the packet: hands its refund back to go on with it.
260    fn admit(mut self) -> SurbRefund {
261        std::mem::take(&mut self.0)
262    }
263}
264
265impl Drop for ParkedSurbRefund {
266    fn drop(&mut self) {
267        // A no-op after `admit`, which leaves an empty refund behind.
268        self.0.give_back();
269    }
270}
271
272/// Aborts the wrapped task when dropped, which neither a join handle nor an [`AbortHandle`] does on
273/// its own drop. Built through `From` from any [`Abortable`].
274struct AbortOnDrop(Box<dyn Abortable + Send + Sync>);
275
276impl<A: Abortable + Send + Sync + 'static> From<A> for AbortOnDrop {
277    fn from(task: A) -> Self {
278        Self(Box::new(task))
279    }
280}
281
282impl Drop for AbortOnDrop {
283    fn drop(&mut self) {
284        self.0.abort_task();
285    }
286}

288/// How long a teardown waits before retiring its Session's pseudonym from the SURB store's admitted
289/// class.
290///
291/// Derived from the packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window: a return-routed packet whose SURB has
292/// not arrived is retried there for the pipeline's `surb_resolution_wait` — 6 s at the library
293/// default — before it is dropped, and a closing Exit's own notification is exactly such a packet.
294/// The grace must cover the whole wait, so the ring is still there when the resolution stage last
295/// looks; the margin below adds room for the queueing between the send and the lookup, without being
296/// so long that a pseudonym's admitted ring outlives its Session by anything an operator could
297/// notice. The window is operator-configurable, so the grace is derived from it rather than pinned
298/// to a literal that only clears the default.
299fn surb_retire_grace(surb_resolution_wait: Duration) -> Duration {
300    surb_resolution_wait + Duration::from_secs(1)
301}
302
303/// Retires `pseudonym` on behalf of `token`, after a grace derived from the pipeline's
304/// SURB-resolution window (see [`surb_retire_grace`]), when a runtime is running.
305///
306/// Spawned through `Handle::try_current` rather than `tokio::spawn` because the teardowns that
307/// reach this helper are synchronous ([`close_session`], the sessions cache's eviction listener,
308/// [`SessionSlotGuard::drop`]) and can run off-runtime, where `tokio::spawn` panics. The
309/// off-runtime fallback retires inline, which is correct rather than merely convenient: a teardown
310/// with no runtime under it has no packet pipeline resolving return routes on its behalf either, so
311/// the SURB-resolution window the deferral exists to cover cannot be in progress — there is nothing
312/// to wait out.
313fn defer_admission_retire(
314    admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
315    #[cfg_attr(
316        not(any(feature = "runtime-tokio", test, feature = "testing")),
317        allow(unused_variables)
318    )]
319    grace: Duration,
320    session_id: &SessionId,
321    token: AdmissionToken,
322) {
323    let Some(admission) = admission else {
324        return;
325    };
326
327    // The runtime check needs tokio, which this crate carries only behind `runtime-tokio` (and in
328    // test builds). Without it the crate is runtime-agnostic by design, so there is no runtime to
329    // ask for — which is the `Err` branch: retire inline.
330    #[cfg(any(feature = "runtime-tokio", test, feature = "testing"))]
331    match tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() {
332        Ok(runtime) => {
333            let session_id = *session_id;
334            let retire = async move {
335                tokio::time::sleep(grace).await;
336                tracing::debug!(%session_id, "retiring session pseudonym from the SURB store's admitted class");
337                admission.retire(&session_id, token);
338            };
339            runtime.spawn(retire);
340        }
341        // No runtime: see the doc comment — retire inline, as the synchronous world always did.
342        Err(_) => admission.retire(session_id, token),
343    }
344    #[cfg(not(any(feature = "runtime-tokio", test, feature = "testing")))]
345    admission.retire(session_id, token);
346}

348/// How often a data packet held back for the keep-alive reserve looks at the SURB estimate again.
349const SURB_RESERVE_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
350
351/// How often an Exit checks whether a forward receipt is due.
352const FORWARD_RECEIPT_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);
353
354/// SURBs the Exit keeps back from its data, so that its keep-alives can still be sent.
355///
356/// The Exit's SURB-level reports and its distress signals each need a SURB, and nothing else the Exit
357/// sends is as important to the Entry: a report is how a balancer that cannot see the Exit's stock
358/// learns it is running dry. One percent of the Entry's buffer target, at least 32, keeps that many
359/// reports and distress signals sendable: at one report per `surb_balance_notify_period` (15 s in the
360/// node's default configuration) that outlasts minutes of a total outage, long enough for the Entry to
361/// hear it and refill.
362///
363/// Never more than a quarter of the target, as for the PIX fill reserve
364/// ([`effective_surb_reserve`]): an Entry that asks for a buffer shallower than the floor must not
365/// find the Exit unable to send it anything at all.
366fn keep_alive_surb_reserve(target: u64) -> u64 {
367    (target / 100).max(32).min(target / 4)
368}
369
370/// How often the Exit's loss driver re-reads the Session's forward path.
371///
372/// The same value as the rate limiter's re-read interval (`MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`), because that is the
373/// granularity at which a changed notification period takes effect anyway: polling faster would only
374/// wake up to find the stream not yet listening.
375const SURB_DEGRADED_POLL: Duration = MAX_WAIT_CHUNK;
376
377/// How long a frame loss keeps the Exit's notification at its degraded period.
378///
379/// Longer than one degraded period and shorter than the normal one: the point is to keep reporting at
380/// the fast cadence through a burst of loss (a lost frame is detected when its reassembly times out,
381/// which arrives in gaps) without staying fast once the forward path is whole again. Three seconds at
382/// one report per second is three reports, which is what a dead-relayer verdict needs.
383const SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);
384
385/// How long the Exit's frames have to stall before the forward path counts as degraded without a loss yet.
386///
387/// A loss is known only when a frame's reassembly times out, three to six seconds into an outage at the
388/// default 3 s frame timeout (see [`FrameLossSignal`]), and every second of that is a second the Entry's
389/// verdict on a dead relayer waits for its first report. A forward path that delivers segments but no
390/// frames shows sooner: segments of two frames arriving with neither completing. One second is several
391/// frames' worth of a stream moving data, and far below the frame timeout.
392const SURB_DEGRADED_STALL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
393
394/// How often the Exit reports its SURB level while its frames stall: while the forward path is dark.
395///
396/// Dark, the Exit's reports are the only replies the Entry gets. Each spends one of the Session's oldest SURBs,
397/// a share of which runs through the dead relayer, and the Entry's verdict needs three races lost by it: three
398/// times the first SURB of a pair out while the second is home. At the degraded period of a second that took
399/// tens of seconds whenever the dead relayer carried a modest share of the reports' return paths. Measured on
400/// forward-dark relayer loss: at one report a second, 8 of 38 runs missed the 15 s recovery boundary; at one
401/// every 100 ms, none of 22 did.
402///
403/// Only while the frames stall, which takes multi-segment frames that stop completing: a Session that merely
404/// loses frames now and then, and every Session of single-segment datagrams, keeps the degraded period. The
405/// keep-alive reserve bounds this cadence like the degraded one, so a dark Session spends at most its stock
406/// above the reserve, ten SURBs a second, and only until the Entry's verdict lets its frames through.
407const SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_millis(100);
408
409/// Whether the Exit holds a SURB target the Entry announced for this Session.
410///
411/// A `NoRateControl` Session runs no balancer on this side and stores none (`0`). A rate-controlled Session whose
412/// Entry announces nothing runs its balancer at the fallback target, which the Exit cannot tell from an announced one,
413/// so it holds a non-zero value and is not covered by this rule; a zero target is what is. With none, the keep-alive
414/// reserve is `0`, which would let degraded reports spend down to the last SURB.
415fn has_announced_surb_target(balancer: &BalancerStateValues) -> bool {
416    balancer.target_surb_buffer_size.load(Ordering::Relaxed) > 0
417}
418
419/// Whether the Exit should report its SURB level faster than its normal period.
420///
421/// Four conditions, all of them required:
422///
423/// * **The forward path is losing frames, or they stall.** The Exit's echo replies are what corroborate a dead
424///   relayer's overdue races. While frames do not reassemble, no reply goes out, and the Entry's only remaining
425///   evidence is this report. Without loss there is nothing to report faster about. A loss is known only once a frame
426///   times out, so frames that stalled for [`SURB_DEGRADED_STALL`] count as well (`recently_stalled`, which the driver
427///   holds for [`SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD`] like a loss): that is the same dark forward path, seconds before its first frame
428///   times out.
429/// * **The Entry reads the reports.** As [`PixFillControl::admit`] decides anyway, but also here: a report to an Entry
430///   with no balancer spends a SURB to say nothing, and reporting one per second to it would do so fifteen times as
431///   often.
432/// * **The Exit holds an announced SURB target.** Without one (a `NoRateControl` Session, which stores none) the
433///   Session never degrades and keeps the normal period: there is no reserve to budget the reports against.
434/// * **The stock is above the keep-alive reserve.** This is the budget: at or below the reserve, the normal period is
435///   what the Exit can afford, and the reserve is what keeps those reports sendable.
436fn exit_forward_path_is_degraded(
437    loss_signal: &FrameLossSignal,
438    estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
439    balancer: &BalancerStateValues,
440    recently_stalled: bool,
441) -> bool {
442    has_announced_surb_target(balancer)
443        && (loss_signal.lost_within(SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD) || recently_stalled)
444        && balancer.counterparty_refills()
445        && estimator.saturating_diff() > current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(balancer)
446}
447
448/// What the Exit's loss driver last told the notification stream, so that it acts only when the answer changes.
449///
450/// The driver re-evaluates [`exit_forward_path_is_degraded`] every [`SURB_DEGRADED_POLL`], and most polls
451/// repeat the previous answer. Each switch re-derives the stream's rate and is logged, so only a change
452/// gets through.
453///
454/// It also holds when frames were last seen stalled. A stall ends at the first frame that completes, and
455/// a forward path that delivers a frame now and then is still a dark one, so a stall counts for
456/// [`SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD`] after it was last seen, as a loss does.
457#[derive(Debug, Default)]
458struct DegradedSwitch {
459    degraded: bool,
460    dark: bool,
461    last_stall: Option<Instant>,
462}
463
464impl DegradedSwitch {
465    /// Notes whether frames are stalled now, and returns whether they were within [`SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD`].
466    fn note_stall(&mut self, stalled: bool, now: Instant) -> bool {
467        if stalled {
468            self.last_stall = Some(now);
469        }
470        self.last_stall
471            .is_some_and(|at| now.saturating_duration_since(at) <= SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD)
472    }
473
474    /// Returns `Some(next)` when `next` differs from what was last applied, and records it; `None` otherwise.
475    fn change_to(&mut self, next: bool) -> Option<bool> {
476        (self.degraded != next).then(|| {
477            self.degraded = next;
478            next
479        })
480    }
481
482    /// As [`change_to`](Self::change_to), for whether the degraded forward path is dark: degraded by frames
483    /// that stalled, rather than by frames lost while others still complete.
484    fn change_dark_to(&mut self, next: bool) -> Option<bool> {
485        (self.dark != next).then(|| {
486            self.dark = next;
487            next
488        })
489    }
490}

492/// The keep-alive reserve of a Session whose Entry currently asks for the target `balancer` holds.
493///
494/// Read at every check rather than fixed when the Session opens: the Entry may lower its target while
495/// the Session runs (a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive updates it), and its balancer then keeps the stock
496/// near the new one. A reserve fixed at the opening target could sit above every stock the Entry now
497/// keeps, and data would be held for good.
498fn current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(balancer: &BalancerStateValues) -> u64 {
499    keep_alive_surb_reserve(balancer.target_surb_buffer_size.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
500}
501
502/// Holds an outgoing data packet back while the Exit's SURB stock is down to its keep-alive reserve
503/// (see [`current_keep_alive_surb_reserve`]).
504///
505/// Returns `None`, with nothing allocated, in the common case of a stock above the reserve. Otherwise
506/// the future resolves once the stock has risen above it, polling the estimate every
507/// [`SURB_RESERVE_POLL`]. It has no deadline of its own: the Session's own deadlines apply, and a
508/// Session that is closed drops the future with the sink.
509///
510/// Only once the Entry has shown that it refills the stock
511/// ([`BalancerStateValues::counterparty_refills`]): that is, a keep-alive from its balancer, which only an
512/// Entry with a SURB balancer sends (a manual ping, [`KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing`], is not one). An Entry without one
513/// can run a rate-controlled Session too: it announces no target (one that predates this announces the balancer-rate
514/// fallback, which the Exit cannot tell from a real target), attaches one SURB to each data packet and sends no
515/// keep-alives but the odd manual ping. So the announcement says nothing about a balancer either way. A reply held for
516/// a stock above the reserve would then wait until the Entry sent that many more packets.
517///
518/// The Exit's keep-alives do not come through here: its keep-alive stream sends on the message sender
519/// directly (see [`SessionManager::spawn_exit_keep_alive`]), and the PIX fill packets are bounded by
520/// their own `min_surb_reserve`. That is the point of the reserve: they are what it is held for.
521///
522/// `pix` says whether the Session runs a PIX egress gate, and only labels the hold episode: the
523/// hold itself is the same either way.
524fn hold_for_surb_reserve(
525    session_id: SessionId,
526    estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
527    balancer: &Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
528    pix: bool,
529    instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>,
530) -> Option<futures::future::BoxFuture<'static, ()>> {
531    if !balancer.counterparty_refills() {
532        return None;
533    }
534
535    let stock = estimator.saturating_diff();
536    let reserve = current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(balancer);
537    if stock > reserve {
538        return None;
539    }
540
541    debug!(%session_id, stock, reserve, "holding data back: the SURB stock is down to its keep-alive reserve");
542    let (estimator, balancer, instance) = (estimator.clone(), balancer.clone(), instance.clone());
543
544    // The episode begins here, before the future's first poll, and is carried into it by value so
545    // that its `Drop` closes it however the hold ends: the stock rises and the future resolves, the
546    // Session is torn down and the future is dropped mid-poll, or the caller drops it before ever
547    // polling it. Created only on this path, so a packet above the reserve records nothing.
548    //
549    // This clock is the authoritative one, and it deliberately starts earlier than the debug log's
550    // `held_for` below: the metric measures the time the Exit held data, which begins when the
551    // future is created, whereas the log measures the polling loop's own run and so misses any
552    // interval between creation and the first poll. That is the issue's requirement, not a bug —
553    // do not "fix" either clock to match the other.
554    let episode = SurbReserveHoldEpisode::begin(pix);
555    Some(Box::pin(async move {
556        // Never read: its `Drop` at the end of this future — on the release path below, on
557        // cancellation, or when the future is dropped unpolled — is what records the duration.
558        let _episode = episode;
559        let held_since = Instant::now();
560        // Also ends once `instance` is superseded: the caller then fails the write instead of leaving it parked.
561        while estimator.saturating_diff() <= current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer) && !instance.is_superseded() {
562            hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(SURB_RESERVE_POLL).await;
563        }
564        tracing::debug!(
565            %session_id,
566            held_for = ?held_since.elapsed(),
567            stock = estimator.saturating_diff(),
568            reserve = current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer),
569            "releasing held data: the SURB stock is above its keep-alive reserve again"
570        );
571    }))
572}
573
574/// The Exit's data egress for a rate-controlled Session: holds each packet back while the SURB stock
575/// is down to the keep-alive reserve of the target `balancer` holds (once the Entry refills it, see
576/// [`hold_for_surb_reserve`]), books the SURB it consumes, and passes it through the PIX egress gate.
577///
578/// Built as one piece, and not inline where the Session is set up, so that the order of its three
579/// steps can be tested: the SURB is booked only when the packet goes on, so a packet that is held is
580/// not counted against the very stock it is waiting for.
581///
582/// The SURB is booked with the refund that gives it back (see [`count_return_packet_surb`]), as on
583/// every other path a return packet takes: a packet the gate refuses, or one routing resolution drops
584/// for want of a SURB, does not keep the stock the reserve is measured against one low.
585///
586/// `keeps_alive` says whether the Exit runs a keep-alive stream for the Session (a SURB-level
587/// notification period, or PIX fill; see [`SessionManager::spawn_exit_keep_alive`]). The reserve is
588/// kept for that stream, so without one nothing is held back.
589fn exit_data_egress<Si>(
590    sink: Si,
591    session_id: SessionId,
592    estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
593    balancer: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
594    gate: Option<Arc<ServiceGate>>,
595    keeps_alive: bool,
596    instance: Arc<SlotInstance>,
597) -> impl Sink<EgressItem, Error = std::io::Error>
598where
599    Si: Sink<EgressItem, Error = std::io::Error>,
600{
601    sink.with(move |(routing, data): EgressItem| -> EgressPermit {
602        // Before anything is counted: a Session whose slot is gone sends nothing, and a refused
603        // packet must leave the SURB accounting as it found it.
604        if instance.is_superseded() {
605            return futures::future::Either::Left(std::future::ready(Err(superseded_write_error())));
606        }
607        // Each outgoing packet consumes one SURB, given back if the packet never takes it
608        let book_consumed = move |estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, data: ApplicationDataOut| {
609            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
610            telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
611            count_return_packet_surb(estimator, data)
612        };
613        let held = keeps_alive
614            .then(|| hold_for_surb_reserve(session_id, &estimator, &balancer, gate.is_some(), &instance))
615            .flatten();
616        match held {
617            None => acquire_egress_permit_for(&instance, gate.clone(), routing, book_consumed(&estimator, data)),
618            Some(held) => {
619                let (estimator, gate, instance) = (estimator.clone(), gate.clone(), instance.clone());
620                futures::future::Either::Right(Box::pin(async move {
621                    held.await;
622                    // The hold can last as long as the stock is thin; the slot may be gone by its end.
623                    if instance.is_superseded() {
624                        return Err(superseded_write_error());
625                    }
626                    acquire_egress_permit_for(&instance, gate, routing, book_consumed(&estimator, data)).await
627                }))
628            }
629        }
630    })
631}

633/// Closes an established Session.
634///
635/// Logs the counterpart of "new session established" (see [`SessionSlotGuard::commit`]): one line
636/// per Session at INFO, so its whole lifetime can be read from a production log without the
637/// per-frame detail of the socket.
638///
639/// `admission` is the SURB-store seam, forwarded to [`release_session_slot`]; `None` only ever
640/// reaches here from a teardown that had no seam to call.
641fn close_session(
642    session_id: SessionId,
643    session_data: SessionSlot,
644    reason: ClosureReason,
645    admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
646    grace: Duration,
647    token: AdmissionToken,
648) {
649    tracing::info!(%session_id, %reason, "session closed");
650    release_session_slot(session_id, session_data, reason, admission, grace, token);
651}
652
653/// Tears down a Session slot: stops its tasks and returns what it holds.
654///
655/// Logs nothing at INFO, because it also cleans up a Session whose setup failed before it was
656/// established (see [`SessionSlotGuard`]). An established Session is closed with [`close_session`].
657///
658/// Takes the slot off `METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS`, which counts slots from their allocation (see
659/// [`SessionManager::allocate_session_slot`]), so a slot torn down before its commit is paired too.
660///
661/// Parks the Entry's PIX ledger and last challenge, unless [`remove_slot_if`] already did when it took
662/// the slot out (see [`SlotInstance::park_records`]).
663///
664/// Retires the Session's pseudonym from the SURB store's admitted class, but not immediately: the
665/// retire is pushed past the packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window, so the return-routed
666/// notification a closing Exit has just enqueued — the PIX-failure notice is the one such packet —
667/// still finds its ring when the resolution stage comes to look it up. Retiring inline destroyed
668/// that ring mid-lookup, the packet was dropped, and the Entry never learned that its Session was
669/// gone (hoprnet#8515's `deposit_timeout_closes_session` fails exactly there).
670///
671/// Deferring is only safe because the retire carries the [`AdmissionToken`] its `admit` returned and
672/// the store honours it only while it still names the pseudonym's current admission. Without that
673/// guard, a retire landing in the window could invalidate a *successor* Session's ring: the
674/// pseudonym is client-chosen ([`SessionClientConfig::pseudonym`]) and freely reusable, so a Session
675/// can be re-established on the same one while the previous teardown is still waiting. That failure
676/// is worse than the one being fixed — the successor would go on inserting its SURBs into the small
677/// un-admitted quarantine with nothing logged anywhere — which is why the token is load-bearing here
678/// rather than an optional nicety. Conversely, the guard means no teardown path needs its retire
679/// suppressed: a stale retire is a no-op at the store, never a lost one.
680///
681/// Synchronous-or-spawned, decided by the runtime: when one is running, the delayed retire is spawned
682/// on it; when none is — a `Drop` or the public `close_session` can run off-runtime — the retire
683/// happens inline. The fallback is correct because a teardown with no runtime has no packet pipeline
684/// resolving anything on its behalf either: the SURB-resolution window the deferral exists for is a
685/// property of that pipeline, so there is nothing to wait out, and retiring inline is exactly the
686/// behaviour the synchronous world had before the deferral.
687///
688/// Idempotent by contract, so a rollback — a Session that was never committed, hence never admitted
689/// — pays a no-op here rather than needing a separate "was it admitted?" flag threaded through the
690/// guard.
691///
692/// [`SessionClientConfig::pseudonym`]: crate::SessionClientConfig::pseudonym
693#[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(session_data, admission))]
694fn release_session_slot(
695    session_id: SessionId,
696    session_data: SessionSlot,
697    reason: ClosureReason,
698    admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
699    grace: Duration,
700    token: AdmissionToken,
701) {
702    debug!("closing session");
703
704    // Deferred past the packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window — see the doc comment above — and
705    // made safe by the token, so the retire is never suppressed: a stale one is a no-op at the store.
706    // Cloned rather than moved: the teardown below keeps using `session_id` for the metrics and the
707    // channel bookkeeping that follow the retire.
708    defer_admission_retire(admission, grace, &session_id, token);
709
710    // The teardown is of this slot's instance only: a successor under the same pseudonym keeps its own
711    // lifecycle state and gauges.
712    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
713    {
714        let owner = session_data.instance.id();
715        if telemetry::owns_session_metrics(&session_id, owner) {
716            set_session_state(&session_id, SessionLifecycleState::Closed);
717        }
718        remove_session_metrics_state(&session_id, session_data.pix_egress_gate.get().is_some(), owner);
719    }
720
721    // The data plane is gone: a `HoprSession` still held for it must not send any more. Idempotent
722    // with `remove_slot_if`; this is the path of idle and size evictions.
723    session_data.instance.supersede();
724    session_data.pix_supervisor.mark_torn_down();
725
726    // The Entry's PIX ledger and last challenge leave the slot for their retention caches on every
727    // teardown path, so their retention starts now and not when the Session was initiated. Every removal
728    // through `remove_slot_if` has parked them already, inside the removal, and this is then a no-op;
729    // this call parks for the slots the cache itself evicted (idle expiry, capacity).
730    session_data.instance.park_records(session_id);
731
732    if reason != ClosureReason::EmptyRead {
733        // Closing the data sender will also cause it to close from the read side
734        debug!("data tx channel closed on session");
735    }
736
737    // Poison the egress gate before aborting anything. A writer parked on an exhausted predeposit
738    // budget is waiting for a supervisor that is about to stop existing, so it has to be failed
739    // rather than left pending — aborting the tasks first would remove the only thing that could
740    // still have woken it.
741    if let Some(gate) = session_data.pix_egress_gate.get() {
742        gate.poison();
743    }
744
745    // Return this Session's share of the node-level PIX aggregates, after the gate is poisoned so
746    // that no permit it was still handing out is missed. Explicit rather than left to `Drop` for the
747    // reason `CycleBudgetReservation` gives below, and one more: the supervisor worker is spawned
748    // detached and stops only when the last command sender goes with the slot — which the cache does
749    // during a later maintenance pass. Until then the node would report Sessions and cycles that no
750    // longer exist. Idempotent, so the `Drop` backstop is free to run afterwards.
751    if let Some(supervisor) = session_data.pix_supervisor.get() {
752        supervisor.telemetry.release();
753    }
754
755    // Terminate any additional tasks spawned by the Session. This is also what releases the PIX
756    // reconstructor state: the action driver holds a commitment guard per live cycle, and aborting
757    // it drops them.
758    session_data.abort_handles.lock().abort_all();
759
760    // And return the memory those cycles were admitted against, now rather than whenever the last
761    // clone of this slot happens to be dropped. Idempotent, so the slot's own `Drop` — including
762    // the cache's deferred one — is free to run afterwards.
763    if let Some(reservation) = session_data.cycle_budget.as_ref() {
764        reservation.release();
765    }
766
767    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
768    METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS.decrement(1.0);
769}
770
771/// How a close is answered for a Session whose SURB buffer is already draining.
772///
773/// A `WriteClosed`/`EmptyRead` is the end-of-stream our own ingress abort produces, so it is absorbed
774/// and the drain continues; anything else — a second operator close, or a peer `SessionError` —
775/// overrules the drain by falling through to the hard teardown.
776///
777/// [`begin_surb_drain`](SessionManager::begin_surb_drain) asks it twice, because a Session can be
778/// found draining either before the transition or by losing it to a concurrent close.
779fn answer_while_draining(reason: ClosureReason) -> Option<bool> {
780    matches!(reason, ClosureReason::WriteClosed | ClosureReason::EmptyRead).then_some(true)
781}
782
783fn initiation_timeout_max_one_way(base: Duration, hops: usize) -> Duration {
784    base * (hops as u32)
785}
786
787/// How long `new_session` waits for the answer to a `StartSession` over the given hop counts.
788fn initiation_wait(base: Duration, forward_hops: usize, return_hops: usize) -> Duration {
789    initiation_timeout_max_one_way(base, forward_hops + return_hops + 2)
790}
791
792/// TTL of the pending-initiation caches: the longest [`initiation_wait`] plus the time the
793/// `StartSession` send may take before that wait starts.
794fn initiation_cache_ttl(base: Duration) -> Duration {
795    initiation_wait(
796        base,
797        RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS,
798        RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS,
799    ) + EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT
800}
801
802/// Conservative lower bound on how many coefficient commitments fit into one `SsaCommit` message.
803///
804/// Mirrors the sizing in `SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple`: payload minus the fixed
805/// prefix (`ssa_index` + `coefficient_index` + `num_polys` + the Start header) and minus a generous
806/// allowance for the CBOR-encoded session id, divided by the per-entry cost
807/// (`PolynomialIndex` + one serialized group element). Using a *lower* bound here means the derived
808/// message count is an over-estimate, which is the safe direction for sizing a queue.
809///
810/// The commitment proof of knowledge is subtracted as well. Every message carries it, since every
811/// message is a constant-term message.
812const MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG: usize = {
813    const FIXED_PREFIX: usize = 12;
814    // A `SessionId` is a 10-byte pseudonym; 64 bytes is a large allowance for its CBOR framing.
815    const CBOR_SESSION_ID_ALLOWANCE: usize = 64;
816    const PER_ENTRY: usize = size_of::<hopr_protocol_pix::PolynomialIndex>() + size_of::<HoprPixGroupElement>();
817
818    let usable = ApplicationData::PAYLOAD_SIZE
819        .saturating_sub(FIXED_PREFIX + CBOR_SESSION_ID_ALLOWANCE + HOPR_PIX_COMMITMENT_PROOF_SIZE);
820    let per_msg = usable / PER_ENTRY;
821    if per_msg == 0 { 1 } else { per_msg }
822};
823
824/// Slack added on top of the PIX commitment burst to cover non-PIX Start protocol traffic
825/// (session initiations, establishments, errors, keep-alives).
826const START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE: usize = 10;
827
828/// How many drops of a full queue may pass between two `warn!` lines.
829///
830/// Warning per drop would reproduce the per-packet log spam these quiet drops exist to remove.
831const FULL_QUEUE_WARN_INTERVAL: usize = 256;
832
833/// Whether the drop that saw `drops_so_far` prior full-queue drops is the one that logs.
834fn is_full_queue_warn_due(drops_so_far: usize) -> bool {
835    drops_so_far.is_multiple_of(FULL_QUEUE_WARN_INTERVAL)
836}
837
838/// How many queued `StartSession`s may wait per handler.
839///
840/// Two is enough to keep the pool fed without queuing work beyond a peer's initiation timeout.
841const START_SESSION_LANE_DEPTH_FACTOR: usize = 2;
842
843/// `StartSession` handlers allowed in hand at once.
844///
845/// Mirrors `incoming_session_capacity` in `hopr-lib` (256), the other bound on a handshake; that
846/// figure is not reachable from [`SessionManagerConfig`].
847const MAX_CONCURRENT_START_SESSIONS: usize = 256;
848
849/// Concurrent session-server admission waits, held below the lane size so a slow server refuses
850/// with `Busy` instead of parking every handler.
851///
852/// The session server bounds its own worker pool by the same figure: a permit is released when the
853/// transport stops waiting, not when `admit` returns, so the server needs its own bound.
854pub const START_SESSION_ADMISSION_CONCURRENCY: usize = 64;
855
856/// Capacity of the control Start protocol lane (every variant but `StartSession`).
857///
858/// Fed by [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`] with `try_send`, and an overflow **drops** the
859/// message. For most Start messages that is recoverable, but a dropped `SsaCommit` is not: there is
860/// no NACK or retransmission, so the coefficient cell stays empty forever, the commitment never
861/// completes, and the cycle dies on the supervisor's `max_deposit_wait` deadline. It therefore keeps
862/// the whole PIX commitment term.
863///
864/// PIX load is the *entire* commitment set of an SSA cycle, chunked into packet-sized messages.
865/// Batching multiplies it: an Exit may ask for up to
866/// [`ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request) SSAs at once, so the per-cycle
867/// term is scaled by the configured maximum even when dynamic admission selects less.
868///
869/// The per-cycle burst is bounded by two independent limits, and the capacity takes the smaller:
870///
871/// * `quota_range.end() / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE` is `polys × (threshold + surplus)`, an over-estimate by that whole
872///   second factor, since a cycle carries one constant term per polynomial and nothing else. The quota alone does not
873///   reveal how the product splits, so the over-estimate cannot be undone from it.
874/// * [`MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA`] is the number of polynomials [`SessionManager::check_pix_params`] will accept, whatever the
875///   quota says. It therefore bounds the commitments a cycle can ever deliver.
876///
877/// Clamping to the second matters because this capacity is *reserved*: an operator-settable
878/// `quota_range` feeding an unclamped derivation is an allocation with no upper bound — at
879/// `quota_range.end() = 1e13` it asks for 77 GB. At the default dimensions the commitments reach
880/// the [`MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA`] ceiling, so the capacity term is the resulting burst plus
881/// `START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE`: the margin over the burst is the reserve itself.
882///
883/// The batch factor is bounded by [`MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE`] for the same allocation reason, and is
884/// clamped here rather than taken on trust from the config, so callers that build a
885/// [`SessionManagerConfig`] without going through [`SessionManager::new`] cannot inflate it.
886///
887/// Deliberately **not** sized by `maximum_sessions`: that quantity sizes the session lane, where a
888/// `StartSession` flood's own drops are taken, and this lane is the one a flood must not touch.
889fn start_control_channel_capacity(cfg: &SessionManagerConfig) -> usize {
890    let max_commitments = (*cfg.pix_config.quota_range.end() / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE).min(MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64);
891    let max_commit_msgs = max_commitments.div_ceil(MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG as u64);
892    let ssas_per_request = cfg.pix_config.supervision.ssas_per_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE) as u64;
893
894    // `usize::try_from` cannot fail on 64-bit targets; saturate rather than panic on 32-bit ones.
895    usize::try_from(max_commit_msgs.saturating_mul(ssas_per_request))
896        .unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
897        .saturating_add(START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE)
898}
899
900/// Capacity of the `StartSession` lane.
901///
902/// Sized from the handler pool, not from `maximum_sessions`: a queued `StartSession` is drained only
903/// as fast as a handler frees up, and each may park for `session_admission_timeout`. A lane sized by
904/// the session limit would queue minutes of work in front of the pool, so the peer long since gave
905/// up by the time it is handled.
906fn start_session_channel_capacity() -> usize {
907    (MAX_CONCURRENT_START_SESSIONS * START_SESSION_LANE_DEPTH_FACTOR).saturating_add(START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE)
908}
909
910/// Minimum time the SURB buffer must endure if no SURBs are being produced.
911pub const MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
912/// Minimum time between SURB buffer notifications to the Entry.
913pub const MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);
914
915/// How many idle reports fit into the Entry's slot idle timeout at the longest backoff.
916///
917/// On an idle Session the Exit's reports are the only thing refreshing the Entry's slot idle timer (the
918/// session cache's `time_to_idle`, [`SessionManagerConfig::idle_timeout`]). A quarter of it means that with
919/// two lost reports the next still lands a quarter of the timeout before the Entry's slot expires.
920///
921/// The Entry announces its idle timeout when it opens the Session (see [`into_initiation_additional_data`]),
922/// and the cap is a quarter of that. An Entry that announces none, as older releases do, is assumed to use the
923/// Exit's idle timeout, which bounds the node's cap (both default to 3 minutes).
924const IDLE_NOTIFY_PERIODS_PER_IDLE_TIMEOUT: u32 = 4;
925
926/// Idle reports sent at the base period before backing off: the first idle minute at 15 s.
927const IDLE_REPORTS_AT_BASE: u32 = 4;
928
929/// The report period after `idle_reports` idle reports: `base` for the first [`IDLE_REPORTS_AT_BASE`], then
930/// doubling up to `cap`. At 15 s and 60 s the gaps run 15, 15, 15, 30, 60, 60, ...
931fn backed_off_notify_period(base: Duration, cap: Duration, idle_reports: u32) -> Duration {
932    let doublings = idle_reports.saturating_sub(IDLE_REPORTS_AT_BASE - 1);
933    // Capped so the shift stays inside `u32`.
934    let factor = 1u32.checked_shl(doublings.min(31)).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
935    base.checked_mul(factor).map_or(cap, |period| period.min(cap)).max(base)
936}
937
938/// Tells the Exit's keep-alive stream, if it runs one, that application data moved.
939///
940/// Looked up per packet: the data path is built before `spawn_exit_keep_alive` publishes the control.
941#[inline]
942fn note_exit_data_activity(activity: &OnceLock<Arc<PixFillControl>>) {
943    if let Some(control) = activity.get() {
944        control.note_data_activity();
945    }
946}
947
948/// Fastest return-path rate a Session is assumed to sustain, in packets per second.
949///
950/// Bounds the PIX `max_recovery_time` from below: a deadline this rate cannot meet is treated as one
951/// no Session can, so without fill it is the floor itself, and with fill it caps the `fill.max_rate`
952/// the floor may count on. Stated in packets, because per-packet work is what limits a Session, so it does not
953/// move with any packet or segment size; it carries ≈ 58 Mbps of Session data at full
954/// [`SESSION_MTU`] segments.
955pub const MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE: u64 = 5000;
956
957/// The first challenge value used in Start protocol to initiate a session.
958pub(crate) const MIN_CHALLENGE: StartChallenge = 1;
959
960/// Maximum time to wait for counterparty to receive the target number of SURBs.
961const SESSION_READINESS_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
962
963/// How long the Entry holds a *near-miss* `SsaRequest` while the Exit's returned data catches up to
964/// the successor boundary.
965///
966/// Absorbs mixer reordering between the returned packets and the `SsaRequest` they earned — the two
967/// travel the same mixed path, so the request can arrive ahead of the last few packets that
968/// justified it. Nothing longer: a sustained shortfall never reaches this wait, because the gate only
969/// enters it for a request already within one emission window of the boundary.
970///
971/// Comfortably inside the Exit's `max_ssa_delivery_time` (20 s by default, batch-scaled), which is
972/// what closes the Session as `CommitmentTimeout` if no `SsaCommit` follows. That budget also has to
973/// cover generating the commitments and shipping the burst, so this takes a small slice of it.
974const SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);
975
976/// How often [`SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT`] re-reads the returned-packet count.
977///
978/// Polled rather than notified: the alternative is waking a waiter from the Session receive path,
979/// which would put a branch on every inbound packet to serve a case that arises once per SSA cycle.
980const SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_POLL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);
981
982/// How long after a batch's commitments last went out the Entry takes a repeat of its request to
983/// mean that they were lost on the way, rather than that the repeat crossed them.
984///
985/// The Exit repeats a successor request while some member of it has received no part of its
986/// commitment. A repeat it sent before the burst reached it can still be arriving up to a round trip
987/// after the burst went out, and answering that one would spend a retransmission on a burst that is
988/// not lost. A repeat that arrives later says the burst went out and none of it arrived. Publishing
989/// a burst only means the local transport took it, and a relayer that dies on the forward path loses
990/// all of it. The Exit then has no part it could name in a scoped re-request, so the repeat is the
991/// only prompt there is. See [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`].
992///
993/// Well over a round trip, and equal to the Exit's default re-send interval. A path slower than this
994/// costs at most one needless re-send per grace, and each re-send spends one of the cycle's
995/// [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS).
996const SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);
997
998/// Standard deviations below an honest Exit's expected returned packets at which the successor gate
999/// sets its bar — see [`successor_required_packets`].
1000///
1001/// Four put the chance that an Exit losing exactly the tolerated share fraction falls short of the
1002/// bar at 3 × 10⁻⁵, and that it falls short by more than the near-miss window — refused without
1003/// waiting — at about one in 1.5 million at the deployed split (normal approximation). A shortfall
1004/// inside the window still gets [`SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT`] for the Session's ongoing traffic to
1005/// make it up. The price is ~0.33 % of the boundary added to what an Exit can withhold and still be
1006/// funded: the deployed bar moves from 41.3 % of a cycle's packets to 41.0 %.
1007const SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS: f64 = 4.0;
1008
1009/// Returned packets the successor gate demands of an Exit whose boundary is `target` packets, at the
1010/// share loss `tolerated_loss` the negotiated split survives.
1011///
1012/// `floor(max(0, μ − zσ))` for an Exit's arrivals at exactly that loss, `Binomial(target, 1 − L)`:
1013/// `μ = target · (1 − L)`, `σ = √(target · L · (1 − L))` and `z` [`SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS`].
1014/// A split with no surplus tolerates no loss, so σ is zero and the whole target is demanded exactly.
1015///
1016/// A tolerance near one floors at one packet, not zero, for any non-zero target: the bound is at most
1017/// `μ ≤ target`, so one is never more than the boundary itself. Without it a tiny boundary under a
1018/// huge surplus (`128 × (2 + 255)`: μ 10.8, σ 3.2) demands nothing, the near-miss wait never starts
1019/// on zero returned packets, and the successor is funded on the Entry's own emission alone. An Exit
1020/// that has returned nothing since its first commitment has shown no service whatever split the Entry
1021/// chose. The cost is an honest Exit at the tolerated loss returning nothing with probability
1022/// `L^target` — 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ at `128 × (2 + 255)`, the order of the 4σ bound's own 3 × 10⁻⁵ — and
1023/// it bites only at degenerate cycles of a few dozen packets (`8 × (2 + 255)`: 0.59), where no
1024/// statistic means anything.
1025///
1026/// An `f64` carries both terms to well under a packet below a watermark of 10⁹ cycles.
1027fn successor_required_packets(target: u64, tolerated_loss: f64) -> u64 {
1028    let bar_floor = target.min(1);
1029    let target = target as f64;
1030    let delivered = 1.0 - tolerated_loss;
1031    let mean = target * delivered;
1032    let deviation = (target * tolerated_loss * delivered).sqrt();
1033    // The cast floors, the clamped bound being non-negative.
1034    let bound = (mean - SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * deviation).max(0.0) as u64;
1035    bound.max(bar_floor)
1036}
1037
1038/// Minimum timeout until an unfinished frame is discarded.
1039const MIN_FRAME_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(10);
1040
1041/// Hard ceiling on both SSA batch-size knobs, whatever the configuration says.
1042///
1043/// The current maximum value of 9 is based on the current available pool limitations.
1044///
1045/// Deliberately far below the wire limit (`StartProtocol::MAX_SSAS_PER_REQUEST`, 27), which only
1046/// bounds what can be *decoded*. The real cost is paid on both sides of the exchange and neither is
1047/// small at the profiled dimensions:
1048///
1049/// * Entry: every entry in the batch is a full `new_ssa_commitment` (hundreds of thousands of EC commitments), its own
1050///   burst of thousands of `SsaCommit` packets, and its own `ReadyToDeposit` — i.e. its own on-chain deposit.
1051/// * Exit: every entry is a live reconstructor cycle, held until that cycle recovers — worst case ≈15.4 MiB at the
1052///   deployed dimensions (`hopr_protocol_pix::peak_cycle_bytes`), so ≈138 MiB per Session at this ceiling, before the
1053///   pipelining factor. That is what a Session reserves against [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::max_live_cycle_bytes`], so
1054///   raising the batch size directly divides how many PIX Sessions the node will accept.
1055///
1056/// It also bounds the supervisor's deadline scaling: a batch multiplies both
1057/// [`max_ssa_delivery_time`](crate::SupervisorConfig::max_ssa_delivery_time) and
1058/// [`max_deposit_wait`](crate::SupervisorConfig::max_deposit_wait), and that product is what decides
1059/// how long a Session may be served unincentivized.
1060///
1061/// Both [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request) and
1062/// [`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`] are clamped to `1..=Self` where they are read,
1063/// so a programmatically built config that never calls `validate()` cannot exceed it.
1064pub const MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE: usize = 9;
1065
1066// The Entry's retention of commitment material has to outlast the batch that material belongs to.
1067// `hopr-protocol-pix` cannot see this figure, so it derives its cap from it in prose; this is the
1068// half of that derivation which has to hold. A cycle must stay retransmittable at least until its
1069// own batch has finished being committed, or a commitment packet lost early in a large batch becomes
1070// unrepairable while the rest of the batch is still arriving. Slack beyond one batch is a judgement
1071// call, which is why this is an inequality and not the equality the two figures satisfy today.
1072const _: () = assert!(
1073    hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_RETAINED_COMMITMENT_CYCLES >= MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE,
1074    "MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE exceeds MAX_RETAINED_COMMITMENT_CYCLES, so a cycle can be evicted from the Entry's retention \
1075     before its own batch is fully committed and its commitment stops being repairable"
1076);
1077
1078/// How long an Exit waits for the deposit pool to answer a
1079/// [`DepositDataRequest`](HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest) before sending the batch
1080/// without what has not arrived.
1081pub const DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);
1082
1083/// SSA batches whose reconstructor state can be live on the Exit at the same moment.
1084///
1085/// Two, enforced at allocation rather than inferred from share-order policy. The supervisor tags
1086/// every requested generation and defers a successor while this many generations still own live
1087/// reconstructor state; it also checks the equivalent full-batch cycle count charged below. Full
1088/// recovery releases cycle state immediately, after which a deferred request is retried.
1089///
1090/// Used as the pipelining factor when a Session reserves against
1091/// [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::max_live_cycle_bytes`].
1092pub const MAX_OVERLAPPING_BATCHES: u64 = 2;
1093
1094/// What a PIX Session at these dimensions costs the node's live-cycle budget.
1095///
1096/// The worst case one cycle can hold, times every cycle that can be live at once. Both factors come
1097/// from configuration rather than observation, because the charge is made before the Session exists.
1098/// `ssas_per_request` is clamped for the reason [`SessionManager::new`] clamps it — a
1099/// programmatically built config must not be able to understate the reservation and then overrun it.
1100pub fn cycle_budget_for(params: &PixParams, ssas_per_request: usize) -> u64 {
1101    hopr_protocol_pix::peak_cycle_bytes::<HoprPixSpec>(params)
1102        .saturating_mul(ssas_per_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE) as u64)
1103        .saturating_mul(MAX_OVERLAPPING_BATCHES)
1104}
1105
1106/// The largest reservation any offer inside a `quota_range` ending at `quota_bytes` can produce.
1107///
1108/// The quota fixes `polys × (threshold + surplus)` but not the split, and the two terms of
1109/// [`hopr_protocol_pix::peak_cycle_bytes`] pull opposite ways — the share buffers want a high
1110/// threshold, the per-polynomial overhead wants many polynomials — so the maximum is found by
1111/// walking the thresholds rather than by a closed form. 254 iterations, once, at config load.
1112///
1113/// `surplus = 0` throughout, which is what makes each candidate the worst of its threshold: the
1114/// surplus is priced into the quota but holds no reconstructor state, so any surplus at all buys
1115/// fewer polynomials for the same quota.
1116///
1117/// Used to reject a [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::max_live_cycle_bytes`] that could never admit even
1118/// one Session at the dimensions its own `quota_range` advertises.
1119pub fn max_cycle_budget_for_quota(quota_bytes: u64, ssas_per_request: usize) -> u64 {
1120    let quota_shares = quota_bytes / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE;
1121
1122    (hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_POLY_THRESHOLD..=hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_POLY_THRESHOLD)
1123        .filter_map(|threshold| {
1124            let polys = u16::try_from((quota_shares / threshold as u64).min(MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64)).ok()?;
1125            PixParams::try_new(polys, threshold, 0, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE).ok()
1126        })
1127        .map(|params| cycle_budget_for(&params, ssas_per_request))
1128        .max()
1129        .unwrap_or_default()
1130}
1131
1132/// Default for [`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`] — how many SSA commitments an Entry
1133/// accepts in a single [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`].
1134///
1135/// Pipelining needs at most one cycle in flight ahead of the active one, so 2 leaves room for an Exit
1136/// batching at the default without turning one inbound packet into an unbounded amount of Entry work
1137/// and on-chain deposits.
1138pub const DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST: usize = 2;
1139
1140/// Default for [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request) —
1141/// how many SSAs an Exit may ask for in a single [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`]. It is the maximum
1142/// in dynamic mode and the exact batch in fixed mode.
1143///
1144/// One, so that the default configuration produces exactly the unbatched exchange: same wire bytes,
1145/// same supervisor deadlines, same Start protocol channel capacity.
1146pub const DEFAULT_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST: usize = 1;
1147
1148/// Timeout when sending Start protocol messages to the sink
1149const EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);
1150
1151// Needs to use an UnboundedSender instead of oneshot
1152// because Moka cache requires the value to be Clone, which oneshot Sender is not.
1153// It also cannot be enclosed in an Arc, since calling `send` consumes the oneshot Sender.
1154// The Session initiation cache is only present on the Entry (client) side.
1155type SessionInitiationCache = moka::sync::Cache<
1156    StartChallenge,
1157    crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::One<Result<InitiationReply, StartErrorType<SessionId>>>>,
1158>;
1159
1160/// What the Exit answered to an initiation.
1161#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
1162enum InitiationReply {
1163    /// A fresh Session: the Exit holds nothing of a predecessor's.
1164    Established(StartEstablished<SessionId>),
1165    /// The Exit took over a Session it still held: both sides number the stream from `stream_base`.
1166    Resumed(StartResumed<SessionId>),
1167}
1168
1169impl InitiationReply {
1170    fn session_id(&self) -> SessionId {
1171        match self {
1172            Self::Established(est) => est.session_id,
1173            Self::Resumed(res) => res.session_id,
1174        }
1175    }
1176
1177    fn orig_challenge(&self) -> StartChallenge {
1178        match self {
1179            Self::Established(est) => est.orig_challenge,
1180            Self::Resumed(res) => res.orig_challenge,
1181        }
1182    }
1183
1184    /// The agreed stream base, `None` for a fresh Session.
1185    fn stream_base(&self) -> Option<u32> {
1186        match self {
1187            Self::Established(_) => None,
1188            Self::Resumed(res) => Some(res.stream_base),
1189        }
1190    }
1191}
1192
1193/// Handles to streams and tasks spawned by the Session.
1194#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
1195enum SessionHandles {
1196    /// Handle to the stream that facilitates ingress of data from the HOPR network into the Session.
1197    Ingress,
1198    /// Handle to the process that sends keep-alive messages to the Session recipient (Exit).
1199    KeepAlive,
1200    /// Handle to the one-shot timer that turns the SURB-level notification on after its first period.
1201    ///
1202    /// Registered rather than fired and forgotten: it holds an `Arc<PixFillControl>` for as long as
1203    /// the period lasts, and no maximum is enforced on that period, so an unregistered task keeps a
1204    /// closed Session's fill control alive for however long the operator configured.
1205    SurbNotifyDelay,
1206    /// Handle to the driver that switches the SURB-level notification to its degraded period.
1207    ///
1208    /// Runs only on an Exit Session that is configured for the degraded period *and* has a frame
1209    /// loss signal to read, which is what tells it that the forward path went dark.
1210    SurbNotifyDegraded,
1211    /// Handle to the process that monitors and balances SURBs.
1212    Balancer,
1213    /// Handle to the task that executes the PIX supervisor's actions.
1214    ///
1215    /// One per Session rather than one per cycle: the supervisor multiplexes every SSA it tracks
1216    /// onto a single action stream.
1217    PixActionDriver,
1218    /// Handle to the process that awaits the PIX deposit for one SSA.
1219    ///
1220    /// Carries the inner `SsaIndex` value so that each cycle's observer is independent — pipelining
1221    /// must not cancel an earlier cycle's.
1222    PixDepositObserver(u32),
1223    /// Handle to the task that sends forward receipts to the Entry.
1224    ForwardReceipts,
1225    /// Handle to the timer that ends a detached Exit PIX Session's resume window.
1226    ///
1227    /// Registered under one key, so arming a new window aborts any earlier one; the takeover aborts
1228    /// it too, and a teardown with the rest of the Session's tasks.
1229    ResumeWindow,
1230}
1231
1232impl std::fmt::Display for SessionHandles {
1233    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
1234        match self {
1235            Self::Ingress => write!(f, "Ingress"),
1236            Self::KeepAlive => write!(f, "KeepAlive"),
1237            Self::SurbNotifyDelay => write!(f, "SurbNotifyDelay"),
1238            Self::SurbNotifyDegraded => write!(f, "SurbNotifyDegraded"),
1239            Self::Balancer => write!(f, "Balancer"),
1240            Self::PixActionDriver => write!(f, "PixActionDriver"),
1241            Self::PixDepositObserver(idx) => write!(f, "PixDepositObserver({idx})"),
1242            Self::ForwardReceipts => write!(f, "ForwardReceipts"),
1243            Self::ResumeWindow => write!(f, "ResumeWindow"),
1244        }
1245    }
1246}
1247
1248/// How a PIX deposit observer ended.
1249#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1250enum DepositObserverEnd {
1251    /// The supervisor stopped accepting events, so the channel's end was not reported.
1252    SupervisorGone,
1253    /// The deposit channel ended after a non-zero confirmation was forwarded.
1254    Funded,
1255    /// The deposit channel ended without a non-zero confirmation being forwarded.
1256    Unfunded,
1257}
1258
1259/// Forwards confirmations while the deposit channel remains open.
1260///
1261/// The supervisor owns the deadline, so the observer carries none — a timeout here would
1262/// have been a second authority racing the first.
1263async fn observe_deposits<S, F, Fut>(
1264    confirmations: S,
1265    session_id: SessionId,
1266    ssa_id: SsaId<HoprPseudonym>,
1267    mut report: F,
1268) -> DepositObserverEnd
1269where
1270    S: futures::Stream<Item = (PixAddressId, HoprBalance)>,
1271    F: FnMut(SessionPixEvent) -> Fut,
1272    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<(), ()>>,
1273{
1274    let filtered_confirmations = confirmations.filter(|(evt_id, _)| {
1275        futures::future::ready(evt_id.ssa_index() == ssa_id.ssa_index() && &evt_id.session_id() == ssa_id.pseudonym())
1276    });
1277    futures::pin_mut!(filtered_confirmations);
1278    let mut funded = false;
1279    let mut confirmations = 0_u32;
1280    while let Some((_, amount)) = filtered_confirmations.next().await {
1281        info!(%session_id, %ssa_id, %amount, "ssa deposit confirmed");
1282        if report(SessionPixEvent::DepositConfirmed { ssa_id, amount })
1283            .await
1284            .is_err()
1285        {
1286            return DepositObserverEnd::SupervisorGone;
1287        }
1288        funded |= amount != HoprBalance::zero();
1289        confirmations = confirmations.saturating_add(1);
1290    }
1291    let end = if funded {
1292        debug!(%session_id, %ssa_id, confirmations, "deposit channel closed after confirmation");
1293        DepositObserverEnd::Funded
1294    } else {
1295        warn!(%session_id, %ssa_id, confirmations, "deposit channel closed without confirmation");
1296        DepositObserverEnd::Unfunded
1297    };
1298    // Always report the deposit channel ending: the supervisor decides whether the cycle is lost,
1299    // and its phase guard makes this event a no-op for a funded cycle.
1300    let _ = report(SessionPixEvent::DepositObserverClosed(ssa_id)).await;
1301    end
1302}
1303
1304/// The PIX dimensions this Session negotiated, on the Exit side.
1305///
1306/// Once carried the SSA index and a fault counter as well. Both moved to the supervisor: it decides
1307/// *when* a cycle is requested, so it is also what allocates the index, and it is what enforces the
1308/// fault limit. Leaving a second copy of either here would have meant two authorities for one fact.
1309#[derive(Debug)]
1310struct SessionSsaState {
1311    /// The dimensions this Session negotiated, as they went on the wire.
1312    params: PixParams,
1313    /// Highest SSA index this Session has had the generator commit to, `0` before the first batch.
1314    ///
1315    /// A deliberate second copy of a fact the generator already holds, and the only one of the three
1316    /// that came back. The generator's own watermark lives in a cache with an idle retention, so
1317    /// "absent" there conflates *never committed* with *state discarded* — and those must not be
1318    /// treated alike, because the first is the opening batch every Session begins with and the second
1319    /// is a Session whose Entry can no longer serve the cycles it already committed to. This copy
1320    /// lives exactly as long as the Session does, so it can tell them apart. See the successor gate in
1321    /// [`SessionManager::handle_ssa_request`].
1322    ///
1323    /// Entry-side only; an Exit never commits and leaves it at zero. [`SsaIndex`] is a `NonZero<u32>`,
1324    /// which is what makes `0` an unambiguous "none" rather than a sentinel that has to be defended.
1325    committed_ssa_watermark: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
1326    /// [`SessionSlot::returned_packets`] as it stood when this Session first committed.
1327    ///
1328    /// The successor gate counts service *since* that instant, not since the Session opened. Before
1329    /// the first commitment the generator holds no polynomials, so the SURBs going out carry no
1330    /// shares — and an Exit may legitimately be served up to `max_predeposit_packets` of them before
1331    /// any deposit exists. Crediting that prefix would let the Exit bank unpaid service against the
1332    /// first cycle it *is* paid for. Everything after this point rides a share.
1333    returned_at_first_commit: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
1334    /// Lowest SSA index of the request this Session most recently committed to, `0` before the first.
1335    ///
1336    /// What lets the Entry tell a *repeat* of a request it already served from a *stale* one. Both
1337    /// ask for an index at or below [`committed_ssa_watermark`](Self::committed_ssa_watermark); only
1338    /// a repeat names the batch that was last committed. The Exit re-sends an unanswered successor
1339    /// request until it hears back, so a repeat is the ordinary case once a request is admitted and
1340    /// the first burst is still on its way, and answering it with a second commitment would fund the
1341    /// same cycle twice.
1342    ///
1343    /// Stored once phase two has staged the whole request rather than after the burst is published.
1344    /// A burst that fails to send has still moved the generator, so its re-sends must read as repeats —
1345    /// read as stale instead, each of them would be logged as a fault. Not stored any earlier, though:
1346    /// a batch that fails *during* phase two after moving the generator can never be committed, and
1347    /// that failure closes the Session rather than leaving its re-sends to be told apart. And a repeat
1348    /// is not always a no-op: while [`unpublished`](Self::unpublished) still holds members of that
1349    /// batch, the repeat is the Exit's prompt to finish publishing them, and once it has been published
1350    /// a repeat that comes too late to have crossed the bursts is the prompt to send them again.
1351    last_committed_first: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
1352    /// Members of the batch last staged whose commitment burst and `ReadyToDeposit` have not both gone
1353    /// out, with exactly the announcement that is still owed for each.
1354    ///
1355    /// Phase three sends a member's whole burst and only then announces its deposit address, and the
1356    /// transport can fail between any two messages (it gives up on a send after
1357    /// [`EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT`]). Without this record the generator has moved on and the failure is
1358    /// final: the Exit's re-sends read as repeats of a batch the Entry believes it served, and a
1359    /// scoped re-request completes the commitment it names without ever announcing the deposit, so the
1360    /// Exit holds a complete commitment for a cycle nobody was told to fund.
1361    ///
1362    /// Filled at the end of phase two for every staged member, before anything is sent. **A member is
1363    /// published by whoever removes it from here, under this mutex**, and by nobody else: phase three
1364    /// claims each member just before its burst, and the resumption that finishes an interrupted batch
1365    /// ([`resume_publication`]) claims the same way. Whoever holds the claim announces the deposit once
1366    /// its whole burst is out, so the announcement happens at most once per member however many
1367    /// resumers there are — which matters, because the scoped re-request path does not take the
1368    /// per-pseudonym request lock. A claimant that fails puts its member back, and a member that was
1369    /// never claimed was never touched.
1370    ///
1371    /// A newer batch replaces whatever is left of an older one: the Exit asks for a successor only
1372    /// after the commitment and the deposit of its predecessor, so an older member still here has been
1373    /// given up on. That, and the batch size the Entry accepts, bound the map. A claimant of an older
1374    /// batch that fails after it was replaced finds its member not wanted back (see [`OwedPublications`]).
1375    ///
1376    /// **What this recovers, and what it does not.** Only the Exit can prompt a resumption: by a repeat
1377    /// of the request, or by a scoped re-request that names an owed cycle. The Exit re-requests the
1378    /// parts of a commitment that has started to arrive and gone quiet, so a member cut part-way
1379    /// through its burst is finished by the re-request wherever its batch stands — and that resumption
1380    /// publishes every member still owed, not only the one named. A member with *no message of it out*
1381    /// has nothing to re-request, and only a repeat can reach it. The Exit repeats a successor batch,
1382    /// whole, for as long as any member of it has reported nothing, **but only while the batch is behind
1383    /// the front**: a batch at the front is never re-sent (a successor admitted just before the front
1384    /// moved joins it). The opening batch is the exception, as it has no front to reach: it is repeated a
1385    /// bounded number of times, whatever the front. So, per member, nothing
1386    /// prompts a resumption in two cases, and a third is given up on:
1387    ///
1388    /// * a member with no message of it out that nothing will repeat for: any member of the opening batch once its
1389    ///   re-sends are spent, or, in a successor batch at the front, a member after a cut that lands exactly on a
1390    ///   member boundary there, when no earlier member of the batch is itself still owed (its own burst cut part-way),
1391    ///   whose re-request would resume it too. The member times out on its commitment deadline;
1392    /// * a burst that went out whole whose `ReadyToDeposit` could not be queued because the PIX event channel was
1393    ///   full. The Exit then holds a complete commitment and never asks again. The member is kept owed, in case
1394    ///   something does;
1395    /// * a cycle whose retransmissions are spent, which can never be published again. It is dropped from here with one
1396    ///   warning (see [`resume_publication`]).
1397    ///
1398    /// A member that has been published is out of the owed set, but publishing only means the local
1399    /// transport took the burst. If a relayer on the forward path dies, the whole burst can still be
1400    /// lost. The Exit then has no part it could re-request, so only a repeat reaches the member. A
1401    /// repeat that arrives more than [`SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE`] after the batch last went out has the
1402    /// whole burst of every announced member sent again, and nothing announced (see
1403    /// [`OwedPublications::announced`]). The limits are the same as for a resumption: a successor batch
1404    /// at the front is never repeated, an opening batch is repeated only as often as its cap allows, and each re-send
1405    /// spends one of the cycle's retransmissions.
1406    ///
1407    /// None of these strands a deposit, because nothing was announced for the member concerned: the
1408    /// Exit's own deadline ends the cycle. The opposite hazard exists, though. A resumed burst answers a
1409    /// re-request, and the Exit's re-request timer asks until just before the cycle's commitment
1410    /// deadline without moving it, so the resumption — or a repeat delayed on the way — can arrive after
1411    /// the Exit has retired the cycle. A re-send is a second source of the same thing: re-sends go on
1412    /// up to the deadline of a member that has reported a part, which the tick does not push, so the
1413    /// last one — sent up to one interval before the Exit retires that member — can resume and announce
1414    /// it afterwards. The Entry then announces a deposit for an address nobody can reconstruct.
1415    unpublished: parking_lot::Mutex<OwedPublications>,
1416    /// The refusal this Session last logged, as `(lowest index asked for, SsaRefusal)`, `0` for none.
1417    ///
1418    /// Only to keep the log honest. The Exit re-sends a refused request every few seconds, so the
1419    /// same refusal repeats for as long as the gate stays shut, and a line per re-send would bury the
1420    /// one that matters: the first.
1421    last_refusal: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
1422    /// What this Exit sent as deposit data, per SSA index, for cycles whose deposit address it has
1423    /// not learned yet.
1424    sent_deposit_data: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<SsaIndex, HoprPixDepositPayload>>>,
1425}
1426
1427/// The members of the batch last staged that are still owed their publication, and the ones that
1428/// have had it.
1429///
1430/// The members are what is owed; the `batch` counter is there for one reason. A member that was
1431/// claimed is out of the map while its publication is attempted, and if that attempt fails it is put
1432/// back — but not if a newer batch has been staged meanwhile, whose members have replaced the older
1433/// ones. Which batch a returning member belongs to cannot be read off its index, since a member
1434/// returning to its own batch can sit below the ones still in the map just as an old one does, so each
