1435/// staging gets a number and each claim carries it.
1436#[derive(Debug, Default)]
1437struct OwedPublications {
1438    /// Which staging the members belong to. Incremented every time a batch is staged.
1439    batch: u64,
1440    members: BTreeMap<SsaIndex, AgreedSsaQuota>,
1441    /// Members of the same batch whose publication completed: their whole burst went out and their
1442    /// `ReadyToDeposit` was queued.
1443    ///
1444    /// The only members a late repeat may have sent again
1445    /// ([`SessionSsaState::claim_republication`]). Sending the burst of a member that is owed, or
1446    /// that someone is publishing right now, would hand the Exit a complete commitment for a cycle
1447    /// nobody has yet been told to fund.
1448    announced: BTreeSet<SsaIndex>,
1449    /// When a burst of this batch last went out in full, `None` before the first.
1450    last_sent: Option<Instant>,
1451}
1452
1453/// A member taken out of [`OwedPublications`] by whoever is publishing it.
1454///
1455/// Holding one is the right to publish the member and announce its deposit. It is either spent by
1456/// completing the publication ([`SessionSsaState::complete_publication`]) or handed back to
1457/// [`SessionSsaState::restore_unpublished`].
1458#[derive(Debug)]
1459struct ClaimedPublication {
1460    /// The staging the member was claimed from.
1461    batch: u64,
1462    /// What `ReadyToDeposit` is to say once the member's burst is out.
1463    quota: AgreedSsaQuota,
1464}
1465
1466/// Why `handle_ssa_request` dropped a request without committing to it, short of refusing the Session.
1467///
1468/// Part of the key `SessionSsaState::note_refusal` deduplicates the log on, and the discriminant is
1469/// what goes into it, so the values are never `0`.
1470#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1471enum SsaRefusal {
1472    /// The batch committed up to now has not been emitted far enough for any conforming Exit to ask.
1473    Early = 1,
1474    /// Emission is far enough, but the packets that came back are fewer than the batch has earned.
1475    /// Expected on a multi-hop path, where the Entry sees the packets that survive the whole return
1476    /// path and the Exit counts the ones its first relayer acknowledged.
1477    UnderServed = 2,
1478    /// The request names indices at or below what was committed, and not the batch committed last.
1479    Stale = 3,
1480}
1481
1482impl SsaRefusal {
1483    /// Logs one refusal at the level its kind and novelty call for.
1484    ///
1485    /// An under-served request is the expected way a transient shortfall looks, so its first
1486    /// occurrence is information; an early one comes from an Exit that is not conforming, and a stale
1487    /// one from an Exit that has lost track of the Session, so theirs are warnings. Every repeat is a
1488    /// debug line — the first already said it.
1489    fn log(self, first_time: bool, session_id: &SessionId, error: &SessionManagerError) {
1490        let what = match self {
1491            Self::Early => "refused an early SSA request",
1492            Self::UnderServed => "refused an under-served SSA request",
1493            Self::Stale => "refused a stale SSA request",
1494        };
1495        match (first_time, self) {
1496            (false, _) => tracing::debug!(%session_id, %error, "{what} (repeated)"),
1497            (true, Self::UnderServed) => tracing::info!(%session_id, %error, "{what}"),
1498            (true, Self::Early | Self::Stale) => tracing::warn!(%session_id, %error, "{what}"),
1499        }
1500    }
1501}
1502
1503impl SessionSsaState {
1504    pub fn new(params: PixParams) -> Self {
1505        Self {
1506            params,
1507            committed_ssa_watermark: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0),
1508            returned_at_first_commit: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0),
1509            last_committed_first: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32::new(0),
1510            unpublished: Default::default(),
1511            last_refusal: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0),
1512            sent_deposit_data: Default::default(),
1513        }
1514    }
1515
1516    /// Files the deposit data of a batch the Exit is about to send, for
1517    /// [`take_sent_deposit_data`](Self::take_sent_deposit_data) to hand back once the matching
1518    /// deposit address is known.
1519    pub fn remember_sent_deposit_data(&self, deposit_data: &HashMap<SsaIndex, HoprPixDepositPayload>) {
1520        let mut sent = self.sent_deposit_data.lock();
1521        for (&ssa_index, payload) in deposit_data {
1522            sent.insert(ssa_index, payload.clone());
1523        }
1524    }
1525
1526    /// Removes and returns what this Exit sent for `ssa_index`, or empty data if it sent none.
1527    pub fn take_sent_deposit_data(&self, session_id: &SessionId, ssa_index: SsaIndex) -> PixDepositData {
1528        PixDepositData {
1529            id: PixAddressId::new(session_id, ssa_index),
1530            data: self
1531                .sent_deposit_data
1532                .lock()
1533                .remove(&ssa_index)
1534                .map(|payload| payload.0)
1535                .unwrap_or_default(),
1536        }
1537    }
1538
1539    /// Highest SSA index committed for this Session, `None` before the first batch.
1540    #[inline]
1541    pub fn committed_watermark(&self) -> Option<SsaIndex> {
1542        SsaIndex::new(self.committed_ssa_watermark.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
1543    }
1544
1545    /// Raises the committed-index watermark to `index` if it is higher, taking the returned-packet
1546    /// baseline on the first commitment.
1547    ///
1548    /// `fetch_max` rather than a store: the gate serialises requests per pseudonym, but a Session's
1549    /// slot is shared and monotonicity here must not depend on that lock staying where it is. Its
1550    /// *previous* value is also what makes the baseline race-free without leaning on that lock —
1551    /// exactly one caller can observe a prior watermark of zero, so exactly one stores.
1552    #[inline]
1553    pub fn note_committed(&self, index: SsaIndex, returned_packets: u64) {
1554        if self.committed_ssa_watermark.fetch_max(index.get(), Ordering::Relaxed) == 0 {
1555            self.returned_at_first_commit.store(returned_packets, Ordering::Relaxed);
1556        }
1557    }
1558
1559    /// Lowest index of the request last committed to, `None` before the first.
1560    #[inline]
1561    pub fn last_committed_first(&self) -> Option<SsaIndex> {
1562        SsaIndex::new(self.last_committed_first.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
1563    }
1564
1565    /// Records `index` as the lowest index of the request just committed to.
1566    ///
1567    /// A plain store: requests are serialised per pseudonym by the request lock, so there is no
1568    /// concurrent writer to order against, unlike the watermark's `fetch_max`.
1569    #[inline]
1570    pub fn note_committed_first(&self, index: SsaIndex) {
1571        self.last_committed_first.store(index.get(), Ordering::Relaxed);
1572    }
1573
1574    /// Records `members` as staged and not yet published, replacing whatever an older batch left.
1575    ///
1576    /// Called once phase two has staged the whole request and before phase three sends anything, so
1577    /// that a failure at any point of publication finds the whole batch still owed.
1578    pub fn stage_unpublished(&self, members: impl IntoIterator<Item = AgreedSsaQuota>) {
1579        let mut unpublished = self.unpublished.lock();
1580        unpublished.batch += 1;
1581        unpublished.members = members
1582            .into_iter()
1583            .map(|quota| (quota.ssa_id.ssa_index(), quota))
1584            .collect();
1585        unpublished.announced.clear();
1586        unpublished.last_sent = None;
1587    }
1588
1589    /// Takes the right to publish `index`, or `None` if nothing is owed for it or someone else holds it.
1590    ///
1591    /// The caller owns the announcement from here: it must either complete the publication or hand the
1592    /// member back through [`restore_unpublished`](Self::restore_unpublished).
1593    pub fn claim_unpublished(&self, index: SsaIndex) -> Option<ClaimedPublication> {
1594        let mut unpublished = self.unpublished.lock();
1595        let batch = unpublished.batch;
1596        unpublished
1597            .members
1598            .remove(&index)
1599            .map(|quota| ClaimedPublication { batch, quota })
1600    }
1601
1602    /// Hands back a claimed member whose publication did not complete, so that it is owed again.
1603    ///
1604    /// Dropped instead when a newer batch has been staged since the claim, which has replaced the one
1605    /// this member belonged to; there is nothing left for it to be owed to.
1606    pub fn restore_unpublished(&self, claim: ClaimedPublication) {
1607        let mut unpublished = self.unpublished.lock();
1608        if claim.batch == unpublished.batch {
1609            unpublished.members.insert(claim.quota.ssa_id.ssa_index(), claim.quota);
1610        }
1611    }
1612
1613    /// Spends a claim whose publication completed at `now`: the member's whole burst is out and its
1614    /// `ReadyToDeposit` queued.
1615    ///
1616    /// Recorded only while the claim's batch is the current one. A newer batch has replaced it
1617    /// otherwise, and the Exit no longer repeats the request this member belonged to.
1618    pub fn complete_publication(&self, claim: ClaimedPublication, now: Instant) {
1619        let mut unpublished = self.unpublished.lock();
1620        if claim.batch == unpublished.batch {
1621            unpublished.announced.insert(claim.quota.ssa_id.ssa_index());
1622            unpublished.last_sent = Some(now);
1623        }
1624    }
1625
1626    /// The announced members whose bursts a repeat arriving at `now` should have sent again, or
1627    /// nothing if the batch last went out less than `grace` ago.
1628    ///
1629    /// When it returns members, the batch counts as sent at `now`. The repeats that follow therefore
1630    /// wait out a whole `grace` again, and so do the ones that were already on their way. Whether
1631    /// the re-send then gets out does not matter: one that fails is retried no sooner than one that
1632    /// succeeded, which keeps a congested transport from being handed a burst on every repeat.
1633    pub fn claim_republication(&self, now: Instant, grace: Duration) -> Vec<SsaIndex> {
1634        let mut unpublished = self.unpublished.lock();
1635        let recently_sent = unpublished
1636            .last_sent
1637            .is_some_and(|sent| now.saturating_duration_since(sent) < grace);
1638        if recently_sent || unpublished.announced.is_empty() {
1639            return Vec::new();
1640        }
1641        unpublished.last_sent = Some(now);
1642        unpublished.announced.iter().copied().collect()
1643    }
1644
1645    /// Stops counting `index` as announced once the generator will not rebuild its burst, so later
1646    /// repeats do not ask for it again.
1647    pub fn forget_announced(&self, index: SsaIndex) {
1648        self.unpublished.lock().announced.remove(&index);
1649    }
1650
1651    /// Indices still owed a publication, ascending.
1652    pub fn unpublished_indices(&self) -> Vec<SsaIndex> {
1653        self.unpublished.lock().members.keys().copied().collect()
1654    }
1655
1656    /// Records a refusal, returning whether it differs from the one recorded before it.
1657    ///
1658    /// `first` is the lowest index the request asked for. A refusal repeated for the same index and
1659    /// the same reason returns `false`, so only its first occurrence is logged loudly.
1660    pub fn note_refusal(&self, first: Option<SsaIndex>, refusal: SsaRefusal) -> bool {
1661        let key = (u64::from(first.map_or(0, SsaIndex::get)) << 8) | refusal as u64;
1662        self.last_refusal.swap(key, Ordering::Relaxed) != key
1663    }
1664
1665    /// Exit → Entry packets received since this Session's first commitment.
1666    ///
1667    /// Saturating rather than wrapping: `returned_packets` is monotonic and the baseline is a past
1668    /// value of it, so an underflow is impossible — and if one ever became possible, reporting zero
1669    /// service closes the successor gate rather than opening it.
1670    #[inline]
1671    pub fn served_since_first_commit(&self, returned_packets: u64) -> u64 {
1672        returned_packets.saturating_sub(self.returned_at_first_commit.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
1673    }
1674
1675    /// Data quota one SSA cycle of these dimensions covers.
1676    ///
1677    /// The whole cycle, surplus included, as per [`pix_params_to_quota`]: every share a cycle emits
1678    /// rides one Exit → Entry packet, so all of them are priced.
1679    #[inline]
1680    pub const fn quota_per_ssa(&self) -> SsaQuota {
1681        pix_params_to_quota(&self.params)
1682    }
1683}
1684
1685/// How long an Entry keeps the PIX accounting of a pseudonym after its last Session ended.
1686///
1687/// Counted from the teardown of the Session (a live Session carries its ledger itself), and equal to
1688/// the idle retention of the share generator's per-pseudonym state (`SsaShareGenerator`, 1800 s): the
1689/// ledger and that state are two halves of one fact, the commitments made and the service they were
1690/// measured against, and one outliving the other is a mismatch the Entry has to repair.
1691const PIX_LEDGER_IDLE_RETENTION: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1800);
1692
1693/// How many ledgers the cache holds per permitted Session. A ledger outlives its Session by
1694/// [`PIX_LEDGER_IDLE_RETENTION`] and is a few words, so the bound only has to stop a churn of
1695/// pseudonyms from growing the cache without limit.
1696const PIX_LEDGER_CAPACITY_FACTOR: u64 = 8;
1697
1698/// The Entry-side PIX accounting of one pseudonym, shared by every Session this process opens under it.
1699///
1700/// Holds exactly the `Arc`s an Entry slot carries, so a slot keeps its field types and the Exit side
1701/// is untouched. Kept in [`SessionManager::pix_ledgers`] so that a Session reconnecting under the same
1702/// pseudonym continues the accounting where its predecessor left off, instead of starting from a
1703/// fresh watermark against a generator that remembers.
1704#[derive(Clone)]
1705struct EntryPixLedger {
1706    ssa_state: Arc<OnceLock<SessionSsaState>>,
1707    returned_packets: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
1708}
1709
1710impl EntryPixLedger {
1711    fn new(params: PixParams) -> Self {
1712        let ssa_state = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
1713        let _ = ssa_state.set(SessionSsaState::new(params));
1714        Self {
1715            ssa_state,
1716            returned_packets: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),
1717        }
1718    }
1719
1720    fn params(&self) -> Option<PixParams> {
1721        self.ssa_state.get().map(|state| state.params)
1722    }
1723
1724    /// Whether the ledger remembers a committed cycle.
1725    fn has_watermark(&self) -> bool {
1726        self.ssa_state
1727            .get()
1728            .is_some_and(|state| state.committed_watermark().is_some())
1729    }
1730}
1731
1732/// The retention cache of ledgers no live Session holds.
1733type PixLedgerCache = moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, EntryPixLedger>;
1734
1735/// Where an Entry slot's ledger goes at teardown.
1736///
1737/// The slot carries its ledger for its whole lifetime, so a live Session's accounting cannot expire; only
1738/// when the slot is torn down is the ledger put into the [`PixLedgerCache`], and its retention starts
1739/// there.
1740struct LedgerHome {
1741    ledger: EntryPixLedger,
1742    cache: PixLedgerCache,
1743}
1744
1745/// The retention cache of the highest challenge this node used per pseudonym.
1746type LastChallengeCache = moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, StartChallenge>;
1747
1748/// Where an Entry slot's challenge goes at teardown; the counterpart of [`LedgerHome`].
1749///
1750/// The challenge a live Session was established by must not expire while it is live: reusing its
1751/// pseudonym needs a greater one, and a lower one is refused by an Exit that still holds the Session. So the
1752/// slot carries it, and only at teardown is it put into the [`LastChallengeCache`], starting its retention.
1753struct ChallengeHome {
1754    cache: LastChallengeCache,
1755}
1756
1757/// Records `challenge` as the highest used under `pseudonym`, keeping the larger of it and any record already
1758/// in `cache`.
1759fn note_challenge_in(cache: &LastChallengeCache, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, challenge: StartChallenge) {
1760    cache.entry(pseudonym).and_compute_with(
1761        |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, StartChallenge>>| match entry {
1762            Some(entry) if *entry.value() >= challenge => moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop,
1763            _ => moka::ops::compute::Op::Put(challenge),
1764        },
1765    );
1766}
1767
1768/// A ledger `new_session` has taken for an initiation that has not produced a slot yet.
1769///
1770/// Parks the ledger again when dropped, so that a failed initiation leaves the ledger where a retry
1771/// finds it. Defused once a slot carries the ledger: its teardown parks it from then on.
1772struct LedgerClaim {
1773    ledger: EntryPixLedger,
1774    cache: PixLedgerCache,
1775    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
1776    armed: bool,
1777}
1778
1779impl LedgerClaim {
1780    fn defuse(&mut self) {
1781        self.armed = false;
1782    }
1783}
1784
1785impl Drop for LedgerClaim {
1786    fn drop(&mut self) {
1787        if self.armed {
1788            self.cache.insert(self.pseudonym, self.ledger.clone());
1789        }
1790    }
1791}
1792
1793/// The identity of one *establishment* of a Session slot.
1794///
1795/// A pseudonym ([`SessionId`]) is client-chosen and reusable, so a successor Session can take the key
1796/// of a predecessor whose `HoprSession`, notifier closures, driver tasks or telemetry are still alive.
1797/// Everything that can outlive a slot's data plane therefore carries the `Arc<SlotInstance>` of the
1798/// slot it belongs to, and acts only while the cached slot for its pseudonym still *is* that instance
1799/// (by `Arc::ptr_eq`). Keying a close by [`SessionId`] alone lets a stale object tear down, or drain,
1800/// its successor.
1801///
1802/// Deliberately distinct from the slot's *control plane* (the PIX supervisor handle, see
1803/// [`PixControlPlane`]): a later takeover may swap the data plane under a new instance while the
1804/// control plane carries on.
1805pub(crate) struct SlotInstance {
1806    /// Unique within the process; also what a public handle (the `HoprSession`) carries to name it.
1807    id: u64,
1808    /// The `StartSession` challenge that established this slot. On the Exit it is the Entry's, on the
1809    /// Entry the one `new_session` reserved.
1810    challenge: StartChallenge,
1811    /// Set by [`SessionSlotGuard::commit`]: the Session got as far as being established.
1812    established: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
1813    /// Set once the slot's data plane is gone or replaced. A writer still holding the Session's sink
1814    /// must not send through it any more.
1815    superseded: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
1816    /// When this instance was created; the origin of `last_refresh_ms`.
1817    created: std::time::Instant,
1818    /// Milliseconds after `created` at which an Entry write last refreshed the slot's idle timer.
1819    last_refresh_ms: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
1820    /// Where an Entry slot's PIX ledger goes when the slot is torn down, see [`LedgerHome`].
1821    ledger_home: OnceLock<LedgerHome>,
1822    /// Set by the first [`park_records`](Self::park_records): what the slot parks leaves it once.
1823    parked: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
1824    /// The reason the Exit gave for closing this Session, during its setup or after it.
1825    ///
1826    /// Shared with the [`HoprSession`] built for this instance, which reads it once the Session is in the
1827    /// app's hands, see [`HoprSession::refusal`].
1828    refusal: Arc<OnceLock<StartErrorReason>>,
1829    /// Where an Entry slot's challenge goes when the slot is torn down, see [`ChallengeHome`].
1830    challenge_home: OnceLock<ChallengeHome>,
1831    /// Whether the Entry that established this instance announced `Capability::Resumable` (Exit only).
1832    ///
1833    /// Decides how the Exit addresses a post-establishment `SessionError` to it: by this instance's challenge
1834    /// for a resumable Entry, which closes exactly this instance, by the Session ID for an older one.
1835    resume_capable: bool,
1836    /// The progress of the stream of this instance's data plane (Exit only), see
1837    /// [`HoprSession::stream_progress`]. Set when the plane is built; empty for a raw Session.
1838    stream_progress: OnceLock<StreamProgress>,
1839    /// Why the Session object built for this instance ended, if it has.
1840    ///
1841    /// Set by the instance's closure notifier before it reports, so that an end which happens before the
1842    /// instance is the slot's current one (a takeover delivers the new Session to the session server before
1843    /// it swaps the slot) is not lost: the report is dropped as stale, the mark is not.
1844    ended: OnceLock<ClosureReason>,
1845    /// The sink to tell when this Entry instance ends, if it asked for forward receipts.
1846    receipts: OnceLock<Arc<dyn ForwardReceiptSink>>,
1847    /// Set by the first [`park_records`](Self::park_records), which also tells the `receipts` sink.
1848    receipts_ended: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
1849}
1850
1851impl SlotInstance {
1852    fn new(challenge: StartChallenge) -> Arc<Self> {
1853        Self::new_with(challenge, false)
1854    }
1855
1856    /// A new instance established by a request with `challenge`, whose sender is resumable or not.
1857    fn new_with(challenge: StartChallenge, resume_capable: bool) -> Arc<Self> {
1858        static NEXT_INSTANCE_ID: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64 = std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(1);
1859        Arc::new(Self {
1860            id: NEXT_INSTANCE_ID.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
1861            challenge,
1862            established: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1863            superseded: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1864            created: std::time::Instant::now(),
1865            last_refresh_ms: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0),
1866            ledger_home: OnceLock::new(),
1867            parked: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1868            refusal: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
1869            challenge_home: OnceLock::new(),
1870            resume_capable,
1871            stream_progress: OnceLock::new(),
1872            ended: OnceLock::new(),
1873            receipts: OnceLock::new(),
1874            receipts_ended: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
1875        })
1876    }
1877
1878    /// Records the Exit's reason for closing this Session, so a setup still in progress fails with it.
1879    fn refuse(&self, reason: StartErrorReason) {
1880        let _ = self.refusal.set(reason);
1881    }
1882
1883    /// The Exit's reason for closing this Session, during its setup or after it, if it gave one.
1884    fn refusal(&self) -> Option<StartErrorReason> {
1885        self.refusal.get().copied()
1886    }
1887
1888    /// The error a setup in progress fails with: the Exit's refusal, or `Closed` if this instance was
1889    /// replaced or torn down meanwhile. The refusal wins when both are set, as it also supersedes the instance.
1890    ///
1891    /// Supersession is read first. A refusal is recorded before the close that supersedes the instance, and
1892    /// the `Acquire` load here pairs with the `Release` store in [`supersede`](Self::supersede), so a setup
1893    /// that sees the instance superseded also sees the refusal. Read the other way round, a close landing
1894    /// between the two reads would turn the Exit's reason into `Closed`.
1895    fn setup_failure(&self) -> Option<TransportSessionError> {
1896        let superseded = self.is_superseded();
1897        if let Some(reason) = self.refusal() {
1898            return Some(TransportSessionError::Rejected(reason));
1899        }
1900        superseded.then_some(TransportSessionError::Closed)
1901    }
1902
1903    /// Counts an Entry data write as activity: reads the slot (which resets its `time_to_idle`), at
1904    /// most once per `period`. With `period = idle_timeout / 4`, an Entry that stops writing can
1905    /// expire as early as ¾ of the idle timeout after its last write. Call only after the `is_superseded` check:
1906    /// removal supersedes inside the compute, so a successor under the same pseudonym exists only once this
1907    /// instance is superseded.
1908    fn touch_slot_on_write(
1909        &self,
1910        sessions: &moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
1911        id: &SessionId,
1912        period: Duration,
1913    ) {
1914        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
1915        let now = self.created.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
1916        let last = self.last_refresh_ms.load(Relaxed);
1917        if now.saturating_sub(last) >= period.as_millis() as u64
1918            && self
1919                .last_refresh_ms
1920                .compare_exchange(last, now, Relaxed, Relaxed)
1921                .is_ok()
1922        {
1923            let _ = sessions.get(id);
1924        }
1925    }
1926
1927    /// Binds this Entry slot instance's challenge to `cache`, where it is recorded when the slot is torn down.
1928    fn attach_challenge_home(&self, cache: LastChallengeCache) {
1929        let _ = self.challenge_home.set(ChallengeHome { cache });
1930    }
1931
1932    /// Whether the Entry announced `Capability::Resumable` when it established this instance.
1933    fn is_resume_capable(&self) -> bool {
1934        self.resume_capable
1935    }
1936
1937    /// Marks the Session object of this instance as ended, with the first reason given.
1938    fn mark_ended(&self, reason: ClosureReason) {
1939        let _ = self.ended.set(reason);
1940    }
1941
1942    /// Why the Session object of this instance ended, if it has.
1943    fn ended_with(&self) -> Option<ClosureReason> {
1944        self.ended.get().copied()
1945    }
1946
1947    /// Binds the Entry's PIX ledger to this slot instance, to be parked in `cache` when the slot is torn down.
1948    fn attach_ledger(&self, ledger: EntryPixLedger, cache: PixLedgerCache) {
1949        let _ = self.ledger_home.set(LedgerHome { ledger, cache });
1950    }
1951
1952    /// The PIX ledger this slot carries, if it is an Entry slot with one.
1953    fn ledger(&self) -> Option<EntryPixLedger> {
1954        self.ledger_home.get().map(|home| home.ledger.clone())
1955    }
1956
1957    /// Parks what a reconnect under `pseudonym` continues from in the retention caches, starting their
1958    /// retention now: the slot's PIX ledger, and its challenge as the last one used under the pseudonym.
1959    /// Either is skipped for a slot without a home for it (an Exit slot has neither).
1960    ///
1961    /// Called by every teardown of the slot. While a Session is live nothing reads the parked records, and
1962    /// they would not reliably survive a long Session in the caches, which is why they go there only now.
1963    ///
1964    /// Parks **once per instance**: [`remove_slot_if`] parks inside the removal itself, so that no reader
1965    /// can find the slot gone and its records not yet parked, and the later call from
1966    /// [`release_session_slot`] must not put back a ledger a successor has meanwhile claimed (a live Session
1967    /// holds its ledger alone). A slot removed some other way (the cache's own eviction) is parked by that
1968    /// later call, the first one it sees.
1969    fn park_records(&self, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym) {
1970        if self.parked.swap(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::AcqRel) {
1971            return;
1972        }
1973        // Every teardown path parks, so this is where the Session's receipt recording ends. The sink ends only this
1974        // instance's registration: a successor under the pseudonym keeps its own.
1975        if let Some(sink) = self.receipts.get()
1976            && !self.receipts_ended.swap(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::AcqRel)
1977        {
1978            sink.session_ended(pseudonym, self.id);
1979        }
1980        if let Some(home) = self.ledger_home.get() {
1981            home.cache.insert(pseudonym, home.ledger.clone());
1982        }
1983        if let Some(home) = self.challenge_home.get() {
1984            note_challenge_in(&home.cache, pseudonym, self.challenge);
1985        }
1986    }
1987
1988    pub(crate) fn id(&self) -> u64 {
1989        self.id
1990    }
1991
1992    fn mark_established(&self) {
1993        self.established.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
1994    }
1995
1996    fn is_established(&self) -> bool {
1997        self.established.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire)
1998    }
1999
2000    /// Marks the data plane as gone. Idempotent.
2001    fn supersede(&self) {
2002        self.superseded.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
2003    }
2004
2005    fn is_superseded(&self) -> bool {
2006        self.superseded.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire)
2007    }
2008}

2010impl std::fmt::Debug for SlotInstance {
2011    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
2012        f.debug_struct("SlotInstance")
2013            .field("id", &self.id)
2014            .field("challenge", &self.challenge)
2015            .field("established", &self.is_established())
2016            .field("superseded", &self.is_superseded())
2017            .finish()
2018    }
