2021/// The closure notifier an Exit `HoprSession` is constructed with.
2022type ExitClosureNotifier = Box<dyn FnOnce(SessionId, ClosureReason) + Send + Sync>;
2023
2024/// The notifier of an Exit `HoprSession`: reports its end to the closure consumer, naming the slot
2025/// `instance` it was built for, so that the report is acted on only while that instance is current.
2026fn exit_closure_notifier(
2027    close_session_notifier: crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<(SessionId, ClosureReason, Arc<SlotInstance>)>>,
2028    instance: Arc<SlotInstance>,
2029) -> ExitClosureNotifier {
2030    Box::new(move |session_id: SessionId, reason: ClosureReason| {
2031        // Before the report, which a closure consumer drops while the instance is not the slot's current one.
2032        instance.mark_ended(reason);
2033        if let Err(error) = close_session_notifier.try_send((session_id, reason, instance)) {
2034            error!(%session_id, %error, %reason, "failed to notify session closure");
2035        }
2036    })
2037}
2038
2039/// The error a write gets once the slot it belongs to has been torn down or replaced.
2040fn superseded_write_error() -> std::io::Error {
2041    std::io::Error::new(
2042        std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe,
2043        "the session's slot was torn down or replaced",
2044    )
2045}
2046
2047/// What identifies a Session's PIX control plane: the supervisor cell its slots share.
2048///
2049/// Every clone of a [`SessionSlot`] shares this `Arc`, so it is the same value for the slot in the
2050/// cache, in the guard and in the action driver. A driver that looks its Session up by pseudonym acts
2051/// on the slot found only if it carries this very cell, so a lingering driver of a torn-down Session
2052/// can never touch a fresh one under the same pseudonym.
2053type PixControlPlane = Arc<PixPlane>;
2054
2055/// The shared state of a [`PixControlPlane`]: the supervisor handle and whether its slot is gone.
2056#[derive(Default)]
2057pub(crate) struct PixPlane {
2058    supervisor: OnceLock<SessionPixSupervisorHandle>,
2059    /// Set when the slot is removed or evicted, never by a mere change of instance. Lets a lingering
2060    /// driver check ownership without a cache lookup, which would refresh a successor's idle timer.
2061    torn_down: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
2062}
2063
2064impl PixPlane {
2065    fn mark_torn_down(&self) {
2066        self.torn_down.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
2067    }
2068
2069    fn is_torn_down(&self) -> bool {
2070        self.torn_down.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire)
2071    }
2072}
2073
2074impl std::ops::Deref for PixPlane {
2075    type Target = OnceLock<SessionPixSupervisorHandle>;
2076
2077    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
2078        &self.supervisor
2079    }
2080}
2081
2082/// Which slot a close is allowed to act on.
2083#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
2084enum CloseScope<'a> {
2085    /// Whatever slot is current under the pseudonym: the operator's close.
2086    Any,
2087    /// Only this slot instance: a notification from the Session object that was built for it.
2088    Instance(&'a Arc<SlotInstance>),
2089    /// Only the slot instance with this id: the public handle's own close.
2090    InstanceId(u64),
2091    /// Only a slot driven by this control plane: the PIX action driver's own teardown.
2092    ControlPlane(&'a PixControlPlane),
2093    /// Only this slot instance *and only while it is detached*: the end of its resume window.
2094    ///
2095    /// Scoped by the detached instance, not by control plane, which a takeover keeps. A takeover
2096    /// replaces the instance (and aborts the timer), so a timer that fires after one finds a slot it
2097    /// does not admit, even if the successor has been detached again by then: that detach armed a
2098    /// timer of its own for its own instance.
2099    DetachedInstance(&'a Arc<SlotInstance>),
2100}
2101
2102impl CloseScope<'_> {
2103    fn admits(&self, slot: &SessionSlot) -> bool {
2104        match self {
2105            Self::Any => true,
2106            Self::Instance(instance) => Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.instance, instance),
2107            Self::InstanceId(id) => slot.instance.id() == *id,
2108            Self::ControlPlane(plane) => Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.pix_supervisor, plane),
2109            Self::DetachedInstance(instance) => Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.instance, instance) && slot.is_detached(),
2110        }
2111    }
2112}
2113
2114/// How [`begin_surb_drain`](SessionManager::begin_surb_drain)'s transition, run inside a compute on the
2115/// slot, came out.
2116enum DrainStep {
2117    /// This call made the transition: the drain is ours to carry out.
2118    Entered,
2119    /// A concurrent close made it first.
2120    Lost,
2121    /// The slot is gone, or the scope does not admit what is there.
2122    Gone,
2123    /// The slot was replaced by another instance the scope admits; the drain is evaluated afresh.
2124    Replaced,
2125}
2126
2127/// What [`try_detach`](SessionManager::try_detach)'s compute found.
2128enum DetachStep {
2129    /// This call detached the slot.
2130    Detached,
2131    /// The slot was detached already.
2132    AlreadyDetached,
2133}
2134
2135/// How one evaluation of [`begin_surb_drain`](SessionManager::begin_surb_drain) ended.
2136enum DrainAttempt {
2137    /// The close was answered: `begin_surb_drain`'s own return value.
2138    Answered(Option<bool>),
2139    /// The slot was swapped for a successor the scope admits, which has to be evaluated in its turn.
2140    Replaced,
2141}
2142
2143/// How many times a drain is evaluated afresh because its slot was swapped under it.
2144const DRAIN_REEVALUATIONS: usize = 3;
2145
2146/// How the Exit addresses a `SessionError` about the instance holding `slot`: by its challenge for an Entry that
2147/// announced `Capability::Resumable`, by the Session ID otherwise.
2148fn error_identifier_of(slot: &SessionSlot, id: &SessionId) -> ErrorIdentifier<SessionId> {
2149    if slot.instance.is_resume_capable() {
2150        ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(slot.instance.challenge)
2151    } else {
2152        ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(*id)
2153    }
2154}
2155
2156/// Removes the slot under `id` if `pred` accepts it, atomically with respect to any other compute on
2157/// the same key.
2158///
2159/// Built on the cache's compute rather than `remove`, which does not serialise with a concurrent
2160/// compute: a plain `remove` could take out a successor allocated an instant after the check.
2161///
2162/// Parks the slot's PIX ledger inside that compute, before the slot is removed. A reconnect under the same
2163/// pseudonym that no longer finds the slot therefore always finds the ledger in the retention cache; one
2164/// that still finds the slot reads the ledger from it, and its claim takes the parked copy (the same
2165/// ledger) out. Parking later, in [`release_session_slot`], left a window between the two in which the
2166/// reconnect found neither and started a fresh ledger against a generator that still remembered.
2167///
2168/// The one removal that does not go through here is the cache's own eviction, which parks in
2169/// [`release_session_slot`] from the eviction listener. A client cannot learn of such a close before that
2170/// park: the Session's channel closes when the slot is dropped and its tasks are aborted, both after it.
2171/// A reconnect that comes regardless (after an outage that let the slot idle out) does not miss it
2172/// either: [`SessionManager::new_session`] first runs the cache's pending tasks, which evict an expired
2173/// slot and run the listener synchronously, before it looks the slot up. Only a slot whose idle time
2174/// runs out within that call's own few microseconds escapes this.
2175fn remove_slot_if(
2176    sessions: &moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
2177    id: &SessionId,
2178    pred: impl FnOnce(&SessionSlot) -> bool,
2179) -> Option<SessionSlot> {
2180    match sessions
2181        .entry(*id)
2182        .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| match entry {
2183            Some(entry) if pred(entry.value()) => {
2184                // Inside the removal, so no writer or driver of this slot outlives it into a successor.
2185                entry.value().instance.supersede();
2186                entry.value().pix_supervisor.mark_torn_down();
2187                entry.value().instance.park_records(*id);
2188                moka::ops::compute::Op::Remove
2189            }
2190            _ => moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop,
2191        }) {
2192        moka::ops::compute::CompResult::Removed(entry) => Some(entry.into_value()),
2193        _ => None,
2194    }
2195}
2196
2197/// The admission-token cell a [`SessionSlot`] shares with the [`SessionSlotGuard`] that allocated it.
2198///
2199/// Behind an `Arc` for two reasons. The slot is cloned into the sessions cache and into the guard, so
2200/// the token `commit` writes through the guard has to land in the *cached* copy every teardown reads
2201/// from — the `Arc` is that one shared cell. And it lets [`commit_slot_guard`] recognise its own slot
2202/// when it re-reads the cache by key: the key is a reusable pseudonym, so the entry found there may be
2203/// a successor Session's, and comparing this cell by identity is what rejects a foreign slot.
2204type AdmissionCell = Arc<OnceLock<AdmissionToken>>;
2205
2206#[derive(Clone)]
2207pub(crate) struct SessionSlot {
2208    // Sender does not need to be in Arc, because the receiver part is always
2209    // wrapped inside DropAbortable wrapper, with abort handle added to `abort_handles`.
2210    session_tx: crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<ApplicationDataIn>>,
2211    routing_opts: DestinationRouting,
2212    // Additional tasks spawned by the Session.
2213    abort_handles: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<AbortableList<SessionHandles>>>,
2214    // Allows reconfiguring of the SURB balancer on-the-fly
2215    // Set on both Entry and Exit sides.
2216    surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
2217    // SURB flow updates happening outside of Session protocol
2218    // (e.g., due to Start protocol messages).
2219    surb_estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
2220    // Contains currently active SSA for this Session and its quota
2221    current_ssa_state: Arc<OnceLock<SessionSsaState>>,
2222    /// Handle to this Session's PIX supervisor, on the Exit side of a PIX-enabled Session.
2223    ///
2224    /// Populated before the [`HoprSession`] is constructed, so the egress adapters below observe a
2225    /// gate rather than racing its installation. Empty on the Entry side and on non-PIX Sessions —
2226    /// the Exit is authoritative for the lifecycle, so the Entry runs no supervisor.
2227    pix_supervisor: PixControlPlane,
2228    /// The egress gate every outgoing data packet of a supervised Session must pass.
2229    ///
2230    /// Held separately from `pix_supervisor` because the egress path touches it per packet and has
2231    /// no use for the rest of the handle.
2232    pix_egress_gate: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<ServiceGate>>>,
2233    /// Steers the Exit's own Exit → Entry keep-alive stream, where the Session has one.
2234    ///
2235    /// Exit-side, and populated for every PIX Session as well as for any Session with a configured
2236    /// `surb_balance_notify_period` — the two producers share one stream, so they share one handle.
2237    /// Empty on the Entry side, whose keep-alives are driven by its SURB balancer instead, and on an
2238    /// Exit Session that is neither PIX nor notifying, which originates nothing at all.
2239    ///
2240    /// A `OnceLock` for the same reason the two fields above are: the action driver that sets rates
2241    /// on it is spawned after the slot is published, so it must find the handle rather than race its
2242    /// installation.
2243    pix_fill: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<PixFillControl>>>,
2244    /// This Session's live frame loss signal, where the Exit created one for it.
2245    ///
2246    /// Exit-side, and set only for a Session that can report at the degraded period — an Exit with a
2247    /// notification period, a degraded one and frames to lose (`Capability::Segmentation`). The socket
2248    /// records into it and the keep-alive driver reads it, each through its own clone. Nothing in
2249    /// production reads this slot: it is kept so that tests can reach the very signal the driver
2250    /// watches and inject loss into it, which they cannot do through the socket.
2251    exit_loss_signal: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<FrameLossSignal>>>,
2252    /// Exit → Entry Session packets received on this Session, ever.
2253    ///
2254    /// Entry-side only; stays zero on the Exit, which is the side that *sends* them. This includes
2255    /// both Session data and Start-protocol traffic such as the Exit's SURB-level keep-alives. Each
2256    /// packet consumed one return SURB, and a SURB carries at most one PIX share which the Exit can
2257    /// only decrypt by using it — so this counts shares the Exit has unlocked, measured without
2258    /// asking it. That is what makes it usable as a deposit gate: see the successor gate in
2259    /// [`SessionManager::handle_ssa_request`].
2260    ///
2261    /// Deliberately *not* [`surb_estimator`](Self::surb_estimator)`.consumed`, which increments on
2262    /// the same event on this side today. That field is documented as an *estimate* feeding the PID
2263    /// balancer, and it is only wired when `surb_management` is enabled; this one decides whether
2264    /// money is spent and must be neither. Carrying the increment twice is the cheaper mistake: a
2265    /// receive path that forgets this counter makes the gate stricter, never laxer.
2266    ///
2267    /// Credited from exactly two places, and both of them have to stay:
2268    ///
2269    /// * the `session_rx` inspectors in `new_session`, once per Session data packet handed to the reader — one in each
2270    ///   of the balanced and unbalanced branches;
2271    /// * the Start-protocol branch of [`dispatch_message`](SessionManager::dispatch_message), which credits every
2272    ///   Start-protocol message arriving on an outgoing Session because that traffic bypasses `session_rx` entirely.
2273    ///
2274    /// The second is what makes the Exit's keep-alives count, and the gate depends on it: an Exit
2275    /// whose application has nothing to say can still complete a funded cycle by keep-alive alone, and
2276    /// if those packets earned nothing here its successor would be refused as under-served and the
2277    /// Session would die on `CommitmentTimeout` with neither side able to name the cause. It is
2278    /// credited at the dispatch level rather than inside a per-message handler on purpose — the credit
2279    /// is owed for the SURB the packet consumed, which is true whatever the message turns out to be,
2280    /// including one this build fails to parse. Adding a second increment inside
2281    /// [`handle_keep_alive`](SessionManager::handle_keep_alive) would double-count it.
2282    returned_packets: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
2283    /// This Session's share of the node's live reconstructor-cycle budget.
2284    ///
2285    /// Exit-side and PIX-only; `None` everywhere else, since nothing else holds cycle state. Behind
2286    /// an `Arc` so the budget is returned when the last clone of this slot goes: a slot is cloned
2287    /// into the Session cache and into its [`SessionSlotGuard`], so no single one of them can be
2288    /// made responsible for the release.
2289    ///
2290    /// [`close_session`] returns it explicitly, which is what makes the release simultaneous with
2291    /// the closure; the `Drop` behind the `Arc` is the backstop for anything that bypasses that
2292    /// function. Both are safe to run because the release is idempotent.
2293    cycle_budget: Option<Arc<CycleBudgetReservation>>,
2294    /// The SURB-store admission this Session's `commit` obtains, threaded to the teardown so its
2295    /// retire can be matched to the admission it belongs to.
2296    ///
2297    /// Behind an `Arc` and empty until `commit` because the guard — which performs the `admit` — and
2298    /// the slot in the sessions cache are two clones of one value: the token has to land in the
2299    /// cached copy, and `commit` runs after the slot was inserted. Every teardown reads the token
2300    /// from the slot it removes, so it travels with the Session however long the teardown is delayed;
2301    /// empty stays [`AdmissionToken::NONE`], which matches no admission, so a rolled-back Session's
2302    /// retire is the no-op the seam's idempotency is there for.
2303    ///
2304    /// The same cell is what identifies this slot to the commit that allocated it — see
2305    /// [`AdmissionCell`].
2306    admission_token: AdmissionCell,
2307    /// The largest SURB target a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive has announced for this Session, or
2308    /// `None` while none has.
2309    ///
2310    /// Kept because the Exit answers `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so the Entry's ramp can
2311    /// announce a raised target in that window: the ring is sized at `commit`, from the target
2312    /// announced at establishment, and a raise that arrived earlier would otherwise be lost until the
2313    /// Entry announced it again. The commit applies this figure too, and every later raise widens the
2314    /// ring on the spot (see [`SurbAdmissionControl::raise_target`]).
2315    raised_surb_target: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
2316    /// Tags of the Session packets received, where the Entry asked for forward receipts.
2317    ///
2318    /// Exit-side only.
2319    forward_receipts: Option<Arc<ExitReceipts>>,
2320    /// Which establishment of this pseudonym the slot is. See [`SlotInstance`].
2321    instance: Arc<SlotInstance>,
2322    /// What an Exit PIX slot keeps for a successor data plane; see [`ExitResume`].
2323    exit_resume: Arc<ExitResume>,
2324    /// The `StartSession` an Exit admitted this Session for; `None` on the Entry side.
2325    opening: Option<Arc<ExitOpening>>,
2326}
2327
2328/// What the control plane of an Exit PIX slot carries beyond the supervisor, for detaching the slot
2329/// and for a successor to take it over.
2330///
2331/// Behind an `Arc` on the slot, so every clone of the slot (the cache's, the guard's, a driver's)
2332/// sees one value, and so it survives a takeover that replaces the slot's data plane: the takeover
2333/// puts `SessionSlot { session_tx, instance, ..old }`.
2334#[derive(Default)]
2335struct ExitResume {
2336    /// Set while the slot's data plane is gone and its control plane is waiting out the resume
2337    /// window. Only ever changed inside a compute on the slot (see [`SessionManager::try_detach`] and
2338    /// the takeover), which is what serialises a detach, a takeover and a window expiry against each
2339    /// other.
2340    detached: AtomicBool,
2341    /// Whether the Entry has ever sent any part of a commitment to this Session.
2342    ///
2343    /// Together with [`ServiceGate::ever_funded`] this is what makes a Session worth keeping: an
2344    /// Entry that has answered the commitment request is mid-way through paying, and a deposit may be
2345    /// on its way to an address this Session's commitments define.
2346    entry_answered: AtomicBool,
2347    /// The terms the slot was established on, which a takeover must match. Set once, at
2348    /// establishment.
2349    terms: OnceLock<ExitTerms>,
2350}
2351
2352/// The establishment terms a takeover has to match, and the part of the data plane that is rebuilt
2353/// from the slot.
2354struct ExitTerms {
2355    /// The SSA batch size the Exit selected for this Session.
2356    ssas_per_request: usize,
2357    /// The capabilities the Entry's `StartSession` asked for.
2358    capabilities: Capabilities,
2359    /// The behaviour bits of the initiation's `additional_data` ([`INITIATION_BEHAVIOUR_BITS`]).
2360    behaviour_bits: u128,
2361    /// The egress rate limiter of a rate-controlled Session, shared with its balancer, which keeps
2362    /// steering it across a takeover. `None` for a `NoRateControl` Session.
2363    egress_rate_control: Option<RateController>,
2364}
2365
2366/// Why a held slot may not be taken over by a request, for the log; `None` from
2367/// [`SessionSlot::takeover_refusal`] means it may.
2368type TakeoverRefusal = &'static str;
2369
2370impl SessionSlot {
2371    /// Whether the slot's data plane is gone and it is awaiting its client's return.
2372    fn is_detached(&self) -> bool {
2373        self.exit_resume.detached.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire)
2374    }
2375
2376    /// Whether the Session runs on the stateless frame-based socket, the only kind that may be detached or taken
2377    /// over.
2378    ///
2379    /// Two conditions, both about the stream the successor has to be told apart from:
2380    ///
2381    /// * The Session has frames: [`Capability::Segmentation`]. A raw Session has no frame ids, so no stream base can
2382    ///   separate a successor's data from the predecessor's.
2383    /// * The socket does not retransmit: either retransmission capability selects the stateful (acknowledging) socket,
2384    ///   which cannot number its stream from a base, and whose stale acknowledgements would also credit the
2385    ///   flow-control window of a successor.
2386    ///
2387    /// A Session that is neither keeps today's behaviour: no detach, and a re-initiation is refused.
2388    fn is_stateless(&self) -> bool {
2389        self.exit_resume.terms.get().is_some_and(|terms| {
2390            terms.capabilities.contains(Capability::Segmentation)
2391                && !terms.capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionAck)
2392                && !terms.capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionNack)
2393        })
2394    }
2395
2396    /// Whether this Exit PIX Session holds something paid for, or being paid for, that a
2397    /// reconnecting client would otherwise pay for again.
2398    fn holds_paid_cycle(&self) -> bool {
2399        self.pix_egress_gate.get().is_some_and(|gate| gate.ever_funded())
2400            || self
2401                .exit_resume
2402                .entry_answered
2403                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire)
2404    }
2405
2406    /// Whether the slot's control plane is live: an established Exit PIX Session with a supervisor,
2407    /// a gate that has not been poisoned and a fill that is not draining.
2408    fn control_plane_is_live(&self) -> bool {
2409        matches!(self.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Return(_))
2410            && self.instance.is_established()
2411            && self.pix_supervisor.get().is_some()
2412            && self.pix_egress_gate.get().is_some_and(|gate| !gate.is_poisoned())
2413            && self.pix_fill.get().is_some_and(|fill| !fill.is_draining())
2414    }
2415
2416    /// Whether this slot's data plane may be set aside rather than the Session closed: a live control
2417    /// plane that holds a paid cycle, for an Entry that announced `Capability::Resumable`.
2418    fn is_detachable(&self) -> bool {
2419        self.is_stateless()
2420            && self.instance.is_resume_capable()
2421            && self.control_plane_is_live()
2422            && self.holds_paid_cycle()
2423    }
2424
2425    /// Why a request may not take this slot over, or `None` if it may.
2426    ///
2427    /// The request's challenge must be **greater** than that of the instance holding the slot, live or
2428    /// detached alike. Equal is a duplicate of the request that established it, which keeps today's
2429    /// refusal. Lower is an older attempt: `connect_to` retries `new_session` under fresh challenges
2430    /// (the Entry draws them increasing per pseudonym), so an attempt the client has abandoned can
2431    /// arrive, delayed in the mixnet, after a newer one has taken the Session over and is in use, and
2432    /// must never take it over again. The Session must run on the stateless socket (see
2433    /// [`is_stateless`](Self::is_stateless)), and the request must ask for the same terms: PIX parameters,
2434    /// capabilities, behaviour bits and, once admission has chosen it, batch size.
2435    fn takeover_refusal(
2436        &self,
2437        challenge: StartChallenge,
2438        params: &PixParams,
2439        ssas_per_request: usize,
2440        capabilities: Capabilities,
2441        additional_data: u128,
2442    ) -> Option<TakeoverRefusal> {
2443        if let Some(why) =
2444            self.takeover_refusal_before_admission(challenge, Some(params), capabilities, additional_data)
2445        {
2446            return Some(why);
2447        }
2448        match self.exit_resume.terms.get() {
2449            Some(terms) if terms.ssas_per_request == ssas_per_request => None,
2450            _ => Some("different batch size"),
2451        }
2452    }
2453
2454    /// The part of [`takeover_refusal`](Self::takeover_refusal) that needs nothing admission decides, so that it can
2455    /// run before the session server is asked. Only the batch size depends on the admission result. The PIX
2456    /// parameters are compared when the request offered any.
2457    fn takeover_refusal_before_admission(
2458        &self,
2459        challenge: StartChallenge,
2460        offered: Option<&PixParams>,
2461        capabilities: Capabilities,
2462        additional_data: u128,
2463    ) -> Option<TakeoverRefusal> {
2464        if !matches!(self.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Return(_)) {
2465            return Some("not an Exit-side session");
2466        }
2467        if !self.instance.is_established() {
2468            return Some("not established");
2469        }
2470        if self.instance.challenge == challenge {
2471            return Some("established by this very request");
2472        }
2473        if challenge < self.instance.challenge {
2474            return Some("an older attempt than the one the held session was established by");
2475        }
2476        if self.pix_supervisor.get().is_none() {
2477            return Some("not a PIX session");
2478        }
2479        if !self.is_stateless() {
2480            return Some("only a frame-based Session on the stateless socket can be taken over");
2481        }
2482        if !self.instance.is_resume_capable() {
2483            return Some("established by an Entry that did not announce Resumable");
2484        }
2485        if self.pix_fill.get().is_none_or(|fill| fill.is_draining()) {
2486            return Some("draining");
2487        }
2488        if self.pix_egress_gate.get().is_none_or(|gate| gate.is_poisoned()) {
2489            return Some("its egress gate is poisoned");
2490        }
2491        if !self.holds_paid_cycle() {
2492            return Some("nothing paid for yet");
2493        }
2494        if offered.is_some_and(|params| self.current_ssa_state.get().map(|state| state.params) != Some(*params)) {
2495            return Some("different PIX parameters");
2496        }
2497        match self.exit_resume.terms.get() {
2498            Some(terms) if terms.capabilities != capabilities => Some("different capabilities"),
2499            Some(terms) if terms.behaviour_bits != additional_data & INITIATION_BEHAVIOUR_BITS => {
2500                Some("different behaviour bits")
2501            }
2502            Some(_) => None,
2503            None => Some("established without terms"),
2504        }
2505    }
2506}
2507
2508/// The challenge an Exit slot was opened under, which marks a repeated `StartSession` as a repeat.
2509pub(crate) struct ExitOpening {
2510    challenge: StartChallenge,
2511    /// How many repeats of the opening have been answered so far.
2512    answered_repeats: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU32,
2513    /// The stream base the opening was answered with, if it was a resume attempt a takeover satisfied.
2514    resumed_stream_base: Option<u32>,
2515}
2516
2517impl SessionSlot {
2518    /// Claims the slot's admission-token cell on behalf of a teardown and returns what it holds.
2519    ///
2520    /// Empty means no `commit` has run yet, and the teardown claims the cell by storing
2521    /// [`AdmissionToken::NONE`] into it. That write is what lets a `commit` racing this teardown tell
2522    /// it lost: its own `set` then fails, and it retires the admission it just made instead of leaving
2523    /// a ring no teardown will ever remove. Without the claim, a teardown that read the empty cell
2524    /// would schedule a no-op retire, and a `commit` landing afterwards would admit a Session that is
2525    /// already gone — the leak the exit-side `SessionEstablished`-before-commit ordering makes
2526    /// reachable. Returns the token a later `commit` would have stored, or `NONE` when this teardown
2527    /// got there first (or the Session was never admitted at all).
2528    fn claim_admission_token(&self) -> AdmissionToken {
2529        *self.admission_token.get_or_init(|| AdmissionToken::NONE)
2530    }
2531
2532    /// The token this slot holds, or [`AdmissionToken::NONE`] while no `commit` has run.
2533    ///
2534    /// Read-only, unlike [`claim_admission_token`](Self::claim_admission_token): a keep-alive asking
2535    /// the store to widen this Session's ring must not *claim* the cell, or it would initialize it and
2536    /// make the establishment's own `commit` fail its `set` — retiring the live admission and leaving
2537    /// the Session's SURBs unadmitted.
2538    fn peek_admission_token(&self) -> AdmissionToken {
2539        self.admission_token.get().copied().unwrap_or(AdmissionToken::NONE)
2540    }
2541
2542    /// Records a target announced by a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive, if it is the largest so far.
2543    ///
2544    /// Monotone on purpose, matching the ring it widens: the announcement stream is a slew, and the
2545    /// last value seen is the one the Entry is filling toward. Recorded even before `commit` has
2546    /// sized the ring, which is the window the Exit's `SessionEstablished`-before-commit ordering
2547    /// opens; [`peek_raised_surb_target`](Self::peek_raised_surb_target) then lets the commit start
2548    /// from the largest figure already announced rather than from establishment's.
2549    fn note_raised_surb_target(&self, target: usize) {
2550        self.raised_surb_target
2551            .fetch_max(target, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
2552        // Pairs with the fence after `commit` records the admission token. The two sides are a
2553        // store-then-load handshake across *two* cells: this side records the target and then reads
2554        // the token, `commit` writes the token and then reads the target. With both sides `Relaxed`
2555        // and no fence, a weakly ordered CPU lets each read the other's old value — the keep-alive
2556        // sees no token (so its raise is a no-op) while `commit` sees no target (so it sizes from the
2557        // establishment figure). The balancer set-point has already moved by then, so the
2558        // `!= announced` guard in `handle_keep_alive` never retries the raise and the ring stays
2559        // undersized for the Session's life. The fence makes sure at least one side sees the other.
2560        std::sync::atomic::fence(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);
2561    }
2562
2563    /// The largest target announced since establishment, or `None` while none has been.
2564    fn peek_raised_surb_target(&self) -> Option<usize> {
2565        match self.raised_surb_target.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
2566            0 => None,
2567            target => Some(target),
2568        }
2569    }
2570}
2571
2572/// Counts the SURB a return packet will take as consumed in `estimator`, and attaches the refund that
2573/// gives it back.
2574///
2575/// The Exit counts as it hands a packet on, because its reserve and admission decisions need the count
2576/// at once. The packet can still be dropped before it takes a SURB: the PIX egress gate may never admit
2577/// it (see [`acquire_egress_permit`]), and routing resolution may find no SURB within its wait. The
2578/// refund then counts the SURB as given back in this estimator (see [`SurbRefund`]). It points at the
2579/// estimator itself, so it reaches the Session that counted the packet whatever has happened to the
2580/// Session's slot since, and it never touches the slot.
2581///
2582/// Not only Session data and keep-alives: the Exit's own Start-protocol sends on a Session
2583/// (`SessionEstablished`, the SSA requests and their re-sends, the commitment re-requests) are return
2584/// packets that take a SURB too, and are counted through [`send_counted_via_msg_sender`]. Left
2585/// uncounted they would leave the estimate showing SURBs the handshake has already spent.
2586///
2587/// The refund restores the held count the fill reserve and the drain budget read, and nothing else:
2588/// the balancer's level, which the egress rate and the level reports follow, saturates at zero and
2589/// has already absorbed a count made while it was empty (see
2590/// [`SurbFlowEstimator::estimate_surbs_refunded`]).
2591fn count_return_packet_surb(estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, mut data: ApplicationDataOut) -> ApplicationDataOut {
2592    estimator.consumed.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
2593    data.surb_refund = SurbRefund::to(estimator.refunded.clone());
2594    data
2595}
2596
2597/// What `spawn_exit_keep_alive` takes from the Entry's Session request.
2598#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
2599struct EntryAnnouncement {
2600    /// The SURB buffer target the Entry asked for; what the fill reserve is derived against (see
2601    /// [`effective_surb_reserve`]).
2602    surb_target: u64,
2603    /// The longest idle report period this Session backs off to (see [`session_idle_notify_cap`]).
2604    idle_notify_cap: Option<Duration>,
2605}
2606
2607/// The Exit's control over the single Exit → Entry keep-alive stream a Session runs.
2608///
2609/// One stream, two producers with different jobs, and this is what reconciles them:
2610///
2611/// * the **SURB-level notification**, sent every `surb_balance_notify_period`, which tells the Entry's balancer how
2612///   many SURBs the Exit believes it holds. It is the signal that asks for more, so it is exempt from the SURB reserve;
2613///   but it is a return packet like any other, so it goes out only to an Entry that has shown it refills, and only
2614///   while the Exit's estimate shows a SURB to send it on (see [`admit`](Self::admit));
2615/// * **PIX fill**, whose rate the supervisor plans once a second so that a funded cycle completes inside its own
2616///   deadline even if the application never sends a byte.
2617///
2618/// The effective rate is the faster of the two, because both are the same packet: a keep-alive
2619/// carrying the SURB level is exactly what fill needs to send, and sending two streams of them would
2620/// double the traffic to say the same thing twice. Every shipped Entry already parses it, counts it
2621/// as a consumed SURB so its balancer refills, and — since the fix that precedes this — credits it as
2622/// service against the successor gate.
2623pub(crate) struct PixFillControl {
2624    session_id: SessionId,
2625    /// The rate limiter of the keep-alive stream this steers.
2626    controller: RateController,
2627    /// The configured SURB-level notification period, if the node has one.
2628    ///
2629    /// `None` disables the notification half entirely; the stream then runs at the fill rate alone,
2630    /// which is how a PIX Session on a node with `surb_balance_notify_period: None` still fills.
2631    notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2632    /// The period to report at while the Session's forward path is degraded, if one is configured.
2633    ///
2634    /// See [`set_degraded`](Self::set_degraded). `None` leaves the notification at
2635    /// [`notify_period`](Self::notify_period) whatever happens to the forward path.
2636    degraded_notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2637    /// The longest period the notification backs off to while idle; `None` unless above `notify_period`.
2638    idle_notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2639    /// Whether application data has moved since the last SURB-level report. An atomic so the data path
2640    /// only takes the lock for the first packet after a report.
2641    data_since_report: AtomicBool,
2642    /// The `session` label of `hopr_exit_control_packets_total`.
2643    session_kind: ExitSessionKind,
2644    /// SURBs that must remain estimated-available before a *fill* packet is let through.
2645    ///
2646    /// The *effective* reserve for this Session, not the configured one: the Entry decides how deep
2647    /// the Exit's SURB buffer for the Session is, so a reserve above what the Entry ever intends to
2648    /// supply would refuse every fill packet forever. Not stored, but derived at every read from the
2649    /// target in force — see [`surb_reserve`](Self::surb_reserve) — so there is no second figure to
2650    /// keep in step with it. See [`effective_surb_reserve`].
2651    reserve_basis: SurbReserveBasis,
2652    /// The target the Entry last announced with a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive, or [`NO_ANNOUNCEMENT`]
2653    /// while it has announced none.
2654    ///
2655    /// Held here rather than on the slot because the ring's record of the announced target is
2656    /// monotone (`fetch_max`) on purpose: it only ever widens, so it cannot say that the Entry has
2657    /// announced a *lower* target since. The reserve has to follow a lower announcement, so it keeps
2658    /// the last figure as announced, and it is the only figure that changes.
2659    announced_surb_target: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64,
2660    /// Whether the order-of-magnitude lowering has already been logged for this Session.
2661    ///
2662    /// The target is peer-controlled, so without it an Entry alternating a deep and a shallow target
2663    /// sets the `warn!` cadence for the Session's whole life. Once is enough to say the Session's
2664    /// shape and the operator's intent have parted.
2665    warned_lowered_reserve: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
2666    /// The Session's SURB flow estimate, which is what the reserve is measured against.
2667    estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
2668    /// The Session's balancer state, read for whether the Entry has shown that it refills this side's
2669    /// SURBs ([`counterparty_refills`](BalancerStateValues::counterparty_refills)): the evidence that a
2670    /// SURB-level notification has a reader.
2671    surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
2672    state: parking_lot::Mutex<PixFillState>,
2673}
2674
2675struct PixFillState {
2676    /// Whether the initial notification delay has elapsed.
2677    ///
2678    /// The notification stream deliberately waits one period before starting, so a Session that
2679    /// closes immediately never sends one. Fill does not wait, and must not be held behind this.
2680    notify_started: bool,
2681    /// The rate the PIX supervisor last asked for. [`FillRate::ZERO`] when it is not filling.
2682    fill: FillRate,
2683    /// When a packet was last let through as the SURB-level notification.
2684    ///
2685    /// The two producers share a stream, so nothing about a packet says which of them it belongs to.
2686    /// This is what makes the distinction: one packet per notification period is the notification and
2687    /// is exempt from the SURB reserve, and everything above that rate is fill and is not.
2688    last_notify_at: Option<Instant>,
2689    /// Whether the SURB reserve is currently withholding fill, so `hopr_pix_sessions_stalled` counts
2690    /// this Session once per stall rather than once per refused packet.
2691    withholding: bool,
2692    /// Whether this stream is draining the SURB buffer of a Session that has already been closed.
2693    ///
2694    /// Set once, by [`PixFillControl::enter_drain`], and never cleared: a drain ends with the
2695    /// Session, and the stream with it.
2696    draining: bool,
2697    /// Whether the Session's forward path is degraded, so the notification runs faster.
2698    ///
2699    /// Set by the Exit's loss driver (see [`SessionManager::spawn_exit_keep_alive`]) and cleared the
2700    /// same way. Only meaningful with a [`degraded_notify_period`](PixFillControl::degraded_notify_period)
2701    /// configured.
2702    degraded: bool,
2703    /// Whether the degraded forward path is dark, so the notification runs at [`SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD`].
2704    ///
2705    /// Set by the same driver, and only while `degraded` is.
2706    dark: bool,
2707    /// Idle SURB reports in a row, which the backoff period is a function of. A change that alters
2708    /// [`period`](PixFillControl::period) must be followed by [`PixFillControl::apply`] under the same lock.
2709    idle_reports: u32,
2710}
2711
2712/// What one Session's fill reserve is derived from (see [`effective_surb_reserve`]).
2713///
2714/// Two figures of the one reserve, named so a call site cannot pass them swapped.
2715#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
2716struct SurbReserveBasis {
2717    /// The configured reserve, which is the ceiling the effective reserve is derived against.
2718    ///
2719    /// Kept next to the target so a later announcement is derived against the same ceiling
2720    /// establishment used, rather than against whatever is in force at the time.
2721    configured: u64,
2722    /// The target in force at establishment: the Entry's announcement, or this node's fallback when
2723    /// it announced none (a `NoRateControl` Session, or one without `surb_management`).
2724    establishment_target: u64,
2725}
2726
2727impl PixFillControl {
2728    fn new(
2729        session_id: SessionId,
2730        controller: RateController,
2731        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2732        degraded_notify_period: Option<Duration>,
2733        reserve_basis: SurbReserveBasis,
2734        estimator: AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
2735        surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
2736    ) -> Self {
2737        Self {
2738            session_id,
2739            controller,
2740            notify_period,
2741            // Normalized rather than asserted, so the invariant holds by construction: a degraded
2742            // period with no normal one would make the notification run at the degraded cadence for
2743            // the Session's whole life, which is not what "report faster while degraded" means.
2744            degraded_notify_period: degraded_notify_period.filter(|_| notify_period.is_some()),
2745            idle_notify_period: None,
2746            data_since_report: AtomicBool::new(false),
2747            session_kind: ExitSessionKind::Plain,
2748            reserve_basis,
2749            // Empty until the Entry announces a target, so the first announcement is a change
2750            // whatever it says and is treated exactly as a later one is.
2751            announced_surb_target: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(NO_ANNOUNCEMENT),
2752            warned_lowered_reserve: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
2753            estimator,
2754            surb_mgmt,
2755            state: parking_lot::Mutex::new(PixFillState {
2756                notify_started: false,
2757                fill: FillRate::ZERO,
2758                last_notify_at: None,
2759                withholding: false,
2760                draining: false,
2761                degraded: false,
2762                dark: false,
2763                idle_reports: 0,
2764            }),
2765        }
2766    }
2767
2768    /// Lets the notification back off to `cap` while idle (see [`admit`](Self::admit)).
2769    ///
2770    /// A builder, to keep [`new`](Self::new) within clippy's argument limit. A `cap` not above the normal
2771    /// period is dropped, since it would not back off at all.
2772    fn with_idle_notify_period(mut self, cap: Option<Duration>) -> Self {
2773        self.idle_notify_period = cap.filter(|cap| self.notify_period.is_some_and(|base| *cap > base));
2774        self
2775    }
2776
2777    /// Sets the `session` label of the packets this stream counts.
2778    fn for_session(mut self, session_kind: ExitSessionKind) -> Self {
2779        self.session_kind = session_kind;
2780        self
2781    }
2782
2783    /// The SURBs a fill packet must leave estimated-available in this Session.
2784    ///
2785    /// Derived at every read from the target in force, rather than kept as a figure of its own: one
2786    /// cell changes, and the reserve is whatever that cell implies, so there is no second figure to
2787    /// fall out of step with it. The cost is a `min` and a division per packet, beside an estimator
2788    /// read that is several atomic loads.
2789    ///
2790    /// Relaxed is enough throughout: the reserve is read for a heuristic, and every use either
2791    /// compares it against an estimate read the same way or is a log line. A packet that races an
2792    /// announcement gets the reserve of one of the two targets, both of which are valid for the
2793    /// Session; the next read gets the new one.
2794    fn surb_reserve(&self) -> u64 {
2795        self.reserve_for(self.announced_surb_target.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
2796    }
2797
2798    /// Records a target the Entry has just announced; the reserve follows it from the next read.
2799    ///
2800    /// The Entry chooses how deep the Exit's SURB buffer is and can change it mid-Session, so the
2801    /// reserve follows in both directions: too shallow for a raised target (fill spends the margin
2802    /// meant to be kept) and too deep for a lowered one (the estimate never reaches it, so fill is
2803    /// withheld and the cycle strands on `max_recovery_time`). See [`effective_surb_reserve`].
2804    ///
2805    /// `announced` is already clamped to `maximum_surb_buffer_size`, as the ring is sized from it. A
2806    /// repeat changes nothing and logs nothing; the warning below fires only when the reserve actually
2807    /// falls through the order-of-magnitude threshold.
2808    ///
2809    /// A `NoRateControl` Session's Entry could not influence anything here before; it drives this
2810    /// reserve now, self-inflicted on one Session — announcing four moves the reserve to one.
2811    ///
2812    /// Ignored once the Session is draining. The supervisor admits a drain once, against the
2813    /// [`drainable_surbs`](Self::drainable_surbs) reported at the close, and never re-reads it, while
2814    /// the slot (and so this keep-alive path) stays in place for the whole drain. A raise in that
2815    /// window would have fill withhold the very packets the drain was admitted to spend, stranding the
2816    /// cycle on its deadline; a lowering would spend past what the drain was planned against. The
2817    /// check and the swap happen under the state lock that [`enter_drain`](Self::enter_drain) takes,
2818    /// so an announcement either lands before the drain begins or not at all.
2819    pub(crate) fn set_announced_target(&self, announced: u64) {
2820        let previous_announced = {
2821            let state = self.state.lock();
2822            if state.draining {
2823                trace!(
2824                    session_id = %self.session_id,
2825                    announced,
2826                    reserve = self.surb_reserve(),
2827                    "ignoring a target announced during a drain: the drain keeps the reserve it was admitted against"
2828                );
2829                return;
2830            }
2831            self.announced_surb_target.swap(announced, Ordering::Relaxed)
2832        };
2833        if previous_announced == announced {
2834            return;
2835        }
2836
2837        let previous_reserve = self.reserve_for(previous_announced);
2838        let reserve = self.reserve_for(announced);
2839        trace!(
2840            session_id = %self.session_id,
2841            announced,
2842            configured = self.reserve_basis.configured,
2843            previous = previous_reserve,
2844            reserve,
2845            "the PIX fill SURB reserve follows the target the entry announced"
2846        );
2847
2848        // The same warning `spawn_exit_keep_alive` emits at establishment, applied to a target changed
2849        // afterwards: an Entry that starts deep and drops its target while the Session runs moves the
2850        // reserve by more than an order of magnitude with nothing else in the log to say so. Only on
2851        // the crossing *down*, from at or over the threshold to under it, and only once per Session: the
2852        // target is peer-controlled, so an Entry alternating 7 000 and 180 would otherwise pick the log
2853        // rate for as long as the Session lasts. A lowering that starts under the threshold crosses
2854        // nothing, so it neither warns nor spends the latch, which is set only when a warning actually
2855        // goes out: a Session that started under it, and warned at establishment, can still report a
2856        // later crossing.
2857        let under_threshold = |figure: u64| figure.saturating_mul(10) < self.reserve_basis.configured;
2858        if !under_threshold(previous_reserve)
2859            && under_threshold(reserve)
2860            && !self.warned_lowered_reserve.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed)
2861        {
2862            warn!(
2863                session_id = %self.session_id,
2864                configured = self.reserve_basis.configured,
2865                previous = previous_reserve,
2866                effective = reserve,
2867                announced,
2868                "the PIX fill SURB reserve was lowered by more than an order of magnitude to fit the SURB buffer \
2869                 target the entry announced for this session"
2870            );
2871        }
2872    }
2873
2874    /// The reserve `announced` implies here, or the establishment figure for [`NO_ANNOUNCEMENT`].
2875    fn reserve_for(&self, announced: u64) -> u64 {
2876        let target = if announced == NO_ANNOUNCEMENT {
2877            self.reserve_basis.establishment_target
2878        } else {
2879            announced
2880        };
2881        effective_surb_reserve(self.reserve_basis.configured, target)
2882    }

2884    /// The notification period the stream is running at, normal or degraded.
2885    ///
2886    /// Degraded only while the Session's forward path is degraded *and* a degraded period is
2887    /// configured: `None` there means the operator wants one cadence whatever the path is doing.
2888    fn period(&self, state: &PixFillState) -> Option<Duration> {
2889        if state.degraded {
2890            // `PixFillControl::new` only keeps a degraded period alongside a normal one, so this
2891            // shortens the cadence the Session would have had rather than giving it one.
2892            match self.degraded_notify_period {
2893                // Dark is a degraded forward path at its worst; with no degraded period configured
2894                // there is no faster cadence to have.
2895                Some(degraded) if state.dark => Some(degraded.min(SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD)),
2896                degraded => degraded.or(self.notify_period),
2897            }
2898        } else {
2899            match (self.notify_period, self.idle_notify_period) {
2900                // Only while fill is zero; any fill rate keeps the base period.
2901                (Some(base), Some(cap)) if state.fill.is_zero() => {
2902                    Some(backed_off_notify_period(base, cap, state.idle_reports))
2903                }
2904                (base, _) => base,
2905            }
2906        }
2907    }
2908
2909    /// Enters or leaves the degraded notification period, and re-applies the rate if that changed it.
2910    ///
2911    /// The driver that calls this lives in [`SessionManager::spawn_exit_keep_alive`] and owns the
2912    /// decision of when the forward path is degraded (a recent frame loss at the Exit, a reader on the
2913    /// Entry, and a SURB stock above the keep-alive reserve). What is here is only the consequence:
2914    /// the notification half of the stream reports at the degraded period instead of the normal one.
2915    ///
2916    /// Entering degraded mode after the last notification is already older than the degraded period
2917    /// makes the next released packet the notification at once, because
2918    /// [`admit_at`](Self::admit_at) measures the gap against the period in force rather than against
2919    /// the one that was in force when the last report went out. That is what turns a 15 s cadence into
2920    /// a 1 s one within the rate limiter's re-read interval, rather than a period later.
2921    ///
2922    /// PIX fill is unaffected either way: it is classified and admitted exactly as before, and the
2923    /// notification keeps its exemption from the SURB reserve.
2924    pub(crate) fn set_degraded(&self, on: bool) {
2925        let mut state = self.state.lock();
2926        if state.degraded == on {
2927            return;
2928        }
2929        state.degraded = on;
2930        // A Session in trouble is not idle. Reset before `apply`.
2931        state.idle_reports = 0;
2932        self.apply(&state);
2933    }
2934
2935    /// Marks the degraded forward path as dark or not, and re-applies the rate if that changed it.
2936    ///
2937    /// Dark takes effect only while the stream is degraded (see [`period`](Self::period)): the notification
2938    /// then runs at [`SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD`] rather than the degraded period. As with
2939    /// [`set_degraded`](Self::set_degraded), the gap since the last notification is measured against the
2940    /// period in force, so turning dark releases the next notification at once if it is overdue at the new
2941    /// cadence.
2942    pub(crate) fn set_dark(&self, on: bool) {
2943        let mut state = self.state.lock();
2944        if state.dark == on {
2945            return;
2946        }
2947        state.dark = on;
2948        self.apply(&state);
2949    }

2954        self.state.lock().degraded

2987    /// Turns the SURB-level notification on, after its initial delay.
2988    ///
2989    /// A no-op once the Session is draining, for the reason [`enter_drain`](Self::enter_drain)
2990    /// gives — and it has to be checked here rather than only there, because the one-shot delay task
2991    /// holds a clone of this control and nothing bounds how long an operator may make its period.
2992    pub(crate) fn start_notify(&self) {
2993        let mut state = self.state.lock();
2994        if state.draining {
2995            return;
2996        }
2997        state.notify_started = true;
2998        self.apply(&state);
2999    }
3000
3001    /// Puts the stream into post-close drain mode, silencing the SURB-level notification.
3002    ///
3003    /// Returns `false` if the stream was draining already, which is how two closes racing through
3004    /// `begin_surb_drain` settle which of them owns the drain. The read and the write have to be one
3005    /// lock acquisition for that: callers that each saw [`is_draining`](Self::is_draining) before
3006    /// either wrote it would both start a drain, and both tell the supervisor about it.
3007    ///
3008    /// The notification is the single packet [`admit_at`](Self::admit_at) exempts from the SURB
3009    /// reserve, and the exemption exists for one reason: it is the message that asks the Entry for
3010    /// more SURBs. It asks on behalf of a Session that a drain has already lost — the Entry itself
3011    /// may well still be there, but nothing is left to act on the request — so leaving it on would
3012    /// originate below the reserve into a buffer nothing is refilling, which is the one failure mode
3013    /// [`PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve`](crate::supervision::PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve)
3014    /// exists to prevent, since a return packet with no SURB holds up every packet this node
3015    /// originates. With it off, `notification_due` is always false and the reserve is the only gate.
3016    pub(crate) fn enter_drain(&self) -> bool {
3017        let mut state = self.state.lock();
3018        if state.draining {
3019            return false;
3020        }
3021        state.draining = true;
3022        state.notify_started = false;
3023        self.apply(&state);
3024        true
3025    }
3026
3027    /// Whether this Session is draining its SURB buffer after having been closed.
3028    pub(crate) fn is_draining(&self) -> bool {
3029        self.state.lock().draining
3030    }
3031
3032    /// The SURBs this Session could still spend on a drain, net of the reserve it must leave behind.
3033    ///
3034    /// An estimate and an upper bound at that — ring-buffer overwrites, store eviction and
3035    /// invalidated relayers are all unobserved — which is why the supervisor weighs it against a
3036    /// cycle's whole remaining emission rather than a discounted one. The reserve subtracted is the
3037    /// *effective* one in force for this Session, not the configured ceiling, and it follows the
3038    /// target the Entry last announced until the Session starts draining, after which it is frozen.
3039    pub(crate) fn drainable_surbs(&self) -> u64 {
3040        self.estimator.saturating_diff().saturating_sub(self.surb_reserve())
3041    }
3042
3043    /// Applies a rate planned by the PIX supervisor.
3044    pub(crate) fn set_fill(&self, rate: FillRate) {
3045        let mut state = self.state.lock();
3046        if state.fill == rate {
3047            return;
3048        }
3049        // The idle count restarts whenever fill crosses zero.
3050        if state.fill.is_zero() != rate.is_zero() {
3051            state.idle_reports = 0;
3052        }
3053        state.fill = rate;
3054        self.apply(&state);
3055    }

3057    /// Notes that application data moved, in either direction, and resets the idle backoff at once.
3058    ///
3059    /// Promptly, not at the next report, so a Session that turns busy does not wait out a backed-off period.
3060    /// Cheap on the hot path: after the first packet since a report it is one relaxed load.
3061    pub(crate) fn note_data_activity(&self) {
3062        if self.data_since_report.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
3063            return;
3064        }
3065        let mut state = self.state.lock();
3066        // Under the lock, to order against `note_report`'s swap.
3067        self.data_since_report.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
3068        self.reset_idle_reports(&mut state, "application data moved");
3069    }
3070
3071    /// Restarts the idle count and re-applies the rate if that shortened the period, which releases an
3072    /// overdue report at once (see [`admit`](Self::admit)).
3073    fn reset_idle_reports(&self, state: &mut PixFillState, why: &'static str) {
3074        if state.idle_reports == 0 {
3075            return;
3076        }
3077        let before = self.period(state);
3078        state.idle_reports = 0;
3079        if self.period(state) != before {
3080            debug!(
3081                session_id = %self.session_id,
3082                why,
3083                period = ?self.period(state),
3084                "reset the exit SURB-level notification to its base period"
3085            );
3086            self.apply(state);
3087        }
3088    }
3089
3090    /// Whether the SURB stock leaves room for an idle report: above the keep-alive reserve after the report,
3091    /// which spends one SURB itself.
3092    fn report_leaves_stock_above_reserve(&self) -> bool {
3093        self.estimator.saturating_diff() > current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&self.surb_mgmt).saturating_add(1)
3094    }
3095
3096    /// Ends the idle backoff if the stock no longer allows it.
3097    ///
3098    /// The stock is otherwise only checked when a report is admitted. Called when SURBs are evicted (a new SURB
3099    /// generation wipes the stock) and when an announced target changes the reserve, so the Entry does not wait out
3100    /// a backed-off period while the Exit runs low.
3101    pub(crate) fn recheck_reserve(&self) {
3102        let mut state = self.state.lock();
3103        if state.idle_reports > 0 && !self.report_leaves_stock_above_reserve() {
3104            self.reset_idle_reports(&mut state, "SURB stock at the keep-alive reserve");
3105        }
3106    }
3107
3108    /// Books an admitted report against the idle count, and re-applies the rate if the period changed.
3109    ///
3110    /// Idle means nothing moved since the last report; see the rules on [`admit`](Self::admit).
3111    fn note_report(&self, state: &mut PixFillState) {
3112        let moved = self.data_since_report.swap(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
3113        let idle = !moved && state.fill.is_zero() && !state.degraded && self.report_leaves_stock_above_reserve();
3114
3115        let before = self.period(state);
3116        state.idle_reports = if idle { state.idle_reports.saturating_add(1) } else { 0 };
3117        let after = self.period(state);
3118        if after != before {
3119            debug!(
3120                session_id = %self.session_id,
3121                idle_reports = state.idle_reports,
3122                period = ?after,
3123                "changed the exit SURB-level notification period"
3124            );
3125            // Same lock as the count change, so the rate never disagrees with `period()`.
3126            self.apply(state);
3127        }
3128    }
3129
3130    /// The rate the stream is currently running at — the faster of the two producers.
3131    ///
3132    /// The production path never asks: [`apply`](Self::apply) derives it and hands it straight to the
3133    /// controller, which is the only consumer that matters. This exists so the merge rule can be
3134    /// tested as the rule it is, rather than inferred from packet timings.
3135    #[cfg(test)]
3136    pub(crate) fn effective_rate(&self) -> FillRate {
3137        let state = self.state.lock();
3138        Self::effective(&state, self.period(&state))
3139    }
3140
3141    fn effective(state: &PixFillState, notify_period: Option<Duration>) -> FillRate {
3142        let notify = state
3143            .notify_started
3144            .then_some(notify_period)
3145            .flatten()
3146            .map(FillRate::once_per);
3147        let fill = (!state.fill.is_zero()).then_some(state.fill);
3148        match (notify, fill) {
3149            (Some(notify), Some(fill)) if fill.as_packets_per_sec() > notify.as_packets_per_sec() => fill,
3150            (Some(notify), _) => notify,
3151            (None, Some(fill)) => fill,
3152            (None, None) => FillRate::ZERO,
3153        }
3154    }
3155
3156    fn apply(&self, state: &PixFillState) {
3157        let rate = Self::effective(state, self.period(state));
3158        // A zero period would trip the controller's own assertion. `FillRate` never carries one —
3159        // `ZERO` is one second and the two constructors take a validated period — so this is a
3160        // belt-and-braces floor rather than a case that arises.
3161        self.controller
3162            .set_rate_per_unit(rate.packets as usize, rate.per.max(Duration::from_micros(1)));
3163        trace!(
3164            session_id = %self.session_id,
3165            packets = rate.packets,
3166            per = ?rate.per,
3167            "applied the exit keep-alive rate"
3168        );
3169    }
3170
3171    /// Decides whether the next keep-alive may go out, and books it if so.
3172    ///
3173    /// The SURB-level notification is exempt from the SURB reserve: it is the message that asks the Entry
3174    /// for more SURBs, so holding it to the reserve would be refusing to ask for the thing that is
3175    /// scarce. It still needs two things, because it is a return packet like any other.
3176    ///
3177    /// * **A reader.** The Entry must have shown that it refills this side's SURBs
3178    ///   ([`counterparty_refills`](BalancerStateValues::counterparty_refills)), which is any keep-alive from its
3179    ///   balancer, flagged or not, but not a manual ping ([`KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing`]): only an Entry with a SURB
3180    ///   balancer sends one of its own accord. An Entry without a balancer attaches a SURB to each data packet and acts
3181    ///   on no report, so every report to it spends a SURB to say nothing. This is decided from what this side has seen
3182    ///   and not from the target the Entry announced, because that is a figure the peer picks, and a report sent on the
3183    ///   strength of it can find no SURB.
3184    /// * **A SURB to send it on.** The estimate must be above zero. With none, the report would not go: the routing
3185    ///   resolver holds a return packet that finds no SURB for the whole of `surb_resolution_wait` and holds every
3186    ///   packet this node originates with it (gnosis_vpn#748).
3187    ///
3188    /// A notification that is due and withheld on either count keeps its slot: the next packet to ask is still
3189    /// classified as the notification, and goes out as soon as both hold. The withheld packet has used its release
3190    /// from the rate limiter, though, so with no fill running that next packet is up to a notification period away,
3191    /// and with one running it is the next fill packet. A withheld notification is also not mistaken for fill. While
3192    /// the PIX supervisor runs a fill, the packet is fill and meets the reserve like any other; while none runs, it
3193    /// is dropped.
3194    ///
3195    /// Fill above that rate is refused while the estimate is below the reserve, and that refusal is
3196    /// not an optimisation. A return packet that finds no SURB is not dropped — the routing resolver
3197    /// holds it, and with it every packet this node originates, for the whole of
3198    /// `surb_resolution_wait`. An Exit filling a cycle down to its last SURB would therefore stall
3199    /// the Session it is filling for, and every other Session on the node with it.
3200    ///
3201    /// # Which packet is the notification
3202    ///
3203    /// Nothing about a packet says which producer it belongs to, so the notification is the first one
3204    /// released no sooner than a period after the last — *less a slack of
3205    /// `min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 2)`* (`period / 10` while degraded, see below), which is what keeps the
3206    /// classification from resting on scheduling latency. The rate limiter that releases these packets sleeps in
3207    /// chunks of [`MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`], re-reads its controller on each wake, and rounds a rate into an integer
3208    /// packet count, so a stream asked for one packet per period releases them a shade over or a
3209    /// shade under it. Compared against the period exactly, a period the controller rounds short by a
3210    /// microsecond would classify every other notification as fill — counted in
3211    /// `hopr_session_pix_fill_packets_total` and, below the reserve, dropped. That is the signal
3212    /// asking the Entry for the SURBs whose absence caused the drop, and it runs on every Exit
3213    /// Session with a `surb_balance_notify_period` configured, PIX or not.
3214    ///
3215    /// The slack cannot let fill masquerade as the notification: `last_notify_at` advances to the
3216    /// instant the packet actually went out, so only the *first* packet past the slack window is the
3217    /// notification, and every fill packet that follows it inside the period is still fill and is
3218    /// still bounded by the reserve. The cap at half the period is what stops a very short period
3219    /// from having its window widened away to nothing.
3220    ///
3221    /// While the Session is degraded the slack is `min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 10)` instead: 100 ms at the
3222    /// one-second degraded default. A half-period slack would make a notification due 500 ms after the last, so a
3223    /// degraded PIX Session with fill running (where fill packets are released between the notifications) would
3224    /// report about twice a second and spend twice the SURBs the degraded period promises. A tenth is still
3225    /// wider than the rate limiter's rounding, and keeps the cadence at about one report per degraded period.
3226    ///
3227    /// # Budget
3228    ///
3229    /// A degraded report is a notification and is exempt from the data reserve, exactly as a normal one is; what
3230    /// stops degraded reports at the keep-alive reserve ([`keep_alive_surb_reserve`]) is the loss driver, which
3231    /// leaves degraded mode once the stock is at or below it (see [`exit_forward_path_is_degraded`]). A Session for
3232    /// which the Exit holds no announced SURB target (`NoRateControl`) is never
3233    /// degraded and keeps the normal period. That holds on PIX Sessions too. PIX fill itself is not affected by
3234    /// degradation: it keeps its own reserve (`min_surb_reserve`) and is classified and admitted as it is outside
3235    /// degraded mode.
3236    ///
3237    /// # Idle backoff
3238    ///
3239    /// Reports to an idle Session mostly waste SURBs, and a multi-hop return path costs the Exit a ticket for
3240    /// each. With an `idle_notify_period` configured, the first [`IDLE_REPORTS_AT_BASE`] idle reports go out
3241    /// at the base period and the period then doubles per report up to the cap
3242    /// ([`backed_off_notify_period`]). A report is idle if nothing moved since the previous one:
3243    ///
3244    /// * **PIX fill is zero.** Any fill rate, the 60 s heartbeat included, keeps the base period; the count restarts
3245    ///   when fill returns to zero.
3246    /// * **Not degraded or dark.** Those cadences are shorter on purpose; entering degraded mode restarts the count.
3247    /// * **Stock above the keep-alive reserve** ([`current_keep_alive_surb_reserve`]) after the report. Otherwise the
3248    ///   Exit is in trouble and the Entry should hear it as often as before. Also checked between reports, when SURBs
3249    ///   are evicted or the announced target changes ([`recheck_reserve`](Self::recheck_reserve)).
3250    /// * **No application data in either direction.** [`note_data_activity`](Self::note_data_activity) resets the count
3251    ///   at once. The Entry's keep-alives and the SURBs they carry do *not* count: its balancer decay refills an idle
3252    ///   Session about once a minute, which would defeat the backoff.
3253    ///
3254    /// Withheld reports (no reader, no SURB) leave the count alone.
3255    ///
3256    /// ## Known limit
3257    ///
3258    /// The Exit learns of a degraded forward path only from what arrives. If a relayer dies during an idle stretch
3259    /// and none of the Entry's packets arrive afterwards, reports stay at the backed-off period, which slows the
3260    /// Entry's dead-relayer verdict. Any packet that does arrive resets the backoff and releases an overdue report
3261    /// at once, and stall or loss detection then switches to the degraded cadence.
3262    ///
3263    /// ## The rate must follow the period
3264    ///
3265    /// While fill is zero the stream's rate must equal `1 / period()`. A packet released before it is due as a
3266    /// notification falls through to the fill branch and is *sent*, so a faster rate sends reports early. Every
3267    /// count change that alters the period is therefore followed by [`apply`](Self::apply) under the same lock
3268    /// ([`note_report`](Self::note_report), [`reset_idle_reports`](Self::reset_idle_reports)). A shorter period
3269    /// releases an overdue report at once, as for [`set_degraded`](Self::set_degraded), and takes effect within
3270    /// [`MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`]; a longer one is safe because `admit` runs before the limiter polls for the next packet.
3271    pub(crate) fn admit(&self) -> bool {
3272        self.admit_at(Instant::now())
3273    }
3274
3275    /// [`admit`](Self::admit) against a caller-supplied instant, so the classification can be tested
3276    /// as the rule it is rather than by sleeping out a period and hoping the scheduler cooperates.
3277    fn admit_at(&self, now: Instant) -> bool {
3278        let mut state = self.state.lock();
3279
3280        // Due *slightly early*: see the classification rule on `admit`. The slack is what keeps this
3281        // from resting on the scheduling latency of the stream that releases the packet.
3282        let notification_due = state.notify_started
3283            && self.period(&state).is_some_and(|period| {
3284                let slack = MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(period / if state.degraded { 10 } else { 2 });
3285                state
3286                    .last_notify_at
3287                    .is_none_or(|at| now.saturating_duration_since(at) >= period.saturating_sub(slack))
3288            });
3289
3290        if notification_due {
3291            if self.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills() && self.estimator.saturating_diff() > 0 {
3292                state.last_notify_at = Some(now);
3293                // Withheld reports never get here, so they leave the idle count alone.
3294                self.note_report(&mut state);
3295                record_exit_control(ExitControlKind::SurbReport, self.session_kind, ExitControlOutcome::Sent);
3296                return true;
3297            }
3298
3299            // Withheld. With no fill running, the slot is not fill either: letting it fall through to the reserve
3300            // check would send a report every period, labelled as fill, from any Session that is above the reserve
3301            // and has no Entry reading it.
3302            if state.fill.is_zero() {
3303                return false;
3304            }
3305        }
3306
3307        let reserve = self.surb_reserve();
3308        if self.estimator.saturating_diff() >= reserve {
3309            Self::set_withholding(&mut state, false);
3310            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
3311            telemetry::record_pix_fill_packet();
3312            record_exit_control(ExitControlKind::PixFill, self.session_kind, ExitControlOutcome::Sent);
3313            return true;
3314        }
3315
3316        debug!(
3317            session_id = %self.session_id,
3318            reserve,
3319            estimate = self.estimator.saturating_diff(),
3320            "withholding a PIX fill keep-alive to stay above the SURB reserve"
3321        );
3322        Self::set_withholding(&mut state, true);
3323        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
3324        telemetry::pix::record_pix_fill_backoff(telemetry::pix::PixFillBackoff::SurbReserve);
3325        false
3326    }
3327
3328    /// Moves the `surb_starved` gauge on the edges only, so it counts stalled Sessions rather than
3329    /// refused packets — the same distinction `PixGateBlockEpisode` draws for the egress gate.
3330    fn set_withholding(state: &mut PixFillState, withholding: bool) {
3331        if state.withholding == withholding {
3332            return;
3333        }
3334        state.withholding = withholding;
3335        crate::supervision::telemetry::emit_sessions_stalled(
3336            crate::supervision::telemetry::PixStallCause::SurbStarved,
3337            if withholding { 1 } else { -1 },
3338        );
3339    }
3340}
3341
3342/// Returns this Session's `surb_starved` count if it was withholding when it went away.
3343///
3344/// `Drop` rather than a call on the close paths, for the reason `PixGateBlockEpisode` gives: a
3345/// Session can end by teardown, by drain, or by its last `Arc` going out of scope in a task nobody
3346/// is waiting on, and this is the one mechanism that covers all three. Without it a Session that
3347/// dies mid-stall leaves the gauge standing for the life of the process.
3348impl Drop for PixFillControl {
3349    fn drop(&mut self) {
3350        Self::set_withholding(self.state.get_mut(), false);
3351    }
3352}
3353
3354/// Stands for "the Entry has announced no target" in [`PixFillControl`]'s record of the last one.
3355///
3356/// Unreachable as a real figure: an announcement is clamped to the node's `maximum_surb_buffer_size`,
3357/// which derives from the SURB ring's `rb_capacity` and so is far below `u64::MAX` on every target
3358/// this code is built for.
3359const NO_ANNOUNCEMENT: u64 = u64::MAX;
3360
3361/// The SURB reserve one Session's fill actually respects.
3362///
3363/// [`PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve`](crate::supervision::PixFillConfig::min_surb_reserve) is a
3364/// *ceiling* rather than the value used, and it has to be, because the two sides of the comparison
3365/// are chosen by different nodes. The reserve is measured against the Exit's estimate of its own SURB
3366/// buffer for the Session, and how deep that buffer is is the *Entry's* decision — it announces its
3367/// balancer target in the lower 32 bits of the options word in `StartInitiation::additional_data`. An operator sizing
3368/// the reserve against a production buffer therefore also decides, unintentionally, that every Session
3369/// whose Entry asks for a shallower one can never be filled at all: the estimate never reaches the
3370/// reserve, every fill packet is withheld, and the funded cycle strands on `max_recovery_time` while
3371/// the logs report only a backoff.
3372///
3373/// A quarter of the announced target is what the reserve is for expressed as a proportion: it leaves
3374/// fill three quarters of whatever buffer the Entry chose and keeps the last quarter for the
3375/// application, which is the side that has something waiting on it. The configured value still binds
3376/// wherever it is the smaller of the two — at the shipped 500 against the worked profile's 7 000-SURB
3377/// target, a quarter is 1 750, so the derivation is inert on a production-sized Session and only
3378/// engages on one whose Entry asked for less than four times the configured reserve.
3379///
3380/// Floored at one, for the same reason the constructor clamps: a zero reserve is fill spending the
3381/// Session's last SURB, and an Entry announcing a three-SURB buffer would otherwise produce exactly
3382/// that.
3383fn effective_surb_reserve(configured: u64, announced_target: u64) -> u64 {
3384    configured.min(announced_target / 4).max(1)
3385}
3386
3387/// One Session's reservation against the node's live reconstructor-cycle budget.
3388///
3389/// Charged when a PIX Session is accepted and returned when its Session closes. Deliberately a
3390/// projection rather than a measurement: the alternative is to weigh the reconstructor's actual
3391/// state and refuse a share once it is too large, which loses the cycle of whichever Session
3392/// happened to arrive last rather than of the one that inflated it. A reservation taken up front can
3393/// only ever refuse a Session that does not exist yet.
3394#[derive(Debug)]
3395pub(crate) struct CycleBudgetReservation {
3396    bytes: u64,
3397    outstanding: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
3398    /// Whether [`release`](Self::release) has already run, so it can be called from both the close
3399    /// path and `Drop` without the budget being returned twice.
3400    released: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool,
3401}
3402
3403impl CycleBudgetReservation {
3404    /// Returns the reservation to the node's budget. Idempotent.
3405    ///
3406    /// Called explicitly by [`close_session`], and by `Drop` as the backstop.
3407    ///
