4725/// request can equally be lost on the return path. So while a successor batch is unanswered — none
4726/// of its commitment has arrived — and an earlier generation is still being served, the supervisor
4727/// emits `ResendSsaRequest` every
4728/// [`ssa_request_resend_interval`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssa_request_resend_interval), which has
4729/// the action driver send the stored message again, byte for byte, and pushes the batch's
4730/// `max_ssa_delivery_time` deadline with it. The Entry answers a repeat of a request it already
4731/// committed to with a no-op once it has published the batch in full. The exception is a repeat
4732/// that arrives more than `SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE` after the batch went out, which says the
4733/// bursts were lost after the transport took them; they are sent again, without a second
4734/// `ReadyToDeposit`. A batch whose publication the transport cut short is finished instead, with
4735/// whole bursts and the `ReadyToDeposit`s still owed, whenever the Exit asks again. A request that
4736/// arrives while the Entry is still processing another one is dropped rather than queued. The
4737/// re-sends end once every member of the batch has reported a part of its commitment, and once the
4738/// batch reaches the front nothing is sent and the deadline runs out as it always did.
4739///
4740/// ### 3. Entry SSA Commitment (`SsaCommit` → Exit)
4741///
4742/// Upon receiving the [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`], the Entry's `handle_ssa_request`
4743/// generates a *client commitment* using the shared [`SsaShareGenerator`] (which is also
4744/// used by the packet pipeline to embed PIX shares into return-path SURBs). The client
4745/// commitment is combined with the Exit commitment to derive the on-chain deposit address
4746/// via [`HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address`].
4747///
4748/// The Entry then sends one or more [`SsaClientCommitmentMessage`]s back to the Exit and
4749/// emits a [`HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit`] to the upper layer, signaling that
4750/// funds can be deposited at the computed address.
4751///
4752/// "One or more" is well over a hundred at the deployed dimensions — one commitment per polynomial,
4753/// chunked to packet size — and the Exit can use *none* of it until every message has landed, since
4754/// the SSA commitment is the sum of them all. A single lost packet therefore used to cost the whole
4755/// Session on `max_ssa_delivery_time`, typically after the Entry had already been told to fund the
4756/// address.
4757///
4758/// So a partially delivered commitment is repaired rather than waited out. Each arriving message
4759/// reports `SessionPixEvent::CommitmentProgress`, which arms (and re-arms) the supervisor's
4760/// [`commitment_recommit_interval`](crate::SupervisorConfig::commitment_recommit_interval); if
4761/// delivery then goes quiet with the set incomplete, `RequestCommitmentRetransmission` has
4762/// `send_commitment_retransmission_request` ask the Entry — via an `SsaRequest` whose
4763/// [`missing`](hopr_protocol_start::SsaServerCommitmentMessage::missing) scope names the polynomial
4764/// runs the reconstructor never received — to re-send exactly those. The Entry answers in
4765/// `handle_ssa_recommit` from the bytes it sent the first time, advancing nothing and announcing no
4766/// second deposit. A cycle for which *nothing* arrived never asks: it has no scope to name, and the
4767/// delivery deadline remains what ends it.
4768///
4769/// ### 4. Deposit Awaiting (Exit Side)
4770///
4771/// The Exit receives the client commitment messages in `handle_ssa_commit`, inserts the
4772/// coefficient commitments into the [`SsaReconstructor`], and extracts the deposit address.
4773/// It emits [`HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded`] to the upper layer with the
4774/// [`AgreedSsaQuota`] and a deposit channel for confirmations.
4775///
4776/// A verifiable commitment is what starts the deposit clock, so the supervisor is told
4777/// (`CommitmentVerified`) before anything can be reported against it. A `PixDepositObserver` task
4778/// forwards every confirmation arriving on the deposit channel as `DepositConfirmed` until the
4779/// upper layer drops the sender. A cycle is funded once at least one non-zero confirmation has
4780/// been forwarded. A zero-amount confirmation does not make it funded or stop the observer.
4781/// When the deposit channel ends, the observer always reports `DepositObserverClosed`; the
4782/// supervisor's phase guard ignores it for a funded cycle.
4783///
4784/// A funded deposit channel ending is logged at DEBUG. The observer warns only when no non-zero
4785/// confirmation was forwarded, because an unfunded cycle still awaiting its deposit is written
4786/// off by the supervisor, which logs "closing PIX SSA". The observer carries no timeout of its
4787/// own — `max_deposit_wait` is the deadline, and a second authority racing the first is exactly
4788/// what the supervisor exists to prevent.
4789///
4790/// Once the deposit suffices, the SSA moves to *recovering*. Its recovery deadlines start when it
4791/// reaches the front, and its deposit releases the egress gate only while it is there. When a paid
4792/// front leaves—whether recovered or retired after a tolerated failure—an unfunded successor
4793/// restores its own bounded predeposit allowance; an already funded successor stays open but starts
4794/// a fresh served-without-progress ceiling.
4795///
4796/// ### 5. SSA Collection, Recovery and Pipelining
4797///
4798/// As the Entry sends return-path SURBs during the Session, each SURB can carry a PIX
4799/// share generated from the client's polynomial set. The Exit's [`SsaReconstructor`]
4800/// collects these shares and reports how far the cycle has got via
4801/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress`]; `dispatch_pix_event` forwards those snapshots to
4802/// the supervisor, which uses them both to reset `max_recovery_idle` and to keep the gate serving.
4803///
4804/// When the last cycle of a batch reaches the *early recovery threshold* (≈85%), an
4805/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaAlmostRecovered`] event fires and the supervisor answers with a
4806/// `RequestSsa` action for the next batch — pipelining the costly commitment exchange with the tail
4807/// of share collection. If that cycle is still awaiting its own commitment or deposit, the request
4808/// waits for funding; if two generations still own cycle state, it waits for one to be fully
4809/// released. Those checks are independent of the configurable share-order policy.
4810///
4811/// Once fully recovered, [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered`] fires, allowing the Exit to
4812/// unlock and redeem the deposited funds. The reconstructor releases the live cycle immediately;
4813/// the supervisor retains a short tombstone, whose expiry emits `RetireSsa` to drop that cycle's
4814/// [`SsaCommitmentGuard`] and abort its deposit observer. The next batch is requested here if
4815/// `SsaAlmostRecovered` has not already done so. Observers are keyed by SSA index, so retiring one
4816/// cycle never cancels a pipelined successor's.
4817///
4818/// ### 6. Unverifiable Shares
4819///
4820/// Shares are not checked individually. Once a polynomial has collected `threshold` of them,
4821/// the reconstructor interpolates its constant term and compares it against the commitment; if
4822/// they disagree, at least one of those shares did not come from the committed polynomial and an
4823/// [`HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares`] event fires, carrying the reconstructor's running
4824/// total for the SSA rather than a delta.
4825///
4826/// The first such report closes the Session, unconditionally and with nothing to configure. The
4827/// failed polynomial is never retried, and the SSA is the sum of every polynomial's constant term,
4828/// so the cycle is already unrecoverable and can never pay; closing immediately caps what a
4829/// malicious Entry is served at `threshold` packets. The running total is logged rather than
4830/// accumulated. See `SessionPixSupervisor::on_unverifiable_shares` for why no tolerance is offered.
4831///
4832/// ### Configuring PIX at the Exit
4833///
4834/// The Exit configures PIX via [`IncomingSessionPixConfig`] within [`SessionManagerConfig`].
4835///
4836/// The [`PixToolbox`] (holding the [`SsaShareGenerator`] and [`SsaReconstructor`]) must
4837/// be provided via [`SessionManager::start`] for PIX to function.
4838pub struct SessionManager<S> {
4839    // Keeps track of Session initiations requests on the Client side.
4840    session_initiations: SessionInitiationCache,
4841    session_notifiers: Arc<OnceLock<SessionNotifiers>>,
4842    /// `StartSession` only: the lane that may park on admission.
4843    start_session_tx: StartProtocolMsgSink,
4844    /// Every other Start variant: the lane a session flood must never delay.
4845    start_control_tx: StartProtocolMsgSink,
4846    /// Authoritative session count for admission control.
4847    /// Incremented atomically inside `allocate_session_slot` before the cache insertion,
4848    /// and decremented at every removal path (explicit close, eviction, guard rollback).
4849    active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>,
4850    sessions: moka::sync::Cache<SessionId, SessionSlot>,
4851    msg_sender: Arc<OnceLock<S>>,
4852    pix_toolbox: Arc<OnceLock<PixToolbox>>,
4853    cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
4854    /// Per-SessionId waiters notified when a new session slot is allocated. Lets message
4855    /// handlers that arrive before the slot insertion completes (e.g. SsaRequest vs
4856    /// SessionEstablished) await the slot once instead of busy-looping with sleeps.
4857    /// Keyed by SessionId so that only waiters for the relevant session are woken.
4858    ///
4859    /// Holds at most one live waiter per SessionId: `handle_ssa_request` refuses a request that
4860    /// finds another one already waiting, rather than parking a second shared Start handler.
4861    slot_allocated: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<SessionId, Vec<oneshot::Sender<()>>>>>,
4862    /// Pseudonyms of outgoing Session initiations currently in flight.
4863    ///
4864    /// `session_initiations` is keyed by challenge, but a Start message arriving from the peer
4865    /// names the Session by its pseudonym. This is the pseudonym-keyed half, so `dispatch_message`
4866    /// can tell in one lookup whether an inbound `SsaRequest` belongs to an initiation this node is
4867    /// still making — the only case in which waiting for a slot is legitimate. Entries are removed
4868    /// by [`PendingOutgoingGuard`] on every failure path and once the slot exists; the TTL is a
4869    /// backstop matching `session_initiations`'.
4870    ///
4871    /// An initiation claims its entry atomically (see `new_session`), so a marker is owned by at
4872    /// most one attempt at a time: a second initiation for a pseudonym that is still pending is
4873    /// refused rather than allowed to overwrite the first one's reservation. The value is a
4874    /// per-claim token, which lets [`PendingOutgoingGuard`] tell its own claim from a newer one
4875    /// that reused the name after the TTL backstop expired the older marker.
4876    pending_outgoing: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>,
4877    /// Challenges of incoming `StartSession`s being admitted, by pseudonym, so a repeat is not admitted twice.
4878    incoming_openings: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, Arc<InFlightOpening>>,
4879    /// Serialises `handle_ssa_request` per pseudonym.
4880    ///
4881    /// Start messages are processed under `for_each_concurrent`, so without this several
4882    /// `SsaRequest`s for one pseudonym run at once — and each reads the successor gate's admission
4883    /// state before any of them has advanced it. Every racer passes, and the Entry commits to (and
4884    /// funds) as many batches as the Exit cared to send, which is exactly what the gate exists to
4885    /// stop. The generator's own monotonic index is the backstop that keeps this from being a
4886    /// correctness hole, but it only rejects *equal or lower* indices: an Exit numbering its batches
4887    /// upwards races past it.
4888    ///
4889    /// An async lock rather than a blocking one because the guarded region awaits — commitment
4890    /// generation goes to a blocking pool, and publication awaits the transport. It is only ever
4891    /// `try_lock`ed, though: a request that finds it held is refused rather than parked on a shared
4892    /// Start handler behind the holder (see `handle_ssa_request`).
4893    ///
4894    /// A `moka` cache rather than a map, for its idle eviction: a `HashMap` keyed by pseudonym would
4895    /// otherwise retain one entry per Session for the life of the process.
4896    ssa_request_locks: moka::future::Cache<HoprPseudonym, Arc<futures::lock::Mutex<()>>>,
4897    /// The Entry's PIX accounting per pseudonym, outliving the Sessions that use it.
4898    ///
4899    /// Lets a Session reconnecting under a pseudonym it used before in this process continue its PIX
4900    /// accounting: the generator keeps its per-pseudonym state for [`PIX_LEDGER_IDLE_RETENTION`], and
4901    /// the watermark and served count it is measured against must outlive the Session too. Not
4902    /// persistent: reuse across process restarts is unsupported.
4903    pix_ledgers: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, EntryPixLedger>,
4904    /// The highest challenge this node has initiated a Session with, per pseudonym.
4905    ///
4906    /// Kept apart from [`pix_ledgers`](Self::pix_ledgers) because that exists only for PIX Sessions,
4907    /// while the first Session under a pseudonym may be a random one that is reused later. Same idle
4908    /// retention and capacity rule as the ledger.
4909    last_challenges: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, StartChallenge>,
4910    /// Live reconstructor-cycle bytes this node has committed to, summed over every PIX Session.
4911    ///
4912    /// The counterpart of `active_sessions`, and the reason that one is not sufficient: a Session is
4913    /// admitted on a slot count, but what it costs the reconstructor is set by the dimensions its
4914    /// peer offered. Charged in `handle_incoming_session_initiation` and returned by
4915    /// [`CycleBudgetReservation`]'s `Drop`, so no removal path has to remember to decrement it.
4916    live_cycle_bytes: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
4917    /// Where incoming Sessions are put to the session server for an admission decision.
4918    ///
4919    /// Unset on a node that runs no session server — an Entry, or a relay — where there is nobody to
4920    /// ask and every Session is admitted on this node's own terms.
4921    /// Behind a `Mutex` so every request goes through *one* sender.
4922    ///
4923    /// `futures::channel::mpsc` gives each cloned `Sender` its own guaranteed slot on top of the
4924    /// buffer, so sending through a fresh clone each time would let the queue grow with the number
4925    /// of concurrent initiations — the bound would not bound. `try_send` never blocks, so the lock
4926    /// is held only for the enqueue itself.
4927    admission_tx: Arc<OnceLock<parking_lot::Mutex<SessionAdmissionSink>>>,
4928    /// The SURB-store admission seam, set once by the composition root after construction.
4929    ///
4930    /// Injected late — rather than through [`SessionManager::new`] — because the only in-tree
4931    /// implementation wraps the SURB store, which is built in the same crate as this manager's
4932    /// caller but cannot be named here (`hopr-transport-session` does not depend on
4933    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`). A manager without one still works: it simply never admits, and every
4934    /// Session's SURBs then live in the store's quarantine class, which is why
4935    /// [`set_surb_admission`](Self::set_surb_admission) exists and why a missed call is observable
4936    /// in the store's own admission metrics rather than silent here.
4937    surb_admission: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>>,
4938    /// Where the Entry hands the forward receipts of its Sessions, set once by the composition root.
4939    forward_receipt_sink: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn ForwardReceiptSink>>>,
4940    /// Permits for concurrent session-server admission waits, so a slow server refuses with `Busy`
4941    /// instead of parking every `StartSession` handler.
4942    admission_permits: Arc<hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::Semaphore>,
4943    /// The node-wide refusal reply budget, shared by every clone; `None` when unbounded.
4944    refusal_replies: Option<Arc<RefusalReplyBucket>>,
4945}
4946
4947impl<S> Clone for SessionManager<S> {
4948    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
4949        Self {
4950            session_initiations: self.session_initiations.clone(),
4951            session_notifiers: self.session_notifiers.clone(),
4952            start_session_tx: self.start_session_tx.clone(),
4953            start_control_tx: self.start_control_tx.clone(),
4954            active_sessions: self.active_sessions.clone(),
4955            live_cycle_bytes: self.live_cycle_bytes.clone(),
4956            sessions: self.sessions.clone(),
4957            cfg: self.cfg.clone(),
4958            msg_sender: self.msg_sender.clone(),
4959            pix_toolbox: self.pix_toolbox.clone(),
4960            slot_allocated: Arc::clone(&self.slot_allocated),
4961            pending_outgoing: self.pending_outgoing.clone(),
4962            incoming_openings: self.incoming_openings.clone(),
4963            ssa_request_locks: self.ssa_request_locks.clone(),
4964            pix_ledgers: self.pix_ledgers.clone(),
4965            last_challenges: self.last_challenges.clone(),
4966            admission_tx: self.admission_tx.clone(),
4967            surb_admission: self.surb_admission.clone(),
4968            forward_receipt_sink: self.forward_receipt_sink.clone(),
4969            admission_permits: self.admission_permits.clone(),
4970            refusal_replies: self.refusal_replies.clone(),
4971        }
4972    }
4973}
4974
4975fn session_config(cfg: &SessionManagerConfig, capabilities: Capabilities) -> HoprSessionConfig {
4976    session_config_with(cfg, capabilities, None)
4977}
4978
4979/// As [`session_config`], with the initiating session's own head-of-line bound.
4980///
4981/// `None` inherits the node default; `Some(0)` disables the bound for this session; `Some(n)` sets
4982/// it. The zero-disables convention matches the node setting, so the per-session
4983/// and node-wide knobs cannot mean opposite things by the same value.
4984///
4985/// Sessions accepted from a peer pass `None`: the bound governs how *we* reassemble what arrives,
4986/// so it is ours to choose, not the initiator's to impose on us.
4987fn session_config_with(
4988    cfg: &SessionManagerConfig,
4989    capabilities: Capabilities,
4990    max_frames_behind_gap: Option<usize>,
4991) -> HoprSessionConfig {
4992    // Only a session that cannot recover the missing frame should abandon it early. With
4993    // retransmission the gap is a request away, so waiting is productive and cutting it short
4994    // would discard data that was on its way back; without it the wait is for something that is
4995    // never coming, and every frame behind the gap is held for nothing.
4996    let can_retransmit =
4997        capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionAck) || capabilities.contains(Capability::RetransmissionNack);
4998
4999    // The session's own value when it stated one, the node's otherwise. `Some(0)` disables the
5000    // bound at either level -- a threshold of zero would abandon every gap before a single frame
5001    // arrived behind it, which nobody wants and which the sequencer would silently clamp to one.
5002    let bound = match max_frames_behind_gap.or(cfg.max_frames_behind_gap) {
5003        Some(0) | None => None,
5004        Some(n) => Some(n),
5005    };
5006
5007    HoprSessionConfig {
5008        capabilities,
5009        frame_mtu: cfg.frame_mtu,
5010        frame_timeout: cfg.max_frame_timeout,
5011        max_buffered_segments: cfg.max_buffered_segments,
5012        max_frames_behind_gap: (!can_retransmit).then_some(bound).flatten(),
5013        stream_base: None,
5014    }
5015}
5016
5017/// The challenge an initiation under one pseudonym tries next.
5018///
5019/// `previous` is the challenge just tried and found taken, and `last` the highest this node has used for
5020/// the pseudonym. With a `last`, the first try is `last + 1` and each collision probes upward by one:
5021/// strictly greater than every earlier challenge of the pseudonym. Without one, the first try is random
5022/// within the lower half of the range, so that per-pseudonym increments cannot realistically wrap.
5023fn next_challenge(last: Option<StartChallenge>, previous: Option<StartChallenge>) -> StartChallenge {
5024    use hopr_api::types::crypto_random::{MAX_RANDOM_INTEGER, random_integer};
5025
5026    match (previous, last) {
5027        (Some(taken), _) => ((taken + 1) % MAX_RANDOM_INTEGER).max(MIN_CHALLENGE),
5028        (None, Some(last)) => ((last + 1) % MAX_RANDOM_INTEGER).max(MIN_CHALLENGE),
5029        (None, None) => random_integer(MIN_CHALLENGE, Some(MAX_RANDOM_INTEGER / 2)),
5030    }
5031}
5032
5033/// How far above the highest frame id the held Session's stream has used the successor's stream base lies.
5034///
5035/// A margin, because the predecessor may still have frames in flight when the base is chosen (a live takeover,
5036/// or a late segment of a detached one): all of them are below the base as long as fewer than this many frames
5037/// were sent after the base was read.
5038const STREAM_BASE_MARGIN: u32 = 1 << 16;
5039
5040/// The first frame id of the successor of the Session of `held`, in both directions: above every frame id the
5041/// predecessor's stream sent or received, by [`STREAM_BASE_MARGIN`].
5042///
5043/// `None` when the predecessor has no stream to continue (a raw Session), or when the base would exceed
5044/// [`MAX_STREAM_BASE`]: the takeover is then refused, and the Entry establishes a Session of its own.
5045fn successor_stream_base(held: &SlotInstance) -> Option<u32> {
5046    let progress = held.stream_progress.get()?;
5047    let highest = progress.highest_received().max(progress.highest_sent());
5048    highest
5049        .checked_add(STREAM_BASE_MARGIN)
5050        .filter(|base| *base <= MAX_STREAM_BASE)
5051}
5052
5053/// The resume window a manager works to: the configured one, capped at half the session idle timeout.
5054///
5055/// A detached slot lives in the same cache as every Session, which evicts a slot idle for the idle
5056/// timeout, and eviction would end the wait on the idle path rather than through the window. Half of
5057/// it leaves the slot's idle timer, refreshed when it is detached, the other half to spare. `0`
5058/// (detaching off) stays `0`. The second value says whether the cap applied, for one warning at
5059/// construction.
5060fn effective_resume_window(configured: Duration, idle_timeout: Duration) -> (Duration, bool) {
5061    let cap = idle_timeout / 2;
5062    if configured > cap {
5063        (cap, true)
5064    } else {
5065        (configured, false)
5066    }
5067}
5068
5069#[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5070fn initialize_session_telemetry(
5071    session_id: SessionId,
5072    cfg: &SessionManagerConfig,
5073    capabilities: Capabilities,
5074    surb_estimator: Option<&AtomicSurbFlowEstimator>,
5075    surb_mgmt: Option<&Arc<BalancerStateValues>>,
5076    owner: u64,
5077) {
5078    initialize_session_metrics(session_id, session_config(cfg, capabilities), owner);
5079    set_session_state(&session_id, SessionLifecycleState::Active);
5080    if let (Some(estimator), Some(mgmt)) = (surb_estimator, surb_mgmt) {
5081        set_session_balancer_data(&session_id, estimator.clone(), mgmt.clone());
5082    }
5083}
5084
5085/// Caps how many SURBs an outgoing Session data packet may carry, per the SURB balancer.
5086///
5087/// Every finite `max_surbs` is gated by the balancer's target: the packet carries the client's number
5088/// of SURBs while the counterparty is estimated to be below its target, and none once it is at or above
5089/// it. The default of `1` is the plain case. A larger client value, which exists to save the balancer
5090/// work on highly asymmetric traffic, is gated the same way, so no setting but `usize::MAX` can hold
5091/// the counterparty more than one packet's SURBs above the target. An explicit `0` always wins, whatever
5092/// the estimate. `usize::MAX` leaves the packet's existing limit untouched and is the one way to opt out
5093/// of the gate.
5094///
5095/// The gate is [`BalancerStateValues::organic_surbs_per_packet`], which yields `0` once the
5096/// counterparty is estimated to be at its target. That zero is the whole point of the function:
5097/// without it, the balancer can silence its keep-alives and still have organic SURBs pouring into a
5098/// full buffer, where each one evicts an older SURB and destroys the PIX share it carried. It also
5099/// bounds the stock the counterparty holds, which is what lets a SURB generation change wipe it at a
5100/// cost the PIX surplus can absorb.
5101///
5102/// One exception: while data goes out into a silence (see [`BalancerStateValues::silence_sustain`]),
5103/// a closed gate gives exactly one SURB per packet, whatever the client asked for. The estimate that
5104/// closed it is fed by the counterparty, and the counterparty has not been heard from for a while, so
5105/// the estimate cannot see the stock draining and would hold the gate shut until it is empty. One SURB
5106/// per data packet is about what the counterparty spends answering it: no burst, bounded by the data
5107/// rate, and it ends with the first report or reply.
5108///
5109/// Nothing else has to change to keep the SURB accounting straight. This runs in front of the
5110/// counting sink, so `estimate_surbs_with_msg` reports the capped figure; and the PIX share for a
5111/// SURB is drawn per SURB while it is built, so a cap of `0` draws no share at all and leaves it
5112/// queued for a packet that can actually deliver it.
5113fn cap_organic_surbs(data: &mut ApplicationDataOut, max_surbs: usize, surb_mgmt: &BalancerStateValues) {
5114    if max_surbs == usize::MAX {
5115        return;
5116    }
5117    // This packet is going out, which is what a silence is measured against.
5118    surb_mgmt.note_sent();
5119    let cap = if max_surbs == 0 {
5120        0
5121    } else if surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet() > 0 {
5122        max_surbs
5123    } else if surb_mgmt.silence_sustain() {
5124        1
5125    } else {
5126        0
5127    };
5128    data.packet_info.get_or_insert_default().max_surbs_in_packet = cap;
5129}
5130
5131/// Books what a Start-protocol packet did to an incoming Session's SURB store: the SURBs it carried and
5132/// the ones the store lost to it. A no-op for an outgoing Session, whose counterparty stores no SURBs of
5133/// ours.
5134///
5135/// Every Start message from the Entry delivers SURBs into the Session's ring exactly as a data packet
5136/// does, whatever the message is: a keep-alive, an `SsaCommit`, the opening `StartSession`. Booking only
5137/// the keep-alives left the others' SURBs out of the Exit's level while the evictions they caused later
5138/// were booked, so once a ring sized off the announced target ran full, the estimate sank below the
5139/// target for good and the Exit's egress controller, which follows it, sent nothing at all.
5140///
5141/// What the packet carried is booked, not a message's `max_surbs()`: that is how many fit beside it,
5142/// what the sender was allowed to send rather than what the store took. And the evictions, which are
5143/// how a SURB generation wipe, and any overflow, reaches the Exit's level.
5144///
5145/// Returns whether it booked anything, i.e. whether `slot` is an incoming Session.
5146fn book_start_message_surbs(slot: &SessionSlot, session_id: &SessionId, stored: SurbsStored) -> bool {
5147    if !matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Return(_)) {
5148        return false;
5149    }
5150    account_incoming_surbs(&slot.surb_estimator, stored.saved, stored.evicted);
5151    if stored.evicted > 0 {
5152        // The stock may have fallen to the reserve, which ends the idle report backoff.
5153        if let Some(control) = slot.pix_fill.get() {
5154            control.recheck_reserve();
5155        }
5156    }
5157    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5158    telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(session_id, stored.saved);
5159    #[cfg(not(feature = "telemetry"))]
5160    let _ = session_id;
5161    true
5162}
5163
5164/// Shared result handling for both Start lanes.
5165fn report_start_result(result: errors::Result<()>) {
5166    match result {
5167        Ok(()) => {}
5168        // Dropped on purpose and not a fault: the request lock, the successor gate (early or
5169        // under-served), the stale-index check and a repeat whose interrupted publication could not
5170        // be finished all refuse this way. The handler has already logged the first occurrence at
5171        // the level it deserves, and the peer re-asks — which can succeed for all of them but a
5172        // stale request.
5173        Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(reason))) => {
5174            tracing::debug!(%reason, "Start protocol message not admitted");
5175        }
5176        Err(error) => tracing::error!(%error, "failed to process Start protocol message"),
5177    }
5178}
5179
5180/// Books an incoming packet's SURBs into the Exit's flow estimator.
5181///
5182/// `saved` SURBs entered the store and `evicted` older ones were dropped to make room for them. Both
5183/// are recorded so that `produced - consumed - evicted` tracks what the store actually holds: without
5184/// the eviction term the estimate stays inflated by every SURB the full store ever discarded, long
5185/// after they are gone -- which leaves the keep-alive level report and the PIX fill reserve both
5186/// reading a level that never falls. `evicted` also carries the stock a newer SURB generation wiped,
5187/// which is what lets the Exit's level report drop to match after the Entry advances the generation.
5188///
5189/// Called for every packet that delivers SURBs to an incoming Session, and there are two kinds: Session
5190/// data packets, in the `session_rx` inspectors of `new_session`, and Start protocol messages, through
5191/// [`book_start_message_surbs`], which `dispatch_message` calls for every Start message and the Start
5192/// task for an opening `StartSession`. The Entry's balancer mints its SURBs as keep-alives as much as in
5193/// data, so a booking in only one of them misses the other's share. Split out from the receive closure
5194/// so the accounting can be unit-tested on its own.
5195fn account_incoming_surbs(estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, saved: u64, evicted: u64) {
5196    estimator
5197        .produced
5198        .fetch_add(saved, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
5199    estimator
5200        .evicted
5201        .fetch_add(evicted, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
5202}
5203
5204/// Removes an outgoing Session's pseudonym from the manager's pending index when dropped.
5205///
5206/// The index is keyed by the pseudonym the initiation is made under, but the paths that would
5207/// otherwise clear it key on the peer-supplied `session_id`, which arrives in the establishment
5208/// reply and is never checked against the pseudonym — a mismatched one would clear someone else's
5209/// marker, and every early return and a dropped future would clear no one's. The guard ties the
5210/// cleanup to the pseudonym actually inserted, so no path has to remember it.
5211///
5212/// The removal is ownership-checked rather than a plain `remove`, because the marker's TTL is only
5213/// a backstop and the guard can outlive it: an initiation that times out runs almost to the TTL,
5214/// so a few ticks of clock skew — or a task descheduled between the await resolving and the future
5215/// being polled to completion — put the drop past expiry. Once expired, moka reports the key as
5216/// absent, so a newer initiation for the same pseudonym can claim the name again; when this guard
5217/// then drops, an unconditional `remove` would tear down the newer attempt's marker and leave its
5218/// in-flight initiation invisible to the dispatch filter, which would drop that Session's
5219/// `SsaRequest`s as `StaleStartMessage`. Comparing the entry's generation token restricts the
5220/// removal to the marker this guard's own claim created.
5221struct PendingOutgoingGuard<'a> {
5222    pending: &'a moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>,
5223    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
5224    token: PendingOutgoingToken,
5225}
5226
5227impl Drop for PendingOutgoingGuard<'_> {
5228    fn drop(&mut self) {
5229        // `and_compute_with` reads under moka's per-key compute lock and reports an expired entry
5230        // as absent, so an expired marker of ours falls through to `Op::Nop` and nothing is left
5231        // to clean up; a marker another attempt claimed after our expiry is likewise left to that
5232        // attempt's own guard.
5233        self.pending.entry(self.pseudonym).and_compute_with(
5234            |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, PendingOutgoingToken>>| {
5235                match entry {
5236                    // Still ours.
5237                    Some(entry) if entry.value() == &self.token => moka::ops::compute::Op::Remove,
5238                    // Absent (expired, or already removed by the success path), or a newer
5239                    // attempt's claim: nothing to do.
5240                    _ => moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop,
5241                }
5242            },
5243        );
5244    }
5245}
5246
5247/// Per-claim token distinguishing one initiation's marker from another attempt's under the same
5248/// pseudonym.
5249///
5250/// Uniqueness only has to hold for the lifetime of one claim, which the atomic claim in
5251/// `new_session` serialises: two guards for the same pseudonym never overlap on a live marker.
5252/// A per-process counter is enough for that, and `Copy` keeps the token cheap to move into and
5253/// compare inside the compute closure.
5254#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
5255struct PendingOutgoingToken(u64);
5256
5257impl PendingOutgoingToken {
5258    fn next() -> Self {
5259        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
5260        static NEXT: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
5261        Self(NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed))
5262    }
5263}
5264
5265/// How many repeats of one `StartSession` an Exit answers with a `SessionEstablished`.
5266const MAX_ANSWERED_START_REPEATS: u32 = 4;
5267
5268/// An opening being admitted, with what its repeats did to the SURB store meanwhile (no slot exists to book it to).
5269struct InFlightOpening {
5270    challenge: StartChallenge,
5271    /// `Some` while the original is in flight; the original takes it, and later repeats book directly.
5272    pending: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<SurbsStored>>,
5273}
5274
5275/// Books to `slot` what dispatch left of a replayed repeat plus what repeats carried onto its claim meanwhile.
5276fn book_replay_surbs(opening: &InFlightOpening, slot: &SessionSlot, pseudonym: &SessionId, stored: SurbsStored) {
5277    // Taken, so later repeats on this claim book to the slot directly.
5278    let carried = opening.pending.lock().take().unwrap_or_default();
5279    let total = SurbsStored {
5280        saved: stored.saved + carried.saved,
5281        evicted: stored.evicted + carried.evicted,
5282    };
5283    if total != SurbsStored::default() {
5284        let _ = book_start_message_surbs(slot, pseudonym, total);
5285    }
5286}
5287
5288/// Releases an Exit's claim on a pseudonym's opening in `incoming_openings` when the handler is done.
5289struct IncomingOpeningGuard {
5290    openings: moka::sync::Cache<HoprPseudonym, Arc<InFlightOpening>>,
5291    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
5292    opening: Arc<InFlightOpening>,
5293}
5294
5295impl Drop for IncomingOpeningGuard {
5296    fn drop(&mut self) {
5297        self.openings.entry(self.pseudonym).and_compute_with(
5298            |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, Arc<InFlightOpening>>>| match entry {
5299                Some(entry) if entry.value().challenge == self.opening.challenge => moka::ops::compute::Op::Remove,
5300                _ => moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop,
5301            },
5302        );
5303    }
5304}
5305
5306/// What an Exit made of an incoming `StartSession`, before any admission work.
5307enum OpeningClaim {
5308    /// The same opening is being admitted right now; its handler will answer.
5309    InFlightRepeat(Arc<InFlightOpening>),
5310    /// The Session for this opening exists already; the slot is the one to answer through.
5311    EstablishedRepeat(Box<SessionSlot>, IncomingOpeningGuard),
5312    /// Not a repeat; the guard, if any, holds the claim until the handler returns.
5313    New(Option<IncomingOpeningGuard>),
5314}
5315
5316async fn send_via_msg_sender<S, D>(
5317    msg_sender: &mut S,
5318    routing: DestinationRouting,
5319    data: D,
5320    error_context: &'static str,
5321) -> errors::Result<()>
5322where
5323    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
5324    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5325    D: TryInto<ApplicationData>,
5326    D::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
5327{
5328    let app_data: ApplicationData = data.try_into().map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5329    msg_sender
5330        .send((routing, ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(app_data)))
5331        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
5332        .await
5333        .map_err(|_| {
5334            error!("timeout sending {error_context}");
5335            TransportSessionError::Timeout
5336        })?
5337        .map_err(|error| {
5338            error!(%error, "failed to send {error_context}");
5339            SessionManagerError::other(error)
5340        })?;
5341    Ok(())
5342}
5343
5344/// Refreshes the pending registration of every member of a batch, and says whether all of them still exist.
5345///
5346/// A read of a registration postpones its expiry (see `SsaReconstructor::missing_commitment_runs`), which
5347/// is what keeps one alive while the Entry is silent. Every member is read, not only up to the first one
5348/// that is gone.
5349fn refresh_registrations(reconstructor: &SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>, ssa_ids: &[SsaId<HoprPseudonym>]) -> bool {
5350    // Collected first, so that no short-circuit leaves a later member unread.
5351    let present: Vec<bool> = ssa_ids
5352        .iter()
5353        .map(|ssa_id| reconstructor.missing_commitment_runs(ssa_id, 1).is_some())
5354        .collect();
5355    present.into_iter().all(|present| present)
5356}
5357
5358/// As [`send_via_msg_sender`], for an Exit's Start-protocol send over a Session's return path: the packet
5359/// takes a SURB, so it is counted in the Session's `estimator` (see [`count_return_packet_surb`]) and
5360/// the resolver gives the count back if it drops the packet for want of a SURB.
5361///
5362/// `routing` must be the Session's return routing; a forward-routed send takes no SURB and must go
5363/// through [`send_via_msg_sender`].
5364async fn send_counted_via_msg_sender<S, D>(
5365    msg_sender: &mut S,
5366    routing: DestinationRouting,
5367    data: D,
5368    estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator,
5369    session_id: &SessionId,
5370    error_context: &'static str,
5371) -> errors::Result<()>
5372where
5373    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
5374    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5375    D: TryInto<ApplicationData>,
5376    D::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
5377{
5378    let app_data: ApplicationData = data.try_into().map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5379    let data = count_return_packet_surb(estimator, ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(app_data));
5380    let refund = data.surb_refund.clone();
5381    let started = std::time::Instant::now();
5382    let timed_out = |_| {
5383        error!("timeout sending {error_context}");
5384        TransportSessionError::Timeout
5385    };
5386
5387    // The SURB is given back only while the sink has not taken the packet: once it has, the packet may
5388    // already be on its way and the debit stands. The one timeout covers readiness and the flush, so a
5389    // sink that stays pending drops a packet it never accepted, and must not leave the estimate down.
5390    futures::future::poll_fn(|cx| msg_sender.poll_ready_unpin(cx))
5391        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
5392        .await
5393        .map_err(|error| {
5394            refund.give_back();
5395            timed_out(error)
5396        })?
5397        .map_err(|error| {
5398            refund.give_back();
5399            error!(%error, "failed to send {error_context}");
5400            SessionManagerError::other(error)
5401        })?;
5402    msg_sender.start_send_unpin((routing, data)).map_err(|error| {
5403        refund.give_back();
5404        error!(%error, "failed to send {error_context}");
5405        SessionManagerError::other(error)
5406    })?;
5407    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
5408    telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(session_id, 1);
5409    #[cfg(not(feature = "telemetry"))]
5410    let _ = session_id;
5411
5412    futures::future::poll_fn(|cx| msg_sender.poll_flush_unpin(cx))
5413        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(
5414            EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT.saturating_sub(started.elapsed()),
5415        ))
5416        .await
5417        .map_err(timed_out)?
5418        .map_err(|error| {
5419            error!(%error, "failed to send {error_context}");
5420            SessionManagerError::other(error)
5421        })?;
5422    Ok(())
5423}
5424
5425/// Counts a send's outcome in `hopr_exit_control_packets_total`, passing the result through.
5426fn count_exit_control_send(
5427    kind: ExitControlKind,
5428    session: ExitSessionKind,
5429    result: errors::Result<()>,
5430) -> errors::Result<()> {
5431    let outcome = if result.is_ok() {
5432        ExitControlOutcome::Sent
5433    } else {
5434        ExitControlOutcome::SendFailed
5435    };
5436    record_exit_control(kind, session, outcome);
5437    result
5438}
5439
5440/// The batch most recently put on the wire by the PIX action driver, with the message that carried it.
5441///
5442/// The one thing [`SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest`] can send again. See
5443/// [`SessionManager::spawn_pix_action_driver`].
5444type LastSsaRequest = (Vec<SsaId<HoprPseudonym>>, HoprStartProtocol);
5445
5446/// What the action driver does with a [`SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest`].
5447///
5448/// The decision is separate from the driver so that each refusal is observable on its own: all of them
5449/// look the same from outside — nothing goes on the wire and the supervisor is told the batch can no
5450/// longer be sent — and the driver's I/O loop is the wrong place to pin which of the three it was.
5451#[derive(Debug)]
5452enum ResendDecision<'a> {
5453    /// Send this message, which is the stored request itself and so goes out byte for byte as before.
5454    Send(&'a HoprStartProtocol),
5455    /// The ids are not the batch last sent: a report about an earlier batch, or the batch has been
5456    /// retired since. Another tick would meet the same answer.
5457    NotLastRequest,
5458    /// A member's Exit registration no longer exists — retired, or idled out past
5459    /// `incomplete_commitment_lifetime` — so the Entry's answer would find nothing to match
5460    /// (`MissingSsaCommitment`).
5461    RegistrationGone,
5462    /// Every member's commitment is already complete. The Entry has answered in full; what is left is
5463    /// not a request to send again.
5464    CommitmentComplete,
5465}
5466
5467/// Decides whether `ssa_ids` can be re-sent, and with what.
5468///
5469/// Sent only if `ssa_ids` is exactly the batch of `last_request`, every member still has a
5470/// registration, and at least one of them is still waiting for its commitment (a non-empty
5471/// `missing_commitment_runs`). A member whose commitment is complete is no reason to refuse: the
5472/// supervisor re-sends the whole batch until *every* member has heard from the Entry, because the
5473/// Entry publishes a batch one member after another and may have been cut short before the later ones,
5474/// and the Entry's repeat branch publishes only the members it still owes. It sends the bursts of the
5475/// others again only when the repeat comes long enough after the batch went out to mean they were lost.
5476///
5477/// Every member is read, with no early exit, because reading a registration refreshes its idle timer —
5478/// see [`SsaReconstructor::missing_commitment_runs`] — which is what keeps a registration alive across
5479/// the Entry's silence. A mismatch is decided before any registration is read, since the batch is not
5480/// one this driver can send anyway; a missing registration decides before completeness does.
5481fn resend_payload<'a>(
5482    last_request: Option<&'a LastSsaRequest>,
5483    ssa_ids: &[SsaId<HoprPseudonym>],
5484    processor: &SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>,
5485) -> ResendDecision<'a> {
5486    let Some((_, message)) = last_request.filter(|(sent_ids, _)| sent_ids.as_slice() == ssa_ids) else {
5487        return ResendDecision::NotLastRequest;
5488    };
5489
5490    let (mut gone, mut pending) = (false, false);
5491    for ssa_id in ssa_ids {
5492        match processor.missing_commitment_runs(ssa_id, 1) {
5493            None => gone = true,
5494            Some(runs) => pending |= !runs.is_empty(),
5495        }
5496    }
5497    match (gone, pending) {
5498        (true, _) => ResendDecision::RegistrationGone,
5499        (false, false) => ResendDecision::CommitmentComplete,
5500        (false, true) => ResendDecision::Send(message),
5501    }
5502}
5503
5504/// Forgets `last_request` when `retired` is one of its members.
5505///
5506/// A batch with a retired member is not one the Entry can still be asked to commit to as a whole, and
5507/// the supervisor ends its re-sends. The stored message goes with it, so a `ResendSsaRequest` that was
5508/// already queued finds nothing to send. Left to the registration check in [`resend_payload`] alone,
5509/// that refusal would depend on the reconstructor having dropped the retired member's registration.
5510fn forget_request_of(last_request: &mut Option<LastSsaRequest>, retired: &SsaId<HoprPseudonym>) {
5511    if last_request
5512        .as_ref()
5513        .is_some_and(|(sent_ids, _)| sent_ids.contains(retired))
5514    {
5515        *last_request = None;
5516    }
5517}
5518
5519/// The messages of one cycle's client commitment, as [`SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple`] splits it.
5520type CommitmentBurst = Vec<SsaClientCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixCommitmentProof>>;
5521
5522/// Puts one cycle's commitment burst on the wire and, only once all of it is out, announces its deposit
5523/// address.
5524///
5525/// The order is the point: the deposit must not begin before the Exit holds the complete commitment it
5526/// derives the deposit key from. If a send fails the burst stops where it is and nothing is announced;
5527/// the caller still owes the cycle its publication and decides what to do about that. The same goes
5528/// for an announcement that cannot be queued: the Exit then holds the whole commitment, but the
5529/// upper layer was never told to fund it.
5530async fn publish_commitment<S>(
5531    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
5532    msg_sender: &mut S,
5533    routing: &DestinationRouting,
5534    burst: CommitmentBurst,
5535    quota: &AgreedSsaQuota,
5536    error_context: &'static str,
5537) -> errors::Result<()>
5538where
5539    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
5540    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5541{
5542    let ssa_index = quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
5543    for commitment_msg in burst {
5544        send_via_msg_sender(
5545            msg_sender,
5546            routing.clone(),
5547            HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
5548            error_context,
5549        )
5550        .await?;
5551    }
5552
5553    tracing::debug!(%ssa_index, "all Entry SSA commitment messages were sent out");
5554
5555    // Notify the new SSA deposit address *after* all commitment messages have been sent out
5556    // successfully, so the deposit cannot begin before the Exit has the complete commitment to
5557    // reconstruct the deposit key.
5558    pix_toolbox
5559        .pix_events
5560        .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit(quota.clone()))
5561        .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!("failed to notify new deposit ssa")))?;
5562    tracing::info!(
5563        %ssa_index, deposit_address = %quota.deposit_address, quota_per_ssa = quota.quota_per_ssa,
5564        "generated client SSA commitment and deposit address"
5565    );
5566    Ok(())
5567}
5568
5569/// Puts a claimed member back after its publication failed, and reports the cut.
5570///
5571/// The single place a cut-short publication is logged — once, at `warn!`, with the member and how many
5572/// are still owed — and turned into an error: the non-fatal [`SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted`], whichever
5573/// path was publishing. The Session is untouched and the Exit is told nothing; whether it asks again is
5574/// its own business (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]).
5575fn publication_cut_short(
5576    session_id: SessionId,
5577    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
5578    claim: ClaimedPublication,
5579    cause: &TransportSessionError,
5580) -> TransportSessionError {
5581    let ssa_index = claim.quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
5582    ssa_state.restore_unpublished(claim);
5583    let still_owed = ssa_state.unpublished_indices().len();
5584    tracing::warn!(
5585        %session_id, %ssa_index, still_owed, error = %cause,
5586        "publishing the SSA commitment was cut short; it stays owed until the Exit asks again"
5587    );
5588    SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
5589        "publication of the SSA commitment for {ssa_index} was cut short ({cause}); {still_owed} member(s) still owed"
5590    ))
5591    .into()
5592}
5593
5594/// Finishes publishing the batch an interrupted publication left behind, member by member in ascending
5595/// order, stopping at the first transport failure.
5596///
5597/// Each member still owed is *claimed* first — removed from [`SessionSsaState`]'s unpublished set,
5598/// which is what makes it this call's alone — and then published in full: its whole burst, rebuilt
5599/// from the material the generator retains for the cycle, and only then the `ReadyToDeposit` that was
5600/// owed. Every member that is published here is published whole, and by exactly one caller, so a
5601/// resumption can neither announce a deposit twice nor race the original publication or another
5602/// resumption into doing so. A member whose publication fails goes back, the failure is reported
5603/// through [`publication_cut_short`], and the members after it were never claimed, so all of them stay
5604/// owed for the next attempt.
5605///
5606/// The whole burst is re-sent rather than only what went missing, because what went missing is not
5607/// known: the Entry's send failed at some message and says nothing about the ones the transport
5608/// accepted before it, and the Exit's request names parts of a commitment it may not even have started
5609/// to receive. That costs one of the cycle's
5610/// [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS) answers, and
5611/// that cap is what bounds how often a cycle can be re-published. Once it is spent the generator
5612/// refuses (`PixError::InvalidInput`), and so it does when nothing is retained for the cycle any more
5613/// (`PixError::MissingSsaCommitment`): either way the cycle can never be published again, so it is
5614/// dropped from the owed set with a single warning rather than kept to cost a blocking `recommit` and
5615/// a log line on every re-send. It is never announced, and nothing is stranded by that. Dropping one
5616/// member does not stop the others, and the call is successful if the rest were published.
5617///
5618/// A resumption is reached only through a repeat of the request or a scoped re-request that names an
5619/// owed cycle, so it covers what the Exit asks about. See [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`] for what
5620/// nothing prompts.
5621async fn resume_publication<S>(
5622    session_id: SessionId,
5623    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
5624    routing: &DestinationRouting,
5625    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
5626    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
5627    msg_sender: &mut S,
5628) -> errors::Result<()>
5629where
5630    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
5631    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5632{
5633    /// How resuming one member ended, short of a transport failure.
5634    enum Resumed {
5635        Published,
5636        /// The generator will never produce this cycle's burst again.
5637        Unpublishable(hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError<HoprPseudonym>),
5638    }
5639
5640    let whole_cycle = [(
5641        0,
5642        ssa_state.params.polys_per_ssa() as hopr_protocol_pix::PolynomialIndex - 1,
5643    )];
5644
5645    for ssa_index in ssa_state.unpublished_indices() {
5646        let Some(claim) = ssa_state.claim_unpublished(ssa_index) else {
5647            // Published, or being published, by someone else since the list was read.
5648            continue;
5649        };
5650
5651        let generator = pix_toolbox.share_generator.clone();
5652        let outcome: errors::Result<Resumed> = async {
5653            let recommitted = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
5654                move || generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, whole_cycle),
5655                "client_ssa_recommitment",
5656            )
5657            .await
5658            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5659            let commitment = match recommitted {
5660                Ok(commitment) => commitment,
5661                Err(
5662                    error @ (hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::InvalidInput
5663                    | hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::MissingSsaCommitment),
5664                ) => return Ok(Resumed::Unpublishable(error)),
5665                Err(error) => return Err(SessionManagerError::PixError(error).into()),
5666            };
5667            let burst =
5668                SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5669            publish_commitment(
5670                pix_toolbox,
5671                msg_sender,
5672                routing,
5673                burst,
5674                &claim.quota,
5675                "re-published client SSA commitment message",
5676            )
5677            .await?;
5678            Ok(Resumed::Published)
5679        }
5680        .await;
5681
5682        match outcome {
5683            Ok(Resumed::Published) => {
5684                ssa_state.complete_publication(claim, Instant::now());
5685                tracing::info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, "finished publishing an interrupted SSA commitment");
5686            }
5687            Ok(Resumed::Unpublishable(cause)) => {
5688                // Not put back: it can never be published, so owing it would only repeat this.
5689                tracing::warn!(
5690                    %session_id, %ssa_index, error = %cause,
5691                    "the SSA commitment can no longer be published and is dropped; its deposit is never announced"
5692                );
5693                drop(claim);
5694            }
5695            Err(error) => return Err(publication_cut_short(session_id, ssa_state, claim, &error)),
5696        }
5697    }
5698    Ok(())
5699}
5700
5701/// Sends the whole burst of each of `members` again, rebuilt from the material the generator
5702/// retains, and announces nothing.
5703///
5704/// This answers a repeat that arrives too late to have crossed the batch's bursts (see
5705/// [`SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE`]): some member's burst went out and none of it reached the Exit. The
5706/// repeat names the whole batch, not the member that is missing, so every announced member is sent
5707/// again, and a member the Exit already holds absorbs the copy. There is no `ReadyToDeposit`,
5708/// because each of `members` was announced when its publication completed (see
5709/// [`OwedPublications::announced`]).
5710///
5711/// Each re-send spends one of the cycle's
5712/// [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS), the same
5713/// budget a scoped re-request draws on. Once the generator refuses to rebuild a cycle, because that
5714/// budget is spent or its material is gone, the cycle is no longer counted as announced, so later
5715/// repeats do not ask again. A transport failure stops the re-send where it is and is the non-fatal
5716/// [`SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted`]. The Exit's next repeat after the grace tries again.
5717async fn republish_commitments<S>(
5718    session_id: SessionId,
5719    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
5720    routing: &DestinationRouting,
5721    ssa_state: &SessionSsaState,
5722    pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
5723    msg_sender: &mut S,
5724    members: Vec<SsaIndex>,
5725) -> errors::Result<()>
5726where
5727    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Unpin,
5728    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5729{
5730    let whole_cycle = [(
5731        0,
5732        ssa_state.params.polys_per_ssa() as hopr_protocol_pix::PolynomialIndex - 1,
5733    )];
5734
5735    for ssa_index in members {
5736        let generator = pix_toolbox.share_generator.clone();
5737        let recommitted = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
5738            move || generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, whole_cycle),
5739            "client_ssa_recommitment",
5740        )
5741        .await
5742        .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5743        let commitment = match recommitted {
5744            Ok(commitment) => commitment,
5745            Err(
5746                error @ (hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::InvalidInput
5747                | hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError::MissingSsaCommitment),
5748            ) => {
5749                ssa_state.forget_announced(ssa_index);
5750                tracing::warn!(
5751                    %session_id, %ssa_index, error = %error,
5752                    "a lost SSA commitment can no longer be re-sent"
5753                );
5754                continue;
5755            }
5756            Err(error) => return Err(SessionManagerError::PixError(error).into()),
5757        };
5758
5759        let burst =
5760            SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
5761        let num_messages = burst.len();
5762        for commitment_msg in burst {
5763            if let Err(error) = send_via_msg_sender(
5764                msg_sender,
5765                routing.clone(),
5766                HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
5767                "re-sent client SSA commitment message",
5768            )
5769            .await
5770            {
5771                tracing::warn!(
5772                    %session_id, %ssa_index, %error,
5773                    "re-sending a lost SSA commitment was cut short; the Exit's next repeat tries again"
5774                );
5775                return Err(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
5776                    "re-sending the SSA commitment for {ssa_index} was cut short ({error})"
5777                ))
5778                .into());
5779            }
5780        }
5781
5782        tracing::info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, num_messages, "re-sent the whole commitment of a published SSA");
5783    }
5784    Ok(())
5785}
5786
5787impl<S> SessionManager<S>
5788where
5789    S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
5790    S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
5791{
5792    /// Creates a new instance given the [`config`](SessionManagerConfig).
5793    pub fn new(mut cfg: SessionManagerConfig) -> Self {
5794        let maximum_sessions = cfg.maximum_sessions;
5795        let (resume_window, capped) = effective_resume_window(cfg.pix_config.resume_window, cfg.idle_timeout);
5796        if capped {
5797            warn!(
5798                configured = ?cfg.pix_config.resume_window,
5799                effective = ?resume_window,
5800                idle_timeout = ?cfg.idle_timeout,
5801                "the PIX resume window is capped at half the session idle timeout"
5802            );
5803        }
5804        cfg.pix_config.resume_window = resume_window;
5805        cfg.surb_balance_notify_period = cfg
5806            .surb_balance_notify_period
5807            .map(|p| p.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD));
5808        cfg.surb_degraded_notify_period = cfg
5809            .surb_degraded_notify_period
5810            .map(|p| p.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD));
5811        // Said once, here, rather than per Session: a degraded period that does not report faster than
5812        // the normal one is a switch between two equal cadences, so it is treated as off.
5813        // With no normal period there is nothing to speed up, which is the default of a node that reports
5814        // no levels at all, so that case is silent.
5815        if let (Some(degraded), Some(normal)) = (cfg.surb_degraded_notify_period, cfg.surb_balance_notify_period)
5816            && degraded >= normal
5817        {
5818            warn!(
5819                degraded = ?degraded,
5820                normal = ?normal,
5821                "the degraded SURB notification period is not faster than the normal one, so it is disabled"
5822            );
5823        }
5824        // Floored, then clamped to a quarter of the idle timeout so the Entry's slot survives two lost reports (see
5825        // `IDLE_NOTIFY_PERIODS_PER_IDLE_TIMEOUT`).
5826        if let (Some(cap), Some(normal)) = (cfg.surb_idle_notify_period, cfg.surb_balance_notify_period) {
5827            let ceiling =
5828                (cfg.idle_timeout / IDLE_NOTIFY_PERIODS_PER_IDLE_TIMEOUT).max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD);
5829            let cap = cap.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD);
5830            let clamped = cap.min(ceiling);
5831            if clamped < cap {
5832                warn!(
5833                    configured = ?cap,
5834                    clamped = ?clamped,
5835                    idle_timeout = ?cfg.idle_timeout,
5836                    "the idle SURB notification period is longer than a quarter of the session idle timeout, so \
5837                     it is lowered to it: the Entry's slot must survive two lost reports"
5838                );
5839            }
5840            if clamped <= normal {
5841                warn!(
5842                    idle = ?clamped,
5843                    normal = ?normal,
5844                    "the idle SURB notification period is not slower than the normal one, so the idle backoff is \
5845                     disabled"
5846                );
5847            }
5848            cfg.surb_idle_notify_period = Some(clamped);
5849        }
5850        cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration = cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION);
5851
5852        // Ensure the Frame MTU is at least the size of the Session segment MTU payload
5853        cfg.frame_mtu = cfg.frame_mtu.max(SESSION_MTU);
5854        cfg.max_frame_timeout = cfg.max_frame_timeout.max(MIN_FRAME_TIMEOUT);
5855
5856        // Both SSA batch knobs are range-validated in `HoprProtocolConfig`, but nothing in this crate
5857        // calls `validate()` — clamp here so a programmatically built config cannot ask for a batch of
5858        // zero (no request would ever be sent) or one large enough to blow past what
5859        // `MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE` exists to bound.
5860        cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request = cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE);
5861        cfg.pix_config.supervision.ssas_per_request =
5862            cfg.pix_config.supervision.ssas_per_request.clamp(1, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE);
5863
5864        // Every supervisor duration, for the same reason and with more riding on it. A duration the
5865        // monotonic clock cannot represent makes `Instant::checked_add` return `None`, and every phase
5866        // reads an absent deadline as *no deadline* — so an over-large value does not produce a distant
5867        // deadline, it silently disables the rule. `validate_pix_supervision` rejects such a config, but
5868        // only a node built from a config file goes through it.
5869        //
5870        // Representability is necessary and not sufficient, though: `max_recovery_idle` also has to
5871        // stay under the reconstructor's `unused_verifier_lifetime`, or the supervisor waits on a
5872        // cycle whose state was reclaimed hours earlier. Clamping only to the monotonic-clock cap left
5873        // exactly that — `Duration::MAX` became 24 h against a 30-minute default lifetime — so the
5874        // normalized config was representable and still invalid.
5875        //
5876        // The reconstructor is not installed until `start`, so the *default* configuration is what
5877        // this can normalize against. `start` re-checks against the one actually installed, which is
5878        // where a caller pairing a non-default reconstructor is caught.
5879        //
5880        // The two batch-scaled deadlines are clamped by the scaled value, since that is what is armed;
5881        // dividing by the batch size (already clamped to at least 1 above) is what keeps the product
5882        // under the cap.
5883        {
5884            use hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig;
5885
5886            let sup = &mut cfg.pix_config.supervision;
5887            let cap = crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION;
5888            let per_cycle_cap = cap / sup.ssas_per_request as u32;
5889            sup.max_ssa_delivery_time = sup.max_ssa_delivery_time.min(per_cycle_cap);
5890            sup.max_deposit_wait = sup.max_deposit_wait.min(per_cycle_cap);
5891            sup.max_recovery_time = sup.max_recovery_time.min(cap);
5892            sup.tombstone_retention_window = sup.tombstone_retention_window.min(cap);
5893
5894            // Strictly under the lifetime, which is what `validate_pix_supervision` requires; a
5895            // saturating subtraction keeps a pathologically short lifetime from wrapping. The lower
5896            // bound is not clamped: raising a too-small value would be inventing a policy rather than
5897            // bounding one, and it is what `validate_pix_supervision` reports.
5898            let idle_cap = SsaReconstructorConfig::default()
5899                .unused_verifier_lifetime
5900                .saturating_sub(Duration::from_secs(1))
5901                .min(cap);
5902            sup.max_recovery_idle = sup.max_recovery_idle.min(idle_cap);
5903
5904            // The fill heartbeat is armed as a deadline like the rest, so it takes the same cap. The
5905            // rate ceiling is clamped for a different reason: `RateController::MIN_DELAY` makes
5906            // anything above `MAX_FILL_RATE` unrepresentable, and a controller that silently ignores
5907            // the one bound on this node's self-generated egress is worse than one that is loud about
5908            // refusing it — which is what `validate_pix_supervision` does for a config that was
5909            // validated. This branch is for the programmatic ones that never were.
5910            //
5911            // The heartbeat needs the *lower* bound for the same reason the ceiling needs its upper
5912            // one, and it is the one that bites: a zero period makes `FillRate::as_packets_per_sec`
5913            // report zero, so the planner's own floor is zero, every branch of `FillPlanner::bound`
5914            // that returns the heartbeat returns a zero period, and `PixFillControl::apply` hands
5915            // `set_rate_per_unit(1, 1µs)` to the controller — which `MIN_DELAY` turns into 10 000
5916            // packets/s. The one clamp that exists to bound self-generated egress is bypassed by the
5917            // one field that was left unbounded below. The floor is the exact dual of the ceiling —
5918            // the period of `MAX_FILL_RATE` — rather than a new number, so the two cannot drift; an
5919            // inverted heartbeat/ceiling pair is already resolved ceiling-wins inside `bound`, which
5920            // is what makes any positive floor safe here.
5921            sup.fill.heartbeat = sup
5922                .fill
5923                .heartbeat
5924                .clamp(Duration::from_secs(1) / crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE, cap);
5925            sup.fill.max_rate = sup.fill.max_rate.clamp(1, crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE);
5926        }
5927
5928        // The admission wait is spent inside the peer's initiation timeout, so a value at or above
5929        // it buys nothing: the peer has already given up by the time the wait expires, and the
5930        // Session was refused anyway. Clamped to one leg of that budget, leaving the other for the
5931        // Start exchange the decision is part of. Clamped rather than rejected because every other
5932        // cross-field rule in this constructor normalizes, and because the ceiling is derived from a
5933        // field the caller may also have left at its default.
5934        cfg.session_admission_timeout = cfg.session_admission_timeout.min(initiation_timeout_max_one_way(
5935            cfg.initiation_timeout_base,
5936            RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS,
5937        ));
5938
5939        // The bucket floors the period too; this keeps the config in line with what is enforced.
5940        if let Some(budget) = cfg.refusal_reply_budget.as_mut() {
5941            budget.refill_period = budget.refill_period.max(MIN_REFUSAL_REPLY_REFILL_PERIOD);
5942        }
5943        let refusal_replies = cfg.refusal_reply_budget.map(|b| Arc::new(RefusalReplyBucket::new(b)));
5944
5945        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
5946        METRIC_ACTIVE_SESSIONS.set(0.0);
5947
5948        let active_sessions: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize> = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
5949        let active_sessions_for_listener = active_sessions.clone();
5950
5951        let msg_sender = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
5952        let initiation_timeout = initiation_cache_ttl(cfg.initiation_timeout_base);
5953        let pix_toolbox: Arc<OnceLock<PixToolbox>> = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
5954        // Captured by the eviction listener below, which is built here and has no `&self` to read
5955        // later — same shape as `active_sessions_for_listener`. Cloned before the closure moves the
5956        // last binding, since the struct literal needs its own handle to the same lock.
5957        let surb_admission_for_listener: Arc<OnceLock<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>> = Arc::default();
5958        let surb_admission_in_struct = surb_admission_for_listener.clone();
5959        // The retire grace the listener's teardowns wait out, captured for the same reason: the
5960        // closure has no `&self`, and the window is operator-configurable, so it cannot be re-derived
5961        // from a literal at the call site.
5962        let surb_resolution_wait_for_listener = cfg.surb_resolution_wait;
5963        Self {
5964            msg_sender: msg_sender.clone(),
5965            session_initiations: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
5966                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
5967                .time_to_live(initiation_timeout)
5968                .build(),
5969            sessions: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
5970                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
5971                .time_to_idle(cfg.idle_timeout)
5972                .eviction_listener(move |session_id: Arc<SessionId>, entry: SessionSlot, reason| {
5973                    // The seam is captured at cache-build time rather than read from the
5974                    // manager here: this closure is not `&self`, and the eviction may fire
5975                    // long after the manager that built the cache has been cloned elsewhere.
5976                    let surb_admission = surb_admission_for_listener.get().cloned();
5977                    // The cache has already removed the slot, and the ledger is parked only by the
5978                    // `close_session` below. A client cannot learn of the close before that: its
5979                    // channel closes when the slot is dropped, and its tasks are aborted, both after
5980                    // the park in `release_session_slot`. Nor can a reconnect that comes on its own
5981                    // (after an outage that let the slot idle out, say) miss it: `new_session` runs the
5982                    // cache's pending tasks first, which evicts an expired slot and calls this
5983                    // listener on its own thread before the slot is looked up.
5984                    match &reason {
5985                        moka::notification::RemovalCause::Expired | moka::notification::RemovalCause::Size => {
5986                            trace!(?session_id, ?reason, "session evicted from the cache");
5987                            // Reconstructor state is released by `close_session` aborting the PIX
5988                            // action driver: the driver owns an `SsaCommitmentGuard` per live cycle,
5989                            // and dropping its future drops them. That bounds the release to the
5990                            // cycles actually in flight, where enumerating every index this Session
5991                            // had ever used was unbounded in its lifetime.
5992                            active_sessions_for_listener.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5993                            let token = entry.claim_admission_token();
5994                            close_session(
5995                                *session_id.as_ref(),
5996                                entry,
5997                                ClosureReason::Eviction,
5998                                surb_admission,
5999                                surb_retire_grace(surb_resolution_wait_for_listener),
6000                                token,
6001                            );
6002                        }
6003                        _ => {}
6004                    }
6005                })
6006                .build(),
6007            pix_toolbox,
6008            session_notifiers: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
6009            start_session_tx: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
6010            start_control_tx: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
6011            active_sessions,
6012            live_cycle_bytes: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),
6013            cfg,
6014            slot_allocated: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
6015            pending_outgoing: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
6016                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
6017                .time_to_live(initiation_timeout)
6018                .build(),
6019            incoming_openings: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
6020                .max_capacity(maximum_sessions as u64)
6021                .time_to_live(initiation_timeout)
6022                .build(),
6023            // Idle rather than live TTL, and generous: the entry only has to outlive the requests that
6024            // race for it, and one evicted between two cycles is simply recreated by the next request.
6025            // Matches the generator's own per-pseudonym cache, which is what the guarded region reads.
6026            ssa_request_locks: moka::future::Cache::builder()
6027                .time_to_idle(Duration::from_secs(1800))
6028                .build(),
6029            pix_ledgers: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
6030                .max_capacity((maximum_sessions as u64).saturating_mul(PIX_LEDGER_CAPACITY_FACTOR))
6031                .time_to_idle(PIX_LEDGER_IDLE_RETENTION)
6032                .build(),
6033            last_challenges: moka::sync::Cache::builder()
6034                .max_capacity((maximum_sessions as u64).saturating_mul(PIX_LEDGER_CAPACITY_FACTOR))
6035                .time_to_idle(PIX_LEDGER_IDLE_RETENTION)
6036                .build(),
6037            admission_tx: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
6038            surb_admission: surb_admission_in_struct,
6039            forward_receipt_sink: Arc::new(OnceLock::new()),
6040            admission_permits: Arc::new(hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::Semaphore::new(
6041                START_SESSION_ADMISSION_CONCURRENCY,
6042            )),
6043            refusal_replies,
6044        }
6045    }
6046
6047    /// Starts the instance with the given `msg_sender` `Sink`
6048    /// and a channel `new_session_notifier` used to notify when a new incoming session is opened to us.
6049    ///
6050    /// Optionally, the PIX processor and event sink can be provided for handling PIX protocol.
6051    /// If not specified, the `SessionManager` will not handle PIX protocol.
6052    ///
6053    /// `admission` is where incoming Sessions are put to the session server for a per-Session
6054    /// decision before they are established. Without it — an Entry, or a relay, or any caller that
6055    /// installed no session server — every Session is admitted on this node's own configured terms,
6056    /// which is the behaviour of a node that does not distinguish between targets.
6057    ///
6058    /// This method must be called prior to any calls to [`SessionManager::new_session`] or
6059    /// [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`].
6060    pub fn start<T>(
6061        &self,
6062        msg_sender: S,
6063        new_session_notifier: T,
6064        pix: Option<PixToolbox>,
6065        admission: Option<SessionAdmissionSink>,
6066    ) -> errors::Result<Vec<AbortHandle>>
6067    where
6068        T: futures::Sink<IncomingSession> + Send + 'static,
6069        T::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
6070    {
6071        // Every fallible check runs before the first `OnceLock::set` below.
6072        //
6073        // `start` publishes the manager's started state through those locks, and a `OnceLock` cannot
6074        // be un-set. Validating after `msg_sender` had been filled left a manager that reports
6075        // `is_started() == false` — no workers, no notifier — and yet refuses every retry with
6076        // `AlreadyStarted`: neither running nor recoverable, out of what is an ordinary configuration
6077        // error the caller could have corrected and retried on the same instance.
6078        if let Some(pix) = pix.as_ref() {
