7392                    "internal error: sender has been closed without completing the session establishment"
7393                ))
7394                .into())
7395            }
7396            Ok(Err(error)) => {
7397                // The other side did not allow us to establish a session
7398                let challenge = match error.identifier {
7399                    ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(c) => c,
7400                    ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(_) => {
7401                        // This arm should only ever receive pre-establishment errors.
7402                        // Log the id if it matters for debugging.
7403                        0
7404                    }
7405                };
7406                error!(
7407                    %challenge, ?error,
7408                    "the other party rejected the session initiation with error"
7409                );
7410                // The Exit cannot resume: forget the pseudonym's PIX state, so the next attempt is a fresh one.
7411                if error.reason == StartErrorReason::NotResumable
7412                    && resuming
7413                    && let Some(claim) = ledger_claim.as_mut()
7414                {
7415                    self.forget_pix_state(pseudonym, claim).await;
7416                }
7417                // A rejected initiation can never become a Session, so nothing legitimate can name
7418                // its pseudonym any more. `handle_session_error` removes the *challenge*, but only
7419                // this call knows the pseudonym the rejection was made under — which the guard
7420                // removes here.
7421                Err(TransportSessionError::Rejected(error.reason))
7422            }
7423            Err(_) => {
7424                // Timeout waiting for a session establishment
7425                error!(challenge, "session initiation attempt timed out");
7426
7427                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
7428                METRIC_RECEIVED_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&["timeout"]);
7429
7430                self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge);
7431                Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)
7432            }
7433        }
7434    }
7435
7436    /// Classifies an incoming `StartSession` as a repeat of an opening in flight, of an established Session, or new.
7437    ///
7438    /// The claim is put-if-absent and made before the slot is looked up, so an original finishing in between
7439    /// is still seen as established. A different challenge under a used pseudonym is not a repeat.
7440    fn claim_opening(&self, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, challenge: StartChallenge) -> OpeningClaim {
7441        use moka::ops::compute::{CompResult, Op};
7442
7443        let opening = Arc::new(InFlightOpening {
7444            challenge,
7445            pending: parking_lot::Mutex::new(Some(SurbsStored::default())),
7446        });
7447        let claim = self.incoming_openings.entry(pseudonym).and_compute_with(
7448            |entry: Option<moka::Entry<HoprPseudonym, Arc<InFlightOpening>>>| {
7449                if entry.is_none() {
7450                    Op::Put(opening.clone())
7451                } else {
7452                    Op::Nop
7453                }
7454            },
7455        );
7456        match claim {
7457            CompResult::Inserted(_) => {
7458                let guard = IncomingOpeningGuard {
7459                    openings: self.incoming_openings.clone(),
7460                    pseudonym,
7461                    opening,
7462                };
7463                match self.sessions.get(&pseudonym) {
7464                    // A detached or superseded instance has no data plane to confirm, so its repeat takes the
7465                    // ordinary path (a resume attempt is refused there as a duplicate, which the Entry retries).
7466                    Some(slot)
7467                        if slot
7468                            .opening
7469                            .as_ref()
7470                            .is_some_and(|opening| opening.challenge == challenge)
7471                            && !slot.is_detached()
7472                            && !slot.instance.is_superseded() =>
7473                    {
7474                        OpeningClaim::EstablishedRepeat(Box::new(slot), guard)
7475                    }
7476                    _ => OpeningClaim::New(Some(guard)),
7477                }
7478            }
7479            CompResult::Unchanged(entry) if entry.value().challenge == challenge => {
7480                OpeningClaim::InFlightRepeat(entry.into_value())
7481            }
7482            _ => OpeningClaim::New(None),
7483        }
7484    }
7485
7486    /// Adds a repeat's unbooked SURBs to the original's claim, or books them to the slot once the original has.
7487    fn carry_or_book_repeat_surbs(&self, opening: &InFlightOpening, pseudonym: &SessionId, stored: SurbsStored) {
7488        match &mut *opening.pending.lock() {
7489            Some(carried) => {
7490                carried.saved += stored.saved;
7491                carried.evicted += stored.evicted;
7492            }
7493            None => {
7494                if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(pseudonym) {
7495                    let _ = book_start_message_surbs(&slot, pseudonym, stored);
7496                }
7497            }
7498        }
7499    }
7500
7501    /// Answers a repeated `StartSession` for an established Session with `SessionEstablished` alone, up to a cap.
7502    async fn answer_repeated_opening(
7503        &self,
7504        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
7505        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
7506        slot: &SessionSlot,
7507    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
7508        crate::counters::START_SESSION_REPEATS_RECEIVED.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
7509        // As for the SSA re-send: a return packet that finds no SURB stalls everything this node originates.
7510        if slot.surb_estimator.saturating_diff() == 0 {
7511            debug!(
7512                challenge = session_req.challenge,
7513                "not answering a repeated session request: no SURB held"
7514            );
7515            return Ok(());
7516        }
7517        let answered = slot.opening.as_ref().map_or(MAX_ANSWERED_START_REPEATS, |opening| {
7518            opening.answered_repeats.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
7519        });
7520        if answered >= MAX_ANSWERED_START_REPEATS {
7521            debug!(
7522                challenge = session_req.challenge,
7523                "dropping a repeated session request past the cap"
7524            );
7525            return Ok(());
7526        }
7527
7528        info!(challenge = session_req.challenge, %pseudonym, "repeated session request — answering it again");
7529        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7530        // The repeat started a new SURB generation, so the oldest SURB left is its own. A resume attempt
7531        // is answered as it was the first time: a plain `SessionEstablished` would make the Entry refuse it.
7532        let answer = match slot.opening.as_ref().and_then(|opening| opening.resumed_stream_base) {
7533            Some(stream_base) => HoprStartProtocol::SessionResumed(StartResumed {
7534                orig_challenge: session_req.challenge,
7535                session_id: pseudonym,
7536                stream_base,
7537            }),
7538            None => HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(StartEstablished {
7539                orig_challenge: session_req.challenge,
7540                session_id: pseudonym,
7541            }),
7542        };
7543        count_exit_control_send(
7544            ExitControlKind::SessionEstablishedReplay,
7545            ExitSessionKind::of(session_req.capabilities.0),
7546            send_counted_via_msg_sender(
7547                &mut msg_sender,
7548                slot.routing_opts.clone(),
7549                answer,
7550                &slot.surb_estimator,
7551                &pseudonym,
7552                "repeated session establishment message",
7553            )
7554            .await,
7555        )
7556    }
7557
7558    /// When the next `StartSession` repeat is due, if one still is.
7559    ///
7560    /// Repeat `k` (from 0) goes out `interval * (2^(k+1) - 1)` after the first send, and only before `deadline`.
7561    fn next_initiation_resend(&self, started: Instant, resends: u32, deadline: Instant) -> Option<Instant> {
7562        if resends >= self.cfg.max_initiation_resends {
7563            return None;
7564        }
7565        let factor = 2_u32.saturating_pow(resends + 1) - 1;
7566        started
7567            .checked_add(self.cfg.initiation_resend_interval.saturating_mul(factor))
7568            .filter(|at| *at < deadline)
7569    }
7570
7571    /// Sends a keep-alive packet with the given [`SessionId`].
7572    ///
7573    /// This currently "fires & forgets" and does not expect nor await any "pong" response.
7574    ///
7575    /// The keep-alive is marked as a manual ping ([`KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing`]), so an Exit does not
7576    /// take it for a sign that this Session's Entry runs a SURB balancer: a ping, whatever SURBs it
7577    /// brings, starts neither the Exit's SURB-level reports nor the reserve it keeps for them. An Exit
7578    /// that predates the mark does take it for one.
7579    pub async fn ping_session(&self, id: &SessionId) -> errors::Result<()> {
7580        self.ping_session_scoped(id, None).await
7581    }
7582
7583    /// Same as [`ping_session`](Self::ping_session), but only if the slot under `id` is the slot instance
7584    /// `instance_id` (see [`HoprSession::slot_instance`]).
7585    ///
7586    /// For callers that hold a handle to one specific Session object: once its pseudonym is reused, a
7587    /// ping through that stale handle must not be sent over the successor Session. Fails with
7588    /// [`SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession`] when the slot is gone or belongs to another instance.
7589    pub async fn ping_session_instance(&self, id: &SessionId, instance_id: u64) -> errors::Result<()> {
7590        self.ping_session_scoped(id, Some(instance_id)).await
7591    }
7592
7593    async fn ping_session_scoped(&self, id: &SessionId, instance_id: Option<u64>) -> errors::Result<()> {
7594        let routing_opts = self
7595            .sessions
7596            .get(id)
7597            .filter(|s| instance_id.is_none_or(|i| s.instance.id() == i))
7598            .map(|s| s.routing_opts.clone());
7599        if let Some(routing_opts) = routing_opts {
7600            trace!(session_id = ?id, "pinging manually session");
7601            let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
7602            send_via_msg_sender(
7603                &mut msg_sender,
7604                routing_opts,
7605                HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
7606                    session_id: *id,
7607                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(),
7608                    additional_data: 0,
7609                }),
7610                "session ping message",
7611            )
7612            .await
7613            .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)
7614        } else {
7615            Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into())
7616        }
7617    }
7618
7619    /// Asks the deposit pool for the data to attach to a batch of SSAs, and collects its answers.
7620    ///
7621    /// A shortfall is told apart by its cause, because the causes call for different answers to the Entry.
7622    /// A request queue that is full or an answer that misses the deadline is the pool being too slow, a
7623    /// [`DepositPoolTooSlow`](SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow) that a retry may well get past. No
7624    /// listener, a reply channel the pool closed before it had answered everything, and answers for other
7625    /// SSAs are [`MissingDepositData`](SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData): faults of this node that a
7626    /// retry will meet again.
7627    async fn request_deposit_data(
7628        pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
7629        session_id: SessionId,
7630        ssa_indices: &[SsaIndex],
7631    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
7632        Self::request_deposit_data_within(pix_toolbox, session_id, ssa_indices, DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT).await
7633    }
7634
7635    /// [`request_deposit_data`](Self::request_deposit_data) with the deadline as a parameter, so that tests
7636    /// need not wait out the real one.
7637    async fn request_deposit_data_within(
7638        pix_toolbox: &PixToolbox,
7639        session_id: SessionId,
7640        ssa_indices: &[SsaIndex],
7641        deadline: Duration,
7642    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
7643        let deposit_ids = ssa_indices
7644            .iter()
7645            .map(|&ssa_index| PixAddressId::new(&session_id, ssa_index))
7646            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
7647
7648        let (deposit_data_created, deposit_data_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(ssa_indices.len().max(1));
7649
7650        if let Err(error) = pix_toolbox
7651            .pix_events
7652            .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest(PixDepositDataRequest {
7653                deposit_ids,
7654                deposit_data_created,
7655            }))
7656        {
7657            return Err(if matches!(error, crossfire::TrySendError::Full(_)) {
7658                SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow(format!(
7659                    "session {session_id} found the deposit data request queue full"
7660                ))
7661            } else {
7662                SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(format!(
7663                    "session {session_id} has no listener for the deposit data request"
7664                ))
7665            }
7666            .into());
7667        }
7668
7669        let asked = ssa_indices
7670            .iter()
7671            .map(|&ssa_index| PixAddressId::new(&session_id, ssa_index))
7672            .collect::<std::collections::HashSet<_>>();
7673        let mut outstanding = asked.clone();
7674        let requested = outstanding.len();
7675
7676        let mut deposit_data = HoprPixDepositData::with_capacity(requested);
7677        let mut foreign = 0usize;
7678        let timed_out = {
7679            let replies = deposit_data_rx
7680                .take(2 * requested)
7681                .take_until(futures_time::task::sleep(futures_time::time::Duration::from(deadline)));
7682            futures::pin_mut!(replies);
7683            while let Some(entry) = replies.next().await {
7684                if !asked.contains(&entry.id) {
7685                    foreign += 1;
7686                }
7687                outstanding.remove(&entry.id);
7688                deposit_data.push(entry);
7689                if outstanding.is_empty() {
7690                    break;
7691                }
7692            }
7693            // Set only when the deadline resolved; `is_stopped` is also true once the stream itself ended.
7694            replies.take_result().is_some()
7695        };
7696
7697        // Counted here rather than left to `deposit_data_for_batch`, which sees the same shortfall
7698        // but cannot tell a pool that went quiet from one that answered about the wrong SSAs. Only
7699        // the first is fixed by making the pool faster.
7700        if !outstanding.is_empty() {
7701            let detail = format!(
7702                "session {session_id} got {} of {requested} requested deposit data entries ({} replies read in total, \
7703                 {foreign} for other SSAs)",
7704                requested - outstanding.len(),
7705                deposit_data.len(),
7706            );
7707            return Err(if foreign > 0 {
7708                SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(format!("{detail}: the pool answered for other SSAs"))
7709            } else if timed_out {
7710                SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow(format!("{detail}: not within {deadline:?}"))
7711            } else {
7712                SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(format!(
7713                    "{detail}: the pool stopped answering before it had answered them all"
7714                ))
7715            }
7716            .into());
7717        }
7718
7719        Ok(deposit_data)
7720    }
7721
7722    /// Spawns the task that carries out one Session's supervisor actions.
7723    ///
7724    /// The supervisor decides; this executes. Keeping the two apart is what lets the state machine
7725    /// be pure and exhaustively tested, and it means every side effect a PIX Session can have is
7726    /// visible in one `match`.
7727    ///
7728    /// The task owns an [`SsaCommitmentGuard`] per SSA it has requested and one Session retirement
7729    /// scope. Terminal actions retire through the frontier before releasing their guard; aborting
7730    /// the task drops every remaining guard and then the Session's compact frontier. No state grows
7731    /// with the number of cycles the Session completed.
7732    fn spawn_pix_action_driver(
7733        &self,
7734        session_id: SessionId,
7735        slot: &SessionSlot,
7736        action_rx: ActionRx,
7737        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
7738    ) -> hopr_utils::runtime::AbortHandle {
7739        let myself = self.clone();
7740        let gate = slot
7741            .pix_egress_gate
7742            .get()
7743            .cloned()
7744            .expect("the gate is installed before the driver is spawned");
7745        let share_processor = self
7746            .pix_toolbox
7747            .get()
7748            .expect("the PIX toolbox is installed before a PIX action driver is spawned")
7749            .share_processor
7750            .clone();
7751        let retirement_scope = share_processor.begin_retirement_scope(session_id);
7752        // Captured rather than looked up per report: the lookup that finds a slot refreshes its idle
7753        // timer, and the one arm that must not do that is the re-send of an unanswered request.
7754        let supervisor = slot.pix_supervisor.get().cloned();
7755        // This driver's control plane. Every lookup below by pseudonym acts on the slot found only if
7756        // it carries it, so a driver outliving its Session cannot touch a fresh one under the same
7757        // pseudonym.
7758        let control_plane = slot.pix_supervisor.clone();
7759        // Shares its counters with the slot's, so reading it needs no lookup either. The re-send arm
7760        // asks it whether the Session holds a SURB to send over at all.
7761        let surb_estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
7762
7763        hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
7764            let _retirement_scope = retirement_scope;
7765            // The vector owns each registration until a terminal action explicitly retires it or
7766            // dropping this future releases it during whole-Session teardown.
7767            let mut owned_ssas: Vec<SsaCommitmentGuard<HoprPixSpec>> = Vec::new();
7768            // The batch most recently put on the wire, with the exact message that carried it.
7769            //
7770            // What `ResendSsaRequest` sends again. Kept rather than rebuilt because a rebuilt request is
7771            // not the same request: its Exit secrets are random, so it would commit the Exit to a
7772            // different set than the one registered, and the deposit pool answers a batch once. Only the
7773            // latest batch is kept — the supervisor re-sends only an unanswered one, and a batch is
7774            // requested only after the one before it has been answered. Dropped when a member is
7775            // retired, since a request for a registration that no longer exists can only be refused.
7776            let mut last_request: Option<LastSsaRequest> = None;
7777
7778            let close_reason = loop {
7779                let Ok(action) = action_rx.recv().await else {
7780                    // The worker is gone without having said why, which is a failure of the
7781                    // supervisor itself rather than of the Session it was watching.
7782                    break Some(SessionPixCloseReason::SupervisorUnavailable);
7783                };
7784
7785                match action {
7786                    SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params } => {
7787                        let Some(slot) = myself.slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane) else {
7788                            // The Session went away underneath us; report the failure so the
7789                            // supervisor stops waiting on an action that can never complete.
7790                            myself
7791                                .report_ssa_request(
7792                                    &session_id,
7793                                    &control_plane,
7794                                    SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params },
7795                                    false,
7796                                )
7797                                .await;
7798                            continue;
7799                        };
7800                        match myself.send_ssa_request(session_id, &slot, &ssa_ids, params).await {
7801                            Ok((guards, request)) => {
7802                                owned_ssas.extend(guards);
7803                                last_request = Some((ssa_ids.clone(), request));
7804                                // The deadline starts when the supervisor sees the event below, and the
7805                                // send took time: refresh again so the answer has the whole lifetime.
7806                                refresh_registrations(&share_processor, &ssa_ids);
7807                                // One confirmation per index: the supervisor arms each cycle's
7808                                // commitment deadline on its own `SsaRequestSent`, and they were all
7809                                // put on the wire by the one send that just succeeded.
7810                                if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
7811                                    for ssa_id in &ssa_ids {
7812                                        if supervisor
7813                                            .send_event(SessionPixEvent::SsaRequestSent(*ssa_id))
7814                                            .await
7815                                            .is_err()
7816                                        {
7817                                            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting events");
7818                                            break;
7819                                        }
7820                                    }
7821                                }
7822                            }
7823                            Err(error) => {
7824                                // Every guard was dropped by the early return inside
7825                                // `send_ssa_request`, so the whole batch of indices is released — none
7826                                // of them is left registered for a cycle that will never be asked for.
7827                                error!(
7828                                    %session_id, %error, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(),
7829                                    "failed to send ssa request"
7830                                );
7831
7832                                // A pool that could not supply deposit data ends the Session here
7833                                // rather than reporting the failure onwards. The other failures are
7834                                // transient or already self-correcting, and the supervisor is the
7835                                // right judge of them; this one is neither. The data only ever
7836                                // travels in the `SsaRequest` that carries the commitments, so it
7837                                // cannot be supplied later, and this Session cannot go on without it.
7838                                //
7839                                // A pool that missed the deadline, had a full request queue, or
7840                                // answered after the registrations lapsed is too slow for now. That is
7841                                // local and transient: the Entry is told the Exit is busy and may
7842                                // retry, and nothing blames the supervisor.
7843                                if matches!(
7844                                    error,
7845                                    TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow(_))
7846                                ) {
7847                                    myself.stop_pix_fill(&session_id, &control_plane);
7848                                    gate.poison();
7849                                    owned_ssas.clear();
7850                                    myself
7851                                        .close_session_scoped_and_notify(
7852                                            &session_id,
7853                                            ClosureReason::DepositPoolTooSlow,
7854                                            &control_plane,
7855                                            reply_routing.clone(),
7856                                            StartErrorReason::Busy,
7857                                            "session error due to a deposit pool too slow for the registrations",
7858                                        )
7859                                        .await;
7860                                    return;
7861                                }
7862
7863                                // No listener, a pool that failed to generate some entries, or answers
7864                                // for other SSAs are faults of this Exit that a retry would meet again,
7865                                // so the Entry is told with a permanent reason and does not retry.
7866                                //
7867                                // Named rather than folded into the supervisor's `PixFailure`,
7868                                // because it points at this node's own pool while every reason the
7869                                // supervisor has points at the peer. Locally the closure keeps its own
7870                                // reason, so the metrics tell it from a pool that was too slow.
7871                                if matches!(
7872                                    error,
7873                                    TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(_))
7874                                ) {
7875                                    myself.stop_pix_fill(&session_id, &control_plane);
7876                                    gate.poison();
7877                                    owned_ssas.clear();
7878                                    myself
7879                                        .close_session_scoped_and_notify(
7880                                            &session_id,
7881                                            ClosureReason::MissingDepositData,
7882                                            &control_plane,
7883                                            reply_routing.clone(),
7884                                            StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
7885                                            "session error due to missing deposit data",
7886                                        )
7887                                        .await;
7888                                    return;
7889                                }
7890
7891                                if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get()
7892                                    && supervisor
7893                                        .send_action_result(
7894                                            // Only the discriminant and the ids are read on the
7895                                            // failure path, so the dimensions are echoed back
7896                                            // rather than zeroed — `PixParams` has no zero value,
7897                                            // and inventing one would be a lie about what was sent.
7898                                            SessionPixAction::RequestSsa { ssa_ids, params },
7899                                            false,
7900                                        )
7901                                        .await
7902                                        .is_err()
7903                                {
7904                                    error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
7905                                }
7906                            }
7907                        }
7908                    }
7909                    SessionPixAction::RequestCommitmentRetransmission { ssa_id, params } => {
7910                        // Failure is logged and dropped rather than reported back. Unlike
7911                        // `RequestSsa` this action is not a step the Session depends on: it repeats
7912                        // on its own interval, and the commitment deadline is still the backstop, so
7913                        // a dropped ask costs one interval rather than the Session.
7914                        if let Some(slot) = myself.slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane)
7915                            && let Err(error) = myself
7916                                .send_commitment_retransmission_request(session_id, &slot, ssa_id, params)
7917                                .await
7918                        {
7919                            error!(%session_id, %ssa_id, %error, "failed to re-request ssa commitment parts");
7920                        }
7921                    }
7922                    SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest { ssa_ids } => {
7923                        // `contains_key` rather than `get`, which would refresh the Session's idle
7924                        // timer: a Session that is otherwise dead would then be kept alive by its own
7925                        // re-sends for as long as the predecessor's clocks run. The routing needs no
7926                        // slot — it is the reply routing this driver was spawned with.
7927                        // A torn-down plane is checked first: `contains_key` is true for a successor.
7928                        if control_plane.is_torn_down() || !myself.sessions.contains_key(&session_id) {
7929                            continue;
7930                        }
7931
7932                        // Never `send_ssa_request`: it registers a fresh Exit commitment, which the
7933                        // reconstructor refuses as a duplicate of the pending one, and its failure
7934                        // path closes the Session as `SupervisorUnavailable`. A re-send is allowed to
7935                        // fail without costing the Session anything.
7936                        //
7937                        // Deciding also reads each member's registration, which is what keeps it from
7938                        // idling out after `incomplete_commitment_lifetime`: a pending registration
7939                        // is not refreshed by anything else while the Entry is silent. A batch that
7940                        // is not the last one sent, or whose registration is gone or complete, can
7941                        // only be refused, so it is not sent.
7942                        let message = match resend_payload(last_request.as_ref(), &ssa_ids, &share_processor) {
7943                            ResendDecision::Send(message) => message,
7944                            refusal => {
7945                                tracing::debug!(
7946                                    %session_id, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(), ?refusal,
7947                                    "cannot re-send the SSA request"
7948                                );
7949                                if let Some(supervisor) = supervisor.as_ref()
7950                                    && supervisor
7951                                        .send_action_result(SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest { ssa_ids }, false)
7952                                        .await
7953                                        .is_err()
7954                                {
7955                                    tracing::error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
7956                                }
7957                                continue;
7958                            }
7959                        };
7960
7961                        // A re-send is best-effort, and a return packet that finds no SURB is retried
7962                        // for up to `surb_resolution_wait` while everything else this node originates
7963                        // queues behind it, so one is not sent while the Session holds none. The
7964                        // estimate is trustworthy for this because the Exit counts its control sends
7965                        // (`SessionEstablished`, the SSA requests) as consumed, like its data. The
7966                        // registration was refreshed above all the same. Nothing is reported back: the
7967                        // attempt counts against the supervisor's cap and the next one tries again.
7968                        if surb_estimator.saturating_diff() == 0 {
7969                            tracing::debug!(
7970                                %session_id, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(),
7971                                "skipping the SSA request re-send — the Session holds no SURB to send it over"
7972                            );
7973                            record_exit_control(
7974                                ExitControlKind::SsaRequestResend,
7975                                ExitSessionKind::Pix,
7976                                ExitControlOutcome::SkippedNoSurb,
7977                            );
7978                            continue;
7979                        }
7980
7981                        // Failure is logged and dropped, as for the re-request above, and nothing is
7982                        // reported back: the supervisor pushed the batch's deadline when it emitted
7983                        // this and will emit another on its next tick. `SsaRequestSent` is not sent
7984                        // either — the batch was confirmed when it was first requested.
7985                        match myself.msg_sender.get().cloned() {
7986                            Some(mut msg_sender) => {
7987                                if let Err(error) = count_exit_control_send(
7988                                    ExitControlKind::SsaRequestResend,
7989                                    ExitSessionKind::Pix,
7990                                    send_counted_via_msg_sender(
7991                                        &mut msg_sender,
7992                                        reply_routing.clone(),
7993                                        message.clone(),
7994                                        &surb_estimator,
7995                                        &session_id,
7996                                        "re-sent session SSA commitment request message",
7997                                    )
7998                                    .await,
7999                                ) {
8000                                    tracing::error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to re-send the ssa request");
8001                                }
8002                            }
8003                            None => {
8004                                tracing::error!(%session_id, "cannot re-send the ssa request - manager not started")
8005                            }
8006                        }
8007                    }
8008                    SessionPixAction::ReleaseService => {
8009                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8010                        crate::telemetry::set_pix_gate_mode(&session_id, true);
8011                    }
8012                    SessionPixAction::WithholdService => {
8013                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8014                        crate::telemetry::set_pix_gate_mode(&session_id, false);
8015                    }
8016                    // Gate control is applied synchronously by the supervisor worker. The action
8017                    // reaches this I/O driver only to preserve observability and ordering, which
8018                    // makes it the one periodic point with the reconstructor in hand: refresh the
8019                    // node-wide occupancy gauge here. The walk covers every live cycle on the node and
8020                    // notifications come per acknowledgement batch per Session, so it runs at most once
8021                    // a second node-wide (`HELD_SHARES_REFRESH_PERIOD`), not on every notification.
8022                    // Progress behind the front asks for the same refresh, with nothing for the gate.
8023                    SessionPixAction::ProgressNotification | SessionPixAction::RefreshHeldShares =>
8024                    {
8025                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8026                        if crate::telemetry::pix::held_shares_refresh_due() {
8027                            crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
8028                        }
8029                    }
8030                    SessionPixAction::SetFillRate(rate) => {
8031                        // Looked up per action rather than captured, because the Session may already
8032                        // be gone: the supervisor plans against state it holds itself, and the slot
8033                        // can be evicted underneath it. A missing slot needs no rate — its stream is
8034                        // already aborted.
8035                        if let Some(slot) = myself.slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane)
8036                            && let Some(fill) = slot.pix_fill.get()
8037                        {
8038                            fill.set_fill(rate);
8039                            // Inside the guard for the same reason the lookup is: `close_session`
8040                            // removes this Session's metric state and *then* aborts the tasks, and
8041                            // the abort is not synchronous, so a queued `SetFillRate` can still be
8042                            // processed afterwards. Setting the gauge there would re-create the
8043                            // `session_id` label series with nothing left to remove it again.
8044                            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8045                            crate::telemetry::set_pix_fill_rate(&session_id, rate.as_packets_per_sec());
8046                        }
8047                    }
8048                    SessionPixAction::RetireSsa(ssa_id) => {
8049                        share_processor.retire_ssa(ssa_id);
8050                        // The retired cycle's shares are gone, and nothing else refreshes the gauge
8051                        // until another notification comes due, which a node with no other PIX
8052                        // Session may never send. Retirement is once per cycle, so unthrottled.
8053                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8054                        crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
8055                        owned_ssas.retain(|guard| guard.ssa_id() != Some(&ssa_id));
8056                        forget_request_of(&mut last_request, &ssa_id);
8057                        if let Some(slot) = myself.slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane) {
8058                            slot.abort_handles
8059                                .lock()
8060                                .abort_one(&SessionHandles::PixDepositObserver(ssa_id.ssa_index().get()));
8061                        }
8062                    }
8063                    SessionPixAction::Close(reason) => break Some(reason),
8064                }
8065            };
8066
8067            let Some(reason) = close_reason else {
8068                // The cycles this driver holds go with it; see the refresh after the teardown below.
8069                owned_ssas.clear();
8070                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8071                crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
8072                return;
8073            };
8074
8075            // Read before `stop_pix_fill`, which silences the stream either way. Keyed on the drain
8076            // rather than on the reason, which is a strict superset of it: a *stalled* drain closes
8077            // with `RecoveryIdle` or `RecoveryDeadline`, and that is likewise the ordinary end of a
8078            // Session an operator has already closed rather than something to page anyone about.
8079            let draining = myself
8080                .slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane)
8081                .is_some_and(|slot| slot.pix_fill.get().is_some_and(|fill| fill.is_draining()));
8082            if draining {
8083                info!(%session_id, %reason, "pix supervisor ended the post-close SURB drain");
8084            } else {
8085                error!(%session_id, %reason, "pix supervisor closed the session");
8086            }
8087
8088            // Unblock anything parked on the gate before tearing down: the supervisor that would
8089            // have woken it is the thing that just stopped. Fill is silenced alongside it, and for a
8090            // sharper reason — the gate holds packets back, while fill would go on *originating*
8091            // them, return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are about to be gone.
8092            myself.stop_pix_fill(&session_id, &control_plane);
8093            gate.poison();
8094            owned_ssas.clear();
8095            // Releasing the guards removed the Session's cycles from the reconstructor; refresh the
8096            // gauge now rather than leave their shares counted until another Session's notification.
8097            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8098            crate::telemetry::pix::set_held_shares(share_processor.held_shares());
8099
8100            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8101            crate::telemetry::pix::record_pix_closure(reason);
8102
8103            // Return this Session's share of the node-level aggregates now, rather than leaving it
8104            // to `close_session` below. The notification between here and there is a network send
8105            // with its own timeout, and for the whole of it the Session is closed — its supervisor
8106            // has stopped and its gate is poisoned — while `hopr_pix_sessions_active` would still
8107            // be counting it. Idempotent, so `close_session` remains the backstop for every other
8108            // path into it.
8109            if let Some(slot) = myself.slot_of_control_plane(&session_id, &control_plane)
8110                && let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get()
8111            {
8112                supervisor.telemetry.release();
8113            }
8114
8115            // Tell the Entry, so it can drop its side rather than wait out its own timeout. The
8116            // Session is closed either way, so a send failure here changes nothing.
8117            //
8118            // Except after a drain, where the Session the report would be about is already gone and
8119            // the report is return-routed: sending it would spend a SURB out of a buffer that may
8120            // already be empty, which is precisely the origination this whole path exists to avoid.
8121            // It would also be new behaviour rather than preserved behaviour, since an Exit-side
8122            // close sends the Entry nothing today — and `draining` is set before the supervisor's
8123            // verdict, so this covers a refused drain as well as a completed one.
8124            //
8125            // Sent only for a slot this teardown removed, and addressed by that slot, so that a successor
8126            // which took the slot meanwhile is not named. Before the slot's tasks are stopped, which include
8127            // this one.
8128            if let Some(slot) = remove_slot_if(&myself.sessions, &session_id, |slot| {
8129                Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.pix_supervisor, &control_plane)
8130            }) {
8131                myself.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
8132                if !draining {
8133                    myself
8134                        .notify_session_error(
8135                            session_id,
8136                            error_identifier_of(&slot, &session_id),
8137                            reply_routing,
8138                            StartErrorReason::Unknown,
8139                            "session error after pix failure",
8140                        )
8141                        .await;
8142                }
8143                let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
8144                close_session(
8145                    session_id,
8146                    slot,
8147                    ClosureReason::PixFailure,
8148                    myself.surb_admission.get().cloned(),
8149                    surb_retire_grace(myself.cfg.surb_resolution_wait),
8150                    token,
8151                );
8152            }
8153        })
8154    }
8155
8156    /// Starts the Exit's single Exit → Entry keep-alive stream and installs the handle that steers it.
8157    ///
8158    /// Called for every PIX Session, and for any Session with a configured
8159    /// `surb_balance_notify_period` — the SURB-level notification and PIX fill are the same packet
8160    /// sent for different reasons, so they share one stream and one rate controller. See
8161    /// [`PixFillControl`].
8162    ///
8163    /// Returns without spawning anything when neither producer applies, which is an Exit Session that
8164    /// is not PIX on a node that has switched the notification off. Such a Session originates nothing,
8165    /// which is what it did before this existed.
8166    ///
8167    /// The notification is not sent to just any Entry. A report spends one of the Session's SURBs, and
8168    /// an Entry with no SURB balancer reads nothing: it attaches a SURB to each data packet and sends
8169    /// no keep-alives. [`PixFillControl::admit`] therefore lets a report out only once the Entry has
8170    /// shown that it refills (by a keep-alive, flagged or not, but not a manual ping) and the Exit's own estimate shows
8171    /// a SURB to spend on it. That is decided per packet rather than here, once, because the evidence arrives
8172    /// after the Session is established.
8173    ///
8174    /// Deliberately not passed through the PIX egress gate. These packets carry no payload; gating
8175    /// them would let an exhausted predeposit budget silence the very signal the Entry needs in order
8176    /// to fund the Session, turning a stall into a teardown. The bound that does apply is
8177    /// [`PixFillControl::admit`]'s SURB reserve, which is about this node's own ability to send at
8178    /// all rather than about what the peer has paid for.
8179    ///
8180    /// `announced.surb_target` is the SURB buffer target the Entry asked for, and it is what that
8181    /// reserve is derived against — see [`effective_surb_reserve`]. It has to be, because the
8182    /// configured reserve is an absolute count while the buffer it is measured against is the Entry's
8183    /// choice; a Session whose Entry asks for a shallower buffer than the configured reserve could
8184    /// otherwise never be filled at all.
8185    ///
8186    /// That derivation is only the establishment figure: the Entry may change its target later with a
8187    /// `BalancerTarget` keep-alive, and [`handle_keep_alive`](Self::handle_keep_alive) re-derives the
8188    /// reserve from it then. The configured ceiling is passed through so that re-derivation uses the
8189    /// same one this derivation does.
8190    fn spawn_exit_keep_alive(
8191        &self,
8192        session_id: SessionId,
8193        slot: &SessionSlot,
8194        msg_sender: S,
8195        is_pix: bool,
8196        announced: EntryAnnouncement,
8197        loss_signal: Option<Arc<FrameLossSignal>>,
8198    ) {
8199        let notify_period = self.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period;
8200        if notify_period.is_none() && !is_pix {
8201            return;
8202        }
8203
8204        // Only when it actually reports faster: a degraded period at or above the normal one would be
8205        // a switch that changes nothing. `notify_period` being `None` already makes it inapplicable.
8206        let degraded_period = self
8207            .cfg
8208            .surb_degraded_notify_period
8209            .filter(|degraded| notify_period.is_some_and(|normal| *degraded < normal));
8210
8211        let configured_reserve = self.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill.min_surb_reserve;
8212        let min_surb_reserve = effective_surb_reserve(configured_reserve, announced.surb_target);
8213
8214        // Created here and shared: the sink wrapper below has to hold the same control the stream is
8215        // rate-limited by, so that it can tell a notification packet from a fill packet.
8216        let controller = RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1));
8217        let control = Arc::new(
8218            PixFillControl::new(
8219                session_id,
8220                controller.clone(),
8221                notify_period,
8222                degraded_period,
8223                SurbReserveBasis {
8224                    configured: configured_reserve,
8225                    establishment_target: announced.surb_target,
8226                },
8227                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
8228                slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
8229            )
8230            .with_idle_notify_period(announced.idle_notify_cap)
8231            .for_session(if is_pix {
8232                ExitSessionKind::Pix
8233            } else {
8234                ExitSessionKind::Plain
8235            }),
8236        );
8237
8238        let control_for_admission = control.clone();
8239        let surb_estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
8240        let ka_abort_handle = utils::spawn_keep_alive_stream(
8241            session_id,
8242            // Consumption is counted in the sink rather than at the rate limiter, so it counts what
8243            // was actually sent: a packet the admission predicate dropped consumed no SURB, and
8244            // counting it would walk the Exit's own level estimate down until it starved itself of
8245            // the very reserve that dropped it.
8246            msg_sender.with(move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
8247                let data = count_return_packet_surb(&surb_estimator, data);
8248                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8249                telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
8250                futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
8251            }),
8252            slot.routing_opts.clone(),
8253            SurbNotificationMode::Level(slot.surb_estimator.clone()),
8254            slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
8255            &controller,
8256            move || control_for_admission.admit(),
8257        );
8258
8259        slot.abort_handles
8260            .lock()
8261            .insert(SessionHandles::KeepAlive, ka_abort_handle);
8262        let _ = slot.pix_fill.set(control.clone());
8263
8264        if let Some(period) = notify_period {
8265            // Delayed by one period, as it always was: a Session that closes immediately should not
8266            // have sent a level report about SURBs it never used. Fill is not held behind this — the
8267            // supervisor's first rate applies the moment it is planned.
8268            //
8269            // Registered so `close_session` can abort it. It is a one-shot, but it holds a clone of
8270            // the control for the whole period, and nothing bounds how long an operator may make that.
8271            let notify_control = control.clone();
8272            let notify_delay = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
8273                hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(period).await;
8274                notify_control.start_notify();
8275            });
8276            slot.abort_handles
8277                .lock()
8278                .insert(SessionHandles::SurbNotifyDelay, notify_delay);
8279        }
8280
8281        // No notification period means nothing to make faster, and `degraded_period` is already `None`
8282        // in that case; the driver needs both a period to speed up and a signal that says when.
8283        if let (Some(degraded_period), Some(loss_signal)) = (degraded_period, loss_signal) {
8284            let driver_control = control.clone();
8285            let surb_estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
8286            let surb_mgmt = slot.surb_mgmt.clone();
8287            let driver = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
8288                // The normal start path is kept: until the one-shot delay has turned the notification
8289                // on there is no period to be faster than, so the driver waits for it rather than
8290                // counting the same period out again from its own start. A drain clears
8291                // `notify_started` for good, so that is also where the driver stops waiting — there is
8292                // no notification left for it to be faster than.
8293                loop {
8294                    if driver_control.is_draining() {
8295                        return;
8296                    }
8297                    if driver_control.notify_started() {
8298                        break;
8299                    }
8300                    hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(SURB_DEGRADED_POLL).await;
8301                }
8302                let mut switch = DegradedSwitch::default();
8303                loop {
8304                    // A drain silences the notification outright, and the driver holds a clone of the
8305                    // control for as long as it runs: stop rather than outlive the stream it steers.
8306                    if driver_control.is_draining() {
8307                        return;
8308                    }
8309                    let recently_stalled =
8310                        switch.note_stall(loss_signal.stalled_for(SURB_DEGRADED_STALL), Instant::now());
8311                    let next =
8312                        exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&loss_signal, &surb_estimator, &surb_mgmt, recently_stalled);
8313                    // Degraded by frames that stalled is a dark forward path, which reports faster still
8314                    // (`SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD`); degraded by loss alone keeps the degraded period.
8315                    let dark = next && recently_stalled;
8316                    if let Some(next) = switch.change_to(next) {
8317                        debug!(
8318                            %session_id,
8319                            degraded = next,
8320                            dark,
8321                            ?degraded_period,
8322                            stock = surb_estimator.saturating_diff(),
8323                            reserve = current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&surb_mgmt),
8324                            "switched the exit SURB-level notification cadence"
8325                        );
8326                        driver_control.set_degraded(next);
8327                    }
8328                    if let Some(dark) = switch.change_dark_to(dark) {
8329                        debug!(%session_id, dark, "switched the exit SURB-level notification's dark cadence");
8330                        driver_control.set_dark(dark);
8331                    }
8332                    hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(SURB_DEGRADED_POLL).await;
8333                }
8334            });
8335            slot.abort_handles
8336                .lock()
8337                .insert(SessionHandles::SurbNotifyDegraded, driver);
8338        }
8339
8340        // An order of magnitude is the point at which the operator's intent and the Session's shape
8341        // have stopped being about the same deployment. A configured reserve of `R` is a reserve
8342        // sized for a buffer of `4R`; the derivation only lowers it tenfold once the Entry announces
8343        // under `4R / 10`, so this fires exactly on a Session whose buffer is an order of magnitude
8344        // shallower than the one this node was configured against. Fill still runs — a derived
8345        // reserve is strictly better than one that refuses every packet forever — but it is worth
8346        // saying out loud once, when the stream starts, rather than once per withheld packet.
8347        if min_surb_reserve.saturating_mul(10) < configured_reserve {
8348            warn!(
8349                %session_id,
8350                configured = configured_reserve,
8351                effective = min_surb_reserve,
8352                announced_surb_target = announced.surb_target,
8353                "the PIX fill SURB reserve was lowered by more than an order of magnitude to fit the SURB buffer \
8354                 target the entry announced for this session"
8355            );
8356        }
8357
8358        debug!(
8359            %session_id, ?notify_period, is_pix,
8360            surb_reserve = min_surb_reserve,
8361            announced_surb_target = announced.surb_target,
8362            "started the exit keep-alive stream"
8363        );
8364    }
8365
8366    /// Starts the task that sends the Session's forward receipts to the Entry, if the Entry asked for them.
8367    ///
8368    /// Sends only while the Entry refills SURBs, the stock is above the keep-alive reserve and PIX is not
8369    /// draining, and counts each receipt like a keep-alive.
8370    fn spawn_exit_forward_receipts(&self, session_id: SessionId, slot: &SessionSlot, msg_sender: S) {
8371        let Some(receipts) = slot.forward_receipts.clone() else {
8372            return;
8373        };
8374        let Some(mut woken) = receipts.take_wake() else {
8375            return;
8376        };
8377        let (estimator, balancer, fill) = (
8378            slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
8379            slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
8380            slot.pix_fill.clone(),
8381        );
8382        let routing = slot.routing_opts.clone();
8383        let mut sender = {
8384            let estimator = estimator.clone();
8385            msg_sender.with(move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
8386                let data = count_return_packet_surb(&estimator, data);
8387                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
8388                telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
8389                futures::future::ok::<_, S::Error>((routing, data))
8390            })
8391        };
8392
8393        let handle = hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
8394            loop {
8395                // Also when an interval fills up, so that a fast Session does not overflow it, or a burst window
8396                // opens; and faster while it is open
8397                let poll = if receipts.burst_open_at(Instant::now()) {
8398                    BURST_POLL
8399                } else {
8400                    FORWARD_RECEIPT_POLL
8401                };
8402                futures::select! {
8403                    _ = futures::FutureExt::fuse(hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(poll)) => {}
8404                    _ = futures::StreamExt::next(&mut woken) => {}
8405                }
8406                if !balancer.counterparty_refills()
8407                    || estimator.saturating_diff() <= current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer)
8408                    || fill.get().is_some_and(|control| control.is_draining())
8409                {
8410                    continue;
8411                }
8412                let Some(Receipt { seq, first_seq, tags }) = receipts.take_due(Instant::now()) else {
8413                    continue;
8414                };
8415                let count = tags.len();
8416                // Two copies inside a burst window, where the receipts are the ones that judge and the paths are
8417                // not yet known to be good, if the stock stays above the reserve after the first
8418                let copies = if receipts.burst_open_at(Instant::now())
8419                    && estimator.saturating_diff() > current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer) + 1
8420                {
8421                    2
8422                } else {
8423                    1
8424                };
8425                for copy in 0..copies {
8426                    // Data sent meanwhile may have used the stock the second copy was counted on
8427                    if copy > 0 && estimator.saturating_diff() <= current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&balancer) {
8428                        break;
8429                    }
8430                    let msg = HoprStartProtocol::ForwardReceipts(ForwardReceiptsMessage {
8431                        session_id,
8432                        seq,
8433                        first_seq,
8434                        tags: tags.clone(),
8435                    });
8436                    match send_via_msg_sender(&mut sender, routing.clone(), msg, "forward receipts").await {
8437                        Ok(()) => {
8438                            FORWARD_RECEIPTS_SENT.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
8439                            debug!(%session_id, seq, first_seq, tags = count, "forward receipts sent");
8440                        }
8441                        Err(error) => debug!(%session_id, %error, "failed to send forward receipts"),
8442                    }
8443                }
8444            }
8445        });
8446        slot.abort_handles
8447            .lock()
8448            .insert(SessionHandles::ForwardReceipts, handle);
8449    }
8450
8451    /// The slot under `session_id`, if it is driven by `control_plane` (see [`PixControlPlane`]).
8452    ///
8453    /// A lookup that refreshes the slot's idle timer, like any `get`; skipped once the plane is torn
8454    /// down, so a stale driver cannot refresh a successor's timer.
8455    fn slot_of_control_plane(&self, session_id: &SessionId, control_plane: &PixControlPlane) -> Option<SessionSlot> {
8456        if control_plane.is_torn_down() {
8457            return None;
8458        }
8459        self.sessions
8460            .get(session_id)
8461            .filter(|slot| Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.pix_supervisor, control_plane))
8462    }
8463
8464    /// Silences a Session's PIX fill, leaving its SURB-level notification alone.
8465    ///
8466    /// Called on every path that is about to tear a Session down. `close_session` aborts the stream
8467    /// outright, so this is not what stops it — it is what stops the *extra* traffic in the window
8468    /// between a supervisor deciding the Session is over and the teardown reaching the stream. Every
8469    /// packet originated in that window is return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are gone, and one
8470    /// packet the routing resolver cannot resolve holds up every packet this node originates.
8471    ///
8472    /// Acts only on the slot `control_plane` drives (see [`PixControlPlane`]): the driver of a torn-down
8473    /// Session must not silence the fill of a fresh one under the same pseudonym.
8474    fn stop_pix_fill(&self, session_id: &SessionId, control_plane: &PixControlPlane) {
8475        if let Some(slot) = self.slot_of_control_plane(session_id, control_plane)
8476            && let Some(fill) = slot.pix_fill.get()
8477        {
8478            fill.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
8479        }
8480    }
8481
8482    /// Reports an action outcome to the supervisor of `control_plane`, if it has one.
8483    ///
8484    /// Never looked up by pseudonym, which could find a successor Session's supervisor.
8485    async fn report_ssa_request(
8486        &self,
8487        session_id: &SessionId,
8488        control_plane: &PixControlPlane,
8489        action: SessionPixAction,
8490        ok: bool,
8491    ) {
8492        if let Some(supervisor) = control_plane.get()
8493            && supervisor.send_action_result(action, ok).await.is_err()
8494        {
8495            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor stopped accepting results");
8496        }
8497    }
8498
8499    /// Best-effort `SessionError` for an already-established Session, identified by its `SessionId`.
8500    ///
8501    /// Best-effort in the strict sense: the outcome is logged and discarded. Every caller is on a path
8502    /// that has already decided the Session is over, so there is nothing a failed send could change —
8503    /// and the peer has a deadline of its own as the backstop either way. What the notice buys is
8504    /// promptness and attribution: the peer tears down in about a round trip, with the reason in its
8505    /// log, instead of waiting out a timer that names the timer rather than the cause.
8506    ///
8507    /// The peer's `handle_session_error` closes the Session on a `SessionId`-identified error and sends
8508    /// nothing back, so there is no error exchange to loop.
8509    ///
8510    /// The `identifier` names what the peer is to close. An Exit addresses a resumable Entry by the
8511    /// challenge of the instance it means (see [`exit_error_identifier`](Self::exit_error_identifier)), so that
8512    /// the notice can only end that instance and not a successor under the same pseudonym.
8513    async fn notify_session_error(
8514        &self,
8515        session_id: SessionId,
8516        identifier: ErrorIdentifier<SessionId>,
8517        routing: DestinationRouting,
8518        reason: StartErrorReason,
8519        context: &'static str,
8520    ) {
8521        let Some(mut msg_sender) = self.msg_sender.get().cloned() else {
8522            warn!(%session_id, %reason, context, "cannot send session error - manager not started");
8523            return;
8524        };
8525        // Counted for `Return` routing only (the Exit's); it sends one only to end a PIX Session, hence `Pix`.
8526        let exit_sends = matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(_));
8527        let sent = send_via_msg_sender(
8528            &mut msg_sender,
8529            routing,
8530            HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType { identifier, reason }),
8531            context,
8532        )
8533        .await;
8534        let sent = if exit_sends {
8535            count_exit_control_send(ExitControlKind::SessionError, ExitSessionKind::Pix, sent)
8536        } else {
8537            sent
8538        };
8539        match sent {
8540            Ok(()) => {
8541                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
8542                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
8543            }
8544            Err(error) => warn!(%session_id, %reason, %error, context, "failed to send session error"),
8545        }
8546    }
8547
8548    /// How the Exit addresses a post-establishment `SessionError` to the Entry of the Session driven by
8549    /// `control_plane`, or `None` when that Session is no longer there to be told about.
8550    ///
8551    /// By the challenge of the slot's *current* instance when the Entry that established it announced
8552    /// `Capability::Resumable`: the Entry closes the instance that challenge opened and nothing else, so a notice that
8553    /// is delayed past a takeover, or sent about a plane that has since been replaced, cannot end the successor.
8554    /// By the Session ID for an Entry that does not understand that, as it always was.
8555    fn exit_error_identifier(
8556        &self,
8557        session_id: &SessionId,
8558        control_plane: &PixControlPlane,
8559    ) -> Option<ErrorIdentifier<SessionId>> {
8560        let slot = self.slot_of_control_plane(session_id, control_plane)?;
8561        Some(error_identifier_of(&slot, session_id))
8562    }
8563
8564    /// Closes the slot under `id` as [`close_session_scoped`](Self::close_session_scoped) does, and tells the
8565    /// Entry why, but only if this call acted: the notice is addressed by the slot that was removed, so a
8566    /// successor that took the slot in the meantime is neither closed nor named. The notice goes out before
8567    /// the removed slot's tasks are stopped, which may include the caller's own.
8568    async fn close_session_scoped_and_notify(
8569        &self,
8570        id: &SessionId,
8571        reason: ClosureReason,
8572        control_plane: &PixControlPlane,
8573        routing: DestinationRouting,
8574        error_reason: StartErrorReason,
8575        context: &'static str,
8576    ) -> bool {
8577        let scope = CloseScope::ControlPlane(control_plane);
8578        if let Some(handled) = self.try_detach(id, reason, scope) {
8579            return handled;
8580        }
8581        if let Some(handled) = self.begin_surb_drain(id, reason, scope) {
8582            // The slot stays in place while it drains, and a draining one cannot be taken over.
8583            if handled && let Some(identifier) = self.exit_error_identifier(id, control_plane) {
8584                self.notify_session_error(*id, identifier, routing, error_reason, context)
8585                    .await;
8586            }
8587            return handled;
8588        }
8589        let Some(slot) = remove_slot_if(&self.sessions, id, |slot| scope.admits(slot)) else {
8590            return false;
8591        };
8592        self.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
8593        let identifier = error_identifier_of(&slot, id);
8594        self.notify_session_error(*id, identifier, routing, error_reason, context)
8595            .await;
8596        let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
8597        close_session(
8598            *id,
8599            slot,
8600            reason,
8601            self.surb_admission.get().cloned(),
8602            surb_retire_grace(self.cfg.surb_resolution_wait),
8603            token,
8604        );
8605        true
8606    }
8607
8608    /// Registers an Exit commitment for every index in `ssa_indices` and asks the Entry to commit to
8609    /// the matching SSAs — all in a single [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`].
8610    ///
8611    /// Driven by the supervisor's [`RequestSsa`](SessionPixAction::RequestSsa) action, which is what
8612    /// allocates the indices and fixes the dimensions — this only carries it out. Taking them as
8613    /// arguments rather than re-reading them from the slot keeps one source of truth for what was
8614    /// negotiated: the commitments registered here and the parameters the message advertises cannot
8615    /// disagree with what the supervisor is timing.
8616    ///
8617    /// One message for the whole batch, and one `params` field covering all of it, which is correct:
8618    /// every SSA in a Session uses the same negotiated dimensions. The Entry enforces its own ceiling
8619    /// on how many it will accept ([`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`]) and refuses an
8620    /// over-cap batch in full, so a batch larger than the peer allows loses the Session — see
8621    /// [`SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request`](crate::SupervisorConfig::ssas_per_request).
8622    ///
8623    /// Installs no deadline of its own: every timeout that used to be armed here now belongs to the
8624    /// supervisor, which can see the whole cycle rather than just this one step.
8625    ///
8626    /// Returns the exact [`HoprStartProtocol`] message that went on the wire alongside the guards, so the
8627    /// caller can send *that* again for [`ResendSsaRequest`](SessionPixAction::ResendSsaRequest). A
8628    /// rebuilt request would not be the same one: the Exit secrets behind its commitments are random,
8629    /// and the deposit data is whatever the pool answered the first time. The message is cloned before
8630    /// it is sent, and its encoding is deterministic, so a repeat is byte-identical.
8631    ///
8632    /// The returned [`SsaCommitmentGuard`]s own their registrations until the caller transfers or drops
8633    /// them. Handing them out rather than retaining them here is what makes the failure path safe:
8634    /// this function has fallible steps after the registrations exist — including partway through the
8635    /// batch — and an early return from any of them releases every one of them. That matters more for
8636    /// a batch than for a single SSA: without it one failed send would strand every index it had
8637    /// registered, and since the supervisor does not reuse an index, the Session could never recover.
8638    async fn send_ssa_request(
8639        &self,
8640        session_id: SessionId,
8641        slot: &SessionSlot,
8642        ssa_ids: &[SsaId<HoprPseudonym>],
8643        params: PixParams,
8644    ) -> errors::Result<(Vec<SsaCommitmentGuard<HoprPixSpec>>, HoprStartProtocol)> {
8645        let Some(first_ssa_id) = ssa_ids.first().copied() else {
8646            return Err(SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow!("ssa request with no indices")).into());
8647        };
8648
8649        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
8650        // Clone kept on this task: `pix_toolbox` itself is moved into the blocking commitment task,
8651        // while the deposit-data request below needs it here.
8652        let pix_toolbox_local = pix_toolbox.clone();
8653        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
8654
8655        // One blocking task for the whole batch rather than one per SSA: each commitment is a single
8656        // random scalar and one generator multiplication, so per-task overhead would dominate.
8657        let ids = ssa_ids.to_vec();
8658        let (exit_commitments, guards) = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
8659            move || {
8660                let mut commitments = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());
8661                let mut guards = Vec::with_capacity(ids.len());
8662                for ssa_id in ids {
8663                    let (commitment, guard) = pix_toolbox
8664                        .share_processor
8665                        .new_guarded_exit_commitment(ssa_id, params)?;
8666                    commitments.push((ssa_id.ssa_index(), HoprPixGroupElement(commitment.to_bytes())));
8667                    guards.push(guard);
8668                }
8669                Ok::<_, hopr_protocol_pix::errors::PixError<HoprPseudonym>>((commitments, guards))
8670            },
8671            "server_ssa_commitment",
8672        )
8673        .await
8674        .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
8675        .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
8676
8677        info!(
8678            %session_id, batch_size = ssa_ids.len(), %params, %first_ssa_id,
8679            "generated exit commitments for the SSA batch"
8680        );
8681
8682        // Ask the deposit pool for the data to attach to this batch, and keep what it produced: the
8683        // Exit needs it twice. Once now, to put on the wire, and once per SSA later, to hand back to
8684        // the pool with the deposit address in `DepositNeeded` — by which point the batch it came
8685        // from is long gone.
8686        //
8687        // A pool that does not answer fails the batch here, which drops `guards` and releases every
8688        // registration it made. That is the only safe direction: deposit data reaches the Entry in
8689        // this message or not at all, so a batch sent without it buys service the Entry can never
8690        // pay for.
8691        let ssa_indices = ssa_ids.iter().map(|ssa_id| ssa_id.ssa_index()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
8692        let deposit_data = Self::request_deposit_data(&pix_toolbox_local, session_id, &ssa_indices).await?;
8693
8694        if !self.sessions.contains_key(&session_id) {
8695            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
8696        }
8697
8698        let deposit_data = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &ssa_indices, deposit_data)?;
8699
8700        // The pool may have taken a good part of the registrations' lifetime, and the commitment
8701        // deadline only starts at `SsaRequestSent`, after this send. Reading each registration
8702        // refreshes it, so the answer to this request gets the whole lifetime after the send. One that
8703        // lapsed while the pool answered is not sent for: the Entry would answer a request the Exit can
8704        // no longer match, after it has been told to deposit.
8705        if !refresh_registrations(&pix_toolbox_local.share_processor, ssa_ids) {
8706            return Err(SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow(format!(
8707                "session {session_id} had its commitment registrations lapse while the pool answered"
8708            ))
8709            .into());
8710        }
8711
8712        // Only a request that is going out has its deposit data kept for the `DepositNeeded` to come.
8713        if let Some(ssa_state) = slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
8714            ssa_state.remember_sent_deposit_data(&deposit_data);
8715        }
8716
8717        // Construct and send the Exit SSA commitment request message.
8718        // The parameters were previously verified to be acceptable.
8719        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
8720            session_id,
8721            params,
8722            exit_commitments,
8723            deposit_data,
8724        ));
8725
8726        // Only PIX Sessions ask for SSA commitments.
8727        count_exit_control_send(
8728            ExitControlKind::SsaRequest,
8729            ExitSessionKind::Pix,
8730            send_counted_via_msg_sender(
8731                &mut msg_sender,
8732                slot.routing_opts.clone(),
8733                data.clone(),
8734                &slot.surb_estimator,
8735                &session_id,
8736                "session SSA commitment request message",
8737            )
8738            .await,
8739        )
8740        .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)?;
8741
8742        Ok((guards, data))
8743    }
8744
8745    /// Asks the Entry to re-send the parts of one SSA's commitment that never arrived.
8746    ///
8747    /// The Entry's answer to an `SsaRequest` is hundreds of packets and the reconstructor can use
8748    /// none of it until every one has landed, so a single drop used to cost the Session on
8749    /// `max_ssa_delivery_time` — after the Entry had already been told to fund the cycle. This is the
8750    /// repair: the reconstructor says which polynomial runs are missing, and the Entry re-sends
8751    /// exactly those.
8752    ///
8753    /// Deliberately *not* built on [`send_ssa_request`](Self::send_ssa_request), whose every step is
8754    /// wrong here. It registers no Exit commitment — the cycle already has one, and registering a
