8755    /// second for the same index is refused as a duplicate — allocates no index, and asks the deposit
8756    /// pool for nothing, since the deposit data of this cycle travelled with the request that created
8757    /// it. Nothing it does can earn the Entry a deposit, which is what makes it safe to repeat.
8758    ///
8759    /// The scope is read here rather than carried in the action: what is missing changes as the burst
8760    /// continues to arrive, and the freshest answer is both smaller and the one that converges.
8761    async fn send_commitment_retransmission_request(
8762        &self,
8763        session_id: SessionId,
8764        slot: &SessionSlot,
8765        ssa_id: SsaId<HoprPseudonym>,
8766        params: PixParams,
8767    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
8768        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
8769        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
8770
8771        // Asked of the encoder, so the scope cannot be sized against a restated layout — see
8772        // `StartProtocol::max_missing_runs`.
8773        let max_runs = HoprStartProtocol::max_missing_runs(&session_id).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
8774
8775        let Some(runs) = pix_toolbox.share_processor.missing_commitment_runs(&ssa_id, max_runs) else {
8776            // The registration is gone — retired, or expired after
8777            // `incomplete_commitment_lifetime` — so there is nothing left for a retransmission to
8778            // complete. The commitment deadline is what ends the Session; saying so here is the only
8779            // way an operator learns which of the two it was.
8780            warn!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "cannot re-request commitment parts for a cycle the reconstructor no longer holds");
8781            return Ok(());
8782        };
8783
8784        if runs.is_empty() {
8785            // The commitment completed between the timer firing and this running. Its
8786            // `CommitmentVerified` is already on its way to the supervisor, which clears the timer.
8787            debug!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "commitment completed before its parts could be re-requested");
8788            return Ok(());
8789        }
8790
8791        let missing_polynomials: u32 = runs.iter().map(|(first, last)| (last - first) as u32 + 1).sum();
8792        info!(
8793            %session_id, %ssa_id, runs = runs.len(), missing_polynomials,
8794            "re-requesting the SSA commitment parts that did not arrive"
8795        );
8796
8797        count_exit_control_send(
8798            ExitControlKind::CommitmentRetransmissionRequest,
8799            ExitSessionKind::Pix,
8800            send_counted_via_msg_sender(
8801                &mut msg_sender,
8802                slot.routing_opts.clone(),
8803                HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
8804                    session_id,
8805                    params,
8806                    [(ssa_id.ssa_index(), runs)],
8807                )),
8808                &slot.surb_estimator,
8809                &session_id,
8810                "ssa commitment retransmission request",
8811            )
8812            .await,
8813        )
8814        .map_err(TransportSessionError::packet_sending)?;
8815
8816        Ok(())
8817    }
8818
8819    /// Returns the current number of active sessions.
8820    pub fn num_active_sessions(&self) -> usize {
8821        self.active_sessions.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
8822    }
8823
8824    /// Returns [`SessionIds`](SessionId) of all currently active sessions.
8825    pub fn active_sessions(&self) -> Vec<SessionId> {
8826        self.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
8827        self.sessions.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect()
8828    }
8829
8830    /// Explicitly closes the session with the given `id`.
8831    ///
8832    /// Removes the entry from the internal session cache, closes the data channel,
8833    /// and aborts any auxiliary tasks. Returns `true` if a session was found and
8834    /// closed, `false` otherwise.
8835    ///
8836    /// This avoids waiting for the idle timeout (`time_to_idle`) or the LRU
8837    /// capacity bound to evict the entry, which is the desired behaviour when
8838    /// the caller (e.g. REST `DELETE /session`) knows the session is finished.
8839    ///
8840    /// One case departs from that: an Exit-side PIX Session with
8841    /// [`fill.drain_after_close`](crate::PixFillConfig::drain_after_close) on and spendable SURBs
8842    /// left starts a SURB drain instead of being torn down (see `begin_surb_drain`). The data path
8843    /// still ends at once, but the session slot and the keep-alive stream stay in place until the
8844    /// supervisor closes the Session — whether because the funded cycle recovered or because the
8845    /// drain was refused — and `true` then means "found, and now draining" rather than "found and
8846    /// closed".
8847    pub fn close_session(&self, id: &SessionId) -> bool {
8848        self.close_session_with_reason(id, ClosureReason::Eviction)
8849    }
8850
8851    /// Closes the Session under `id` only if it is the slot instance `instance_id` (see
8852    /// [`HoprSession::slot_instance`]).
8853    ///
8854    /// For callers that hold a handle to one specific Session object and must not tear down a
8855    /// successor that has since taken the same pseudonym. Same semantics as
8856    /// [`close_session`](Self::close_session) when the instance matches; `false` when the slot is gone
8857    /// or belongs to another instance.
8858    pub fn close_session_instance(&self, id: &SessionId, instance_id: u64) -> bool {
8859        self.close_session_scoped(id, ClosureReason::Eviction, CloseScope::InstanceId(instance_id))
8860    }
8861
8862    /// Answers an Exit-side close by draining the Session's buffered SURBs, when that is worth doing.
8863    ///
8864    /// A PIX Session can end long before the cycle it was funded for does. The deposit that cycle was
8865    /// paid is released only once its whole emission has ridden back to the Entry, and the address it
8866    /// sits at derives from both nodes' commitments — so tearing the Session down mid-cycle strands
8867    /// money both sides have already parted with. When the Exit still holds enough SURBs to finish,
8868    /// it keeps the keep-alive stream running instead, and the Session's slot with it, until the
8869    /// supervisor closes the Session for good.
8870    ///
8871    /// Returns `None` when this close was **not** answered here, which is every case the caller must
8872    /// handle exactly as it always has; `Some(v)` is the value
8873    /// [`close_session_with_reason`](Self::close_session_with_reason) should return. `Some` currently
8874    /// always carries `true` — a drain is only ever started for a Session that was found — but the
8875    /// value is returned rather than assumed so that the two outcomes stay distinguishable if a
8876    /// future refusal path wants to report one.
8877    ///
8878    /// The order of the checks is load-bearing:
8879    ///
8880    /// 1. the configuration, so that with `drain_after_close` (or `fill.enabled`) off nothing below runs and every
8881    ///    close path is byte-for-byte what it was;
8882    /// 2. the slot, by `get` rather than `remove` — the lookup also refreshes the idle timer the drain lives on;
8883    /// 3. an Exit-side PIX Session, so an Entry-side or non-PIX Session falls straight through;
8884    /// 4. an already-draining Session: a `WriteClosed`/`EmptyRead` is the end-of-stream our own ingress abort produces
8885    ///    and is absorbed, while anything else — a second operator close, or a peer `SessionError` — forces the hard
8886    ///    teardown, which is the operator's way to overrule a drain;
8887    /// 5. a PIX failure already tearing the Session down, which nothing here should interfere with;
8888    /// 6. the SURB estimate, which is the one half of the predicate this layer can answer — see the comment on it for
8889    ///    why answering it here rather than leaving it all to the supervisor matters;
8890    /// 7. and only then the stream is put into drain mode, **before** the supervisor is told, so that no packet can be
8891    ///    classified as the reserve-exempt notification in the window between the supervisor deciding and the stream
8892    ///    learning.
8893    ///
8894    /// What it does *not* do is decrement `active_sessions` or remove the slot: the supervisor's own
8895    /// `Close` teardown does both, whether the drain completes or is refused a channel hop later.
8896    /// `Balancer`, `KeepAlive`, `SurbNotifyDelay`, `PixActionDriver` and the deposit observers are
8897    /// all left running; only the ingress is aborted, so the session server sees its end of the
8898    /// stream as promptly as it would have.
8899    fn begin_surb_drain(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason, scope: CloseScope<'_>) -> Option<bool> {
8900        let fill_cfg = &self.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill;
8901        if !(fill_cfg.enabled && fill_cfg.drain_after_close) {
8902            return None;
8903        }
8904
8905        // A slot swapped for a successor between the read and the transition is evaluated afresh, the
8906        // way the close would have gone had it arrived a moment later. Bounded: a pseudonym replaced
8907        // this often is being fought over, and the plain close is the answer to that.
8908        for _ in 0..DRAIN_REEVALUATIONS {
8909            match self.try_begin_surb_drain(id, reason, scope) {
8910                DrainAttempt::Answered(answer) => return answer,
8911                DrainAttempt::Replaced => continue,
8912            }
8913        }
8914        None
8915    }
8916
8917    /// One evaluation of [`begin_surb_drain`](Self::begin_surb_drain) against the slot currently under
8918    /// `id`.
8919    fn try_begin_surb_drain(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason, scope: CloseScope<'_>) -> DrainAttempt {
8920        use DrainAttempt::Answered;
8921
8922        let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(id) else {
8923            return Answered(None);
8924        };
8925        if !scope.admits(&slot) {
8926            return Answered(Some(false));
8927        }
8928        let (Some(supervisor), Some(fill)) = (slot.pix_supervisor.get(), slot.pix_fill.get()) else {
8929            return Answered(None);
8930        };
8931
8932        if fill.is_draining() {
8933            return Answered(answer_while_draining(reason));
8934        }
8935
8936        if matches!(
8937            reason,
8938            ClosureReason::PixFailure | ClosureReason::MissingDepositData | ClosureReason::DepositPoolTooSlow
8939        ) {
8940            return Answered(None);
8941        }
8942
8943        // Nothing to drain *with* is decidable here, and cheaply, unlike whether there is anything
8944        // worth draining *for* — which needs the cycle state only the supervisor holds. Asking it
8945        // anyway would defer the teardown of every PIX Session by however long the action driver
8946        // takes to reach the answer, and a driver mid-`send_ssa_request` can be seconds away from
8947        // that. So a Session whose estimate is already at or below its reserve is torn down here and
8948        // now, exactly as it always was: no rate the supervisor could plan would put a packet on the
8949        // wire against a buffer that shallow.
8950        let drainable_surbs = fill.drainable_surbs();
8951        if drainable_surbs == 0 {
8952            return Answered(None);
8953        }
8954
8955        // The check above is only a fast path: `close_session_with_reason` is reached from the
8956        // operator, the closure notifier and `handle_session_error` independently, so two closes can
8957        // both read it as false. The transition is what actually decides, and the loser is answered
8958        // as it would have been had the two been serialized rather than concurrent — which is what
8959        // keeps the supervisor from being told a Session closed twice.
8960        //
8961        // Taken inside a compute on the slot, so it serialises with a removal (and with a replacement
8962        // of the slot) instead of racing it: a drain must not begin on a slot that has just gone, or
8963        // on a successor's.
8964        let mut step = DrainStep::Gone;
8965        self.sessions
8966            .entry(*id)
8967            .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| {
8968                if let Some(entry) = entry {
8969                    step = if !scope.admits(entry.value()) {
8970                        DrainStep::Gone
8971                    } else if !Arc::ptr_eq(&entry.value().instance, &slot.instance) {
8972                        DrainStep::Replaced
8973                    } else if fill.enter_drain() {
8974                        DrainStep::Entered
8975                    } else {
8976                        DrainStep::Lost
8977                    };
8978                }
8979                moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop
8980            });
8981        match step {
8982            DrainStep::Entered => {}
8983            DrainStep::Lost => return Answered(answer_while_draining(reason)),
8984            // Nothing of the one we meant to drain is left, and what is there is not ours to close.
8985            DrainStep::Gone => return Answered(Some(false)),
8986            // The caller's scope admits the replacement, which is evaluated in its own right.
8987            DrainStep::Replaced => return DrainAttempt::Replaced,
8988        }
8989
8990        // Re-read now that the reserve is frozen (see `PixFillControl::set_announced_target`): an
8991        // announcement that landed between the fast path above and the transition moved the reserve
8992        // the drain will be held to, and the supervisor must plan against that one. Falling through to
8993        // the teardown from here is what a refused event below does too.
8994        let drainable_surbs = fill.drainable_surbs();
8995        if drainable_surbs == 0 {
8996            return Answered(None);
8997        }
8998
8999        if !supervisor.try_send_event(SessionPixEvent::SessionClosed { drainable_surbs }) {
9000            return Answered(None);
9001        }
9002
9003        // A drain ends the wait for a client's return, if there was one: the Session is not resumable
9004        // from here on, and a takeover refuses a draining slot.
9005        slot.exit_resume
9006            .detached
9007            .store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
9008        slot.abort_handles.lock().abort_one(&SessionHandles::ResumeWindow);
9009
9010        // The data path ends here regardless of what the supervisor decides: a writer parked on the
9011        // egress gate is waiting for a Session that has gone, and the reader's end-of-stream is what
9012        // the session server is waiting for.
9013        if let Some(gate) = slot.pix_egress_gate.get() {
9014            gate.poison();
9015        }
9016        slot.abort_handles.lock().abort_one(&SessionHandles::Ingress);
9017
9018        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9019        set_session_state(id, SessionLifecycleState::Closing);
9020
9021        info!(
9022            session_id = %id,
9023            ?reason,
9024            drainable_surbs,
9025            "session closed at the exit — draining its buffered SURBs into the funded cycle"
9026        );
9027        Answered(Some(true))
9028    }
9029
9030    /// [`close_session`](Self::close_session) with the reason spelled out.
9031    ///
9032    /// The reason is what the operator reads when a PIX Session stops, and the failures are hard to
9033    /// tell apart from the outside, so a caller that knows which one it is says so.
9034    ///
9035    /// `true` means the Session was found and dealt with. Since
9036    /// [`begin_surb_drain`](Self::begin_surb_drain), "dealt with" also covers "found, and now
9037    /// draining its remaining SURBs into a funded cycle" — in which case the slot is deliberately
9038    /// left in place until the supervisor's own teardown removes it.
9039    fn close_session_with_reason(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason) -> bool {
9040        self.close_session_scoped(id, reason, CloseScope::Any)
9041    }
9042
9043    /// [`close_session_with_reason`](Self::close_session_with_reason), acting only on a slot `scope`
9044    /// admits. A slot it does not admit is left exactly as it is, and the answer is `false`.
9045    fn close_session_scoped(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason, scope: CloseScope<'_>) -> bool {
9046        if let Some(handled) = self.try_detach(id, reason, scope) {
9047            return handled;
9048        }
9049
9050        if let Some(handled) = self.begin_surb_drain(id, reason, scope) {
9051            return handled;
9052        }
9053
9054        if let Some(slot) = remove_slot_if(&self.sessions, id, |slot| scope.admits(slot)) {
9055            self.active_sessions.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9056            // Reconstructor state is released by `close_session` aborting the PIX action driver,
9057            // whose commitment guards retire on drop.
9058            let token = slot.claim_admission_token();
9059            close_session(
9060                *id,
9061                slot,
9062                reason,
9063                self.surb_admission.get().cloned(),
9064                surb_retire_grace(self.cfg.surb_resolution_wait),
9065                token,
9066            );
9067            true
9068        } else {
9069            false
9070        }
9071    }
9072
9073    /// Sets the data plane of a paid Exit PIX Session aside instead of closing the Session, for its
9074    /// client to return to within [`resume_window`](IncomingSessionPixConfig::resume_window).
9075    ///
9076    /// Answers the close, returning `Some(true)`, only when **all** of these hold, and returns `None`
9077    /// otherwise, leaving the close to run as it always has (drain, or hard close):
9078    ///
9079    /// * the window is not disabled (`resume_window > 0`);
9080    /// * the reason is `EmptyRead` (the client ended the stream; the Exit's own `WriteClosed` is not enough) and the
9081    ///   scope is [`CloseScope::Instance`]: the data plane of that very slot instance has ended. An operator close, a
9082    ///   PIX failure and a peer `SessionError` are none of these;
9083    /// * the Session runs on the stateless socket ([`SessionSlot::is_stateless`]);
9084    /// * the slot is an established Exit-side PIX slot whose gate is not poisoned and whose fill is not draining;
9085    /// * it holds something paid for: its gate has been funded, or the Entry has answered the commitment request
9086    ///   ([`SessionSlot::holds_paid_cycle`]).
9087    ///
9088    /// A slot that is already detached answers `Some(true)` without doing anything: a second end of the
9089    /// same data plane is no news.
9090    ///
9091    /// Detaching marks the instance superseded (which fails the writes of the dead `HoprSession`),
9092    /// aborts the ingress, flags the slot detached and arms the window's timer. It does **not** poison
9093    /// the gate or stop the supervisor, which is only woken to the new data-plane level: the supervisor, the
9094    /// action driver, the keep-alive stream and the fill carry on, so the funded cycle keeps being recovered
9095    /// through the gap. All of it runs inside one compute on the slot, which is what serialises it against a
9096    /// takeover (that swaps the instance in its own compute) and against the window's expiry.
9097    fn try_detach(&self, id: &SessionId, reason: ClosureReason, scope: CloseScope<'_>) -> Option<bool> {
9098        let window = self.cfg.pix_config.resume_window;
9099        if window.is_zero() || !matches!(reason, ClosureReason::EmptyRead | ClosureReason::WriteClosed) {
9100            return None;
9101        }
9102        let CloseScope::Instance(instance) = scope else {
9103            return None;
9104        };
9105
9106        // Only the client ending the stream (`EmptyRead`) starts a detach. A `WriteClosed` is the
9107        // Exit's own application closing its end: the Entry may be alive and well, and a Session kept
9108        // for a client that is not coming back would let it fund a successor that the window's end
9109        // then strands. A second end of a plane that is already detached is absorbed whichever it is.
9110        let may_start = matches!(reason, ClosureReason::EmptyRead);
9111        match self.detach_instance(id, instance, window, may_start)? {
9112            DetachStep::AlreadyDetached => Some(true),
9113            DetachStep::Detached => {
9114                info!(
9115                    session_id = %id,
9116                    ?reason,
9117                    ?window,
9118                    "session detached, awaiting resumption"
9119                );
9120                Some(true)
9121            }
9122        }
9123    }
9124
9125    /// Detaches the slot under `id` if it is `instance` and detachable (see
9126    /// [`try_detach`](Self::try_detach), which is the close path's way in), arming a window of
9127    /// `window`. `None` when the slot is gone, is another instance, or holds nothing worth keeping.
9128    ///
9129    /// Counts the detach; a call for a slot already detached is `AlreadyDetached` and counts nothing.
9130    fn detach_instance(
9131        &self,
9132        id: &SessionId,
9133        instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>,
9134        window: Duration,
9135        may_start: bool,
9136    ) -> Option<DetachStep> {
9137        let mut step = None;
9138        self.sessions
9139            .entry(*id)
9140            .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| {
9141                if let Some(entry) = entry.filter(|entry| Arc::ptr_eq(&entry.value().instance, instance)) {
9142                    let slot = entry.value();
9143                    step = if slot.is_detached() {
9144                        Some(DetachStep::AlreadyDetached)
9145                    } else if may_start && slot.is_detachable() {
9146                        slot.instance.supersede();
9147                        // Flagged before the timer exists, so a timer that fires at once finds the slot
9148                        // detached.
9149                        slot.exit_resume
9150                            .detached
9151                            .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
9152                        if let Some(gate) = slot.pix_egress_gate.get() {
9153                            // Read by the supervisor's worker: no new successor request while detached.
9154                            gate.set_data_plane_detached(true);
9155                        }
9156                        if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
9157                            // A wake-up for an idle worker; the level is on the gate.
9158                            let _ = supervisor.try_send_event(SessionPixEvent::DataPlaneChanged);
9159                        }
9160                        let mut handles = slot.abort_handles.lock();
9161                        handles.abort_one(&SessionHandles::Ingress);
9162                        handles.insert(
9163                            SessionHandles::ResumeWindow,
9164                            self.spawn_resume_window(*id, slot.instance.clone(), window),
9165                        );
9166                        drop(handles);
9167                        // The data plane is gone but the Session is not closing: it is awaiting its
9168                        // client. (The closure consumer marked it `Closing` before asking.)
9169                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9170                        set_session_state(id, SessionLifecycleState::Active);
9171                        Some(DetachStep::Detached)
9172                    } else {
9173                        None
9174                    };
9175                }
9176                moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop
9177            });
9178
9179        if matches!(step, Some(DetachStep::Detached)) {
9180            // A lookup refreshes the idle timer the detached slot lives on.
9181            self.sessions.get(id);
9182            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9183            telemetry::pix::record_resumption(telemetry::pix::PixResumption::Detached);
9184        }
9185        step
9186    }
9187
9188    /// The timer that ends a resume window: after `window`, the slot of `instance`, if it is still
9189    /// detached, is drained or closed as it would have been without the window.
9190    fn spawn_resume_window(&self, session_id: SessionId, instance: Arc<SlotInstance>, window: Duration) -> AbortHandle {
9191        let manager = self.clone();
9192        hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
9193            hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(window).await;
9194            // `EmptyRead` is what ended the data plane, so it is what the deferred close reports.
9195            if manager.close_session_scoped(
9196                &session_id,
9197                ClosureReason::EmptyRead,
9198                CloseScope::DetachedInstance(&instance),
9199            ) {
9200                info!(%session_id, ?window, "the resume window of a detached session ran out");
9201                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9202                telemetry::pix::record_resumption(telemetry::pix::PixResumption::WindowExpired);
9203            }
9204        })
9205    }

9207    /// Updates the configuration of the SURB balancer on the given [`SessionId`].
9208    ///
9209    /// Returns an error if the Session with the given `id` does not exist, or
9210    /// if it does not use SURB balancing.
9211    pub fn update_surb_balancer_config(&self, id: &SessionId, config: SurbBalancerConfig) -> errors::Result<()> {
9212        self.update_surb_balancer_config_scoped(id, None, config)
9213    }

9215    /// Same as [`update_surb_balancer_config`](Self::update_surb_balancer_config), but only if the slot
9216    /// under `id` is the slot instance `instance_id` (see [`HoprSession::slot_instance`]).
9217    ///
9218    /// For callers that hold a handle to one specific Session object: once its pseudonym is reused, an
9219    /// update through that stale handle must not change the successor Session's balancer. Fails with
9220    /// [`SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession`] when the slot is gone or belongs to another instance.
9221    pub fn update_surb_balancer_config_instance(
9222        &self,
9223        id: &SessionId,
9224        instance_id: u64,
9225        config: SurbBalancerConfig,
9226    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
9227        self.update_surb_balancer_config_scoped(id, Some(instance_id), config)
9228    }

9230    fn update_surb_balancer_config_scoped(
9231        &self,
9232        id: &SessionId,
9233        instance_id: Option<u64>,
9234        config: SurbBalancerConfig,
9235    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
9236        let cfg = self
9237            .sessions
9238            .get(id)
9239            .filter(|s| instance_id.is_none_or(|i| s.instance.id() == i))
9240            .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession)?
9241            .surb_mgmt;
9242
9243        // Only update the config if there already was one before
9244        if !cfg.is_disabled() {
9245            cfg.update(&config);
9246            Ok(())
9247        } else {
9248            Err(SessionManagerError::other(anyhow!("session does not use SURB balancing")).into())
9249        }
9250    }

9290    /// Gets estimations produced/received and consumed SURBs by the Session.
9291    ///
9292    /// For an outgoing Session (Entry) the pair is the number of SURBs sent (by us) and used (by the Exit).
9293    /// For an incoming Session (Exit) the pair is the number of SURBs received (from Entry) and used (by us).
9294    ///
9295    /// Returns an error if the Session with the given `id` does not exist.
9296    pub fn get_surb_level_estimates(&self, id: &SessionId) -> errors::Result<(u64, u64)> {
9297        match self.sessions.get(id) {
9298            Some(session) => Ok((
9299                session
9300                    .surb_estimator
9301                    .produced
9302                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
9303                session
9304                    .surb_estimator
9305                    .consumed
9306                    .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
9307            )),
9308            None => Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into()),
9309        }
9310    }
9311
9312    /// Forwards a PIX protocol observation to the Session's supervisor.
9313    ///
9314    /// The manager no longer interprets these. Deciding what an early-recovery signal or a failed
9315    /// share means for a Session's lifecycle needs the whole picture — which SSAs are in flight,
9316    /// what phase each is in, how much service has been consumed — and that lives in the supervisor.
9317    ///
9318    /// A `NonExistingSession` error is expected traffic rather than a fault: acknowledgements
9319    /// outlive their Session by up to the reconstructor's ack window, so events for a just-closed
9320    /// Session are routine. Callers distinguish it for exactly that reason.
9321    pub async fn dispatch_pix_event(&self, event: HoprSessionInPixEvent) -> errors::Result<()> {
9322        // Copied rather than borrowed, so the match below can move the event's payload out.
9323        let session_id = *event.pseudonym();
9324        let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) else {
9325            debug!(%session_id, "pix event for a session that is no longer registered");
9326            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
9327        };
9328
9329        let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() else {
9330            // Entry side, or a Session that negotiated no PIX: nothing supervises it, so there is
9331            // nothing an observation could act on.
9332            trace!(%session_id, "pix event on a session without a supervisor");
9333            return Ok(());
9334        };
9335
9336        // Progress is the one input whose rate is set by traffic rather than by lifecycle
9337        // transitions, so it is delivered without backpressure — awaiting channel capacity here
9338        // would put the supervisor's scheduling latency on the acknowledgement path. Safe by
9339        // construction rather than by tolerance: snapshots carry absolute counters and the state
9340        // machine keeps the maximum it has seen, so a dropped one is indistinguishable from a late
9341        // one, and the next one supersedes it.
9342        if let HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress(progress) = event {
9343            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9344            telemetry::set_pix_recovery_progress(&session_id, progress.useful_shares, progress.target_useful_shares);
9345
9346            if !supervisor.try_send_progress(progress) {
9347                trace!(%session_id, "dropped a pix progress snapshot on a full supervisor channel");
9348            }
9349            return Ok(());
9350        }
9351
9352        let sent = match event {
9353            HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaAlmostRecovered(ssa_id) => {
9354                supervisor.send_event(SessionPixEvent::AlmostRecovered(ssa_id)).await
9355            }
9356            HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id) => {
9357                supervisor.send_event(SessionPixEvent::Recovered(ssa_id)).await
9358            }
9359            HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
9360                ssa_id,
9361                observed_total,
9362                peer,
9363            } => {
9364                supervisor
9365                    .send_event(SessionPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
9366                        ssa_id,
9367                        observed_total,
9368                        peer,
9369                    })
9370                    .await
9371            }
9372            HoprSessionInPixEvent::RecoveryProgress(_) => unreachable!("handled above"),
9373        };
9374
9375        if sent.is_err() {
9376            error!(%session_id, "pix supervisor is no longer accepting events");
9377        }
9378
9379        Ok(())
9380    }
9381
9382    /// Sets how many SURBs of `session`, held in the counterparty's store, are invalid: their return
9383    /// path runs through a relayer judged dead on any hop. Also their share of what it was handed, so the
9384    /// balancer replaces them. `false` if there is no such Session.
9385    pub fn set_invalid_surbs(&self, session: &SessionId, count: u64, share: f64) -> bool {
9386        self.sessions
9387            .get(session)
9388            .map(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.set_invalid_surbs(count, share))
9389            .is_some()
9390    }
9391
9392    /// Whether an `SsaRequest` for `session_id` names SSA state this node holds or is making.
9393    ///
9394    /// Only the Exit asks for SSA commitments, and only of its own Entry: a Session this node holds
9395    /// as an outgoing (`Forward`) slot, or one this node is still initiating (`pending_outgoing`).
9396    /// An Exit-side (`Return`) slot never legitimately receives one, so a request naming one is
9397    /// refused.
9398    ///
9399    /// Lives on [`Self::start_message_is_for_local_state`] only. [`Self::handle_ssa_request`]
9400    /// re-checks the two cheap halves of it (slot present, or initiation pending) as a backstop, but
9401    /// deliberately not the variant — see there.
9402    fn ssa_request_names_local_state(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> bool {
9403        self.pending_outgoing.contains_key(session_id)
9404            || self
9405                .sessions
9406                .get(session_id)
9407                .is_some_and(|slot| matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }))
9408    }
9409
9410    /// Whether a Start-protocol message names Session state this node actually holds.
9411    ///
9412    /// Start control messages share one bounded worker pool, and several handlers park a worker on state a
9413    /// bogus message will never have — `handle_ssa_request` waits up to a second for a Session slot
9414    /// a random pseudonym never gets. Deciding admission here, where the session lookup is already
9415    /// being done, keeps those messages off the pool entirely.
9416    fn start_message_is_for_local_state(&self, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, msg: &HoprStartProtocol) -> bool {
9417        match msg {
9418            // Creates the state the other arms are checked against.
9419            HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(_) => true,
9420
9421            // Per-Session control traffic. The pseudonym a Start message arrives under is the
9422            // Session's own pseudonym on both sides, so a mismatch names someone else's Session.
9423            HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(m) => m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&m.session_id),
9424            HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(m) => m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&m.session_id),
9425
9426            // From the Exit, so for an outgoing Session only.
9427            HoprStartProtocol::ForwardReceipts(m) => {
9428                m.session_id == *pseudonym
9429                    && self
9430                        .sessions
9431                        .get(&m.session_id)
9432                        .is_some_and(|slot| matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }))
9433            }
9434
9435            // Only the Exit asks for SSA commitments, and only of its own Entry: an outgoing
9436            // (Forward) Session, or one this node is still initiating. An Exit-side (Return) slot
9437            // never legitimately receives one.
9438            HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(m) => {
9439                m.session_id == *pseudonym && self.ssa_request_names_local_state(&m.session_id)
9440            }
9441
9442            // Both are replies to something this node sent: an initiation named by challenge, or —
9443            // for `SessionError` only — a post-establishment error naming a registered Session by
9444            // its id.
9445            HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(est) => self.session_initiations.contains_key(&est.orig_challenge),
9446            HoprStartProtocol::SessionResumed(res) => self.session_initiations.contains_key(&res.orig_challenge),
9447            HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err) => match err.identifier {
9448                // A pending initiation, or a Session of this node under the sender's pseudonym that this
9449                // very challenge opened, set up or not (a challenge-scoped post-reply error).
9450                ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(challenge) => {
9451                    self.session_initiations.contains_key(&challenge)
9452                        || self.forward_instance_of_challenge(pseudonym, challenge).is_some()
9453                }
9454                ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(id) => id == *pseudonym && self.sessions.contains_key(&id),
9455            },
9456        }
9457    }
9458
9459    /// Tells `session` that its counterparty dropped every SURB it held, because the session's SURB
9460    /// generation advanced: the counterparty clears its store on the first batch of the new one.
9461    ///
9462    /// The balancer restarts its level estimate from empty and paces the refill, instead of reading
9463    /// back the level the counterparty last reported. `false` if there is no such Session.
9464    pub fn on_counterparty_surbs_wiped(&self, session: &SessionId) -> bool {
9465        self.sessions
9466            .get(session)
9467            .map(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.on_counterparty_wiped())
9468            .is_some()
9469    }
9470
9471    /// The main method to be called whenever data are received.
9472    ///
9473    /// It tries to recognize the message and correctly dispatches either
9474    /// the Session protocol or Start protocol messages.
9475    ///
9476    /// If the data are not recognized, they are returned as [`DispatchResult::Unrelated`].
9477    pub fn dispatch_message(
9478        &self,
9479        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
9480        in_data: ApplicationDataIn,
9481    ) -> errors::Result<DispatchResult> {
9482        if in_data.data.application_tag == HoprStartProtocol::START_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_TAG {
9483            // Start-protocol traffic bypasses `session_rx`, but an Exit → Entry message still
9484            // consumed one return SURB and unlocked one PIX share. Count it on outgoing Sessions
9485            // before anything else: the decode and the admission filter below can both drop the
9486            // message, and a packet that is dropped here has already spent its return SURB, so the
9487            // credit must not depend on it being decodable or admitted. Incoming Sessions receive
9488            // this traffic from the Entry over the forward path and must not be credited.
9489            if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&pseudonym)
9490                && matches!(&session_slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. })
9491            {
9492                session_slot
9493                    .returned_packets
9494                    .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9495
9496                // The only place the Exit's SURB supply can be heard from a quiet Session. The
9497                // conversion below takes `in_data.data` and drops the packet info with it, so by the
9498                // time `handle_keep_alive` runs the signals are gone -- and keep-alives are all a
9499                // Session that has stopped exchanging data still sends.
9500                session_slot
9501                    .surb_mgmt
9502                    .observe_counterparty_signals(in_data.packet_info.signals_from_sender);
9503            }
9504
9505            // What the packet did to the SURB store, taken before the decode below consumes the data
9506            // it is counted from; see [`SurbsStored`]. An incoming Session books it here, where every
9507            // kind of Start message passes, and before the decode and the admission filter below can drop
9508            // the message: the pipeline stored the SURBs before this ran, so they are in the ring whether
9509            // or not the message is handled. The opening `StartSession` finds no Session yet; the Start
9510            // protocol task books it once the Session exists, and only what was not booked here goes
9511            // along: an opening repeated for a Session that already exists is booked here, and must not
9512            // be booked again when the task refuses it, or a wipe it reports is subtracted twice.
9513            let stored = SurbsStored::of(&in_data);
9514            let booked = self
9515                .sessions
9516                .get(&pseudonym)
9517                .is_some_and(|session_slot| book_start_message_surbs(&session_slot, &pseudonym, stored));
9518            let unbooked = if booked { SurbsStored::default() } else { stored };
9519
9520            // Decode once, then decide locally whether anything on this node could handle it.
9521            // Without this check a peer spraying Start messages for pseudonyms it invented occupies
9522            // the Start-protocol worker pool — several handlers park a worker on state such
9523            // a message never has — and the bounded queue then fills, dropping every message behind
9524            // it.
9525            //
9526            // A decode failure is a quiet drop: anyone can send a Start-tagged packet for free.
9527            let msg = match HoprStartProtocol::try_from(in_data.data) {
9528                Ok(msg) => msg,
9529                Err(error) => {
9530                    trace!(%pseudonym, %error, "dropping malformed Start protocol message");
9531                    crate::counters::SESSION_MALFORMED_START_MESSAGES
9532                        .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9533                    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9534                    METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_malformed_start"], 1);
9535                    return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::MalformedStartMessage));
9536                }
9537            };
9538
9539            if !self.start_message_is_for_local_state(&pseudonym, &msg) {
9540                // Quiet on purpose: a peer spraying Start messages for pseudonyms we never issued
9541                // must not be able to fill the log any more than it can fill the handler pool.
9542                trace!(%pseudonym, "dropping Start protocol message that names no local session");
9543                crate::counters::SESSION_STALE_START_MESSAGES.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9544                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9545                METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_stale_start"], 1);
9546                return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage));
9547            }
9548
9549            // Forward receipts are handled here: they only feed the sink, and they cost the Entry a SURB.
9550            if let HoprStartProtocol::ForwardReceipts(receipts) = &msg {
9551                // A receipt rides on a SURB; a packet that came over a forward path has a tag and spent none
9552                if in_data.packet_info.forward_receipt_tag.is_some() {
9553                    trace!(%pseudonym, "dropping forward receipts that did not arrive on a SURB");
9554                    crate::counters::SESSION_STALE_START_MESSAGES.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9555                    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9556                    METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_stale_start"], 1);
9557                    return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage));
9558                }
9559                if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&pseudonym) {
9560                    // Spent like a keep-alive, not a reply: it must not count as one heard
9561                    slot.surb_mgmt.note_keep_alive_consumed(&slot.surb_estimator);
9562                    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9563                    telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&pseudonym, 1);
9564                }
9565                if let Some(sink) = self.forward_receipt_sink.get() {
9566                    sink.receipts(pseudonym, receipts.seq, receipts.first_seq, &receipts.tags);
9567                }
9568                FORWARD_RECEIPTS_RECEIVED.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9569                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9570                METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["processed"], 1);
9571                return Ok(DispatchResult::Processed);
9572            }
9573
9574            // This is a Start protocol message, so we send it to the handler, with the packet info
9575            // and what the packet did to the SURB store. `StartSession` parks on admission, so it
9576            // gets its own lane; a flood of it must not delay a live Session's control traffic.
9577            trace!("dispatching Start protocol message");
9578            let is_session_lane = matches!(msg, HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(_));
9579            let lane = if is_session_lane {
9580                self.start_session_tx.get()
9581            } else {
9582                self.start_control_tx.get()
9583            };
9584
9585            if let Some(lane) = lane {
9586                match lane.try_send((pseudonym, msg, in_data.packet_info, unbooked, tracing::Span::current())) {
9587                    Ok(()) => {}
9588                    // Backpressure, not a fault: rate-limited so a sustained flood cannot become
9589                    // per-packet log spam. Control drops keep their own counter, so a StartSession
9590                    // flood cannot hide a lost SsaCommit, which is unrecoverable.
9591                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
9592                        let counter = if is_session_lane {
9593                            &crate::counters::START_PROTOCOL_SEND_DROPS
9594                        } else {
9595                            &crate::counters::START_CONTROL_SEND_DROPS
9596                        };
9597                        let prev = counter.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9598                        if is_full_queue_warn_due(prev) {
9599                            let lane = if is_session_lane { "session" } else { "control" };
9600                            warn!(
9601                                %pseudonym,
9602                                lane,
9603                                total_start_queue_full_drops = prev + 1,
9604                                "Start protocol lane full, dropping message (backpressure)"
9605                            );
9606                        }
9607                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9608                        {
9609                            let lane = if is_session_lane {
9610                                "dropped_start_session_queue_full"
9611                            } else {
9612                                "dropped_start_control_queue_full"
9613                            };
9614                            METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&[lane], 1);
9615                        }
9616                        return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StartQueueFull));
9617                    }
9618                    // A closed queue means the manager is shutting down, which is a real fault.
9619                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
9620                        crate::counters::START_PROTOCOL_SEND_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9621                        return Err(
9622                            SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("Start protocol queue is closed")).into(),
9623                        );
9624                    }
9625                }
9626            } else {
9627                return Err(SessionManagerError::NotStarted.into());
9628            }
9629
9630            #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9631            METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["processed"], 1);
9632
9633            return Ok(DispatchResult::Processed);
9634        } else if in_data.data.application_tag == SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG {
9635            // This is traffic that belongs to one of the Sessions
9636            let session_id = pseudonym;
9637
9638            return if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
9639                trace!(%session_id, "received data for a registered session");
9640
9641                // Recorded here rather than once the Session reads the packet, because the send
9642                // below can drop it for local backpressure and the reader would never see it. What
9643                // the counterparty says about its own SURB supply is the override on the organic
9644                // SURB gate, so losing it to a full inbox would leave production shut off on an
9645                // estimate the counterparty has just contradicted.
9646                if matches!(&session_slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }) {
9647                    session_slot
9648                        .surb_mgmt
9649                        .observe_counterparty_signals(in_data.packet_info.signals_from_sender);
9650                }
9651
9652                // A detached slot's data plane is gone and its sender may still have room: whatever
9653                // arrives now belongs to the Session that ended, and the successor locks onto its own
9654                // stream. Dropped here, quietly, like a packet for a sink that has closed.
9655                if session_slot.instance.is_superseded() {
9656                    trace!(%session_id, "dropping data for a session whose data plane is gone");
9657                    crate::counters::SESSION_INBOX_CLOSED_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9658                    #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9659                    METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_sink_closed"], 1);
9660                    return Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::SinkClosed));
9661                }
9662
9663                if let (Some(receipts), Some(tag)) =
9664                    (&session_slot.forward_receipts, in_data.packet_info.forward_receipt_tag)
9665                {
9666                    receipts.note(tag);
9667                }
9668
9669                match session_slot.session_tx.try_send(in_data) {
9670                    Ok(_) => {
9671                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9672                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["processed"], 1);
9673
9674                        Ok(DispatchResult::Processed)
9675                    }
9676                    // Benign teardown race: the slot is still registered but its data sink was
9677                    // dropped. Quiet on purpose — see [`DropReason`].
9678                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Disconnected(_)) => {
9679                        trace!(%session_id, "dropping data for a session whose sink has closed");
9680                        crate::counters::SESSION_INBOX_CLOSED_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9681                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9682                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_sink_closed"], 1);
9683                        Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::SinkClosed))
9684                    }
9685                    // Genuine backpressure: the reader is not keeping up. Rate-limited so a
9686                    // sustained overload cannot become per-packet log spam.
9687                    Err(crossfire::TrySendError::Full(_)) => {
9688                        let prev =
9689                            crate::counters::SESSION_INBOX_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9690                        if is_full_queue_warn_due(prev) {
9691                            warn!(%session_id, total_inbox_full_drops = prev + 1, "session inbox full, dropping data (backpressure)");
9692                        }
9693                        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9694                        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_sink_full"], 1);
9695                        Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::SinkFull))
9696                    }
9697                }
9698            } else {
9699                // Fully deregistered session: packets still in flight for a torn-down session.
9700                // Quiet — see [`DropReason::Unregistered`].
9701                trace!(%session_id, "dropping data for an unregistered session");
9702                crate::counters::SESSION_UNKNOWN_DATA_DROPS.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9703                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9704                METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["dropped_unregistered"], 1);
9705                Ok(DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::Unregistered))
9706            };
9707        }
9708
9709        trace!(tag = %in_data.data.application_tag, "received data not associated with session protocol or any existing session");
9710
9711        crate::counters::SESSION_UNRELATED_DATA_DISPATCHES.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
9712
9713        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
9714        METRIC_DISPATCHED_MSGS.increment_by(&["unrelated"], 1);
9715
9716        Ok(DispatchResult::Unrelated(in_data))
9717    }

9719    /// Installs a bounded Start queue without workers and returns a drain operation for benchmarks.
9720    ///
9721    /// Keeping dequeue work outside the timed section makes dispatch measurements independent of
9722    /// worker scheduling. Returns `AlreadyStarted` if a processing queue is already installed.
9723    #[cfg(any(feature = "benchmark", test))]
9724    pub fn benchmark_start_queue(&self, capacity: usize) -> errors::Result<impl FnMut() -> usize + use<S>> {
9725        let (session_tx, session_rx) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async(capacity);
9726        let (control_tx, control_rx) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async(capacity);
9727        self.start_session_tx
9728            .set(session_tx)
9729            .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
9730        self.start_control_tx
9731            .set(control_tx)
9732            .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::AlreadyStarted)?;
9733        Ok(move || {
9734            let mut drained = 0;
9735            while session_rx.try_recv().is_ok() {
9736                drained += 1;
9737            }
9738            while control_rx.try_recv().is_ok() {
9739                drained += 1;
9740            }
9741            drained
9742        })
9743    }

9745    /// Pre-populates the sessions cache with a session slot for benchmarking.
9746    ///
9747    /// Intended for benchmarks that need a session to exist before calling
9748    /// [`SessionManager::dispatch_message`].
9749    ///
9750    /// Requires the `"benchmark"` feature (or a test build).
9751    #[cfg(any(feature = "benchmark", test))]
9752    pub fn pre_populate_session(&self, session_id: SessionId, routing_opts: DestinationRouting) {
9753        let (session_tx, _) =
9754            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(self.cfg.session_forward_capacity);
9755        let slot = SessionSlot {
9756            session_tx,
9757            routing_opts,
9758            abort_handles: Default::default(),
9759            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default()),
9760            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
9761            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
9762            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
9763            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
9764            pix_fill: Default::default(),
9765            exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
9766            returned_packets: Default::default(),
9767            // Never PIX, so there is no reconstructor state to charge for.
9768            cycle_budget: None,
9769            admission_token: Default::default(),
9770            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
9771            forward_receipts: None,
9772            exit_resume: Default::default(),
9773            instance: SlotInstance::new(0),
9774            opening: None,
9775        };
9776        self.sessions.insert(session_id, slot);
9777        self.slot_allocated
9778            .lock()
9779            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
9780            .remove(&session_id);
9781    }

9824    /// Charges `params`' worth of reconstructor state against the node-wide budget.
9825    ///
9826    /// Returns `None` if the node has already committed to as much as
9827    /// [`IncomingSessionPixConfig::max_live_cycle_bytes`] allows — the caller must then refuse the
9828    /// Session, because nothing later in establishment can give the memory back.
9829    ///
9830    /// A CAS loop rather than an unconditional `fetch_add` with a rollback: an add that is
9831    /// provisionally over the ceiling is briefly visible to every concurrent initiation, and with
9832    /// enough of them arriving at once the budget would appear exhausted to Sessions that do fit.
9833    fn reserve_cycle_budget(&self, params: &PixParams, ssas_per_request: usize) -> Option<Arc<CycleBudgetReservation>> {
9834        let bytes = cycle_budget_for(params, ssas_per_request);
9835        let ceiling = self.cfg.pix_config.max_live_cycle_bytes;
9836
9837        self.live_cycle_bytes
9838            .fetch_update(Ordering::Relaxed, Ordering::Relaxed, |held| {
9839                held.checked_add(bytes).filter(|total| *total <= ceiling)
9840            })
9841            .ok()
9842            .map(|_| {
9843                // Reports only this reservation's own bytes, not an outstanding total. Initiations
9844                // are processed concurrently, so any total computed here can be published out of
9845                // order with another reservation's; the gauge adds instead, which commutes.
9846                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
9847                crate::telemetry::pix::record_cycle_bytes_reserved(bytes);
9848
9849                Arc::new(CycleBudgetReservation {
9850                    bytes,
9851                    outstanding: self.live_cycle_bytes.clone(),
9852                    released: std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false),
9853                })
9854            })
9855    }

9857    /// Asks the session server on what terms this Session may be admitted.
9858    ///
9859    /// Fails closed. A refusal, a server that does not answer in time, a full request channel and a
9860    /// dropped reply all end the Session here rather than falling back to the node's own terms:
9861    /// falling back would mean an overloaded or wedged server silently disables every rule the
9862    /// operator wrote, and the peer would be served on terms nobody chose.
9863    ///
9864    /// The two failure kinds are reported differently because they call for different responses. A
9865    /// server that answered `Err` has decided, and re-asking will not change the answer, so the peer
9866    /// is told [`StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted`]. Everything else is this node being unable to
9867    /// ask right now, which is transient, so the peer is told [`StartErrorReason::Busy`] and may
9868    /// retry.
9869    ///
9870    /// A node with no session server has nobody to ask, and admits on its own terms.
9871    async fn request_admission(
9872        &self,
9873        session_id: SessionId,
9874        req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
9875        offered: Option<PixParams>,
9876    ) -> Result<SessionAdmissionDecision, StartErrorReason> {
9877        let Some(admission_tx) = self.admission_tx.get() else {
9878            return Ok(SessionAdmissionDecision::default());
9879        };
9880
9881        let (reply_tx, reply_rx) = oneshot::channel();
9882        // The capability bits travel as the peer sent them; the offer travels decoded, since the
9883        // wire encoding is this crate's to read and the server has no business unpacking it.
9884        let request = SessionAdmissionRequest::new(session_id, req.target.clone(), req.capabilities.0.bits());
9885        let request = match offered {
9886            Some(params) => request.with_offer(OfferedIncentivization::new(
9887                params.polys_per_ssa(),
9888                params.shares_per_poly(),
9889                params.surplus_shares(),
9890                pix_params_to_quota(&params),
9891            )),
9892            None => request,
9893        };
9894
9895        // A permit bounds how many requests may be in flight at the server at once, so a slow server
9896        // makes the excess wait here rather than in its own queue. The two waits below share one
9897        // deadline, so a request the node spent on queuing is left that much less for the round trip
9898        // and answers `Busy` — a transient failure the peer retries.
9899        let deadline = futures_time::time::Instant::now() + self.cfg.session_admission_timeout.into();
9900        let Ok(_permit) = self.admission_permits.acquire().timeout(deadline).await else {
9901            // Any peer can trigger this, so it must not become the log at one line per refusal.
9902            debug!(%session_id, "session admission is saturated; refusing the session as busy");
9903            return Err(StartErrorReason::Busy);
9904        };
9905
9906        // `try_send` rather than an awaited send: waiting for room in the queue would hold this
9907        // initiation past the peer's own timeout, and the queue being full is exactly the condition
9908        // the bound exists to report.
9909        if let Err(error) = admission_tx.lock().try_send((request, reply_tx)) {
9910            warn!(
9911                %session_id,
9912                %error,
9913                "cannot ask the session server to admit this session; refusing it as busy"
9914            );
9915            return Err(StartErrorReason::Busy);
9916        }
9917
9918        match reply_rx.timeout(deadline).await {
9919            Ok(Ok(Ok(decision))) => Ok(decision),
9920            Ok(Ok(Err(error))) => {
9921                debug!(%session_id, %error, "the session server refused this session's target");
9922                Err(StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted)
9923            }
9924            // The server dropped the reply without answering, which is a bug in it rather than a
9925            // decision, so it is reported as transient like the timeout it resembles.
9926            Ok(Err(_)) => {
9927                error!(
9928                    %session_id,
9929                    "the session server dropped an admission request without answering it"
9930                );
9931                Err(StartErrorReason::Busy)
9932            }
9933            Err(_) => {
9934                warn!(
9935                    %session_id,
9936                    timeout = ?self.cfg.session_admission_timeout,
9937                    "the session server did not decide in time; refusing the session as busy"
9938                );
9939                Err(StartErrorReason::Busy)
9940            }
9941        }
9942    }
9943
9944    /// Checks the offer against the terms this Session was admitted on.
9945    ///
9946    /// Judged against `policy` — the node's configuration as narrowed by the session server's
9947    /// decision for this Session — rather than against the node's configuration directly, which is
9948    /// what makes the accepted quota a property of the target as well as of the node.
9949    ///
9950    /// `offered` is what [`decode_pix_offer`] read, so this is only the
9951    /// policy question; the wire has already been judged.
9952    ///
9953    /// Returns the validated parameters and selected SSA batch size, or `None` if the offer cannot
9954    /// satisfy that policy.
9955    fn check_pix_params(
9956        &self,
9957        challenge: StartChallenge,
9958        offered: Option<PixParams>,
9959        policy: &EffectivePixAdmission,
9960    ) -> Option<(PixParams, usize)> {
9961        if let Some(params) = offered {
9962            let quota_per_ssa = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
9963            let ssas_per_request = policy.ssa_batch_size_for_quota(quota_per_ssa);
9964            let accepted_quota = ssas_per_request.and_then(|batch_size| quota_per_ssa.checked_mul(batch_size as u64));
9965            debug!(
9966                challenge,
9967                %params,
9968                acceptable_range = ?policy.quota_range,
9969                node_range = ?self.cfg.pix_config.quota_range,
9970                dynamic_batches = policy.allow_dynamic_ssa_batches,
9971                configured_max_ssas_per_request = policy.ssas_per_request,
9972                selected_ssas_per_request = ?ssas_per_request,
9973                offered_quota_mb_per_ssa = quota_per_ssa as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0),
9974                accepted_quota_mb = ?accepted_quota.map(|quota| quota as f64 / (1024.0 * 1024.0)),
9975                "client offered PIX SSA quota"
9976            );
9977
9978            // A window narrowed to nothing means the session server's rule and this node's envelope
9979            // do not overlap, which is a misconfiguration rather than a peer offering badly: no
9980            // offer whatsoever could have been accepted, so it is worth saying out loud once per
9981            // Session rather than leaving it to look like a rejected client.
9982            if ssas_per_request.is_none() && policy.quota_range.is_empty() {
9983                warn!(
9984                    challenge,
9985                    admitted_range = ?policy.quota_range,
9986                    node_range = ?self.cfg.pix_config.quota_range,
9987                    "the admitted quota range for this target is empty, so no offer can be accepted"
9988                );
9989            }
9990
9991            ssas_per_request.map(|batch_size| (params, batch_size))
9992        } else if policy.enforce_pix {
9993            // Client didn't offer PIX, but PIX is enforced
9994            None
9995        } else {
9996            // Client didn't offer PIX, and PIX is not enforced, so set default values
9997            // which are not going to be used.
9998            Some((DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS, 1))
9999        }
10000    }
10001
10002    /// Answers a refused `StartSession` with a `SessionError`, if the [`RefusalReplyBudget`] allows.
10003    ///
10004    /// Every refusal goes through here so that they share the one budget. A dropped reply is `Ok`:
10005    /// the refusal is carried out either way.
10006    async fn refuse_session_start(
10007        &self,
10008        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
10009        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10010        refusal: PixAdmissionRejection,
10011        reason: StartErrorReason,
10012        error_context: &'static str,
10013    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10014        let capabilities = session_req.capabilities.0;
10015        let kind = ExitControlKind::from(refusal);
10016        let session = ExitSessionKind::of(capabilities);
10017
10018        // Counted before the send: it counts decisions, and a struggling node's sends fail most.
10019        refusal.record_if_pix(capabilities);
10020
10021        // The per-refusal logs are `debug!` since a peer can provoke them for free; this rate-limited
10022        // summary is what shows at the default level.
10023        let refused_before = START_REFUSALS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
10024        if is_full_queue_warn_due(refused_before) {
10025            warn!(
10026                refused = refused_before + 1,
10027                dropped = START_REFUSAL_REPLY_DROPS.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
10028                last_reason = %refusal,
10029                "refusing StartSessions"
10030            );
10031        }
10032
10033        // Before the token, so a refusal that cannot be sent never spends one.
10034        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10035
10036        // Not refunded if the send fails: under backpressure a refund would hold every later refusal
10037        // for the send timeout, where a spent token drops them at once.
10038        if self.refusal_replies.as_ref().is_some_and(|bucket| !bucket.try_take()) {
10039            let drops_so_far = START_REFUSAL_REPLY_DROPS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
10040            record_exit_control(kind, session, ExitControlOutcome::DroppedBudget);
10041            debug!(
10042                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10043                %refusal,
10044                error_context,
10045                "dropping a StartSession refusal: the refusal reply budget is spent"
10046            );
10047            if is_full_queue_warn_due(drops_so_far) {
10048                warn!(
10049                    dropped = drops_so_far + 1,
10050                    "refusal replies to StartSession are being dropped because the refusal reply budget is spent; \
10051                     requesters will time out instead of being told why"
10052                );
10053            }
10054            return Ok(());
10055        }
10056
10057        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(StartErrorType {
10058            identifier: ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(session_req.challenge),
10059            reason,
10060        });
10061        match send_via_msg_sender(&mut msg_sender, reply_routing, data, error_context).await {
10062            Ok(()) => {
10063                record_exit_control(kind, session, ExitControlOutcome::Sent);
10064                #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
10065                METRIC_SENT_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
10066                Ok(())
10067            }
10068            Err(error) => {
10069                record_exit_control(kind, session, ExitControlOutcome::SendFailed);
10070                Err(error)
10071            }
10072        }
10073    }
10074
10075    /// Refuses a PIX offer whose initiation packet carried a SURB with a direct (0-hop) return path.
10076    ///
10077    /// A PIX share is decrypted with the acknowledgement of the return path's first relayer, and a
10078    /// direct return path has none, so the Entry mints such SURBs share-less and the Session could never
10079    /// make PIX progress (RFC-0012, Appendix 2). A conforming Entry refuses to offer PIX over one in
10080    /// `new_session`; without this check, a non-conforming one would be served until the commitment
10081    /// deadline closed the Session as `CommitmentTimeout`, a reason that names the clock rather than
10082    /// the fault.
10083    ///
10084    /// The hop count is the SURB creator's word (its declared Proof-of-Relay chain length), so this
10085    /// turns a misconfigured Entry away early rather than bounding a malicious one — the egress gate
10086    /// does that. Only the initiation packet is inspected: a conforming Entry keeps its return-path
10087    /// hop count for the lifetime of the Session. A node with no PIX support lets the offer through, so
10088    /// `handle_incoming_session_initiation` refuses it for that more fundamental reason.
10089    ///
10090    /// Returns `true` if the offer was refused; the `SessionError` is sent only if the refusal reply
10091    /// budget allows (see [`refuse_session_start`](Self::refuse_session_start)).
10092    async fn refuse_pix_over_direct_return_path(
10093        &self,
10094        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
10095        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10096        min_return_path_hops: Option<u8>,
10097    ) -> errors::Result<bool> {
10098        if !session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX)
10099            || min_return_path_hops != Some(0)
10100            || self.pix_toolbox.get().is_none()
10101        {
10102            return Ok(false);
10103        }
10104
10105        debug!(
10106            challenge = session_req.challenge,
10107            "client offered PIX over a direct return path"
10108        );
10109        self.refuse_session_start(
10110            DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()),
10111            session_req,
10112            PixAdmissionRejection::DirectReturnPath,
10113            StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
10114            "session error due to a PIX offer over a direct return path",
10115        )
10116        .await?;
10117        Ok(true)
10118    }
10119
10120    /// Records `challenge` as the highest used under `pseudonym`, keeping the larger of it and any
10121    /// concurrent record.
10122    fn note_challenge(&self, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, challenge: StartChallenge) {
10123        note_challenge_in(&self.last_challenges, pseudonym, challenge);
10124    }
10125
10126    /// The SURB buffer target an Exit Session works to, from the raw figure its Entry announced (the
10127    /// lower 32 bits of the initiation's options): the figure clamped to the node's maximum, or the
10128    /// balancer-rate fallback when none was announced. See where `handle_incoming_session_initiation`
10129    /// uses it for what the fallback does and does not serve.
10130    fn resolved_surb_target(&self, announced: u32) -> u64 {
10131        if announced > 0 {
10132            (announced as u64).min(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64)
10133        } else {
10134            self.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
10135                * self
10136                    .cfg
10137                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
10138                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
10139                    .as_secs()
10140        }
10141    }
10142
10143    /// A fresh ingress channel for the data plane of an Exit Session: the sender dispatch feeds, the
10144    /// stream the `HoprSession` reads, and the handle that ends it (which drops the receiver, see
10145    /// [`DropAbortable`](hopr_utils::runtime::DropAbortable)).
10146    fn new_exit_ingress(
10147        &self,
10148    ) -> (
10149        crossfire::MTx<crossfire::mpsc::Array<ApplicationDataIn>>,
10150        impl futures::Stream<Item = ApplicationDataIn> + Send + Unpin + 'static,
10151        AbortHandle,
10152    ) {
10153        let (session_tx, session_rx) =
10154            crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(self.cfg.session_forward_capacity);
10155        let (session_rx, session_rx_ah) = hopr_utils::runtime::DropAbortable::new(session_rx.into_stream());
10156        (session_tx, session_rx, session_rx_ah)
10157    }
10158
10159    /// Builds the data plane of an Exit Session: the `HoprSession` that reads `session_rx` and writes
10160    /// back over the slot's return path, through the slot's PIX gate and SURB accounting.
10161    ///
10162    /// Used for a fresh Session and for a takeover alike, so both are built the same way. Everything
10163    /// the plane shares with the rest of the Session comes from `slot` (the gate, the SURB estimator
10164    /// and balancer state, the fill control, the loss signal, and the egress limiter in its
10165    /// [`ExitTerms`]); what is specific to this plane is passed in: its ingress, its `instance` and the
10166    /// closure notifier that reports for that instance, and the SURB buffer the Entry announced, which
10167    /// sizes the egress buffer.
10168    ///
10169    /// `stream_base` is `Some(base)` for a plane that replaces another on the same pseudonym: its socket
10170    /// sends from and expects `base`. A fresh Session has no predecessor, and passes `None`.
10171    ///
10172    /// A rate-controlled Session (every one without [`Capability::NoRateControl`]) writes through the
10173    /// SURB reserve hold and the rate limiter; a `NoRateControl` one still passes the PIX gate, since
10174    /// a Session that opts out of rate control is exactly the one that could drain the most service
10175    /// before funding, and leaving it ungated would make the predeposit budget optional.
10176    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
10177    fn build_exit_data_plane<Rx>(
10178        &self,
10179        slot: &SessionSlot,
10180        session_id: SessionId,
10181        capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities,
10182        session_rx: Rx,
10183        instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>,
10184        closure_notifier: ExitClosureNotifier,
10185        announced_surb_target: u64,
10186        stream_base: Option<u32>,
10187    ) -> errors::Result<HoprSession>
10188    where
10189        Rx: futures::Stream<Item = ApplicationDataIn> + Send + Unpin + 'static,
10190    {
10191        let msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10192        let reply_routing = slot.routing_opts.clone();
10193        let loss_signal = slot.exit_loss_signal.get().cloned();
10194        let config = HoprSessionConfig {
10195            stream_base,
10196            ..session_config(&self.cfg, capabilities.into())
10197        };
10198
10199        // Resolved once, here, rather than per packet: the gate was installed before this point,
10200        // so the egress path never has to look inside the `OnceLock` again.
10201        let egress_gate = slot.pix_egress_gate.get().cloned();
10202        let surb_estimator_tx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
10203        let surb_estimator_rx = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
10204        // Resolved per packet: `spawn_exit_keep_alive` publishes the control after this is built.
10205        let activity_tx = slot.pix_fill.clone();
10206        let activity_egress = slot.pix_fill.clone();
10207        let activity_rx = slot.pix_fill.clone();
10208
10209        let session = if let Some(egress_rate_control) = slot
10210            .exit_resume
10211            .terms
10212            .get()
10213            .and_then(|terms| terms.egress_rate_control.as_ref())
10214        {
10215            // Because of SURB scarcity, control the egress rate of incoming sessions
10216            HoprSession::new_with_surb_state(
10217                session_id,
10218                reply_routing,
10219                config,
10220                (
10221                    // Sent packets = SURB consumption estimate. Data is held back once the stock is down
10222                    // to the reserve for the keep-alives, but only after the Entry's first keep-alive has
10223                    // shown that a balancer on its side acts on what the Exit reports, and only if the
10224                    // Exit runs a keep-alive stream to hold it for (see `spawn_exit_keep_alive`). An
10225                    // Entry without a balancer runs this branch too, and what it announces says nothing
10226                    // either way: it announces no target, or the balancer-rate fallback if it predates
10227                    // that. The `NoRateControl` branch below has no such reserve.
10228                    exit_data_egress(
