10229                        msg_sender.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other),
10230                        session_id,
10231                        surb_estimator_tx,
10232                        slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
10233                        egress_gate,
10234                        self.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period.is_some() || slot.pix_supervisor.get().is_some(),
10235                        instance.clone(),
10236                    )
10237                    // Where the limiter releases a reply, so a burst draining slowly stays activity until it is out.
10238                    .with(move |item: EgressItem| {
10239                        note_exit_data_activity(&activity_egress);
10240                        futures::future::ready(Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(item))
10241                    })
10242                    .rate_limit_with_controller(egress_rate_control)
10243                    .buffer((2 * announced_surb_target) as usize)
10244                    // Outermost, so the write is noted on entry, ahead of the limiter that holds replies while
10245                    // the stock is thin.
10246                    .with(move |item: EgressItem| {
10247                        note_exit_data_activity(&activity_tx);
10248                        futures::future::ready(Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(item))
10249                    }),
10250                    // Received packets = SURB retrieval estimate. Session data packets only: the
10251                    // SURBs of a Start message, a keep-alive among them, are booked by
10252                    // `book_start_message_surbs`, from `dispatch_message`.
10253                    session_rx.inspect(move |data| {
10254                        note_exit_data_activity(&activity_rx);
10255                        // SURBs saved into the store, and older ones the full store evicted to make room.
10256                        let produced = data.num_surbs_with_msg() as u64;
10257                        let evicted = data.packet_info.num_evicted_surbs as u64;
10258                        account_incoming_surbs(&surb_estimator_rx, produced, evicted);
10259                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10260                        telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(&session_id, produced);
10261                    }),
10262                ),
10263                Some(closure_notifier),
10264                None,
10265                None,
10266                loss_signal,
10267            )?
10268        } else {
10269            let egress_instance = instance.clone();
10270            HoprSession::new_with_surb_state(
10271                session_id,
10272                reply_routing,
10273                config,
10274                (
10275                    msg_sender.sink_map_err(std::io::Error::other).with(
10276                        move |(routing, data): (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)| {
10277                            // Before the activity note and the SURB count: see `exit_data_egress`.
10278                            if egress_instance.is_superseded() {
10279                                return futures::future::Either::Left(std::future::ready(
10280                                    Err(superseded_write_error()),
10281                                ));
10282                            }
10283                            note_exit_data_activity(&activity_tx);
10284                            // Counted here too, though nothing on this branch balances anything. The
10285                            // estimate is what the fill reserve is measured against, and a reserve
10286                            // measured against a counter that only ever counts in one direction is a
10287                            // reserve that either never binds or never releases. `NoRateControl` is
10288                            // also the branch that can drain SURBs fastest, so it is the one where
10289                            // that matters most.
10290                            let data = count_return_packet_surb(&surb_estimator_tx, data);
10291                            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10292                            telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
10293                            acquire_egress_permit_for(&egress_instance, egress_gate.clone(), routing, data)
10294                        },
10295                    ),
10296                    session_rx.inspect(move |data| {
10297                        note_exit_data_activity(&activity_rx);
10298                        // SURBs saved into the store, and older ones the full store evicted to make room.
10299                        let produced = data.num_surbs_with_msg() as u64;
10300                        let evicted = data.packet_info.num_evicted_surbs as u64;
10301                        account_incoming_surbs(&surb_estimator_rx, produced, evicted);
10302                        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10303                        telemetry::record_session_surb_produced(&session_id, produced);
10304                    }),
10305                ),
10306                Some(closure_notifier),
10307                None,
10308                None,
10309                loss_signal,
10310            )?
10311        };
10312
10313        // What a takeover of this plane's Session computes the successor's stream base from.
10314        if let Some(progress) = session.stream_progress() {
10315            let _ = instance.stream_progress.set(progress);
10316        }
10317
10318        Ok(session.with_slot_instance(instance.id(), instance.refusal.clone()))
10319    }
10320
10321    /// Hands a paid Exit PIX Session, which a client has come back for, to its new data plane: the
10322    /// takeover half of [`handle_incoming_session_initiation`](Self::handle_incoming_session_initiation).
10323    ///
10324    /// The slot's *control plane* is kept as it is: the supervisor, the egress gate, the action driver
10325    /// with its commitment guards, the deposit observers, the cycle-budget reservation, the SURB
10326    /// admission and ring, the balancer, the keep-alive stream and the PIX fill. Only the *data
10327    /// plane* is replaced (`session_tx` and the ingress handle, the `HoprSession` and the
10328    /// `IncomingSession` the session server gets). So nothing here spawns a supervisor, asks for an
10329    /// SSA, reserves budget or commits the slot: from the PIX layer's view the Session simply carries
10330    /// on, and the next PIX message is the SSA request of the next cycle. A takeover never sends an
10331    /// opening `SsaRequest`; the Entry, which sees none, carries its ledger on.
10332    ///
10333    /// In order:
10334    ///
10335    /// 1. The held slot must be eligible ([`SessionSlot::takeover_refusal`]): the Session is a frame-based one on the
10336    ///    stateless socket, and a stream base fits above its stream (see [`successor_stream_base`]). Else the request
10337    ///    is refused with [`PixAdmissionRejection::TakeoverIneligible`] (`NotResumable` on the wire), and the slot is
10338    ///    not touched. Eligibility is the pseudonym alone: whoever starts a Session under it, with a greater challenge,
10339    ///    takes it over. See hoprnet#8723 for binding a takeover to a secret of the original Entry.
10340    /// 2. The new data plane is built, but handed to nobody yet.
10341    /// 3. The swap is one compute on the slot: the slot must still be the instance that was judged and have a live
10342    ///    control plane. In it the old instance is superseded (its writes fail), the window timer is cleared, the new
10343    ///    ingress handle goes in (which aborts the old one), and telemetry ownership is handed over. The supervisor
10344    ///    stays told the data plane is detached. A loser of a race (a concurrent takeover, an expired window, an
10345    ///    operator close, an eviction) drops its plane, which nobody has seen, and is refused.
10346    /// 4. The newly announced SURB target is applied, unless the new instance has ended already (it is then closed,
10347    ///    scoped to its instance, and nothing is sent).
10348    /// 5. `SessionResumed`, naming the stream base, is sent in place of `SessionEstablished`. If the send fails the new
10349    ///    instance is *detached* (the window applies again) rather than closing the funded control plane with it.
10350    /// 6. Unless the instance has been replaced meanwhile, the plane is delivered to the session server. On failure the
10351    ///    instance is detached as above and the Entry is sent a `Busy` error addressed by its challenge.
10352    /// 7. Only then is the data plane attached, which lets the supervisor issue the successor requests it deferred.
10353    async fn take_over_session(
10354        &self,
10355        session_id: SessionId,
10356        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10357        client_params: PixParams,
10358        ssas_per_request: usize,
10359        held: SessionSlot,
10360    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10361        let reply_routing = held.routing_opts.clone();
10362
10363        if let Some(why) = held.takeover_refusal(
10364            session_req.challenge,
10365            &client_params,
10366            ssas_per_request,
10367            session_req.capabilities.0,
10368            session_req.additional_data,
10369        ) {
10370            debug!(
10371                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10372                %session_id,
10373                why,
10374                "refusing a PIX session: the pseudonym's held session cannot be taken over"
10375            );
10376            return self
10377                .refuse_takeover(session_req, reply_routing, "held session not eligible")
10378                .await;
10379        }
10380
10381        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10382        let (new_session_notifier, close_session_notifier) = self
10383            .session_notifiers
10384            .get()
10385            .cloned()
10386            .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10387
10388        // The Entry's idle timeout is not re-read: the idle-notify cap of the kept fill stream was set
10389        // from the first establishment's, and a client reconnecting in place is the same process with
10390        // the same configuration. A different one is bounded all the same: the cap only lengthens the
10391        // report period of an idle Session, and any data brings the base period back at once.
10392        let surb_target = initiation_options(session_req.additional_data) as u32;
10393        let announced_surb_target = self.resolved_surb_target(surb_target);
10394
10395        // Both sockets of the successor number its stream from a base above every frame id the predecessor's
10396        // used, so that nothing of the predecessor's, a close marker included, can pass for the successor's.
10397        let Some(stream_base) = successor_stream_base(&held.instance) else {
10398            debug!(
10399                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10400                %session_id,
10401                "refusing a PIX session: no stream base above the held session's stream fits"
10402            );
10403            return self
10404                .refuse_takeover(
10405                    session_req,
10406                    reply_routing,
10407                    "no stream base above the held session's stream",
10408                )
10409                .await;
10410        };
10411
10412        let (new_tx, new_rx, new_ingress) = self.new_exit_ingress();
10413        let instance = SlotInstance::new_with(
10414            session_req.challenge,
10415            session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::Resumable),
10416        );
10417        let session = self.build_exit_data_plane(
10418            &held,
10419            session_id,
10420            session_req.capabilities,
10421            new_rx,
10422            &instance,
10423            exit_closure_notifier(close_session_notifier, instance.clone()),
10424            announced_surb_target,
10425            Some(stream_base),
10426        )?;
10427
10428        // The swap. The closure runs once, under the key's lock, so it serialises against a detach, a
10429        // drain, a removal and another takeover; everything that must be atomic with the swap is done
10430        // in it. The plane is not handed to anyone yet, so a loser has written and sent nothing.
10431        let observed = held.instance.clone();
10432        let mut new_ingress = Some(new_ingress);
10433        let mut new_tx = Some(new_tx);
10434        let mut taken_over = None;
10435        self.sessions
10436            .entry(session_id)
10437            .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| {
10438                let Some(entry) = entry.filter(|entry| {
10439                    Arc::ptr_eq(&entry.value().instance, &observed) && entry.value().control_plane_is_live()
10440                }) else {
10441                    return moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop;
10442                };
10443                let old = entry.value();
10444
10445                // The old plane's writers fail from here on (see `superseded_write_error`), and a
10446                // writer of it parked on the gate is not released onto the new plane.
10447                old.instance.supersede();
10448                old.exit_resume
10449                    .detached
10450                    .store(false, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
10451                if let Some(gate) = old.pix_egress_gate.get() {
10452                    // The supervisor's level stays detached until `attach_data_plane`, after `SessionResumed`
10453                    // and the delivery, so that no successor request precedes them. A live predecessor is
10454                    // held the same way.
10455                    gate.set_data_plane_detached(true);
10456                }
10457                {
10458                    let mut handles = old.abort_handles.lock();
10459                    handles.abort_one(&SessionHandles::ResumeWindow);
10460                    // Aborts the old ingress under the same key: the old reader gets EOF.
10461                    if let Some(ingress) = new_ingress.take() {
10462                        handles.insert(SessionHandles::Ingress, ingress);
10463                    }
10464                }
10465                // Established before the slot is visible, so that a detach or a second takeover that
10466                // follows at once finds an instance that counts.
10467                instance.mark_established();
10468                #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10469                telemetry::adopt_session_metrics(&session_id, instance.id());
10470
10471                taken_over = Some(());
10472                moka::ops::compute::Op::Put(SessionSlot {
10473                    session_tx: new_tx.take().expect("the swap closure runs once"),
10474                    instance: instance.clone(),
10475                    // The repeat of this attempt is answered with the same `SessionResumed`.
10476                    opening: Some(Arc::new(ExitOpening {
10477                        challenge: session_req.challenge,
10478                        answered_repeats: Default::default(),
10479                        resumed_stream_base: Some(stream_base),
10480                    })),
10481                    ..old.clone()
10482                })
10483            });
10484
10485        if taken_over.is_none() {
10486            // Lost a race, or the slot went away: the plane was never handed out, and is dropped.
10487            if let Some(ingress) = new_ingress.take() {
10488                ingress.abort();
10489            }
10490            instance.supersede();
10491            drop(session);
10492            return self
10493                .refuse_takeover_with(
10494                    session_req,
10495                    reply_routing,
10496                    PixAdmissionRejection::Busy,
10497                    StartErrorReason::Busy,
10498                    "held session changed under the takeover",
10499                )
10500                .await;
10501        }
10502
10503        // The plane may have ended on its own between its construction and the swap, which made it the
10504        // current instance: the Entry is not told it has a Session that is already over. The end is carried
10505        // out now, for this instance only and by the rules a report of it would have been handled by (a
10506        // client's end detaches, within the window). Past this point, the session server is the only one
10507        // that can end it, and its report is handled as it arrives, since the instance is current.
10508        if let Some(reason) = instance.ended_with() {
10509            warn!(
10510                %session_id,
10511                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10512                ?reason,
10513                "the taken over session ended before it took the slot — not confirming it"
10514            );
10515            self.close_session_scoped(&session_id, reason, CloseScope::Instance(&instance));
10516            return Ok(());
10517        }
10518
10519        let new_slot = self.sessions.get(&session_id);
10520        if let Some(new_slot) = &new_slot {
10521            self.apply_announced_surb_target(new_slot, session_id, surb_target as u64);
10522        }
10523
10524        let established = HoprStartProtocol::SessionResumed(StartResumed {
10525            orig_challenge: session_req.challenge,
10526            session_id,
10527            stream_base,
10528        });
10529        if let Err(error) = count_exit_control_send(
10530            ExitControlKind::SessionEstablished,
10531            ExitSessionKind::of(session_req.capabilities.0),
10532            send_counted_via_msg_sender(
10533                &mut msg_sender,
10534                reply_routing.clone(),
10535                established,
10536                &held.surb_estimator,
10537                &session_id,
10538                "session resumption message of a taken over session",
10539            )
10540            .await,
10541        ) {
10542            // The Entry has not been told. The control plane is paid for and is not to be destroyed
10543            // for that: the new instance is detached and its window applies as it would have after
10544            // any other end of a data plane. Where detaching is off, the close is the ordinary one.
10545            warn!(%session_id, %error, "could not answer a takeover — detaching the session again");
10546            self.detach_taken_over(&session_id, &instance);
10547            drop(session);
10548            return Err(error);
10549        }
10550
10551        // The send may have been pending while another takeover, a close or an eviction replaced this instance: its
10552        // plane is then not handed out, as with a lost swap, and the replacement is left to answer for the Session.
10553        if instance.is_superseded()
10554            || !self
10555                .sessions
10556                .get(&session_id)
10557                .is_some_and(|slot| Arc::ptr_eq(&slot.instance, &instance))
10558        {
10559            warn!(
10560                %session_id,
10561                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10562                "the taken over session was replaced while it was being answered — not delivering it"
10563            );
10564            drop(session);
10565            return Ok(());
10566        }
10567
10568        let incoming_session = IncomingSession {
10569            id: session_id,
10570            session,
10571            target: session_req.target.clone(),
10572        };
10573        let delivered = async {
10574            let mut guard = new_session_notifier.lock().await;
10575            guard.send(incoming_session).await
10576        }
10577        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
10578        .await;
10579        let failure = match delivered {
10580            Ok(Ok(())) => None,
10581            Err(_) => {
10582                error!(%session_id, "timeout to notify about a taken over incoming session");
10583                Some(TransportSessionError::Timeout)
10584            }
10585            Ok(Err(error)) => {
10586                error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to notify about a taken over incoming session");
10587                Some(SessionManagerError::other(error).into())
10588            }
10589        };
10590        if let Some(failure) = failure {
10591            // The Entry has been told, so this is no refusal: the new instance waits out the window as after
10592            // a failed answer, and successor requests stay deferred.
10593            #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10594            telemetry::pix::record_resumption(telemetry::pix::PixResumption::Refused);
10595            self.detach_taken_over(&session_id, &instance);
10596            // The Entry closes exactly this instance and can reconnect, which can take over the detached Session.
10597            self.notify_session_error(
10598                session_id,
10599                ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(instance.challenge),
10600                reply_routing,
10601                StartErrorReason::Busy,
10602                "session error due to a taken over session that could not be delivered",
10603            )
10604            .await;
10605            return Err(failure);
10606        }
10607
10608        // Only now may the supervisor issue what it deferred: after `SessionResumed`, with the plane in the
10609        // session server's hands.
10610        self.attach_data_plane(&session_id, &instance);
10611
10612        info!(
10613            %session_id,
10614            challenge = session_req.challenge,
10615            stream_base,
10616            "session taken over"
10617        );
10618        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10619        telemetry::pix::record_resumption(telemetry::pix::PixResumption::TakenOver);
10620        Ok(())
10621    }
10622
10623    /// Detaches a taken-over `instance` whose answer or delivery failed, or closes it, scoped to it, when it cannot
10624    /// be detached (it is already ending, or has gone to another instance).
10625    fn detach_taken_over(&self, session_id: &SessionId, instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>) {
10626        // A takeover only happens with a window above zero (see the caller), so this detaches.
10627        let window = self.cfg.pix_config.resume_window;
10628        if self.detach_instance(session_id, instance, window, true).is_none() {
10629            self.close_session_scoped(session_id, ClosureReason::EmptyRead, CloseScope::Instance(instance));
10630        }
10631    }
10632
10633    /// Tells the supervisor the data plane of `instance` is attached, unless it has been detached again or is no
10634    /// longer the slot's instance. Under the slot's key, so it is ordered against a detach.
10635    fn attach_data_plane(&self, session_id: &SessionId, instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>) {
10636        self.sessions
10637            .entry(*session_id)
10638            .and_compute_with(|entry: Option<moka::Entry<SessionId, SessionSlot>>| {
10639                if let Some(entry) = entry.filter(|entry| Arc::ptr_eq(&entry.value().instance, instance)) {
10640                    let slot = entry.value();
10641                    if !slot.is_detached() {
10642                        if let Some(gate) = slot.pix_egress_gate.get() {
10643                            gate.set_data_plane_detached(false);
10644                        }
10645                        if let Some(supervisor) = slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
10646                            // A wake-up for an idle worker; the level is on the gate.
10647                            let _ = supervisor.try_send_event(SessionPixEvent::DataPlaneChanged);
10648                        }
10649                    }
10650                }
10651                moka::ops::compute::Op::Nop
10652            });
10653    }
10654
10655    /// Answers a resume request that carries the challenge of the `held` instance: `NoSlotsAvailable`, as an
10656    /// occupied pseudonym is, while that instance still holds the slot, and `NotResumable` once it is gone,
10657    /// since a resume request must never allocate a fresh Session.
10658    async fn refuse_duplicate_resume(
10659        &self,
10660        session_id: SessionId,
10661        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10662        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
10663        held: &SessionSlot,
10664    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10665        if self
10666            .sessions
10667            .get(&session_id)
10668            .is_some_and(|now| Arc::ptr_eq(&now.instance, &held.instance))
10669        {
10670            return self
10671                .refuse_session_start(
10672                    reply_routing,
10673                    session_req,
10674                    PixAdmissionRejection::NoSessionSlot,
10675                    StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable,
10676                    "session error message due to lack of slots",
10677                )
10678                .await;
10679        }
10680        self.refuse_session_start(
10681            reply_routing,
10682            session_req,
10683            PixAdmissionRejection::NotResumable,
10684            StartErrorReason::NotResumable,
10685            "session error due to a resume request without a resumable session",
10686        )
10687        .await
10688    }
10689
10690    /// Refuses a takeover of an ineligible held Session: `NotResumable` on the wire and
10691    /// [`PixAdmissionRejection::TakeoverIneligible`] in the metrics.
10692    async fn refuse_takeover(
10693        &self,
10694        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10695        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
10696        error_context: &'static str,
10697    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10698        self.refuse_takeover_with(
10699            session_req,
10700            reply_routing,
10701            PixAdmissionRejection::TakeoverIneligible,
10702            StartErrorReason::NotResumable,
10703            error_context,
10704        )
10705        .await
10706    }
10707
10708    /// Refuses a takeover of a held Session with the given metric label and wire reason, counting it as a refusal.
10709    async fn refuse_takeover_with(
10710        &self,
10711        session_req: &StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10712        reply_routing: DestinationRouting,
10713        rejection: PixAdmissionRejection,
10714        reason: StartErrorReason,
10715        error_context: &'static str,
10716    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10717        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
10718        telemetry::pix::record_resumption(telemetry::pix::PixResumption::Refused);
10719        self.refuse_session_start(reply_routing, session_req, rejection, reason, error_context)
10720            .await
10721    }
10722
10723    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, session_req))]
10724    async fn handle_incoming_session_initiation(
10725        &self,
10726        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
10727        session_req: StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>,
10728    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
10729        trace!(challenge = session_req.challenge, "received session initiation request");
10730
10731        let resume_requested = announced_resume_attempt(session_req.additional_data);
10732
10733        debug!("got new session request, searching for a free session slot");
10734
10735        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10736
10737        // Reply routing uses SURBs only with the pseudonym of this Session's ID
10738        let reply_routing = DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into());
10739
10740        // Reject UsePIX if this node is not configured with a PixToolbox
10741        // (e.g. relay nodes that do not participate in PIX processing).
10742        if self.pix_toolbox.get().is_none() && session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
10743            debug!(
10744                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10745                "client offered PIX but this node has no PIX support installed"
10746            );
10747            return self
10748                .refuse_session_start(
10749                    reply_routing,
10750                    &session_req,
10751                    PixAdmissionRejection::NoPixSupport,
10752                    StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
10753                    "session error due to missing PIX support",
10754                )
10755                .await;
10756        }
10757
10758        // Ask whoever runs the session server on what terms this target may be served, before
10759        // anything is allocated for the Session. This is the only place the target can influence
10760        // admission: the transport cannot read a sealed target, and by the time the server sees the
10761        // established Session the terms have already been fixed.
10762        // Read the offer before anyone is asked about it: an offer this node cannot read, or whose
10763        // curve it does not share, is refused without a round trip to the session server, and the
10764        // server is told what was offered rather than having to unpack the wire itself.
10765        let offered = match decode_pix_offer(&session_req) {
10766            Ok(offered) => offered,
10767            Err(reason) => {
10768                debug!(
10769                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
10770                    "client offered unacceptable PIX parameters"
10771                );
10772                return self
10773                    .refuse_session_start(
10774                        reply_routing,
10775                        &session_req,
10776                        PixAdmissionRejection::UnacceptableParams,
10777                        reason,
10778                        "session error message due to unacceptable PIX parameters",
10779                    )
10780                    .await;
10781            }
10782        };
10783
10784        // A resume request is only for a held PIX Session, with takeover enabled: anything else is refused
10785        // before anything is reserved, and the Entry continues under a fresh pseudonym.
10786        let held = if resume_requested {
10787            let held = (session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX)
10788                && !self.cfg.pix_config.resume_window.is_zero())
10789            .then(|| self.sessions.get(&pseudonym))
10790            .flatten()
10791            .filter(|held| {
10792                matches!(held.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Return(_)) && held.pix_supervisor.get().is_some()
10793            });
10794            if held.is_none() {
10795                debug!(
10796                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
10797                    "client asked to resume a Session this node does not hold or cannot resume"
10798                );
10799                return self
10800                    .refuse_session_start(
10801                        reply_routing,
10802                        &session_req,
10803                        PixAdmissionRejection::NotResumable,
10804                        StartErrorReason::NotResumable,
10805                        "session error due to a resume request without a resumable session",
10806                    )
10807                    .await;
10808            }
10809            held
10810        } else {
10811            None
10812        };
10813
10814        let session_id: SessionId = pseudonym;
10815
10816        // What does not depend on the admission result is judged first, so that a request that cannot take the
10817        // held Session over never asks the session server, and is told `NotResumable` rather than whatever
10818        // admission would have said. A request by the very challenge that established the held slot is a
10819        // duplicate: refused as an occupied pseudonym is while that instance still holds the slot, and
10820        // `NotResumable` once it is gone, since a resume attempt never allocates a fresh Session.
10821        if let Some(held) = &held {
10822            if held.instance.challenge == session_req.challenge {
10823                return self
10824                    .refuse_duplicate_resume(session_id, &session_req, reply_routing, held)
10825                    .await;
10826            }
10827            if let Some(why) = held.takeover_refusal_before_admission(
10828                session_req.challenge,
10829                offered.as_ref(),
10830                session_req.capabilities.0,
10831                session_req.additional_data,
10832            ) {
10833                debug!(
10834                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
10835                    %session_id,
10836                    why,
10837                    "refusing a PIX session: the pseudonym's held session cannot be taken over"
10838                );
10839                return self
10840                    .refuse_takeover(&session_req, reply_routing, "held session not eligible")
10841                    .await;
10842            }
10843        }
10844
10845        let admission = match self.request_admission(session_id, &session_req, offered).await {
10846            Ok(decision) => decision,
10847            Err(reason) => {
10848                // `request_admission` distinguishes these two on purpose — a refused target will not
10849                // be served however the request is phrased, while `Busy` is this node being unable
10850                // to ask right now and is worth retrying — so the aggregate keeps them apart too.
10851                let refusal = match reason {
10852                    StartErrorReason::TargetNotAdmitted => PixAdmissionRejection::TargetPolicy,
10853                    _ => PixAdmissionRejection::Busy,
10854                };
10855                return self
10856                    .refuse_session_start(
10857                        reply_routing,
10858                        &session_req,
10859                        refusal,
10860                        reason,
10861                        "session error due to a refused admission",
10862                    )
10863                    .await;
10864            }
10865        };
10866        let pix_policy = self.cfg.pix_config.effective_for(&admission);
10867
10868        // Verify the offer against the terms this Session was admitted on.
10869        let Some((client_params, ssas_per_request)) =
10870            self.check_pix_params(session_req.challenge, offered, &pix_policy)
10871        else {
10872            debug!(
10873                challenge = session_req.challenge,
10874                "client offered unacceptable PIX parameters"
10875            );
10876
10877            // A resume attempt for a held Session is refused as any ineligible takeover is: the Entry then forgets
10878            // its PIX state and switches pseudonym, where `UnacceptablePixParams` would have it retry the resume.
10879            if held.is_some() {
10880                return self
10881                    .refuse_takeover(
10882                        &session_req,
10883                        reply_routing,
10884                        "held terms no longer fit the admitted quota",
10885                    )
10886                    .await;
10887            }
10888
10889            // Notify the sender that the session could not be established
10890            return self
10891                .refuse_session_start(
10892                    reply_routing,
10893                    &session_req,
10894                    PixAdmissionRejection::UnacceptableParams,
10895                    StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
10896                    "session error message due to unacceptable PIX parameters",
10897                )
10898                .await;
10899        };
10900
10901        info!(params = %client_params, ssas_per_request, "client offered acceptable PIX parameters");
10902
10903        // A resume attempt (bit 33) for a held PIX Session is a client coming back for the Session it paid for.
10904        // Decided before anything is reserved, so that nothing is reserved twice: a takeover keeps the
10905        // slot's cycle budget, and a refusal reserves nothing. A request that is not an attempt never takes over.
10906        if let Some(held) = held {
10907            return self
10908                .take_over_session(session_id, &session_req, client_params, ssas_per_request, held)
10909                .await;
10910        }
10911
10912        // Charge this Session's reconstructor state against the node-wide budget before anything is
10913        // allocated for it. Only a PIX Session holds cycle state, so only a PIX Session is charged —
10914        // `check_pix_params` hands back nominal parameters for a peer that offered none, and
10915        // reserving on those would bill Sessions that never reconstruct anything.
10916        //
10917        // Refused here rather than at the successor request, which is the other place the ceiling
10918        // could be applied: by then the Entry has funded a cycle and refusing costs it that deposit,
10919        // whereas a Session refused now is one the peer can retry elsewhere at no charge.
10920        let cycle_budget = if session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX) {
10921            let Some(reservation) = self.reserve_cycle_budget(&client_params, ssas_per_request) else {
10922                debug!(
10923                    challenge = session_req.challenge,
10924                    requested = cycle_budget_for(&client_params, ssas_per_request),
10925                    outstanding = self.live_cycle_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
10926                    ceiling = self.cfg.pix_config.max_live_cycle_bytes,
10927                    "refusing a PIX session: the node's live reconstructor-cycle budget is exhausted"
10928                );
10929
10930                // The refusal this whole aggregate exists to separate from the one below. Both are
10931                // `NoSlotsAvailable` on the wire, but this one says the node is healthy and full of
10932                // reconstructor state, and the other says it is at its Session limit.
10933                return self
10934                    .refuse_session_start(
10935                        reply_routing,
10936                        &session_req,
10937                        PixAdmissionRejection::LiveCycleCapacity,
10938                        StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable,
10939                        "session error message due to an exhausted live-cycle budget",
10940                    )
10941                    .await;
10942            };
10943            Some(reservation)
10944        } else {
10945            None
10946        };
10947
10948        let (new_session_notifier, close_session_notifier) = self
10949            .session_notifiers
10950            .get()
10951            .cloned()
10952            .ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
10953
10954        // Use constant application tag for all sessions
10955        self.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
10956
10957        let (session_tx, session_rx, session_rx_ah) = self.new_exit_ingress();
10958
10959        let wants_forward_receipts =
10960            self.cfg.forward_receipts && session_req.additional_data & FORWARD_RECEIPTS_REQUESTED != 0;
10961        let forward_receipts = wants_forward_receipts.then(|| Arc::new(ExitReceipts::new(Instant::now())));
10962        let instance = SlotInstance::new_with(
10963            session_req.challenge,
10964            session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::Resumable),
10965        );
10966        let slot = SessionSlot {
10967            session_tx,
10968            routing_opts: reply_routing.clone(),
10969            abort_handles: Default::default(),
10970            surb_mgmt: Default::default(),
10971            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
10972            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
10973            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
10974            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
10975            pix_fill: Default::default(),
10976            exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
10977            returned_packets: Default::default(),
10978            cycle_budget,
10979            admission_token: Default::default(),
10980            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
10981            forward_receipts,
10982            exit_resume: Default::default(),
10983            instance: instance.clone(),
10984            opening: Some(Arc::new(ExitOpening {
10985                challenge: session_req.challenge,
10986                answered_repeats: Default::default(),
10987                resumed_stream_base: None,
10988            })),
10989        };
10990        slot.abort_handles.lock().insert(SessionHandles::Ingress, session_rx_ah);
10991        // What a takeover has to match, and the limiter the balancer and any successor data plane
10992        // share. Set before anything is built from the slot.
10993        let _ = slot.exit_resume.terms.set(ExitTerms {
10994            ssas_per_request,
10995            capabilities: session_req.capabilities.0,
10996            behaviour_bits: session_req.additional_data & INITIATION_BEHAVIOUR_BITS,
10997            egress_rate_control: (!session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::NoRateControl))
10998                .then(|| RateController::new(self.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate, Duration::from_secs(1))),
10999        });
11000
11001        // Insert the slot and get a guard. Any failure from here on rolls the slot
11002        // back, otherwise it would block this pseudonym until idle eviction. The atomic
11003        // insert (inside the helper) also prevents a TOCTOU race, so only one concurrent
11004        // request can claim the slot for a given pseudonym.
11005        let Some(mut slot_guard) = self.allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone()) else {
11006            // No slots available for this pseudonym
11007            debug!("no slots available for this pseudonym");
11008            return self
11009                .refuse_session_start(
11010                    reply_routing.clone(),
11011                    &session_req,
11012                    PixAdmissionRejection::NoSessionSlot,
11013                    StartErrorReason::NoSlotsAvailable,
11014                    "session error message due to lack of slots",
11015                )
11016                .await;
11017        };
11018
11019        debug!(?session_req, "assigned a new session");
11020
11021        // Stand the supervisor up before the `HoprSession` is constructed, so the egress adapters
11022        // below see a populated gate. Installing it afterwards would leave a window in which packets
11023        // are served ungated — small, but exactly the window an unfunded Entry would aim for.
11024        //
11025        // Its first `RequestSsa` action is deliberately *not* carried out here: the action driver
11026        // spawned after publication does it, which is what keeps `SessionEstablished` ahead of
11027        // `SsaRequest` on the wire.
11028        let pix: Option<ActionRx> = if self.pix_toolbox.get().is_some()
11029            && session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::UsePIX)
11030        {
11031            // We use the same dimensions the client offered.
11032            slot.current_ssa_state
11033                .set(SessionSsaState::new(client_params))
11034                .map_err(|_| SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("session pix state must be uninitialized")))?;
11035
11036            let supervisor_config = SupervisorConfig {
11037                ssas_per_request,
11038                ..self.cfg.pix_config.supervisor_config()
11039            };
11040            let (handle, action_rx) =
11041                spawn_supervisor_worker(supervisor_config, client_params, session_id, std::time::Instant::now());
11042
11043            let _ = slot.pix_egress_gate.set(handle.gate.clone());
11044            let _ = slot.pix_supervisor.set(handle);
11045            Some(action_rx)
11046        } else {
11047            None
11048        };
11049
11050        // The SURB buffer target the Entry asked for, resolved once for both branches below.
11051        //
11052        // The Session request carries a "hint" as additional data telling what the Session initiator
11053        // has configured as its target buffer size in the Balancer. The lower 32 bits of the options
11054        // word contain the SURB target; its upper 32 bits carry PIX parameters and must be masked out.
11055        //
11056        // Resolved even for an Entry that announces none (a `NoRateControl` one, or a rate-controlled one
11057        // without a SURB balancer), and on the `NoRateControl` branch, which runs no balancer: the Exit's
11058        // keep-alive stream derives its fill SURB reserve from this figure, and the fallback below — the
11059        // same one a rate-controlled Exit's balancer runs at — is the only estimate of the buffer there is.
11060        //
11061        // That fallback serves the balancer and the fill reserve only. It is not what the SURB ring is
11062        // sized from when nothing was announced: see `ring_surb_target` below.
11063        let surb_target = initiation_options(session_req.additional_data) as u32;
11064        let announced_surb_target = self.resolved_surb_target(surb_target);
11065
11066        // The Entry's idle timeout bounds how far the idle reports may back off, as they are what keeps its slot
11067        // alive (see `IDLE_NOTIFY_PERIODS_PER_IDLE_TIMEOUT`).
11068        let entry_idle_timeout = announced_idle_timeout(session_req.additional_data);
11069        let idle_notify_cap = session_idle_notify_cap(self.cfg.surb_idle_notify_period, entry_idle_timeout);
11070        if idle_notify_cap != self.cfg.surb_idle_notify_period {
11071            debug!(
11072                %session_id,
11073                ?entry_idle_timeout,
11074                node_cap = ?self.cfg.surb_idle_notify_period,
11075                cap = ?idle_notify_cap,
11076                "the Entry's idle timeout lowers the idle SURB notification period"
11077            );
11078        }
11079        let announcement = EntryAnnouncement {
11080            surb_target: announced_surb_target,
11081            idle_notify_cap,
11082        };
11083
11084        // The target this Session's SURB ring is sized from: the one the Entry announced, or, when it
11085        // announced none, the largest this node allows (`maximum_surb_buffer_size`).
11086        //
11087        // Decided from the raw figure on the wire and not from `announced_surb_target`, which is
11088        // clamped and has already fallen back when nothing was announced.
11089        //
11090        // The fallback is a balancer-rate estimate (`initial_return_session_egress_rate` times the
11091        // minimum buffer duration, 50 at the defaults), not a buffer anyone asked for, and the store
11092        // turns it into a ring of 75. An Entry that runs no balancer announces nothing at establishment
11093        // (a `NoRateControl` one, or a rate-controlled one without `surb_management`; an Entry that
11094        // predates that announced the fallback itself, which cannot be told from a real target of 50),
11095        // and it sends no keep-alives to announce a target later either, so nothing would ever widen
11096        // that ring: a Session that bursts replies finds its SURBs evicted past the 75th, and the
11097        // replies without one. The ring is a ceiling and not a reservation (it
11098        // allocates with occupancy, see `SurbStoreConfig::rb_capacity`), so a large one costs at most
11099        // what it has held: its storage grows with the SURBs stored and never shrinks below that
11100        // high-water mark, but is not taken up front. And any Entry can have the same ring by
11101        // announcing the maximum target, so a smaller one for an Entry that announces nothing protects
11102        // nothing here; it only starves the Entries that cannot announce one, such as a Session opened
11103        // without `surb_management`. The transport sets the maximum to two thirds of
11104        // `rb_capacity`, which the store's headroom, at its default of 50 %, turns into a ring of
11105        // `rb_capacity` (to within a SURB of integer rounding).
11106        let ring_surb_target = if surb_target > 0 {
11107            announced_surb_target
11108        } else {
11109            self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64
11110        };
11111
11112        let closure_notifier = exit_closure_notifier(close_session_notifier, instance.clone());
11113
11114        // One per Exit Session, and only when the degraded cadence can actually run — a notification
11115        // period to speed up and a faster period to speed it up to — and the Session has frames to
11116        // lose (`Capability::Segmentation`; a raw Session has none, and its socket never takes a
11117        // signal). Otherwise the socket records into a signal nobody reads, and the driver is never
11118        // spawned (see `spawn_exit_keep_alive`).
11119        let loss_signal = self
11120            .cfg
11121            .surb_degraded_notify_period
11122            .zip(self.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period)
11123            .filter(|(degraded, normal)| degraded < normal)
11124            .filter(|_| session_req.capabilities.0.contains(Capability::Segmentation))
11125            .map(|_| Arc::new(FrameLossSignal::new()));
11126        // Published on the slot rather than only handed to the two users, so that what the driver
11127        // decides and what the tests inject refer to the same signal.
11128        if let Some(signal) = &loss_signal {
11129            let _ = slot.exit_loss_signal.set(signal.clone());
11130        }
11131
11132        let session = self.build_exit_data_plane(
11133            &slot,
11134            session_id,
11135            session_req.capabilities,
11136            session_rx,
11137            &instance,
11138            closure_notifier,
11139            announced_surb_target,
11140            None,
11141        )?;
11142
11143        if let Some(egress_rate_control) = slot
11144            .exit_resume
11145            .terms
11146            .get()
11147            .and_then(|terms| terms.egress_rate_control.clone())
11148        {
11149            let target_surb_buffer_size = announced_surb_target;
11150
11151            // The SURB balancer will start intervening by rate-limiting the
11152            // egress of the Session, once the estimated number of SURBs drops below
11153            // the target defined here. Otherwise, the maximum egress is allowed.
11154            let balancer_config = SurbBalancerConfig {
11155                target_surb_buffer_size,
11156                // At maximum egress, the SURB buffer drains in `minimum_surb_buffer_duration` seconds
11157                max_surbs_per_sec: target_surb_buffer_size / self.cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs(),
11158                // No SURB decay at the Exit, since we know almost exactly how many SURBs
11159                // were received
11160                surb_decay: None,
11161            };
11162
11163            slot.surb_mgmt.update(&balancer_config);
11164            slot.surb_mgmt
11165                .set_counterparty_buffer_capacity(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64);
11166
11167            // Spawn the SURB balancer only once we know we have registered the
11168            // abort handle with the pre-allocated Session slot
11169            debug!(%session_id, ?balancer_config ,"spawning exit SURB balancer");
11170            let balancer = SurbBalancer::new(
11171                session_id,
11172                SimpleBalancerController::default(),
11173                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
11174                SurbControllerWithCorrection(egress_rate_control, 1), // 1 SURB per egress packet
11175                slot.surb_mgmt.clone(),
11176            );
11177
11178            // Assign the SURB balancer and abort handles to the already allocated Session slot
11179            let (_, balancer_abort_handle) = balancer.start_control_loop(self.cfg.balancer_sampling_interval);
11180            slot.abort_handles
11181                .lock()
11182                .insert(SessionHandles::Balancer, balancer_abort_handle);
11183        }
11184
11185        // Reports the SURB buffer level towards the Entry, and — on a PIX Session — carries the
11186        // Exit's own fill. On a `NoRateControl` Session, which runs no balancer, it is the only task
11187        // the Session starts beyond the data plane.
11188        self.spawn_exit_keep_alive(
11189            session_id,
11190            &slot,
11191            msg_sender.clone(),
11192            pix.is_some(),
11193            announcement,
11194            loss_signal,
11195        );
11196
11197        self.spawn_exit_forward_receipts(session_id, &slot, msg_sender.clone());
11198
11199        // Extract useful information about the session from the Start protocol message
11200        let incoming_session = IncomingSession {
11201            id: session_id,
11202            session,
11203            target: session_req.target,
11204        };
11205
11206        // Notify that a new incoming session has been created. Lock the sink and send
11207        // directly into it, so no extra forwarding task between channels is needed.
11208        match async {
11209            let mut guard = new_session_notifier.lock().await;
11210            guard.send(incoming_session).await
11211        }
11212        .timeout(futures_time::time::Duration::from(EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT))
11213        .await
11214        {
11215            Err(_) => {
11216                error!(%session_id, "timeout to notify about new incoming session");
11217                return Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout);
11218            }
11219            Ok(Err(error)) => {
11220                error!(%session_id, %error, "failed to notify about new incoming session");
11221                return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
11222            }
11223            _ => {}
11224        };
11225
11226        trace!(?session_id, "session notification sent");
11227
11228        // Notify the sender that the session has been established.
11229        // Set our peer ID in the session ID sent back to them.
11230        let data = HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(StartEstablished {
11231            orig_challenge: session_req.challenge,
11232            session_id,
11233        });
11234
11235        count_exit_control_send(
11236            ExitControlKind::SessionEstablished,
11237            ExitSessionKind::of(session_req.capabilities.0),
11238            send_counted_via_msg_sender(
11239                &mut msg_sender,
11240                reply_routing.clone(),
11241                data,
11242                &slot.surb_estimator,
11243                &session_id,
11244                "session establishment message",
11245            )
11246            .await,
11247        )?;
11248
11249        // The slot may have been torn down while the send was pending: its teardown has already
11250        // aborted the handles, and initialising metrics would overwrite a successor's owner.
11251        #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
11252        if !instance.is_superseded() {
11253            initialize_session_telemetry(
11254                session_id,
11255                &self.cfg,
11256                session_req.capabilities.0,
11257                Some(&slot.surb_estimator),
11258                Some(&slot.surb_mgmt),
11259                instance.id(),
11260            );
11261        }
11262
11263        // The session is published, so the supervisor's actions can now be carried out. The first of
11264        // them is the initial `RequestSsa`, which is why this runs after `SessionEstablished` has
11265        // gone out: the Entry must see the two in that order.
11266        if let Some(action_rx) = pix {
11267            // Checked under the handles' lock: teardown supersedes before it takes the lock to abort,
11268            // so a driver inserted here is never missed by it.
11269            let mut handles = slot.abort_handles.lock();
11270            if !instance.is_superseded() {
11271                let driver = self.spawn_pix_action_driver(session_id, &slot, action_rx, reply_routing.clone());
11272                handles.insert(SessionHandles::PixActionDriver, driver);
11273            }
11274        }
11275
11276        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
11277        METRIC_NUM_ESTABLISHED_SESSIONS.increment();
11278
11279        // `ring_surb_target` — the buffer the Entry asked for, or the largest this node allows when it
11280        // asked for none — is what the store sizes the admitted ring off. It is live only from its
11281        // resolution at the top of this function, which is why the admit rides on `commit` rather than
11282        // on slot allocation. See where it is resolved for why an Entry that announced nothing is not
11283        // given the balancer's fallback figure, on both branches.
11284        commit_slot_guard(
11285            &mut slot_guard,
11286            &self.sessions,
11287            session_id,
11288            self.surb_admission.clone(),
11289            ring_surb_target as usize,
11290        );
11291
11292        Ok(())
11293    }
11294
11295    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, est))]
11296    async fn handle_session_established(&self, est: InitiationReply) -> errors::Result<()> {
11297        debug!(
11298            session_id = ?est.session_id(),
11299            stream_base = ?est.stream_base(),
11300            "received session establishment confirmation"
11301        );
11302        let challenge = est.orig_challenge();
11303        let session_id = est.session_id();
11304
11305        if let Some(tx_est) = self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge) {
11306            if let Err(error) = tx_est.try_send(Ok(est)) {
11307                error!(%challenge, %session_id, %error, "failed to send session establishment confirmation");
11308                return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
11309            }
11310            debug!(?session_id, challenge, "session establishment complete");
11311        } else {
11312            // Expected once a repeated `StartSession` has been answered more than once.
11313            debug!(%session_id, challenge, "unknown session establishment attempt or expired");
11314        }
11315        Ok(())
11316    }
11317
11318    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self))]
11319    async fn handle_session_error(
11320        &self,
11321        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
11322        error_type: StartErrorType<SessionId>,
11323    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
11324        let reason = error_type.reason;
11325        match error_type.identifier {
11326            ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(challenge) => {
11327                trace!(%challenge, error = ?error_type.reason, "session initiation error received");
11328                if let Some(tx_est) = self.session_initiations.remove(&challenge) {
11329                    if let Err(error) = tx_est.try_send(Err(error_type)) {
11330                        error!(%error, "could not send session error message");
11331                        return Err(SessionManagerError::other(error).into());
11332                    }
11333                    error!(%challenge, "session establishment error received");
11334                } else if let Some(instance) = self.forward_instance_of_challenge(&pseudonym, challenge) {
11335                    // An error an Exit sends to a resumable Entry after its reply, scoped to the
11336                    // Session instance this challenge opened: the pseudonym is reusable, so an error
11337                    // that names a challenge of an earlier Session of it must not close this one. A
11338                    // setup still in progress fails with the reason.
11339                    error!(
11340                        %pseudonym, %challenge, %reason,
11341                        "received post-establishment session error naming the challenge of this Session — closing it"
11342                    );
11343                    instance.refuse(reason);
11344                    self.close_session_scoped(&pseudonym, ClosureReason::Eviction, CloseScope::Instance(&instance));
11345                } else {
11346                    debug!(
11347                        %pseudonym, %challenge,
11348                        "dropping a session error naming a challenge that is neither pending nor this Session's"
11349                    );
11350                }
11351            }
11352            ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(session_id) => {
11353                if session_id != pseudonym {
11354                    debug!(%pseudonym, %session_id, "dropping session error naming a different session");
11355                    return Ok(());
11356                }
11357                error!(
11358                    %session_id, %reason,
11359                    "received post-establishment session error — closing session"
11360                );
11361                // Best-effort close; the session may have already been removed. An error about a Session that is
11362                // not resumable (a non-PIX Session, or one whose Exit predates resumption) names it by Session ID,
11363                // so a stale one can still close a successor: the wire format cannot name the instance. For an
11364                // outgoing Session the reason is recorded on the instance that is closed, so the app can read it.
11365                // A stale error about an earlier Session under this pseudonym can thus be recorded here.
11366                let outgoing = self
11367                    .sessions
11368                    .get(&session_id)
11369                    .filter(|slot| matches!(slot.routing_opts, DestinationRouting::Forward { .. }))
11370                    .map(|slot| slot.instance.clone());
11371                if let Some(instance) = outgoing {
11372                    instance.refuse(reason);
11373                    self.close_session_scoped(&session_id, ClosureReason::Eviction, CloseScope::Instance(&instance));
11374                } else {
11375                    self.close_session(&session_id);
11376                }
11377            }
11378        }
11379
11380        #[cfg(all(feature = "telemetry", not(test)))]
11381        METRIC_RECEIVED_SESSION_ERRS.increment(&[&reason.to_string()]);
11382
11383        Ok(())
11384    }
11385
11386    /// Handles a keep-alive.
11387    ///
11388    /// On an incoming Session (the Exit) a keep-alive from the Entry is also a delivery of SURBs, booked
11389    /// with those of every other Start message in [`dispatch_message`](Self::dispatch_message); see
11390    /// [`book_start_message_surbs`].
11391    #[tracing::instrument(level = "trace", skip(self, msg))]
11392    async fn handle_keep_alive(
11393        &self,
11394        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
11395        msg: KeepAliveMessage<SessionId>,
11396    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
11397        // The pseudonym a Start message arrives under is the Session's own pseudonym on both sides,
11398        // so a mismatch means the sender is naming someone else's Session. Pseudonyms are 80 random
11399        // bits, so this only matters on a leak — which is exactly when it matters.
11400        if msg.session_id != pseudonym {
11401            debug!(%pseudonym, session_id = %msg.session_id, "dropping keep-alive naming a different session");
11402            return Ok(());
11403        }
11404
11405        let session_id = msg.session_id;
11406        if let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
11407            trace!(?session_id, "received keep-alive message");
11408            match &session_slot.routing_opts {
11409                // Session is outgoing - keep-alive was received from the Exit
11410                DestinationRouting::Forward { .. } => {
11411                    if msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) && !session_slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled() {
11412                        // Record the reported level and let it infer the counterparty's real store
11413                        // capacity from a plateau. Every report is fed in, including one that repeats
11414                        // the last value -- a level that stops rising while we are still minting is
11415                        // exactly the plateau signal, so this must not dedup equal reports.
11416                        let changed = session_slot.surb_mgmt.buffer_level() != msg.additional_data;
11417                        session_slot.surb_mgmt.observe_reported_level(msg.additional_data);
11418                        if changed {
11419                            debug!(%session_id, surb_level = msg.additional_data, "keep-alive updated SURB buffer size from the Exit");
11420                        }
11421                    }
11422
11423                    // Increase the number of consumed SURBs in the estimator, as a keep-alive and not a reply
11424                    session_slot
11425                        .surb_mgmt
11426                        .note_keep_alive_consumed(&session_slot.surb_estimator);
11427                    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
11428                    telemetry::record_session_surb_consumed(&session_id, 1);
11429                }
11430                // Session is incoming - keep-alive was received from the Entry
11431                DestinationRouting::Return(_) => {
11432                    // Only an Entry's SURB balancer sends keep-alives of its own accord: from now on the
11433                    // Exit's data can be held back for its keep-alive reserve, which this Entry will
11434                    // refill, and the Exit's SURB-level reports can go out, since this Entry has a
11435                    // balancer to read them (see `PixFillControl::admit`).
11436                    //
11437                    // Not a manual ping, though: an Entry without a balancer pings by hand through
11438                    // `ping_session` too, and would otherwise be taken for one that has. The mark is the
11439                    // only way to tell the two apart, as a balancer that does not announce its target
11440                    // sends its keep-alives unflagged (`surb_target_notify` off). The SURBs a ping
11441                    // carries are booked all the same, with those of every Start message
11442                    // (`book_start_message_surbs`). An Entry that predates the mark sends its pings
11443                    // unflagged, and is taken for a balancer as it always was.
11444                    if !msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing) {
11445                        session_slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
11446                    }
11447
11448                    // Allow updating the SURB balancer target based on the received Keep-Alive message.
11449                    if msg.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget) {
11450                        self.apply_announced_surb_target(&session_slot, session_id, msg.additional_data);
11451                    }
11452                }
11453            }
11454        } else {
11455            debug!(%session_id, "received keep-alive request for an unknown session");
11456        }
11457
11458        Ok(())
11459    }
11460
11461    /// Applies a SURB buffer target the Entry announced for an Exit-side Session: the balancer's
11462    /// set-point, the SURB ring and the fill reserve.
11463    ///
11464    /// What a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive does with its figure, and what a takeover does with the
11465    /// figure its `StartSession` carries, since the successor's Entry may have changed its target
11466    /// since the Session was established. `announced_raw` is the Entry's word and is clamped here.
11467    fn apply_announced_surb_target(&self, session_slot: &SessionSlot, session_id: SessionId, announced_raw: u64) {
11468        // Allow updating SURB balancer target based on the received Keep-Alive message.
11469        //
11470        // Clamped exactly as establishment clamps it, and for every use below. The value
11471        // is a peer's claim: the balancer's set-point and the ring's ceiling are two
11472        // views of one figure, and letting an over-announcing Entry set them apart would
11473        // have the Exit aim at a buffer the ring can never hold.
11474        //
11475        // A `NoRateControl` Session runs no balancer on this side, so there is no
11476        // set-point to move (its target is never set). Its ring is the same bounded
11477        // store, though, sized at establishment from the target the Entry announced then.
11478        // A Session whose Entry announced nothing was given the full ring at that point
11479        // (see `ring_surb_target` in `handle_incoming_session_initiation`), so there is nothing left to
11480        // widen; the raise matters for one that announced a target at establishment and
11481        // has since raised it, for the same reason as for any other
11482        // (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739). With no set-point to compare against, a raise is
11483        // whatever exceeds the largest figure already recorded on the slot; the ring
11484        // only ever widens, so a repeated announcement changes nothing.
11485        //
11486        // That widen-only rule is the ring's, and below it the block is only entered for
11487        // a raise. The fill reserve is re-derived separately, after it, from the same
11488        // clamped figure: it follows a lowered target too.
11489        let announced = announced_raw.min(self.cfg.maximum_surb_buffer_size as u64);
11490        let balanced = !session_slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled();
11491        // A flagged announcement of zero is "no target", not "a target of zero": the Exit
11492        // reads zero that way everywhere (`BalancerStateValues::is_disabled`, the ring's
11493        // own guard below), so the reserve keeps the figure it has rather than following
11494        // zero to `effective_surb_reserve`'s floor of one. An Entry that drops its buffer
11495        // without disabling its balancer announces a small non-zero target instead.
11496        let announces_target = announced > 0;
11497        if announces_target
11498            && if balanced {
11499                session_slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target() != announced
11500            } else {
11501                session_slot
11502                    .peek_raised_surb_target()
11503                    .is_none_or(|raised| announced as usize > raised)
11504            }
11505        {
11506            if balanced {
11507                // Update the target buffer size as sent to us from the Entry
11508                session_slot
11509                    .surb_mgmt
11510                    .target_surb_buffer_size
11511                    .store(announced, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
11512                // Update maximum SURBs per second based on the new target
11513                session_slot.surb_mgmt.max_surbs_per_sec.store(
11514                    announced / self.cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs(),
11515                    std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed,
11516                );
11517            }
11518
11519            // The store sized this Session's ring once, off the target announced at
11520            // establishment. A target raised afterwards must widen it, or every SURB
11521            // minted toward the new one is evicted on arrival — under PIX, together with
11522            // the share it carried. See `SurbAdmissionControl::raise_target`.
11523            //
11524            // Recorded on the slot before the call as well: the Exit answers
11525            // `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so this can arrive before the ring
11526            // exists. The commit sizes the ring from the recorded figure; once the
11527            // admission exists, the raise widens it on the spot.
11528            session_slot.note_raised_surb_target(announced as usize);
11529            if let Some(admission) = self.surb_admission.get() {
11530                admission.raise_target(&session_id, session_slot.peek_admission_token(), announced as usize);
11531            }
11532
11533            // The target sets the keep-alive reserve, which may now reach the stock.
11534            if let Some(control) = session_slot.pix_fill.get() {
11535                control.recheck_reserve();
11536            }
11537
11538            if balanced {
11539                debug!(%session_id, target_surb_buffer_size = announced, "keep-alive updated SURB balancer target buffer size from the Entry");
11540            } else {
11541                debug!(%session_id, target_surb_buffer_size = announced, "keep-alive target recorded for the SURB ring of a session without a balancer");
11542            }
11543        }
11544
11545        // The reserve follows the announcement in *both* directions, unlike the ring
11546        // above, which only widens and ignores a lower announcement on a `NoRateControl`
11547        // Session. It is decided on its own, not by the ring's raise-only guard; a repeat
11548        // dedupes inside `set_announced_target`. A flagged zero means "no target", so the
11549        // reserve keeps the figure it has.
11550        if announces_target && let Some(fill) = session_slot.pix_fill.get() {
11551            fill.set_announced_target(announced);
11552        }
11553    }
11554
11555    /// Handled by the Exit, when Entry replies with PIX commitment
11556    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, msg))]
11557    async fn handle_ssa_commit(
11558        &self,
11559        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
11560        msg: SsaClientCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixCommitmentProof>,
11561    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
11562        let Some(pix_toolbox) = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned() else {
11563            return Err(SessionManagerError::UnsupportedMessage.into());
11564        };
11565
11566        let session_id = msg.session_id;
11567
11568        if pseudonym != session_id {
11569            error!(%pseudonym, %msg.session_id, "received SSA client commitment for a different session");
11570            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11571        }
11572
11573        let Some(session_slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) else {
11574            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11575        };
11576
11577        // See if we haven't received an SSA commitment for a Session that we did not register as PIX-capable
11578        let Some(ssa_state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() else {
11579            return Err(SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!("no SSA state for session {session_id}")).into());
11580        };
11581        let quota_per_ssa = ssa_state.quota_per_ssa();
11582
11583        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, msg.ssa_index);
11584
11585        // Decode the accompanying proof of knowledge, if the message carries one. A malformed proof
11586        // is rejected here rather than being passed on as absent, so that it cannot be mistaken for
11587        // a peer that simply did not send one.
11588        let commitment_proof = msg
11589            .commitment_proof
11590            .map(|proof| proof.try_into_pix_proof())
11591            .transpose()
11592            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
11593
11594        // Insert the newly received coefficients into the SSA Reconstructor, off the shared CPU pool
11595        let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
11596        let ssa_client_commitment_state =
11597            crate::pix_pool::spawn_pix_blocking(crate::pix_pool::PixPoolOperation::CommitmentIngest, move || {
11598                pix_toolbox_clone
11599                    .share_processor
11600                    .insert_coefficient_commitments(
11601                        ssa_id,
11602                        msg.coefficient_index,
11603                        commitment_proof,
11604                        msg.coefficient_commitments.into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k, v.0)),
11605                    )
11606                    .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)
11607            })
11608            .await
11609            .map_err(|_| {
11610                SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!(
11611                    "failed to insert SSA coefficients into the SSA reconstructor"
11612                ))
11613            })??;
11614
11615        // A verifiable commitment is what starts the deposit clock, so tell the supervisor before
11616        // the observer below can report anything against it.
11617        //
11618        // An *incomplete* one is reported too, and per message: that is what arms the supervisor's
11619        // re-request timer and keeps pushing it out while the burst is still arriving, so it fires
11620        // only once delivery has actually stalled. It is also the only evidence that the Entry
11621        // answered at all, which is what separates a cycle worth re-asking for from one where
11622        // nothing was ever delivered and there is no scope to name.
11623        // The Entry has answered: it is paying for this Session, which is what makes the Session worth
11624        // keeping through a reconnect even before any deposit has funded a cycle.
11625        session_slot
11626            .exit_resume
11627            .entry_answered
11628            .store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release);
11629
11630        if let Some(supervisor) = session_slot.pix_supervisor.get() {
11631            let event = if ssa_client_commitment_state.is_verifiable {
11632                SessionPixEvent::CommitmentVerified(ssa_id)
11633            } else {
11634                SessionPixEvent::CommitmentProgress(ssa_id)
11635            };
11636            if supervisor.send_event(event).await.is_err() {
11637                error!(%session_id, %ssa_id, "pix supervisor is no longer accepting events");
11638            }
11639        }
11640
11641        if ssa_client_commitment_state.deposit_address_first_encountered
11642            && let Some(deposit_address) = ssa_client_commitment_state.ssa_deposit_address
11643        {
11644            // Inside the guard on purpose: every other `SsaCommit` of a cycle takes the other branch,
11645            // so allocating this before the `if` built and dropped a channel per message.
11646            let (deposit_done_tx, deposit_done_rx) =
11647                futures::channel::mpsc::channel::<(PixAddressId, hopr_api::HoprBalance)>(10);
11648            // Report deposits for as long as they arrive rather than waiting for the first one and
