11649            // stopping: the pool may report more than once for a cycle, and a first message carrying
11650            // a zero balance asserts nothing, so the one that funds the cycle need not be the first.
11651            let supervisor = session_slot.pix_supervisor.get().cloned();
11652            session_slot.abort_handles.lock().insert(
11653                SessionHandles::PixDepositObserver(ssa_id.ssa_index().get()),
11654                hopr_utils::spawn_as_abortable!(async move {
11655                    let Some(supervisor) = supervisor else {
11656                        // No supervisor: a Session that negotiated PIX always has one, so this is
11657                        // only reachable if it died between the check above and here.
11658                        return;
11659                    };
11660                    observe_deposits(deposit_done_rx, session_id, ssa_id, |ev| {
11661                        let supervisor = supervisor.clone();
11662                        async move { supervisor.send_event(ev).await }
11663                    })
11664                    .await;
11665                }),
11666            );
11667
11668            // Notify upstream that deposit is needed
11669            pix_toolbox
11670                .pix_events
11671                .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(
11672                    AgreedSsaQuota {
11673                        ssa_id,
11674                        deposit_address,
11675                        quota_per_ssa,
11676                        // Handed back to the pool that produced it, now that the address it pays for
11677                        // is known. Consumed here: this branch is reached once per cycle.
11678                        deposit_data: ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, ssa_id.ssa_index()),
11679                    },
11680                    deposit_done_tx,
11681                ))
11682                .map_err(|_| {
11683                    SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("failed to send pix event for needed deposit"))
11684                })?;
11685            info!(%ssa_id, %deposit_address, quota_per_ssa, "retrieved first client SSA commitment and deposit address");
11686        }
11687
11688        Ok(())
11689    }
11690
11691    /// Tells the Exit that its [`SsaServerCommitmentMessage`] was refused, and tears down this half
11692    /// of the Session.
11693    ///
11694    /// Without the notice the refusal is invisible to the Exit, and it has no way to recover from it.
11695    /// Its supervisor registered an Exit commitment per requested index and armed each cycle's
11696    /// commitment deadline the moment the request went out; it will never receive an `SsaCommit`, and
11697    /// nothing can make it re-ask, because a new `RequestSsa` only comes from share-recovery events and
11698    /// no shares exist for a cycle the Entry never committed to. So it serves the Session
11699    /// unincentivized for the whole batch-scaled `max_ssa_delivery_time` and then closes it as
11700    /// `CommitmentTimeout` — a reason that names the clock rather than the refusal, on the one node
11701    /// whose operator can act on it.
11702    ///
11703    /// Closing this half too is what stops the Entry sitting on a Session that can never make PIX
11704    /// progress: a refusal is terminal either way, since the Exit re-derives every request from state
11705    /// that cannot drift within a Session, so a later one would be refused identically. Left alone the
11706    /// slot would survive until the idle timeout.
11707    ///
11708    /// That holds for the refusals that come through here — parameters, the batch cap, an undecodable
11709    /// commitment and lost generator state. It does *not* hold for the successor gate, whose two
11710    /// refusals (early, under-served) and the stale-index drop are `NotAdmitted` and never reach this
11711    /// function: they depend on how far the predecessor has been served, which changes, and the
11712    /// Exit's supervisor re-sends its unanswered successor request while that generation is still
11713    /// being served. Closing on one of those would end a Session over a shortfall that the next
11714    /// re-send repairs.
11715    ///
11716    /// No new capability is handed to an attacker by closing on a refusal: an `SsaRequest` only reaches
11717    /// here with `pseudonym == session_id`, and relayers never see that pseudonym — a relayer can garble
11718    /// a packet in transit but not forge one for this Session — so only the Exit can produce one, and
11719    /// the Exit can already close the Session whenever it likes.
11720    async fn refuse_ssa_request(
11721        &self,
11722        session_id: SessionId,
11723        routing: DestinationRouting,
11724        instance: &Arc<SlotInstance>,
11725    ) {
11726        // The scoped close comes first, and the notice goes only if it acted: a handler of a predecessor that is no
11727        // longer current must not have the Exit close its successor. A `SessionId` notice cannot name the instance,
11728        // so a successor installed between the close and the notice is still exposed to it.
11729        if !self.close_session_scoped(&session_id, ClosureReason::Eviction, CloseScope::Instance(instance)) {
11730            return;
11731        }
11732        error!(%session_id, "closed session after refusing the Exit's SSA request");
11733        self.notify_session_error(
11734            session_id,
11735            ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(session_id),
11736            routing,
11737            StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams,
11738            "session error due to a refused SSA request",
11739        )
11740        .await;
11741    }
11742
11743    /// Handled by the Entry, when the Exit says it never received parts of a commitment this node
11744    /// already published.
11745    ///
11746    /// Re-sends the named polynomial commitments and nothing else. Emits no
11747    /// [`ReadyToDeposit`](HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit): the deposit address of a cycle is
11748    /// fixed when it is first committed, and the caller was told it then, so announcing it again
11749    /// would invite a second deposit against one quota.
11750    ///
11751    /// That holds for a cycle whose publication completed. For one whose publication was cut short —
11752    /// the transport failed part-way through its burst, or between its burst and the announcement — the
11753    /// caller was *not* told, and the scoped parts would hand the Exit a complete commitment for a
11754    /// cycle nobody was asked to fund. Such a cycle is answered instead by resuming the publication of
11755    /// the batch it belongs to: whole bursts and the owed `ReadyToDeposit`s, in ascending order, each
11756    /// published by whoever claims it (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]) so that a deposit is
11757    /// announced once however many requests arrive. The cycles of the request that were not cut short
11758    /// are answered with their scoped parts as before. This is reached only when the Exit asks, so it
11759    /// is the answer for a burst that got part of the way out: a cycle with no message out, or one
11760    /// whose burst was whole and only its announcement failed, prompts no request and is not covered
11761    /// (see [`SessionSsaState::unpublished`]). A resumption the transport cuts short again is the
11762    /// non-fatal `NotAdmitted`.
11763    ///
11764    /// A failure here is reported to the caller of the Start-message dispatcher and otherwise
11765    /// dropped. It is deliberately not [`refuse_ssa_request`](Self::refuse_ssa_request), which closes
11766    /// the Session: an Exit that asks for a cycle this node cannot serve is asking for something
11767    /// already lost, and its own commitment deadline ends the Session either way — whereas closing on
11768    /// a request that merely raced our own state would throw away a Session that was about to work.
11769    ///
11770    /// Two separate bounds keep this from being a packet-amplification lever, because one request may
11771    /// name a whole cycle's polynomials and the answer to that is the entire commitment burst again.
11772    /// The generator bounds how often it answers for *one* cycle
11773    /// ([`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`](hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS)); this
11774    /// function bounds how many cycles one request may set going. Neither stands in for the other —
11775    /// the first bounds repeats, the second bounds breadth.
11776    async fn handle_ssa_recommit(
11777        &self,
11778        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
11779        session_slot: &SessionSlot,
11780        msg: SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload>,
11781    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
11782        // The wire bounds the *runs* a request carries, not the number of cycles they are spread
11783        // over — one run of 8 bytes can name a whole cycle — so without this a single packet names
11784        // every retained cycle and is answered with a full commitment burst for each. The generator's
11785        // per-cycle attempt cap does not bound that: it bounds repeats of one cycle, not breadth
11786        // across cycles.
11787        //
11788        // The same cap as the new-SSA path, so repairing a batch can never cost more than committing
11789        // to it did, and the Exit's own requests name a single cycle. Dropped rather than refused
11790        // with `refuse_ssa_request`: the peer is already inside its own commitment deadline and
11791        // learns nothing from a refusal it does not learn from that, and replying at all would hand
11792        // back some of the amplification the request was reaching for.
11793        let max_ssas_per_request = self.cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request;
11794        if msg.missing.len() > max_ssas_per_request {
11795            return Err(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
11796                "Exit asked for retransmissions across {} SSA cycles in a single request, at most \
11797                 {max_ssas_per_request} allowed",
11798                msg.missing.len()
11799            ))
11800            .into());
11801        }
11802
11803        let pix_toolbox = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
11804        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
11805        let session_id = msg.session_id;
11806
11807        // Cycles named here whose publication never completed. Decided before anything is sent, and
11808        // answered once for all of them: resuming publishes every member that is owed, not only the
11809        // ones this request names, and the ones it names are then not also answered with a scoped
11810        // re-send — their whole burst has just gone out, and a second answer would spend another of
11811        // the cycle's retransmissions on parts the Exit now has.
11812        let cut_short: Vec<SsaIndex> = session_slot
11813            .current_ssa_state
11814            .get()
11815            .map(|state| {
11816                state
11817                    .unpublished_indices()
11818                    .into_iter()
11819                    .filter(|ssa_index| msg.missing.contains_key(ssa_index))
11820                    .collect()
11821            })
11822            .unwrap_or_default();
11823
11824        // A resumption's failure is kept rather than returned at once. The cycles of this request
11825        // that were published in full are repairs of their own, and a resumption the transport cut
11826        // short is no reason to make them wait a whole re-request interval. It is reported once they
11827        // have been sent.
11828        let resumed = match session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
11829            Some(ssa_state) if !cut_short.is_empty() => {
11830                tracing::info!(%session_id, ?cut_short, "a re-request names cycles whose publication was cut short — resuming it");
11831                resume_publication(
11832                    session_id,
11833                    pseudonym,
11834                    &session_slot.routing_opts,
11835                    ssa_state,
11836                    &pix_toolbox,
11837                    &mut msg_sender,
11838                )
11839                .await
11840            }
11841            _ => Ok(()),
11842        };
11843
11844        for (ssa_index, runs) in msg.missing {
11845            if cut_short.contains(&ssa_index) {
11846                continue;
11847            }
11848
11849            // Rebuilt from the bytes that went out the first time, so the peer's already-filled slots
11850            // see a re-delivery rather than a contradiction.
11851            let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
11852            let commitment = hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu::spawn_blocking(
11853                move || pix_toolbox_clone.share_generator.recommit(&pseudonym, ssa_index, runs),
11854                "client_ssa_recommitment",
11855            )
11856            .await
11857            .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
11858            .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
11859
11860            let commitment_msgs =
11861                SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, commitment).map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
11862            let num_messages = commitment_msgs.len();
11863
11864            for commitment_msg in commitment_msgs {
11865                send_via_msg_sender(
11866                    &mut msg_sender,
11867                    session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
11868                    HoprStartProtocol::SsaCommit(commitment_msg),
11869                    "re-sent client SSA commitment message",
11870                )
11871                .await?;
11872            }
11873
11874            info!(%session_id, %ssa_index, num_messages, "re-sent the requested SSA commitment parts");
11875        }
11876
11877        resumed
11878    }
11879
11880    /// Handled by the Entry, when the Exit sends PIX initiation request
11881    #[tracing::instrument(level = "debug", skip(self, msg))]
11882    async fn handle_ssa_request(
11883        &self,
11884        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
11885        msg: SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload>,
11886    ) -> errors::Result<()> {
11887        let Some(pix_toolbox) = self.pix_toolbox.get().cloned() else {
11888            return Err(SessionManagerError::UnsupportedMessage.into());
11889        };
11890
11891        if pseudonym != msg.session_id {
11892            error!(%pseudonym, %msg.session_id, "received SSA server commitment for a different session");
11893            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11894        }
11895
11896        // Deliberately narrower than the dispatch filter's `SsaRequest` arm
11897        // (`ssa_request_names_local_state`), which additionally requires the slot to be an outgoing
11898        // (`Forward`) one: a compliant peer never sends an `SsaRequest` to an Exit-side (Return)
11899        // slot, so dispatch drops that case outright, and re-checking the variant here would only
11900        // re-decide what dispatch already decided on the same in-memory state. This guard is the
11901        // backstop for the state changing between the two — a message that sat queued long enough
11902        // for the session it names to close, or for a `pending_outgoing` initiation to be removed —
11903        // and for callers that bypass dispatch entirely. Refusing here rather than after the wait
11904        // below is what kept a flood of bogus requests from parking the shared handler pool.
11905        if self.sessions.get(&msg.session_id).is_none() && !self.pending_outgoing.contains_key(&msg.session_id) {
11906            trace!(session_id = %msg.session_id, "refusing an SSA request for a session this node does not hold");
11907            return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11908        }
11909
11910        // The SsaRequest can arrive before new_session() or handle_incoming_session_initiation
11911        // has finished allocating the session slot, since both SessionEstablished and SsaRequest
11912        // are sent by the Exit back-to-back and processed concurrently by the Start protocol handler.
11913        // Instead of busy-looping, await the allocation notification for this specific SessionId.
11914        let session_slot = {
11915            use std::collections::hash_map::Entry;
11916            let session_id = msg.session_id;
11917            let waiter_deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
11918            loop {
11919                if Instant::now() >= waiter_deadline {
11920                    debug!(%session_id, "session slot waiter deadline exceeded");
11921                    return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11922                }
11923                // Optimistic cache check
11924                if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
11925                    break slot;
11926                }
11927
11928                // Register a waiter under the lock, then recheck the cache to avoid the
11929                // TOCTOU race between the initial cache check and waiter registration.
11930                let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel::<()>();
11931                {
11932                    let mut map = self.slot_allocated.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
11933                    // Recheck while holding the lock: the slot may have been inserted
11934                    // between the optimistic check and now. If so, don't register.
11935                    if self.sessions.get(&session_id).is_some() {
11936                        drop(map);
11937                        continue;
11938                    }
11939
11940                    // At most one request per Session waits here; any other is refused at once, for
11941                    // the reason `ssa_request_locks` below is only `try_lock`ed. The dispatch filter
11942                    // admits every request naming a pending initiation, and each one waiting here
11943                    // parks a shared Start handler — so whoever holds SURBs for the pseudonym could
11944                    // occupy all of them before the slot exists. A conforming Exit sends only its
11945                    // opening request before then; a retransmission names commitments that only an
11946                    // existing slot can have sent.
11947                    let waiters = map.entry(session_id).or_default();
11948                    if waiters.iter().any(|w| !w.is_canceled()) {
11949                        return Err(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
11950                            "an SSA request for {session_id} is already waiting for its session slot"
11951                        ))
11952                        .into());
11953                    }
11954                    waiters.push(tx);
11955                }
11956
11957                let timeout = futures_time::time::Duration::from(Duration::from_millis(1000));
11958                match rx.timeout(timeout).await {
11959                    Ok(Ok(())) => {
11960                        // Notified — recheck the cache
11961                        continue;
11962                    }
11963                    _ => {
11964                        // Timeout or the sender was dropped (cancelled). Clean up our
11965                        // waiter entry to avoid unbounded accumulation in the map.
11966                        let mut map = self.slot_allocated.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
11967                        if let Entry::Occupied(mut e) = map.entry(session_id) {
11968                            e.get_mut().retain(|w| !w.is_canceled());
11969                            if e.get().is_empty() {
11970                                e.remove();
11971                            }
11972                        }
11973                        drop(map);
11974
11975                        // Final cache recheck before giving up — the slot might have
11976                        // been inserted while we were cleaning up.
11977                        if let Some(slot) = self.sessions.get(&session_id) {
11978                            break slot;
11979                        }
11980
11981                        debug!(%session_id, "session slot not found after awaiting allocation");
11982                        return Err(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession.into());
11983                    }
11984                }
11985            }
11986        };
11987
11988        debug!(
11989            num_server_commitments = msg.commitments.len(),
11990            "received Exit SSA commitments"
11991        );
11992
11993        // Cap how many SSAs a single request may ask us to commit to.
11994        //
11995        // The wire format alone permits `MAX_SSAS_PER_REQUEST` (27) commitments per message, and
11996        // every accepted entry costs a full `new_ssa_commitment` (hundreds of thousands of EC
11997        // commitments) plus thousands of outbound `SsaCommit` packets, and emits its own
11998        // `ReadyToDeposit` — i.e. its own on-chain deposit. Without a cap, a single packet from a
11999        // misbehaving Exit amplifies into minutes of Entry CPU, a large packet burst, and up to 27
12000        // simultaneous deposits bounded only by the per-deposit allocation limit.
12001        //
12002        // Rejecting the whole message rather than the surplus is deliberate: a truncated batch would
12003        // leave the Exit holding reconstructor cycles for indices it will never receive commitments
12004        // for, which its own kill switch then has to clean up.
12005        let max_ssas_per_request = self.cfg.max_ssas_per_ssa_request;
12006        if msg.commitments.len() > max_ssas_per_request {
12007            let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
12008                "Exit requested {} SSA commitments in a single request, at most {max_ssas_per_request} allowed",
12009                msg.commitments.len()
12010            ));
12011            self.refuse_ssa_request(
12012                msg.session_id,
12013                session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
12014                &session_slot.instance,
12015            )
12016            .await;
12017            return Err(error.into());
12018        }
12019
12020        let Some(ssa_state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() else {
12021            return Err(
12022                SessionManagerError::Other(anyhow::anyhow!("no SSA state for session {}", msg.session_id)).into(),
12023            );
12024        };
12025        let our_params = ssa_state.params;
12026
12027        // The Entry enforces that the Exit's SSA parameters match exactly the ones we offered in the
12028        // Session Initiation message.  Negotiation (accepting an Exit-chosen quota within our
12029        // bounds) is not implemented, so any mismatch is rejected.
12030        //
12031        // The whole quadruple is compared rather than the scalar quota it implies.  Quota equality
12032        // was once argued to be sufficient — the Exit does not pick the dimensions independently, so
12033        // a matching product implied matching `(polys, shares)` from any Exit running unmodified
12034        // code.  The quota now prices three of the four, so it is no longer blind to the surplus,
12035        // but it is still a product: it cannot tell `polys x threshold` from a transposition of the
12036        // two, and those are not interchangeable to the protocol.  Comparing the params is both
12037        // stricter and simpler, and costs nothing now that all four travel together.
12038        //
12039        // The fourth, the curve suite, is why the Entry needs no separate curve check of its own:
12040        // the Exit refused a foreign suite before it sent this message, and an Exit that echoed a
12041        // different one back than the Entry offered fails right here.
12042        //
12043        // Malformed params never reach this comparison as a mismatch: `dimensions()` fails first,
12044        // and that failure takes the same refusal path, so the Exit is told either way rather than
12045        // being left waiting on a dropped packet.
12046        let server_params = match msg.dimensions() {
12047            Ok(params) => params,
12048            Err(error) => {
12049                self.refuse_ssa_request(
12050                    msg.session_id,
12051                    session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
12052                    &session_slot.instance,
12053                )
12054                .await;
12055                return Err(
12056                    SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!("Exit sent malformed PIX parameters: {error}")).into(),
12057                );
12058            }
12059        };
12060        if our_params != server_params {
12061            let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
12062                "Exit sent unacceptable PIX parameters {server_params} (ours are {our_params})"
12063            ));
12064            self.refuse_ssa_request(
12065                msg.session_id,
12066                session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
12067                &session_slot.instance,
12068            )
12069            .await;
12070            return Err(error.into());
12071        }
12072        // A request naming missing commitment parts asks for nothing new — see
12073        // `SsaServerCommitmentMessage` — and none of what follows may run for it.
12074        //
12075        // That placement is the whole safety argument for reusing this message. The successor gate
12076        // below would refuse an index that is *already* being served, which is every index a
12077        // retransmission can name; the served-packet gate prices service against a batch nobody is
12078        // asking for; and `new_ssa_commitment` rejects an index at or below the watermark, which
12079        // again is every index this can name. Above this line is what a retransmission does need:
12080        // the pseudonym check, the session slot, and the parameter comparison.
12081        if !msg.missing.is_empty() {
12082            return self.handle_ssa_recommit(pseudonym, &session_slot, msg).await;
12083        }
12084
12085        let quota_per_ssa = pix_params_to_quota(&our_params);
12086
12087        // Everything from here to the end of the batch is serialised per pseudonym. Start messages run
12088        // under `for_each_concurrent`, so the successor gate below would otherwise be read by several
12089        // requests before any of them advanced it, and every one would pass. See `ssa_request_locks`.
12090        //
12091        // Taken without waiting. A request that finds the lock held is one the Exit is going to send
12092        // again — a repeat of the batch being committed right now, or a request racing it — and
12093        // queueing behind the holder would park a `for_each_concurrent` slot for as long as that
12094        // holder runs: the near-miss wait below, or generating a commitment (a fraction of a second per
12095        // cycle at the deployed dimensions, longer for wide dimensions or a full batch). The
12096        // Exit re-sends an unanswered request every few seconds, so a queue of them would be a lever
12097        // on exactly those slots. Dropping it costs nothing: either the holder admits the batch and the
12098        // repeat is moot, or it does not and the repeat is the next attempt.
12099        //
12100        // Kept after the recommit branch, which needs no serialisation and must stay reachable while
12101        // the commitment it repairs is still being published. And kept after the slot waiter above:
12102        // `ssa_request_locks` is uncapped, so taking it any earlier would let a request naming a
12103        // pseudonym with no Session create an entry, for as long as the cache's idle timer holds it.
12104        let request_lock = self
12105            .ssa_request_locks
12106            .get_with(pseudonym, async { Arc::new(futures::lock::Mutex::new(())) })
12107            .await;
12108        let Some(_request_guard) = request_lock.try_lock_owned() else {
12109            let error =
12110                SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!("another SSA request for {pseudonym} is being processed"));
12111            tracing::debug!(session_id = %msg.session_id, %error, "dropped an SSA request that found the request lock held");
12112            return Err(error.into());
12113        };
12114
12115        // A request that asks for what has already been committed to. It comes first under the lock,
12116        // before either half of the successor gate, because neither half has anything to say about it.
12117        //
12118        // Two things look the same from the watermark and are not. A *repeat* names the batch this
12119        // Session committed to last: the Exit re-sends an unanswered successor request until a part of
12120        // every member's commitment reaches it, so once one is admitted the re-sends already in flight
12121        // arrive at an Entry that has nothing left to do for them. For a batch that was published in
12122        // full they succeed without effect — no second burst, no second `ReadyToDeposit`, and above all
12123        // no second deposit. That holds while they arrive within `SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE` of the batch
12124        // last going out. A repeat that arrives later was sent after the bursts should have reached the
12125        // Exit, so one of them was lost after the transport took it. Every announced member's burst
12126        // then goes out again, still with no `ReadyToDeposit`. A batch whose publication was cut short
12127        // is the other exception: members still owed are published now, whole, and the repeat succeeds
12128        // only if that did (see `SessionSsaState::unpublished`); otherwise it is a non-fatal refusal
12129        // and the Exit's next re-send tries again. A *stale* request names indices at or below the
12130        // watermark that are not that batch; it is dropped, and is not `refuse_ssa_request`, since it
12131        // can be nothing worse than an Exit that lost track of what it asked for, which its own
12132        // deadlines already end. The one other way to have committed past the batch last recorded is
12133        // a batch that moved the generator and then failed to stage, and that failure ends the
12134        // Session instead (see phase two below).
12135        //
12136        // The opening batch has no watermark and passes this untouched.
12137        let first_asked = msg.commitments.keys().next().copied();
12138
12139        // A resumed Session keeps its ledger and generator, so an opening request on it is judged below like
12140        // any other: as a repeat or a stale one.
12141        //
12142        // What remains is a request the ledger cannot measure: a later index than the opening batch, against
12143        // a ledger without a watermark. With the generator holding state, the served-packet half of the
12144        // successor gate has nothing to measure: terminal.
12145        let is_opening = first_asked == Some(SsaIndex::MIN);
12146        if !is_opening
12147            && ssa_state.committed_watermark().is_none()
12148            && pix_toolbox.share_generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).is_some()
12149        {
12150            let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
12151                "Exit asked for SSAs from {first_asked:?} on a Session whose ledger has no committed cycle, while the \
12152                 generator still holds state for {pseudonym}; the successor cannot be measured"
12153            ));
12154            warn!(session_id = %msg.session_id, %error, "refused a successor SSA request the Entry cannot judge");
12155            self.refuse_ssa_request(
12156                msg.session_id,
12157                session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
12158                &session_slot.instance,
12159            )
12160            .await;
12161            return Err(error.into());
12162        }
12163        if let Some(first) = first_asked
12164            && let Some(watermark) = ssa_state.committed_watermark()
12165            && first <= watermark
12166        {
12167            if ssa_state.last_committed_first() == Some(first) {
12168                if !ssa_state.unpublished_indices().is_empty() {
12169                    tracing::info!(
12170                        session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark,
12171                        "a repeat of an SSA request whose publication was cut short — resuming it"
12172                    );
12173                    let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
12174                    return resume_publication(
12175                        msg.session_id,
12176                        pseudonym,
12177                        &session_slot.routing_opts,
12178                        ssa_state,
12179                        &pix_toolbox,
12180                        &mut msg_sender,
12181                    )
12182                    .await;
12183                }
12184
12185                let lost = ssa_state.claim_republication(Instant::now(), SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE);
12186                if lost.is_empty() {
12187                    tracing::debug!(
12188                        session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark,
12189                        "ignored a repeat of an SSA request this Session already committed to"
12190                    );
12191                    return Ok(());
12192                }
12193
12194                tracing::info!(
12195                    session_id = %msg.session_id, %first, %watermark, members = ?lost,
12196                    "a repeat of an SSA request long after it was published — re-sending its commitments"
12197                );
12198                let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
12199                return republish_commitments(
12200                    msg.session_id,
12201                    pseudonym,
12202                    &session_slot.routing_opts,
12203                    ssa_state,
12204                    &pix_toolbox,
12205                    &mut msg_sender,
12206                    lost,
12207                )
12208                .await;
12209            }
12210
12211            let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
12212                "Exit asked for SSAs from {first}, at or below the committed {watermark}, and the batch last \
12213                 committed to starts at {:?}",
12214                ssa_state.last_committed_first()
12215            ));
12216            SsaRefusal::Stale.log(
12217                ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::Stale),
12218                &msg.session_id,
12219                &error,
12220            );
12221            return Err(error.into());
12222        }
12223
12224        // Successor gate, the Entry's half of the one in `SessionPixSupervisor`. A correct Exit asks
12225        // for the next batch when the *last* cycle of the current one is nearly recovered, by which
12226        // point we have long been emitting that cycle's shares. An Exit that asks earlier is asking
12227        // for deposits it cannot have earned, so nothing here commits and nothing is deposited.
12228        //
12229        // Two conditions, and the second is what the first alone cannot give. Emission must have
12230        // reached the last committed cycle — which, with the window clamped to one cycle, means every
12231        // earlier one is exhausted — *and* it must be far enough into that cycle. Checking only the
12232        // index admitted a successor batch on the last cycle's very first share, i.e. ~0 % of the way
12233        // through the batch rather than the ~79 % at which a conforming Exit asks. That is nearly a
12234        // whole cycle of unearned deposits, on a gate whose entire purpose is to prevent them.
12235        //
12236        // The boundary is derived rather than guessed — see `min_emission_for_early_recovery`, which
12237        // accounts for the Exit counting *polynomials* and for emission running in lockstep windows
12238        // that spend their whole surplus before the next window starts. A flat fraction of the cycle
12239        // gets this badly wrong in the unsafe direction: 0.85 over the 3.47× surplus factor is 24.5 %,
12240        // against a true boundary of 78.6 % at the deployed dimensions.
12241        //
12242        // Being early is refused rather than fatal, and deliberately not via `refuse_ssa_request`,
12243        // which closes the Session: that message is dropped as `NotAdmitted` and the Session left
12244        // running. A correct Exit never lands there. One that does is not told, but it is not lost
12245        // either: the Exit's supervisor sends an unanswered successor request again every
12246        // `ssa_request_resend_interval` while the batch before it is still being served, so the same
12247        // request is admitted as soon as emission has caught up, and an Exit that never sends it again
12248        // has its own deadline for the cycles it already allocated. Either way nothing is paid for
12249        // before it is earned. Lost generator state is the one arm that *is* fatal, for the reason
12250        // given at it.
12251        //
12252        // First index rather than each: `commitments` is a `BTreeMap`, so the lowest index leads, and
12253        // checking it before the loop is also what stops a batch that fails partway from having
12254        // already emitted `ReadyToDeposit` for its earlier members.
12255        //
12256        // Computed at the protocol floor rather than at our own reconstructor's threshold. The value
12257        // that decides when a correct Exit asks is *its* setting, which does not travel on the wire;
12258        // gating on ours refused a peer configured lower, silently — two valid configurations that
12259        // could not talk, and which the Exit's re-sends only turn from fatal into a stream of refusals
12260        // until emission catches up. See `MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD`, which every Exit is held to by
12261        // `validate_pix_supervision` and which is therefore the earliest any conforming peer can ask.
12262        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
12263            &our_params,
12264            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
12265        );
12266        match pix_toolbox.share_generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym) {
12267            Some(progress) if !progress.is_serving_last_committed() || progress.front_emitted < min_emitted => {
12268                let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
12269                    "Exit asked for SSAs from {first_asked:?} while emission has reached {:?} ({} of {min_emitted} \
12270                     shares needed for an early-recovery signal) of the batch committed up to {}",
12271                    progress.highest_emitted, progress.front_emitted, progress.last_committed
12272                ));
12273                SsaRefusal::Early.log(
12274                    ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::Early),
12275                    &msg.session_id,
12276                    &error,
12277                );
12278                return Err(error.into());
12279            }
12280            // No generator state, but this Session has committed before: the entry was discarded
12281            // under us and the gate above has nothing left to measure.
12282            //
12283            // Absent state is otherwise the ordinary opening batch, which is why the gate treats it as
12284            // admissible — and that is the whole of the hole this closes. The generator keeps its
12285            // per-pseudonym entry in a cache with an idle retention, refreshed by share *emission*; a
12286            // Session kept alive on KeepAlives alone while the Entry sends nothing outlives it. An Exit
12287            // that arranges exactly that gets the successor gate deleted rather than merely relaxed —
12288            // no emission boundary, and no monotonic index either, since the discarded entry took the
12289            // high-watermark with it — and can then farm a fresh deposit per retention period.
12290            //
12291            // Terminal rather than a dropped message. The polynomials for the committed cycles went
12292            // with the entry, so `next_share` yields nothing and no share of them will ever be emitted:
12293            // whatever the Exit deposited against them is already unrecoverable and this half of the
12294            // Session can make no further PIX progress. Refusing quietly would leave the Exit to
12295            // discover that by timing out on commitments we have decided never to send.
12296            None if session_slot
12297                .current_ssa_state
12298                .get()
12299                .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark)
12300                .is_some() =>
12301            {
12302                let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
12303                    "generator state for {pseudonym} was discarded while the Session was live; the cycles committed \
12304                     up to {:?} can no longer be served",
12305                    session_slot
12306                        .current_ssa_state
12307                        .get()
12308                        .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark)
12309                ));
12310                warn!(session_id = %msg.session_id, %error, "refused an SSA request against lost generator state");
12311                self.refuse_ssa_request(
12312                    msg.session_id,
12313                    session_slot.routing_opts.clone(),
12314                    &session_slot.instance,
12315                )
12316                .await;
12317                return Err(error.into());
12318            }
12319            _ => {}
12320        }
12321
12322        // Second half of the successor gate, and the one that measures the Exit rather than us.
12323        //
12324        // Emission above is this node's own work: it counts shares handed to the local packet
12325        // pipeline by `create_surb_for_path`, a consumption that is not even rolled back when the
12326        // rest of the packet build fails. An Exit that requests, is funded, and then returns nothing
12327        // still walks that counter forward for as long as we keep sending, so on its own it prices
12328        // deposits against work we did to ourselves.
12329        //
12330        // What is checked here is service that actually arrived. A share is encrypted with the first
12331        // relayer's challenge solution and rides a return SURB, so the Exit can only decrypt it by
12332        // *using* that SURB — one returned packet is one SURB consumed is one share unlocked. The
12333        // Exit cannot inflate this without unlocking exactly as many shares, which advances the
12334        // recovery it is claiming to have made. Nothing it reports is trusted.
12335        //
12336        // Skipped before the first commitment: the opening batch is the one nothing has been paid
12337        // for yet, and there is no service to have been rendered against it.
12338        if let Some(state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get()
12339            && let Some(watermark) = state.committed_watermark()
12340        {
12341            let shares_per_cycle = our_params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * our_params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
12342            let target = (watermark.get() as u64 - 1) * shares_per_cycle + min_emitted;
12343
12344            // Discounted, because the Exit unlocks a share when the *first relayer* acknowledges,
12345            // which is upstream of us: every packet lost after that point is progress it legitimately
12346            // has and we cannot see. Demanding the undiscounted figure would refuse conforming Exits
12347            // on any lossy path.
12348            //
12349            // By the loss a cycle actually survives, not by the surplus ratio `s/(t+s)` this used to
12350            // take. The ratio is break-even — the loss at which a polynomial receives `t` shares on
12351            // average — and a cycle needs every polynomial to clear it, so at break-even it fails. At
12352            // the deployed `4096 × (32 + 79)` the ratio is 71.2 % against a tolerance of 50.3 % — a
12353            // cycle losing 71.2 % of its shares does not recover — and discounting by it put the bar
12354            // at 23.9 % of a cycle's packets, below even the 111 424 shares a lossless Exit must have
12355            // unlocked to reach its early-recovery point. The tolerance puts the mean at 41.3 %; the bound
12356            // below sets the bar at 41.0 %.
12357            //
12358            // The discount is also what an Exit can withhold for as long as it likes and still have
12359            // every next deposit funded — one whose first return relayer is its own acknowledges each
12360            // packet, unlocking the share, and drops it. So it is the design tolerance and no more:
12361            // the loss the negotiated surplus carries at the 99 % target `default_surplus_for` sizes
12362            // it to. That is the tolerance the *Entry* bought, as insurance against the return
12363            // relayers it picked — one expecting unreliable relayers buys more surplus and thereby
12364            // loosens its own gate. How strict the gate is follows from that choice; it is not a knob
12365            // of its own, and the Exit, which judges an offer by its quota alone, does not set it.
12366            //
12367            // Not at the mean of what an Exit losing that much returns, though, but well below it. One
12368            // losing exactly the tolerance downstream of its first return relayer still unlocks every
12369            // share and asks at the lossless boundary, and the packets of it that reach us are
12370            // `Binomial(target, 1 − L)`: short of their mean half the time, and at the deployed split
12371            // one time in five by more than the near-miss window below — refused at once, and left to
12372            // the Exit's next re-send to retry rather than to the Session's deadline.
12373            // `SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS` standard deviations under the mean make that negligible
12374            // for a fraction of a percent more that an Exit can withhold. The deviation is the same
12375            // binomial's, so the bound still follows the split the Entry chose; a split without
12376            // surplus is demanded its whole target.
12377            let required = successor_required_packets(target, our_params.tolerated_share_loss());
12378
12379            let served = |slot: &SessionSlot| {
12380                state.served_since_first_commit(slot.returned_packets.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed))
12381            };
12382            let mut observed = served(&session_slot);
12383
12384            if observed < required {
12385                // A conforming Exit asks the instant its reconstructor crosses the threshold, and the
12386                // request travels the same mixed path as the packets that earned it — so it can
12387                // overtake the last few of them. Refusing that is not free even though the Exit
12388                // re-sends: the next one is an interval away (`ssa_request_resend_interval`, the
12389                // Exit's setting, 3 s by default), and on a path that is merely a few packets behind
12390                // it would have been admitted at once. A short wait costs nothing and saves the
12391                // interval.
12392                //
12393                // Entered only for a near miss, and that is what keeps the wait from being a lever:
12394                // this handler runs under a bounded `for_each_concurrent` and holds the
12395                // per-pseudonym request lock, so an Exit must already have returned all but one
12396                // emission window of what it owes to occupy either. Anything further out is refused
12397                // on the spot, at no cost to us.
12398                //
12399                // One window rather than a fraction of `required`: it is the unit emission advances
12400                // in, so a shortfall below it is genuinely in-flight, and a percentage would round to
12401                // zero at exactly the small dimensions where this matters most.
12402                let near_miss = observed > 0 && required - observed <= hopr_protocol_pix::SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64;
12403                if near_miss {
12404                    let deadline = Instant::now() + SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT;
12405                    while observed < required && Instant::now() < deadline {
12406                        hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::sleep(SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_POLL).await;
12407                        observed = served(&session_slot);
12408                    }
12409                }
12410            }
12411
12412            if observed < required {
12413                let error = SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(format!(
12414                    "Exit asked for SSAs having returned {observed} of the {required} packets its batch committed up \
12415                     to {watermark} has been paid for"
12416                ));
12417                SsaRefusal::UnderServed.log(
12418                    ssa_state.note_refusal(first_asked, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
12419                    &msg.session_id,
12420                    &error,
12421                );
12422                return Err(error.into());
12423            }
12424        }
12425
12426        let mut msg_sender = self.msg_sender.get().cloned().ok_or(SessionManagerError::NotStarted)?;
12427        let session_id = msg.session_id;
12428
12429        // The server can theoretically send multiple SSA commitments asking us to make the equal
12430        // number of client commitments and deposits, and the batch is all-or-nothing: either every
12431        // member gets a commitment and a `ReadyToDeposit`, or none does.
12432        //
12433        // Hence three phases rather than one loop. Interleaving them meant a batch whose *second*
12434        // exit commitment failed to decode had already sent the first member's `SsaCommit` burst and
12435        // emitted its `ReadyToDeposit` — an on-chain deposit instruction — before the failure was
12436        // reached. The Exit, whose own request was rejected as a whole, has no cycle to spend it on.
12437        //
12438        // The server is authoritative in giving the ssa_index; the client only verifies that it is
12439        // strictly monotonic. That monotonicity is enforced inside `new_ssa_commitment` in phase two,
12440        // which rejects any `ssa_index` that is `<=` the last one generated for this pseudonym with
12441        // `PixError::InvalidInput` (see `SsaShareGenerator::new_ssa_commitment`). Because that call
12442        // happens in a phase before anything is published, a stale, duplicate, or out-of-order
12443        // `SsaRequest` cannot cause a deposit — the whole message is rejected first. The
12444        // per-pseudonym baseline lives in the generator's `polynomials` cache (30-min idle TTL,
12445        // refreshed on every use), so it persists for the life of an active session. Gaps (an index
12446        // strictly greater than the last, but not the immediate successor) are allowed by design,
12447        // since the Exit may advance by more than one SSA at a time.
12448
12449        // Phase 1 — validate. Decoding is the only step that consumes attacker-supplied bytes:
12450        // `try_into_pix_group` decompresses the point and rejects anything outside the prime-order
12451        // subgroup. Doing every one of them up front is what makes a malformed later member cost
12452        // nothing, and it is cheap relative to phase two.
12453        // Taken out before the loop consumes `msg.commitments`, and drained as the loop goes: an SSA
12454        // is committed to once, so its deposit data is needed once.
12455        let mut deposit_payloads = msg.deposit_data;
12456
12457        let mut validated = Vec::with_capacity(msg.commitments.len());
12458        for (ssa_index, exit_commitment) in msg.commitments {
12459            trace!(ssa_index, "received Exit SSA commitment");
12460            match exit_commitment.try_into_pix_group() {
12461                Ok(point) => validated.push((ssa_index, point)),
12462                Err(error) => {
12463                    // Terminal, like every other unacceptable-parameter case here. A peer that cannot
12464                    // produce a valid group element is not going to produce one on a retry, and the
12465                    // Exit would otherwise wait out `max_ssa_delivery_time` on commitments that are
12466                    // never coming.
12467                    let error = SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(format!(
12468                        "Exit sent an undecodable SSA commitment for index {ssa_index}: {error}"
12469                    ));
12470                    self.refuse_ssa_request(session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone(), &session_slot.instance)
12471                        .await;
12472                    return Err(error.into());
12473                }
12474            }
12475        }
12476
12477        // Phase 2 — stage. Generates every client commitment and derives every deposit address,
12478        // publishing none of them. This is the expensive phase, and it still mutates the generator:
12479        // `new_ssa_commitment` appends to the per-pseudonym polynomial queue. Failing here therefore
12480        // leaves queued polynomials the Exit never learns of — wasted work rather than a leaked
12481        // deposit instruction, and the generator's own monotonic index keeps them from being mistaken
12482        // for a later cycle's. That same index makes a failure after the first member was generated
12483        // the end of the Session, below.
12484        let watermark_before = ssa_state.committed_watermark();
12485        let mut staged: Vec<(AgreedSsaQuota, CommitmentBurst)> = Vec::with_capacity(validated.len());
12486        let staging: errors::Result<()> = async {
12487            for (ssa_index, exit_point) in validated {
12488                // Use the global `pix_toolbox.share_generator` to generate the client
12489                // commitment. The generator is shared with the packet pipeline's
12490                // `next_share`, so polynomials created here will be used when the
12491                // pipeline embeds PIX shares into return-path SURBs.
12492                //
12493                // The generator dimension (polys × threshold) must match what the
12494                // Exit's reconstructor expects — both are set from the session's
12495                // negotiated PIX params (pix_global_config on Entry → SsaRequest
12496                // params on Exit).  If the client sends commitments that exceed the
12497                // Exit's expected dimensions, the Exit rejects them as InvalidInput.
12498                let pix_toolbox_clone = pix_toolbox.clone();
12499                let client_commitment = crate::pix_pool::spawn_pix_blocking(
12500                    crate::pix_pool::PixPoolOperation::CommitmentGeneration,
12501                    move || {
12502                        pix_toolbox_clone
12503                            .share_generator
12504                            .new_ssa_commitment(&pseudonym, ssa_index)
12505                    },
12506                )
12507                .await
12508                .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?
12509                .map_err(SessionManagerError::PixError)?;
12510
12511                // The generator has been advanced for this index, so the Session records it now rather
12512                // than after the publish phase. Recording it early is the safe direction: the watermark
12513                // only ever makes the successor gate stricter, and a batch abandoned between here and
12514                // publication has still moved the generator.
12515                if let Some(state) = session_slot.current_ssa_state.get() {
12516                    state.note_committed(
12517                        ssa_index,
12518                        session_slot.returned_packets.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
12519                    );
12520                }
12521
12522                // Construct the full SSA by adding the client and exit commitments, getting the deposit address
12523                let full_ssa = client_commitment.ssa_commitment + exit_point;
12524                let deposit_address = HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address(full_ssa).ok_or(
12525                    SessionManagerError::other(anyhow::anyhow!("failed to convert SSA to deposit address")),
12526                )?;
12527
12528                // Split the SSA client commitment into Start protocol commitment messages
12529                let commitment_msgs = SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(session_id, client_commitment)
12530                    .map_err(SessionManagerError::other)?;
12531                debug!(%ssa_index, count = commitment_msgs.len(), "generated client SSA commitment messages");
12532
12533                // What `ReadyToDeposit` will say, fixed here with the address. Kept whole so that a
12534                // publication that is cut short can still announce it later: nothing about it can be
12535                // derived again once this request is gone, the deposit data least of all.
12536                let quota = AgreedSsaQuota {
12537                    ssa_id: SsaId::new(pseudonym, ssa_index),
12538                    deposit_address,
12539                    quota_per_ssa,
12540                    // Rebuilt rather than carried: the `id` is not on the wire, because this message
12541                    // already says which Session and which SSA these bytes belong to.
12542                    deposit_data: PixDepositData {
12543                        id: PixAddressId::new(&pseudonym, ssa_index),
12544                        data: deposit_payloads
12545                            .remove(&ssa_index)
12546                            .map(|payload| payload.0)
12547                            .unwrap_or_default(),
12548                    },
12549                };
12550                staged.push((quota, commitment_msgs));
12551            }
12552            Ok(())
12553        }
12554        .await;
12555        if let Err(error) = staging {
12556            // Nothing generated yet means nothing moved, and the Exit's next re-send tries the whole
12557            // batch again. Once a member has been generated, though, the batch can never be committed.
12558            // The generator refuses that member's index for good, so every re-send of this request
12559            // would be dropped as stale until the Exit's deadline closed the Session,
12560            // and meanwhile the polynomials it queued would go on to be emitted for a cycle whose
12561            // commitment the Exit never receives. Terminal, like lost generator state, and for the
12562            // same reason: this half of the Session can make no further PIX progress.
12563            if ssa_state.committed_watermark() != watermark_before {
12564                tracing::error!(
12565                    %session_id, %error,
12566                    "staging an admitted SSA batch failed after part of it was generated; it can never be committed"
12567                );
12568                self.refuse_ssa_request(session_id, session_slot.routing_opts.clone(), &session_slot.instance)
12569                    .await;
12570            }
12571            return Err(error);
12572        }
12573
12574        // Recorded once phase two has staged the whole request, and before anything is published: a
12575        // burst that then fails to send has still moved the generator, and the re-sends of this request
12576        // must be recognised as repeats of it. See `SessionSsaState::last_committed_first`. The same
12577        // moment records every member as owed its publication, which is what lets a repeat finish the
12578        // job when phase three is cut short.
12579        ssa_state.stage_unpublished(staged.iter().map(|(quota, _)| quota.clone()));
12580        if let Some((quota, _)) = staged.first() {
12581            ssa_state.note_committed_first(quota.ssa_id.ssa_index());
12582        }
12583
12584        // Phase 3 — publish. Nothing below can fail on the *content* of the request; only the
12585        // transport can, and under ordinary backpressure it does: a send gives up after
12586        // `EXTERNAL_SEND_TIMEOUT`. A failed send does not fail the Session. The member being published
12587        // goes back to the owed set and a non-fatal `NotAdmitted` is returned, logged once at `warn!`;
12588        // members after it were never claimed and stay owed too. What happens next is up to the Exit,
12589        // which has two ways to ask again: its automatic repeat of this request, sent only while some
12590        // member of the batch has reported nothing and the batch is behind the front, and its scoped
12591        // re-request for a member whose commitment began to arrive, which works wherever the batch
12592        // stands and resumes every owed member, not only the one named, but only when the member it
12593        // names is itself still owed, because its own burst was cut part-way. Two cases are therefore
12594        // not recovered. A member of which no message went out, whose batch holds the front (the
12595        // opening batch always does), is resumed only as a side effect of a re-request for an earlier
12596        // member of the same batch that is itself still owed. And a member whose whole burst went out
12597        // but whose `ReadyToDeposit` could not be queued prompts no request at all, since the Exit
12598        // already holds its complete commitment. In both the Exit's own deadline ends the cycle, and
12599        // nothing is stranded for that member because nothing was announced for it. See
12600        // `SessionSsaState::unpublished` and `resume_publication`.
12601        for (staged_quota, burst) in staged {
12602            // Claimed just before its burst, so that nobody else can publish this member while this
12603            // call is doing so, and so that only the claimant announces it.
12604            let ssa_index = staged_quota.ssa_id.ssa_index();
12605            let Some(claim) = ssa_state.claim_unpublished(ssa_index) else {
12606                tracing::debug!(%ssa_index, "another task is already publishing this SSA's commitment");
12607                continue;
12608            };
12609
12610            match publish_commitment(
12611                &pix_toolbox,
12612                &mut msg_sender,
12613                &session_slot.routing_opts,
12614                burst,
12615                &claim.quota,
12616                "client SSA commitment message",
12617            )
12618            .await
12619            {
12620                Ok(()) => ssa_state.complete_publication(claim, Instant::now()),
12621                Err(error) => return Err(publication_cut_short(session_id, ssa_state, claim, &error)),
12622            }
12623        }
12624
12625        trace!(quota_per_ssa, "Exit commitment message has been fully processed");
12626        Ok(())
12627    }
12628}

12651    #[tokio::test]
12652    async fn deposit_observer_forwards_each_confirmation_for_its_cycle() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12653        let warnings = Arc::new(WarnCounter::default());
12654        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();

12656        let address_id = PixAddressId::new(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN);
12657        let other_index = SsaIndex::new(2).context("index two is non-zero")?;
12658        let first_amount = HoprBalance::zero();
12659        let second_amount = HoprBalance::new_base(1000);
12660        let confirmations = futures::stream::iter([
12661            (address_id, first_amount),
12662            (PixAddressId::new(&session_id, other_index), second_amount),
12663            (
12664                PixAddressId::new(&HoprPseudonym::random(), SsaIndex::MIN),

12672            events.lock().push(event);
12673            futures::future::ready(Ok(()))

12680            warnings.count(),

12689                SessionPixEvent::DepositObserverClosed(closed_id),

12691                && *first == first_amount && *second == second_amount

12694    }

12823    /// A [`PixToolbox`] whose deposit-data requests are answered, for tests that do not read the
12824    /// PIX event stream themselves.
12825    ///
12826    /// An Exit cannot send an `SsaRequest` without the pool answering, so a test that only needs the
12827    /// request to *happen* would otherwise be asserting against `MissingDepositData`.
12828    fn pix_toolbox_with_pool(
12829        generator: Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
12830        reconstructor: Arc<SsaReconstructor<HoprPixSpec>>,
12831    ) -> PixToolbox {
12832        let (toolbox, events) = PixToolbox::new(generator, reconstructor);
12833        // The answering task owns `events`, and lives until the toolbox is dropped. The forwarded
12834        // stream is discarded: these tests do not read PIX events.
12835        drop(crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(events, |_| Vec::new()));
12836        toolbox
12837    }

12868    #[tokio::test]
12869    async fn abort_on_drop_stops_the_task() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
12870        let (started_tx, started_rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<()>();
12871        let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<()>();
12872        let guard = AbortOnDrop::from(hopr_utils::runtime::prelude::spawn(async move {
12873            let _tx = tx;
12874            let _ = started_tx.send(());
12875            std::future::pending::<()>().await;
12876        }));
12877        started_rx.await.context("the task never ran")?;
12878        drop(guard);
12879
12880        let result = timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), rx)
12881            .await
12882            .context("the task was not aborted")?;
12883        assert!(result.is_err(), "the sender must have been dropped without sending");
12884        Ok(())
12885    }

12907    /// The head-of-line bound must reach a session that cannot recover a missing frame, and must
12908    /// not reach one that can.
12909    ///
12910    /// Both halves matter. Without the first, a session with no retransmission holds every frame
12911    /// behind a gap for the full frame timeout, waiting for something that is never coming —
12912    /// measured on a cluster as 98.5 % of bytes arriving over the wire and 0.60 % reaching the
12913    /// application. Without the second, a session that *would* have retransmitted the gap instead
12914    /// abandons it, turning recoverable frames into loss.
12915    #[test]
12916    fn session_config_should_bound_the_gap_only_without_retransmission() {
12917        assert_eq!(
12918            SessionManagerConfig::default().max_frames_behind_gap,
12919            Some(256),
12920            "the default must bound the gap, or the stall stays in place unless opted out of"
12921        );
12922
12923        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
12924            max_frames_behind_gap: Some(8),
12925            ..Default::default()
12926        };
12927
12928        for reliable in [Capability::RetransmissionAck, Capability::RetransmissionNack] {
12929            assert_eq!(
12930                session_config(&cfg, reliable.into()).max_frames_behind_gap,
12931                None,
12932                "{reliable:?} can recover the gap, so the wait is productive and must be left alone"
12933            );
12934        }
12935
12936        for unreliable in [Capabilities::empty(), Capability::Segmentation.into()] {
12937            assert_eq!(
12938                session_config(&cfg, unreliable).max_frames_behind_gap,
12939                Some(8),
12940                "without retransmission the gap must be bounded"
12941            );
12942        }
12943    }

12945    /// The right value tracks throughput x latency spread, which is a property of the *session*,
12946    /// not of the node: a bulk data session and a control session on the same node have entirely
12947    /// different reordering depths. A caller that knows its own traffic must be able to say so.
12948    #[test]
12949    fn a_session_should_be_able_to_override_the_nodes_gap_bound() {
12950        let node = SessionManagerConfig {
12951            max_frames_behind_gap: Some(256),
12952            ..Default::default()
12953        };
12954
12955        assert_eq!(
12956            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), Some(16)).max_frames_behind_gap,
12957            Some(16),
12958            "the session's own value must win over the node default"
12959        );
12960        assert_eq!(
12961            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), None).max_frames_behind_gap,
12962            Some(256),
12963            "saying nothing must inherit the node default"
12964        );
12965        assert_eq!(
12966            session_config_with(&node, Capabilities::empty(), Some(0)).max_frames_behind_gap,
12967            None,
12968            "zero disables the bound for this session, matching the env knob's semantics"
12969        );
12970    }

12972    /// A per-session override must not be able to re-enable the bound where waiting is productive.

12974    fn a_session_override_should_not_reach_a_session_that_can_retransmit() {
12975        let node = SessionManagerConfig::default();
12976        assert_eq!(
12977            session_config_with(&node, Capability::RetransmissionAck.into(), Some(4)).max_frames_behind_gap,
12978            None,
12979            "retransmission can recover the gap, so no caller should be able to cut the wait short"

13006    /// Balancer state with the given target sitting at the given level.
13007    fn gate_state(target: u64, buffer_level: u64) -> BalancerStateValues {
13008        let state = BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
13009            target_surb_buffer_size: target,
13010            ..Default::default()

13013            .buffer_level

13018    /// How a stand-in sink treats the one packet a control send hands it.
13019    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
13020    enum SinkMode {
13021        NeverReady,
13022        StartSendFails,
13023        FlushFails,
13024        FlushNeverCompletes,
13025        Accepts,
13026    }
13027
13028    #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
13029    struct StandInSinkError;
13030
13031    impl std::fmt::Display for StandInSinkError {
13032        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
13033            f.write_str("stand-in sink failure")
13034        }
13035    }
13036
13037    impl std::error::Error for StandInSinkError {}
13038
13039    struct StandInSink(SinkMode);
13040
13041    impl Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> for StandInSink {
13042        type Error = StandInSinkError;
13043
13044        fn poll_ready(
13045            self: std::pin::Pin<&mut Self>,
13046            _: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
13047        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
13048            match self.0 {
13049                SinkMode::NeverReady => std::task::Poll::Pending,
13050                _ => std::task::Poll::Ready(Ok(())),
13051            }
13052        }
13053
13054        fn start_send(
13055            self: std::pin::Pin<&mut Self>,
13056            _: (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut),
13057        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
13058            match self.0 {
13059                SinkMode::StartSendFails => Err(StandInSinkError),
13060                _ => Ok(()),
13061            }
13062        }
13063
13064        fn poll_flush(
13065            self: std::pin::Pin<&mut Self>,
13066            _: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
13067        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
13068            match self.0 {
13069                SinkMode::FlushFails => std::task::Poll::Ready(Err(StandInSinkError)),
13070                SinkMode::FlushNeverCompletes => std::task::Poll::Pending,
13071                _ => std::task::Poll::Ready(Ok(())),
13072            }
13073        }
13074
13075        fn poll_close(
13076            self: std::pin::Pin<&mut Self>,
13077            _: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
13078        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
13079            std::task::Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
13080        }
13081    }
13082
13083    /// Sends one counted control packet into a sink of `mode`, and returns the result with the estimator's
13084    /// `(consumed, refunded)`.
13085    async fn counted_control_send(mode: SinkMode) -> anyhow::Result<(errors::Result<()>, u64, u64)> {
13086        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
13087
13088        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
13089        let mut sink = StandInSink(mode);
13090        let result = send_counted_via_msg_sender(
13091            &mut sink,

13154    /// A packet short enough to have room for a SURB. `max_surbs_with_message` is
13155    /// `(PAYLOAD_SIZE - len) / SURB_SIZE`, so anything past roughly half the payload already caps
13156    /// itself at zero and would make the assertions below pass for the wrong reason.
13157    fn small_outgoing_packet() -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationDataOut> {
13158        let data = ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG, b"short")?);
13159        anyhow::ensure!(
13160            data.estimate_surbs_with_msg() >= 1,
13161            "fixture must have room for a SURB, otherwise the cap is not what is being measured"
13162        );
13163        Ok(data)
13164    }
13165
13166    /// `account_incoming_surbs` must keep the estimator's held count (`saturating_diff`) equal to
13167    /// what a bounded store of capacity `CAP` would actually hold across a fill-past-capacity-then-drain
13168    /// sequence. The eviction term is what makes the held count fall back to zero once the overflow is
13169    /// drained -- and so what stops the keep-alive report and the PIX fill reserve from reading a level
13170    /// that never falls.
13171    #[test]
13172    fn account_incoming_surbs_tracks_a_bounded_store_through_overflow_and_drain() {
13173        const CAP: u64 = 100;
13174        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
13175        let mut occupancy: u64 = 0;
13176
13177        let mut receive = |batch: u64| {
13178            let evicted = (occupancy + batch).saturating_sub(CAP);
13179            occupancy = (occupancy + batch).min(CAP);
13180            account_incoming_surbs(&estimator, batch, evicted);
13181        };
13182
13183        for _ in 0..5 {
13184            receive(40);
13185        }
13186        assert_eq!(occupancy, CAP, "the model store is full");
13187        assert_eq!(
13188            estimator.saturating_diff(),
13189            CAP,
13190            "held count tracks a full store, not the {}-SURB total received",
13191            5 * 40
13192        );
13193
13194        for _ in 0..CAP {
13195            estimator.consumed.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
13196            occupancy -= 1;
13197        }
13198        assert_eq!(occupancy, 0, "the model store is empty");
13199        assert_eq!(
13200            estimator.saturating_diff(),
13201            0,
13202            "held count returns to zero after the drain; the evicted surplus is not counted as held"
13203        );
13204    }

13206    /// The gate primitive itself mints whenever the level is below the effective target. A level
13207    /// short of target with no capacity inferred yet still mints -- the stop for a smaller-than-target
13208    /// store comes from inferring its capacity over successive reports (see
13209    /// `a_plateau_below_target_infers_the_counterparty_capacity` in `balancer/controller.rs`), which
13210    /// lowers the effective target rather than changing this primitive.

13220        assert_eq!(

13222            data.estimate_surbs_with_msg(),

13224        );
13225        Ok(())
13226    }

13412            {

13415                    .get(&pseudonym)

13417                assert_eq!(
13418                    balancing,

13421                );
13422                assert!(
13423                    !slot.surb_mgmt.refill_pacing_active(),
13424                    "{why}: no pacing at the Exit's start"
13425                );
13426            }
13427
13428            sender.close_channel();
13429            transport.await??;
13430        }

13451    fn mock_packet_planning(
13452        sender: MockMsgSender,
13453    ) -> (
13454        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
13455        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
13456    ) {
13457        let (tx, rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
13458        let handle = tokio::task::spawn(async move {
13459            pin_mut!(rx);
13460            while let Some((routing, data)) = rx.next().await {
13461                sender.send_message(routing, data).await?;
13462            }
13463            Ok(())
13464        });
13465        (tx, handle)
13466    }

13490    /// Waits (bounded) until the manager reports no active sessions.
13491    ///
13492    /// The session-slot rollback runs on a spawned task, so its effect is observed
13493    /// asynchronously; this polls [`SessionManager::active_sessions`] until it drains.
13494    async fn wait_for_no_active_sessions(
13495        mgr: &SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
13496    ) -> bool {
13497        for _ in 0..50 {
13498            if mgr.active_sessions().is_empty() {
13499                return true;
13500            }
13501            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
13502        }
13503        mgr.active_sessions().is_empty()
13504    }
