13506    const SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY: usize = 10000;
13507
13508    /// Waits (bounded) until `admission` has recorded at least `count` retires of `pseudonym`.
13509    ///
13510    /// The retire is deferred past the SURB-resolution window by [`release_session_slot`], and the
13511    /// teardown that asks for it does not always run on the test's own task — the slot-guard rollback
13512    /// removes the slot on a spawned task, and the cache's eviction listener runs on moka's
13513    /// maintenance thread — so a test that counts immediately after triggering a teardown would race
13514    /// it twice over. Polling keeps the test honest about the ordering it actually asserts (retire
13515    /// happens, and after the admit) without sleeping a fixed delay in every test that touches the
13516    /// seam. `surb_retire_grace`'s one-second margin is what bounds the wait below the ten-second
13517    /// ceiling even when a test keeps the default `surb_resolution_wait`.
13518    async fn wait_for_retire(admission: &RecordingAdmission, pseudonym: &SessionId, count: usize) -> usize {
13519        for _ in 0..200 {
13520            let retired = admission.retired(pseudonym);
13521            if retired >= count {
13522                return retired;
13523            }
13524            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
13525        }
13526        admission.retired(pseudonym)
13527    }

13529    /// A return packet the Exit counted as consumed, and routing resolution then dropped for want of a
13530    /// SURB, spent nothing. Its refund counts the SURB as given back in the estimator that counted it,
13531    /// on a counter of its own rather than one fewer consumed: the balancer reads the counters as deltas
13532    /// between samples and rejects a snapshot in which one of them went down. The held count takes the
13533    /// SURB back; the balancer's delta does not (see `a_refund_should_not_raise_the_balancer_level`).
13534    #[test]
13535    fn a_counted_return_packet_should_give_its_surb_back_to_the_estimator_that_counted_it() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13536        use crate::balancer::{SimpleSurbFlowEstimator, SurbFlowEstimator};
13537
13538        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
13539        estimator.produced.fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
13540        let data = count_return_packet_surb(&estimator, small_outgoing_packet()?);
13541        assert!(data.surb_refund.is_counted(), "a counted packet carries its refund");
13542        assert_eq!(9, estimator.saturating_diff(), "counted as it was handed on");
13543
13544        let before = SimpleSurbFlowEstimator::from(&estimator);
13545        data.surb_refund.give_back();
13546        assert_eq!(
13547            10,
13548            estimator.saturating_diff(),
13549            "the starved packet's SURB is back in the held count"
13550        );
13551        assert_eq!(
13552            Some(0),
13553            SimpleSurbFlowEstimator::from(&estimator).estimated_surb_buffer_change(&before),
13554            "every counter still grows, and the balancer's delta leaves the refund out"
13555        );
13556        Ok(())
13557    }

13559    /// Verifies that a session's SURB balancer config can be retrieved and updated via the manager API.
13560    ///
13561    /// ## Steps
13562    /// 1. A session slot is manually inserted into Alice's manager with a known `SurbBalancerConfig`
13563    ///    (`target_surb_buffer_size: 1000`, `max_surbs_per_sec: 100`).
13564    /// 2. `get_surb_balancer_config` returns the config, confirming round-trip storage.
13565    /// 3. `update_surb_balancer_config` is called with a new config (`target: 2000`, `max: 200`).
13566    /// 4. `get_surb_balancer_config` is called again and the returned config matches the updated values.
13567    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13568    async fn session_manager_should_update_surb_balancer_config() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13569        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
13570        let session_id = alice_pseudonym;
13571        let balancer_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
13572            target_surb_buffer_size: 1000,
13573            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
13574            ..Default::default()
13575        };
13576
13577        let alice_mgr =
13578            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
13579
13580        let (dummy_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
13581        alice_mgr.sessions.insert(
13582            session_id,
13583            SessionSlot {
13584                session_tx: dummy_tx,
13585                routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(alice_pseudonym)),
13586                abort_handles: Default::default(),
13587                surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(balancer_cfg)),
13588                surb_estimator: Default::default(),
13589                current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
13590                pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
13591                pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
13592                pix_fill: Default::default(),
13593                exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
13594                returned_packets: Default::default(),
13595                cycle_budget: None,
13596                admission_token: Default::default(),
13597                raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
13598                forward_receipts: None,
13599                exit_resume: Default::default(),
13600                instance: SlotInstance::new(0),
13601                opening: None,
13602            },
13603        );
13604
13605        let actual_cfg = alice_mgr
13606            .get_surb_balancer_config(&session_id)?
13607            .ok_or(anyhow!("session must have a surb balancer config"))?;
13608        assert_eq!(actual_cfg, balancer_cfg);
13609
13610        let new_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
13611            target_surb_buffer_size: 2000,
13612            max_surbs_per_sec: 200,
13613            ..Default::default()
13614        };
13615        alice_mgr.update_surb_balancer_config(&session_id, new_cfg)?;
13616
13617        let actual_cfg = alice_mgr
13618            .get_surb_balancer_config(&session_id)?
13619            .ok_or(anyhow!("session must have a surb balancer config"))?;
13620        assert_eq!(actual_cfg, new_cfg);
13621
13622        Ok(())
13623    }

13625    /// Verifies that a self-initiated session is rejected with `SessionManagerError::Loopback`.
13626    ///
13627    /// ## Steps
13628    /// 1. Alice's manager is started with a mock transport that delivers messages back to itself.
13629    /// 2. Alice initiates a session toward `bob_peer`; the mock routes her `StartSession` back to her own manager
13630    ///    (simulating a network loopback).
13631    /// 3. Alice's manager processes `StartSession` as incoming, auto-responds with `SessionEstablished`, and the mock
13632    ///    delivers it back to complete the handshake.
13633    /// 4. `new_session` returns `Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Loopback))`.
13634    /// 5. Exactly one active session is present — the incoming slot accepted from the self-delivered `StartSession`.
13635    ///    The rejection fires after slot insertion, not before.
13636    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13637    async fn session_manager_should_not_allow_loopback_sessions() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13638        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
13639        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
13640
13641        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
13642
13643        let mut sequence = mockall::Sequence::new();
13644        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
13645
13646        // Alice sends the StartSession message
13647        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
13648        alice_transport
13649            .expect_send_message()
13650            .once()
13651            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
13652            .withf(move |peer, data| {
13653                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
13654                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
13655            })
13656            .returning(move |_, data| {
13657                // But the message is again processed by Alice due to Loopback
13658                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
13659                Box::pin(async move {
13660                    alice_mgr_clone
13661                        .dispatch_message(
13662                            alice_pseudonym,
13663                            ApplicationDataIn {
13664                                data: data.data,
13665                                packet_info: Default::default(),
13666                            },
13667                        )
13668                        ?;
13669                    Ok(())
13670                })
13671            });
13672
13673        // Alice sends the SessionEstablished message (as Bob)
13674        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
13675        alice_transport
13676            .expect_send_message()
13677            .once()
13678            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
13679            .withf(move |peer, data| {
13680                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished)
13681                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
13682            })
13683            .returning(move |_, data| {
13684                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
13685
13686                Box::pin(async move {
13687                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
13688                        alice_pseudonym,
13689                        ApplicationDataIn {
13690                            data: data.data,
13691                            packet_info: Default::default(),
13692                        },
13693                    )?;
13694                    Ok(())
13695                })
13696            });
13697
13698        // Start Alice
13699        let (new_session_tx_alice, new_session_rx_alice) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
13700        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
13701        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?;
13702        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
13703
13704        let alice_session = alice_mgr
13705            .new_session(
13706                bob_peer,
13707                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
13708                SessionClientConfig {
13709                    capabilities: None.into(),
13710                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
13711                    surb_management: None,
13712                    ..Default::default()
13713                },
13714            )
13715            .await;
13716
13717        println!("{alice_session:?}");
13718        assert!(matches!(
13719            alice_session,
13720            Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Loopback))
13721        ));
13722        // There is one session in the manager, which is the incoming one that Alice's manager
13723        // accepted when it received the StartSession message from itself.
13724        assert_eq!(alice_mgr.num_active_sessions(), 1);
13725
13726        drop(new_session_rx_alice);
13727
13728        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
13729        alice_sender.close_channel();
13730        alice_handle.await??;
13731
13732        Ok(())
13733    }

13735    /// A failed initiation must leave no `pending_outgoing` marker behind: the marker is what lets
13736    /// an `SsaRequest` for the pseudonym wait for a slot at dispatch, and a marker outliving its
13737    /// attempt would park a handler on a Session that never arrives — one per leaked attempt, for
13738    /// as long as the entry's TTL. The marker was once cleared by hand on each failure path and
13739    /// keyed by the peer-supplied `session_id`; the guard that replaces it removes it keyed by the
13740    /// pseudonym it was inserted under, on every path.
13741    ///
13742    /// ## Steps
13743    /// 1. The transport swallows the `StartSession` message, so the initiation is never answered and times out (the
13744    ///    deterministic failure path; a loopback needs a live manager for it to bounce off).
13745    /// 2. `new_session` under a fixed pseudonym fails with `Timeout`.
13746    /// 3. An `SsaRequest` naming that pseudonym must be dropped as stale at dispatch — no marker left to admit it.
13747    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13748    async fn a_failed_session_initiation_must_leave_no_pending_outgoing_marker() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13749        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
13750
13751        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
13752            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(100),
13753            ..Default::default()
13754        };
13755        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(cfg);
13756
13757        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
13758        // Swallow the StartSession: the initiation times out.
13759        alice_transport
13760            .expect_send_message()
13761            .once()
13762            .withf(move |peer, data| {
13763                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
13764                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
13765            })
13766            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
13767
13768        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
13769        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
13770        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
13771        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
13772
13773        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
13774        let result = alice_mgr
13775            .new_session(
13776                bob_peer,
13777                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
13778                SessionClientConfig {
13779                    capabilities: None.into(),
13780                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
13781                    surb_management: None,
13782                    ..Default::default()
13783                },
13784            )
13785            .await;
13786        assert!(
13787            matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)),
13788            "the fixture must actually fail the initiation, got {result:?}"
13789        );
13790
13791        // With no marker left, the same request a fast Exit could have raced ahead of is refused at
13792        // dispatch instead of parking a handler on a slot that will never exist.
13793        let refused = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
13794        assert!(
13795            matches!(refused, DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage)),
13796            "an SsaRequest for a failed initiation's pseudonym must be stale, got {refused:?}"
13797        );
13798
13799        Ok(())
13800    }

13802    /// When a `StartSession` was sent, and its bytes.
13803    type SentRequest = (Instant, Vec<u8>);
13804
13805    /// What the Entry-side repeat tests need: a manager whose transport records every `StartSession` it is given.
13806    struct RepeatingEntry {
13807        mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>,
13808        sent: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<SentRequest>>>,
13809        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
13810        bob: Address,
13811        _transport: tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
13812    }
13813
13814    /// An Entry that repeats after `interval` at most `max_resends` times, waiting `base * 2` for an answer.
13815    fn repeating_entry(base: Duration, interval: Duration, max_resends: u32) -> anyhow::Result<RepeatingEntry> {
13816        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
13817            initiation_timeout_base: base,
13818            initiation_resend_interval: interval,
13819            max_initiation_resends: max_resends,
13820            ..Default::default()
13821        });
13822        let sent = Arc::new(parking_lot::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
13823        let recorded = sent.clone();
13824        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
13825        transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
13826            recorded.lock().push((Instant::now(), data.data.plain_text.to_vec()));
13827            Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
13828        });
13829        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
13830        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
13831        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
13832        Ok(RepeatingEntry {
13833            mgr,
13834            sent,
13835            pseudonym: HoprPseudonym::random(),
13836            bob: (&ChainKeypair::random()).into(),
13837            _transport: handle,
13838        })
13839    }
13840
13841    impl RepeatingEntry {
13842        async fn new_session(&self) -> errors::Result<HoprSession> {
13843            self.mgr
13844                .new_session(
13845                    self.bob,
13846                    SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().expect("valid address"))),
13847                    SessionClientConfig {
13848                        capabilities: None.into(),
13849                        pseudonym: self.pseudonym.into(),
13850                        surb_management: None,
13851                        ..Default::default()
13852                    },
13853                )
13854                .await
13855        }
13856
13857        async fn wait_for_sends(&self, count: usize) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13858            timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
13859                while self.sent.lock().len() < count {
13860                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await;
13861                }
13862            })
13863            .await
13864            .with_context(|| format!("only {} StartSessions were sent, not {count}", self.sent.lock().len()))
13865        }
13866    }

13868    /// An unanswered `StartSession` is repeated, byte for byte, at doubling gaps, and the attempt still times out.
13869    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13870    async fn an_unanswered_start_session_is_repeated_with_doubling_gaps() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13871        let entry = repeating_entry(Duration::from_millis(500), Duration::from_millis(50), 3)?;
13872
13873        let began = Instant::now();
13874        let result = entry.new_session().await;
13875        let elapsed = began.elapsed();
13876
13877        assert!(matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)), "got {result:?}");
13878        assert!(
13879            elapsed >= Duration::from_secs(1),
13880            "the deadline must not move, took {elapsed:?}"
13881        );
13882        let sent = entry.sent.lock();
13883        assert_eq!(4, sent.len(), "the request and its three repeats");
13884        assert!(
13885            sent.iter().all(|(_, bytes)| bytes == &sent[0].1),
13886            "every repeat is identical"
13887        );
13888        // Repeats are due 50, 150 and 350 ms after the first send; a little slack for the clock read.
13889        for (at, due) in sent[1..].iter().map(|(at, _)| at).zip([50, 150, 350]) {
13890            assert!(
13891                at.duration_since(sent[0].0) + Duration::from_millis(10) >= Duration::from_millis(due),
13892                "a repeat came before {due} ms"
13893            );
13894        }
13895        Ok(())
13896    }

13898    /// A repeat that would fall at or after the deadline is not sent.
13899    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13900    async fn a_start_session_repeat_due_at_or_after_the_deadline_is_not_sent() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13901        // The wait is 100 ms; repeats would be due at 50, 150, 350 ... ms.
13902        let entry = repeating_entry(Duration::from_millis(50), Duration::from_millis(50), 10)?;
13903
13904        let result = entry.new_session().await;
13905
13906        assert!(matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)), "got {result:?}");
13907        assert_eq!(2, entry.sent.lock().len(), "only the repeat due before the deadline");
13908        Ok(())
13909    }

13911    /// Once the Exit answers, no further repeat goes out and the Session is returned.
13912    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13913    async fn the_start_session_repeats_stop_once_the_exit_answers() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13914        let entry = repeating_entry(Duration::from_millis(500), Duration::from_millis(50), 3)?;
13915        let attempt = tokio::spawn({
13916            let mgr = entry.mgr.clone();
13917            let (bob, pseudonym) = (entry.bob, entry.pseudonym);
13918            async move {
13919                mgr.new_session(
13920                    bob,
13921                    SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
13922                    SessionClientConfig {
13923                        capabilities: None.into(),
13924                        pseudonym: pseudonym.into(),
13925                        surb_management: None,
13926                        ..Default::default()
13927                    },
13928                )
13929                .await
13930                .map_err(anyhow::Error::from)
13931            }
13932        });
13933
13934        entry.wait_for_sends(2).await?;
13935        let Some(HoprStartProtocol::StartSession(request)) = entry.sent.lock().first().and_then(|(_, bytes)| {
13936            HoprStartProtocol::decode(HoprStartProtocol::START_PROTOCOL_MESSAGE_TAG, bytes).ok()
13937        }) else {
13938            anyhow::bail!("the first message must be a StartSession");
13939        };
13940        entry.mgr.dispatch_message(
13941            entry.pseudonym,
13942            start_packet(HoprStartProtocol::SessionEstablished(StartEstablished {
13943                orig_challenge: request.challenge,
13944                session_id: entry.pseudonym,
13945            }))?,
13946        )?;
13947
13948        let session = timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), attempt)
13949            .await
13950            .context("the attempt never finished")??
13951            .context("the attempt must succeed once answered")?;
13952        // The next repeat would have been due 100 ms after the previous one.
13953        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
13954        assert_eq!(2, entry.sent.lock().len(), "no repeat after the answer");
13955        drop(session);
13956        Ok(())
13957    }

13959    /// A cap of 0 sends the `StartSession` once, as before repeats existed.

13971    /// A repeat the transport fails to send is logged and skipped; the attempt runs on to the later ones.
13972    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
13973    async fn a_failed_repeat_does_not_end_the_initiation() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
13974        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
13975            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(250),
13976            initiation_resend_interval: Duration::from_millis(30),
13977            max_initiation_resends: 2,
13978            ..Default::default()
13979        });
13980        use std::{
13981            pin::Pin,
13982            task::{Context, Poll},
13983        };
13984
13985        // A sink that refuses its second item, which is the first repeat.
13986        #[derive(Clone)]
13987        struct FlakySink(Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize>);
13988        impl Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> for FlakySink {
13989            type Error = futures::channel::mpsc::SendError;
13990
13991            fn poll_ready(self: Pin<&mut Self>, _: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
13992                Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
13993            }
13994
13995            fn start_send(
13996                self: Pin<&mut Self>,
13997                _: (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut),
13998            ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
13999                if self.0.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) == 1 {
14000                    let (mut closed, receiver) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<()>();
14001                    drop(receiver);
14002                    return closed.start_send(());
14003                }
14004                Ok(())
14005            }
14006
14007            fn poll_flush(self: Pin<&mut Self>, _: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
14008                Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
14009            }
14010
14011            fn poll_close(self: Pin<&mut Self>, _: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
14012                Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
14013            }
14014        }
14015        let attempts = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
14016        let sender = FlakySink(attempts.clone());
14017        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
14018        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14019
14020        let result = mgr
14021            .new_session(
14022                (&ChainKeypair::random()).into(),
14023                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14024                SessionClientConfig {
14025                    capabilities: None.into(),
14026                    surb_management: None,
14027                    ..Default::default()
14028                },
14029            )
14030            .await;
14031
14032        assert!(matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)), "got {result:?}");
14033        assert_eq!(3, attempts.load(Ordering::Relaxed), "the second repeat is still sent");
14034        Ok(())
14035    }
14036
14037    /// Records each `advance_generation` with how many `StartSession`s had been sent by then.
14038    struct GenerationRecorder {
14039        sent: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<SentRequest>>>,
14040        calls: parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<(usize, SessionId)>>,
14041    }
14042
14043    impl SurbAdmissionControl for GenerationRecorder {
14044        fn admit(&self, _: &SessionId, _: usize) -> AdmissionToken {
14045            AdmissionToken::NONE
14046        }
14047
14048        fn retire(&self, _: &SessionId, _: AdmissionToken) {}
14049
14050        fn advance_generation(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId) {
14051            self.calls.lock().push((self.sent.lock().len(), *pseudonym));
14052        }
14053    }

14062        });

14064
14065        let result = entry.new_session().await;
14066
14067        assert!(matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)), "got {result:?}");
14068        assert_eq!(
14069            vec![(1, entry.pseudonym), (2, entry.pseudonym), (3, entry.pseudonym)],
14070            *recorder.calls.lock(),
14071            "one call per repeat, each after the sends before it and before its own"
14072        );
14073        Ok(())

14093    /// A second initiation for a pseudonym already claimed by one in flight must be refused, not
14094    /// silently overwrite the first one's `pending_outgoing` reservation.
14095    ///
14096    /// `moka`'s `insert` overwrites an existing entry, so the claim the first initiation holds used
14097    /// to be a single shared marker: whichever attempt finished first removed it while the other
14098    /// was still awaiting establishment, and an `SsaRequest` for that Session then failed the
14099    /// dispatch filter and was dropped as `StaleStartMessage` — a false negative, the exact class
14100    /// of miss the filter must not have. `new_session` therefore claims the name atomically and
14101    /// refuses the overlap.
14102    ///
14103    /// ## Steps
14104    /// 1. Alice's transport swallows the first `StartSession` (expectation `.once()`), so that initiation stays in
14105    ///    flight; its `pending_outgoing` marker is held by its guard.
14106    /// 2. A second `new_session` under the SAME pseudonym must fail with `Unacceptable` — and must not have sent
14107    ///    anything (the refusal happens before the send).
14108    /// 3. The refusal must not have consumed a challenge slot: `session_initiations.entry_count()` stays at 1, the
14109    ///    first attempt's reservation.
14110    /// 4. The first initiation still owns the marker (its `SsaRequest` dispatches as in flight), and then times out
14111    ///    cleanly, leaving no marker and no challenge reservation behind.
14112    ///
14113    /// Sequential rather than `tokio::join!`-concurrent: the property pinned is that the *second*
14114    /// call sees the first one's live claim, which is what the atomic compute serialises — running
14115    /// them concurrently would only randomise which call is "first" without strengthening the
14116    /// assertion, while the in-flight fixture (swallowed send) requires the first call to be
14117    /// parked in its await for the second to observe the claim.
14118    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14119    async fn a_second_initiation_for_a_pending_pseudonym_must_be_refused_without_consuming_a_challenge_slot()
14120    -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14121        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
14122
14123        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
14124            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(100),
14125            ..Default::default()
14126        };
14127        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(cfg);
14128
14129        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
14130        // Swallow the FIRST StartSession only: that initiation stays in flight holding its claim.
14131        // The refused attempt must never reach the transport, so `.once()` also pins that.
14132        alice_transport
14133            .expect_send_message()
14134            .once()
14135            .withf(move |peer, data| {
14136                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
14137                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
14138            })
14139            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
14140
14141        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
14142        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
14143        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14144        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
14145
14146        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
14147        let client_cfg = SessionClientConfig {
14148            capabilities: None.into(),
14149            pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
14150            surb_management: None,
14151            ..Default::default()
14152        };
14153
14154        // Park the first initiation in flight: the transport swallowed its StartSession, so it
14155        // holds both its challenge reservation and its pending-outgoing claim for the whole of
14156        // this call's initiation timeout.
14157        let in_flight = alice_mgr.new_session(
14158            bob_peer,
14159            SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14160            client_cfg.clone(),
14161        );
14162        futures::pin_mut!(in_flight);
14163
14164        // Poll the in-flight attempt exactly once, which runs it up to its first await: the claim
14165        // (and the challenge reservation) are taken before the send, so a single pending poll is
14166        // enough to make the overlap observable — no sleeps, and no runtime-dependent ordering.
14167        assert!(
14168            futures::poll!(in_flight.as_mut()).is_pending(),
14169            "fixture: the swallowed StartSession must leave the initiation pending"
14170        );
14171
14172        // The first attempt's claim is live: an SsaRequest naming the pseudonym is admitted at
14173        // dispatch as belonging to an initiation this node is still making (it goes to the handler
14174        // pool rather than being dropped as stale).
14175        let admitted = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
14176        assert!(
14177            matches!(admitted, DispatchResult::Processed),
14178            "an SsaRequest for the in-flight initiation must be admitted, got {admitted:?}"
14179        );
14180
14181        let before = {
14182            // moka defers the write op: without this the count is read before the insertion lands.
14183            alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
14184            alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count()
14185        };
14186        assert_eq!(
14187            before, 1,
14188            "fixture: the in-flight initiation must hold exactly one challenge reservation"
14189        );
14190
14191        // The overlap: the same pseudonym, still pending. Must be refused, not allowed to
14192        // overwrite the first attempt's reservation.
14193        let refused = alice_mgr
14194            .new_session(
14195                bob_peer,
14196                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14197                client_cfg,
14198            )
14199            .await;
14200        assert!(
14201            matches!(
14202                refused,
14203                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
14204            ),
14205            "a second initiation under a pending pseudonym must be refused as Unacceptable, got {refused:?}"
14206        );
14207
14208        // The refusal happened after the challenge reservation but before the send, and released
14209        // its own reservation: exactly the in-flight one remains, none consumed by the refusal.
14210        alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
14211        let after = alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count();
14212        assert_eq!(
14213            after, before,
14214            "the refused attempt must not consume a challenge slot (before: {before}, after: {after})"
14215        );
14216        assert_eq!(
14217            alice_mgr.num_active_sessions(),
14218            0,
14219            "neither attempt may have allocated a session slot"
14220        );
14221
14222        // The first initiation is unaffected by the refusal and still owns the claim.
14223        let still_admitted = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
14224        assert!(
14225            matches!(still_admitted, DispatchResult::Processed),
14226            "the refusal must not have cleared the in-flight initiation's claim, got {still_admitted:?}"
14227        );
14228
14229        // The in-flight initiation then times out cleanly: no marker, no challenge reservation.
14230        let timed_out = in_flight.await;
14231        assert!(
14232            matches!(timed_out, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)),
14233            "the first initiation must still fail on its own timeout, got {timed_out:?}"
14234        );
14235        assert_eq!(
14236            {
14237                alice_mgr.session_initiations.run_pending_tasks();
14238                alice_mgr.session_initiations.entry_count()
14239            },
14240            0,
14241            "the timed-out initiation must release its challenge reservation"
14242        );
14243        let stale = alice_mgr.dispatch_message(alice_pseudonym, ssa_request_packet(alice_pseudonym)?)?;
14244        assert!(
14245            matches!(stale, DispatchResult::Dropped(DropReason::StaleStartMessage)),
14246            "after the timeout, the pseudonym's marker must be gone, got {stale:?}"
14247        );
14248
14249        Ok(())
14250    }
14251
14252    /// The pending-initiation entries must outlive the longest wait `new_session` can make.
14253    #[test]
14254    fn initiation_cache_ttl_outlasts_the_longest_wait() {
14255        let max = RoutingOptions::MAX_INTERMEDIATE_HOPS;
14256        for base in [Duration::from_millis(100), Duration::from_secs(5)] {
14257            assert!(initiation_cache_ttl(base) > initiation_wait(base, max, max));
14258        }
14259        assert_eq!(
14260            initiation_cache_ttl(Duration::from_secs(5)),
14261            Duration::from_millis(40_200)
14262        );
14263    }

14265    /// Verifies that a session initiation returns `TransportSessionError::Timeout` when the peer
14266    /// never processes or responds to the `StartSession` message.

14271    /// 2. Alice calls `new_session`; her `StartSession` is captured by the mock and silently discarded.
14272    /// 3. The 100ms timeout expires; `new_session` returns `Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)`.
14273    /// 4. `num_active_sessions` is 0, confirming no orphaned slot was left in the cache.

14284        let bob_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
14285
14286        let mut sequence = mockall::Sequence::new();

14288        let bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();

14292            .expect_send_message()
14293            .once()
14294            .in_sequence(&mut sequence)
14295            .withf(move |peer, data| {
14296                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
14297                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
14298            })
14299            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
14300
14301        // Start Alice
14302        let (new_session_tx_alice, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
14303        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);

14307        // Start Bob

14309        let (bob_sender, _bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
14310        bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?;
14311        assert!(bob_mgr.is_started());

14313        let result = alice_mgr
14314            .new_session(
14315                bob_peer,
14316                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14317                SessionClientConfig {
14318                    capabilities: None.into(),
14319                    pseudonym: None,
14320                    surb_management: None,
14321                    ..Default::default()
14322                },
14323            )
14324            .await;

14326        assert!(matches!(result, Err(TransportSessionError::Timeout)));
14327        assert_eq!(alice_mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
14328
14329        Ok(())

14332    /// Verifies that a failed incoming session establishment does not register any telemetry.
14333    ///
14334    /// ## Steps
14335    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is started with the `telemetry` feature enabled.
14336    /// 2. The new-session notification channel's receiver is dropped immediately, so notifying about a new incoming
14337    ///    session will fail.
14338    /// 3. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with a random pseudonym. The slot is inserted first, then
14339    ///    notifying about the new session fails (receiver is gone).
14340    /// 4. `wait_for_no_active_sessions` polls until there are no active sessions, confirming the partially-inserted
14341    ///    slot was rolled back.
14342    /// 5. `num_active_sessions` is 0, proving the rollback prevented any telemetry registration for the failed session.
14343    #[cfg(feature = "telemetry")]
14344    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14345    async fn failed_incoming_session_establishment_does_not_register_telemetry() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14346        let mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
14347
14348        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
14349        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
14350        drop(new_session_rx);
14351        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
14352        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14353        assert!(mgr.is_started());
14354
14355        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
14356        let result = mgr
14357            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
14358                pseudonym,
14359                StartInitiation {
14360                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
14361                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14362                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
14363                    additional_data: 0,
14364                },
14365            )
14366            .await;
14367
14368        assert!(result.is_err());
14369
14370        // The slot inserted before the failure must be rolled back, so it neither
14371        // counts towards `maximum_sessions` nor registers any telemetry.
14372        assert!(
14373            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
14374            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
14375        );
14376        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
14377
14378        // Cleanup: close sender and await handle
14379        sender.close_channel();
14380        _handle.await??;
14381
14382        Ok(())
14383    }

14385    /// Verifies that a session slot is rolled back if session setup fails after the slot is inserted.
14386    ///
14387    /// ## Steps
14388    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is started; the new-session notification channel's receiver is dropped, so notifying about
14389    ///    a new incoming session will fail.
14390    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with a random pseudonym. The slot is inserted into the cache
14391    ///    first, then notifying about the new session fails (because the receiver is gone).
14392    /// 3. The call returns an error, and `wait_for_no_active_sessions` confirms the slot was removed.
14393    /// 4. `num_active_sessions` is 0, proving the rollback removed the slot and freed the pseudonym.
14394    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14395    async fn session_manager_should_roll_back_slot_when_incoming_session_setup_fails() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14396        let mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
14397
14398        // Drop the receiver so that notifying about the new incoming session fails
14399        // *after* the session slot has already been inserted into the cache.
14400        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
14401        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
14402        drop(new_session_rx);
14403        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
14404        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14405        assert!(mgr.is_started());
14406
14407        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
14408
14409        // The setup fails after the slot is inserted (notifying about the new
14410        // incoming session errors out because the receiver is gone), so the slot
14411        // must be rolled back instead of lingering until idle eviction.
14412        let result = mgr
14413            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
14414                pseudonym,
14415                StartInitiation {
14416                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
14417                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14418                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
14419                    additional_data: 0,
14420                },
14421            )
14422            .await;
14423        assert!(result.is_err());
14424
14425        // An empty active-session set proves the slot was removed and, since
14426        // sessions are keyed by pseudonym, that the pseudonym is free again.
14427        assert!(
14428            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
14429            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
14430        );
14431
14432        // Cleanup
14433        sender.close_channel();
14434        handle.await??;
14435
14436        Ok(())
14437    }

14439    /// Collects everything that arrives on `rx` during `window`, returning once it elapses.
14440    async fn originated_during(
14441        rx: &mut futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
14442        window: Duration,
14443    ) -> Vec<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> {
14444        let mut collected = Vec::new();
14445        let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + window;
14446        while let Ok(Some(item)) = timeout(
14447            deadline.saturating_duration_since(tokio::time::Instant::now()),
14448            rx.next(),
14449        )
14450        .await
14451        {
14452            collected.push(item);
14453        }
14454        collected
14455    }
14456
14457    /// The manager floors the keep-alive period at [`MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD`], so this
14458    /// is as fast as an Exit keep-alive can be made to run, and it sets the pace of these tests.
14459    const KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD: Duration = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
14460
14461    type RecordingManager = SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>;
14462    type Originated = futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>;
14463
14464    /// Brings up an Exit-side session and returns once its keep-alive stream is observably running.
14465    ///
14466    /// The "observably running" part is load-bearing for every caller: `nothing was originated` is
14467    /// equally true of a stream that stopped and one that never started, so a test that does not
14468    /// first establish the stream is alive proves nothing when it later sees silence.
14469    ///
14470    /// The Exit's level report goes only to an Entry that has shown it refills, and only while the
14471    /// Exit holds a SURB to send it on (see [`PixFillControl::admit`]). Nothing here runs an Entry, so
14472    /// the fixture stands in for both: the Session is marked as refilled and given a stock of SURBs
14473    /// to report from, which is what an Entry's first keep-alive would have done.
14474    async fn exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
14475        cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
14476        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
14477    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
14478        RecordingManager,
14479        Originated,
14480        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
14481        HoprPseudonym,
14482    )> {
14483        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
14484            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
14485            ..cfg
14486        });
14487
14488        if let Some(admission) = admission {
14489            assert!(
14490                mgr.set_surb_admission(admission),
14491                "a freshly constructed fixture manager must accept the SURB admission seam"
14492            );
14493        }
14494
14495        let (msg_tx, mut msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
14496        // Returned rather than dropped: a second establishment on the same manager — the
14497        // pseudonym-reuse test — would otherwise fail its notification and roll back.
14498        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
14499        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14500
14501        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
14502        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
14503            pseudonym,
14504            StartInitiation {
14505                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
14506                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14507                // Empty capabilities keep rate control on, which is what spawns the balancer and
14508                // the keep-alive stream. `NoRateControl` would skip both and make this vacuous.
14509                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
14510                additional_data: 0,
14511            },
14512        )
14513        .await?;
14514
14515        // The reports are one SURB each; this outlasts every test that uses the fixture many times over.
14516        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
14517        slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
14518        slot.surb_estimator
14519            .produced
14520            .fetch_add(1_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
14521        drop(slot);
14522
14523        let observed = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 2 + Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
14524        let keep_alives = observed
14525            .iter()
14526            .filter(|(routing, data)| {
14527                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
14528                    && matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if p == &pseudonym)
14529            })
14530            .count();
14531        anyhow::ensure!(
14532            keep_alives > 0,
14533            "no return-routed keep-alive was originated, so this test cannot tell a stopped stream from one that \
14534             never ran; {} message(s) were observed in total",
14535            observed.len()
14536        );
14537
14538        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, new_session_rx, pseudonym))
14539    }
14540
14541    /// How long the level reports of an Exit Session are watched: three notification periods, and half a
14542    /// second over so that the third report is not decided by a scheduling tick.
14543    const REPORT_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_millis(3_500);
14544
14545    /// SURBs the simulated Entry delivers. A keep-alive only carries as many as fit beside it, so the
14546    /// number the Exit ends up counting is read back from its estimate rather than assumed.
14547    const ENTRY_SURBS: usize = 3;
14548
14549    /// An Entry as the Exit has come to know it by the time its level reports are watched.
14550    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
14551    enum SimulatedEntry {
14552        /// An Entry whose SURB balancer is running: its keep-alives refill the Exit and carry `surbs`
14553        /// SURBs. `target_notify` says whether they announce its target (`BalancerTarget`) or not.
14554        Balancing { target_notify: bool, surbs: usize },
14555        /// An Entry with no SURB balancer: it sends no keep-alive, and its `surbs` SURBs arrived with
14556        /// data.
14557        WithoutBalancer { surbs: usize },
14558        /// An Entry with no SURB balancer that pings by hand (`ping_session`): its only keep-alives are
14559        /// marked as manual pings, and each carries `surbs` SURBs, as a real one does.
14560        PingingByHand { surbs: usize },
14561    }
14562
14563    /// What the Exit's level reports are expected to do.
14564    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
14565    enum Expect {
14566        /// They flow.
14567        Reports,
14568        /// They do not, until the Entry turns into a reader (a keep-alive carrying SURBs arrives).
14569        /// Silence alone proves nothing: a stream that never ran is as quiet, so the case then shows
14570        /// the reports start.
14571        SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
14572    }
14573
14574    /// A non-PIX Exit Session on a manager with the level reports on, with the Entry's announcement
14575    /// under the caller's control.
14576    ///
14577    /// `announced_target` is what the Entry puts in `StartInitiation::additional_data`.
14578    async fn exit_session_reporting_levels(
14579        capabilities: Capabilities,
14580        announced_target: u64,
14581    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
14582        RecordingManager,
14583        Originated,
14584        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
14585        HoprPseudonym,
14586    )> {
14587        exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
14588            capabilities,
14589            announced_target,
14590            SessionManagerConfig {
14591                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
14592                ..Default::default()
14593            },
14594        )
14595        .await
14596    }
14597
14598    /// [`exit_session_reporting_levels`] over a manager configuration the caller supplies.
14599    ///
14600    /// The degraded notification period is what the caller changes here: with the notification at
14601    /// [`KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD`] a degraded period can only be *at* it, which is the disabled case, so the
14602    /// degraded tests use a slower normal period and a faster degraded one.
14603    async fn exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
14604        capabilities: Capabilities,
14605        announced_target: u64,
14606        cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
14607    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
14608        RecordingManager,
14609        Originated,
14610        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
14611        HoprPseudonym,
14612    )> {
14613        exit_session_reporting_levels_for_entry(capabilities, announced_target, Duration::ZERO, cfg).await
14614    }

14616    /// [`exit_session_reporting_levels_with`] for an Entry that announces `entry_idle_timeout`
14617    /// (zero: it announces none).
14618    async fn exit_session_reporting_levels_for_entry(
14619        capabilities: Capabilities,
14620        announced_target: u64,
14621        entry_idle_timeout: Duration,
14622        cfg: SessionManagerConfig,
14623    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
14624        RecordingManager,
14625        Originated,
14626        futures::channel::mpsc::Receiver<IncomingSession>,
14627        HoprPseudonym,
14628    )> {
14629        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(cfg);
14630        let (msg_tx, msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
14631        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
14632        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
14633
14634        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
14635        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
14636            pseudonym,
14637            StartInitiation {
14638                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
14639                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
14640                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
14641                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced_target, entry_idle_timeout),
14642            },
14643        )
14644        .await?;
14645
14646        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, new_session_rx, pseudonym))
14647    }

14649    /// Waits (bounded) until the Exit has handled a keep-alive from the Entry. The manager's Start
14650    /// protocol task does that after `dispatch_message` returns.
14651    async fn wait_for_counterparty_refills(mgr: &RecordingManager, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14652        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
14653            loop {
14654                if mgr
14655                    .sessions
14656                    .get(pseudonym)
14657                    .is_some_and(|slot| slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills())
14658                {
14659                    break;
14660                }
14661                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
14662            }
14663        })
14664        .await
14665        .context("the Exit never handled the Entry's keep-alive")
14666    }
14667
14668    /// The levels carried by the Exit's return-routed keep-alives for `pseudonym` over `window`, in the
14669    /// order they were sent.
14670    async fn level_reports_during(rx: &mut Originated, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, window: Duration) -> Vec<u64> {
14671        originated_during(rx, window)
14672            .await
14673            .iter()
14674            .filter(|(routing, _)| matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == pseudonym))
14675            .filter_map(|(_, data)| {
14676                match HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text).ok()? {
14677                    StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) if ka.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) => {
14678                        Some(ka.additional_data)
14679                    }
14680                    _ => None,
14681                }
14682            })
14683            .collect()
14684    }
14685
14686    /// Makes `entry` known to the Exit Session of `pseudonym`, and returns the SURBs the Exit counts.
14687    async fn show_exit_its_entry(
14688        mgr: &RecordingManager,
14689        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
14690        entry: SimulatedEntry,
14691    ) -> anyhow::Result<u64> {
14692        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
14693        match entry {
14694            SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify, surbs } => {
14695                let flags: KeepAliveFlags = if target_notify {
14696                    KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into()
14697                } else {
14698                    None.into()
14699                };
14700                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(mgr, pseudonym, flags, surbs, 0)?;
14701                wait_for_counterparty_refills(mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
14702            }
14703            SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs } => {
14704                // Its SURBs arrive with data, which books them like this and tells the Exit nothing
14705                // about a balancer.
14706                slot.surb_estimator
14707                    .produced
14708                    .fetch_add(surbs as u64, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
14709                assert!(
14710                    !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
14711                    "fixture: an Entry without a balancer has sent no keep-alive"
14712                );
14713            }
14714            SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs } => {
14715                // The Exit books the SURBs the ping carried, as with every Start message, but is told
14716                // nothing about a balancer.
14717                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(), surbs, 0)?;
14718            }
14719        }
14720        Ok(slot.surb_estimator.saturating_diff())
14721    }
14722
14723    /// A Session that loses frames reports at the degraded period, and returns to the normal one when
14724    /// the loss stops.
14725    ///
14726    /// The loss is injected into the Session's own signal — the same handle the socket records into —
14727    /// rather than produced by a real faulty socket: what is under test here is the driver's decision
14728    /// and its effect on the stream (the socket end is covered in `hopr-protocol-session`). The normal
14729    /// period is deliberately much longer than the degraded one, so the two cadences cannot be
14730    /// confused within a test-length window.
14731    ///
14732    /// The stock is above the keep-alive reserve throughout: a report that could not be sent would
14733    /// make the comparison about SURB scarcity rather than about cadence.
14734    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14735    async fn a_losing_exit_session_reports_faster_until_the_loss_stops() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14736        // A normal period long enough that the normal cadence cannot fit twice in the windows below,
14737        // and a degraded period fast enough to fit several times.
14738        let normal = Duration::from_secs(4);
14739        let degraded = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
14740        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
14741            Capability::Segmentation.into(),
14742            64,
14743            SessionManagerConfig {
14744                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(normal),
14745                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(degraded),
14746                ..Default::default()
14747            },
14748        )
14749        .await?;
14750
14751        let (signal, control) = {
14752            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
14753            (
14754                slot.exit_loss_signal
14755                    .get()
14756                    .cloned()
14757                    .context("an Exit Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
14758                slot.pix_fill
14759                    .get()
14760                    .cloned()
14761                    .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?,
14762            )
14763        };
14764
14765        // A balancing Entry, and SURBs far above the keep-alive reserve so the report is never withheld.
14766        show_exit_its_entry(
14767            &mgr,
14768            pseudonym,
14769            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
14770                target_notify: true,
14771                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
14772            },
14773        )
14774        .await?;
14775        {
14776            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
14777            slot.surb_estimator
14778                .produced
14779                .fetch_add(10_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
14780        }
14781
14782        // The stream is alive before anything is measured: the first report waits one normal period,
14783        // so without this the degraded case could be read out of a stream that never started.
14784        let window = Duration::from_millis(1_500);
14785        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
14786            while !control.notify_started() {
14787                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
14788            }
14789        })
14790        .await
14791        .context("the notification never started, so no cadence could be observed")?;
14792        let _first = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
14793        assert!(
14794            !control.is_degraded(),
14795            "a whole forward path reports at the normal period"
14796        );
14797
14798        // Loss now, kept alive for the whole window as a continuously faulty path would. The window is
14799        // four degraded periods, so the degraded cadence has room for several reports where the normal
14800        // period (four times the degraded one) cannot fit even two. The margin is deliberate: entering
14801        // degraded mode can lag by one poll and the rate limiter releases a packet up to one chunk
14802        // late, so a two-and-a-half-period window left the second report on the edge of it.
14803        let loss_window = degraded * 4;
14804        let lossy = async {
14805            let deadline = tokio::time::Instant::now() + loss_window;
14806            while tokio::time::Instant::now() < deadline {
14807                signal.record();
14808                tokio::time::sleep(degraded / 4).await;
14809            }
14810        };
14811        let (reports, ()) = futures::join!(level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, loss_window), lossy);
14812        // The report count and the control's own state are two independent statements of the same
14813        // thing: the stream says it is degraded, and it says it in reports.
14814        assert!(
14815            control.is_degraded(),
14816            "a Session that lost a frame within the hold must be degraded"
14817        );
14818        assert!(
14819            reports.len() >= 2,
14820            "a losing Session must report at the degraded period ({degraded:?}) rather than the normal one \
14821             ({normal:?}), but {} report(s) arrived over {loss_window:?}: {reports:?}",
14822            reports.len()
14823        );
14824
14825        // The loss stops; once the hold has passed, the normal period is back.
14826        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
14827            loop {
14828                if !control.is_degraded() {
14829                    break;
14830                }
14831                tokio::time::sleep(SURB_DEGRADED_POLL).await;
14832            }
14833        })
14834        .await
14835        .context("the Session never left degraded mode after its loss stopped")?;
14836        assert!(
14837            !exit_forward_path_is_degraded(
14838                &signal,
14839                &mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).unwrap().surb_estimator,
14840                &mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).unwrap().surb_mgmt,
14841                false
14842            ),
14843            "the rule and the control must agree on the recovery"
14844        );
14845
14846        // And the cadence is the normal one again: over a window shorter than the normal period, at
14847        // most one report can be due — where the degraded period would have produced several.
14848        let _in_flight = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
14849        let after = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
14850        assert!(
14851            after.len() <= 1,
14852            "back at the normal period ({normal:?}), {window:?} holds at most one report, but {} arrived: {after:?}",
14853            after.len()
14854        );
14855
14856        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
14857        Ok(())
14858    }
14859
14860    /// The manager floors the degraded period at `MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD`, like the
14861    /// normal one, and keeps "not faster" as the disabled case rather than rewriting the value.
14862    #[test]
14863    fn the_degraded_period_is_floored_and_kept_above_the_normal_one() {
14864        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
14865            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(15)),
14866            surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_millis(50)),
14867            ..Default::default()
14868        });
14869        assert_eq!(
14870            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
14871            mgr.cfg.surb_degraded_notify_period,
14872            "a sub-second degraded period must be raised to the floor the normal one has"
14873        );
14874
14875        // A degraded period no faster than the normal one is left as configured: the switch that
14876        // consumes it treats it as off, so both a value above and one equal to the normal period are
14877        // the same disabled case and neither has to be rewritten.
14878        for (normal, degraded) in [
14879            (Duration::from_secs(1), Duration::from_secs(1)),
14880            (Duration::from_secs(15), Duration::from_secs(15)),
14881            (Duration::from_secs(15), Duration::from_secs(20)),
14882        ] {
14883            let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
14884                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(normal),
14885                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(degraded),
14886                ..Default::default()
14887            });
14888            assert_eq!(
14889                Some(degraded),
14890                mgr.cfg.surb_degraded_notify_period,
14891                "a degraded period no faster than the normal one ({normal:?}) is not rewritten"
14892            );
14893            assert_eq!(Some(normal), mgr.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period);
14894        }
14895
14896        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
14897            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(15)),
14898            surb_degraded_notify_period: None,
14899            ..Default::default()
14900        });
14901        assert_eq!(
14902            None, mgr.cfg.surb_degraded_notify_period,
14903            "`None` stays `None`: the operator switched the fast cadence off"
14904        );
14905    }
14906
14907    /// A degraded period is normalized away when there is no normal period to speed up.
14908    ///
14909    /// The pair is only meaningful together: without a normal period the notification would otherwise
14910    /// run at the degraded cadence for the Session's whole life, which is a different feature.
14911    #[test]
14912    fn a_degraded_period_without_a_normal_one_is_normalized_away() {
14913        let control = fill_control_degraded(None, Some(Duration::from_secs(1)), 1, 10);
14914        control.start_notify();
14915        control.set_degraded(true);
14916        assert_eq!(
14917            None,
14918            control.period(&control.state.lock()),
14919            "there is no normal period for the degraded one to shorten"
14920        );
14921        assert_eq!(
14922            FillRate::ZERO,
14923            control.effective_rate(),
14924            "and so nothing to report: the degraded period must not conjure a notification"
14925        );
14926    }

14929    ///
14930    /// The Session publishes no loss signal, so the socket never stamps one and the driver is never
14931    /// spawned: "no faster" must cost nothing at all rather than run a switch between two equal
14932    /// cadences. The operator is warned once at construction (`SessionManager::new`).
14933    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14934    async fn a_degraded_period_no_faster_than_the_normal_one_disables_the_feature() -> anyhow::Result<()> {

14936            let (mgr, _msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
14937                Capability::Segmentation.into(),

14948            assert!(
14949                slot.exit_loss_signal.get().is_none(),

14951            );
14952            drop(slot);
14953
14954            assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
14955        }
14956        Ok(())

14959    /// Only a Session with frames to lose gets a loss signal and a driver.
14960    ///
14961    /// A raw Session (no `Capability::Segmentation`) has no frames, and its socket never takes a signal, so
14962    /// one would be recorded into by nothing and read by a driver with nothing to see.
14963    #[rstest]
14964    #[case::raw(Capabilities::empty(), false)]
14965    #[case::raw_without_rate_control(Capability::NoRateControl.into(), false)]
14966    #[case::segmented(Capability::Segmentation.into(), true)]
14967    #[case::segmented_without_rate_control(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, true)]
14968    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
14969    async fn only_a_segmented_exit_session_gets_a_loss_signal_and_driver(
14970        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
14971        #[case] expect_signal: bool,
14972    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
14973        let (mgr, _msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
14974            capabilities,
14975            64,
14976            SessionManagerConfig {
14977                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(15)),
14978                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
14979                ..Default::default()
14980            },
14981        )
14982        .await?;
14983
14984        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
14985        assert_eq!(expect_signal, slot.exit_loss_signal.get().is_some());
14986        assert_eq!(
14987            expect_signal,
14988            slot.abort_handles.lock().contains(&SessionHandles::SurbNotifyDegraded),
14989            "the driver runs exactly when there is a signal for it to read"
14990        );
14991        drop(slot);
14992
14993        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
14994        Ok(())
