14997    /// Keeps a Session's SURB estimate at `level` while it runs, so that the reports it sends do not walk the
14998    /// stock off the point a test is about. Dropping the guard stops it.
14999    fn hold_stock_at(estimator: &AtomicSurbFlowEstimator, level: u64) -> AbortOnDrop {
15000        let estimator = estimator.clone();
15001        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
15002            loop {
15003                let held = estimator.saturating_diff();
15004                if held < level {
15005                    estimator
15006                        .produced
15007                        .fetch_add(level - held, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15008                } else if held > level {
15009                    estimator
15010                        .consumed
15011                        .fetch_add(held - level, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15012                }
15013                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
15014            }
15015        });
15016        AbortOnDrop::from(task)
15017    }
15018
15019    /// Records a loss into `signal` every `every` until the guard is dropped, as a continuously faulty path does.
15020    fn lose_frames_continuously(signal: Arc<FrameLossSignal>, every: Duration) -> AbortOnDrop {
15021        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
15022            loop {
15023                signal.record();
15024                tokio::time::sleep(every).await;
15025            }
15026        });
15027        AbortOnDrop::from(task)
15028    }
15029
15030    /// The Session stops reporting at the degraded period exactly at the keep-alive reserve, and not one SURB
15031    /// above it.
15032    ///
15033    /// The reserve is the real one: `keep_alive_surb_reserve` of the target the Exit holds for the Session
15034    /// (400 here, so 32; a hundredth of it would be 4). The stock is held at it, or one SURB above it, while the
15035    /// path keeps losing frames, so the two cases differ in nothing but that SURB. The normal period is four
15036    /// times the degraded one, which makes the cadences tell apart in a short window: at most one report fits
15037    /// the window at the normal period, and the degraded one fits several. The reserve is what the fast reports
15038    /// are paid for out of, so at it the Session is back to the normal period; the companion above it shows the
15039    /// stream was alive and would have reported faster.
15040    #[rstest]
15041    #[case::at_the_reserve(0, false)]
15042    #[case::one_surb_above_it(1, true)]
15043    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15044    async fn a_session_reports_at_the_degraded_period_only_above_its_reserve(
15045        #[case] above_reserve: u64,
15046        #[case] degraded: bool,
15047    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15048        let normal = Duration::from_secs(4);
15049        let period = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
15050        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
15051            Capability::Segmentation.into(),
15052            400,
15053            SessionManagerConfig {
15054                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(normal),
15055                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(period),
15056                ..Default::default()
15057            },
15058        )
15059        .await?;
15060
15061        let (signal, control, estimator, reserve) = {
15062            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15063            let target = slot
15064                .surb_mgmt
15065                .target_surb_buffer_size
15066                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15067            (
15068                slot.exit_loss_signal
15069                    .get()
15070                    .cloned()
15071                    .context("an Exit Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
15072                slot.pix_fill
15073                    .get()
15074                    .cloned()
15075                    .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?,
15076                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
15077                keep_alive_surb_reserve(target),
15078            )
15079        };
15080        anyhow::ensure!(
15081            reserve == 32,
15082            "fixture: the reserve of a 400-SURB target is 32, and it is {reserve}"
15083        );
15084
15085        // The stream is running before anything is measured, so that silence afterwards means the reserve
15086        // and not a stream that had yet to start. The reader comes last: nothing is sent to an Entry that
15087        // has not been heard.
15088        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
15089            while !control.notify_started() {
15090                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
15091            }
15092        })
15093        .await
15094        .context("the notification never started")?;
15095        show_exit_its_entry(
15096            &mgr,
15097            pseudonym,
15098            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
15099                target_notify: false,
15100                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
15101            },
15102        )
15103        .await?;
15104        let _stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, reserve + above_reserve);
15105        let _loss = lose_frames_continuously(signal, period / 4);
15106
15107        // The first report is due the moment there is a reader, and is not a cadence.
15108        let _first = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1_500)).await;
15109
15110        let window = Duration::from_millis(2_500);
15111        // Sampled across the window rather than read once at its end: every degraded report spends a SURB and
15112        // the stock holder refills on a 5 ms sleep, so under load the stock can sit at the reserve for a poll and
15113        // switch degraded mode off for a moment. One SURB above the reserve, "was degraded at some point" is what
15114        // holds; at the reserve, never.
15115        let ever_degraded = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
15116        let sampler = {
15117            let (control, ever_degraded) = (control.clone(), ever_degraded.clone());
15118            AbortOnDrop::from(tokio::spawn(async move {
15119                loop {
15120                    if control.is_degraded() {
15121                        ever_degraded.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15122                    }
15123                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15124                }
15125            }))
15126        };
15127        let reports = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
15128        drop(sampler);
15129        let ever_degraded = ever_degraded.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15130        if degraded {
15131            assert!(
15132                ever_degraded,
15133                "with the stock {above_reserve} SURB(s) above the reserve of {reserve} the Session must have been \
15134                 degraded at some point in {window:?}"
15135            );
15136        } else {
15137            assert!(
15138                !ever_degraded && !control.is_degraded(),
15139                "with the stock at the reserve of {reserve} the Session must never be degraded"
15140            );
15141        }
15142        if degraded {
15143            assert!(
15144                reports.len() >= 2,
15145                "one SURB above the reserve the Session reports at the degraded period ({period:?}), which fits \
15146                 several times in {window:?}: {reports:?}"
15147            );
15148        } else {
15149            assert!(
15150                reports.len() <= 1,
15151                "at the reserve the Session reports at the normal period ({normal:?}), so a {window:?} window holds \
15152                 at most one report where the degraded period would produce several: {reports:?}"
15153            );
15154        }
15155
15156        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
15157        Ok(())
15158    }
15159
15160    /// A Session whose frames stall reports at the dark cadence, and once frames complete again, while it still
15161    /// loses some, at the degraded period.
15162    ///
15163    /// Two frames are under way and neither completes: the forward path delivers segments but no frames, the
15164    /// Session is dark from the moment the stall has lasted [`SURB_DEGRADED_STALL`], and it reports every
15165    /// [`SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD`]. A frame completing ends the stall; the loss that goes on keeps the Session
15166    /// degraded, and once the stall's hold has passed, at the degraded period only.
15167    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15168    async fn a_session_whose_frames_stall_reports_at_the_dark_cadence() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15169        let normal = Duration::from_secs(4);
15170        let degraded = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
15171        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
15172            Capability::Segmentation.into(),
15173            400,
15174            SessionManagerConfig {
15175                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(normal),
15176                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(degraded),
15177                ..Default::default()
15178            },
15179        )
15180        .await?;
15181        let (signal, control, estimator) = {
15182            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15183            (
15184                slot.exit_loss_signal
15185                    .get()
15186                    .cloned()
15187                    .context("an Exit Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
15188                slot.pix_fill
15189                    .get()
15190                    .cloned()
15191                    .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?,
15192                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
15193            )
15194        };
15195        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
15196            while !control.notify_started() {
15197                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
15198            }
15199        })
15200        .await
15201        .context("the notification never started")?;
15202        show_exit_its_entry(
15203            &mgr,
15204            pseudonym,
15205            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
15206                target_notify: false,
15207                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
15208            },
15209        )
15210        .await?;
15211        // Far above the reserve of 32, so the stock never ends the fast cadence here.
15212        let _stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, 10_000);
15213
15214        signal.segment_received(1);
15215        signal.segment_received(2);
15216        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
15217            while !control.is_dark() {
15218                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
15219            }
15220        })
15221        .await
15222        .context("stalled frames never made the Session dark")?;
15223        assert!(control.is_degraded(), "dark is a degraded forward path");
15224        assert_eq!(0, signal.lost_total(), "and it went dark before any frame was lost");
15225
15226        let window = Duration::from_millis(1_500);
15227        let _settle = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
15228        let dark_reports = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
15229        assert!(
15230            dark_reports.len() >= 8,
15231            "dark, the Session reports every {SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD:?}, about 15 times in {window:?}: \
15232             {dark_reports:?}"
15233        );
15234
15235        // A frame completes, and loss goes on: the Session stays degraded, and once the stall's hold has
15236        // passed it is no longer dark.
15237        signal.frame_completed();
15238        let _loss = lose_frames_continuously(signal.clone(), degraded / 4);
15239        timeout(SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD + Duration::from_secs(3), async {
15240            while control.is_dark() {
15241                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
15242            }
15243        })
15244        .await
15245        .context("the Session stayed dark after its frames completed again")?;
15246        assert!(control.is_degraded(), "the loss that goes on keeps it degraded");
15247        let _settle = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
15248        let degraded_reports = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(2_500)).await;
15249        assert!(
15250            (1..=4).contains(&degraded_reports.len()),
15251            "degraded by loss alone, the Session reports at the degraded period ({degraded:?}), two or three times in \
15252             2.5 s: {degraded_reports:?}"
15253        );
15254
15255        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
15256        Ok(())
15257    }

15259    /// A Session for which the Exit holds no announced SURB target never goes degraded, however lossy its path,
15260    /// however many SURBs it holds and however well its Entry reads: its keep-alive reserve is 0, so a degraded
15261    /// report would have nothing to stop it short of the last SURB.
15262    ///
15263    /// A `NoRateControl` Session runs no balancer on the Exit, so none stores a target. (A rate-controlled Session
15264    /// whose Entry announces none is given the balancer-rate fallback target, which the Exit cannot tell from a
15265    /// real one, so it is not a no-target case.) The stock is far above any reserve a target would give.
15266    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15267    async fn a_session_without_a_target_never_goes_degraded() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15268        let capabilities = Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl;
15269        let normal = Duration::from_secs(4);
15270        let period = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
15271        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
15272            capabilities,
15273            0,
15274            SessionManagerConfig {
15275                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(normal),
15276                surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(period),
15277                ..Default::default()
15278            },
15279        )
15280        .await?;
15281
15282        let (signal, control, estimator) = {
15283            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15284            anyhow::ensure!(
15285                !has_announced_surb_target(&slot.surb_mgmt),
15286                "fixture: the Exit must hold no target for this Session"
15287            );
15288            (
15289                slot.exit_loss_signal
15290                    .get()
15291                    .cloned()
15292                    .context("an Exit Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
15293                slot.pix_fill
15294                    .get()
15295                    .cloned()
15296                    .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?,
15297                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
15298            )
15299        };
15300
15301        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
15302            while !control.notify_started() {
15303                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
15304            }
15305        })
15306        .await
15307        .context("the notification never started")?;
15308        show_exit_its_entry(
15309            &mgr,
15310            pseudonym,
15311            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
15312                target_notify: false,
15313                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
15314            },
15315        )
15316        .await?;
15317        let _stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, 1_000);
15318        let _loss = lose_frames_continuously(signal, period / 4);
15319
15320        let ever_degraded = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
15321        let _sampler = {
15322            let (control, ever_degraded) = (control.clone(), ever_degraded.clone());
15323            AbortOnDrop::from(tokio::spawn(async move {
15324                loop {
15325                    if control.is_degraded() {
15326                        ever_degraded.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15327                    }
15328                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
15329                }
15330            }))
15331        };
15332
15333        // Past the 500 ms the driver takes to act on what it sees, over several degraded periods.
15334        let window = Duration::from_millis(2_500);
15335        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1_000)).await;
15336        let reports = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
15337        assert!(
15338            !ever_degraded.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
15339            "a Session with no announced target must never be degraded"
15340        );
15341        assert!(
15342            reports.len() <= 1,
15343            "with no target the Session reports at the normal period ({normal:?}), at most once in {window:?}: \
15344             {reports:?}"
15345        );
15346
15347        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
15348        Ok(())
15349    }

15351    /// The Exit's SURB-level reports follow what the Exit has seen of its Entry, for every kind of
15352    /// Session and every kind of Entry.
15353    ///
15354    /// A report spends one of the Session's SURBs, so it is sent only to an Entry that has shown it
15355    /// refills (any keep-alive from its balancer, whether or not it announces its target, but not a manual ping) and
15356    /// only while the Exit holds a SURB to send it on. What it says depends on whether the Exit runs a balancer:
15357    /// the balancer's level on a rate-controlled Session, the Exit's own count of its SURBs on a
15358    /// `NoRateControl` one, which has none.
15359    ///
15360    /// What the Entry announced when the Session was established decides nothing: the target is a
15361    /// figure the peer picks, and an Entry that announces one can still run no balancer
15362    /// (`d_entry_announcing_without_balancer`), or announce none and run one
15363    /// (`c_balancing_entry`, `c_balancing_entry_without_target_notify`).
15364    ///
15365    /// The cases that expect silence then let the Entry read, and want the reports to start: a stream
15366    /// that never ran would be as quiet.
15367    ///
15368    /// An Entry that only pings by hand (`a_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand`, `d_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand`)
15369    /// runs no balancer, though it sends keep-alives, and each of them brings SURBs. The mark on its pings
15370    /// is all that tells it from a balancing one, and the Exit stays quiet for it.
15371    #[rstest]
15372    #[case::a_balancing_entry(
15373        Capabilities::empty(),
15374        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15375        64,
15376        Expect::Reports,
15377        false
15378    )]
15379    #[case::a_balancing_entry_without_target_notify(
15380        Capabilities::empty(),
15381        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15382        64,
15383        Expect::Reports,
15384        false
15385    )]
15386    #[case::b_entry_without_balancer(
15387        Capabilities::empty(),
15388        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15389        64,
15390        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15391        false
15392    )]
15393    #[case::c_balancing_entry(
15394        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15395        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15396        0,
15397        Expect::Reports,
15398        false
15399    )]
15400    #[case::c_balancing_entry_without_target_notify(
15401        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15402        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15403        0,
15404        Expect::Reports,
15405        false
15406    )]
15407    #[case::c_balancing_entry_announcing(
15408        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15409        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15410        64,
15411        Expect::Reports,
15412        false
15413    )]
15414    #[case::d_entry_without_balancer(
15415        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15416        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15417        0,
15418        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15419        false
15420    )]
15421    #[case::d_entry_announcing_without_balancer(
15422        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15423        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15424        64,
15425        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15426        false
15427    )]
15428    #[case::a_balancing_entry_empty_store(
15429        Capabilities::empty(),
15430        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: 0 },
15431        64,
15432        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15433        false
15434    )]
15435    #[case::c_balancing_entry_empty_store(
15436        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15437        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: true, surbs: 0 },
15438        0,
15439        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15440        false
15441    )]
15442    #[case::a_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand(
15443        Capabilities::empty(),
15444        SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15445        64,
15446        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15447        false
15448    )]
15449    #[case::d_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand(
15450        Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
15451        SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15452        0,
15453        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15454        false
15455    )]
15456    #[case::degraded_c_balancing_entry(
15457        Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl,
15458        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15459        0,
15460        Expect::Reports,
15461        true
15462    )]
15463    #[case::degraded_d_entry_without_balancer(
15464        Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl,
15465        SimulatedEntry::WithoutBalancer { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15466        0,
15467        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15468        true
15469    )]
15470    #[case::degraded_c_balancing_entry_empty_store(
15471        Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl,
15472        SimulatedEntry::Balancing { target_notify: false, surbs: 0 },
15473        0,
15474        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15475        true
15476    )]
15477    #[case::degraded_d_entry_that_only_pings_by_hand(
15478        Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl,
15479        SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { surbs: ENTRY_SURBS },
15480        0,
15481        Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads,
15482        true
15483    )]
15484    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15485    async fn exit_level_reports_follow_the_entry(
15486        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
15487        #[case] entry: SimulatedEntry,
15488        #[case] announced: u64,
15489        #[case] expect: Expect,
15490        #[case] degraded: bool,
15491    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15492        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
15493        // A degraded case runs the same Entry on a path that keeps losing frames, with a normal period of
15494        // four seconds against a degraded one of one. What an Entry does or does not read must decide the
15495        // reports there as well, and the cadence is only the faster one once the path is lossy.
15496        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = if degraded {
15497            exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
15498                capabilities,
15499                announced,
15500                SessionManagerConfig {
15501                    surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(4)),
15502                    surb_degraded_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
15503                    ..Default::default()
15504                },
15505            )
15506            .await?
15507        } else {
15508            exit_session_reporting_levels(capabilities, announced).await?
15509        };
15510        let _loss = if degraded {
15511            let (signal, control) = {
15512                let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
15513                (
15514                    slot.exit_loss_signal
15515                        .get()
15516                        .cloned()
15517                        .context("an Exit Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
15518                    slot.pix_fill
15519                        .get()
15520                        .cloned()
15521                        .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?,
15522                )
15523            };
15524            // The first notification waits one normal period, and reports before that say nothing about a
15525            // cadence: start measuring once the stream is on, with the reader still to come.
15526            timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
15527                while !control.notify_started() {
15528                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
15529                }
15530            })
15531            .await
15532            .context("the notification never started")?;
15533            Some(lose_frames_continuously(signal, KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD / 4))
15534        } else {
15535            None
15536        };
15537        let held = show_exit_its_entry(&mgr, pseudonym, entry).await?;
15538
15539        let levels = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, REPORT_WINDOW).await;
15540        match expect {
15541            Expect::Reports => {
15542                anyhow::ensure!(
15543                    held > 0,
15544                    "fixture: the Entry must have delivered SURBs for a report to be sent on"
15545                );
15546                // A degraded case holds no announced target, so it keeps the normal period (four seconds), whose
15547                // first report may fall past the window: only the cadence is asserted for it, below.
15548                anyhow::ensure!(
15549                    degraded || !levels.is_empty(),
15550                    "{entry:?} holds {held} SURB(s) of the Exit and refills it, yet no level report arrived over \
15551                     {REPORT_WINDOW:?}"
15552                );
15553                if rate_controlled {
15554                    // The Exit's balancer is running and the report is its level.
15555                    assert!(
15556                        levels.iter().all(|level| (1..=held).contains(level)),
15557                        "a rate-controlled Session reports its balancer's level, which is within 1..={held}: \
15558                         {levels:?}"
15559                    );
15560                } else {
15561                    // No balancer: the report is the Exit's own count, and every report spent one.
15562                    assert_eq!(
15563                        (!levels.is_empty()).then_some(held),
15564                        levels.first().copied(),
15565                        "a NoRateControl Session reports the SURBs it holds, not its balancer's unwritten zero: \
15566                         {levels:?}"
15567                    );
15568                    assert!(
15569                        levels.windows(2).all(|pair| pair[1] <= pair[0]),
15570                        "each report spent a SURB, so the count it carries cannot rise: {levels:?}"
15571                    );
15572                }
15573                if degraded {
15574                    // Every degraded case here has no announced target on the Exit (`announced` is 0 and the
15575                    // Session is `NoRateControl`), so it never degrades: at the normal period (four seconds)
15576                    // the window holds one report at most, however lossy the path.
15577                    assert_eq!(0, announced, "fixture: a degraded case holds no announced target");
15578                    assert!(
15579                        levels.len() <= 1,
15580                        "a Session without an announced target keeps the normal period while losing frames, which \
15581                         fits once in {REPORT_WINDOW:?}: {levels:?}"
15582                    );
15583                }
15584            }
15585            Expect::SilenceUntilTheEntryReads => {
15586                assert!(
15587                    levels.is_empty(),
15588                    "{entry:?} gives the Exit no reason to report, yet it sent {} report(s) {levels:?}",
15589                    levels.len()
15590                );
15591
15592                if matches!(entry, SimulatedEntry::PingingByHand { .. }) {
15593                    // Handled by now, over a window of several periods, so this is not just a ping
15594                    // that has yet to be looked at.
15595                    assert!(
15596                        !mgr.sessions
15597                            .get(&pseudonym)
15598                            .context("the session slot must exist")?
15599                            .surb_mgmt
15600                            .counterparty_refills(),
15601                        "a manual ping must not be taken for a sign that the Entry runs a balancer"
15602                    );
15603                }
15604
15605                // The Entry becomes a reader: a balancing one's keep-alive, carrying SURBs.
15606                dispatch_entry_keep_alive(&mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), ENTRY_SURBS, 0)?;
15607                wait_for_counterparty_refills(&mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
15608
15609                let levels = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, REPORT_WINDOW).await;
15610                assert!(
15611                    !levels.is_empty(),
15612                    "the silence was the gate and not a dead stream: once the Entry refills the Exit and delivers \
15613                     SURBs, the reports must start, and none arrived over {REPORT_WINDOW:?}"
15614                );
15615            }
15616        }
15617
15618        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
15619        Ok(())
15620    }
15621
15622    /// Asserts `mgr` originates nothing further for `pseudonym`.
15623    ///
15624    /// Packets already handed to the sender before the closure are in flight rather than newly
15625    /// originated, so they are drained first and only what appears afterwards counts.
15626    async fn assert_no_further_origination(rx: &mut Originated, closure: &str) {
15627        let _in_flight = originated_during(rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
15628
15629        let window = KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 3;
15630        let after = originated_during(rx, window).await;
15631        assert!(
15632            after.is_empty(),
15633            "an Exit session closed by {closure} originated {} further packet(s) over {window:?} — each one is \
15634             return-routed to a pseudonym whose SURBs are gone, and one such packet is enough to stall all \
15635             origination on the node",
15636            after.len()
15637        );
15638    }
15639
15640    /// Records the `admit`/`retire` calls the manager makes, in order.
15641    ///
15642    /// Deliberately not mockall: the seam is two one-word methods on a trait whose implementations
15643    /// the tests assert about *sequentially* (admit must precede the retire that ends the Session),
15644    /// and a plain log the test can filter is easier to read than expectations wired against a
15645    /// sequence that cross-thread `Drop` validation cannot order anyway. The log is `Arc<Mutex<Vec>>`
15646    /// for the same reason the manager's own fields are: `admit` runs on whatever task commits the
15647    /// Session and `retire` on whatever task tears it down.
15648    #[derive(Clone, Default)]
15649    struct RecordingAdmission {
15650        events: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(String, SessionId)>>>,
15651        /// The tokens `admit` minted, in call order.
15652        ///
15653        /// Kept separate from the retires so each list answers one question: what admissions were
15654        /// distinguished, and what a teardown actually presented. One combined list cannot — a
15655        /// retire's token would read as a mint, so a regression that presented the wrong token would
15656        /// hide behind the admit that also wrote the list.
15657        admit_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
15658        /// The tokens `retire` presented, in call order.
15659        retire_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
15660        /// The tokens `raise_target` presented, in call order.
15661        raise_tokens: Arc<Mutex<Vec<AdmissionToken>>>,
15662        /// The `expected_surbs` each `admit` was called with, in call order.
15663        admit_targets: Arc<Mutex<Vec<usize>>>,
15664        /// Mints the tokens `admit` returns, so each admission of a pseudonym is distinguishable —
15665        /// the property the token guard below pins.
15666        token_counter: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
15667    }
15668
15669    impl RecordingAdmission {
15670        fn admitted(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> usize {
15671            self.events
15672                .lock()
15673                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15674                .iter()
15675                .filter(|(event, id)| event == "admit" && id == session_id)
15676                .count()
15677        }
15678
15679        fn retired(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> usize {
15680            self.events
15681                .lock()
15682                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15683                .iter()
15684                .filter(|(event, id)| event == "retire" && id == session_id)
15685                .count()
15686        }
15687
15688        fn retire_precedes_admit(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> bool {
15689            let events = self.events.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner());
15690            match (
15691                events.iter().position(|(e, id)| e == "retire" && id == session_id),
15692                events.iter().position(|(e, id)| e == "admit" && id == session_id),
15693            ) {
15694                (Some(retired_at), Some(admitted_at)) => retired_at < admitted_at,
15695                _ => false,
15696            }
15697        }
15698
15699        /// The full `admit`/`retire` sequence recorded for `session_id`, in order.
15700        ///
15701        /// Counting admits and retires separately is not enough once a pseudonym can be reused: the
15702        /// property the store depends on is the *interleaving* — the teardown's retire must land
15703        /// between the two admits of a Session that was closed and re-established on the same
15704        /// pseudonym — and only the order of the log shows that.
15705        fn sequence(&self, session_id: &SessionId) -> Vec<String> {
15706            self.events
15707                .lock()
15708                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15709                .iter()
15710                .filter(|(_, id)| id == session_id)
15711                .map(|(event, _)| event.clone())
15712                .collect()
15713        }
15714
15715        /// Every token minted by an `admit` of this mock, in call order.
15716        ///
15717        /// Admissions of the same pseudonym must be distinguishable — that is what lets a deferred
15718        /// retire name the admission it belongs to rather than "whatever is admitted now".
15719        fn minted_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
15720            self.admit_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
15721        }
15722
15723        /// The tokens presented by retires, in call order.
15724        fn retire_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
15725            self.retire_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
15726        }
15727
15728        /// The `expected_surbs` each `admit` was called with, in call order.
15729        fn admitted_targets(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
15730            self.admit_targets.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
15731        }
15732
15733        /// The tokens presented by `raise_target`, in call order.
15734        fn raise_tokens(&self) -> Vec<AdmissionToken> {
15735            self.raise_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).clone()
15736        }
15737
15738        /// The targets `raise_target` was called with, in call order.
15739        fn raised_targets(&self) -> Vec<usize> {
15740            self.events
15741                .lock()
15742                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15743                .iter()
15744                .filter_map(|(event, _)| event.strip_prefix("raise_target:")?.parse().ok())
15745                .collect()
15746        }
15747    }
15748
15749    impl SurbAdmissionControl for RecordingAdmission {
15750        fn admit(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, expected_surbs: usize) -> AdmissionToken {
15751            self.events
15752                .lock()
15753                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15754                .push(("admit".into(), *pseudonym));
15755            self.admit_targets
15756                .lock()
15757                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15758                .push(expected_surbs);
15759            // `expected_surbs` is only observable here, so assert the contract inline rather than
15760            // thread a second channel out of the mock: a manager that admitted with a zero target
15761            // would defeat the store's sizing, so it is worth catching at the one point it happens.
15762            assert!(
15763                expected_surbs <= MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS,
15764                "admit was called with a target of {expected_surbs}, which no configuration in this crate produces"
15765            );
15766            // Distinct per admit, mirroring what the store does: the guard test below relies on a
15767            // stale retire never matching a successor's admission.
15768            let token =
15769                AdmissionToken::from_raw(self.token_counter.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) + 1);
15770            self.admit_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
15771            token
15772        }
15773
15774        fn retire(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, token: AdmissionToken) {
15775            self.events
15776                .lock()
15777                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15778                .push(("retire".into(), *pseudonym));
15779            self.retire_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
15780        }
15781
15782        fn raise_target(&self, pseudonym: &SessionId, token: AdmissionToken, expected_surbs: usize) {
15783            // Recorded with the target, since a raise that names the wrong ring is only visible from
15784            // both halves at once.
15785            self.events
15786                .lock()
15787                .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
15788                .push((format!("raise_target:{expected_surbs}"), *pseudonym));
15789            self.raise_tokens.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()).push(token);
15790        }
15791    }
15792
15793    /// Upper bound the recording mock asserts `admit` targets against. Matches the manager config
15794    /// the fixtures below run with, which is the only place a target comes from.
15795    const MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS: usize = 10_000;
15796
15797    /// An Exit session must originate nothing once it has been closed explicitly.
15798    ///
15799    /// The Exit's keep-alive stream is a `repeat_with` on a rate limiter: it produces a
15800    /// return-routed packet every period regardless of whether a SURB exists to carry it. That is
15801    /// fine while the initiator is present and replenishing, and it is the *supply* side of the
15802    /// `london-01` outage once the initiator is gone — every such packet is one the routing
15803    /// resolution stage can never resolve, and one unresolvable packet there stalls all origination
15804    /// on the node (see `hopr_transport::path::resolve`).
15805    ///
15806    /// Teardown is therefore the only thing standing between a departed initiator and an unbounded
15807    /// supply of unresolvable packets, which is why each closure path has to be shown to stop the
15808    /// stream rather than merely drop the slot.
15809    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15810    async fn an_exit_session_should_originate_nothing_after_an_explicit_close() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15811        // Default idle timeout (180 s), so eviction cannot confound what the explicit close proves.
15812        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) =
15813            exit_session_originating_keep_alives(Default::default(), None).await?;
15814
15815        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
15816
15817        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close").await;
15818        Ok(())
15819    }
15820
15821    /// An Exit session must originate nothing once it has been evicted for being idle.
15822    ///
15823    /// This is the path that matters most for a departed initiator: nobody closes that session, so
15824    /// idle eviction is what ends it, and eviction runs through a Moka listener rather than the
15825    /// explicit close path. A keep-alive stream that survives eviction would go on originating
15826    /// unresolvable return packets with no session left to account for them.
15827    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
15828    async fn an_exit_session_should_originate_nothing_after_idle_eviction() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
15829        let idle_timeout = KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 3;
15830        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, _) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
15831            SessionManagerConfig {
15832                idle_timeout,
15833                ..Default::default()
15834            },
15835            None,
15836        )
15837        .await?;
15838
15839        // Moka evicts lazily, so drive its maintenance rather than waiting for the manager's own
15840        // (jittered, multi-second) eviction tick: this makes the eviction prompt and deterministic.
15841        for _ in 0..50 {
15842            mgr.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
15843            if mgr.active_sessions().is_empty() {
15844                break;
15845            }
15846            tokio::time::sleep(idle_timeout / 10).await;
15847        }
15848        assert!(
15849            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
15850            "the idle session was never evicted, so this test cannot say anything about eviction"
15851        );
15852
15853        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "idle eviction").await;
15854        Ok(())
15855    }

15857    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
15858    // PIX fill — the Exit's own keep-alives
15859    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
15860
15861    /// A [`PixFillControl`] over a random pseudonym, an empty SURB estimate, and an Entry that has
15862    /// shown it refills.
15863    ///
15864    /// `reserve` is the *effective* reserve, as [`effective_surb_reserve`] would have derived it —
15865    /// these tests are about what `admit` does with one, not about where it came from. Against an
15866    /// estimate that starts empty, any `reserve` above zero refuses fill outright, which is what makes
15867    /// admission a usable assertion that a packet was classified as the notification: a test that
15868    /// wants one admitted gives the estimate a SURB, because the notification is not sent on none.
15869    fn fill_control(notify_period: Option<Duration>, reserve: u64) -> PixFillControl {
15870        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
15871        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
15872        fill_control_for(notify_period, reserve, surb_mgmt)
15873    }
15874
15875    /// [`fill_control`] over a balancer state the caller holds on to, so a test can decide when, if
15876    /// ever, the Entry is shown to refill.
15877    fn fill_control_for(
15878        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
15879        reserve: u64,
15880        surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>,
15881    ) -> PixFillControl {
15882        PixFillControl::new(
15883            HoprPseudonym::random(),
15884            RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
15885            notify_period,
15886            None,
15887            // The establishment target is the one whose derivation gives `reserve`: these tests are
15888            // about what `admit` does with a reserve, not about where it came from. Against a ceiling
15889            // of `reserve` itself, a quarter is below it, so the target is four times the reserve —
15890            // except at the floor, where `effective_surb_reserve` derives 1 from any small target.
15891            // The announcement tests below build their own control to move it.
15892            SurbReserveBasis {
15893                configured: reserve,
15894                establishment_target: reserve.saturating_mul(4),
15895            },
15896            Default::default(),
15897            surb_mgmt,
15898        )
15899    }
15900
15901    /// [`fill_control`] that also has a degraded notification period configured.
15902    ///
15903    /// The Entry is taken as a reader (`fill_control` does that too) and given `stock` SURBs, because
15904    /// a degraded period is only ever reached with both: without a reader or a SURB the notification
15905    /// is withheld before its cadence can matter.
15906    fn fill_control_degraded(
15907        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
15908        degraded_period: Option<Duration>,
15909        reserve: u64,
15910        stock: u64,
15911    ) -> PixFillControl {
15912        let control = PixFillControl::new(
15913            HoprPseudonym::random(),
15914            RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
15915            notify_period,
15916            degraded_period,
15917            // Four times the reserve, so its derivation gives exactly `reserve` against a ceiling of
15918            // `reserve` — see `fill_control_for`.
15919            SurbReserveBasis {
15920                configured: reserve,
15921                establishment_target: reserve.saturating_mul(4),
15922            },
15923            Default::default(),
15924            {
15925                let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
15926                surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
15927                surb_mgmt
15928            },
15929        );
15930        control
15931            .estimator
15932            .produced
15933            .fetch_add(stock, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
15934        control
15935    }
15936
15937    /// Above the fixtures' keep-alive reserve (32), so reports count as idle.
15938    const IDLE_STOCK: u64 = 100;
15939
15940    /// A started control with the idle backoff on. The fill reserve is out of reach, so `admit_at` is true
15941    /// exactly when a report is due.
15942    fn fill_control_idle(base: Duration, cap: Duration, stock: u64) -> PixFillControl {
15943        let surb_mgmt = balancer_with_target(3_200);
15944        let control = PixFillControl::new(
15945            HoprPseudonym::random(),
15946            RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
15947            Some(base),
15948            None,
15949            // The reserve these derive is out of reach.
15950            SurbReserveBasis {
15951                configured: u64::MAX,
15952                establishment_target: u64::MAX,
15953            },
15954            Default::default(),
15955            surb_mgmt,
15956        )
15957        .with_idle_notify_period(Some(cap))
15958        .for_session(ExitSessionKind::Plain);
15959        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(stock, Ordering::Relaxed);
15960        control.start_notify();
15961        control
15962    }
15963
15964    /// How early before its period a report counts as due.
15965    fn due_slack(control: &PixFillControl, period: Duration) -> Duration {
15966        MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(period / if control.is_degraded() { 10 } else { 2 })
15967    }
15968
15969    /// Releases the next report at `from` plus the period in force, checking it is not due earlier.
15970    fn next_report(control: &PixFillControl, from: Instant) -> anyhow::Result<(Instant, Duration)> {
15971        let period = control
15972            .notify_period_in_force()
15973            .context("the control must have a notification period")?;
15974        let early = from + period.saturating_sub(due_slack(control, period) + Duration::from_millis(1));
15975        anyhow::ensure!(
15976            !control.admit_at(early),
15977            "a report went out at {early:?}, before the period of {period:?} that was in force"
15978        );
15979        let due = from + period;
15980        anyhow::ensure!(
15981            control.admit_at(due),
15982            "no report was due after the period of {period:?} that was in force"
15983        );
15984        Ok((due, period))
15985    }
15986
15987    /// The gaps between `count` consecutive reports after the first one at `start`.
15988    fn report_gaps(control: &PixFillControl, start: Instant, count: usize) -> anyhow::Result<Vec<Duration>> {
15989        anyhow::ensure!(control.admit_at(start), "the first report is due at once");
15990        let mut at = start;
15991        let mut gaps = Vec::with_capacity(count);
15992        for _ in 0..count {
15993            let (next, gap) = next_report(control, at)?;
15994            at = next;
15995            gaps.push(gap);
15996        }
15997        Ok(gaps)
15998    }
15999
16000    fn secs(values: &[u64]) -> Vec<Duration> {
16001        values.iter().copied().map(Duration::from_secs).collect()
16002    }
16003
16004    /// The first idle minute stays at the base period; then each report doubles it up to the cap.
16005    #[test]
16006    fn an_idle_session_reports_four_times_at_the_base_period_then_doubles_up_to_the_cap() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16007        let control = fill_control_idle(Duration::from_secs(15), Duration::from_secs(60), IDLE_STOCK);
16008
16009        // Reports at 0, 15, 30 and 45 s are the first minute; the fifth waits 30 s and the sixth 60 s.
16010        let gaps = report_gaps(&control, Instant::now(), 7)?;
16011
16012        assert_eq!(secs(&[15, 15, 15, 30, 60, 60, 60]), gaps);
16013        assert_eq!(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), control.notify_period_in_force());
16014        Ok(())
16015    }

16017    /// A cap that is not a power-of-two multiple of the base is reached exactly.
16018    #[test]
16019    fn the_idle_backoff_stops_at_a_cap_that_is_not_a_power_of_two_of_the_base() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16020        let control = fill_control_idle(Duration::from_secs(10), Duration::from_secs(45), IDLE_STOCK);
16021
16022        let gaps = report_gaps(&control, Instant::now(), 7)?;
16023
16024        assert_eq!(secs(&[10, 10, 10, 20, 40, 45, 45]), gaps);
16025        Ok(())
16026    }

16028    /// Application data resets a backed-off report to the base period at once and restarts the count.
16029    #[test]
16030    fn application_data_resets_a_backed_off_report_to_the_base_period_and_restarts_the_count() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16031        let base = Duration::from_secs(15);
16032        let control = fill_control_idle(base, Duration::from_secs(60), IDLE_STOCK);
16033        let t0 = Instant::now();
16034        report_gaps(&control, t0, 6)?;
16035        assert_eq!(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), control.notify_period_in_force());
16036
16037        control.note_data_activity();
16038
16039        assert_eq!(Some(base), control.notify_period_in_force(), "the reset is prompt");
16040        assert_eq!(0, control.idle_reports());
16041        assert_eq!(
16042            FillRate::once_per(base),
16043            control.effective_rate(),
16044            "the rate follows the period"
16045        );
16046
16047        // The report that finds the data is not idle, so four base-period gaps precede the next doubling.
16048        let t1 = t0 + Duration::from_secs(300);
16049        assert_eq!(secs(&[15, 15, 15, 15, 30]), report_gaps(&control, t1, 5)?);
16050        Ok(())
16051    }

16053    /// A reset releases a report that is overdue at the base period at once.
16054    #[test]
16055    fn a_reset_releases_an_overdue_report_at_once() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16056        let control = fill_control_idle(Duration::from_secs(15), Duration::from_secs(60), IDLE_STOCK);
16057        let t0 = Instant::now();
16058        report_gaps(&control, t0, 6)?;
16059        // Backed off at 60 s, so a report 20 s after the last is not due.
16060        let last = t0 + Duration::from_secs(15 * 3 + 30 + 60 + 60);
16061        let twenty_later = last + Duration::from_secs(20);
16062        assert!(!control.admit_at(twenty_later));
16063
16064        control.note_data_activity();
16065
16066        assert!(
16067            control.admit_at(twenty_later),
16068            "twenty seconds is past the base period, so the report is overdue"
16069        );
16070        Ok(())
16071    }

16073    /// Data between reports keeps the base period.
16074    #[test]
16075    fn data_between_reports_keeps_the_base_period() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16076        let base = Duration::from_secs(15);
16077        let control = fill_control_idle(base, Duration::from_secs(60), IDLE_STOCK);
16078        let mut at = Instant::now();
16079        assert!(control.admit_at(at));
16080
16081        for _ in 0..10 {
16082            control.note_data_activity();
16083            let (next, period) = next_report(&control, at)?;
16084            at = next;
16085            assert_eq!(base, period);
16086            assert_eq!(0, control.idle_reports());
16087        }
16088        Ok(())
16089    }

16093    fn no_backoff_while_pix_fill_runs() -> anyhow::Result<()> {

16099

16106    /// Fill starting resets a backed-off stream, and the count restarts when fill stops.

16134    /// A degraded path is never backed off; entering it restarts the count.

16136    fn no_backoff_while_degraded() -> anyhow::Result<()> {

16172    /// No backoff unless the report leaves the stock above the keep-alive reserve: the report spends a SURB itself.

16195            "two SURBs above the reserve is idle, and counts from its first report"

16248    /// The Entry's idle timeout travels in the low half of `additional_data`, beside the options word.
16249    #[test]
16250    fn the_entry_idle_timeout_is_announced_in_whole_seconds_beside_the_options_word() {
16251        let options = 0xdead_beef_0123_4567u64;
16252        let u32_max = Duration::from_secs(u32::MAX as u64);
16253        for (idle, expected) in [
16254            (Duration::ZERO, None),
16255            (Duration::from_millis(1), Some(Duration::from_secs(1))),
16256            (Duration::from_millis(1_500), Some(Duration::from_secs(1))),
16257            (Duration::from_secs(180), Some(Duration::from_secs(180))),
16258            (u32_max, Some(u32_max)),
16259            (Duration::from_secs(u64::MAX), Some(u32_max)),
16260        ] {
16261            let data = into_initiation_additional_data(options, idle);
16262            assert_eq!(options, initiation_options(data), "options for {idle:?}");
16263            assert_eq!(expected, announced_idle_timeout(data), "announcement for {idle:?}");
16264        }
16265        assert_eq!(
16266            None,
16267            announced_idle_timeout(into_initiation_additional_data(options, Duration::ZERO))
16268        );
16269    }

16271    /// The per-session cap is a quarter of the Entry's announced timeout, never above the node's cap.

16273    fn the_session_idle_notify_cap_follows_the_entry_idle_timeout() {

16279            session_idle_notify_cap(node_cap, None),

16281        );

16283        assert_eq!(Some(Duration::from_secs(30)), announced(120));

16286            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),

16295        assert_eq!(None, control(announced(40).unwrap_or_default()));
16296        assert_eq!(
16297            Some(Duration::from_secs(30)),
16298            control(announced(120).unwrap_or_default())

16302    /// The Entry sends its idle timeout in the `StartSession` it opens a Session with.
16303    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16304    async fn the_entry_announces_its_idle_timeout_in_the_start_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16305        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
16306        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
16307            initiation_timeout_base: Duration::from_millis(100),
16308            idle_timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),
16309            ..Default::default()
16310        });
16311
16312        let sent: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<StartInitiation<SessionTarget, HoprSessionCapabilities>>>> =
16313            Default::default();

16315        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
16316        alice_transport
16317            .expect_send_message()
16318            .once()
16319            .withf(move |_, data| msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession))
16320            .returning(move |_, data| {
16321                if let Ok(StartProtocol::StartSession(init)) =
16322                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
16323                {
16324                    captured.lock().push(init);
16325                }
16326                Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
16327            });
16328
16329        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
16330        let (alice_sender, _alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
16331        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
16332
16333        let _ = alice_mgr
16334            .new_session(
16335                bob_peer,
16336                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
16337                SessionClientConfig {
16338                    capabilities: None.into(),
16339                    pseudonym: HoprPseudonym::random().into(),
16340                    surb_management: None,
16341                    ..Default::default()
16342                },
16343            )
16344            .await;
16345
16346        let sent = sent.lock();
16347        anyhow::ensure!(sent.len() == 1, "exactly one StartSession must have been sent");
16348        assert_eq!(
16349            Some(Duration::from_secs(120)),
16350            announced_idle_timeout(sent[0].additional_data)
16351        );
16352        Ok(())
16353    }

16389    /// A stock wiped below the reserve ends the backoff at once, without waiting for the next report.
16390    #[test]
16391    fn a_stock_that_falls_to_the_reserve_ends_the_backoff_at_once() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16392        let base = Duration::from_secs(15);
16393        let control = fill_control_idle(base, Duration::from_secs(60), IDLE_STOCK);
16394        let t0 = Instant::now();
16395        report_gaps(&control, t0, 6)?;
16396        assert_eq!(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), control.notify_period_in_force());
16397        let last = t0 + Duration::from_secs(15 * 3 + 30 + 60 + 60);
16398        let twenty_later = last + Duration::from_secs(20);
16399        assert!(!control.admit_at(twenty_later));
16400
16401        // Still well above the reserve: nothing changes.
16402        control.recheck_reserve();
16403        assert_eq!(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), control.notify_period_in_force());
16404
16405        // A new SURB generation wipes most of the stock.
16406        control.estimator.evicted.fetch_add(IDLE_STOCK - 2, Ordering::Relaxed);
16407        control.recheck_reserve();
16408
16409        assert_eq!(Some(base), control.notify_period_in_force());
16410        assert_eq!(0, control.idle_reports());
16411        assert!(control.admit_at(twenty_later), "the overdue report goes out at once");
16412        Ok(())
16413    }

16491    /// A reply burst that drains slowly through the egress limiter is activity until it has drained: the
16492    /// hook in front of the buffer alone sees it once, on entry.
16493    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16494    async fn a_burst_draining_slowly_through_the_egress_limiter_is_noted_as_activity() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16495        // A target of 10 at the default 5 s minimum buffer duration limits the egress to 2 packets per second.
16496        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, mut new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
16497            Capabilities::empty(),
16498            10,
16499            SessionManagerConfig {
16500                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
16501                surb_idle_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(4)),
16502                initial_return_session_egress_rate: 2,
16503                ..Default::default()
16504            },
16505        )
16506        .await?;
16507        let control = mgr
16508            .sessions
16509            .get(&pseudonym)
16510            .and_then(|slot| slot.pix_fill.get().cloned())
16511            .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?;
16512        let mut incoming = new_session_rx.next().await.context("the Session was announced")?;
16513        show_exit_its_entry(
16514            &mgr,
16515            pseudonym,
16516            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
16517                target_notify: false,
16518                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
16519            },
16520        )
16521        .await?;
16522        mgr.sessions
16523            .get(&pseudonym)
16524            .context("the session slot must exist")?
16525            .surb_estimator
16526            .produced
16527            .fetch_add(10_000, Ordering::Relaxed);
16528
16529        // Queued at once; at 2 per second this drains for about ten seconds.
16530        let writer = tokio::spawn(async move {
16531            for _ in 0..20 {
16532                incoming.session.write_all(b"burst").await?;
16533            }
16534            incoming.session.flush().await?;
16535            anyhow::Ok(incoming)
16536        });
16537
16538        let mut released = 0;
16539        let mut released_at_half = 0;
16540        for tick in 0..80 {
16541            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)).await;
16542            while let Ok((_, data)) = msg_rx.try_recv() {
16543                released += usize::from(data.data.application_tag == SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG);
16544            }
16545            if tick == 60 {
16546                released_at_half = released;
16547            }
16548            assert_eq!(
16549                Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
16550                control.notify_period_in_force(),
16551                "the period backed off while the burst was still draining (tick {tick}, {released} released)"
16552            );
16553        }
16554        assert!(
16555            released > released_at_half,
16556            "fixture: the burst must still be draining at the end of the window ({released} released)"
16557        );
16558        writer.abort();
16559        Ok(())
16560    }

16636    /// An idle Exit Session backs its reports off to the cap; an Entry keep-alive carrying SURBs does not
16637    /// undo that, application data does. Base 1 s, cap 4 s: the cap is reached in about ten seconds.
16638    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16639    async fn an_idle_exit_session_backs_its_reports_off_until_data_moves() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16640        let cap = Duration::from_secs(4);
16641        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, mut new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
16642            Capabilities::empty(),
16643            64,
16644            SessionManagerConfig {
16645                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
16646                surb_idle_notify_period: Some(cap),
16647                ..Default::default()
16648            },
16649        )
16650        .await?;
16651        let control = mgr
16652            .sessions
16653            .get(&pseudonym)
16654            .and_then(|slot| slot.pix_fill.get().cloned())
16655            .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?;
16656        let mut incoming = new_session_rx.next().await.context("the Session was announced")?;
16657
16658        show_exit_its_entry(
16659            &mgr,
16660            pseudonym,
16661            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
16662                target_notify: false,
16663                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
16664            },
16665        )
16666        .await?;
16667        // Far above the keep-alive reserve (16 for the 64-SURB target), so every report is an idle one.
16668        mgr.sessions
16669            .get(&pseudonym)
16670            .context("the session slot must exist")?
16671            .surb_estimator
16672            .produced
16673            .fetch_add(10_000, Ordering::Relaxed);
16674
16675        timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), async {
16676            while control.notify_period_in_force() != Some(cap) {
16677                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
16678            }
16679        })
16680        .await
16681        .context("an idle Session never backed its reports off to the cap")?;
16682        while msg_rx.try_recv().is_ok() {}
16683
16684        // At most one: a late window start on a loaded runner can reach the next report; the base period gives 3.
16685        let window = Duration::from_millis(3_500);
16686        let idle = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
16687        assert!(
16688            idle.len() <= 1,
16689            "a Session whose period is {cap:?} sent {} report(s) in {window:?}: {idle:?}",
16690            idle.len()
16691        );
16692
16693        // The Entry's refill keep-alive carries SURBs and is not application data.
16694        dispatch_entry_keep_alive(&mgr, pseudonym, None.into(), ENTRY_SURBS, 0)?;
16695        wait_for_counterparty_refills(&mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
16696        assert_eq!(Some(cap), control.notify_period_in_force());
16697        assert!(!control.data_seen_since_report());
16698
16699        // Application data is.
16700        incoming.session.write_all(b"ping").await?;
16701        incoming.session.flush().await?;
16702        assert_eq!(
16703            Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
16704            control.notify_period_in_force(),
16705            "data must bring the base period back at once"
16706        );
16707        while msg_rx.try_recv().is_ok() {}
16708        let busy = level_reports_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, REPORT_WINDOW).await;
16709        assert!(
16710            busy.len() >= 2,
16711            "a Session that has just moved data must report at the base period again, but {} report(s) arrived over \
16712             {REPORT_WINDOW:?}: {busy:?}",
16713            busy.len()
16714        );
16715        Ok(())
16716    }

16718    /// Application data counts as activity in either direction, rate-controlled or not.
16719    #[rstest::rstest]
16720    #[case::rate_controlled_outbound(Capabilities::empty(), false)]
16721    #[case::rate_controlled_inbound(Capabilities::empty(), true)]
16722    #[case::no_rate_control_outbound(Capability::NoRateControl.into(), false)]
16723    #[case::no_rate_control_inbound(Capability::NoRateControl.into(), true)]
16724    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16725    async fn exit_session_data_is_noted_as_activity_in_either_direction(
16726        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
16727        #[case] inbound: bool,
16728    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16729        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, mut new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_reporting_levels_with(
16730            capabilities,
16731            64,
16732            SessionManagerConfig {
16733                surb_balance_notify_period: Some(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD),
16734                surb_idle_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_secs(4)),
16735                ..Default::default()
16736            },
16737        )
16738        .await?;
16739        let control = mgr
16740            .sessions
16741            .get(&pseudonym)
16742            .and_then(|slot| slot.pix_fill.get().cloned())
16743            .context("an Exit Session with a notification period steers a fill control")?;
16744        let mut incoming = new_session_rx.next().await.context("the Session was announced")?;
16745
16746        // Start-protocol traffic, SURBs included, is not application data.
16747        show_exit_its_entry(
16748            &mgr,
16749            pseudonym,
16750            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
16751                target_notify: false,
16752                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
16753            },
16754        )
16755        .await?;
16756        assert!(
16757            !control.data_seen_since_report(),
16758            "fixture: nothing but a keep-alive has moved"
16759        );
16760
16761        if inbound {
16762            mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, session_data_packet(b"hello")?)?;
16763            let mut buffer = [0u8; 16];
16764            timeout(
16765                Duration::from_secs(5),
16766                futures::AsyncReadExt::read(&mut incoming.session, &mut buffer),
16767            )
16768            .await
16769            .context("the Session never read the packet")??;
16770        } else {
16771            // With a stock of three the limiter holds the packet, and the write must be noted on entry
16772            // anyway, so the flush is not awaited for long.
16773            let _ = timeout(Duration::from_millis(300), async {
16774                incoming.session.write_all(b"hello").await?;
16775                incoming.session.flush().await
16776            })
16777            .await;
16778            if !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl) {
16779                // Reports are Start-protocol keep-alives and are ignored here.
16780                let mut released = 0;
16781                while let Ok((_, data)) = msg_rx.try_recv() {
16782                    released += usize::from(data.data.application_tag == SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG);
16783                }
16784                assert_eq!(
16785                    0, released,
16786                    "fixture: the limiter must still be holding the packet, or this does not show that the write is \
16787                     noted before it"
16788                );
16789            }
16790        }
16791
16792        assert!(
16793            control.data_seen_since_report(),
16794            "data {} the Exit must be noted as activity",
16795            if inbound { "reaching" } else { "leaving" }
16796        );
16797        Ok(())
16798    }

16800    /// An Exit PIX Session's establishment, SSA request, reports and fill are counted under their kinds.
16801    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
16802    async fn exit_originated_pix_control_packets_are_counted() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
16803        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
16804
16805        probe::reset();
16806        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
16807            Capabilities::empty(),
16808            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
16809            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
16810                min_surb_reserve: 1,
16811                drain_after_close: false,
16812                ..Default::default()
16813            },
16814            None,
16815        )
16816        .await?;
16817        {
16818            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
16819            slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
16820            slot.surb_estimator.produced.fetch_add(100_000, Ordering::Relaxed);
16821        }
16822
16823        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(3_500)).await;
16824
16825        for series in [
16826            "exit_control/session_established/pix/sent",
16827            "exit_control/ssa_request/pix/sent",
16828            "exit_control/surb_report/pix/sent",
16829            "exit_control/pix_fill/pix/sent",
16830        ] {
16831            assert!(probe::get(series) > 0, "{series} was never counted");
16832        }
16833        Ok(())
16834    }

16836    /// The `surb_starved` gauge moves on the edges, and a control dropped mid-stall returns it.
16837    ///
16838    /// Per refused packet would measure how hard the stream retried rather than how long the
16839    /// Session was starved, and a control that went away while withholding would leave the count
16840    /// standing for the life of the process.
16841    #[test]
16842    fn the_surb_starved_gauge_counts_stalls_and_is_returned_on_drop() {
16843        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
16844
16845        probe::reset();
16846        let control = fill_control(None, 10);
16847        let now = Instant::now();
16848
16849        // The estimator starts empty, so every one of these is below the reserve of ten.
16850        for _ in 0..3 {
16851            assert!(!control.admit_at(now), "fill must be withheld below the reserve");
16852        }
16853        assert_eq!(
16854            1,
16855            probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"),
16856            "three refusals are one stall, not three"
16857        );
16858
16859        // Enough SURBs arrive to clear the reserve.
16860        control
16861            .estimator
16862            .produced
16863            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16864        assert!(control.admit_at(now));
16865        assert_eq!(0, probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"));
16866
16867        // And a control dropped while withholding returns its own.
16868        control
16869            .estimator
16870            .consumed
16871            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16872        assert!(!control.admit_at(now));
16873        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"));
16874        drop(control);
16875        assert_eq!(
16876            0,
16877            probe::get("sessions_stalled/surb_starved"),
16878            "a session that dies mid-stall must not leave the gauge standing"
16879        );
16880    }
