16882    /// The fill reserve reads the estimator's held count, which must not stay inflated by evicted
16883    /// SURBs. After an overflow drains, the real store is empty, yet a raw `produced - consumed` would
16884    /// still read far above the reserve and admit fill into an empty buffer -- the exact failure the
16885    /// reserve exists to prevent (a return packet that finds no SURB stalls every packet the node
16886    /// originates). With evictions counted, the held count is what the store holds, so fill is withheld.
16887    #[test]
16888    fn the_fill_reserve_is_not_defeated_by_a_post_overflow_estimate() {
16889        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
16890
16891        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
16892        let control = fill_control(None, RESERVE);
16893        let now = Instant::now();
16894
16895        // Post-overflow-drain: 1000 SURBs arrived, the full store evicted 900 of them, and the 100 it
16896        // actually held were all spent. The store is empty; `produced - consumed` alone reads 900.
16897        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(1000, Ordering::Relaxed);
16898        control.estimator.evicted.fetch_add(900, Ordering::Relaxed);
16899        control.estimator.consumed.fetch_add(100, Ordering::Relaxed);
16900
16901        assert_eq!(0, control.drainable_surbs(), "an empty store has nothing to drain");
16902        assert!(
16903            !control.admit_at(now),
16904            "fill must be withheld: the real held count is below the reserve"
16905        );
16906    }
16907
16908    /// One stream, two producers, and the faster of them wins.
16909    ///
16910    /// The SURB-level notification and PIX fill are the same packet sent for different reasons, so
16911    /// running two streams of them would double the Exit's return traffic to say the same thing
16912    /// twice. What has to be preserved is the floor: turning fill off must leave the notification
16913    /// running, and a Session with no notification configured must still be fillable — that second
16914    /// case is the deployment's own test fixtures, which pin `surb_balance_notify_period: None`.
16915    #[test]
16916    fn the_exit_keep_alive_rate_is_the_faster_of_its_two_producers() {
16917        let notify = Duration::from_secs(60);
16918        let control = fill_control(Some(notify), 1);
16919
16920        assert_eq!(
16921            FillRate::ZERO,
16922            control.effective_rate(),
16923            "nothing runs before the notification's initial delay has elapsed"
16924        );
16925
16926        control.start_notify();
16927        assert_eq!(FillRate::once_per(notify), control.effective_rate());
16928
16929        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
16930        assert_eq!(
16931            FillRate::per_second(10),
16932            control.effective_rate(),
16933            "fill above the notification rate must take over"
16934        );
16935
16936        control.set_fill(FillRate::once_per(Duration::from_secs(600)));
16937        assert_eq!(
16938            FillRate::once_per(notify),
16939            control.effective_rate(),
16940            "fill below the notification rate must not slow it down"
16941        );
16942
16943        control.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
16944        assert_eq!(
16945            FillRate::once_per(notify),
16946            control.effective_rate(),
16947            "a Session that has stopped filling still reports its SURB level"
16948        );
16949
16950        // And the other way round: no notification configured, so fill is the only producer.
16951        let fill_only = fill_control(None, 1);
16952        fill_only.start_notify();
16953        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, fill_only.effective_rate());
16954        fill_only.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(4));
16955        assert_eq!(FillRate::per_second(4), fill_only.effective_rate());
16956        fill_only.set_fill(FillRate::ZERO);
16957        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, fill_only.effective_rate());
16958    }
16959
16960    /// Fill yields to the Session's own SURB reserve; the SURB-level notification does not, though it
16961    /// still needs a SURB to be sent on.
16962    ///
16963    /// The asymmetry is the whole rule. A return packet that finds no SURB is not dropped — the
16964    /// routing resolver holds it, and every packet this node originates behind it, for the whole of
16965    /// `surb_resolution_wait`. So an Exit that filled a cycle down to its last SURB would stall the
16966    /// Session it was filling for, and every other Session on the node with it. The notification is
16967    /// exempt from the reserve because it is the message that *asks* for more SURBs: refusing to send
16968    /// it when SURBs are scarce is refusing to ask for the thing that is scarce. With none at all, it
16969    /// is the same packet that finds no SURB, and it is withheld like one.
16970    #[test]
16971    fn fill_withholds_below_the_surb_reserve_while_the_level_notification_does_not() {
16972        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
16973        let control = fill_control(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE);
16974        control.start_notify();
16975
16976        assert!(
16977            !control.admit(),
16978            "the level notification has no SURB to be sent on, and must not wait out the resolver for one"
16979        );
16980
16981        // One SURB, 99 short of the reserve: enough for the notification, which the reserve does not
16982        // bind, and the first packet is it.
16983        control
16984            .estimator
16985            .produced
16986            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16987        assert!(control.admit(), "the level notification must go out below the reserve");
16988        // The notification period is an hour, so everything after it is fill — and there is too little
16989        // to spend.
16990        assert!(!control.admit(), "fill must not spend a SURB the Session does not have");
16991
16992        control
16993            .estimator
16994            .produced
16995            .fetch_add(RESERVE - 2, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
16996        assert!(!control.admit(), "one short of the reserve is still short");
16997
16998        control
16999            .estimator
17000            .produced
17001            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17002        assert!(control.admit(), "at the reserve, fill may spend");
17003
17004        // Consumption counted elsewhere walks the estimate back below the reserve.
17005        control
17006            .estimator
17007            .consumed
17008            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17009        assert!(!control.admit());
17010    }
17011
17012    /// Exactly one caller may take a Session into its drain, and doing so silences the notification.
17013    ///
17014    /// `begin_surb_drain` is reached from the operator's close, the closure notifier and
17015    /// `handle_session_error` independently, so two closes can both read [`is_draining`] as false and
17016    /// race for the same drain. The transition is what settles it: the winner is the one caller that
17017    /// tells the supervisor the Session closed, and the loser is answered as though it had arrived
17018    /// afterwards. Were the check and the write separate, both would start a drain and the supervisor
17019    /// would be told twice about one close.
17020    ///
17021    /// [`is_draining`]: PixFillControl::is_draining
17022    #[test]
17023    fn only_one_caller_can_take_a_session_into_its_drain() {
17024        let notify = Duration::from_secs(60);
17025        // A reserve of two over a stock of one, so that fill is refused and a notification, which the
17026        // reserve does not bind, would not be: only the drain can be what refuses the last packet.
17027        let control = fill_control(Some(notify), 2);
17028        control
17029            .estimator
17030            .produced
17031            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17032        control.start_notify();
17033        assert_eq!(FillRate::once_per(notify), control.effective_rate());
17034
17035        assert!(control.enter_drain(), "the first caller takes the drain");
17036        assert!(control.is_draining());
17037        assert!(
17038            !control.enter_drain(),
17039            "a concurrent close must lose the transition rather than start a second drain"
17040        );
17041        assert!(control.is_draining(), "losing the transition must not clear the drain");
17042
17043        assert_eq!(
17044            FillRate::ZERO,
17045            control.effective_rate(),
17046            "a draining stream runs at the fill rate alone, and nothing is filling it"
17047        );
17048        assert!(
17049            !control.admit(),
17050            "the notification is the one packet exempt from the reserve, and a drain silences it"
17051        );
17052
17053        // Nor can the one-shot delay task, which holds a clone of this control, turn it back on.
17054        control.start_notify();
17055        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, control.effective_rate());
17056    }
17057
17058    /// The SURB-level notification is classified by when it was *due*, not by when the scheduler got
17059    /// round to releasing it.
17060    ///
17061    /// The rate limiter that releases these packets does not hit the period exactly: it sleeps in
17062    /// chunks of `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK`, re-reads its controller on each wake, and rounds a rate into an
17063    /// integer packet count. Compared against the period exactly, a period the controller rounds
17064    /// short by a microsecond would classify every other notification as fill — and, below the
17065    /// reserve, drop it. That is the message that *asks* for the SURBs whose absence caused the drop,
17066    /// and it runs on every Exit Session with a notification period configured, PIX or not.
17067    ///
17068    /// The reserve here is the instrument: the estimator holds one SURB against a reserve of a hundred,
17069    /// so a packet the rule classifies as fill is refused and a packet it classifies as the
17070    /// notification is admitted. Admission is therefore the assertion that it was not counted as fill.
17071    #[test]
17072    fn a_level_notification_released_a_shade_early_is_still_the_notification() {
17073        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17074        // Two seconds, so the slack is `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` rather than half the period, and the two
17075        // bounds are distinguishable.
17076        let period = Duration::from_secs(2);
17077        let control = fill_control(Some(period), RESERVE);
17078        // One SURB to send the notification on, far short of the reserve: the notification is not sent
17079        // on none.
17080        control
17081            .estimator
17082            .produced
17083            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17084        control.start_notify();
17085
17086        let t0 = Instant::now();
17087        assert!(
17088            control.admit_at(t0),
17089            "the first packet is the notification, below the reserve"
17090        );
17091
17092        // A shade under the period — the shape a rate rounded down by a microsecond produces.
17093        let early = t0 + period - Duration::from_micros(1);
17094        assert!(
17095            control.admit_at(early),
17096            "a notification released a microsecond early must not be reclassified as fill and dropped"
17097        );
17098
17099        // And it is the notification rather than a free pass: the next packet is measured from when
17100        // this one actually went out, so everything inside the following period is fill.
17101        assert!(
17102            !control.admit_at(early + Duration::from_millis(1)),
17103            "the packet after the notification is fill, and there is nothing to spend"
17104        );
17105        assert!(
17106            !control.admit_at(early + period - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK - Duration::from_millis(1)),
17107            "a packet inside the slack window is still fill"
17108        );
17109
17110        // The slack window opens `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` before the period is up, and not earlier.
17111        assert!(
17112            control.admit_at(early + period - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK),
17113            "at the edge of the slack window the packet is the notification again"
17114        );
17115
17116        // A period short enough that `MAX_WAIT_CHUNK` would swallow it keeps half of itself.
17117        let short = Duration::from_millis(200);
17118        let control = fill_control(Some(short), RESERVE);
17119        control
17120            .estimator
17121            .produced
17122            .fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17123        control.start_notify();
17124        let t0 = Instant::now();
17125        assert!(control.admit_at(t0));
17126        assert!(
17127            !control.admit_at(t0 + short / 2 - Duration::from_millis(1)),
17128            "the slack is capped at half the period, so it cannot widen a short period away to nothing"
17129        );
17130        assert!(control.admit_at(t0 + short / 2));
17131    }
17132
17133    /// The level notification goes only to an Entry that has shown it refills.
17134    ///
17135    /// A report spends one of the Session's own SURBs. An Entry without a SURB balancer acts on no
17136    /// report, so every one sent to it spends a SURB to say nothing, and it is the Entry that has least
17137    /// to give the Exit back (gnosis_vpn#748). What the Exit has seen of it, and not what it announced,
17138    /// is the evidence: the announced target is a figure the peer picks.
17139    ///
17140    /// The withheld notification keeps its slot, so that the next packet to ask is the notification once the Entry is
17141    /// heard.
17142    #[test]
17143    fn a_level_notification_waits_for_an_entry_that_refills() {
17144        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17145        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
17146        let control = fill_control_for(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE, surb_mgmt.clone());
17147        control.start_notify();
17148        // SURBs to send it on, short of the reserve: this is not about the SURBs.
17149        control
17150            .estimator
17151            .produced
17152            .fetch_add(10, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17153
17154        let now = Instant::now();
17155        assert!(
17156            !control.admit_at(now),
17157            "an Entry that has not been heard to refill has nobody reading the report"
17158        );
17159        assert!(!control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(1)));
17160
17161        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
17162        assert!(
17163            control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(2)),
17164            "the withheld notification keeps its slot: the next packet to ask goes out as the notification"
17165        );
17166        assert!(
17167            !control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(3)),
17168            "and it was the notification: the packet after it is fill, below the reserve"
17169        );
17170    }
17171
17172    /// The degraded period reports faster, and leaving it restores the normal one.
17173    ///
17174    /// The admission rule is the instrument again: the stock is one SURB against a reserve of a
17175    /// hundred, so only the notification is admitted. In the normal period that is one packet per
17176    /// period; in the degraded period it is one per degraded period, which is what turns a 15 s
17177    /// cadence into a 1 s one when the Exit's forward path goes dark.
17178    #[test]
17179    fn the_degraded_notification_period_reports_faster_and_leaves_on_request() {
17180        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17181        let normal = Duration::from_secs(3600);
17182        let degraded = Duration::from_secs(1);
17183        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(normal), Some(degraded), RESERVE, 1);
17184        control.start_notify();
17185
17186        let t0 = Instant::now();
17187        assert!(control.admit_at(t0), "the first packet is the notification");
17188        assert!(
17189            !control.admit_at(t0 + degraded),
17190            "inside the normal period, with no degradation, it is fill and there is nothing to spend"
17191        );
17192
17193        control.set_degraded(true);
17194        assert_eq!(
17195            FillRate::once_per(degraded),
17196            control.effective_rate(),
17197            "the stream must run at the degraded period, not only classify at it"
17198        );
17199        // Entering after a gap longer than the degraded period releases the next packet at once,
17200        // because the gap is measured against the period in force.
17201        assert!(
17202            control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(2)),
17203            "entering degraded mode after a long gap makes the next packet the notification at once"
17204        );
17205        assert!(
17206            !control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(2) + degraded / 2 - Duration::from_millis(1)),
17207            "and the cadence that follows it is the degraded one, less the classification slack"
17208        );
17209        assert!(control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(2) + degraded));
17210
17211        control.set_degraded(false);
17212        assert_eq!(
17213            FillRate::once_per(normal),
17214            control.effective_rate(),
17215            "leaving degraded mode restores the normal period"
17216        );
17217        assert_eq!(
17218            Some(normal),
17219            control.period(&control.state.lock()),
17220            "and the notification is classified against it"
17221        );
17222    }
17223
17224    /// Entering degraded mode releases the next notification at once, and leaving it does not.
17225    ///
17226    /// The first half is what makes the switch worth having: a Session that has just lost its forward
17227    /// path has been waiting out the normal period, and the report that corroborates the verdict must
17228    /// go now rather than a period later.
17229    #[test]
17230    fn entering_the_degraded_period_releases_the_next_notification_at_once() {
17231        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17232        let control = fill_control_degraded(
17233            Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)),
17234            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
17235            RESERVE,
17236            1,
17237        );
17238        control.start_notify();
17239
17240        let t0 = Instant::now();
17241        assert!(control.admit_at(t0));
17242        // A long silence, as if the normal period were far longer than the test.
17243        let later = t0 + Duration::from_secs(10);
17244        control.set_degraded(true);
17245        assert!(control.admit_at(later), "a degraded report is due at once");
17246        control.set_degraded(false);
17247        assert!(
17248            !control.admit_at(later + Duration::from_secs(1)),
17249            "back on the normal period, the next report waits for the normal period from the last one"
17250        );
17251    }
17252
17253    /// A degraded switch after a drain cannot bring the notification back.
17254    ///
17255    /// `enter_drain` clears `notify_started`, and nothing re-sets it, so the period the switch picks
17256    /// is never consulted again: `set_degraded` re-derives a rate that is fill's alone. The driver
17257    /// stops on `is_draining`, but this pins the control's own side of the race.
17258    #[test]
17259    fn a_degraded_switch_cannot_revive_a_drained_notification() {
17260        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), Some(Duration::from_secs(1)), 1, 10);
17261        control.start_notify();
17262        control.set_degraded(true);
17263        assert_eq!(
17264            FillRate::once_per(Duration::from_secs(1)),
17265            control.effective_rate(),
17266            "precondition: a degraded report is the stream's only producer"
17267        );
17268
17269        assert!(control.enter_drain());
17270        control.set_degraded(true);
17271        assert_eq!(
17272            FillRate::ZERO,
17273            control.effective_rate(),
17274            "a drain silences the notification, and a degraded switch must not bring it back"
17275        );
17276        control.set_degraded(false);
17277        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, control.effective_rate());
17278    }
17279
17280    /// A degraded mode switch changes nothing about fill, and nothing about what the notification is.
17281    ///
17282    /// Fill above the notification rate is still classified as fill in either mode, still bounded by
17283    /// the reserve, and a withheld notification still keeps its slot.
17284    #[test]
17285    fn the_degraded_period_leaves_fill_and_withholding_alone() {
17286        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17287        // One SURB, far below the reserve: only a notification may spend it.
17288        let control = fill_control_degraded(None, Some(Duration::from_secs(1)), RESERVE, 1);
17289        control.start_notify();
17290        // No notification period at all, so the degraded one cannot be what runs: the period helper
17291        // falls back to the normal one, which is absent.
17292        assert_eq!(None, control.period(&control.state.lock()));
17293        assert_eq!(FillRate::ZERO, control.effective_rate());
17294
17295        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(Duration::from_secs(60)), Some(Duration::from_secs(1)), RESERVE, 1);
17296        control.start_notify();
17297        let t0 = Instant::now();
17298        assert!(control.admit_at(t0), "the notification is exempt from the reserve");
17299        assert!(!control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(10)), "fill is not");
17300
17301        // A fill running above the degraded period takes over the stream, as it does at the normal one.
17302        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
17303        control.set_degraded(true);
17304        assert_eq!(FillRate::per_second(10), control.effective_rate());
17305        control.set_degraded(false);
17306        assert_eq!(FillRate::per_second(10), control.effective_rate());
17307    }
17308
17309    /// The driver's rule: loss, a reader, and a stock above the reserve — all three, every time.
17310    #[test]
17311    fn the_degraded_rule_needs_loss_a_reader_and_a_stock_above_the_reserve() {
17312        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
17313
17314        let signal = FrameLossSignal::new();
17315        let state = BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
17316            target_surb_buffer_size: 10_000,
17317            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
17318            ..Default::default()
17319        });
17320        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
17321        let reserve = current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&state);
17322        assert!(reserve > 0);
17323
17324        // No loss yet, everything else in place.
17325        state.note_counterparty_refills();
17326        estimator.produced.fetch_add(reserve + 1, Relaxed);
17327        assert!(
17328            !exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &estimator, &state, false),
17329            "a whole forward path has nothing to report faster about"
17330        );
17331
17332        // Loss, but the Entry reads nothing: one report a second to it would spend SURBs for nothing.
17333        signal.record();
17334        let unread = BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
17335            target_surb_buffer_size: 10_000,
17336            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
17337            ..Default::default()
17338        });
17339        assert!(
17340            !exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &estimator, &unread, false),
17341            "an Entry that has not shown it refills has no reader for the report"
17342        );
17343
17344        // Loss and a reader, but the stock is at the reserve: the budget is spent.
17345        let at_reserve = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
17346        at_reserve.produced.fetch_add(reserve, Relaxed);
17347        assert!(
17348            !exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &at_reserve, &state, false),
17349            "at the reserve the normal period is what the Exit can afford"
17350        );
17351
17352        // All three.
17353        assert!(
17354            exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &estimator, &state, false),
17355            "loss, a reader and a stock above the reserve is a degraded forward path"
17356        );
17357
17358        // And the loss ages out of the hold, which is what returns the Session to its normal period.
17359        std::thread::sleep(SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD * 2);
17360        assert!(
17361            !exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &estimator, &state, false),
17362            "a loss older than the hold is not a degraded forward path"
17363        );
17364    }
17365
17366    /// Frames that stall degrade the forward path before any of them is lost.
17367    ///
17368    /// A loss is known only once a frame times out, seconds into an outage. Segments of two frames with
17369    /// neither completing is the same dark forward path, and it counts once it has lasted
17370    /// [`SURB_DEGRADED_STALL`]. A frame that completes ends it.
17371    #[test]
17372    fn stalled_frames_degrade_the_forward_path_before_any_is_lost() {
17373        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
17374
17375        let signal = FrameLossSignal::new();
17376        let state = BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
17377            target_surb_buffer_size: 10_000,
17378            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
17379            ..Default::default()
17380        });
17381        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
17382        state.note_counterparty_refills();
17383        estimator
17384            .produced
17385            .fetch_add(current_keep_alive_surb_reserve(&state) + 1, Relaxed);
17386        let mut switch = DegradedSwitch::default();
17387        let mut degraded_at = |now: Instant| {
17388            let recently_stalled = switch.note_stall(signal.stalled_for(SURB_DEGRADED_STALL), now);
17389            exit_forward_path_is_degraded(&signal, &estimator, &state, recently_stalled)
17390        };
17391
17392        signal.segment_received(1);
17393        signal.segment_received(2);
17394        assert!(!degraded_at(Instant::now()), "two frames under way are not a stall yet");
17395
17396        std::thread::sleep(SURB_DEGRADED_STALL + Duration::from_millis(50));
17397        let stalled_at = Instant::now();
17398        assert!(
17399            degraded_at(stalled_at),
17400            "segments of two frames and none completing for the stall time is a degraded forward path"
17401        );
17402        assert_eq!(0, signal.lost_total(), "and no frame has been lost yet");
17403
17404        // A frame gets through now and then on a forward path that is still mostly dark: the stall ends
17405        // with it, and the Session stays degraded for the hold, as after a loss.
17406        signal.frame_completed();
17407        assert!(
17408            degraded_at(stalled_at + SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD),
17409            "a stall counts for the hold after it was last seen"
17410        );
17411        assert!(
17412            !degraded_at(stalled_at + SURB_DEGRADED_HOLD + Duration::from_millis(1)),
17413            "after the hold, with no loss and no stall, the path is whole again"
17414        );
17415    }
17416
17417    /// The level notification is not sent on a SURB the Session does not have.
17418    ///
17419    /// A return packet that finds none is held by the routing resolver for the whole of
17420    /// `surb_resolution_wait`, and every packet this node originates with it. The decision reads the
17421    /// estimate, so SURBs that were spent do not count.
17422    #[test]
17423    fn a_level_notification_waits_for_a_surb_to_send_it_on() {
17424        use std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed;
17425
17426        let period = Duration::from_secs(3600);
17427        let control = fill_control(Some(period), 100);
17428        control.start_notify();
17429
17430        let now = Instant::now();
17431        assert!(
17432            !control.admit_at(now),
17433            "an empty estimate has no SURB to send the notification on"
17434        );
17435
17436        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(2, Relaxed);
17437        assert!(control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(1)));
17438
17439        // A period on, the two SURBs have been spent.
17440        control.estimator.consumed.fetch_add(2, Relaxed);
17441        assert!(
17442            !control.admit_at(now + period),
17443            "SURBs already spent are not SURBs to send on"
17444        );
17445
17446        control.estimator.produced.fetch_add(1, Relaxed);
17447        assert!(
17448            control.admit_at(now + period + Duration::from_millis(1)),
17449            "the notification keeps its slot until there is a SURB for it"
17450        );
17451    }
17452
17453    /// A notification that is due and withheld is not let through as fill.
17454    ///
17455    /// The packet is the same either way, and a withheld notification would otherwise fall through to
17456    /// the reserve check. Above the reserve that check admits, so a Session with no Entry reading its
17457    /// reports would send one every period, labelled as fill. While a fill is running, the packet is
17458    /// fill and meets the reserve like any other, but it is not counted as the notification.
17459    #[test]
17460    fn a_withheld_level_notification_is_not_let_through_as_fill() {
17461        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17462        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
17463        let control = fill_control_for(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), RESERVE, surb_mgmt.clone());
17464        control.start_notify();
17465        // Far above the reserve, so a packet classified as fill would be admitted.
17466        control
17467            .estimator
17468            .produced
17469            .fetch_add(10 * RESERVE, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17470
17471        let now = Instant::now();
17472        for n in 0..3 {
17473            assert!(
17474                !control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(n)),
17475                "with no fill running there is nothing for a withheld notification to be mistaken for"
17476            );
17477        }
17478        assert!(
17479            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(),
17480            "a withheld notification has not been sent, and keeps its slot"
17481        );
17482
17483        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
17484        assert!(
17485            control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(3)),
17486            "while a fill runs the packet is fill, and the estimate is above the reserve"
17487        );
17488        assert!(
17489            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(),
17490            "fill that took the notification's slot did not send the notification"
17491        );
17492
17493        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
17494        assert!(control.admit_at(now + Duration::from_millis(4)));
17495        assert!(
17496            control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_some(),
17497            "once the Entry is heard the notification is sent in its own right"
17498        );
17499    }
17500
17501    /// While degraded, a notification is due a tenth of the period early, and in normal mode half of it.
17502    ///
17503    /// The slack is what keeps the classification from resting on scheduling latency. At the one-second
17504    /// degraded period a half-period slack would make the notification due 500 ms after the last, so a
17505    /// degraded Session with fill running would report about twice a second. The stock is one SURB against a
17506    /// reserve of a hundred, so only a notification is admitted, which makes admission the instrument.
17507    #[test]
17508    fn the_degraded_notification_is_due_a_tenth_of_a_period_early_and_the_normal_one_half() {
17509        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17510        let degraded = Duration::from_secs(1);
17511        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)), Some(degraded), RESERVE, 1);
17512        control.start_notify();
17513        let t0 = Instant::now();
17514        assert!(control.admit_at(t0));
17515
17516        // The notification is exempt from the reserve and the stock stays one, so each of these is decided
17517        // by the classification alone.
17518        control.set_degraded(true);
17519        assert!(
17520            !control.admit_at(t0 + degraded / 2),
17521            "half a degraded period after the last report is not yet due: fill must not pass for it"
17522        );
17523        assert!(
17524            !control.admit_at(t0 + degraded - degraded / 10 - Duration::from_millis(1)),
17525            "nor is anything short of the tenth-of-a-period slack"
17526        );
17527        assert!(
17528            control.admit_at(t0 + degraded - degraded / 10),
17529            "at a tenth of the period before it is up, the next packet is the notification"
17530        );
17531
17532        // Normal mode keeps today's slack, `min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 2)`.
17533        let period = Duration::from_secs(1);
17534        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(period), Some(Duration::from_secs(1)), RESERVE, 1);
17535        control.start_notify();
17536        assert!(control.admit_at(t0));
17537        assert!(!control.admit_at(t0 + period / 2 - Duration::from_millis(1)));
17538        assert!(
17539            control.admit_at(t0 + period / 2),
17540            "outside degraded mode the slack is still half of a one-second period"
17541        );
17542    }
17543
17544    /// A notification withheld while degraded keeps its slot, exactly as it does in normal mode.
17545    ///
17546    /// Without a reader, or with an estimate of zero, a due notification is not sent and not mistaken for
17547    /// fill; the next packet to ask is the notification and goes out as soon as both hold, not a degraded
17548    /// period later.
17549    #[test]
17550    fn a_degraded_notification_withheld_for_a_reader_or_a_stock_keeps_its_slot() {
17551        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17552        let degraded = Duration::from_secs(1);
17553        let control_over = |surb_mgmt: Arc<BalancerStateValues>| {
17554            let control = PixFillControl::new(
17555                HoprPseudonym::random(),
17556                RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
17557                Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)),
17558                Some(degraded),
17559                SurbReserveBasis {
17560                    configured: RESERVE,
17561                    establishment_target: RESERVE.saturating_mul(4),
17562                },
17563                Default::default(),
17564                surb_mgmt,
17565            );
17566            control.start_notify();
17567            control.set_degraded(true);
17568            control
17569        };
17570        let produce = |control: &PixFillControl, n: u64| {
17571            control
17572                .estimator
17573                .produced
17574                .fetch_add(n, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
17575        };
17576
17577        // No reader: SURBs to send on, but nobody reads the report.
17578        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
17579        let control = control_over(surb_mgmt.clone());
17580        produce(&control, 10);
17581        let t0 = Instant::now();
17582        for n in 0..3 {
17583            assert!(
17584                !control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(n)),
17585                "no reader: the due notification is withheld, and not passed as fill"
17586            );
17587        }
17588        assert!(control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(), "it kept its slot");
17589        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
17590        assert!(
17591            control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(3)),
17592            "once the Entry is heard the withheld notification goes out at once, not a degraded period later"
17593        );
17594        assert!(
17595            !control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(4)),
17596            "and having gone out it was the notification: the next packet is fill, below the reserve"
17597        );
17598
17599        // A reader, but no SURB to send the report on.
17600        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
17601        surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
17602        let control = control_over(surb_mgmt);
17603        for n in 0..3 {
17604            assert!(
17605                !control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(n)),
17606                "an estimate of zero has no SURB to send the notification on"
17607            );
17608        }
17609        assert!(control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_none(), "it kept its slot");
17610        produce(&control, 1);
17611        assert!(
17612            control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(3)),
17613            "as soon as there is a SURB the withheld notification goes out"
17614        );
17615        assert!(control.state.lock().last_notify_at.is_some());
17616    }
17617
17618    /// While the degraded forward path is dark, the notification runs at [`SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD`]; dark alone,
17619    /// without degradation or without a degraded period configured, changes nothing.
17620    #[test]
17621    fn a_dark_forward_path_reports_at_the_dark_cadence_only_while_degraded() {
17622        const RESERVE: u64 = 100;
17623        let normal = Duration::from_secs(15);
17624        let degraded = Duration::from_secs(1);
17625        let control = fill_control_degraded(Some(normal), Some(degraded), RESERVE, 1);
17626        control.start_notify();
17627
17628        control.set_dark(true);
17629        assert_eq!(
17630            FillRate::once_per(normal),
17631            control.effective_rate(),
17632            "dark without degradation is not a cadence"
17633        );
17634
17635        control.set_degraded(true);
17636        assert_eq!(FillRate::once_per(SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD), control.effective_rate());
17637        let t0 = Instant::now();
17638        assert!(control.admit_at(t0), "the first packet is the notification");
17639        let slack = SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD / 10;
17640        assert!(
17641            !control.admit_at(t0 + SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD - slack - Duration::from_millis(1)),
17642            "the next is due a dark period later, less a tenth of it"
17643        );
17644        assert!(control.admit_at(t0 + SURB_DARK_NOTIFY_PERIOD));
17645
17646        control.set_dark(false);
17647        assert_eq!(
17648            FillRate::once_per(degraded),
17649            control.effective_rate(),
17650            "a degraded path that is no longer dark reports at the degraded period"
17651        );
17652
17653        let without = fill_control_degraded(Some(normal), None, RESERVE, 1);
17654        without.start_notify();
17655        without.set_degraded(true);
17656        without.set_dark(true);
17657        assert_eq!(
17658            FillRate::once_per(normal),
17659            without.effective_rate(),
17660            "with the degraded period switched off there is no faster cadence to have"
17661        );
17662    }

17664    /// The driver tells the stream about a change of darkness, and only about a change, as for degradation.
17665    #[test]
17666    fn the_driver_switches_the_dark_cadence_only_on_transitions() {
17667        let mut switch = DegradedSwitch::default();
17668        let polled = [false, true, true, false, false, true];
17669        let acted: Vec<Option<bool>> = polled.iter().map(|next| switch.change_dark_to(*next)).collect();
17670        assert_eq!(vec![None, Some(true), None, Some(false), None, Some(true)], acted);

17674    /// The Exit's keep-alive schedule, as a table: for each way of producing keep-alives, which of a
17675    /// few instants (milliseconds after the first) admit a packet.
17676    ///
17677    /// Columns: the notification period, the degraded period, the SURB stock, the fill reserve, whether
17678    /// fill runs, and whether the Session is degraded and dark.
17679    #[rstest]
17680    #[case::level_reports_only(
17681        Some(10_000), None, 1, 100, false, (false, false),
17682        &[(0, true), (1_000, false), (10_000, true), (11_000, false)],
17683    )]
17684    #[case::fill_only(
17685        None, None, 5, 5, true, (false, false),
17686        &[(0, true), (1, true), (1_000, true)],
17687    )]
17688    #[case::reports_only_below_the_fill_reserve(
17689        Some(10_000), None, 1, 5, true, (false, false),
17690        &[(0, true), (1_000, false), (10_000, true), (10_500, false)],
17691    )]
17692    #[case::degraded_period(
17693        Some(3_600_000), Some(10_000), 1, 100, false, (true, false),
17694        &[(0, true), (1_000, false), (10_000, true), (11_000, false)],
17695    )]
17696    #[case::dark_period(
17697        Some(15_000), Some(1_000), 1, 100, false, (true, true),
17698        &[(0, true), (50, false), (100, true), (150, false)],
17699    )]
17700    #[case::nothing_without_surbs(
17701        Some(10_000), None, 0, 5, true, (false, false),
17702        &[(0, false), (1_000, false), (10_000, false)],
17703    )]
17704    fn the_exit_keep_alive_schedule_admits_the_expected_packets(
17705        #[case] notify_ms: Option<u64>,
17706        #[case] degraded_ms: Option<u64>,
17707        #[case] stock: u64,
17708        #[case] reserve: u64,
17709        #[case] fill: bool,
17710        #[case] (degraded, dark): (bool, bool),
17711        #[case] timeline: &[(u64, bool)],
17712    ) {
17713        let control = fill_control_degraded(
17714            notify_ms.map(Duration::from_millis),
17715            degraded_ms.map(Duration::from_millis),
17716            reserve,
17717            stock,
17718        );
17719        control.start_notify();
17720        if fill {
17721            control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
17722        }
17723        control.set_degraded(degraded);
17724        control.set_dark(dark);
17725
17726        let t0 = Instant::now();
17727        for (offset_ms, admitted) in timeline {
17728            assert_eq!(
17729                *admitted,
17730                control.admit_at(t0 + Duration::from_millis(*offset_ms)),
17731                "at +{offset_ms} ms"
17732            );
17733        }
17734    }

17736    /// The driver tells the stream about a change in its answer, and only about a change.
17737    #[test]
17738    fn the_driver_acts_only_on_transitions() {

17740        let polled = [false, false, true, true, true, false, true, false, false];
17741        let acted: Vec<Option<bool>> = polled.iter().map(|next| switch.change_to(*next)).collect();
17742        assert_eq!(
17743            vec![
17744                None,
17745                None,
17746                Some(true),
17747                None,
17748                None,
17749                Some(false),
17750                Some(true),
17751                Some(false),
17752                None
17753            ],
17754            acted,
17755            "a repeated answer is not an action, and every change is one"
17756        );

17759    /// The reserve is a ceiling on a figure derived from the buffer the *Entry* asked for.
17760    ///
17761    /// The configured value is an absolute SURB count, while the buffer it is compared against is
17762    /// sized by the peer. Left absolute, a PIX Session whose Entry targets fewer SURBs than the
17763    /// reserve could never be filled at all — every fill packet withheld, the funded cycle stranded on
17764    /// `max_recovery_time`, and nothing in the logs but a backoff.
17765    #[test]
17766    fn the_fill_surb_reserve_is_capped_at_a_quarter_of_the_entrys_announced_buffer() {
17767        // The shipped reserve against the worked profile's buffer: the configured value binds and the
17768        // derivation is inert, which is what keeps this from quietly weakening production.
17769        assert_eq!(500, effective_surb_reserve(500, 7_000));
17770        // Exactly four times the reserve is the point at which the two agree.
17771        assert_eq!(500, effective_surb_reserve(500, 2_000));
17772
17773        // Below that, the Entry's buffer is what decides. The cluster fixtures' 64-SURB target is the
17774        // case this exists for.
17775        assert_eq!(16, effective_surb_reserve(500, 64));
17776        assert_eq!(12, effective_surb_reserve(500, 50));
17777
17778        // Never zero: an Entry announcing a buffer of three would otherwise let fill spend the
17779        // Session's last SURB, which is the one failure the reserve exists to prevent.
17780        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(500, 3));
17781        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(500, 0));
17782        assert_eq!(1, effective_surb_reserve(0, 7_000));
17783    }
17784
17785    /// An Exit-side slot with a fill control, set up the way `spawn_exit_keep_alive` sets it up.
17786    ///
17787    /// The reserve is derived at establishment from `announced`, against `configured_reserve` as the
17788    /// ceiling — exactly the figures `handle_keep_alive` then re-derives from. A rate-controlled
17789    /// Session's balancer starts at the announced target too, which is the value a `BalancerTarget`
17790    /// keep-alive is compared against to decide whether the target actually changed.
17791    fn exit_slot_with_fill_control(
17792        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
17793        announced: u64,
17794        configured_reserve: u64,
17795    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Arc<PixFillControl>)> {
17796        let mgr =
17797            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
17798                // Wide enough that the announcements below are not clamped by it.
17799                maximum_surb_buffer_size: MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS,
17800                ..Default::default()
17801            });
17802        let estimator = AtomicSurbFlowEstimator::default();
17803        let surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::new(SurbBalancerConfig {
17804            target_surb_buffer_size: announced,
17805            ..Default::default()
17806        }));
17807        let control = Arc::new(PixFillControl::new(
17808            pseudonym,
17809            RateController::new(0, Duration::from_secs(1)),
17810            Some(Duration::from_secs(3600)),
17811            None,
17812            SurbReserveBasis {
17813                configured: configured_reserve,
17814                establishment_target: announced,
17815            },
17816            estimator.clone(),
17817            surb_mgmt.clone(),
17818        ));
17819        let fill = Arc::new(OnceLock::new());
17820        anyhow::ensure!(
17821            fill.set(control.clone()).is_ok(),
17822            "fixture: the fill control is installed once"
17823        );
17824
17825        let (dummy_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
17826        mgr.sessions.insert(
17827            pseudonym,
17828            SessionSlot {
17829                session_tx: dummy_tx,
17830                routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(pseudonym)),
17831                abort_handles: Default::default(),
17832                surb_mgmt,
17833                surb_estimator: estimator,
17834                current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
17835                pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
17836                pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
17837                pix_fill: fill,
17838                exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
17839                returned_packets: Default::default(),
17840                cycle_budget: None,
17841                admission_token: Default::default(),
17842                raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
17843                forward_receipts: None,
17844                exit_resume: Default::default(),
17845                instance: SlotInstance::new(0),
17846                opening: None,
17847            },
17848        );
17849        Ok((mgr, control))
17850    }
17851
17852    /// A keep-alive from the Entry that announces `target` as its SURB buffer target.
17853    fn keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, target: u64) -> KeepAliveMessage<SessionId> {
17854        KeepAliveMessage::<SessionId> {
17855            session_id: pseudonym,
17856            flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
17857            additional_data: target,
17858        }
17859    }
17860
17861    /// A raised target must raise the fill reserve with it.
17862    ///
17863    /// The reserve is derived at establishment from the target the Entry announced then, and the
17864    /// Entry can change that target later. Left at the establishment figure it is far too shallow for
17865    /// a Session whose Entry stepped up to a deeper buffer: at 200 the reserve is 50, and an Entry
17866    /// that moves to 7 000 keeps 500.
17867    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17868    async fn a_raised_target_raises_the_fill_reserve() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17869        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17870        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 200, 500)?;
17871
17872        anyhow::ensure!(
17873            control.surb_reserve() == 50,
17874            "fixture: a 200-SURB target has a fill reserve of 50, not {}",
17875            control.surb_reserve()
17876        );
17877
17878        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 7_000))
17879            .await
17880            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
17881
17882        assert_eq!(
17883            500,
17884            control.surb_reserve(),
17885            "a target raised to 7 000 must move the reserve to a quarter of it, capped at the configured 500"
17886        );
17887        Ok(())
17888    }
17889
17890    /// A lowered target must lower the fill reserve too, unlike the SURB ring, which only widens.
17891    ///
17892    /// A reserve above what the Entry now supplies is never reached by the estimate, so every fill
17893    /// packet is withheld and the funded cycle strands on `max_recovery_time` — the exact failure the
17894    /// derivation exists to prevent.
17895    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17896    async fn a_lowered_target_lowers_the_fill_reserve() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17897        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17898        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 7_000, 500)?;
17899
17900        anyhow::ensure!(
17901            control.surb_reserve() == 500,
17902            "fixture: a 7 000-SURB target has a fill reserve of 500, not {}",
17903            control.surb_reserve()
17904        );
17905
17906        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 400))
17907            .await
17908            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
17909
17910        assert_eq!(
17911            100,
17912            control.surb_reserve(),
17913            "a target lowered to 400 must move the reserve to a quarter of it, not leave it at the establishment 500"
17914        );
17915        Ok(())
17916    }
17917
17918    /// A lowered target lowers the fill reserve on a `NoRateControl` Session too.
17919    ///
17920    /// Such a Session runs no balancer on the Exit, so there is no set-point to move and the ring is
17921    /// widened by a monotone `fetch_max` — a lower announcement is not a raise and the ring ignores it
17922    /// entirely. The reserve must not inherit that asymmetry: it has to follow the target down, or it
17923    /// sits above what the Entry now supplies, the estimate never reaches it, and every fill packet is
17924    /// withheld until the funded cycle strands on `max_recovery_time`. This is the issue's lowered-target
17925    /// case, on the side that has no balancer to notice it.
17926    ///
17927    /// The raise comes first and is not decoration: the ring's recorded figure is what the raise-only
17928    /// guard compares a later announcement against, so without it a first announcement of any size
17929    /// passes the guard and the lowered case would be masked.
17930    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
17931    async fn a_lowered_target_lowers_the_fill_reserve_without_rate_control() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
17932        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
17933        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 200, 500)?;
17934        // `NoRateControl` is a capability of the Session, not of the slot: the disable comes from the
17935        // balancer state, which `spawn_exit_keep_alive` leaves at zero for such a Session.
17936        let mut slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
17937        slot.surb_mgmt = Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::default());
17938        anyhow::ensure!(
17939            slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled(),
17940            "fixture: a NoRateControl Exit runs no balancer, so its state holds no target"
17941        );
17942        mgr.sessions.insert(pseudonym, slot);
17943
17944        anyhow::ensure!(
17945            control.surb_reserve() == 50,
17946            "fixture: a 200-SURB target has a fill reserve of 50, not {}",
17947            control.surb_reserve()
17948        );
17949
17950        // The Entry steps up to its main tier: the ring records 7 000 and the reserve follows.
17951        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 7_000))
17952            .await
17953            .context("the raised keep-alive must be handled")?;
17954        anyhow::ensure!(
17955            control.surb_reserve() == 500,
17956            "fixture: the raise must have moved the reserve to 500, got {}",
17957            control.surb_reserve()
17958        );
17959
17960        // And back down, below where the ring's monotone figure can compare: the ring keeps 7 000,
17961        // the reserve must still follow the Entry to 400.
17962        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 400))
17963            .await
17964            .context("the lowered keep-alive must be handled")?;
17965
17966        assert_eq!(
17967            100,
17968            control.surb_reserve(),
17969            "a target lowered to 400 must move the reserve to a quarter of it, with no balancer to compare against"
17970        );
17971        Ok(())
17972    }

17977        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();

17989        for _ in 0..3 {

18002    /// Before any announcement the reserve is the establishment one, and a repeat of it leaves it so.
18003    ///
18004    /// The establishment figure is the target in force at establishment — the Entry's announcement,
18005    /// or the node's fallback when it made none. Nothing records it as "announced", so the control
18006    /// derives it until a keep-alive says otherwise; a keep-alive repeating it must be a no-op, which
18007    /// is what keeps a regular announcer from re-deriving — and re-warning — on every packet.
18008    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18009    async fn a_first_announcement_of_the_establishment_target_changes_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18010        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18011        // Establishment at 7 000 against a configured 500: the ceiling binds, so the reserve is 500.
18012        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 7_000, 500)?;
18013        anyhow::ensure!(
18014            control.surb_reserve() == 500,
18015            "fixture: establishment at 7 000 must give a reserve of 500, got {}",
18016            control.surb_reserve()
18017        );
18018
18019        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 7_000))
18020            .await
18021            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
18022
18023        assert_eq!(
18024            500,
18025            control.surb_reserve(),
18026            "a keep-alive repeating the establishment target must leave the reserve where establishment put it"
18027        );
18028        Ok(())
18029    }

18119    /// The order-of-magnitude warning is latched, so an Entry alternating targets cannot set its rate.
18120    ///
18121    /// The target is peer-controlled and arrives on a keep-alive the Entry sends as often as it likes.
18122    /// Warning on every downward crossing would let it log at will for the Session's four hours; the
18123    /// latch makes it one line per Session, and only when a warning actually goes out.
18124    ///
18125    /// Counted at the subscriber rather than read off the latch: a regression that warned on every
18126    /// crossing and set the flag as well would leave the flag looking exactly as it does here.
18127    #[test]
18128    fn the_order_of_magnitude_warning_is_latched() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18129        const CONFIGURED: u64 = 500;
18130        // The establishment reserve is 500, above the threshold, so 180 (reserve 45) is a crossing.
18131        // `fill_control` derives its establishment target from the reserve, so the field is set here.
18132        let mut control = fill_control(None, CONFIGURED);
18133        control.reserve_basis.establishment_target = 7_000;
18134        anyhow::ensure!(
18135            control.surb_reserve() == 500,
18136            "fixture: the establishment reserve must be 500, got {}",
18137            control.surb_reserve()
18138        );
18139
18140        // Alternating across the threshold, deep then shallow, twenty times over: one warning in all.
18141        let warnings = Arc::new(WarnCounter::default());
18142        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || {
18143            for _ in 0..20 {
18144                control.set_announced_target(7_000);
18145                control.set_announced_target(180);
18146            }
18147        });
18148        assert_eq!(
18149            1,
18150            warnings.count(),
18151            "an Entry alternating across the threshold must produce exactly one warning per Session"
18152        );
18153
18154        // A fresh control that only repeated its target has not warned, so a later crossing still does.
18155        let mut fresh = fill_control(None, CONFIGURED);
18156        fresh.reserve_basis.establishment_target = 7_000;
18157        let warnings = Arc::new(WarnCounter::default());
18158        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || fresh.set_announced_target(7_000));
18159        assert_eq!(
18160            0,
18161            warnings.count(),
18162            "a repeat of the target in force is not a crossing, so it must not warn"
18163        );
18164        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || {
18165            fresh.set_announced_target(180);
18166            fresh.set_announced_target(7_000);
18167            fresh.set_announced_target(180);
18168        });
18169        assert_eq!(
18170            1,
18171            warnings.count(),
18172            "the first real crossing must warn, and the next one must not"
18173        );
18174        Ok(())
18175    }
18176
18177    /// A lowering that starts under the order-of-magnitude threshold crosses nothing, so it stays quiet.
18178    ///
18179    /// Established at 180 against a configured 500, the reserve starts at 45, under the threshold of 50,
18180    /// and the establishment warning has already said so. Warning again at 160 (reserve 40) would say
18181    /// nothing new and spend the latch, so a later real crossing would go unreported.
18182    #[test]
18183    fn a_lowering_already_under_the_threshold_does_not_warn() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18184        const CONFIGURED: u64 = 500;
18185        let mut control = fill_control(None, CONFIGURED);
18186        control.reserve_basis.establishment_target = 180;
18187        anyhow::ensure!(
18188            control.surb_reserve() == 45,
18189            "fixture: the establishment reserve must be 45, got {}",
18190            control.surb_reserve()
18191        );
18192
18193        let warnings = Arc::new(WarnCounter::default());
18194        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || control.set_announced_target(160));
18195        assert_eq!(
18196            0,
18197            warnings.count(),
18198            "a lowering from under the threshold is not a crossing, so it must not warn"
18199        );
18200
18201        // Back over the threshold and down through it: a real crossing, and the latch is still unspent.
18202        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || {
18203            control.set_announced_target(7_000);
18204            control.set_announced_target(180);
18205        });
18206        assert_eq!(
18207            1,
18208            warnings.count(),
18209            "the first crossing after a lowering under the threshold must warn"
18210        );
18211
18212        // From exactly at the threshold (200 derives 50) to under it (196 derives 49) is a crossing.
18213        let mut at_threshold = fill_control(None, CONFIGURED);
18214        at_threshold.reserve_basis.establishment_target = 200;
18215        let warnings = Arc::new(WarnCounter::default());
18216        tracing::subscriber::with_default(warnings.clone(), || at_threshold.set_announced_target(196));
18217        assert_eq!(
18218            1,
18219            warnings.count(),
18220            "a fall from the threshold itself to under it is a crossing and must warn"
18221        );
18222        Ok(())
18223    }
18224
18225    /// Counts `WARN` events; `enabled` is always true so the logging macros' bodies actually run.
18226    #[derive(Default)]
18227    struct WarnCounter(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64);
18228
18229    impl WarnCounter {
18230        fn count(&self) -> u64 {
18231            self.0.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
18232        }
18233    }
18234
18235    impl tracing::Subscriber for WarnCounter {
18236        fn enabled(&self, _: &tracing::Metadata<'_>) -> bool {
18237            true
18238        }
18239
18240        fn new_span(&self, _: &tracing::span::Attributes<'_>) -> tracing::span::Id {
18241            tracing::span::Id::from_u64(1)
18242        }
18243
18244        fn record(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Record<'_>) {}
18245
18246        fn record_follows_from(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
18247
18248        fn event(&self, event: &tracing::Event<'_>) {
18249            if *event.metadata().level() == tracing::Level::WARN {
18250                self.0.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
18251            }
18252        }
18253
18254        fn enter(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
18255
18256        fn exit(&self, _: &tracing::span::Id) {}
18257    }
18258
18259    /// An admitted drain keeps the reserve it was admitted against, whatever the Entry announces.
18260    ///
18261    /// The supervisor admits a drain once, against the `drainable_surbs` reported at the close, and
18262    /// the slot stays in place for the drain, so the Entry's keep-alives still reach
18263    /// `handle_keep_alive`. A raise followed there would have fill withhold the packets the drain was
18264    /// admitted to spend — 200 announced at establishment is a reserve of 50, and 7 000 afterwards
18265    /// would make it 500, above the 120 held — and the cycle would strand on its deadline. A lowering
18266    /// would spend past the figure the drain was planned against. Neither may move it.
18267    #[rstest]
18268    #[case::raised(7_000)]
18269    #[case::lowered(40)]
18270    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18271    async fn an_announcement_during_a_drain_leaves_the_fill_reserve_alone(
18272        #[case] announced: u64,
18273    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18274        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18275        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 200, 500)?;
18276        control
18277            .estimator
18278            .produced
18279            .fetch_add(120, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18280        anyhow::ensure!(
18281            control.drainable_surbs() == 70,
18282            "fixture: 120 held against a reserve of 50 leaves 70 drainable, got {}",
18283            control.drainable_surbs()
18284        );
18285
18286        anyhow::ensure!(control.enter_drain(), "fixture: the drain must begin");
18287        control.set_fill(FillRate::per_second(10));
18288
18289        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, announced))
18290            .await
18291            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
18292
18293        assert_eq!(
18294            50,
18295            control.surb_reserve(),
18296            "a target of {announced} announced during the drain must not move the reserve it was admitted against"
18297        );
18298        assert_eq!(
18299            70,
18300            control.drainable_surbs(),
18301            "the drain was planned against 70 drainable SURBs, and an announcement must not change that"
18302        );
18303        assert!(
18304            control.admit(),
18305            "with 120 held above the admitted reserve of 50, the drain's fill must still go out"
18306        );
18307        Ok(())
18308    }
18309
18310    /// The reserve follows the announced target down and up, and settles on the last one announced.
18311    ///
18312    /// The announcement tests above each check one move through the manager. This drives the control
18313    /// directly from several threads, which is the shape the real calls take — two keep-alives for one
18314    /// Session are handled as two tasks. It pins two things: that a finished round of announcements
18315    /// leaves the reserve derived from the last figure recorded, and that no announcement can leave a
18316    /// figure whose derived reserve is not what a read returns. The derive-at-read shape is what makes
18317    /// the second hold by construction, rather than by keeping two cells in step.
18318    ///
18319    /// A reader that samples the target and the reserve separately may see the two from either side of
18320    /// one announcement, which is why the per-sample check is against the figure read back, not against
18321    /// the last one written.
18322    #[test]
18323    fn the_announced_target_and_the_reserve_move_together() {
18324        const CONFIGURED: u64 = 500;
18325        let control = Arc::new(fill_control(None, CONFIGURED));
18326
18327        // Figures whose effective reserves differ, so a reserve derived from the wrong one is visible
18328        // rather than coincidentally equal.
18329        let announced: [u64; 6] = [200, 7_000, 400, 3, 2_000, 900];
18330        std::thread::scope(|scope| {
18331            for target in announced {
18332                let control = control.clone();
18333                scope.spawn(move || {
18334                    for _ in 0..2_000 {
18335                        control.set_announced_target(target);
18336                    }
18337                });
18338            }
18339        });
18340
18341        for target in announced {
18342            control.set_announced_target(target);
18343            assert_eq!(
18344                effective_surb_reserve(CONFIGURED, target),
18345                control.surb_reserve(),
18346                "a settled announcement of {target} must be the reserve a read returns"
18347            );
18348        }
18349
18350        // And what is left is the derivation of the last figure recorded, whichever thread wrote it.
18351        let last = control.announced_surb_target.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
18352        assert_eq!(
18353            effective_surb_reserve(CONFIGURED, last),
18354            control.surb_reserve(),
18355            "the reserve must be derived from the announcement the control holds ({last})"
18356        );
18357    }
18358
18359    /// A drain is planned against `drainable_surbs`, so that has to follow the reserve too.
18360    ///
18361    /// Otherwise a Session whose Entry raised its target reports less drainable than it could spend,
18362    /// and one whose Entry lowered it reports more than it should.
18363    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18364    async fn the_drainable_surbs_follow_the_announced_target() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18365        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18366        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 200, 500)?;
18367        control
18368            .estimator
18369            .produced
18370            .fetch_add(120, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18371
18372        anyhow::ensure!(
18373            control.drainable_surbs() == 70,
18374            "fixture: 120 held against a reserve of 50 leaves 70 drainable, got {}",
18375            control.drainable_surbs()
18376        );
18377
18378        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 7_000))
18379            .await
18380            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
18381        assert_eq!(
18382            0,
18383            control.drainable_surbs(),
18384            "with the reserve now 500, 120 held leaves nothing to drain"
18385        );
18386
18387        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 400))
18388            .await
18389            .context("the lowered keep-alive must be handled")?;
18390        assert_eq!(
18391            20,
18392            control.drainable_surbs(),
18393            "with the reserve now 100, 120 held leaves 20 to drain"
18394        );
18395        Ok(())
18396    }
18397
18398    /// A keep-alive on an outgoing Session is from the Exit, so it carries no Entry target to follow.
18399    ///
18400    /// A regression guard for the `Forward` arm rather than evidence of the bug: it also holds on the
18401    /// pre-fix code, which never re-derived the reserve at all. What it protects is the reach of the
18402    /// `Return`-only re-derivation — moving the reserve here would apply the Exit's own report to the
18403    /// Entry's buffer.
18404    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18405    async fn a_keep_alive_on_an_outgoing_session_leaves_the_fill_reserve_alone() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18406        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18407        let (mgr, control) = exit_slot_with_fill_control(pseudonym, 200, 500)?;
18408
18409        // The same slot, but as an Entry's own outgoing Session. The cache hands out clones, so the
18410        // changed slot has to go back in for the manager to see it.
18411        let mut slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
18412        slot.routing_opts = DestinationRouting::Forward {
18413            destination: Box::new(Address::from(&ChainKeypair::random()).into()),
18414            pseudonym: Some(pseudonym),
18415            forward_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(1.try_into()?),
18416            return_options: None,
18417        };
18418        mgr.sessions.insert(pseudonym, slot);
18419
18420        anyhow::ensure!(
18421            control.surb_reserve() == 50,
18422            "fixture: the reserve starts at 50, not {}",
18423            control.surb_reserve()
18424        );
18425
18426        mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive_announcing(pseudonym, 7_000))
18427            .await
18428            .context("the keep-alive must be handled")?;
18429
18430        assert_eq!(
18431            50,
18432            control.surb_reserve(),
18433            "an outgoing Session's keep-alive is the Exit's, and must not touch the Entry's fill reserve"
18434        );
18435        Ok(())
18436    }

18438    /// Test dimensions whose cycle is large enough to need a visible fill rate.
18439    ///
18440    /// [`small_pix_params`] is six packets, which any deadline covers at the heartbeat; these are
18441    /// three hundred, which against the fixture's 40 s recovery budget needs about eleven packets a
18442    /// second — far enough above the one-per-second notification for the two to be told apart.
18443    fn fill_pix_params() -> PixParams {
18444        PixParams::try_new(100, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE).expect("test dimensions must be valid")
18445    }
18446
18447    /// Brings up an Exit-side PIX Session, funds its first cycle, and returns once it is recovering.
18448    ///
18449    /// The Entry half is not simulated: the supervisor is a state machine, and driving it through
18450    /// `SsaRequestSent`, `CommitmentVerified` and `DepositConfirmed` puts its cycle in exactly the
18451    /// state a real commitment and deposit would — which is the state fill is planned from. What is
18452    /// real here is everything downstream of that: the action driver, the rate controller, the
18453    /// admission predicate and the stream.
18454    async fn recovering_exit_pix_session(
18455        capabilities: Capabilities,
18456        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
18457        fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig,
18458        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
18459    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Originated, HoprPseudonym)> {
18460        recovering_exit_pix_session_with(capabilities, notify_period, None, 0, fill, admission).await
18461    }
18462
18463    /// [`recovering_exit_pix_session`] with a degraded notification period and the SURB buffer target the Entry
18464    /// announces, which the keep-alive reserve of a rate-controlled Session is derived from.
18465    async fn recovering_exit_pix_session_with(
18466        capabilities: Capabilities,
18467        notify_period: Option<Duration>,
18468        degraded_notify_period: Option<Duration>,
18469        announced_target: u32,
18470        fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig,
18471        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
18472    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Originated, HoprPseudonym)> {
18473        let params = fill_pix_params();
18474        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
18475            surb_balance_notify_period: notify_period,
18476            surb_degraded_notify_period: degraded_notify_period,
18477            // The admission tests over this fixture wait out the deferred retire; a short window
18478            // keeps them fast without changing the seam they exercise.
18479            surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
18480            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
18481                quota_range: 0..=pix_params_to_quota(&params),
18482                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
18483                    // As short as a legal pair gets: the idle deadline must clear the reconstructor's
18484                    // 30 s acknowledgement window, and the hard deadline must exceed the idle one.
18485                    // That is what makes the required fill rate — a whole cycle over 75 % of 40 s,
18486                    // about eleven packets a second — observable inside a test-length window.
18487                    max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(31),
18488                    max_recovery_time: Duration::from_secs(40),
18489                    fill,
18490                    ..Default::default()
18491                },
18492                ..Default::default()
18493            },
18494            ..Default::default()
18495        });
18496
18497        if let Some(admission) = admission {
18498            assert!(
18499                mgr.set_surb_admission(admission),
18500                "a freshly constructed fixture manager must accept the SURB admission seam"
18501            );
18502        }
18503
18504        let (msg_tx, msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
18505        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
18506        mgr.start(
18507            msg_tx,
18508            new_session_tx,
18509            Some(pix_toolbox_with_pool(
18510                Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
18511                    polynomials_per_ssa: params.polys_per_ssa(),
18512                    threshold: params.shares_per_poly(),
18513                    surplus_shares: params.surplus_shares(),
18514                })),
18515                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
18516            )),
18517            None,
18518        )?;
18519
18520        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
18521        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
18522            pseudonym,
18523            StartInitiation {
18524                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
18525                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
18526                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities | Capability::UsePIX),
18527                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
18528                    params.into_additional_data(announced_target),
18529                    Duration::ZERO,
18530                ),
18531            },
18532        )
18533        .await?;
18534
18535        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
18536        let supervisor = slot
18537            .pix_supervisor
18538            .get()
18539            .context("an Exit-side PIX session must have a supervisor")?;
18540
18541        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
18542        for event in [
18543            SessionPixEvent::SsaRequestSent(ssa_id),
18544            SessionPixEvent::CommitmentVerified(ssa_id),
18545            SessionPixEvent::DepositConfirmed {
18546                ssa_id,
18547                amount: hopr_api::HoprBalance::new_base(1000),
18548            },
18549        ] {
18550            supervisor
18551                .send_event(event)
18552                .await
18553                .map_err(|()| anyhow::anyhow!("the supervisor stopped accepting events"))?;
18554        }
18555
18556        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, pseudonym))
18557    }
18558
18559    /// Counts the return-routed keep-alives `mgr` originated for `pseudonym` during `window`.
18560    async fn keep_alives_during(rx: &mut Originated, pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, window: Duration) -> usize {
18561        originated_during(rx, window)
18562            .await
18563            .iter()
18564            .filter(|(routing, data)| {
18565                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
18566                    && matches!(routing, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == pseudonym)
18567            })
18568            .count()
18569    }
18570
18571    /// A funded, idle PIX Session must be filled by the Exit at the rate its own deadline needs.
18572    ///
18573    /// This is the mechanism end to end on one node: the supervisor plans a rate, the action driver
18574    /// applies it to the shared keep-alive controller, the admission predicate lets the packets past,
18575    /// and they come out return-routed to the Entry. The floor asserted is deliberately the
18576    /// *notification* rate rather than the planned one — a regression that leaves the stream running
18577    /// at one packet a second is exactly the failure this exists to prevent, and it looks like
18578    /// success to any assertion that only checks the stream is alive.
