18579    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18580    async fn a_funded_idle_pix_session_is_filled_by_the_exit() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18581        let notify = Duration::from_secs(1);
18582        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
18583            Capabilities::empty(),
18584            Some(notify),
18585            // Draining off, so the trailing close below still means "the stream stopped at once".
18586            // What a drain does instead is the subject of the tests further down.
18587            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18588                min_surb_reserve: 1,
18589                drain_after_close: false,
18590                ..Default::default()
18591            },
18592            None,
18593        )
18594        .await?;
18595
18596        // SURBs to spend, so the reserve is not what this test is measuring.
18597        mgr.sessions
18598            .get(&pseudonym)
18599            .context("the session slot must exist")?
18600            .surb_estimator
18601            .produced
18602            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18603
18604        // One sampling interval for the planner, then a window long enough that the notification
18605        // alone could not account for what is counted.
18606        let _ramp = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
18607        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
18608        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18609
18610        // Counted against the rate the notification is *promoted* at rather than against the period,
18611        // for the reason `admit_at` documents: the classification window is one slack shorter than the
18612        // period, so a notification-only stream produces rather more than `window / period` packets.
18613        // Taking the period at face value here would set the floor too low and let a stream that had
18614        // stopped filling pass.
18615        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
18616        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
18617        assert!(
18618            observed > notify_only,
18619            "a funded idle cycle produced {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, which the {notify:?} SURB-level \
18620             notification alone could have produced ({notify_only}, one every {promote_every:?})"
18621        );
18622
18623        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
18624        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close of a filling PIX session").await;
18625        Ok(())
18626    }
18627
18628    /// A PIX Session enters and leaves degraded mode, reporting about once a second while it does, with its fill
18629    /// running throughout.
18630    ///
18631    /// The stock sits between the keep-alive reserve (32 for the 400-SURB target) and the fill reserve (100), so
18632    /// fill is planned and running but withheld, and the packets the stream puts out are the notifications alone:
18633    /// their count is the report rate. That is the regression this guards. The stream releases packets at the
18634    /// fill rate, any of which may be classified as the notification once one is due, so a due time of half a
18635    /// degraded period made a degraded PIX Session report twice a second. The window holds six degraded
18636    /// periods: the one-second cadence gives about six reports in it, the old slack gave eleven.
18637    ///
18638    /// Then the stock goes far above the fill reserve and fill must flow as before, degraded or not; and last,
18639    /// at the keep-alive reserve, the degraded reports stop on a PIX Session as on any other.
18640    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18641    async fn a_degraded_pix_session_reports_about_once_a_second_with_fill_running() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18642        let normal = Duration::from_secs(4);
18643        let period = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
18644        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session_with(
18645            Capability::Segmentation.into(),
18646            Some(normal),
18647            Some(period),
18648            400,
18649            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18650                min_surb_reserve: 500,
18651                drain_after_close: false,
18652                ..Default::default()
18653            },
18654            None,
18655        )
18656        .await?;
18657
18658        let (signal, control, estimator, g2, fill_reserve) = {
18659            let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
18660            let control = slot
18661                .pix_fill
18662                .get()
18663                .cloned()
18664                .context("a PIX session has a fill control")?;
18665            let target = slot
18666                .surb_mgmt
18667                .target_surb_buffer_size
18668                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18669            (
18670                slot.exit_loss_signal
18671                    .get()
18672                    .cloned()
18673                    .context("a PIX Session with a degraded period must publish a loss signal")?,
18674                control.clone(),
18675                slot.surb_estimator.clone(),
18676                keep_alive_surb_reserve(target),
18677                control.surb_reserve(),
18678            )
18679        };
18680        anyhow::ensure!(
18681            (g2, fill_reserve) == (32, 100),
18682            "fixture: a 400-SURB target has a keep-alive reserve of 32 and a fill reserve of 100, not ({g2}, \
18683             {fill_reserve})"
18684        );
18685
18686        // Stream on, then a reader, then the stock between the two reserves, and fill running.
18687        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
18688            while !control.notify_started() {
18689                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
18690            }
18691        })
18692        .await
18693        .context("the notification never started")?;
18694        show_exit_its_entry(
18695            &mgr,
18696            pseudonym,
18697            SimulatedEntry::Balancing {
18698                target_notify: false,
18699                surbs: ENTRY_SURBS,
18700            },
18701        )
18702        .await?;
18703        let stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, 60);
18704        timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
18705            while control.effective_rate().as_packets_per_sec() <= 1.0 {
18706                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
18707            }
18708        })
18709        .await
18710        .context("the supervisor never planned a fill rate, so fill is not running")?;
18711        let _ramp = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1_000)).await;
18712
18713        // Not degraded: the normal period, with fill running and withheld. One notification a promotion
18714        // interval (3.5 s), so two at most in four seconds.
18715        let window = Duration::from_secs(4);
18716        let calm = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18717        assert!(!control.is_degraded());
18718        assert!(
18719            calm <= 2,
18720            "a whole forward path reports at the normal period, {calm} keep-alive(s) in {window:?}"
18721        );
18722
18723        // Degraded: about one a second.
18724        let loss = lose_frames_continuously(signal.clone(), period / 4);
18725        let window = Duration::from_secs(6);
18726        let degraded = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18727        assert!(control.is_degraded(), "a PIX Session that loses frames goes degraded");
18728        assert!(
18729            (4..=8).contains(&degraded),
18730            "a degraded PIX Session with fill running reports about once a second: {degraded} keep-alive(s) in \
18731             {window:?} against the one-second period, where half-period slack gives eleven"
18732        );
18733
18734        // Fill is as before: above the fill reserve it flows at its planned rate, degraded.
18735        drop(stock);
18736        let stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, 10_000);
18737        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
18738        let window = Duration::from_millis(1_500);
18739        let filling = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18740        assert!(control.is_degraded());
18741        assert!(
18742            filling >= 8,
18743            "fill must flow at its own rate above its reserve while degraded: {filling} keep-alive(s) in {window:?}"
18744        );
18745
18746        // At the keep-alive reserve the degraded reports stop on a PIX Session too.
18747        drop(stock);
18748        let _stock = hold_stock_at(&estimator, g2);
18749        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
18750            while control.is_degraded() {
18751                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
18752            }
18753        })
18754        .await
18755        .context("a PIX Session at its keep-alive reserve stayed degraded")?;
18756        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
18757        let window = Duration::from_secs(3);
18758        let at_reserve = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18759        assert!(
18760            at_reserve <= 1,
18761            "at the keep-alive reserve a PIX Session reports at the normal period, {at_reserve} keep-alive(s) in \
18762             {window:?}"
18763        );
18764        drop(loss);
18765
18766        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
18767        Ok(())
18768    }
18769
18770    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
18771    // Draining a closed PIX Session
18772    // ---------------------------------------------------------------
18773
18774    /// A funded, filling Exit PIX Session whose SURB estimate covers the rest of its cycle.
18775    ///
18776    /// The 100 000 is not decoration: it is the estimate `begin_surb_drain` nets the reserve out of
18777    /// and hands the supervisor, and against [`fill_pix_params`]' 300-packet cycle it is what makes a
18778    /// drain admissible at all. The ramp is waited out for the reason
18779    /// [`exit_session_originating_keep_alives`] gives — silence after a close says nothing unless the
18780    /// stream was observably running before it.
18781    async fn drainable_exit_pix_session(
18782        notify_period: Duration,
18783        admission: Option<Arc<dyn SurbAdmissionControl>>,
18784    ) -> anyhow::Result<(RecordingManager, Originated, HoprPseudonym)> {
18785        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
18786            Capabilities::empty(),
18787            Some(notify_period),
18788            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18789                min_surb_reserve: 1,
18790                ..Default::default()
18791            },
18792            admission,
18793        )
18794        .await?;
18795
18796        mgr.sessions
18797            .get(&pseudonym)
18798            .context("the session slot must exist")?
18799            .surb_estimator
18800            .produced
18801            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18802
18803        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
18804        anyhow::ensure!(
18805            observed > 0,
18806            "the fixture's keep-alive stream never ran, so nothing below can tell a drain from a Session that was \
18807             silent all along"
18808        );
18809        Ok((mgr, msg_rx, pseudonym))
18810    }
18811
18812    /// A closed PIX Session goes on originating until the cycle it was paid for recovers.
18813    ///
18814    /// The deposit is stranded rather than refunded if the cycle does not complete, so a close that
18815    /// tore the stream down while the Exit still held enough SURBs to finish would throw away money
18816    /// both sides have already paid. What must *not* happen is the mirror image of that: origination
18817    /// continuing past the point it is buying anything. So the recovery is delivered and the slot has
18818    /// to be gone, and the stream silent, on the other side of it.
18819    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18820    async fn a_closed_pix_session_keeps_originating_until_its_cycle_recovers() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18821        let notify = Duration::from_secs(1);
18822        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = drainable_exit_pix_session(notify, None).await?;
18823
18824        assert!(
18825            mgr.close_session(&pseudonym),
18826            "a close that starts a drain is still a close that was handled"
18827        );
18828        assert!(
18829            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
18830            "the slot must survive the close — the drain runs out of it, and the supervisor's own teardown is what \
18831             removes it"
18832        );
18833
18834        // The SURB-level notification is switched off for the whole drain, so every packet counted
18835        // here is fill. The bar is nevertheless the notification-only figure, which keeps this
18836        // comparable with `a_funded_idle_pix_session_is_filled_by_the_exit` above.
18837        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
18838        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
18839        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
18840        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
18841        assert!(
18842            observed > notify_only,
18843            "a closed session with a full SURB buffer originated {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, which is \
18844             no more than the {notify_only} its (now silenced) notification would have accounted for"
18845        );
18846
18847        // Recovery is the end of the drain: there is nothing left to work for, so the Session must go.
18848        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
18849        mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id))
18850            .await?;
18851        assert!(
18852            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
18853            "a recovered cycle must end the drain and tear the Session down"
18854        );
18855        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a completed SURB drain").await;
18856        Ok(())
18857    }
18858
18859    /// A closed PIX Session with too few SURBs to finish is torn down as it always was.
18860    ///
18861    /// A hundred SURBs against [`fill_pix_params`]' 300-packet cycle: enough for the manager to offer
18862    /// the close to the supervisor, and not enough for the supervisor to take it. That is the
18863    /// arithmetic under test — draining on a buffer that runs out partway is strictly worse than not
18864    /// draining at all, since the SURBs are spent down to the reserve, the cycle recovers nothing,
18865    /// and every packet past the last useful one is return-routed on behalf of a Session that is gone.
18866    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18867    async fn a_closed_pix_session_without_enough_surbs_originates_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18868        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
18869            Capabilities::empty(),
18870            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
18871            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18872                min_surb_reserve: 1,
18873                ..Default::default()
18874            },
18875            None,
18876        )
18877        .await?;
18878
18879        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
18880        slot.surb_estimator
18881            .produced
18882            .fetch_add(100, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18883        // An Entry that has been heard, so that the notification is one of the packets that shows the
18884        // stream running before the close, as it was before it was held for a reader. It does not
18885        // depend on the supervisor's first plan, which fill does.
18886        slot.surb_mgmt.note_counterparty_refills();
18887        drop(slot);
18888        anyhow::ensure!(
18889            keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await > 0,
18890            "the stream must be running before the close for its absence afterwards to mean anything"
18891        );
18892
18893        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
18894        assert!(
18895            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
18896            "a drain the supervisor refuses must still tear the Session down"
18897        );
18898        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a close with too few SURBs to drain").await;
18899        Ok(())
18900    }
18901
18902    /// With `drain_after_close` off, every close path is what it was before draining existed.
18903    ///
18904    /// Including the part an operator would notice first: the slot is gone by the time
18905    /// `close_session` returns, rather than one channel hop later once the supervisor has answered.
18906    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18907    async fn a_closed_pix_session_with_draining_disabled_originates_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18908        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
18909            Capabilities::empty(),
18910            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
18911            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18912                min_surb_reserve: 1,
18913                drain_after_close: false,
18914                ..Default::default()
18915            },
18916            None,
18917        )
18918        .await?;
18919
18920        mgr.sessions
18921            .get(&pseudonym)
18922            .context("the session slot must exist")?
18923            .surb_estimator
18924            .produced
18925            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
18926        anyhow::ensure!(
18927            keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await > 0,
18928            "the fixture's keep-alive stream never ran"
18929        );
18930
18931        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
18932        assert!(
18933            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
18934            "with draining disabled the slot must be gone by the time the close returns"
18935        );
18936        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "an explicit close with draining disabled").await;
18937        Ok(())
18938    }
18939
18940    /// Closing a draining Session a second time forces the teardown.
18941    ///
18942    /// The drain is the Exit's decision, taken on the operator's behalf, and this is the operator's
18943    /// way to overrule it: a second `SessionManager::close_session` — or a peer `SessionError`, which
18944    /// arrives on the same path — stops the origination immediately rather than waiting out a cycle.
18945    /// The end-of-stream a close of our own ingress produces is deliberately *not* on this path; it
18946    /// carries `WriteClosed`/`EmptyRead` and is absorbed.
18947    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18948    async fn a_second_close_of_a_draining_session_tears_it_down() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18949        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = drainable_exit_pix_session(Duration::from_secs(1), None).await?;
18950
18951        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the first close starts the drain");
18952        assert!(
18953            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
18954            "the drain must be running for the second close to have anything to overrule"
18955        );
18956
18957        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the second close must find the session");
18958        assert!(
18959            mgr.active_sessions().is_empty(),
18960            "a second explicit close must remove the slot rather than let the drain run on"
18961        );
18962        assert_no_further_origination(&mut msg_rx, "a second explicit close of a draining session").await;
18963        Ok(())
18964    }
18965
18966    /// The same Session, with an Entry that reads its reports but supplies too few SURBs to fill with,
18967    /// must fall back to its SURB-level notification. Both kinds of Session do: the Exit's rule is the
18968    /// same with a balancer running (`rate_controlled`) and without one (`no_rate_control`).
18969    ///
18970    /// "No SURBs to spend" means below the reserve, which is the point at which fill stops: a few SURBs
18971    /// are still held, which is what the notification is sent on. A Session whose Entry has stopped
18972    /// supplying SURBs is the one case where filling harder is actively harmful: the packets cannot be
18973    /// routed, and an unroutable origination holds up every packet the node sends. What must survive is
18974    /// the notification, because it is the message that asks for the SURBs whose absence caused the
18975    /// backoff.
18976    #[rstest]
18977    #[case::rate_controlled(Capabilities::empty())]
18978    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::NoRateControl.into())]
18979    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
18980    async fn fill_backs_off_to_the_notification_when_the_entry_supplies_no_surbs(
18981        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
18982    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
18983        // At `MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD`, so it survives the clamp `SessionManager::new`
18984        // applies. A shorter value would be raised to this one anyway, and the bound below would then
18985        // be computed from a period that is not the one in effect.
18986        let notify = MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD;
18987        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
18988            capabilities,
18989            Some(notify),
18990            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
18991                min_surb_reserve: 500,
18992                ..Default::default()
18993            },
18994            None,
18995        )
18996        .await?;
18997        assert_eq!(
18998            Some(notify),
18999            mgr.cfg.surb_balance_notify_period,
19000            "the fixture's notification period must be the one the manager actually runs"
19001        );
19002
19003        // A balancing Entry has been heard, and it delivered a few SURBs: more than none, short of the
19004        // reserve. The reserve is the effective one, which the Entry's announced buffer lowers.
19005        dispatch_entry_keep_alive(&mgr, pseudonym, KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), 1, 0)?;
19006        wait_for_counterparty_refills(&mgr, &pseudonym).await?;
19007        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
19008        slot.surb_estimator
19009            .produced
19010            .fetch_add(6, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19011        let reserve = slot
19012            .pix_fill
19013            .get()
19014            .context("a PIX session has a fill control")?
19015            .surb_reserve();
19016        let held = slot.surb_estimator.saturating_diff();
19017        anyhow::ensure!(
19018            0 < held && held < reserve,
19019            "fixture: the Exit must hold some SURBs, but fewer than its reserve of {reserve}; it holds {held}"
19020        );
19021
19022        let _ramp = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
19023        let window = Duration::from_millis(1500);
19024        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, window).await;
19025
19026        // A notification is promoted every `period - min(MAX_WAIT_CHUNK, period / 2)`, not every
19027        // period: `admit_at` opens the window a slack early so the classification does not rest on the
19028        // rate limiter's scheduling latency. The ceiling has to be computed from that shorter interval,
19029        // or a stream doing exactly what this test permits would be read as filling.
19030        let promote_every = notify - MAX_WAIT_CHUNK.min(notify / 2);
19031        let notify_only = (window.as_secs_f64() / promote_every.as_secs_f64()).ceil() as usize;
19032        assert!(
19033            observed > 0,
19034            "the SURB-level notification must survive the backoff — it is what asks for the SURBs"
19035        );
19036        assert!(
19037            observed <= notify_only + 1,
19038            "with no SURBs to spend the Exit originated {observed} keep-alive(s) over {window:?}, against the \
19039             {notify_only} its notification alone accounts for at one every {promote_every:?}"
19040        );
19041
19042        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
19043        Ok(())
19044    }
19045
19046    /// An Exit that has not been heard to read its reports originates nothing while it is below its
19047    /// SURB reserve, not even the notification.
19048    ///
19049    /// The other half of the rule above. With no balancer on the Entry's side the notification has no
19050    /// reader, and fill, which the reserve holds back, is the only thing the Session is entitled to
19051    /// send. Both kinds of Session behave alike. Silence alone proves nothing, so the stock is then
19052    /// raised above the reserve and fill must flow: the stream was gated, not dead.
19053    #[rstest]
19054    #[case::rate_controlled(Capabilities::empty())]
19055    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::NoRateControl.into())]
19056    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19057    async fn a_pix_session_without_a_reader_below_its_reserve_originates_nothing(
19058        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
19059    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19060        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
19061            capabilities,
19062            Some(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_NOTIFICATION_PERIOD),
19063            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
19064                min_surb_reserve: 500,
19065                ..Default::default()
19066            },
19067            None,
19068        )
19069        .await?;
19070
19071        // Its SURBs arrived with data, and it has sent no keep-alive: no balancer to read a report.
19072        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
19073        slot.surb_estimator
19074            .produced
19075            .fetch_add(6, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19076        let reserve = slot
19077            .pix_fill
19078            .get()
19079            .context("a PIX session has a fill control")?
19080            .surb_reserve();
19081        anyhow::ensure!(
19082            6 < reserve && !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
19083            "fixture: below the reserve of {reserve}, with an Entry that has not been heard"
19084        );
19085
19086        // Long enough for the supervisor's first plan and for several periods of the notification.
19087        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(3_500)).await;
19088        assert_eq!(
19089            0, observed,
19090            "with nobody reading the reports and too few SURBs to fill with, the Exit originated {observed} \
19091             keep-alive(s)"
19092        );
19093
19094        slot.surb_estimator
19095            .produced
19096            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19097        let observed = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(2_000)).await;
19098        assert!(
19099            observed > 0,
19100            "the silence was the SURB reserve and not a dead stream: above it, fill must flow"
19101        );
19102
19103        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
19104        Ok(())
19105    }
19106
19107    /// A `NoRateControl` PIX Session must still have a SURB level estimate, or its reserve is a lie.
19108    ///
19109    /// That branch runs no balancer, and until now it wired no estimator either: `produced` and
19110    /// `consumed` both stayed at zero for the life of the Session. A reserve measured against that
19111    /// counter would refuse every fill packet forever — which is the branch that can drain SURBs
19112    /// fastest, so it is the one where getting it wrong costs most.
19113    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19114    async fn a_no_rate_control_pix_session_still_estimates_its_surb_level() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19115        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) = recovering_exit_pix_session(
19116            Capability::NoRateControl.into(),
19117            Some(Duration::from_secs(1)),
19118            crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
19119                min_surb_reserve: 1,
19120                ..Default::default()
19121            },
19122            None,
19123        )
19124        .await?;
19125
19126        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
19127        slot.surb_estimator
19128            .produced
19129            .fetch_add(100_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19130
19131        let _ = keep_alives_during(&mut msg_rx, pseudonym, Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
19132
19133        assert!(
19134            slot.surb_estimator.consumed.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) > 0,
19135            "a NoRateControl Session that has sent keep-alives must have counted them as consumed SURBs"
19136        );
19137
19138        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
19139        Ok(())
19140    }
19141
19142    /// An established Session must be admitted exactly once, and a teardown must retire it exactly
19143    /// once — while a SURB drain must retire nothing.
19144    ///
19145    /// This is the seam the SURB store's admission control hangs off (hoprnet#8515). Three properties
19146    /// are load-bearing and none is observable from the store alone:
19147    ///
19148    /// * **admit at establishment, not at allocation.** `handle_incoming_session_initiation` inserts the slot long
19149    ///   before the Start handshake completes; admitting there would put an unauthenticated peer into the store's
19150    ///   admitted class. Only the commit at the end of the Exit's establishment path counts, so the count below being
19151    ///   exactly one after the Session is live — and the fixture's keep-alives proving the Session really was
19152    ///   established, not merely allocated — is the security property itself.
19153    /// * **retire at every teardown.** The explicit close is the one teardown path a test can drive deterministically;
19154    ///   the eviction listener and the PIX-failure path funnel through the same `release_session_slot` this exercises.
19155    /// * **no retire on drain.** `begin_surb_drain` deliberately keeps the slot so the drain can spend the Session's
19156    ///   remaining SURBs; retiring there would size the store for a Session that is still spending. The close below
19157    ///   starts a drain (the fixture funds the buffer), and the retire count staying at zero while the drain runs is
19158    ///   what proves the drain path left the seam alone. The supervisor's own teardown of the drained Session then
19159    ///   supplies the single retire.
19160    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19161    async fn an_established_session_is_admitted_once_retired_once_and_drain_retires_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19162        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
19163        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, pseudonym) =
19164            drainable_exit_pix_session(Duration::from_secs(1), Some(Arc::new(admission.clone()))).await?;
19165
19166        assert_eq!(
19167            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
19168            1,
19169            "an established Session must be admitted exactly once, at commit"
19170        );
19171        assert_eq!(
19172            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
19173            0,
19174            "nothing before the close may retire an established Session"
19175        );
19176
19177        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
19178
19179        // The close starts a drain, so the slot survives it on purpose — and so must the admission.
19180        assert!(
19181            mgr.active_sessions().contains(&pseudonym),
19182            "the drain fixture's close must have started a drain for the assertions below to mean anything"
19183        );
19184        assert_eq!(
19185            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
19186            0,
19187            "a close answered by a SURB drain must not retire the Session — the drain still spends its SURBs"
19188        );
19189        assert!(
19190            !admission.retire_precedes_admit(&pseudonym),
19191            "no retire may be recorded before the Session's own admit"
19192        );
19193
19194        // End the drain the way the supervisor does, and let its teardown run: the retire belongs to
19195        // *that* path, not to the close that started the drain.
19196        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("index one is non-zero"));
19197        mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id))
19198            .await?;
19199        assert!(
19200            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
19201            "a recovered cycle must end the drain and tear the Session down"
19202        );
19203        assert_eq!(
19204            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
19205            1,
19206            "the drain's teardown must retire the Session exactly once"
19207        );
19208
19209        // Drain the packets the teardown is still holding so the fixture's sender task finishes.
19210        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
19211        Ok(())
19212    }
19213
19214    /// A Session whose establishment fails after the slot is inserted must never be admitted.
19215    ///
19216    /// The rollback path is the one place an unestablished peer comes closest to the admitted class:
19217    /// the slot exists, the pseudonym is set, and only the failed notification stands between it and
19218    /// the commit. The admit riding on `commit` — rather than on allocation — is what keeps it out,
19219    /// and the retired count of one is the rollback's own no-op retire flowing through the same seam
19220    /// as every teardown (idempotent against a pseudonym that was never admitted, but recorded here
19221    /// so the path is visibly wired rather than merely harmless).
19222    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19223    async fn a_rolled_back_session_is_never_admitted() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19224        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
19225        // Short grace: the rollback's retire is deferred, and the default window would make this
19226        // test wait out the library default in real time for no added coverage.
19227        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
19228            surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
19229            ..Default::default()
19230        });
19231        mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone()));
19232
19233        // Drop the receiver so that notifying about the new incoming session fails *after* the slot
19234        // has already been inserted — the same fixture the rollback test above uses.
19235        let transport = MockMsgSender::new();
19236        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
19237        drop(new_session_rx);
19238        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
19239        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
19240
19241        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
19242        let result = mgr
19243            .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
19244                pseudonym,
19245                StartInitiation {
19246                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
19247                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
19248                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
19249                    additional_data: 0,
19250                },
19251            )
19252            .await;
19253        assert!(
19254            result.is_err(),
19255            "the fixture's dropped notification channel must fail the establishment"
19256        );
19257
19258        assert!(
19259            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
19260            "the partially established session slot was not rolled back"
19261        );
19262        assert_eq!(
19263            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
19264            0,
19265            "a Session that never committed must never be admitted — admission happens at commit, not at slot \
19266             allocation, and this is the peer the distinction exists to keep out"
19267        );
19268        assert_eq!(
19269            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
19270            1,
19271            "the rollback must run the retire through the same seam as every teardown"
19272        );
19273
19274        sender.close_channel();
19275        handle.await??;
19276        Ok(())
19277    }
19278
19279    /// A teardown on a reused pseudonym must present *its own* admission's token, not the successor's.
19280    ///
19281    /// The pseudonym is client-chosen (`SessionClientConfig::pseudonym`) and freely reusable, so
19282    /// "close Session A, open Session B on the same pseudonym" is a real sequence, not an exotic
19283    /// one. A's retire is deliberately deferred past the packet pipeline's SURB-resolution window —
19284    /// A's own return-routed notification needs its ring while the resolution stage looks it up — so
19285    /// it lands *after* B's commit, and an unconditional retire would invalidate B's already-admitted
19286    /// ring: B would go on inserting its SURBs into the 16-cap un-admitted quarantine and never
19287    /// recover, with nothing logged anywhere.
19288    ///
19289    /// The deferral is guarded by the token: `admit` returns one naming its admission, the teardown
19290    /// threads that token to its retire, and the store honours a retire only while its token still
19291    /// names the pseudonym's current admission. This test pins the manager half of that — the
19292    /// successor's admit is real and distinguished, and A's retire presents A's token rather than B's
19293    /// (the failure a teardown re-looking-up the slot under the pseudonym would produce). The store's
19294    /// own matching is pinned by `a_stale_retire_must_not_clobber_a_successor_admissions_ring` over in
19295    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`, which is where the matching lives.
19296    ///
19297    /// The grace is shortened through `surb_resolution_wait` so the deferral is exercised without
19298    /// waiting out the library default in real time.
19299    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19300    async fn a_reused_pseudonym_keeps_the_successor_ring_when_the_stale_retire_fires() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19301        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
19302        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
19303            SessionManagerConfig {
19304                surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
19305                ..Default::default()
19306            },
19307            Some(Arc::new(admission.clone())),
19308        )
19309        .await?;
19310
19311        assert_eq!(
19312            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
19313            1,
19314            "the first Session must be established for the reuse below to mean anything"
19315        );
19316
19317        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
19318
19319        // Re-establish on the same pseudonym, the way a client reusing its configured pseudonym
19320        // would. The initiation runs the same handshake the first one did, so the second admit
19321        // comes from the same commit point.
19322        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
19323            pseudonym,
19324            StartInitiation {
19325                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
19326                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
19327                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capabilities::empty()),
19328                additional_data: 0,
19329            },
19330        )
19331        .await?;
19332
19333        // The successor's admit is in the log, and A's retire is deferred: the interleaving below is
19334        // the one the grace produces — B's admit first, A's retire after — which is exactly the case
19335        // the token makes safe. Waiting the retire out before asserting keeps the order pinned rather
19336        // than assumed.
19337        assert_eq!(
19338            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
19339            1,
19340            "the first teardown's retire must still be paid — deferred past the SURB-resolution window, never \
19341             suppressed"
19342        );
19343        assert_eq!(
19344            admission.sequence(&pseudonym),
19345            vec!["admit", "admit", "retire"]
19346                .into_iter()
19347                .map(String::from)
19348                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
19349            "the successor must be admitted before A's deferred retire fires — the case the token exists for"
19350        );
19351
19352        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
19353        assert_eq!(
19354            minted.len(),
19355            2,
19356            "two Sessions on one pseudonym must mint two admissions"
19357        );
19358        assert_ne!(
19359            minted[0], minted[1],
19360            "the two admissions must carry distinct tokens, or no retire could tell them apart"
19361        );
19362        assert_eq!(
19363            admission.retire_tokens(),
19364            vec![minted[0]],
19365            "A's retire must present A's token and not B's — a teardown that re-looked-up the slot under the \
19366             pseudonym would present B's and invalidate the live ring"
19367        );
19368
19369        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
19370        Ok(())
19371    }
19372
19373    /// A stale teardown token must not retire a successor Session's admission.
19374    ///
19375    /// This is the manager side of the token guard the deferred retire leans on. The first Session's
19376    /// teardown captures its own token; a successor is then admitted on the same client-chosen
19377    /// pseudonym before that token is presented. The seam is wired so the teardown of a Session can
19378    /// only ever present the token its own `commit` obtained — the slot carries the token `commit`
19379    /// stamped into it, not whatever the teardown could otherwise reach for — which is the property
19380    /// this pins. The store's matching of token against admission is pinned over in
19381    /// `hopr-protocol-hopr`, which is where the matching lives.
19382    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19383    async fn a_teardown_presents_the_token_of_the_session_it_is_tearing_down() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19384        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
19385        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, _new_session_rx, pseudonym) = exit_session_originating_keep_alives(
19386            SessionManagerConfig {
19387                // Shortened so the deferred retire is exercised without waiting out the library
19388                // default in real time.
19389                surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
19390                ..Default::default()
19391            },
19392            Some(Arc::new(admission.clone())),
19393        )
19394        .await?;
19395
19396        assert_eq!(
19397            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
19398            1,
19399            "the first Session must be established for the token threading below to mean anything"
19400        );
19401        let first_token = admission
19402            .minted_tokens()
19403            .first()
19404            .copied()
19405            .ok_or(anyhow!("the first Session's commit must have minted a token"))?;
19406
19407        // Close the first Session: its teardown captures the token its own commit obtained and
19408        // schedules the retire with it. The token is read from the slot the teardown removes, so
19409        // what reaches the retire is that Session's, never a successor's.
19410        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym), "the session must exist to be closed");
19411
19412        // The deferred retire carries the first admission's token, which the mock records; a
19413        // successor admitted in the meantime — as the reuse test above establishes — would then be
19414        // immune to it by construction, since the tokens differ. The retire must still be paid.
19415        assert_eq!(
19416            wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await,
19417            1,
19418            "the teardown must present a token to the store — an unsuppressed retire is the contract, and the store's \
19419             matching is what makes the stale case safe"
19420        );
19421        let presented = admission
19422            .retire_tokens()
19423            .last()
19424            .copied()
19425            .ok_or(anyhow!("the teardown must have presented a token to the store"))?;
19426        assert_eq!(
19427            presented, first_token,
19428            "the teardown must present the token its own Session's commit obtained, not a successor's — a successor \
19429             admitted in the deferred-retire window would otherwise be invalidated"
19430        );
19431        assert!(
19432            !admission.retire_precedes_admit(&pseudonym),
19433            "no retire may be recorded before the Session's own admit"
19434        );
19435
19436        let _ = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
19437        Ok(())
19438    }
19439
19440    /// The ways a Session can be torn down, for the matrix below.
19441    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
19442    enum TearDown {
19443        Close,
19444        SocketClosed,
19445        IdleEviction,
19446        PeerSessionError,
19447        SurbDrain,
19448        RolledBack,
19449    }
19450
19451    /// However a Session ends, it leaves the same state behind: gone from the manager, its admission
19452    /// retired once with the token it was given (a rolled-back Session was never admitted, so none is
19453    /// minted and it retires with `AdmissionToken::NONE`), and the peer is sent no `SessionError`. Only
19454    /// the PIX failure teardowns (not covered here) notify the peer.
19455    #[rstest]
19456    #[case::explicit_close(TearDown::Close)]
19457    #[case::socket_closed(TearDown::SocketClosed)]
19458    #[case::idle_eviction(TearDown::IdleEviction)]
19459    #[case::peer_session_error(TearDown::PeerSessionError)]
19460    #[case::surb_drain(TearDown::SurbDrain)]
19461    #[case::rolled_back(TearDown::RolledBack)]
19462    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19463    async fn every_way_a_session_ends_leaves_the_same_state_behind(#[case] way: TearDown) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19464        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
19465        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
19466            surb_resolution_wait: Duration::from_millis(100),
19467            idle_timeout: if matches!(way, TearDown::IdleEviction) {
19468                KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD * 3
19469            } else {
19470                SessionManagerConfig::default().idle_timeout
19471            },
19472            ..Default::default()
19473        };
19474        let (mgr, mut msg_rx, incoming, pseudonym) = match way {
19475            TearDown::SurbDrain => {
19476                let (mgr, msg_rx, pseudonym) =
19477                    drainable_exit_pix_session(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD, Some(Arc::new(admission.clone()))).await?;
19478                (mgr, msg_rx, None, pseudonym)
19479            }
19480            TearDown::RolledBack => {
19481                let mgr = RecordingManager::new(cfg.clone());
19482                mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone()));
19483                let (msg_tx, msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
19484                // A dropped receiver fails the notification after the slot was inserted.
19485                let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
19486                mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
19487                let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
19488                let started = mgr
19489                    .handle_incoming_session_initiation(
19490                        pseudonym,
19491                        StartInitiation {
19492                            challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
19493                            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
19494                            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
19495                            additional_data: 0,
19496                        },
19497                    )
19498                    .await;
19499                anyhow::ensure!(started.is_err(), "the setup must fail for the rollback to run");
19500                (mgr, msg_rx, None, pseudonym)
19501            }
19502            _ => {
19503                let (mgr, msg_rx, incoming, pseudonym) =
19504                    exit_session_originating_keep_alives(cfg, Some(Arc::new(admission.clone()))).await?;
19505                (mgr, msg_rx, Some(incoming), pseudonym)
19506            }
19507        };
19508
19509        match way {
19510            TearDown::Close | TearDown::SurbDrain => assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym)),
19511            TearDown::SocketClosed => {
19512                let mut incoming = incoming.context("the fixture keeps the incoming session channel")?;
19513                let mut exit_session = incoming
19514                    .next()
19515                    .await
19516                    .context("the Exit must have been handed a Session")?;
19517                exit_session.session.close().await?;
19518            }
19519            TearDown::IdleEviction => {
19520                for _ in 0..50 {
19521                    mgr.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
19522                    tokio::time::sleep(KEEP_ALIVE_PERIOD / 10).await;
19523                }
19524            }
19525            TearDown::PeerSessionError => {
19526                let error = StartErrorType {
19527                    identifier: ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(pseudonym),
19528                    reason: StartErrorReason::Unknown,
19529                };
19530                mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, start_packet(HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(error))?)?;
19531            }
19532            TearDown::RolledBack => {}
19533        }
19534        if matches!(way, TearDown::SurbDrain) {
19535            // The drain keeps the slot; the supervisor's own close, here a recovered cycle, ends it.
19536            let ssa_id = SsaId::new(pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).context("index one is non-zero")?);
19537            mgr.dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::SsaRecovered(ssa_id))
19538                .await?;
19539        }
19540
19541        assert!(
19542            wait_for_no_active_sessions(&mgr).await,
19543            "{way:?} must remove the Session"
19544        );
19545        assert!(mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).is_none(), "{way:?} left a slot behind");
19546        assert_eq!(
19547            mgr.num_active_sessions(),
19548            0,
19549            "{way:?} must give the Session's count back"
19550        );
19551
19552        assert_eq!(wait_for_retire(&admission, &pseudonym, 1).await, 1);
19553        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
19554        assert_eq!(admission.retired(&pseudonym), 1, "{way:?} must retire exactly once");
19555        if matches!(way, TearDown::RolledBack) {
19556            assert!(
19557                admission.minted_tokens().is_empty(),
19558                "a rolled-back Session is never admitted"
19559            );
19560            assert_eq!(
19561                admission.retire_tokens(),
19562                vec![AdmissionToken::NONE],
19563                "a rolled-back Session must retire with `NONE`, which matches no admission"
19564            );
19565        } else {
19566            assert_eq!(
19567                admission.retire_tokens(),
19568                admission.minted_tokens(),
19569                "{way:?} must retire with the token its admission returned"
19570            );
19571        }
19572
19573        let told = originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::from_millis(200))
19574            .await
19575            .iter()
19576            .any(|(_, data)| {
19577                start_msg_match(data, |m| {
19578                    matches!(
19579                        m,
19580                        HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(e) if e.identifier == ErrorIdentifier::SessionId(pseudonym)
19581                    )
19582                })
19583            });
19584        assert!(!told, "{way:?} must not send a SessionError naming the Session");
19585        Ok(())
19586    }
19587
19588    /// Verifies that established sessions exchange `KeepAlive` messages driven by the SURB balancer,
19589    /// that config updates propagate via keep-alives, and that SURB usage statistics are collected.
19590    ///
19591    /// ## Steps
19592    /// 1. Alice's manager is started with no `PixToolbox` and a `SurbBalancerConfig` with `target_surb_buffer_size:
19593    ///    100`. Bob's manager is configured with a 500ms `surb_balance_notify_period`. Alice's first fill is paced, a
19594    ///    fifth of the target a second, and a session is ready at a quarter of the target, so it is ready after 1.25 s
19595    ///    of fill plus up to a sampling tick (1.5 s measured), and not before 0.8 s, which an unpaced fill at this
19596    ///    test's ceiling would beat; Alice's balancer is seen to have armed the pacing, and Bob's not.
19597    /// 2. Alice initiates a session with the balancer config and PIX quota set; the `StartSession` /
19598    ///    `SessionEstablished` handshake completes via mock transports.
19599    /// 3. Both managers report the same `target_surb_buffer_size` via `get_surb_balancer_config` (confirmed from both
19600    ///    Alice and Bob's perspective).
19601    /// 4. A 1500ms sleep allows the SURB balancer's periodic keep-alive timer to fire multiple times.
19602    /// 5. `update_surb_balancer_config` is called to raise the target to 200. After another 1500ms, Bob's manager
19603    ///    reflects the updated target via `get_surb_balancer_config`, confirming keep-alives communicated the change.
19604    ///    That is with Alice's `surb_target_notify` on (`target_notify`). With it off, Alice's keep-alives carry no
19605    ///    `BalancerTarget` flag and no target, and Bob keeps the one announced at establishment.
19606    /// 6. `get_surb_level_estimates` is called on both sides; both report positive sent/received/used counts,
19607    ///    confirming the balancer collected SURB statistics.
19608    /// 7. Alice closes the session; `ping_session` returns `NonExistingSession` after a short wait.
19609    ///
19610    /// Bob's level reports are required in both cases, and are the end-to-end proof that the Exit sends them to
19611    /// an Entry it knows to be balancing by its keep-alives, whether or not those announce its target.
19612    ///
19613    /// The mock transports hand Alice's keep-alives to Bob with the packet info the pipeline would give
19614    /// them (`keep_alive_packet_info`): the SURBs the packet carried. Bob books those, not the message's
19615    /// declared maximum, so a mock that reported none would leave him with no received SURBs.
19616    #[rstest]
19617    #[case::target_notify_on(true)]
19618    #[case::target_notify_off(false)]
19619    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
19620    async fn session_manager_should_send_keep_alives_via_surb_balancer(
19621        #[case] target_notify: bool,
19622    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
19623        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
19624        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
19625
19626        let bob_cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
19627            surb_balance_notify_period: Some(Duration::from_millis(500)),
19628            ..Default::default()
19629        };
19630        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
19631            surb_target_notify: target_notify,
19632            ..Default::default()
19633        });
19634        let bob_mgr = SessionManager::new(bob_cfg.clone());
19635
19636        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
19637        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
19638
19639        // What Alice's keep-alives said: their flags and their additional data, in the order sent.
19640        let alice_keep_alives: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<(KeepAliveFlags, u64)>>> = Default::default();
19641
19642        // The SURBs a keep-alive actually carried, as the wire would report them. Alice's keep-alives
19643        // are the only SURB source in this fixture, so the Exit's estimate has to be built from these
19644        // packet infos rather than from `max_surbs()` alone.
19645        let surbs_carried = |data: &ApplicationDataOut| -> IncomingPacketInfo {
19646            let carried = HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
19647                .map(|msg| match msg {
19648                    StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) => ka.max_surbs().unwrap_or_default(),
19649                    _ => 0,
19650                })
19651                .unwrap_or_default();
19652            IncomingPacketInfo {
19653                num_saved_surbs: carried,
19654                ..Default::default()
19655            }
19656        };
19657
19658        // Alice sends the StartSession message
19659        let mut open_sequence = mockall::Sequence::new();
19660        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
19661        alice_transport
19662            .expect_send_message()
19663            .once()
19664            .in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
19665            .withf(move |peer, data| {
19666                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::StartSession)
19667                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
19668            })
19669            .returning(move |_, data| {
19670                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
19671                Box::pin(async move {
19672                    let packet_info = surbs_carried(&data);
19673                    bob_mgr_clone
19674                        .dispatch_message(
19675                            alice_pseudonym,
19676                            ApplicationDataIn {
19677                                data: data.data,
19678                                packet_info,
19679                            },
19680                        )
19681                        ?;
19682                    Ok(())
19683                })
19684            });
19685
19686        // Bob sends the SessionEstablished message
19687        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
19688        bob_transport
19689            .expect_send_message()
19690            .once()
19691            .in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
19692            .withf(move |peer, data| {
19693                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished)
19694                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
19695            })
19696            .returning(move |_, data| {
19697                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
19698                Box::pin(async move {
19699                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
19700                        alice_pseudonym,
19701                        ApplicationDataIn {
19702                            data: data.data,
19703                            packet_info: Default::default(),
19704                        },
19705                    )?;
19706                    Ok(())
19707                })
19708            });
19709
19710        // Large enough for the paced first fill (a fifth of the target per second) to have delivered
19711        // something by Bob's first level report, 500 ms in; the mock accepts only reports above zero.
19712        const INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET: u64 = 100;
19713
19714        const NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET: u64 = 200;
19715
19716        // Alice sends KeepAlive messages from her balancer, which Bob receives. What they say is
19717        // recorded rather than matched here: with `surb_target_notify` on they announce the balancer
19718        // target (the initial one, then the updated one), and with it off they say nothing, and either
19719        // way they are the evidence to Bob that Alice balances.
19720        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
19721        let alice_keep_alives_clone = alice_keep_alives.clone();
19722        alice_transport
19723            .expect_send_message()
19724            .times(1..)
19725            //.in_sequence(&mut sequence)
19726            .withf(move |peer, data| {
19727                msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::KeepAlive)
19728                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
19729            })
19730            .returning(move |_, data| {
19731                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
19732                let alice_keep_alives_clone = alice_keep_alives_clone.clone();
19733                Box::pin(async move {
19734                    if let Ok(StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka)) =
19735                        HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
19736                    {
19737                        alice_keep_alives_clone.lock().push((ka.flags, ka.additional_data));
19738                    }
19739                    bob_mgr_clone
19740                        .dispatch_message(
19741                            alice_pseudonym,
19742                            ApplicationDataIn {
19743                                packet_info: keep_alive_packet_info(&data.data),
19744                                data: data.data,
19745                            },
19746                        )
19747                        ?;
19748                    Ok(())
19749                })
19750            });
19751
19752        // Bob sends at least 1 Keep Alive back reporting its SURB estimate
19753        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
19754        bob_transport
19755            .expect_send_message()
19756            .times(1..)
19757            //.in_sequence(&mut open_sequence)
19758            .withf(move |peer, data| {
19759                start_msg_match(data, |msg| matches!(msg, StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ka) if ka.flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState) && ka.additional_data > 0))
19760                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(p)) if *p == alice_pseudonym)
19761            })
19762            .returning(move |_, data| {
19763                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
19764                Box::pin(async move {
19765                    alice_mgr_clone
19766                        .dispatch_message(
19767                            alice_pseudonym,
19768                            ApplicationDataIn {
19769                                data: data.data,
19770                                packet_info: Default::default(),
19771                            },
19772                        )
19773                        ?;
19774                    Ok(())
19775                })
19776            });
19777
19778        // Alice sends the terminating segment to close the Session
19779        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
19780        alice_transport
19781            .expect_send_message()
19782            .once()
19783            //.in_sequence(&mut sequence)
19784            .withf(move |peer, data| {
19785                hopr_protocol_session::types::SessionMessage::<{ ApplicationData::PAYLOAD_SIZE }>::try_from(
19786                    data.data.plain_text.as_ref(),
19787                )
19788                .ok()
19789                .and_then(|m| m.try_as_segment())
19790                .map(|s| s.is_terminating())
19791                .unwrap_or(false)
19792                    && matches!(peer, DestinationRouting::Forward { destination, .. } if destination.as_ref() == &bob_peer.into())
19793            })
19794            .returning(move |_, data| {
19795                let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
19796                Box::pin(async move {
19797                    let packet_info = surbs_carried(&data);
19798                    bob_mgr_clone
19799                        .dispatch_message(
19800                            alice_pseudonym,
19801                            ApplicationDataIn {
19802                                data: data.data,
19803                                packet_info,
19804                            },
19805                        )
19806                        ?;
19807                    Ok(())
19808                })
19809            });
19810
19811        let mut ahs = Vec::new();
19812
19813        // Start Alice
19814        let (new_session_tx_alice, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
19815        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
19816        ahs.extend(alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?);
19817        assert!(alice_mgr.is_started());
19818
19819        // Start Bob
19820        let (new_session_tx_bob, new_session_rx_bob) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
19821        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
19822        ahs.extend(bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?);
19823        assert!(bob_mgr.is_started());
19824
19825        let target = SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?);
19826
19827        let balancer_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
19828            target_surb_buffer_size: INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET,
19829            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
19830            ..Default::default()
19831        };
19832
19833        pin_mut!(new_session_rx_bob);
19834        // The first fill is paced, so readiness (a quarter of the target) takes 1.25 s of fill whatever the
19835        // target, plus up to a sampling tick (1.5 s measured); the open is given 4 s. Alice's slot exists
19836        // from before the readiness wait, and the first thing seen of it is whether
19837        // her balancer, the Entry's, armed the pacing of the first fill.
19838        let alice_slot_seen = async {
19839            loop {
19840                if let Some(slot) = alice_mgr.sessions.get(&alice_pseudonym) {
19841                    break slot.surb_mgmt.refill_pacing_active();
19842                }
19843                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5)).await;
19844            }
19845        };
19846        let opened_at = Instant::now();
19847        let (alice_session, bob_session, alice_first_fill_paced) = timeout(
19848            Duration::from_secs(4),
19849            futures::future::join3(
19850                alice_mgr.new_session(
19851                    bob_peer,
19852                    SessionTarget::TcpStream(target.clone()),
19853                    SessionClientConfig {
19854                        pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
19855                        capabilities: Capability::Segmentation.into(),
19856                        surb_management: Some(balancer_cfg),
19857                        ..Default::default()
19858                    },
19859                ),
19860                new_session_rx_bob.next(),
19861                alice_slot_seen,
19862            ),
19863        )
19864        .await?;
19865        let opening = opened_at.elapsed();
19866
19867        let mut alice_session = alice_session?;
19868        let bob_session = bob_session.ok_or(anyhow!("bob must get an incoming session"))?;
19869        // A quarter of a target of 100 at 20 SURBs a second is 1.25 s; the ceiling of this test, 100 a
19870        // second, would have been ready in about a quarter of that.
19871        assert!(
19872            opening >= Duration::from_millis(800),
19873            "a paced first fill cannot make the session ready this fast, it took {opening:?}"
19874        );
19875        assert!(
19876            alice_first_fill_paced,
19877            "the Entry's balancer must pace its first fill like the refill after a wipe"
19878        );
19879        assert!(
19880            !bob_mgr
19881                .sessions
19882                .get(bob_session.session.id())
19883                .ok_or(anyhow!("bob must hold the session slot"))?
19884                .surb_mgmt
19885                .refill_pacing_active(),
19886            "the Exit's balancer does not pace anything at its start"
19887        );
19888
19889        assert!(matches!(bob_session.target, SessionTarget::TcpStream(host) if host == target));
19890
19891        assert_eq!(
19892            Some(balancer_cfg),
19893            alice_mgr.get_surb_balancer_config(alice_session.id())?
19894        );
19895
19896        // The organic SURB gate, on the real slot rather than a hand-built state. Two things it must
19897        // get right, both of which would deadlock a Session if inverted.
19898        {
19899            let alice_slot = alice_mgr
19900                .sessions
19901                .get(alice_session.id())
19902                .ok_or(anyhow!("alice must hold the session slot"))?;
19903
19904            // At cold start the gate must be open: readiness only waits for a quarter of the target, so a
19905            // gate that closed at or below that would stop the very production it is waiting on.
19906            assert_eq!(
19907                1,
19908                alice_slot.surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet(),
19909                "a freshly opened session must still produce organic SURBs"
19910            );
19911
19912            // And it must stay open on the counterparty's word, whatever the local estimate says.
19913            alice_slot
19914                .surb_mgmt
19915                .observe_counterparty_signals(PacketSignal::OutOfSurbs.into());
19916            alice_slot
19917                .surb_mgmt
19918                .buffer_level
19919                .store(u64::MAX, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19920            assert_eq!(
19921                1,
19922                alice_slot.surb_mgmt.organic_surbs_per_packet(),
19923                "a counterparty out of SURBs must override any local estimate"
19924            );
19925
19926            // Leave the slot as it was found; the balancer loop keeps running below.
19927            alice_slot
19928                .surb_mgmt
19929                .observe_counterparty_signals(PacketSignals::default());
19930            alice_slot
19931                .surb_mgmt
19932                .buffer_level
19933                .store(0, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
19934        }
19935
19936        let remote_cfg = bob_mgr
19937            .get_surb_balancer_config(bob_session.session.id())?
19938            .ok_or(anyhow!("no remote config at bob"))?;
19939        assert_eq!(remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size, balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size);
19940        assert_eq!(
19941            remote_cfg.max_surbs_per_sec,
19942            remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
19943                / bob_cfg
19944                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
19945                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
19946                    .as_secs()
19947        );
19948
19949        // Let the Surb balancer send enough KeepAlive messages
19950        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
19951
19952        let new_balancer_cfg = SurbBalancerConfig {
19953            target_surb_buffer_size: NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET,
19954            max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
19955            ..Default::default()
19956        };
19957
19958        // Update to a higher target
19959        alice_mgr.update_surb_balancer_config(alice_session.id(), new_balancer_cfg)?;
19960
19961        // Let the Surb balancer send enough KeepAlive messages
19962        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1500)).await;
19963
19964        // Bob knows about the updated target only if Alice announces it.
19965        let remote_cfg = bob_mgr
19966            .get_surb_balancer_config(bob_session.session.id())?
19967            .ok_or(anyhow!("no remote config at bob"))?;
19968        let expected_remote_target = if target_notify {
19969            new_balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
19970        } else {
19971            balancer_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size
19972        };
19973        assert_eq!(
19974            remote_cfg.target_surb_buffer_size, expected_remote_target,
19975            "Bob learns the raised target exactly when Alice's keep-alives announce it"
19976        );
19977        assert_eq!(
19978            remote_cfg.max_surbs_per_sec,
19979            expected_remote_target / bob_cfg.minimum_surb_buffer_duration.as_secs()
19980        );
19981
19982        // Alice's keep-alives carry `BalancerTarget` with her target exactly when she announces it.
19983        let said = alice_keep_alives.lock().clone();
19984        assert!(!said.is_empty(), "Alice's balancer must have sent keep-alives");
19985        if target_notify {
19986            assert!(
19987                said.iter()
19988                    .all(|(flags, _)| flags.contains(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget)),
19989                "every keep-alive of an announcing Entry names her target: {said:?}"
19990            );
19991            for target in [INITIAL_BALANCER_TARGET, NEXT_BALANCER_TARGET] {
19992                assert!(
19993                    said.iter().any(|(_, announced)| *announced == target),
19994                    "no keep-alive announced the target {target}: {said:?}"
19995                );
19996            }
19997        } else {
19998            assert!(
19999                said.iter()
20000                    .all(|(flags, announced)| flags.is_empty() && *announced == 0),
20001                "with `surb_target_notify` off the keep-alives carry no flag and no target: {said:?}"
20002            );
20003        }
20004
20005        let (alice_surb_sent, alice_surb_used) = alice_mgr.get_surb_level_estimates(alice_session.id())?;
20006        let (bob_surb_recv, bob_surb_used) = bob_mgr.get_surb_level_estimates(bob_session.session.id())?;
20007
20008        alice_session.close().await?;
20009
20010        assert!(alice_surb_sent > 0, "alice must've sent surbs");
20011        assert!(bob_surb_recv > 0, "bob must've received surbs");
20012        assert!(
20013            bob_surb_recv <= alice_surb_sent,
20014            "bob cannot receive more surbs than alice sent"
20015        );
20016
20017        assert!(alice_surb_used > 0, "alice must see bob used surbs");
20018        assert!(bob_surb_used > 0, "bob must've used surbs");
20019        assert!(
20020            alice_surb_used <= bob_surb_used,
20021            "alice cannot see bob used more surbs than bob actually used"
20022        );
20023
20024        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
20025        assert!(matches!(
20026            alice_mgr.ping_session(alice_session.id()).await,
20027            Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession))
20028        ));
20029
20030        futures::stream::iter(ahs)
20031            .for_each(|ah| async move { ah.abort() })
20032            .await;
20033
20034        // Cleanup: close senders and await handles
20035        alice_sender.close_channel();
20036        bob_sender.close_channel();
20037        alice_handle.await??;
20038        bob_handle.await??;
20039
20040        Ok(())
20041    }
