24474    /// A raised `BalancerTarget` must reach the SURB store, so the Session's ring grows with it, on a
24475    /// `NoRateControl` Session as much as on a rate-controlled one.
24476    ///
24477    /// The ring is sized once at establishment from the target then announced. The gnosis_vpn client
24478    /// opens at a ping tier and announces its main tier seconds later (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739); an
24479    /// Exit that only updates the balancer's set-point leaves the ring at the ping tier, and every
24480    /// SURB minted toward the main one is evicted on arrival — losing the PIX share each carried.
24481    /// A `NoRateControl` Session has no set-point to move (`no_rate_control`: its balancer state stays
24482    /// disabled), yet its ring is the same store and has the same need, when its Entry announced a
24483    /// target at establishment for the ring to be sized from. One that announced none starts with the
24484    /// full ring, which leaves nothing to widen
24485    /// (`the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling`).
24486    ///
24487    /// Only a keep-alive that carries `BalancerTarget` raises anything. An Entry whose
24488    /// `surb_target_notify` is off sends its keep-alives without it, and the Exit then learns of no
24489    /// raise (`*_without_target_notify`).
24490    ///
24491    /// The token matters as much as the call: the store widens only the admission the token names,
24492    /// and a raise under a successor's pseudonym must not touch its ring.
24493    #[rstest]
24494    #[case::rate_controlled(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 688, true)]
24495    #[case::no_rate_control(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 688, true)]
24496    #[case::rate_controlled_without_target_notify(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 688, false)]
24497    #[case::no_rate_control_without_target_notify(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 688, false)]
24498    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24499    async fn a_raised_balancer_target_must_widen_the_sessions_ring(
24500        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
24501        #[case] announced: u64,
24502        #[case] target_notify: bool,
24503    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24504        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
24505        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
24506        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
24507            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, None)?;
24508        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
24509
24510        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24511        // The ping tier the Session is admitted with — the low 32 bits of the options word are the
24512        // announced SURB target, which is what the Exit sizes the ring from.
24513        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
24514            pseudonym,
24515            StartInitiation {
24516                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
24517                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced, Duration::ZERO),
24518                ..no_pix_offer()
24519            },
24520        )
24521        .await?;
24522        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
24523        assert_eq!(
24524            !rate_controlled,
24525            slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled(),
24526            "fixture: only a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer"
24527        );
24528
24529        // The Entry's main tier, announced seconds later.
24530        let raised = 6_887_usize;
24531        let flags: KeepAliveFlags = if target_notify {
24532            KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into()
24533        } else {
24534            None.into()
24535        };
24536        let keep_alive = KeepAliveMessage::<SessionId> {
24537            session_id: pseudonym,
24538            flags,
24539            additional_data: raised as u64,
24540        };
24541
24542        if target_notify {
24543            mgr.dispatch_message(
24544                pseudonym,
24545                ApplicationDataIn {
24546                    data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(keep_alive.clone()).try_into()?,
24547                    packet_info: Default::default(),
24548                },
24549            )?;
24550
24551            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
24552                loop {
24553                    if !admission.raised_targets().is_empty() {
24554                        break;
24555                    }
24556                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
24557                }
24558            })
24559            .await
24560            .context("the raised target never reached the SURB store")?;
24561
24562            assert_eq!(
24563                vec![raised],
24564                admission.raised_targets(),
24565                "the announced target, not the one the Session was admitted with, is what the ring is widened to"
24566            );
24567            assert_eq!(
24568                admission.minted_tokens(),
24569                admission.raise_tokens(),
24570                "the raise must name the admission the Session holds, or the store widens nothing"
24571            );
24572
24573            // The Entry repeats the announcement on every keep-alive. Handled here and not dispatched,
24574            // so that it is known to be done when the count is read.
24575            mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive).await?;
24576            assert_eq!(
24577                1,
24578                admission.raised_targets().len(),
24579                "an announcement that raises nothing further must not ask the store again"
24580            );
24581
24582            assert_eq!(
24583                !rate_controlled,
24584                slot.surb_mgmt.is_disabled(),
24585                "a raise must not switch on a balancer the Session does not run"
24586            );
24587            if rate_controlled {
24588                assert_eq!(
24589                    raised as u64,
24590                    slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target(),
24591                    "a rate-controlled Exit follows the Entry's target with its balancer too"
24592                );
24593            }
24594        } else {
24595            // Handled here and not dispatched: nothing happens that could be waited for, and the
24596            // refills flag is set before the raise is decided, so it could not say the handler is done.
24597            mgr.handle_keep_alive(pseudonym, keep_alive).await?;
24598            assert!(
24599                slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
24600                "the keep-alive must have been handled, or its silence proves nothing"
24601            );
24602            assert!(
24603                admission.raised_targets().is_empty(),
24604                "a keep-alive that announces no target raises no ring, whatever value it carries; got {:?}",
24605                admission.raised_targets()
24606            );
24607            if rate_controlled {
24608                assert_eq!(
24609                    announced,
24610                    slot.surb_mgmt.controller_bounds().target(),
24611                    "nor does it move the balancer's target"
24612                );
24613            }
24614        }
24615
24616        sender.close_channel();
24617        transport.await??;
24618        Ok(())
24619    }
24620
24621    /// A keep-alive shows the Exit that its Entry refills it, unless the Entry sent it as a manual ping.
24622    ///
24623    /// An Entry without a SURB balancer can ping a Session by hand (`ping_session`), and that keep-alive
24624    /// brings SURBs like any other. Taken for a balancer's, it would make the Exit send the Entry level
24625    /// reports nothing reads, each at the cost of a reply SURB, and on a rate-controlled Session hold its
24626    /// data at the keep-alive reserve. The mark on the ping is the only way to tell it from a balancer
24627    /// that keeps `surb_target_notify` off, whose keep-alives carry no flag either.
24628    ///
24629    /// Each keep-alive is handled directly, so that the answer is known to be final once it is read. The
24630    /// level reports it decides are covered through the real dispatch by `exit_level_reports_follow_the_entry`.
24631    #[rstest]
24632    #[case::a_manual_ping(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing.into(), false)]
24633    #[case::a_balancer_announcing_its_target(KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(), true)]
24634    #[case::a_balancer_not_announcing_its_target_or_an_older_entrys_ping(None.into(), true)]
24635    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24636    async fn a_keep_alive_shows_the_entry_refills_unless_it_is_a_manual_ping(
24637        #[case] flags: KeepAliveFlags,
24638        #[case] latched: bool,
24639    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24640        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24641        let (mgr, _estimator) = exit_slot_for_keep_alives(pseudonym);
24642        let (new_session_tx, _new_sessions) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
24643        let (mock_sender, _sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
24644        let _ahs = mgr.start(mock_sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24645
24646        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("the session slot must exist")?;
24647        assert!(
24648            !slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
24649            "fixture: nothing has shown the Exit that its Entry refills it"
24650        );
24651
24652        mgr.handle_keep_alive(
24653            pseudonym,
24654            KeepAliveMessage::<SessionId> {
24655                session_id: pseudonym,
24656                flags,
24657                additional_data: 0,
24658            },
24659        )
24660        .await?;
24661
24662        assert_eq!(
24663            latched,
24664            slot.surb_mgmt.counterparty_refills(),
24665            "a keep-alive with flags {flags:?} {} that the Entry refills the Exit",
24666            if latched { "must show" } else { "must not show" }
24667        );
24668        Ok(())
24669    }
24670
24671    /// `ping_session` marks its keep-alive as a manual ping, and it is no bigger than any other.
24672    ///
24673    /// The mark is what stops an Exit from taking the ping of an Entry without a balancer for the sign
24674    /// of a balancer (`a_keep_alive_shows_the_entry_refills_unless_it_is_a_manual_ping`). It must not
24675    /// change how many SURBs the ping can carry, which is what a manual ping is used for.
24676    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24677    async fn ping_session_sends_a_keep_alive_marked_as_a_manual_ping() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24678        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24679        let (mgr, _estimator) = exit_slot_for_keep_alives(pseudonym);
24680        let (new_session_tx, _new_sessions) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
24681        let (mock_sender, mut sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
24682        let _ahs = mgr.start(mock_sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24683
24684        mgr.ping_session(&pseudonym).await?;
24685
24686        let (_, data) = timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), sent.next())
24687            .await
24688            .context("the ping was never sent")?
24689            .context("the manager's sender closed")?;
24690        let StartProtocol::KeepAlive(ping) =
24691            HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)?
24692        else {
24693            anyhow::bail!("not a keep-alive");
24694        };
24695        assert_eq!(pseudonym, ping.session_id);
24696        assert_eq!(
24697            KeepAliveFlags::from(KeepAliveFlag::ManualPing),
24698            ping.flags,
24699            "the ping is marked as one, and as nothing a balancer sends"
24700        );
24701        assert_eq!(0, ping.additional_data);
24702
24703        let unmarked: ApplicationData = HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(pseudonym.into()).try_into()?;
24704        assert_eq!(
24705            unmarked.total_len(),
24706            data.data.total_len(),
24707            "the mark must not change how many SURBs fit beside the ping"
24708        );
24709        Ok(())
24710    }

24712    /// What an Entry with `capabilities` and, if it balances, a SURB balancer targeting `balancer_target`
24713    /// sends to open a Session: its `StartSession`, as the Exit would receive it.
24714    async fn entry_start_session(
24715        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
24716        capabilities: Capabilities,
24717        balancer_target: Option<u64>,
24718    ) -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationData> {
24719        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(Default::default());
24720        let (msg_tx, mut msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
24721        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
24722        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24723
24724        // Nobody answers, so the opening never completes: only the `StartSession` it sends is of interest.
24725        let opening = timeout(
24726            Duration::from_millis(500),
24727            mgr.new_session(
24728                (&ChainKeypair::random()).into(),
24729                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
24730                SessionClientConfig {
24731                    capabilities,
24732                    pseudonym: pseudonym.into(),
24733                    surb_management: balancer_target.map(|target_surb_buffer_size| SurbBalancerConfig {
24734                        target_surb_buffer_size,
24735                        max_surbs_per_sec: 100,
24736                        ..Default::default()
24737                    }),
24738                    ..Default::default()
24739                },
24740            ),
24741        )
24742        .await;
24743        anyhow::ensure!(
24744            opening.is_err(),
24745            "fixture: nobody answered, so the opening cannot have completed"
24746        );
24747
24748        originated_during(&mut msg_rx, Duration::ZERO)
24749            .await
24750            .into_iter()
24751            .map(|(_, data)| data.data)
24752            .find(|data| {
24753                matches!(
24754                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.application_tag, &data.plain_text),
24755                    Ok(StartProtocol::StartSession(_))
24756                )
24757            })
24758            .context("the Entry must have sent a StartSession")
24759    }
24760
24761    /// The SURB target an Entry announces is the one it balances toward, and none otherwise.
24762    ///
24763    /// An Entry that runs no SURB balancer (`surb_management` unset, as for a hoprd `responseBuffer`
24764    /// below two packets) used to announce the balancer-rate fallback on the rate-controlled branch (50 at
24765    /// the defaults), which the Exit cannot tell from a real target of 50. It admitted a ring of 75 for
24766    /// it, and nothing widened that ring. A zero lets the Exit tell, and give such a Session the full ring
24767    /// (`an_exit_gives_an_entry_without_a_balancer_the_full_ring`). A `NoRateControl` Entry announces
24768    /// nothing either way, whether or not it runs a balancer.
24769    ///
24770    /// Only the lower 32 bits of the options word are the SURB target; its upper half carries the PIX
24771    /// parameters, which these cases do not use and the assertion would not look at anyway.
24772    #[rstest]
24773    #[case::rate_controlled_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), Some(300), 300)]
24774    #[case::rate_controlled_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), None, 0)]
24775    #[case::no_rate_control_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, Some(300), 0)]
24776    #[case::no_rate_control_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, None, 0)]
24777    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24778    async fn the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise(
24779        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
24780        #[case] balancer_target: Option<u64>,
24781        #[case] expected: u32,
24782    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24783        let start = entry_start_session(HoprPseudonym::random(), capabilities, balancer_target).await?;
24784        let Ok(StartProtocol::StartSession(initiation)) =
24785            HoprStartProtocol::decode(start.application_tag, &start.plain_text)
24786        else {
24787            anyhow::bail!("not a StartSession");
24788        };
24789
24790        assert_eq!(
24791            expected,
24792            initiation_options(initiation.additional_data) as u32,
24793            "the SURB target in the low 32 bits of the options word"
24794        );
24795        Ok(())
24796    }
24797
24798    /// An Exit gives the Entry's own `StartSession` the ring and the balancer it should: the full ring
24799    /// when the Entry announced no target, its target otherwise, and for a rate-controlled Exit the
24800    /// balancer at the announced target, or at the Exit's own fallback when there was none.
24801    ///
24802    /// The end-to-end half of `the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise`
24803    /// and of `the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling`: a rate-controlled
24804    /// Entry without a balancer is the one whose announcement changed, and it is the case that was left
24805    /// with a ring of 75 SURBs.
24806    #[rstest]
24807    #[case::rate_controlled_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), Some(300), 300)]
24808    #[case::rate_controlled_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation.into(), None, 0)]
24809    #[case::no_rate_control_with_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, Some(300), 0)]
24810    #[case::no_rate_control_without_a_balancer(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, None, 0)]
24811    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24812    async fn an_exit_gives_an_entry_without_a_balancer_the_full_ring(
24813        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
24814        #[case] balancer_target: Option<u64>,
24815        #[case] announced: u32,
24816    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24817        let rate_controlled = !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl);
24818        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24819        let start = entry_start_session(pseudonym, capabilities, balancer_target).await?;
24820
24821        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
24822        let exit = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
24823            maximum_surb_buffer_size: RING_CEILING,
24824            ..Default::default()
24825        });
24826        assert!(exit.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
24827        let (msg_tx, _msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
24828        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
24829        exit.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24830
24831        exit.dispatch_message(
24832            pseudonym,
24833            ApplicationDataIn {
24834                data: start,
24835                packet_info: Default::default(),
24836            },
24837        )?;
24838        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
24839            while admission.admitted_targets().is_empty() {
24840                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
24841            }
24842        })
24843        .await
24844        .context("the Exit never admitted the Session")?;
24845
24846        assert_eq!(
24847            vec![if announced > 0 {
24848                announced as usize
24849            } else {
24850                RING_CEILING
24851            }],
24852            admission.admitted_targets(),
24853            "the ring is sized from what the Entry announced, or from the Exit's ceiling when it announced nothing"
24854        );
24855
24856        if rate_controlled {
24857            let fallback = exit.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
24858                * exit
24859                    .cfg
24860                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
24861                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
24862                    .as_secs();
24863            let balancer = exit
24864                .get_surb_balancer_config(&pseudonym)?
24865                .context("a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer")?;
24866            assert_eq!(
24867                if announced > 0 { announced as u64 } else { fallback },
24868                balancer.target_surb_buffer_size,
24869                "the Exit's balancer follows the announced target, or runs at the Exit's own fallback when none was \
24870                 announced"
24871            );
24872        }
24873
24874        assert!(exit.close_session(&pseudonym));
24875        Ok(())
24876    }
24877
24878    /// The node's `maximum_surb_buffer_size` in the ring tests: well clear of the balancer's fallback
24879    /// (50) and of anything a test announces, and inside the bound the recording admission asserts.
24880    const RING_CEILING: usize = 4_000;
24881    const _: () = assert!(RING_CEILING <= MAXIMUM_SURB_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_TESTS);
24882
24883    /// The SURB ring the Exit admits follows the target the Entry announced, and is the node's ceiling
24884    /// when the Entry announced none.
24885    ///
24886    /// Without an announcement the Exit used to pass the balancer's fallback figure (50 at the defaults)
24887    /// to the store, which turned it into a ring of 75. An Entry that runs no balancer announces
24888    /// nothing (see `the_entry_announces_the_target_it_balances_toward_and_none_otherwise`) and sends no
24889    /// keep-alive to raise a target later, so nothing widened that ring, and a burst of replies found
24890    /// its SURBs evicted past the 75th. The ring is a ceiling that allocates with
24891    /// occupancy, so the Session is given the largest one the node allows (`maximum_surb_buffer_size`)
24892    /// and pays for what it stores. This holds on both kinds of Session, because the ring is the same
24893    /// store whether or not the Exit runs a balancer.
24894    ///
24895    /// An announcement is still the Session's own figure, clamped to the ceiling, however small.
24896    #[rstest]
24897    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_nothing(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 0, RING_CEILING)]
24898    #[case::no_rate_control_announcing_nothing(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 0, RING_CEILING)]
24899    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_64(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 64, 64)]
24900    #[case::no_rate_control_announcing_64(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::NoRateControl, 64, 64)]
24901    #[case::rate_controlled_announcing_more_than_the_ceiling(Capability::Segmentation.into(), 9_999, RING_CEILING)]
24902    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24903    async fn the_admitted_ring_follows_the_announced_target_or_takes_the_ceiling(
24904        #[case] capabilities: Capabilities,
24905        #[case] announced: u64,
24906        #[case] expected: usize,
24907    ) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24908        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
24909        let mgr = RecordingManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
24910            maximum_surb_buffer_size: RING_CEILING,
24911            ..Default::default()
24912        });
24913        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
24914        // Held for the whole test: the establishment answer is sent through it.
24915        let (msg_tx, _msg_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
24916        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(4);
24917        mgr.start(msg_tx, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24918
24919        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24920        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
24921            pseudonym,
24922            StartInitiation {
24923                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
24924                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
24925                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(capabilities),
24926                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(announced, Duration::ZERO),
24927            },
24928        )
24929        .await?;
24930
24931        assert_eq!(
24932            vec![expected],
24933            admission.admitted_targets(),
24934            "the ring is sized from what the Entry announced ({announced}), or from the node's ceiling when it \
24935             announced nothing"
24936        );
24937
24938        // The ring takes the ceiling, but the balancer keeps the figure it always had when nothing was
24939        // announced (so does the fill reserve, which derives from the same one): the rate the Exit starts
24940        // at times the buffer duration it has to outlast, which is a different number from the ring's. A
24941        // NoRateControl Exit runs no balancer, so there is nothing to read there.
24942        if !capabilities.contains(Capability::NoRateControl) {
24943            let fallback = mgr.cfg.initial_return_session_egress_rate as u64
24944                * mgr
24945                    .cfg
24946                    .minimum_surb_buffer_duration
24947                    .max(MIN_SURB_BUFFER_DURATION)
24948                    .as_secs();
24949            anyhow::ensure!(
24950                fallback as usize != RING_CEILING,
24951                "fixture: the fallback must differ from the ring's ceiling for this to tell them apart"
24952            );
24953            let balancer = mgr
24954                .get_surb_balancer_config(&pseudonym)?
24955                .context("a rate-controlled Exit runs a balancer")?;
24956            let expected_target = if announced > 0 { expected as u64 } else { fallback };
24957            assert_eq!(
24958                expected_target, balancer.target_surb_buffer_size,
24959                "the balancer is given what the Entry announced, or the balancer-rate fallback ({fallback}) when it \
24960                 announced nothing, and never the ring's ceiling"
24961            );
24962        }
24963
24964        assert!(mgr.close_session(&pseudonym));
24965        Ok(())
24966    }
24967
24968    /// A keep-alive that arrives *before* the admission is committed must not claim the token cell.
24969    ///
24970    /// The Exit answers `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive can
24971    /// be processed in that window. Reading the cell the way a teardown does would initialize it with
24972    /// `NONE`, and the establishment's own `commit` would then fail its `set` — retiring the live
24973    /// admission and leaving the Session's SURBs in the quarantine, which is precisely the
24974    /// unadmitted-Session failure the seam exists to prevent (hoprnet#8515).
24975    ///
24976    /// Driven deterministically rather than by racing a real establishment: the slot is allocated
24977    /// and left uncommitted, the keep-alive is delivered while its token cell is still empty, and only
24978    /// then does the commit run — which is the ordering the Exit produces on the wire.
24979    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
24980    async fn a_keep_alive_before_commit_must_not_claim_the_admission_token() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
24981        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
24982        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
24983        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
24984        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
24985
24986        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
24987        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
24988        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
24989
24990        // Uncommitted: the Session exists, but nothing has admitted it yet.
24991        let slot = unregistered_slot(pseudonym);
24992        let mut guard = mgr
24993            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, slot.clone())
24994            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
24995        assert_eq!(
24996            AdmissionToken::NONE,
24997            slot.peek_admission_token(),
24998            "fixture: the slot must start uncommitted"
24999        );
25000
25001        // The Entry's ramp announces while the cell is still empty.
25002        mgr.handle_keep_alive(
25003            pseudonym,
25004            KeepAliveMessage {
25005                session_id: pseudonym,
25006                flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
25007                additional_data: 256,
25008            },
25009        )
25010        .await
25011        .context("the keep-alive must be handled without error while uncommitted")?;
25012
25013        assert!(
25014            slot.admission_token.get().is_none(),
25015            "handling a keep-alive must not claim the cell, or the commit's own `set` would fail"
25016        );
25017
25018        // The establishment's commit runs next and must succeed — admitting at the announced target,
25019        // not retiring the admission it just made.
25020        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 64);
25021
25022        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
25023        assert_eq!(1, minted.len(), "the commit must admit exactly once");
25024        assert_eq!(
25025            Some(minted[0]),
25026            slot.admission_token.get().copied(),
25027            "the commit's token must land in the cell the keep-alive left untouched"
25028        );
25029        assert!(
25030            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
25031            "a keep-alive racing the commit must leave it to succeed, not make it retire its own admission; retires \
25032             were {:?}",
25033            admission.retire_tokens()
25034        );
25035        assert_eq!(
25036            vec![256],
25037            admission.admitted_targets(),
25038            "the commit must size the ring from the target the keep-alive announced before it"
25039        );
25040
25041        handle.abort();
25042        Ok(())
25043    }
25044
25045    /// A target announced in the `SessionEstablished`-before-commit window must survive the commit.
25046    ///
25047    /// That window is real — the Exit answers before it commits — and the ring is sized once, at
25048    /// `commit`. A raise processed in it has no admission to widen yet, so the figure is recorded on
25049    /// the slot and the commit sizes the ring from the larger of it and establishment's target.
25050    /// Without that, an Entry that announces its main tier early gets a ping-tier ring, which is the
25051    /// gnosis_vpn shape (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739) reached one interleaving earlier.
25052    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25053    async fn a_target_announced_before_commit_must_survive_the_commit() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25054        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
25055        let (mgr, sender, transport, _err_rx, _incoming) =
25056            started_manager_admitting_small_params(1..=small_params_quota(), false, None)?;
25057        assert!(mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone())));
25058
25059        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
25060        let admitted_with = 688_u64;
25061        let raised = 6_887_usize;
25062
25063        // Establish and announce the main tier in one turn, so the announcement is queued behind the
25064        // establishment — it is processed by the same Start-protocol worker, and whether it lands
25065        // before or after `commit` is the scheduling detail this test must not depend on.
25066        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
25067            pseudonym,
25068            StartInitiation {
25069                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(admitted_with, Duration::ZERO),
25070                ..no_pix_offer()
25071            },
25072        )
25073        .await?;
25074        mgr.dispatch_message(
25075            pseudonym,
25076            ApplicationDataIn {
25077                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
25078                    session_id: pseudonym,
25079                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
25080                    additional_data: raised as u64,
25081                })
25082                .try_into()?,
25083                packet_info: Default::default(),
25084            },
25085        )?;
25086
25087        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
25088            loop {
25089                if admission.raised_targets().contains(&raised) {
25090                    break;
25091                }
25092                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
25093            }
25094        })
25095        .await
25096        .context("the announcement never reached the SURB store")?;
25097
25098        // Whether the raise widened a live admission or the commit sized the ring from it, the store
25099        // must have been told about the raised target and the Session must be admitted, not retired.
25100        assert!(
25101            admission.raised_targets().contains(&raised),
25102            "the commit must start from the recorded target when the raise preceded it, got {:?}",
25103            admission.raised_targets()
25104        );
25105        assert!(
25106            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
25107            "the commit must not retire the admission the raise raced it into"
25108        );
25109
25110        sender.close_channel();
25111        transport.await??;
25112        Ok(())
25113    }
25114
25115    /// The Exit's SURB level must fall by what its store actually lost, not by what a keep-alive
25116    /// could have carried.
25117    ///
25118    /// Keep-alives are Start-protocol traffic, so they never pass through `session_rx`, which is
25119    /// where data packets book both the SURBs saved and the ones the full store evicted. Booking
25120    /// `max_surbs()` alone here counts every SURB a keep-alive *could* carry as if it had been
25121    /// retained: during a PIX fill (the gnosis_vpn report's ~30 keep-alives/s) the Exit reported
25122    /// 10,597–12,263 SURBs for a ring that could hold at most 1,032, and then spent against that
25123    /// figure until the ring was empty.
25124    ///
25125    /// Each keep-alive is booked once, by `dispatch_message`. The test lets the Start task handle both
25126    /// keep-alives before it reads, so a second booking there would show.
25127    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25128    async fn keep_alive_surbs_must_be_booked_with_their_evictions() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25129        let mgr: TestManager = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
25130        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
25131        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25132        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
25133
25134        // The Exit side of a Session: it receives the Entry's keep-alives and books their SURBs.
25135        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
25136        let _rx = mgr.pre_populate_session_with_receiver(pseudonym, DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()));
25137
25138        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("slot must exist")?;
25139        let estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
25140        drop(slot);
25141
25142        // A keep-alive with no SURBs of its own is not evidence that it retained any: the packet
25143        // info says both what arrived and what the full store dropped to make room.
25144        let keep_alive = |saved: usize, evicted: usize| -> anyhow::Result<ApplicationDataIn> {
25145            Ok(ApplicationDataIn {
25146                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
25147                    session_id: pseudonym,
25148                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
25149                    additional_data: 1_000,
25150                })
25151                .try_into()?,
25152                packet_info: IncomingPacketInfo {
25153                    num_saved_surbs: saved,
25154                    num_evicted_surbs: evicted,
25155                    ..Default::default()
25156                },
25157            })
25158        };
25159
25160        // One keep-alive whose SURBs all landed, one whose SURBs were all evicted on arrival. Seven is all a
25161        // keep-alive can carry: eight SURBs fit in an empty packet, and the message takes one's room.
25162        mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, keep_alive(7, 0)?)?;
25163        mgr.dispatch_message(pseudonym, keep_alive(7, 7)?)?;
25164
25165        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
25166            loop {
25167                if estimator.estimate_surbs_produced() == 14 {
25168                    break;
25169                }
25170                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
25171            }
25172        })
25173        .await
25174        .context("the keep-alives never reached the estimator")?;
25175
25176        // A second booking would land after the wait above, once the Start task gets to the keep-alives.
25177        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
25178        assert_eq!(
25179            14,
25180            estimator.estimate_surbs_produced(),
25181            "each keep-alive must be booked once"
25182        );
25183        assert_eq!(
25184            7,
25185            estimator.saturating_diff(),
25186            "the level must be what the store kept, not the SURBs the keep-alives could have carried"
25187        );
25188
25189        handle.abort();
25190        Ok(())
25191    }
25192
25193    /// A keep-alive that carries no SURBs at all must book none.
25194    ///
25195    /// The bound `max_surbs()` is what the message *could* carry, and a keep-alive sent with
25196    /// `max_surbs_in_packet` of zero carries nothing. At the report's fill rate that bound alone
25197    /// inflated the Exit's level by several times the ring's whole capacity.
25198    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25199    async fn a_surbless_keep_alive_must_not_book_surbs() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25200        let mgr: TestManager = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
25201        let (sender, handle) = mock_packet_planning(MockMsgSender::new());
25202        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25203        mgr.start(sender, new_session_tx, None, None)?;
25204
25205        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
25206        let _rx = mgr.pre_populate_session_with_receiver(pseudonym, DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()));
25207
25208        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("slot must exist")?;
25209        let estimator = slot.surb_estimator.clone();
25210        drop(slot);
25211
25212        mgr.dispatch_message(
25213            pseudonym,
25214            ApplicationDataIn {
25215                data: HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
25216                    session_id: pseudonym,
25217                    flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerTarget.into(),
25218                    additional_data: 1_000,
25219                })
25220                .try_into()?,
25221                packet_info: Default::default(),
25222            },
25223        )?;
25224
25225        // Give the Start-protocol worker time to have run, then assert the absence rather than racing it.
25226        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
25227        assert_eq!(
25228            0,
25229            estimator.estimate_surbs_produced(),
25230            "a keep-alive with no SURBs must not be booked as carrying the packet's maximum"
25231        );
25232
25233        handle.abort();
25234        Ok(())
25235    }

25237    /// Verifies that a session is evicted after the `idle_timeout` fires, without needing an explicit close.
25238    ///
25239    /// ## Steps
25240    /// 1. A `SessionManager` is configured with `maximum_sessions: 1` and `idle_timeout: 100ms`.
25241    /// 2. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` creates one session — confirmed active.
25242    /// 3. The test sleeps 200ms (well past the 100ms timeout), then calls `sessions.run_pending_tasks()` to drive the
25243    ///    eviction timer.
25244    /// 4. `active_sessions` is empty, confirming the idle session was cleaned up without an explicit close call.
25245    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25246    async fn session_manager_should_evict_idle_session_and_call_close_callback() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25247        use hopr_utils::network_types::prelude::SealedHost;
25248
25249        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
25250            maximum_sessions: 1,
25251            idle_timeout: Duration::from_millis(100),
25252            ..Default::default()
25253        };
25254        let mgr: SessionManager<futures::channel::mpsc::UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25255            SessionManager::new(cfg);
25256
25257        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
25258        transport
25259            .expect_send_message()
25260            .times(1)
25261            .returning(|_, _| futures::future::ok(()).boxed());
25262
25263        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25264        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
25265            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
25266            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
25267        });
25268        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
25269        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
25270        assert!(mgr.is_started());
25271
25272        // Create first session
25273        let pseudonym1 = HoprPseudonym::random();
25274        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
25275            pseudonym1,
25276            StartInitiation {
25277                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
25278                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
25279                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities::empty(),
25280                additional_data: 0,
25281            },
25282        )
25283        .await?;
25284
25285        // Verify first session exists
25286        assert_eq!(mgr.active_sessions().len(), 1);
25287
25288        // Wait for the session to expire (idle_timeout = 100ms)
25289        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
25290        mgr.sessions.run_pending_tasks();
25291
25292        // Verify session was evicted (cache should be empty now)
25293        assert_eq!(
25294            mgr.active_sessions().len(),
25295            0,
25296            "idle session should be evicted after timeout"
25297        );
25298
25299        Ok(())
25300    }

25390    /// Verifies that `new_session` rejects `UsePIX` when the return path has 0 intermediate hops.
25391    ///
25392    /// PIX shares are encrypted with the first relayer's ticket-challenge solution and carried
25393    /// in return-path SURBs. With 0 intermediate hops (a direct Exit→Entry SURB), there is no
25394    /// relayer to provide the challenge solution, so shares are never embedded — the ongoing
25395    /// PIX share delivery mechanism is dead and the Exit's quota is never replenished.
25396    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25397    async fn new_session_rejects_usepix_with_zero_return_hops() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25398        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25399            SessionManager::new(Default::default());
25400
25401        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
25402        // The error happens before any message is sent, so expect_send_message should NOT fire.
25403        transport.expect_send_message().times(0);
25404
25405        let (sender, _handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
25406        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25407        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
25408        assert!(mgr.is_started());
25409
25410        let result = mgr
25411            .new_session(
25412                Address::from(&ChainKeypair::random()),
25413                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
25414                SessionClientConfig {
25415                    capabilities: Capability::UsePIX.into(),
25416                    surb_management: None,
25417                    forward_path_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(1.try_into()?),
25418                    return_path_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(0.try_into()?),
25419                    ..Default::default()
25420                },
25421            )
25422            .await;
25423
25424        let err = result.unwrap_err();
25425        let msg = format!("{err:?}");
25426        assert!(
25427            msg.contains("UsePIX requires at least 1 intermediate hop on the return path"),
25428            "expected return-path guard error, got: {msg}"
25429        );

25431        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
25432        // No challenge slot was consumed because the validations run before insert_into_next_slot.
25433        assert_eq!(
25434            mgr.session_initiations.entry_count(),
25435            0,
25436            "session_initiations must remain empty when UsePIX is rejected"
25437        );
25438
25439        sender.close_channel();
25440        _handle.await??;
25441        Ok(())
25442    }

25506    /// The fill fractions must be range-checked before anything computes with them.
25507    ///
25508    /// This validator runs *before* `validate_pix_supervision` on both paths that reach it:
25509    /// `SessionManager::start` calls it first, and in `HoprProtocolConfig` it is a field validator
25510    /// while the other is a schema-level one. So it cannot assume the ranges have already been
25511    /// checked — and it feeds `finish_fraction` straight into `Duration::mul_f64`, which panics on a
25512    /// `NaN`, on a negative, and on a product the monotonic clock cannot hold. A single
25513    /// `finish_fraction: .nan` in a YAML file would therefore abort the node at load instead of being
25514    /// reported as the configuration error it is.
25515    ///
25516    /// The finite out-of-range values do not panic, which is why they are here too: they compute a
25517    /// floor that is wrong in the permissive direction, and nothing downstream ever says so.
25518    #[test]
25519    fn fill_fractions_are_rejected_before_the_ceiling_arithmetic_runs() {
25520        let with_fill = |fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig| IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25521            supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25522                fill,
25523                ..Default::default()
25524            },
25525            ..Default::default()
25526        };
25527
25528        for finish_fraction in [f64::NAN, -1.0, f64::INFINITY, 2.0] {
25529            let cfg = with_fill(crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
25530                finish_fraction,
25531                ..Default::default()
25532            });
25533            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
25534            assert!(
25535                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("fill.finish_fraction")),
25536                "a finish_fraction of {finish_fraction} must be refused rather than multiplied, got {outcome:?}"
25537            );
25538        }
25539
25540        for loss_margin in [f64::NAN, -0.5, 1.0] {
25541            let cfg = with_fill(crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
25542                loss_margin,
25543                ..Default::default()
25544            });
25545            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
25546            assert!(
25547                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("fill.loss_margin")),
25548                "a loss_margin of {loss_margin} must be refused, got {outcome:?}"
25549            );
25550        }
25551
25552        validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&IncomingSessionPixConfig::default(), MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE)
25553            .expect("the shipped defaults must still validate");
25554    }

25556    /// A zero recovery deadline must be named as such on both fill paths, rather than reaching the
25557    /// fill arithmetic and being reported as an infinite rate requirement.
25558    #[test]
25559    fn a_zero_recovery_deadline_is_refused_as_zero_with_and_without_fill() {
25560        for enabled in [true, false] {
25561            let cfg = IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25562                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25563                    max_recovery_time: Duration::ZERO,
25564                    fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
25565                        enabled,
25566                        ..Default::default()
25567                    },
25568                    ..Default::default()
25569                },
25570                ..Default::default()
25571            };
25572            let outcome = validate_incoming_session_pix_config(&cfg, MAX_ASSUMED_SESSION_PACKET_RATE);
25573            assert!(
25574                matches!(&outcome, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(msg)) if msg.contains("max_recovery_time must be non-zero")),
25575                "with fill enabled = {enabled}, a zero deadline must be refused as zero, got {outcome:?}"
25576            );
25577        }
25578    }

25580    /// The fill heartbeat is clamped at *both* ends for a programmatically assembled config.
25581    ///
25582    /// The upper clamp is the one every other supervisor duration takes. The lower one is what stops
25583    /// a zero period, which `validate_pix_supervision` rejects and nothing in this crate calls: with
25584    /// it, `FillRate::as_packets_per_sec` reports zero for the heartbeat, so the planner's floor is
25585    /// zero, both heartbeat branches of `FillPlanner::bound` return a zero-period rate, and
25586    /// `PixFillControl::apply` hands `set_rate_per_unit(1, 1µs)` to the controller — which
25587    /// `RateController::MIN_DELAY` turns into 10 000 packets/s. The `max_rate` ceiling never sees it,
25588    /// so the one bound on this node's self-generated egress would be bypassed by the one field left
25589    /// unbounded below.
25590    #[test]
25591    fn programmatic_fill_heartbeat_is_clamped_to_a_positive_period() {
25592        let normalized = |heartbeat: Duration| {
25593            let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25594                SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
25595                    pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25596                        supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25597                            fill: crate::supervision::PixFillConfig {
25598                                heartbeat,
25599                                ..Default::default()
25600                            },
25601                            ..Default::default()
25602                        },
25603                        ..Default::default()
25604                    },
25605                    ..Default::default()
25606                });
25607            mgr.cfg.pix_config.supervision.fill.heartbeat
25608        };
25609
25610        // The exact dual of the `max_rate` ceiling, so the two clamps cannot drift apart.
25611        let floor = Duration::from_secs(1) / crate::supervision::MAX_FILL_RATE;
25612        assert_eq!(
25613            floor,
25614            normalized(Duration::ZERO),
25615            "a zero heartbeat must be raised to the period of MAX_FILL_RATE"
25616        );
25617        assert_eq!(
25618            crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION,
25619            normalized(Duration::MAX),
25620            "an unrepresentable heartbeat must be lowered to the same cap every other deadline takes"
25621        );
25622
25623        // Which is the property the clamp exists for: a rate the planner can divide by.
25624        assert!(
25625            FillRate::once_per(normalized(Duration::ZERO)).as_packets_per_sec() > 0.0,
25626            "the clamped heartbeat must be a rate the planner can compare against its ceiling"
25627        );
25628    }
25629
25630    /// Supervisor durations a programmatic caller supplies must be clamped, not trusted.
25631    ///
25632    /// `validate_pix_supervision` rejects these, but nothing in this crate calls `validate` — a
25633    /// `SessionManagerConfig` assembled in code reaches the supervisor exactly as written. And the
25634    /// failure is silent in the worst direction: `Instant::checked_add` returns `None` for a duration
25635    /// the monotonic clock cannot represent, and every phase reads an absent deadline as *no
25636    /// deadline*, so the over-large value disables the rule rather than relaxing it.
25637    ///
25638    /// The two batch-scaled deadlines are clamped by what is actually armed, so a batch of `n` leaves
25639    /// each of them at a cap `n` times smaller.
25640    #[test]
25641    fn programmatic_supervisor_durations_are_clamped_to_a_representable_deadline() {
25642        const BATCH: usize = 4;
25643        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25644            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
25645                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25646                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25647                        ssas_per_request: BATCH,
25648                        max_ssa_delivery_time: Duration::MAX,
25649                        max_deposit_wait: Duration::MAX,
25650                        max_recovery_idle: Duration::MAX,
25651                        max_recovery_time: Duration::MAX,
25652                        tombstone_retention_window: Duration::MAX,
25653                        ..Default::default()
25654                    },
25655                    ..Default::default()
25656                },
25657                ..Default::default()
25658            });
25659
25660        let sup = &mgr.cfg.pix_config.supervision;
25661        let cap = crate::supervision::MAX_SUPERVISOR_DURATION;
25662        let per_cycle_cap = cap / BATCH as u32;
25663
25664        assert_eq!(per_cycle_cap, sup.max_ssa_delivery_time);
25665        assert_eq!(per_cycle_cap, sup.max_deposit_wait);
25666        assert_eq!(cap, sup.max_recovery_time);
25667        assert_eq!(cap, sup.tombstone_retention_window);
25668
25669        // `max_recovery_idle` is bounded by something tighter than the clock: it must stay strictly
25670        // under the reconstructor's `unused_verifier_lifetime`, or the supervisor waits on a cycle
25671        // whose state was reclaimed long before. Normalized against the default reconstructor, which
25672        // is the one `SessionManager::new` can see; `start` re-checks against the installed one.
25673        let lifetime = hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig::default().unused_verifier_lifetime;
25674        assert!(
25675            sup.max_recovery_idle < lifetime,
25676            "clamped max_recovery_idle ({:?}) must stay under the reconstructor lifetime ({lifetime:?})",
25677            sup.max_recovery_idle
25678        );
25679        // The reconstructor's registration lifetime is raised past the clamped delivery window, which the
25680        // validator requires to be shorter than it; everything else is the default's.
25681        let long_lived = hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig {
25682            incomplete_commitment_lifetime: cap + Duration::from_secs(1),
25683            ..Default::default()
25684        };
25685        crate::supervision::validate_pix_supervision(sup, &long_lived)
25686            .expect("a normalized config must satisfy every cross-component invariant, not only representability");
25687
25688        // Which is exactly the condition that makes every deadline representable.
25689        let now = std::time::Instant::now();
25690        for dur in [
25691            crate::supervision::scaled_deadline(sup.max_ssa_delivery_time, sup.ssas_per_request),
25692            crate::supervision::scaled_deadline(sup.max_deposit_wait, sup.ssas_per_request),
25693            sup.max_recovery_idle,
25694            sup.max_recovery_time,
25695            sup.tombstone_retention_window,
25696        ] {
25697            assert!(
25698                now.checked_add(dur).is_some(),
25699                "a clamped duration ({dur:?}) must still produce a deadline"
25700            );
25701        }
25702    }
25703
25704    /// Normalizing against the default reconstructor is not enough when a caller installs a
25705    /// different one.
25706    ///
25707    /// `SessionManager::new` cannot see the reconstructor — it arrives with the toolbox at `start` —
25708    /// so its clamp can only assume the defaults. A caller pairing a shorter
25709    /// `unused_verifier_lifetime` with a supervisor config that was valid against the defaults gets
25710    /// a supervisor that outlives the state it is waiting on. That must be an error rather than a
25711    /// silent clamp: at `start` both halves were chosen deliberately, and overriding one of them
25712    /// would be answering a question the caller did not ask.
25713    #[test]
25714    fn start_rejects_a_supervisor_config_the_installed_reconstructor_cannot_support() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25715        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
25716
25717        // Valid against the defaults — 10 min sits well under the default 30 min lifetime — and
25718        // therefore untouched by the constructor's clamp.
25719        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
25720            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25721                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25722                    max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(600),
25723                    ..Default::default()
25724                },
25725                ..Default::default()
25726            },
25727            ..Default::default()
25728        };
25729        crate::supervision::validate_pix_supervision(&cfg.pix_config.supervision, &SsaReconstructorConfig::default())
25730            .expect("the fixture must be valid against the default reconstructor");
25731
25732        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> = SessionManager::new(cfg);
25733
25734        // But the reconstructor actually installed reclaims a cycle after 60 s.
25735        let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
25736            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
25737            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig {
25738                unused_verifier_lifetime: Duration::from_secs(60),
25739                ..Default::default()
25740            })
25741            .into(),
25742        );
25743
25744        let (tx, _rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
25745        let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25746        let started = mgr.start(tx, new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None);
25747
25748        assert!(
25749            matches!(started, Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(_))),
25750            "starting with a reconstructor that cannot support the supervisor config must fail, got {started:?}"
25751        );
25752
25753        Ok(())
25754    }

25756    /// A programmatically assembled manager must enforce the same incoming-PIX cross-field rules
25757    /// as the serialized transport configuration before it starts accepting Sessions.
25758    #[allow(clippy::reversed_empty_ranges)]
25759    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25760    async fn start_rejects_each_invalid_incoming_pix_cross_field_combination() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25761        let valid = IncomingSessionPixConfig::default();
25762        let widest = max_cycle_budget_for_quota(*valid.quota_range.end(), valid.supervision.ssas_per_request);
25763        let invalid_configs = [
25764            (
25765                "empty quota range",
25766                IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25767                    quota_range: 100..=10,
25768                    ..valid.clone()
25769                },
25770                "quota_range",
25771            ),
25772            (
25773                "recovery deadline below one accepted cycle",
25774                IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25775                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25776                        max_recovery_time: Duration::from_secs(1),
25777                        ..valid.supervision.clone()
25778                    },
25779                    ..valid.clone()
25780                },
25781                "max_recovery_time",
25782            ),
25783            (
25784                "live-cycle budget below one accepted cycle",
25785                IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25786                    max_live_cycle_bytes: widest - 1,
25787                    ..valid
25788                },
25789                "max_live_cycle_bytes",
25790            ),
25791        ];
25792
25793        for (case, pix_config, expected_field) in invalid_configs {
25794            let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25795                SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
25796                    pix_config,
25797                    ..Default::default()
25798                });
25799            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
25800                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
25801                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
25802            );
25803            let (tx, _rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
25804            let (new_session_tx, _new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25805
25806            match mgr.start(tx, new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None) {
25807                Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(message)) => assert!(
25808                    message.contains(expected_field),
25809                    "{case} should identify {expected_field}, got: {message}"
25810                ),
25811                Err(error) => anyhow::bail!("{case} returned the wrong error: {error}"),
25812                Ok(_) => anyhow::bail!("{case} was accepted"),
25813            }
25814        }
25815
25816        Ok(())
25817    }

25819    /// A rejected PIX configuration must not consume the manager's one-shot start state.
25820    ///
25821    /// Validation is fallible and happens before any worker is spawned, so callers must be able to
25822    /// correct the toolbox (or start without PIX) and retry the same manager. Otherwise `start`
25823    /// reports an ordinary configuration error while leaving `is_started() == false`, but the
25824    /// already-filled message-sender lock makes every retry fail with `AlreadyStarted`.
25825    ///
25826    /// On a runtime because the retry now gets far enough to spawn the manager's workers, which is
25827    /// the whole point — before the fix it returned `AlreadyStarted` before reaching them.
25828    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25829    async fn rejected_pix_start_does_not_poison_a_retry() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25830        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
25831
25832        let mgr: SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>> =
25833            SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
25834                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25835                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
25836                        max_recovery_idle: Duration::from_secs(600),
25837                        ..Default::default()
25838                    },
25839                    ..Default::default()
25840                },
25841                ..Default::default()
25842            });
25843
25844        let (invalid_pix, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
25845            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig::default()).into(),
25846            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig {
25847                unused_verifier_lifetime: Duration::from_secs(60),
25848                ..Default::default()
25849            })
25850            .into(),
25851        );
25852        let (first_tx, _first_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
25853        let (first_notifier, _first_notifications) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25854        assert!(matches!(
25855            mgr.start(first_tx, first_notifier, Some(invalid_pix), None),
25856            Err(TransportSessionError::InvalidConfig(_))
25857        ));
25858        assert!(
25859            !mgr.is_started(),
25860            "a rejected start must not report the manager as running"
25861        );
25862
25863        let (retry_tx, _retry_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
25864        let (retry_notifier, _retry_notifications) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25865        let retry = mgr.start(retry_tx, retry_notifier, None, None);
25866        assert!(
25867            retry.is_ok(),
25868            "a configuration error must leave the manager retryable, got {retry:?}"
25869        );
25870
25871        Ok(())
25872    }

25901    /// Verifies that an incoming Session whose PIX quota cannot reach the acceptable range within
25902    /// the configured dynamic batch ceiling is rejected with
25903    /// `StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams`.
25904    ///
25905    /// ## Steps
25906    /// 1. Bob's manager accepts exactly two times the Entry's per-SSA quota, but leaves the dynamic batch ceiling at
25907    ///    its default of one.
25908    /// 2. The test offers valid PIX dimensions whose quota would therefore need a batch of two.
25909    /// 3. `handle_incoming_session_initiation` is called with `Capability::UsePIX` and the out-of-range quota.
25910    /// 4. Bob's manager sends a `SessionError` back to the peer with reason `UnacceptablePixParams`.
25911    /// 5. The test receives the error on a one-shot channel and asserts `err.reason == UnacceptablePixParams` and
25912    ///    `err.challenge == MIN_CHALLENGE`.
25913    /// 6. `num_active_sessions` is 0, confirming no session slot was created.
25914    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
25915    async fn incoming_session_with_unacceptable_pix_quota_is_rejected() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
25916        use std::sync::Arc;
25917
25918        use hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig;
25919        use hopr_protocol_start::{StartErrorReason, StartInitiation};
25920        use tokio::sync::oneshot;
25921
25922        let params = small_pix_params();
25923        let quota_per_ssa = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
25924        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
25925            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
25926                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
25927                threshold: 2,
25928                surplus_shares: TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES,
25929            })
25930            .into(),
25931            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
25932        );
25933
25934        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
25935            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
25936                quota_range: 2 * quota_per_ssa..=2 * quota_per_ssa,
25937                ..Default::default()
25938            },
25939            ..Default::default()
25940        });
25941
25942        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
25943        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
25944        let tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(tx)));
25945
25946        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
25947            let tx = tx.clone();
25948            Box::pin(async move {
25949                if let Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err)) =
25950                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
25951                    && let Some(tx) = tx.lock().unwrap().take()
25952                {
25953                    let _ = tx.send(err);
25954                }
25955                Ok(())
25956            })
25957        });
25958
25959        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
25960        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
25961        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
25962
25963        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
25964
25965        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
25966            alice_pseudonym,
25967            StartInitiation {
25968                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
25969                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
25970                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
25971                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0), Duration::ZERO),
25972            },
25973        )
25974        .await?;
25975
25976        let err = rx.await.context("send_message was never called")?;
25977        assert_eq!(err.reason, StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams);
25978        assert_eq!(err.identifier, ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(MIN_CHALLENGE));
25979        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0);
25980
25981        bob_sender.close_channel();
25982        bob_handle.await??;
25983        Ok(())
25984    }

26056    /// A node with no `PixToolbox` must refuse an incoming session that asks for `UsePIX`, rather
26057    /// than establish one it cannot run the PIX state machine for.
26058    ///
26059    /// This is the guard at the top of `handle_incoming_session_initiation`, and it was untested:
26060    /// the integration test named for it never negotiated PIX at all, so the absent toolbox was not
26061    /// the operative cause of anything it observed.
26062    ///
26063    /// The offered dimensions have to be ones `check_pix_params` *accepts*, and the test asserts
26064    /// that before exercising the handler. The fallthrough from a rejected `check_pix_params` emits
26065    /// the identical `StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams` under the identical
26066    /// `ErrorIdentifier::Challenge` and creates no session either, so with unacceptable dimensions
26067    /// nothing here could tell the two refusals apart — the guard could be deleted outright and
26068    /// this would still pass.
26069    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
26070    async fn incoming_usepix_session_is_rejected_when_no_pix_toolbox_is_installed() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
26071        use std::sync::Arc;
26072
26073        use hopr_protocol_start::{StartErrorReason, StartInitiation};
26074        use tokio::sync::oneshot;
26075
26076        // PIX not enforced, and the default `quota_range` ends exactly on the quota the default
26077        // dimensions imply, so the offer below sits inside it.
26078        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig::default());
26079
26080        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
26081        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
26082        let tx = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(tx)));
26083
26084        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
26085            let tx = tx.clone();
26086            Box::pin(async move {
26087                if let Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SessionError(err)) =
26088                    HoprStartProtocol::decode(data.data.application_tag, &data.data.plain_text)
26089                    && let Some(tx) = tx.lock().unwrap().take()
26090                {
26091                    let _ = tx.send(err);
26092                }
26093                Ok(())
26094            })
26095        });
26096
26097        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
26098        let (new_session_tx, _) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
26099        // No toolbox — the third argument is what a relay that does not participate in PIX gets.
26100        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, None, None)?;
26101
26102        let req = StartInitiation {
26103            challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
26104            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
26105            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::Segmentation | Capability::UsePIX),
26106            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
26107                DEFAULT_PIX_PARAMS.into_additional_data(0),
26108                Duration::ZERO,
26109            ),
26110        };
26111
26112        // What makes the missing toolbox the sole remaining cause of the refusal below.
26113        assert!(
26114            decode_and_check(&mgr, &req).is_some(),
26115            "the offered dimensions must be acceptable, or the refusal cannot be attributed to the guard"
26116        );
26117
26118        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(HoprPseudonym::random(), req)
26119            .await?;
26120
26121        let err = rx.await.context("send_message was never called")?;
26122        assert_eq!(err.reason, StartErrorReason::UnacceptablePixParams);
26123        assert_eq!(err.identifier, ErrorIdentifier::Challenge(MIN_CHALLENGE));
26124        assert_eq!(mgr.num_active_sessions(), 0, "no slot may be created for a refusal");
26125
26126        bob_sender.close_channel();
26127        bob_handle.await??;
26128        Ok(())
26129    }

26131    /// Verifies that the exit/responder (Bob) rejects an `SsaCommit` for a session that has no PIX
26132    /// state — i.e., the SSA commit is delivered with a session ID that Bob does not hold.
26133    ///
26134    /// ## Steps
26135    /// 1. Bob's manager is started with a `PixToolbox` and a PIX quota config. Alice's session initiation is processed
26136    ///    normally via `handle_incoming_session_initiation`, establishing a session with PIX state.
26137    /// 2. `handle_ssa_commit` is called with a completely different (random) session ID — one that Bob's manager does
26138    ///    not have.
26139    /// 3. The call returns an error matching `TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NonExistingSession)`,
26140    ///    confirming the exit rejects commits for unknown sessions.
26141    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
26142    async fn exit_rejects_ssa_commit_when_session_has_no_pix_state() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
26143        use std::collections::HashMap;
26144
26145        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
26146        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
26147
26148        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
26149            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
26150            threshold: 2,
26151            surplus_shares: 1,
26152        };
26153        let ssa_rec_config = SsaReconstructorConfig::default();
26154
26155        let (pix_toolbox, _) = PixToolbox::new(
26156            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
26157            SsaReconstructor::new(ssa_rec_config).into(),
26158        );
26159
26160        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
26161            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
26162                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
26163                ..Default::default()
26164            },
26165            ..Default::default()
26166        });
26167
26168        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
26169        bob_transport
26170            .expect_send_message()
26171            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
26172        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest.

26223    /// Verifies that a session is closed on the very first `UnverifiableShares` PIX event.

26250

26258
26259        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
26260        bob_transport
26261            .expect_send_message()
26262            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
26263        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest.
26264        bob_transport
26265            .expect_send_message()

26268        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);

26270        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
