27472    /// The boundary is discounted by the loss a cycle tolerates, not by the surplus ratio.
27473    ///
27474    /// The Exit unlocks a share when the *first relayer* acknowledges its returned packet, which is
27475    /// upstream of the Entry — so everything lost after that point is progress the Exit legitimately
27476    /// has and this node cannot observe, and demanding the undiscounted emission boundary would refuse
27477    /// conforming Exits on any lossy path. But the discount is also what an Exit can withhold for good
27478    /// and still be funded, so it may be no larger than the loss a cycle survives.
27479    ///
27480    /// The surplus ratio `s/(t+s)` is break-even, not survival. At the deployed split it discounted
27481    /// 71.2 % where a cycle tolerates 50.3 %, and put the bar at 23.9 % of a cycle — below the shares a
27482    /// lossless Exit has necessarily unlocked by the earliest point it may ask at all.
27483    ///
27484    /// The bar is then set [`SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS`] standard deviations below the mean an
27485    /// Exit at that loss returns, so that one losing exactly the tolerance is not refused for the
27486    /// variance of its own arrivals.
27487    ///
27488    /// Pinned at the deployed dimensions because the resulting fraction is not something a reader can
27489    /// check by inspection, and it is what decides when real money moves.
27490    #[test]
27491    fn the_successor_boundary_is_discounted_by_the_loss_a_cycle_tolerates() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27492        use crate::{DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA, DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY, DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES};
27493
27494        let params = PixParams::try_new(
27495            DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA,
27496            DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY,
27497            DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES,
27498            LOCAL_PIX_SUITE,
27499        )?;
27500        let cycle = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
27501        assert_eq!(454_656, cycle);
27502
27503        let undiscounted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
27504            &params,
27505            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
27506        );
27507        assert_eq!(357_274, undiscounted);
27508
27509        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 357 274 × (1 − L) = 177 606.89 and σ = √(357 274 · L · (1 − L)) =
27510        // 298.86, at L = 0.502 883 257 4… computed independently at 90 significant digits. (At a
27511        // window of 256 the boundary was 377 498 and the bar 186 431.)
27512        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
27513        assert_eq!(176_411, required);
27514
27515        let tolerated = params.tolerated_share_loss();
27516        let mean = undiscounted as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
27517        let deviation = (undiscounted as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
27518        let bound = mean - SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * deviation;
27519        assert!(
27520            required as f64 <= bound && bound < required as f64 + 1.0,
27521            "the bar must be the mean arrivals at the tolerated loss less {SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS} of their \
27522             standard deviations, floored, and nothing else: {bound} against {required}"
27523        );
27524
27525        let fraction = required as f64 / cycle as f64;
27526        assert!(
27527            (0.387..0.389).contains(&fraction),
27528            "the deployed successor boundary must sit at ~38.8% of a cycle's returned packets, got {fraction}"
27529        );
27530
27531        // A lossless conforming Exit asks no earlier than `ceil(0.85 × 4096)` recovered polynomials,
27532        // each of which took `t` unlocked shares before any of its surplus. A bar below that funds the
27533        // next deposit on less delivered service than the useful shares the Exit is claiming to have
27534        // recovered from.
27535        let unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit =
27536            (hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD * DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA as f64).ceil() as u64
27537                * DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY as u64;
27538        assert_eq!(111_424, unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit);
27539        assert!(
27540            required >= unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit,
27541            "the successor boundary ({required}) must not sit below what a lossless Exit has unlocked when it may \
27542             first ask ({unlocked_by_a_lossless_exit})"
27543        );
27544
27545        // Each further cycle of a batch is demanded in full at the same discount, less only what the
27546        // margin grows by — and that grows with the square root of the target, so by less than the
27547        // margin a cycle would get on its own. The floor can move either end by one packet.
27548        let whole_first_cycle = required_returned_packets(&params, 2) - required;
27549        let discounted_cycle = cycle as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
27550        let lone_cycle_margin = SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * (cycle as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
27551        assert!(
27552            (discounted_cycle - lone_cycle_margin - 1.0..=discounted_cycle + 1.0).contains(&(whole_first_cycle as f64)),
27553            "a batch of two must demand the first cycle's whole discounted worth, less under {lone_cycle_margin} of \
27554             margin, plus the second's boundary; got {whole_first_cycle} for the first cycle against \
27555             {discounted_cycle}"
27556        );
27557
27558        Ok(())
27559    }
27560
27561    /// The successor gate follows the surplus the Entry bought.
27562    ///
27563    /// The discount is the tolerance of the *negotiated* split, so an Entry that expects unreliable
27564    /// return relayers and buys more surplus loosens its own gate by exactly that much: how strict the
27565    /// gate is follows from the Entry's insurance choice rather than being a knob of its own. At
27566    /// `4096 × (2 + 102)` a cycle tolerates ~86 % share loss, and the bar falls to ~10.4 % of a cycle's
27567    /// packets against the deployed split's ~38.8 %.
27568    ///
27569    /// Driven through `handle_ssa_request` at the real dimensions rather than only through
27570    /// [`required_returned_packets`], because the property is that the gate reads the Session's own
27571    /// parameters — a mirror of its arithmetic cannot show that.
27572    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
27573    async fn the_successor_gate_follows_the_surplus_the_entry_bought() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27574        let params = PixParams::try_new(4096, 2, 102, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
27575        let cycle = params.polys_per_ssa() as u64 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u64;
27576        let undiscounted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
27577            &params,
27578            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
27579        );
27580
27581        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
27582        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 320 410 × (1 − L) = 45 193.78 and σ = 197.03, at L = 0.858 950 169 2…
27583        // computed independently at 90 significant digits. (At a window of 256: 346 522 and 48 057.)
27584        assert_eq!(320_410, undiscounted);
27585        assert_eq!(44_405, required);
27586
27587        let fraction = required as f64 / cycle as f64;
27588        assert!(
27589            (0.103..0.105).contains(&fraction),
27590            "the successor boundary of 4096 x (2 + 102) must sit at ~10.4% of a cycle's returned packets, got \
27591             {fraction}"
27592        );
27593
27594        // And the gate itself, not only its mirror: with emission past the boundary, one emission
27595        // window short of `required` is refused outright — past the near-miss wait, so at once —
27596        // and the rest of it admits the successor.
27597        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
27598            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
27599        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
27600            pseudonym,
27601            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
27602        )
27603        .await
27604        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
27605        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27606
27607        for sent in 1..=undiscounted as u32 {
27608            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
27609        }
27610
27611        let short = hopr_protocol_pix::SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64 + 1;
27612        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required - short);
27613        let err = mgr
27614            .handle_ssa_request(
27615                pseudonym,
27616                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
27617            )
27618            .await
27619            .expect_err("a successor short of the bought tolerance's boundary must be refused");
27620        assert!(
27621            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
27622            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
27623        );
27624        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27625
27626        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, short);
27627        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
27628            pseudonym,
27629            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
27630        )
27631        .await
27632        .context("a successor at the bought tolerance's boundary must be admitted")?;
27633        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27634
27635        bob_sender.close_channel();
27636        bob_handle.await??;
27637        Ok(())
27638    }
27639
27640    /// A tiny boundary under a huge surplus must still demand one returned packet.
27641    ///
27642    /// At `128 × (2 + 255)` the early-recovery boundary is 237 packets against a tolerated loss of
27643    /// ~95 %: μ − 4σ is below one, and an unfloored bar of zero funds the successor on the Entry's
27644    /// own emission with nothing returned — the near-miss wait is skipped on zero observed packets, so
27645    /// nothing else would stop it.
27646    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
27647    async fn the_successor_gate_demands_a_returned_packet_whatever_the_surplus() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27648        let params = PixParams::try_new(128, 2, 255, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
27649        let target = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
27650            &params,
27651            hopr_protocol_pix::MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD,
27652        );
27653        assert_eq!(237, target);
27654
27655        let tolerated = params.tolerated_share_loss();
27656        let mean = target as f64 * (1.0 - tolerated);
27657        let deviation = (target as f64 * tolerated * (1.0 - tolerated)).sqrt();
27658        let raw_bound = mean - SUCCESSOR_GATE_ARRIVAL_SIGMAS * deviation;
27659        assert!(
27660            raw_bound < 1.0,
27661            "the unfloored bound must be below one packet, got {raw_bound}"
27662        );
27663        assert_eq!(1, required_returned_packets(&params, 1));
27664
27665        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
27666            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
27667        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
27668            pseudonym,
27669            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
27670        )
27671        .await
27672        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
27673        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27674
27675        for sent in 1..=target as u32 {
27676            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
27677        }
27678
27679        let err = mgr
27680            .handle_ssa_request(
27681                pseudonym,
27682                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
27683            )
27684            .await
27685            .expect_err("a successor with no returned packet must be refused");
27686        assert!(
27687            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
27688            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
27689        );
27690        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27691
27692        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1);
27693        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
27694            pseudonym,
27695            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
27696        )
27697        .await
27698        .context("a successor with one returned packet must be admitted")?;
27699        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
27700
27701        bob_sender.close_channel();
27702        bob_handle.await??;
27703        Ok(())
27704    }
27705
27706    /// The bar is a lower confidence bound on an honest Exit's arrivals, not their mean.
27707    ///
27708    /// Pinned against `floor(μ − 4σ)` computed outside this crate from independently computed
27709    /// tolerances: at the deployed split, at one an Entry distrusting its return relayers may buy, and
27710    /// at the derived `2048 × (64 + 123)`, where the mean refused an honest Exit. The ends are what tie
27711    /// the bound to the split — no surplus, no tolerance and so no slack; a tolerance near one asks
27712    /// for one packet rather than for a negative count or nothing.
27713    #[test]
27714    fn the_successor_bar_is_a_lower_confidence_bound_on_honest_arrivals() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27715        for target in [0, 1, 377_498, 1 << 40] {
27716            assert_eq!(
27717                target,
27718                successor_required_packets(target, 0.0),
27719                "a split tolerating no loss must be demanded its whole target"
27720            );
27721        }
27722
27723        // 100 × 0.01 − 4 × √(100 × 0.01 × 0.99) < 0: the margin outweighs the mean.
27724        // ... but never below one packet of a non-zero boundary, and a zero boundary stays zero.
27725        assert_eq!(1, successor_required_packets(100, 0.99));
27726        assert_eq!(1, successor_required_packets(377_498, 1.0));
27727        for loss in [0.0, 0.5, 0.99, 1.0] {
27728            assert_eq!(
27729                0,
27730                successor_required_packets(0, loss),
27731                "a zero boundary demands nothing at L = {loss}"
27732            );
27733        }
27734
27735        // The boundaries of the 512-polynomial emission window, pinned in the tests above. (At a
27736        // window of 256: 377 498 → 186 431, 346 522 → 48 057 and 303 565 → 150 641.)
27737        for (polys, threshold, surplus, target, required) in [
27738            (4096, 32, 79, 357_274, 176_411),
27739            (4096, 2, 102, 320_410, 44_405),
27740            (2048, 64, 123, 319_693, 158_674),
27741        ] {
27742            let params = PixParams::try_new(polys, threshold, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
27743            assert_eq!(
27744                required,
27745                successor_required_packets(target, params.tolerated_share_loss()),
27746                "{polys} x ({threshold} + {surplus}) must demand {required} of a {target}-packet boundary"
27747            );
27748        }
27749
27750        Ok(())
27751    }
27752
27753    /// An honest Exit losing the tolerated share fraction must not lose its Session to the variance
27754    /// of its own arrivals.
27755    ///
27756    /// Losses past the first return relayer cost the Exit nothing — the relayer has acknowledged, so
27757    /// the share is unlocked — and it asks at the lossless boundary with `Binomial(target, 1 − L)` of
27758    /// its packets having reached the Entry. A bar at their mean refused it about half the time, and
27759    /// at this split ~18 % of the time by more than the near-miss window, at once. The Exit's re-sends
27760    /// would since have caught the next one, but a bar that refuses a conforming Exit one time in five
27761    /// still costs it an interval of delay and a request per interval until its packets arrive.
27762    ///
27763    /// The draw is a reproduction of that at the surplus derived for `2048 × 64`: 159 028 of 319 693
27764    /// packets arrived, 777 short of the mean (an independent review's draw at the window of 256 was
27765    /// 391 short; the window is now twice as wide, so the fixture has to fall further short to be more
27766    /// than one window short).
27767    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
27768    async fn an_honest_exit_at_the_tolerated_loss_is_not_refused_for_its_variance() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27769        use hopr_protocol_pix::{MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD, SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW, default_surplus_for};
27770
27771        // 319 693 independent fair bits: `sum(r.getrandbits(1) for _ in range(319_693))` with
27772        // `r = random.Random(60)`. (Seed 3 and 303 565 bits, 151 352 arrivals, at a window of 256.)
27773        const ARRIVED: u64 = 159_028;
27774
27775        let params = PixParams::try_new(2048, 64, default_surplus_for(2048, 64), LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
27776        assert_eq!(123, params.surplus_shares());
27777        assert!(
27778            IncomingSessionPixConfig::default()
27779                .quota_range
27780                .contains(&pix_params_to_quota(&params)),
27781            "the split must be one a default Exit accepts"
27782        );
27783
27784        let boundary = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(&params, MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD);
27785        assert_eq!(319_693, boundary);
27786
27787        // floor(μ − 4σ) for μ = 319 693 × (1 − L) = 159 805.20 and σ = 282.71, at
27788        // L = 0.500 129 201 488 385 6.
27789        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
27790        assert_eq!(158_674, required);
27791
27792        // What this pins: a bar at the mean would have refused the draw outright, never reaching the
27793        // near-miss wait, where the confidence bound admits it.
27794        let at_the_mean = (boundary as f64 * (1.0 - params.tolerated_share_loss())) as u64;
27795        assert_eq!(159_805, at_the_mean);
27796        assert!(
27797            ARRIVED + (SHARE_EMISSION_WINDOW as u64) < at_the_mean,
27798            "the draw must fall more than one emission window short of the mean, or a mean bar would have waited"
27799        );
27800        assert!(ARRIVED >= required, "the draw must clear the confidence bound");
27801
27802        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut events, sender, handle) =
27803            entry_with_pix_session(params, MIN_EARLY_RECOVERY_THRESHOLD).await?;
27804        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
27805            pseudonym,
27806            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
27807        )
27808        .await?;
27809        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut events).await);
27810
27811        for n in 1..=boundary as u32 {
27812            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &n.to_be_bytes())?;
27813        }
27814
27815        // Every packet was acknowledged by the first relayer; the losses are downstream, so the Exit
27816        // asks at the boundary.
27817        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, ARRIVED);
27818        let result = mgr
27819            .handle_ssa_request(
27820                pseudonym,
27821                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
27822            )
27823            .await;
27824
27825        sender.close_channel();
27826        handle.await??;
27827        result.context("honest Exit on a 50 % downstream-loss path lost its only successor request")?;
27828        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut events).await);
27829
27830        Ok(())
27831    }
27832
27833    /// A real Entry Session must advance the counter the successor gate reads.
27834    ///
27835    /// The gate's worst failure is not being too strict, it is being wired to a counter nothing
27836    /// feeds: that closes it permanently, and every PIX Session then dies on its second cycle with
27837    /// the Exit blaming its own commitment deadline. The other tests here drive
27838    /// `returned_packets` by hand, so none of them would notice.
27839    ///
27840    /// Deliberately built with `surb_management: None`. That is the branch which passed `session_rx`
27841    /// through untouched and left `surb_estimator` at its default — the one place where reusing the
27842    /// balancer's estimate instead of a counter of our own would have produced exactly that silent
27843    /// permanent closure.
27844    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
27845    async fn returned_packets_are_counted_on_the_entry_receive_path() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
27846        use hopr_protocol_start::StartProtocolDiscriminants;
27847
27848        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
27849        let bob_peer: Address = (&ChainKeypair::random()).into();
27850
27851        let alice_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
27852        let bob_mgr = SessionManager::new(Default::default());
27853
27854        let mut alice_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
27855        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
27856
27857        // Alice → Bob, and Bob → Alice, with no filtering: the handshake is not what is under test.
27858        let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr.clone();
27859        alice_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
27860            let bob_mgr_clone = bob_mgr_clone.clone();
27861            Box::pin(async move {
27862                let _ = bob_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
27863                    alice_pseudonym,
27864                    ApplicationDataIn {
27865                        data: data.data,
27866                        packet_info: Default::default(),
27867                    },
27868                );
27869                Ok(())
27870            })
27871        });
27872        let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr.clone();
27873        bob_transport
27874            .expect_send_message()
27875            .withf(|_, data| msg_type(data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished))
27876            .returning(move |_, data| {
27877                let alice_mgr_clone = alice_mgr_clone.clone();
27878                Box::pin(async move {
27879                    alice_mgr_clone.dispatch_message(
27880                        alice_pseudonym,
27881                        ApplicationDataIn {
27882                            data: data.data,
27883                            packet_info: Default::default(),
27884                        },
27885                    )?;
27886                    Ok(())
27887                })
27888            });
27889
27890        let (alice_sender, alice_handle) = mock_packet_planning(alice_transport);
27891        let (new_session_tx_alice, _alice_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
27892        alice_mgr.start(alice_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_alice, None, None)?;
27893
27894        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
27895        let (new_session_tx_bob, new_session_rx_bob) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1024);
27896        bob_mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx_bob, None, None)?;
27897        let _bob_notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
27898            pin_mut!(new_session_rx_bob);
27899            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx_bob.next().await {}
27900        });
27901
27902        let alice_session = alice_mgr
27903            .new_session(
27904                bob_peer,
27905                SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
27906                SessionClientConfig {
27907                    pseudonym: alice_pseudonym.into(),
27908                    capabilities: None.into(),
27909                    surb_management: None,
27910                    ..Default::default()
27911                },
27912            )
27913            .await
27914            .context("the session must establish")?;
27915
27916        let counter = alice_mgr
27917            .sessions
27918            .get(&alice_pseudonym)
27919            .expect("alice must hold the session slot")
27920            .returned_packets;
27921        assert_eq!(
27922            0,
27923            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
27924            "nothing has come back yet"
27925        );
27926
27927        // Three packets arriving the way the Exit's return traffic does.
27928        for i in 0..3u8 {
27929            alice_mgr.dispatch_message(
27930                alice_pseudonym,
27931                ApplicationDataIn {
27932                    data: ApplicationData::new(SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG, &[i])?,
27933                    packet_info: Default::default(),
27934                },
27935            )?;
27936        }
27937
27938        // The count is taken as the Session drains its receiver, and the receiver is only polled by a
27939        // reader — which is exactly how it behaves in production, where the client is reading.
27940        let mut alice_session = alice_session;
27941        let mut buffer = [0u8; 16];
27942        for _ in 0..50 {
27943            if counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) >= 3 {
27944                break;
27945            }
27946            let _ = tokio::time::timeout(
27947                Duration::from_millis(20),
27948                futures::AsyncReadExt::read(&mut alice_session, &mut buffer),
27949            )
27950            .await;
27951        }
27952        assert_eq!(
27953            3,
27954            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
27955            "every Exit → Entry packet must be counted, or the successor gate can never open"
27956        );
27957
27958        drop(alice_session);
27959        alice_sender.close_channel();
27960        bob_sender.close_channel();
27961        let _ = alice_handle.await?;
27962        let _ = bob_handle.await?;
27963        Ok(())
27964    }
27965
27966    /// Re-points the fixture's slot at `Forward` routing, the way a real Entry's slot is built.
27967    ///
27968    /// [`entry_with_pix_session`] establishes through `handle_incoming_session_initiation` because
27969    /// that is the path which installs the PIX state the successor gate needs, and it stores the
27970    /// Exit's `Return` reply routing. The gate is an Entry-side rule, and the counter it reads is
27971    /// only credited on Sessions this node *initiated* — Start-protocol traffic on an incoming
27972    /// Session comes from the Entry over the forward path and must not be paid for. So the routing is
27973    /// what decides whether the keep-alives below are read as service arriving or as service being
27974    /// asked for, and the fixture has to be put on the side the rule is about.
27975    ///
27976    /// Re-inserting rather than mutating: the slot lives in a `moka` cache by value, and its routing
27977    /// is a plain field rather than a cell, because nothing in production ever changes it.
27978    fn make_session_outgoing<S>(mgr: &SessionManager<S>, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym, destination: Address)
27979    where
27980        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
27981        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
27982    {
27983        let mut slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).expect("session must exist");
27984        slot.routing_opts = DestinationRouting::Forward {
27985            destination: Box::new(destination.into()),
27986            pseudonym: Some(*pseudonym),
27987            forward_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(hopr_api::types::primitive::bounded::BoundedSize::MIN),
27988            return_options: RoutingOptions::Hops(hopr_api::types::primitive::bounded::BoundedSize::MIN).into(),
27989        };
27990        mgr.sessions.insert(*pseudonym, slot);
27991    }
27992
27993    /// A cycle served only by the Exit's keep-alives must still buy its successor.
27994    ///
27995    /// This is the property that lets the Exit finish a funded cycle whose application has fallen
27996    /// silent: it sends its own Exit → Entry keep-alives, each one consuming a return SURB and
27997    /// therefore unlocking one share, and the cycle completes on those alone. If they earned nothing
27998    /// at this gate the successor would be refused for as long as the Exit relied on them: the Exit's
27999    /// re-sends would be dropped as under-served until the cycle's emission ended, at which point the
28000    /// successor reaches the front, the re-sends stop, and the Session closes on `CommitmentTimeout`,
28001    /// naming a timer rather than the rule that fired.
28002    ///
28003    /// Driven through [`dispatch_message`](SessionManager::dispatch_message) with real encoded
28004    /// keep-alives rather than by touching the counter, because the credit lives on that path and
28005    /// nowhere else: the message never reaches `session_rx`, so the receive-path inspector that
28006    /// [`returned_packets_are_counted_on_the_entry_receive_path`] pins cannot cover for it.
28007    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28008    async fn keep_alives_alone_can_carry_a_cycle_to_its_successor() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28009        let params = wide_pix_params();
28010        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28011            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
28012
28013        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28014            pseudonym,
28015            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28016        )
28017        .await
28018        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
28019        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28020
28021        // Emission reaches the boundary, so service is the only thing left for the gate to weigh.
28022        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
28023            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
28024        }
28025
28026        make_session_outgoing(&mgr, &pseudonym, (&ChainKeypair::random()).into());
28027
28028        let counter = mgr
28029            .sessions
28030            .get(&pseudonym)
28031            .expect("session must exist")
28032            .returned_packets;
28033        assert_eq!(
28034            0,
28035            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
28036            "the fixture must start with nothing served"
28037        );
28038
28039        // Exactly what the gate demands, and every packet of it a keep-alive.
28040        let required = required_returned_packets(&params, 1);
28041        for level in 0..required {
28042            let keep_alive: ApplicationData = HoprStartProtocol::KeepAlive(KeepAliveMessage {
28043                session_id: pseudonym,
28044                flags: KeepAliveFlag::BalancerState.into(),
28045                additional_data: level,
28046            })
28047            .try_into()?;
28048            mgr.dispatch_message(
28049                pseudonym,
28050                ApplicationDataIn {
28051                    data: keep_alive,
28052                    packet_info: Default::default(),
28053                },
28054            )?;
28055        }
28056        assert_eq!(
28057            required,
28058            counter.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
28059            "every keep-alive consumed a return SURB and must be credited as service"
28060        );
28061
28062        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28063            pseudonym,
28064            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
28065        )
28066        .await
28067        .context("a cycle served entirely by keep-alives must still buy its successor")?;
28068        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28069
28070        bob_sender.close_channel();
28071        bob_handle.await??;
28072        Ok(())
28073    }
28074
28075    /// The Entry's half of the successor gate: a batch asked for before emission has reached the last
28076    /// cycle of the batch already committed must be refused, committing nothing and depositing
28077    /// nothing — and the Session must survive it.
28078    ///
28079    /// The Exit-side gate in `SessionPixSupervisor` means a correct peer never lands here. This is
28080    /// what makes a peer that *does* — an unpatched or hostile Exit answering every cycle's
28081    /// early-recovery signal with a fresh batch — cost the Entry nothing rather than one on-chain
28082    /// deposit per surplus request.
28083    ///
28084    /// Ordering across a batch is pinned where it lives, on the generator, by
28085    /// `emission_never_crosses_a_cycle_boundary_early` and
28086    /// `emission_progress_lags_the_commitment_index_across_a_batch`. What this test drives is the
28087    /// wiring and all three points of the gate: nothing emitted at all, emission having merely
28088    /// *reached* the last committed cycle, and emission far enough into it.
28089    ///
28090    /// The middle point is the regression. Admission used to be "emission has reached the last
28091    /// committed index", which becomes true on that cycle's very first share — so a successor batch
28092    /// was admitted ~0 % into the batch rather than the ~85 % at which a conforming Exit asks. See
28093    /// [`MIN_SUCCESSOR_EMISSION_FRACTION`].
28094    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28095    async fn entry_refuses_a_batch_asked_for_before_emission_reaches_the_current_one() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28096        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
28097
28098        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
28099        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
28100
28101        const BATCH: u32 = 3;
28102
28103        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
28104            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
28105            threshold: 2,
28106            surplus_shares: 1,
28107        }));
28108        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
28109            generator.clone(),
28110            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
28111        );
28112        // This manager plays both halves, so its own Exit side opens a cycle and blocks on the
28113        // deposit pool. Answered on the way through; the deposits this test counts pass on unchanged.
28114        let mut pix_events = crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events, |_| Vec::new());
28115
28116        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
28117            max_ssas_per_ssa_request: BATCH as usize,
28118            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
28119                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
28120                ..Default::default()
28121            },
28122            ..Default::default()
28123        });
28124
28125        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
28126        bob_transport
28127            .expect_send_message()
28128            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
28129
28130        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
28131        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
28132        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
28133            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
28134            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
28135        });
28136        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
28137
28138        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
28139        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
28140            pseudonym,
28141            StartInitiation {
28142                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
28143                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
28144                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
28145                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
28146            },
28147        )
28148        .await?;
28149
28150        let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
28151            .expect("identity element must be valid");
28152        let batch = |from: u32| {
28153            (from..from + BATCH)
28154                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
28155                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
28156        };
28157
28158        // The opening batch is accepted: nothing is committed yet, so there is nothing to be early for.
28159        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28160            pseudonym,
28161            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(1), []),
28162        )
28163        .await
28164        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
28165        assert_eq!(
28166            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
28167            BATCH as usize,
28168            "the opening batch must yield one deposit address per SSA"
28169        );
28170
28171        // Fully served for the batch, so emission ordering is the only thing under test here. The
28172        // returned-data half of the gate has its own tests.
28173        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&small_pix_params(), BATCH));
28174
28175        // Asking again before a single share has gone out is a whole batch early.
28176        let err = mgr
28177            .handle_ssa_request(
28178                pseudonym,
28179                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
28180            )
28181            .await
28182            .expect_err("a batch asked for before any share was emitted must be refused");
28183        assert!(
28184            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
28185            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
28186        );
28187        assert_eq!(
28188            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
28189            0,
28190            "a refused batch must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
28191        );
28192        assert_eq!(
28193            mgr.active_sessions(),
28194            vec![pseudonym],
28195            "refusing a request must not close the Session"
28196        );
28197
28198        // Emit until the last cycle of the batch has taken the front — but no further.
28199        let mut sent = 0u32;
28200        let mut emit_until = |pred: &dyn Fn(&hopr_protocol_pix::EmissionProgress) -> bool| -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28201            for _ in 0..1024 {
28202                if generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).as_ref().is_some_and(pred) {
28203                    return Ok(());
28204                }
28205                sent += 1;
28206                generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
28207            }
28208            anyhow::bail!("emission did not reach the expected point")
28209        };
28210        emit_until(&|p| p.is_serving_last_committed())?;
28211
28212        // The boundary the gate actually uses, recomputed from the same negotiated params.
28213        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
28214            &small_pix_params(),
28215            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
28216        );
28217
28218        // Reaching the last cycle is *not* enough, and this is the H2 regression. The index-only gate
28219        // this replaced admitted a successor batch right here — on the last cycle's first share, ~0 %
28220        // of the way through the batch — which is nearly a whole cycle of deposits the Exit has not
28221        // earned, on the one gate whose purpose is to prevent exactly that.
28222        let progress = generator.emission_progress(&pseudonym).expect("committed");
28223        assert!(
28224            progress.front_emitted < min_emitted,
28225            "the test must stand at the start of the last cycle, got {} of {min_emitted}",
28226            progress.front_emitted
28227        );
28228        let err = mgr
28229            .handle_ssa_request(
28230                pseudonym,
28231                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
28232            )
28233            .await
28234            .expect_err("reaching the last cycle must not by itself admit the next batch");
28235        assert!(
28236            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
28237            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
28238        );
28239        assert_eq!(
28240            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
28241            0,
28242            "a batch refused for being early must not emit a single ReadyToDeposit"
28243        );
28244
28245        // Far enough into that last cycle, the same batch is admitted.
28246        emit_until(&|p| p.front_emitted >= min_emitted)?;
28247        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28248            pseudonym,
28249            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(BATCH + 1), []),
28250        )
28251        .await
28252        .context("a batch asked for on time must be accepted")?;
28253
28254        bob_sender.close_channel();
28255        bob_handle.await??;
28256        Ok(())
28257    }
28258
28259    /// How many `SsaCommit` messages the fixture's transport has been given, once that has stopped
28260    /// changing.
28261    ///
28262    /// The count lags the handler by a channel hop to the forwarding task, so a read straight after a
28263    /// call can miss the burst that call sent. Waiting for it to hold still is the cheap way to know
28264    /// the read is the whole of it.
28265    async fn settled_commit_count(wire: &WireRecord) -> usize {
28266        let mut last = wire.count(StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit);
28267        for _ in 0..80 {
28268            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25)).await;
28269            let now = wire.count(StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit);
28270            if now == last {
28271                return now;
28272            }
28273            last = now;
28274        }
28275        last
28276    }
28277
28278    /// Gets a fixture's Exit-side bookkeeping out of the way: the whole of cycle one emitted, and the
28279    /// Exit credited with the service the successor gate asks of it.
28280    fn serve_the_opening_cycle<S>(
28281        mgr: &SessionManager<S>,
28282        generator: &SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>,
28283        pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym,
28284        params: &PixParams,
28285    ) -> anyhow::Result<()>
28286    where
28287        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
28288        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static,
28289    {
28290        for sent in 1..=(params.polys_per_ssa() as u32 * params.emitted_shares_per_poly() as u32) {
28291            generator.next_share(pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
28292        }
28293        credit_returned_packets(mgr, pseudonym, required_returned_packets(params, 1));
28294        Ok(())
28295    }
28296
28297    /// The Exit re-sends an unanswered successor request, so the Entry has to answer the re-sends of
28298    /// one it has already admitted with nothing at all.
28299    ///
28300    /// Once the first copy is admitted the Entry spends a fraction of a second per cycle at the
28301    /// deployed dimensions (longer for wide dimensions or a full batch) generating its commitment, and
28302    /// then publishing it, and every re-send already in flight lands on a watermark that is at or above
28303    /// the index it names. Answering one of them with a second commitment would announce a second
28304    /// deposit address for the same quota and burst the same polynomials again; answering it with a
28305    /// refusal would log a fault, per re-send, for a request that was served. A repeat names the batch
28306    /// committed last, which is what tells it apart from a stale one.
28307    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28308    async fn a_repeat_of_the_committed_successor_is_a_no_op() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28309        let params = wide_pix_params();
28310        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28311        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) = entry_with_recorded_pix_session(
28312            params,
28313            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
28314            wire.clone(),
28315        )
28316        .await?;
28317
28318        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28319            pseudonym,
28320            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28321        )
28322        .await
28323        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
28324        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28325        let after_opening = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28326        assert!(
28327            after_opening > 0,
28328            "the opening batch must have sent its commitment burst"
28329        );
28330
28331        // The opening batch is a repeat of itself too: nothing special-cases it.
28332        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28333            pseudonym,
28334            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28335        )
28336        .await
28337        .context("a repeat of the opening batch must be accepted without effect")?;
28338        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28339        assert_eq!(after_opening, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
28340
28341        serve_the_opening_cycle(&mgr, &generator, &pseudonym, &params)?;
28342        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28343            pseudonym,
28344            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
28345        )
28346        .await
28347        .context("the successor must be admitted once it has been earned")?;
28348        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28349        let after_successor = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28350        assert!(
28351            after_successor > after_opening,
28352            "the successor must have sent a burst of its own"
28353        );
28354
28355        for resend in 1..=3 {
28356            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28357                pseudonym,
28358                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
28359            )
28360            .await
28361            .with_context(|| format!("re-send {resend} of the admitted successor must succeed"))?;
28362        }
28363        assert_eq!(
28364            0,
28365            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
28366            "a repeat must not announce a second deposit for the same cycle"
28367        );
28368        assert_eq!(
28369            after_successor,
28370            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
28371            "a repeat must not burst the same commitment again"
28372        );
28373        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and must not cost the Session");
28374
28375        bob_sender.close_channel();
28376        bob_handle.await??;
28377        Ok(())
28378    }
28379
28380    /// A request for indices the Session has already committed past, and that are not the batch it
28381    /// committed last, is dropped — quietly, and without costing the Session or committing anything.
28382    ///
28383    /// It is not `refuse_ssa_request`, which closes both halves: the worst such a request can be is an
28384    /// Exit that lost track of what it asked for, and the Exit's own deadlines already end that. The
28385    /// repeat of the batch actually committed to must still be recognised afterwards.
28386    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28387    async fn a_stale_request_is_dropped_without_effect() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28388        let params = wide_pix_params();
28389        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28390        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) = entry_with_recorded_pix_session(
28391            params,
28392            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
28393            wire.clone(),
28394        )
28395        .await?;
28396
28397        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28398            pseudonym,
28399            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28400        )
28401        .await
28402        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
28403        serve_the_opening_cycle(&mgr, &generator, &pseudonym, &params)?;
28404        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28405            pseudonym,
28406            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
28407        )
28408        .await
28409        .context("the successor must be admitted once it has been earned")?;
28410        assert_eq!(2, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28411        let committed = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28412
28413        let err = mgr
28414            .handle_ssa_request(
28415                pseudonym,
28416                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28417            )
28418            .await
28419            .expect_err("a request for an index below the last committed batch must not be served");
28420        assert!(
28421            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
28422            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
28423        );
28424        assert_eq!(
28425            0,
28426            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
28427            "a stale request must not announce a deposit"
28428        );
28429        assert_eq!(committed, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "or send a commitment");
28430        assert_eq!(
28431            vec![pseudonym],
28432            mgr.active_sessions(),
28433            "a stale request is dropped, not fatal"
28434        );
28435
28436        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28437            pseudonym,
28438            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(2), []),
28439        )
28440        .await
28441        .context("the batch actually committed to is still recognised as a repeat after a stale request")?;
28442        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28443
28444        bob_sender.close_channel();
28445        bob_handle.await??;
28446        Ok(())
28447    }

28461    /// What `ReadyToDeposit` events a fixture's PIX stream has ready.
28462    ///
28463    /// [`drain_pix_events`], keeping the deposits rather than counting them, for the tests whose
28464    /// subject is *which* announcement was made and not only how many.
28465    async fn drain_deposits(
28466        events: &mut (dyn futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin),
28467    ) -> Vec<AgreedSsaQuota> {
28468        let mut seen = Vec::new();
28469        while let Ok(Some(event)) = timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), events.next()).await {
28470            if let HoprSessionOutPixEvent::ReadyToDeposit(quota) = event {
28471                seen.push(quota);
28472            }
28473        }
28474        seen
28475    }

28477    /// Why [`FlakySender`] refused a message.
28478    #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
28479    struct InjectedSendFailure;
28480
28481    impl std::fmt::Display for InjectedSendFailure {
28482        fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
28483            f.write_str("injected send failure")
28484        }
28485    }
28486
28487    impl std::error::Error for InjectedSendFailure {}
28488
28489    /// How many more `SsaCommit` messages a [`FlakySender`] lets through before it refuses the rest.
28490    ///
28491    /// Only commitment messages are counted: the Exit half of the same manager sends other traffic
28492    /// through the same sender, and a keep-alive spending the budget would move the point at which a
28493    /// burst is cut.
28494    #[derive(Clone)]
28495    struct SendBudget {
28496        allowed: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
28497        /// Commitment messages refused before `allowed` is consulted at all.
28498        refusals: Arc<std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64>,
28499    }
28500
28501    impl SendBudget {
28502        fn unlimited() -> Self {
28503            Self {
28504                allowed: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(u64::MAX)),
28505                refusals: Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicU64::new(0)),
28506            }
28507        }
28508
28509        /// Lets `sends` more commitment messages through, then refuses every one.
28510        fn allow(&self, sends: u64) {
28511            self.allowed.store(sends, Ordering::SeqCst);
28512        }
28513
28514        /// Ends the failure: every send is let through again.
28515        fn restore(&self) {
28516            self.allow(u64::MAX);
28517        }
28518
28519        /// Refuses the next `sends` commitment messages, and goes back to [`allow`](Self::allow)'s
28520        /// budget after them: a transport that gives up once and then recovers.
28521        fn refuse_next(&self, sends: u64) {
28522            self.refusals.store(sends, Ordering::SeqCst);
28523        }
28524
28525        fn take(&self) -> bool {
28526            if self
28527                .refusals
28528                .fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |left| left.checked_sub(1))
28529                .is_ok()
28530            {
28531                return false;
28532            }
28533            self.allowed
28534                .fetch_update(Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst, |left| {
28535                    if left == u64::MAX {
28536                        Some(left)
28537                    } else {
28538                        left.checked_sub(1)
28539                    }
28540                })
28541                .is_ok()
28542        }
28543    }
28544
28545    /// A transport that fails on demand and recovers.
28546    ///
28547    /// A channel sender can only fail by being closed, for good. The failure the Entry's publication
28548    /// has to survive is a send that gives up under backpressure — and the next one succeeds.
28549    #[derive(Clone)]
28550    struct FlakySender {
28551        inner: UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
28552        budget: SendBudget,
28553    }
28554
28555    impl futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> for FlakySender {
28556        type Error = InjectedSendFailure;
28557
28558        fn poll_ready(
28559            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
28560            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
28561        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
28562            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
28563                .poll_ready(cx)
28564                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
28565        }
28566
28567        fn start_send(
28568            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
28569            item: (DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut),
28570        ) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
28571            if crate::testing::msg_type(&item.1, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) && !self.budget.take() {
28572                return Err(InjectedSendFailure);
28573            }
28574            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
28575                .start_send(item)
28576                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
28577        }
28578
28579        fn poll_flush(
28580            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
28581            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
28582        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
28583            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
28584                .poll_flush(cx)
28585                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
28586        }
28587
28588        fn poll_close(
28589            mut self: Pin<&mut Self>,
28590            cx: &mut std::task::Context<'_>,
28591        ) -> std::task::Poll<Result<(), Self::Error>> {
28592            Pin::new(&mut self.inner)
28593                .poll_close(cx)
28594                .map_err(|_| InjectedSendFailure)
28595        }
28596    }
28597
28598    /// [`entry_with_recorded_pix_session`], over a [`FlakySender`] whose failures the test controls.
28599    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
28600    async fn flaky_entry(
28601        params: PixParams,
28602        wire: Arc<WireRecord>,
28603    ) -> anyhow::Result<(
28604        SessionManager<FlakySender>,
28605        Arc<SsaShareGenerator<HoprPixSpec>>,
28606        HoprPseudonym,
28607        impl futures::Stream<Item = HoprSessionOutPixEvent> + Unpin,
28608        SendBudget,
28609        UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>,
28610        tokio::task::JoinHandle<anyhow::Result<()>>,
28611    )> {
28612        let budget = SendBudget::unlimited();
28613        let wrapped = budget.clone();
28614        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, events, sender, handle) = entry_with_wrapped_sender(
28615            params,
28616            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
28617            wire,
28618            move |inner| FlakySender { inner, budget: wrapped },
28619        )
28620        .await?;
28621        Ok((mgr, generator, pseudonym, events, budget, sender, handle))
28622    }

28624    /// The members the Session still owes a publication, ascending.

28638    /// What `ReadyToDeposit` is still owed for `index`, as it was fixed when the cycle was staged.
28639    fn owed_announcement<S>(
28640        mgr: &SessionManager<S>,
28641        pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym,
28642        index: u32,
28643    ) -> anyhow::Result<AgreedSsaQuota>
28644    where
28645        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
28646        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
28647    {
28648        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;

28650            .get()
28651            .context("a PIX session has SSA state")?

28653            .lock()

28660    /// A scoped re-request for the first `polys` polynomials of cycle `index`, as the Exit's own
28661    /// commitment timer would send it.
28662    fn rerequest(
28663        pseudonym: HoprPseudonym,
28664        params: PixParams,
28665        index: u32,
28666        polys: u16,
28667    ) -> SsaServerCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixDepositPayload> {
28668        SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
28669            pseudonym,
28670            params,
28671            [(SsaIndex::new(index).expect("non-zero"), vec![(0u16, polys - 1)])],
28672        )

28675    /// The publication of a batch can be cut short by the transport, and a repeat of the request
28676    /// finishes it: one full burst and one announcement, then nothing more.
28677    ///
28678    /// The generator has moved by the time a commitment is published, and a transport that fails then
28679    /// leaves a watermark and a polynomial queue behind a request that reported an error. The Exit
28680    /// re-sends it all the same. Read as stale, every re-send would be logged as a fault; answered with
28681    /// a silent success, the cycle would never be announced — the Entry's upper layer would never be
28682    /// told to fund an address the Exit is waiting on — and the Exit would close on its deposit
28683    /// timeout. So the batch is recorded as the last one committed once it is staged, not once it is
28684    /// published, and what is still owed is kept until it has been.
28685    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28686    async fn a_repeat_resumes_a_publication_whose_first_send_failed() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28687        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
28688        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28689        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28690            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
28691        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
28692        assert!(burst >= 3, "the fixture needs a burst of several messages, got {burst}");
28693        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28694
28695        // The transport refuses the very first message of the burst.
28696        sends.allow(0);
28697        let failure = mgr
28698            .handle_ssa_request(
28699                pseudonym,
28700                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28701            )
28702            .await
28703            .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
28704        assert!(
28705            is_a_cut_short_publication(&failure),
28706            "the gate admitted this request, so the failure is the transport's — reported as the non-fatal refusal, \
28707             not as a fault the dispatcher logs at `error!`, got {failure:?}"
28708        );
28709        assert_eq!(
28710            Some(SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?),
28711            mgr.sessions
28712                .get(&pseudonym)
28713                .context("session must exist")?
28714                .current_ssa_state
28715                .get()
28716                .and_then(SessionSsaState::committed_watermark),
28717            "the generator moved, so the watermark did too"
28718        );
28719        assert_eq!(vec![SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?);
28720        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "nothing was announced");
28721        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and nothing was sent");
28722        let staged = owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1)?;
28723
28724        // The transport recovers, and the Exit's re-send of the same request lands.
28725        sends.restore();
28726        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28727            pseudonym,
28728            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28729        )
28730        .await
28731        .context("a repeat of a request whose publication was cut short must finish it")?;
28732        assert_eq!(
28733            vec![staged],
28734            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
28735            "exactly one announcement, carrying what was fixed when the cycle was staged"
28736        );
28737        assert_eq!(
28738            before + burst,
28739            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
28740            "and exactly one full burst"
28741        );
28742        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
28743
28744        // Now it is published, so a further repeat is the no-op it always was.
28745        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28746            pseudonym,
28747            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28748        )
28749        .await
28750        .context("a repeat of a published batch must succeed")?;
28751        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28752        assert_eq!(before + burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
28753
28754        bob_sender.close_channel();
28755        bob_handle.await??;
28756        Ok(())
28757    }
28758
28759    /// A batch cut short part-way is finished from where it stopped: members already published are
28760    /// left alone, and the one that was cut is re-published whole.
28761    ///
28762    /// The request repeated here is the whole batch, as a conforming Exit sends it: it re-sends the
28763    /// batch, whole and unchanged, for as long as any member has reported nothing, including the ones
28764    /// whose commitment it already has.
28765    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28766    async fn a_resumed_batch_publishes_only_the_members_still_owed() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28767        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
28768        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28769        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28770            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
28771        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
28772        let batch = |first: u32| -> std::collections::BTreeMap<SsaIndex, HoprPixGroupElement> {
28773            let mut members = ssa_request_for(first);
28774            members.extend(ssa_request_for(first + 1));
28775            members
28776        };
28777
28778        // The first member goes out whole; the second is cut after one message.
28779        sends.allow(burst as u64 + 1);
28780        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28781            pseudonym,
28782            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch(1), []),
28783        )
28784        .await
28785        .expect_err("a batch whose second burst is cut must fail the request");
28786        assert_eq!(
28787            vec![SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?],
28788            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
28789            "the first member is published, the second is owed"
28790        );
28791        assert_eq!(
28792            vec![1],
28793            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events)
28794                .await
28795                .iter()
28796                .map(|quota| quota.ssa_id.ssa_index().get())
28797                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
28798            "only the member whose burst completed was announced"
28799        );
28800        assert_eq!(burst + 1, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
28801
28802        sends.restore();
28803        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28804            pseudonym,
28805            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch(1), []),
28806        )
28807        .await
28808        .context("the repeat must finish the batch")?;
28809        assert_eq!(
28810            vec![2],
28811            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events)
28812                .await
28813                .iter()
28814                .map(|quota| quota.ssa_id.ssa_index().get())
28815                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
28816            "the resumption announces the member that was owed, and not the one already published"
28817        );
28818        assert_eq!(
28819            burst + 1 + burst,
28820            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
28821            "one full burst more, for that member alone"
28822        );
28823
28824        bob_sender.close_channel();
28825        bob_handle.await??;
28826        Ok(())
28827    }
28828
28829    /// A batch cut at its first member stays owed in full, and a resumption publishes it in order.
28830    ///
28831    /// The member that failed is put back and the ones after it were never claimed, so all of them
28832    /// are still there. Handing the first back must not depend on the second being absent.
28833    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28834    async fn a_batch_cut_at_its_first_member_stays_owed_in_full() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28835        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
28836        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28837        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28838            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
28839        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
28840        let mut batch = ssa_request_for(1);
28841        batch.extend(ssa_request_for(2));
28842        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch.clone(), []);
28843
28844        sends.allow(0);
28845        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
28846            .await
28847            .expect_err("a batch whose first burst is refused must fail the request");
28848        assert_eq!(
28849            vec![
28850                SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?,
28851                SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?
28852            ],
28853            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
28854            "the member that failed was put back and the one after it was never claimed"
28855        );
28856        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28857        let staged = [
28858            owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1)?,
28859            owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 2)?,
28860        ];
28861
28862        sends.restore();
28863        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
28864            .await
28865            .context("the repeat must finish the whole batch")?;
28866        assert_eq!(
28867            staged.to_vec(),
28868            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
28869            "both members are announced, in ascending order, each once"
28870        );
28871        assert_eq!(2 * burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "one full burst each");
28872        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
28873
28874        bob_sender.close_channel();
28875        bob_handle.await??;
28876        Ok(())
28877    }

28879    /// A scoped re-request for a cycle whose publication was cut short resumes it instead.
28880    ///
28881    /// The Exit that received part of a burst stops re-sending its request and repairs the commitment
28882    /// with a scoped re-request. That repair completes the commitment it names but never announces the
28883    /// deposit, so for a cycle nobody was told to fund the answer has to be the whole publication.
28884    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28885    async fn a_scoped_rerequest_resumes_a_publication_cut_short_mid_burst() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28886        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
28887        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28888        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28889            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
28890        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
28891        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28892
28893        sends.allow(1);
28894        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
28895            pseudonym,
28896            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
28897        )
28898        .await
28899        .expect_err("a burst cut after one message must fail the request");
28900        assert_eq!(before + 1, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "one message got out");
28901        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28902        let staged = owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 1)?;
28903        sends.restore();
28904
28905        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
28906            .await
28907            .context("a re-request for a cycle cut short must be answered")?;
28908        assert_eq!(
28909            vec![staged],
28910            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
28911            "exactly one announcement for the cycle nobody had been told to fund"
28912        );
28913        assert_eq!(
28914            before + 1 + burst,
28915            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
28916            "answered with the whole burst, not with the ten polynomials the Exit named"
28917        );
28918        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
28919
28920        bob_sender.close_channel();
28921        bob_handle.await??;
28922        Ok(())
28923    }

28925    /// A re-request for a cycle that was published in full stays scoped, and announces nothing.
28926    ///

28928    /// it again would invite a second deposit against one quota.
28929    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28930    async fn a_rerequest_for_a_published_cycle_stays_scoped() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28931        let params = multi_message_pix_params();

28937        mgr.handle_ssa_request(

28939            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),

28941        .await
28942        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;

28947        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))

28951            burst + 1,
