28962    /// A resumption the transport cuts short does not hold up the rest of the re-request that
28963    /// prompted it.
28964    ///
28965    /// A re-request can name a cycle whose publication was cut short beside one that was published in
28966    /// full. The first is answered by resuming the batch and the second by its scoped parts, and the
28967    /// two are separate repairs. Returning on the resumption's failure left the second one waiting a
28968    /// whole re-request interval on the first.
28969    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
28970    async fn a_cut_short_resumption_does_not_hold_up_the_rest_of_a_rerequest() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
28971        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
28972        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
28973        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
28974            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
28975        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
28976        let mut batch = ssa_request_for(1);
28977        batch.extend(ssa_request_for(2));
28978        let (first, second) = (
28979            SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?,
28980            SsaIndex::new(2).context("non-zero")?,
28981        );
28982
28983        // The first member goes out whole; the second is cut after one message.
28984        sends.allow(burst as u64 + 1);
28985        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch, []))
28986            .await
28987            .expect_err("a batch whose second burst is cut must fail the request");
28988        assert_eq!(vec![second], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?);
28989        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
28990        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
28991        sends.restore();
28992
28993        // The Exit asks for ten polynomials of each. The transport gives up on the first message of
28994        // the resumption and recovers straight after.
28995        sends.refuse_next(1);
28996        let failure = mgr
28997            .handle_ssa_request(
28998                pseudonym,
28999                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(
29000                    pseudonym,
29001                    params,
29002                    [(first, vec![(0u16, 9)]), (second, vec![(0u16, 9)])],
29003                ),
29004            )
29005            .await
29006            .expect_err("the resumption that was cut short is still reported");
29007        assert!(
29008            is_a_cut_short_publication(&failure),
29009            "reported as the non-fatal refusal, got {failure:?}"
29010        );
29011        assert_eq!(
29012            before + 1,
29013            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
29014            "the published cycle's ten polynomials went out all the same, in one message"
29015        );
29016        assert_eq!(vec![second], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?, "and the cut cycle stays owed");
29017        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "nothing was announced");
29018
29019        bob_sender.close_channel();
29020        bob_handle.await??;
29021        Ok(())
29022    }
29023
29024    /// Moves the moment the Session's last batch went out back by a whole
29025    /// [`SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE`], as if the repeat about to be handled were arriving that much later.
29026    fn backdate_last_sent<S>(mgr: &SessionManager<S>, pseudonym: &HoprPseudonym) -> anyhow::Result<()>
29027    where
29028        S: futures::Sink<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)> + Clone + Send + Sync + Unpin + 'static,
29029        S::Error: std::error::Error + Send + Sync + Clone + 'static,
29030    {
29031        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
29032        let state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("a PIX session has SSA state")?;
29033        let mut unpublished = state.unpublished.lock();
29034        let sent = unpublished.last_sent.context("the batch must have gone out")?;
29035        unpublished.last_sent = Some(
29036            sent.checked_sub(SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE)
29037                .context("the clock must reach back a grace")?,
29038        );
29039        Ok(())
29040    }
29041
29042    /// A repeat that arrives long after the batch went out in full has its bursts sent again, and
29043    /// nothing announced.
29044    ///
29045    /// Publishing a burst only means the local transport took it. If a relayer on the forward path
29046    /// dies, all of it can be lost, and then the Exit holds no part it could name in a scoped
29047    /// re-request. Its repeat is the only prompt left. A repeat that arrives within the grace may have
29048    /// crossed the burst and gets nothing, which is what keeps the ordinary in-flight repeats from
29049    /// costing a retransmission each.
29050    ///
29051    /// The opening batch stands in for a successor here. Nothing on the Entry tells them apart, and it
29052    /// spares the test serving a cycle first.
29053    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29054    async fn a_late_repeat_sends_the_published_bursts_again_without_announcing_them() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29055        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29056        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29057        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29058            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29059        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
29060        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []);
29061
29062        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29063            .await
29064            .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
29065        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29066        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29067
29068        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29069            .await
29070            .context("a repeat inside the grace must succeed")?;
29071        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and send nothing");
29072
29073        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
29074        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29075            .await
29076            .context("a late repeat must be answered")?;
29077        assert_eq!(
29078            2 * burst,
29079            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
29080            "with the whole burst again"
29081        );
29082        assert_eq!(
29083            0,
29084            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
29085            "and no second announcement for the same cycle"
29086        );
29087
29088        // The re-send starts the grace over, so the repeats that crossed it get nothing.
29089        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29090            .await
29091            .context("a repeat right after a re-send must succeed")?;
29092        assert_eq!(2 * burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29093
29094        // A re-send the transport cuts short is not fatal, and also starts the grace over, so a
29095        // congested transport is not handed a burst on every repeat.
29096        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
29097        sends.allow(1);
29098        let failure = mgr
29099            .handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29100            .await
29101            .expect_err("a re-send that cannot get out must fail the request");
29102        assert!(
29103            matches!(
29104                failure,
29105                TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))
29106            ),
29107            "reported as the non-fatal refusal, got {failure:?}"
29108        );
29109        sends.restore();
29110        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29111            .await
29112            .context("a repeat right after a failed re-send must succeed")?;
29113        assert_eq!(2 * burst + 1, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29114        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29115        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
29116
29117        bob_sender.close_channel();
29118        bob_handle.await??;
29119        Ok(())
29120    }
29121
29122    /// A lost burst whose cycle has no retransmissions left is given up on, once.
29123    ///
29124    /// The re-send of a published burst draws on the same per-cycle budget as a scoped re-request, so
29125    /// a peer cannot farm whole bursts out of this node by repeating its request. Once that budget is
29126    /// spent the generator refuses, and the cycle stops counting as announced, so the repeats after it
29127    /// do not even ask.
29128    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29129    async fn a_lost_burst_with_no_retransmissions_left_is_given_up_on() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29130        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29131        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29132        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, _sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29133            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29134        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
29135        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []);
29136
29137        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29138            .await
29139            .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
29140        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29141        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29142
29143        for _ in 0..hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS {
29144            generator.recommit(&pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?, [(0, 0)])?;
29145        }
29146
29147        backdate_last_sent(&mgr, &pseudonym)?;
29148        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29149            .await
29150            .context("a spent cycle is given up on, which is not a failure of the request")?;
29151        assert_eq!(burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "nothing was sent");
29152        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "and nothing announced");
29153        assert!(
29154            mgr.sessions
29155                .get(&pseudonym)
29156                .context("session must exist")?
29157                .current_ssa_state
29158                .get()
29159                .context("a PIX session has SSA state")?
29160                .unpublished
29161                .lock()
29162                .announced
29163                .is_empty(),
29164            "the cycle is no longer one a late repeat sends again"
29165        );
29166        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
29167
29168        bob_sender.close_channel();
29169        bob_handle.await??;
29170        Ok(())
29171    }
29172
29173    /// Once a cycle has used up its retransmissions it can never be published again, so it is dropped.
29174    ///
29175    /// Resuming spends one of a cycle's [`MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS`] answers, and that cap is
29176    /// what keeps a peer from farming whole bursts out of this node by re-sending a request. Spent, the
29177    /// generator refuses and nothing is sent or announced. Keeping the member owed would only make
29178    /// every later re-send pay a blocking `recommit` and a log line for the same refusal, so it is
29179    /// dropped from the owed set instead, and the repeats after it are plain no-ops.
29180    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29181    async fn a_cycle_with_no_retransmissions_left_is_dropped_and_later_repeats_are_no_ops() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29182        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29183        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29184        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29185            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29186        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
29187
29188        sends.allow(0);
29189        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29190            pseudonym,
29191            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29192        )
29193        .await
29194        .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
29195        sends.restore();
29196
29197        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
29198        for _ in 0..hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS {
29199            generator.recommit(&pseudonym, index, [(0, 0)])?;
29200        }
29201        assert_eq!(vec![index], owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?, "still owed until someone tries");
29202
29203        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29204            pseudonym,
29205            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29206        )
29207        .await
29208        .context("a spent cycle is given up on, which is not a failure of the request")?;
29209        assert!(
29210            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty(),
29211            "the cycle can never be published, so it is no longer owed"
29212        );
29213        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "it was never announced");
29214        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await, "and nothing was sent for it");
29215
29216        for _ in 0..3 {
29217            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29218                pseudonym,
29219                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29220            )
29221            .await
29222            .context("later repeats are plain no-ops")?;
29223        }
29224        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29225        assert_eq!(before, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29226
29227        // A re-request for it is scoped like any other, and the generator refuses it the same way.
29228        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
29229            .await
29230            .expect_err("the spent cycle has nothing left to re-send");
29231        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29232        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session lives");
29233
29234        bob_sender.close_channel();
29235        bob_handle.await??;
29236        Ok(())
29237    }

29239    /// A spent member is dropped without stopping the members after it.
29240    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29241    async fn a_spent_member_does_not_stop_the_rest_of_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29242        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29243        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29244        let (mgr, generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29245            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29246        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
29247        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
29248        let mut batch = ssa_request_for(1);
29249        batch.extend(ssa_request_for(2));
29250        let request = || SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, batch.clone(), []);
29251
29252        sends.allow(0);
29253        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29254            .await
29255            .expect_err("a batch whose first burst is refused must fail the request");
29256        sends.restore();
29257        let second = owed_announcement(&mgr, &pseudonym, 2)?;
29258        for _ in 0..hopr_protocol_pix::MAX_COMMITMENT_RETRANSMISSIONS {
29259            generator.recommit(&pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?, [(0, 0)])?;
29260        }
29261
29262        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, request())
29263            .await
29264            .context("the repeat publishes what can be published")?;
29265        assert_eq!(
29266            vec![second],
29267            drain_deposits(&mut pix_events).await,
29268            "the second member is announced, and the spent first one never is"
29269        );
29270        assert_eq!(
29271            before + burst,
29272            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
29273            "with its one full burst"
29274        );
29275        assert!(owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?.is_empty());
29276
29277        bob_sender.close_channel();
29278        bob_handle.await??;
29279        Ok(())
29280    }

29282    /// A member the generator retains nothing for is dropped too, with nothing sent.
29283    ///
29284    /// The retained material is what a resumption rebuilds the burst from. When it is gone — pushed out
29285    /// by newer cycles — nothing will bring it back, and `recommit` says so with a different error from
29286    /// the spent-cap one.
29287    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29288    async fn a_member_with_nothing_retained_is_dropped_and_nothing_is_sent() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29289        let params = small_pix_params();
29290        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
29291        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
29292            polynomials_per_ssa: params.polys_per_ssa(),
29293            threshold: params.shares_per_poly(),
29294            surplus_shares: params.surplus_shares(),
29295        }));
29296        let (toolbox, _events) = PixToolbox::new(
29297            generator,
29298            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
29299        );
29300        let state = SessionSsaState::new(params);
29301        state.stage_unpublished([owed_quota(pseudonym, 1)?, owed_quota(pseudonym, 2)?]);
29302
29303        let (mut sender, mut sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded::<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>();
29304        resume_publication(
29305            pseudonym,
29306            pseudonym,
29307            &DestinationRouting::Return(pseudonym.into()),
29308            &state,
29309            &toolbox,
29310            &mut sender,
29311        )
29312        .await
29313        .context("members that can never be published are given up on, which is not a failure")?;
29314
29315        assert!(state.unpublished_indices().is_empty(), "neither stays owed");
29316        assert!(sent.try_recv().is_err(), "and nothing went on the wire");
29317        Ok(())
29318    }

29320    /// A resumption that fails again is the same non-fatal refusal on every path, and leaves the cycle owed.
29321    ///
29322    /// Reached by a repeat of the request and by a scoped re-request alike. The dispatcher logs
29323    /// `NotAdmitted` at `debug!`, so a raw transport error from either path would have been an `error!`
29324    /// per attempt for something the Exit retries on its own.
29325    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29326    async fn a_resumption_cut_short_again_is_not_fatal_on_either_path() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29327        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29328        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29329        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29330            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29331        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
29332        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
29333        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
29334
29335        sends.allow(1);
29336        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29337            pseudonym,
29338            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29339        )
29340        .await
29341        .expect_err("a burst cut after one message must fail the request");
29342
29343        // The transport is still refusing, so each resumption is cut after nothing at all.
29344        sends.allow(0);
29345        let by_repeat = mgr
29346            .handle_ssa_request(
29347                pseudonym,
29348                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29349            )
29350            .await
29351            .expect_err("a repeat that cannot be published must not report success");
29352        assert!(is_a_cut_short_publication(&by_repeat), "got {by_repeat:?}");
29353        let by_rerequest = mgr
29354            .handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
29355            .await
29356            .expect_err("a re-request that cannot be published must not report success");
29357        assert!(is_a_cut_short_publication(&by_rerequest), "got {by_rerequest:?}");
29358        assert_eq!(
29359            vec![index],
29360            owed(&mgr, &pseudonym)?,
29361            "the cycle stays owed through both"
29362        );
29363        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29364        assert_eq!(
29365            before + 1,
29366            settled_commit_count(&wire).await,
29367            "only the first message ever got out"
29368        );
29369
29370        // And it is still finished once the transport is back.
29371        sends.restore();
29372        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
29373            .await
29374            .context("the next re-request finishes it")?;
29375        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29376        assert_eq!(before + 1 + burst, settled_commit_count(&wire).await);
29377
29378        bob_sender.close_channel();
29379        bob_handle.await??;
29380        Ok(())
29381    }

29383    /// A member somebody else has claimed is not published by a second resumer.
29384    ///
29385    /// The scoped re-request path does not take the per-pseudonym request lock, so it can run beside
29386    /// the original publication or another resumption. The claim is what keeps them from announcing a
29387    /// deposit twice: whoever removes a member from the owed set is its publisher, and nobody else.
29388    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29389    async fn a_claimed_member_is_not_published_by_a_second_resumer() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29390        let params = multi_message_pix_params();
29391        let wire = Arc::new(WireRecord::default());
29392        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, sends, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29393            flaky_entry(params, wire.clone()).await?;
29394        let burst = burst_len(&pseudonym, &params)?;
29395        let before = settled_commit_count(&wire).await;
29396
29397        sends.allow(0);
29398        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29399            pseudonym,
29400            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29401        )
29402        .await
29403        .expect_err("a burst that cannot be sent must fail the request");
29404        sends.restore();
29405
29406        // Another resumer is part-way through the cycle.
29407        let index = SsaIndex::new(1).context("non-zero")?;
29408        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
29409        let state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("a PIX session has SSA state")?;
29410        let claimed = state
29411            .claim_unpublished(index)
29412            .context("the cycle must be owed to be claimed")?;
29413
29414        // Neither a repeat nor a re-request may publish or announce it meanwhile.
29415        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29416            pseudonym,
29417            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29418        )
29419        .await
29420        .context("a repeat of a batch that is being published is not a fault")?;
29421        mgr.handle_ssa_request(pseudonym, rerequest(pseudonym, params, 1, 10))
29422            .await
29423            .context("a re-request of a cycle that is being published is answered as a published one")?;
29424        assert_eq!(
29425            0,
29426            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
29427            "a second resumer must not announce the claimed member"
29428        );
29429        assert!(
29430            settled_commit_count(&wire).await <= before + 1,
29431            "nor send its burst: at most the scoped message of the re-request went out"
29432        );
29433        assert!(
29434            state.claim_unpublished(index).is_none(),
29435            "a claimed member cannot be claimed twice"
29436        );
29437
29438        // The claimant fails and hands it back; now one resumption publishes it, once.
29439        state.restore_unpublished(claimed);
29440        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29441            pseudonym,
29442            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29443        )
29444        .await
29445        .context("the repeat must finish the publication that was handed back")?;
29446        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29447            pseudonym,
29448            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29449        )
29450        .await?;
29451        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await, "announced exactly once");
29452        assert!(settled_commit_count(&wire).await >= before + burst);
29453
29454        bob_sender.close_channel();
29455        bob_handle.await??;
29456        Ok(())
29457    }

29459    /// The announcement a member of `pseudonym`'s batch would be owed, for the tests that stage members
29460    /// directly rather than through a request.
29461    ///
29462    /// Any deposit address will do; its type depends on the curve this build is configured for, so one
29463    /// is derived rather than written down.
29464    fn owed_quota(pseudonym: HoprPseudonym, index: u32) -> anyhow::Result<AgreedSsaQuota> {
29465        let deposit_address = HoprPixSpec::group_to_deposit_address(
29466            SsaShareGenerator::<HoprPixSpec>::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
29467                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
29468                threshold: 2,
29469                surplus_shares: 1,
29470            })
29471            .new_ssa_commitment(&pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN)?
29472            .ssa_commitment,
29473        )
29474        .context("a commitment has a deposit address")?;
29475        let ssa_index = SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero")?;
29476        Ok(AgreedSsaQuota {
29477            ssa_id: SsaId::new(pseudonym, ssa_index),
29478            deposit_address,
29479            quota_per_ssa: 1,
29480            deposit_data: PixDepositData {
29481                id: PixAddressId::new(&pseudonym, ssa_index),
29482                data: Box::default(),
29483            },
29484        })
29485    }

29487    /// Whether `error` is the non-fatal refusal a publication cut short by the transport is reported as.
29488    ///
29489    /// Told apart from the gate's own `NotAdmitted` refusals by what it says, because the point of the
29490    /// tests using it is that a cut is reported the same way on every path that can meet one.
29491    fn is_a_cut_short_publication(error: &TransportSessionError) -> bool {
29492        matches!(
29493            error,
29494            TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(reason))
29495                if reason.contains("was cut short") && reason.contains("still owed")
29496        )
29497    }
29498
29499    /// The owed set is claimed once, handed back whole, and replaced by a newer batch.
29500    #[test]
29501    fn owed_members_are_claimed_once_and_replaced_by_a_newer_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29502        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
29503        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
29504        let owed = |index: u32| owed_quota(pseudonym, index);
29505        let index = |index: u32| SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero");
29506
29507        state.stage_unpublished([owed(3)?, owed(4)?]);
29508        assert_eq!(vec![index(3)?, index(4)?], state.unpublished_indices());
29509
29510        let claimed = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
29511        assert!(state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).is_none(), "a claim is exclusive");
29512        assert_eq!(
29513            vec![index(4)?],
29514            state.unpublished_indices(),
29515            "and takes the member out of the set"
29516        );
29517
29518        state.restore_unpublished(claimed);
29519        assert_eq!(
29520            vec![index(3)?, index(4)?],
29521            state.unpublished_indices(),
29522            "a member handed back is owed again, in its place"
29523        );
29524
29525        // A newer batch replaces the older one, and a straggling claimant of the old batch cannot
29526        // bring its member back into the new one.
29527        let straggler = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed")?;
29528        state.stage_unpublished([owed(7)?]);
29529        assert_eq!(vec![index(7)?], state.unpublished_indices());
29530        state.restore_unpublished(straggler);
29531        assert_eq!(
29532            vec![index(7)?],
29533            state.unpublished_indices(),
29534            "an older batch's member has nothing left to be owed to"
29535        );
29536        Ok(())
29537    }
29538
29539    /// Only members whose publication completed are sent again, only once the batch has been out for
29540    /// a whole grace, and a re-send starts the grace over.
29541    #[test]
29542    fn a_late_repeat_resends_only_announced_members_once_per_grace() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29543        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
29544        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
29545        let owed = |index: u32| owed_quota(pseudonym, index);
29546        let index = |index: u32| SsaIndex::new(index).context("non-zero");
29547        let grace = SSA_REPEAT_RESEND_GRACE;
29548        let t0 = Instant::now();
29549
29550        state.stage_unpublished([owed(3)?, owed(4)?]);
29551        assert!(
29552            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 10, grace).is_empty(),
29553            "nothing has been announced yet"
29554        );
29555
29556        let first = state.claim_unpublished(index(3)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
29557        state.complete_publication(first, t0);
29558        let second = state.claim_unpublished(index(4)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
29559        assert!(
29560            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace / 2, grace).is_empty(),
29561            "a repeat inside the grace may have crossed the burst"
29562        );
29563        assert_eq!(
29564            vec![index(3)?],
29565            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace, grace),
29566            "a member still being published is not sent again behind its claimant's back"
29567        );
29568        assert!(
29569            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace + grace / 2, grace).is_empty(),
29570            "a re-send starts the grace over"
29571        );
29572
29573        state.complete_publication(second, t0 + grace * 2);
29574        assert_eq!(
29575            vec![index(3)?, index(4)?],
29576            state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 3, grace)
29577        );
29578
29579        state.forget_announced(index(3)?);
29580        assert_eq!(vec![index(4)?], state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 4, grace));
29581
29582        // A newer batch starts with nothing announced, and a straggling claimant of an older one
29583        // adds nothing to it.
29584        state.stage_unpublished([owed(5)?]);
29585        let straggler = state.claim_unpublished(index(5)?).context("owed, so claimable")?;
29586        state.stage_unpublished([owed(7)?]);
29587        state.complete_publication(straggler, t0 + grace * 5);
29588        assert!(state.claim_republication(t0 + grace * 10, grace).is_empty());
29589        Ok(())
29590    }
29591
29592    /// A request that finds another one in progress for the same Session is dropped on the spot.
29593    ///
29594    /// The holder can be anywhere in a long handler — waiting out the near-miss window, or part-way
29595    /// through generating a commitment, which at wide dimensions or a full batch takes seconds — and a
29596    /// queue of the Exit's re-sends behind it would park one `for_each_concurrent` slot each for all of
29597    /// that. Dropping costs nothing: either the holder admits the batch and the repeat is moot, or it
29598    /// does not and the repeat is the next attempt.
29599    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29600    async fn a_request_that_finds_the_lock_held_is_dropped_not_queued() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29601        let params = wide_pix_params();
29602        let (mgr, _generator, pseudonym, mut pix_events, bob_sender, bob_handle) =
29603            entry_with_pix_session(params, SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold).await?;
29604
29605        let lock = mgr
29606            .ssa_request_locks
29607            .get_with(pseudonym, async { Arc::new(futures::lock::Mutex::new(())) })
29608            .await;
29609        let holder = lock.lock().await;
29610
29611        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
29612        let err = timeout(
29613            SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT,
29614            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29615                pseudonym,
29616                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29617            ),
29618        )
29619        .await
29620        .context("a request behind a held lock must come back at once instead of waiting for it")?
29621        .expect_err("a request that finds the lock held must not be served");
29622        assert!(
29623            matches!(err, TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::NotAdmitted(_))),
29624            "expected NotAdmitted, got {err:?}"
29625        );
29626        assert!(
29627            started.elapsed() * 4 < SSA_SUCCESSOR_SERVICE_WAIT,
29628            "dropping took {:?}, which is a wait",
29629            started.elapsed()
29630        );
29631        assert_eq!(0, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29632        assert_eq!(vec![pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions(), "and the Session is untouched");
29633
29634        // Released, the very same request goes through: nothing was remembered against it.
29635        drop(holder);
29636        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29637            pseudonym,
29638            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, params, ssa_request_for(1), []),
29639        )
29640        .await
29641        .context("the request must be served once the lock is free")?;
29642        assert_eq!(1, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29643
29644        bob_sender.close_channel();
29645        bob_handle.await??;
29646        Ok(())
29647    }
29648
29649    /// A refusal is logged loudly once, and the repeats of it are not.
29650    ///
29651    /// The Exit re-sends a refused request every few seconds for as long as the gate stays shut, so
29652    /// the same refusal arrives over and over. Keyed on the lowest index asked for and the reason: a
29653    /// different reason for the same index, or the same reason for a different one, is news again.
29654    #[test]
29655    fn only_the_first_of_a_repeated_refusal_is_news() {
29656        let state = SessionSsaState::new(small_pix_params());
29657        let two = SsaIndex::new(2);
29658        let three = SsaIndex::new(3);
29659
29660        assert!(
29661            state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
29662            "the first refusal is news"
29663        );
29664        assert!(
29665            !state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::UnderServed),
29666            "the same refusal for the same index is not"
29667        );
29668        assert!(
29669            state.note_refusal(two, SsaRefusal::Early),
29670            "a different reason for the same index is"
29671        );
29672        assert!(
29673            state.note_refusal(three, SsaRefusal::Early),
29674            "and so is the same reason for a different index"
29675        );
29676        assert!(!state.note_refusal(three, SsaRefusal::Early));
29677        assert!(
29678            state.note_refusal(None, SsaRefusal::Stale),
29679            "a request naming no index at all still has a key, and it is not the zero of 'no refusal yet'"
29680        );
29681    }
29682
29683    /// Concurrent `SsaRequest`s for one pseudonym must admit exactly one batch.
29684    ///
29685    /// Start messages are processed under `for_each_concurrent`, so several requests for the same
29686    /// Session run at once, and each reads the successor gate before any of them has advanced it.
29687    /// Requests are issued at distinct, ascending index ranges because that is the shape the
29688    /// generator's monotonic index cannot refuse — it rejects equal or lower indices, and an Exit
29689    /// numbering its batches upwards never offers one.
29690    ///
29691    /// **What this pins is the invariant, not the mechanism.** At this fixture's dimensions — two
29692    /// polynomials at threshold two — `new_ssa_commitment` returns in microseconds, so the window
29693    /// between reading the gate and advancing it is too narrow to hit: removing
29694    /// [`ssa_request_locks`](SessionManager::ssa_request_locks) leaves the outcome unchanged here.
29695    /// The window is a function of that call's cost, which scales with `polys x threshold` — around a
29696    /// second at the former 8192 x 64, so roughly a quarter of one at the deployed 4096 x 32 — and a
29697    /// fixture that large is not something to build into a unit test. So this test guards the property and the
29698    /// serialisation is justified by the shape of the code rather than by this failing without it.
29699    ///
29700    /// It does earn its place: it is what would catch the gate being made per-entry, the guard being
29701    /// taken after the gate instead of before it, or the handler gaining an await between the two.
29702    #[test_log::test(tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 4))]
29703    async fn concurrent_ssa_requests_for_one_pseudonym_admit_one_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29704        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
29705
29706        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
29707        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
29708
29709        const BATCH: u32 = 2;
29710        const RACERS: u32 = 4;
29711
29712        let generator = Arc::new(SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
29713            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
29714            threshold: 2,
29715            surplus_shares: 1,
29716        }));
29717        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
29718            generator.clone(),
29719            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
29720        );
29721        // This manager plays both halves, so its own Exit side opens a cycle and blocks on the
29722        // deposit pool. Answered on the way through; the deposits this test counts pass on unchanged.
29723        let mut pix_events = crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events, |_| Vec::new());
29724
29725        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
29726            max_ssas_per_ssa_request: BATCH as usize,
29727            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
29728                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
29729                ..Default::default()
29730            },
29731            ..Default::default()
29732        });
29733
29734        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
29735        bob_transport
29736            .expect_send_message()
29737            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
29738
29739        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
29740        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
29741        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
29742            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
29743            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
29744        });
29745        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
29746
29747        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
29748        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
29749            pseudonym,
29750            StartInitiation {
29751                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
29752                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
29753                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
29754                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
29755            },
29756        )
29757        .await?;
29758
29759        let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
29760            .expect("identity element must be valid");
29761        let batch = |from: u32| {
29762            (from..from + BATCH)
29763                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
29764                .collect::<BTreeMap<_, _>>()
29765        };
29766
29767        // The opening batch, then emission far enough into its last cycle that exactly one successor
29768        // batch is legitimately admissible.
29769        mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29770            pseudonym,
29771            SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), batch(1), []),
29772        )
29773        .await
29774        .context("the opening batch must be accepted")?;
29775        assert_eq!(BATCH as usize, drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await);
29776
29777        // Served for the batch, so that serialisation is the only thing deciding the outcome below.
29778        credit_returned_packets(&mgr, &pseudonym, required_returned_packets(&small_pix_params(), BATCH));
29779
29780        let min_emitted = hopr_protocol_pix::min_emission_for_early_recovery(
29781            &small_pix_params(),
29782            SsaReconstructorConfig::default().early_recovery_threshold,
29783        );
29784        let mut sent = 0u32;
29785        for _ in 0..1024 {
29786            if generator
29787                .emission_progress(&pseudonym)
29788                .is_some_and(|p| p.is_serving_last_committed() && p.front_emitted >= min_emitted)
29789            {
29790                break;
29791            }
29792            sent += 1;
29793            generator.next_share(&pseudonym, &sent.to_be_bytes())?;
29794        }
29795
29796        // Real tasks on a multi-threaded runtime, not `join_all`: `join_all` polls in order, so the
29797        // first future runs its gate check and its whole commitment phase before the second is polled
29798        // at all, and the requests never actually overlap. That shape passes with or without the
29799        // serialisation and so proves nothing about it.
29800        let barrier = Arc::new(tokio::sync::Barrier::new(RACERS as usize));
29801        let outcomes = futures::future::join_all((0..RACERS).map(|r| {
29802            let mgr = mgr.clone();
29803            let barrier = barrier.clone();
29804            let commitments = batch(BATCH + 1 + r * BATCH);
29805            tokio::spawn(async move {
29806                barrier.wait().await;
29807                mgr.handle_ssa_request(
29808                    pseudonym,
29809                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(pseudonym, small_pix_params(), commitments, []),
29810                )
29811                .await
29812            })
29813        }))
29814        .await
29815        .into_iter()
29816        .map(|joined| joined.expect("racer task must not panic"))
29817        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
29818
29819        let admitted = outcomes.iter().filter(|o| o.is_ok()).count();
29820        assert_eq!(
29821            1, admitted,
29822            "exactly one of {RACERS} concurrent requests may be admitted, got {admitted}: {outcomes:?}"
29823        );
29824        assert_eq!(
29825            BATCH as usize,
29826            drain_pix_events(&mut pix_events).await,
29827            "only the admitted batch may produce deposit instructions"
29828        );
29829
29830        bob_sender.close_channel();
29831        bob_handle.await??;
29832        Ok(())
29833    }
29834
29835    /// An `SsaRequest` asking for more than [`SessionManagerConfig::max_ssas_per_ssa_request`] SSA
29836    /// commitments must be rejected outright, before any commitment is generated or any
29837    /// `ReadyToDeposit` is emitted — and a batch *at* the configured cap must be accepted, so that
29838    /// raising the knob is what actually admits a larger batch.
29839    ///
29840    /// Each accepted entry costs a full client commitment plus its own on-chain deposit, so without
29841    /// this cap one inbound packet could amplify into up to `MAX_SSAS_PER_REQUEST` (27) deposits.
29842    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
29843    async fn entry_rejects_ssa_request_exceeding_configured_ssa_cap() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
29844        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
29845
29846        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
29847        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
29848        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
29849
29850        /// Outcome of offering a batch: what `handle_ssa_request` returned, how many `SessionError`
29851        /// messages the Entry sent back, and whether it kept the Session.
29852        struct Outcome {
29853            result: errors::Result<()>,
29854            session_errors: usize,
29855            session_alive: bool,
29856        }
29857
29858        // `batch` entries offered against an Entry configured to accept at most `cap`.
29859        async fn offer_batch(cap: usize, batch: u32) -> anyhow::Result<Outcome> {
29860            // The PIX event stream must stay alive: an accepted batch emits one `ReadyToDeposit` per
29861            // entry, and a dropped receiver would fail the send and mask the acceptance as an error.
29862            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
29863                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
29864                    polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
29865                    threshold: 2,
29866                    surplus_shares: 1,
29867                })
29868                .into(),
29869                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
29870            );
29871
29872            let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
29873                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
29874                    quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
29875                    ..Default::default()
29876                },
29877                max_ssas_per_ssa_request: cap,
29878                ..Default::default()
29879            });
29880
29881            // Count the SessionError replies: a refusal has to be *told* to the Exit, which cannot
29882            // otherwise observe it and has no path back to a new request.
29883            let session_errors = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
29884            let session_errors_tx = session_errors.clone();
29885            let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
29886            bob_transport
29887                .expect_send_message()
29888                .times(1..)
29889                .returning(move |_, data| {
29890                    if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionError) {
29891                        session_errors_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
29892                    }
29893                    Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
29894                });
29895
29896            let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
29897            let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
29898            let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
29899                pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
29900                while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
29901            });
29902            mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
29903
29904            let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
29905
29906            mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
29907                alice_pseudonym,
29908                StartInitiation {
29909                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
29910                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
29911                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
29912                    additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
29913                },
29914            )
29915            .await?;
29916
29917            let session_id = alice_pseudonym;
29918            let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
29919                .expect("identity element must be valid");
29920
29921            // Indices start above whatever the Exit-side establishment already allocated, so the
29922            // accepted case is not rejected for non-monotonicity instead of for its size.
29923            let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = (100..100 + batch)
29924                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
29925                .collect();
29926
29927            let result = mgr
29928                .handle_ssa_request(
29929                    alice_pseudonym,
29930                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
29931                        session_id,
29932                        PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?,
29933                        commitments,
29934                        [],
29935                    ),
29936                )
29937                .await;
29938
29939            let session_alive = mgr.active_sessions().contains(&session_id);
29940
29941            bob_sender.close_channel();
29942            bob_handle.await??;
29943
29944            Ok(Outcome {
29945                result,
29946                session_errors: session_errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
29947                session_alive,
29948            })
29949        }
29950
29951        // One over the default cap is rejected...
29952        let over_cap = offer_batch(
29953            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
29954            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32 + 1,
29955        )
29956        .await?;
29957        assert!(
29958            matches!(
29959                over_cap.result,
29960                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
29961            ),
29962            "an over-cap SsaRequest must be rejected, got {:?}",
29963            over_cap.result
29964        );
29965        // ...and the refusal must be reported rather than left for the Exit to infer from its own
29966        // deposit timeout minutes later, and must not leave a Session behind that can never make PIX
29967        // progress.
29968        assert_eq!(
29969            1, over_cap.session_errors,
29970            "a refused SsaRequest must send exactly one SessionError back to the Exit"
29971        );
29972        assert!(
29973            !over_cap.session_alive,
29974            "a refused SsaRequest must tear down the Entry's half of the Session"
29975        );
29976
29977        // ...and the very same batch is accepted once the cap is raised to admit it, proving the
29978        // rejection is the configured cap talking and not some other validation.
29979        let raised = DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST + 1;
29980        let accepted = offer_batch(raised, raised as u32).await?;
29981        assert!(
29982            accepted.result.is_ok(),
29983            "a batch at the configured cap of {raised} must be accepted, got {:?}",
29984            accepted.result
29985        );
29986        assert_eq!(
29987            0, accepted.session_errors,
29988            "an accepted batch must not send a SessionError"
29989        );
29990        assert!(
29991            accepted.session_alive,
29992            "an accepted batch must leave the Session running"
29993        );
29994
29995        Ok(())
29996    }
29997
29998    /// A retransmission request must be capped on the *cycles* it names, not only on the runs the
29999    /// wire can carry.
30000    ///
30001    /// One 8-byte run names a whole cycle, so a request naming every retained cycle is answered with
30002    /// a full commitment burst for each — thousands of packets out of a single packet in. The
30003    /// generator's per-cycle attempt cap does not bound that: it bounds repeats of one cycle, and
30004    /// each cycle here is being asked for the first time.
30005    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
30006    async fn entry_rejects_a_retransmission_request_naming_too_many_cycles() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30007        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
30008
30009        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
30010        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
30011        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30012
30013        /// Commits `cap` cycles to an Entry capped at `cap`, then asks it to retransmit `cycles` of
30014        /// them, and reports what `handle_ssa_request` made of the second request together with every
30015        /// `SsaCommit` the Entry sent across both — one per cycle at these dimensions, so the
30016        /// commitment alone accounts for `cap` of them.
30017        ///
30018        /// Committing first is what gives the assertions their teeth: an uncapped handler answers
30019        /// every *retained* index it is named before it trips over the first one it does not hold, so
30020        /// the packet count — not the error — is what separates a gate from an accident. The count is
30021        /// read only after the send channel has drained, since the bursts are queued rather than sent
30022        /// inline and a running total would race them.
30023        async fn ask_for_cycles(cap: usize, cycles: u32) -> anyhow::Result<(errors::Result<()>, usize)> {
30024            let (pix_toolbox, _pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
30025                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
30026                    polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
30027                    threshold: 2,
30028                    surplus_shares: 1,
30029                })
30030                .into(),
30031                SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30032            );
30033
30034            let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
30035                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30036                    quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
30037                    ..Default::default()
30038                },
30039                max_ssas_per_ssa_request: cap,
30040                ..Default::default()
30041            });
30042
30043            // The amplification is the thing being bounded, so count what actually goes out.
30044            let commits = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
30045            let commits_tx = commits.clone();
30046            let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
30047            bob_transport
30048                .expect_send_message()
30049                .times(1..)
30050                .returning(move |_, data| {
30051                    if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) {
30052                        commits_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
30053                    }
30054                    Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
30055                });
30056
30057            let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
30058            let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30059            let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30060                pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30061                while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
30062            });
30063            mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
30064
30065            let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
30066            mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
30067                alice_pseudonym,
30068                StartInitiation {
30069                    challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
30070                    target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
30071                    capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
30072                    additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
30073                },
30074            )
30075            .await?;
30076
30077            let params = PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
30078            let identity = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
30079                .expect("identity element must be valid");
30080
30081            // Commit a full batch first, so there is real material for the retransmission to name.
30082            let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = (100..100 + cap as u32)
30083                .map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), identity))
30084                .collect();
30085            mgr.handle_ssa_request(
30086                alice_pseudonym,
30087                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(alice_pseudonym, params, commitments, []),
30088            )
30089            .await?;
30090
30091            // One run apiece, each covering its whole cycle: the cheapest request to send and the
30092            // most expensive to answer.
30093            let missing = (100..100 + cycles).map(|i| (SsaIndex::new(i).expect("non-zero"), vec![(0u16, 1u16)]));
30094
30095            let result = mgr
30096                .handle_ssa_request(
30097                    alice_pseudonym,
30098                    SsaServerCommitmentMessage::recommit(alice_pseudonym, params, missing),
30099                )
30100                .await;
30101
30102            bob_sender.close_channel();
30103            bob_handle.await??;
30104
30105            Ok((result, commits.load(Ordering::Relaxed)))
30106        }
30107
30108        // One cycle over the cap is refused whole, and — the part that matters — answered with
30109        // nothing at all, rather than with a burst for each retained cycle it managed to name first.
30110        let (over_cap, over_cap_commits) = ask_for_cycles(
30111            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
30112            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32 + 1,
30113        )
30114        .await?;
30115        assert!(
30116            matches!(
30117                over_cap,
30118                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
30119            ),
30120            "a retransmission request over the cycle cap must be refused, got {over_cap:?}"
30121        );
30122        assert_eq!(
30123            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST, over_cap_commits,
30124            "a refused request must add nothing to the {DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST} messages the commitment \
30125             itself cost"
30126        );
30127
30128        // ...and the very same cycles are repaired once they fit the cap, so the refusal above is the
30129        // cap talking and not some other validation the request also trips.
30130        let (at_cap, at_cap_commits) = ask_for_cycles(
30131            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
30132            DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST as u32,
30133        )
30134        .await?;
30135        assert!(
30136            at_cap.is_ok(),
30137            "a request at the cycle cap must be answered, got {at_cap:?}"
30138        );
30139        assert_eq!(
30140            2 * DEFAULT_MAX_SSAS_PER_SSA_REQUEST,
30141            at_cap_commits,
30142            "every named cycle must be re-sent, one message each on top of the commitment's own"
30143        );
30144
30145        Ok(())
30146    }
30147
30148    /// A batch with one undecodable member must publish nothing at all.
30149    ///
30150    /// `handle_ssa_request` used to generate, send and emit per entry, deciding each member's fate
30151    /// before looking at the next. A batch whose *second* exit commitment failed to decode had
30152    /// therefore already sent the first member's `SsaCommit` burst and emitted its `ReadyToDeposit`
30153    /// — an instruction to put money on chain — for a request that is then rejected as a whole. The
30154    /// Exit has no cycle to spend that deposit against, and the deposit key needs its half.
30155    ///
30156    /// The first member is valid and the second is not, so a per-entry implementation passes the
30157    /// "batch is refused" half of this test while still leaking the first deposit.
30158    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
30159    async fn a_batch_with_one_undecodable_commitment_publishes_nothing() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30160        use std::collections::BTreeMap;
30161
30162        use futures::FutureExt;
30163        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::HoprPixGroupElement;
30164        use hopr_protocol_pix::{PixGroup, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
30165        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30166
30167        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
30168            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
30169                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
30170                threshold: 2,
30171                surplus_shares: 1,
30172            })
30173            .into(),
30174            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30175        );
30176
30177        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
30178            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30179                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
30180                ..Default::default()
30181            },
30182            ..Default::default()
30183        });
30184
30185        // `SsaCommit` is the observable half of "a commitment was published"; `SessionError` is the
30186        // refusal. Both are counted, because the bug shows up as the two happening together.
30187        let commits = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
30188        let session_errors = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0));
30189        let (commits_tx, errors_tx) = (commits.clone(), session_errors.clone());
30190        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
30191        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
30192            if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaCommit) {
30193                commits_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
30194            }
30195            if crate::testing::msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionError) {
30196                errors_tx.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
30197            }
30198            Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
30199        });
30200
30201        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
30202        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30203        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30204            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30205            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
30206        });
30207        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
30208
30209        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
30210        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
30211            alice_pseudonym,
30212            StartInitiation {
30213                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
30214                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
30215                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
30216                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
30217            },
30218        )
30219        .await?;
30220
30221        let valid = HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes().as_ref())
30222            .expect("identity element must be valid");
30223        // All-ones is not a compressed point on the curve, so it fails before the subgroup check.
30224        // The length is taken from the type rather than written out: the group representation is
30225        // curve-dependent, and a literal silently becomes a *length* rejection under a different
30226        // `HoprPixSpec` — which is a different code path from the one under test.
30227        // Spelled out because the group repr is a `hybrid_array::Array` with several `AsRef` impls.
30228        let repr_len = AsRef::<[u8]>::as_ref(&PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default().to_bytes()).len();
30229        let garbage =
30230            HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(vec![0xffu8; repr_len].as_slice()).expect("length must be accepted");
30231        assert!(
30232            garbage.try_into_pix_group().is_err(),
30233            "the test fixture must actually be undecodable"
30234        );
30235
30236        let commitments: BTreeMap<_, _> = BTreeMap::from([
30237            (SsaIndex::new(100).expect("non-zero"), valid),
30238            (SsaIndex::new(101).expect("non-zero"), garbage),
30239        ]);
30240
30241        let result = mgr
30242            .handle_ssa_request(
30243                alice_pseudonym,
30244                SsaServerCommitmentMessage::new(
30245                    alice_pseudonym,
30246                    PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?,
30247                    commitments,
30248                    [],
30249                ),
30250            )
30251            .await;
30252
30253        let session_alive = mgr.active_sessions().contains(&alice_pseudonym);
30254
30255        // Drain the mock transport before counting: `mock_packet_planning` delivers on a spawned
30256        // task, so a count taken here would race the sends rather than observe them.
30257        bob_sender.close_channel();
30258        bob_handle.await??;
30259
30260        assert!(
30261            matches!(
30262                result,
30263                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::Unacceptable(_)))
30264            ),
30265            "an undecodable member must be refused, got {result:?}"
30266        );
30267        assert_eq!(
30268            0,
30269            commits.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
30270            "no SsaCommit may be sent for a batch that is refused as a whole"
30271        );
30272        assert_eq!(
30273            1,
30274            session_errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
30275            "the refusal must be reported to the Exit"
30276        );
30277        assert!(
30278            !session_alive,
30279            "an undecodable commitment is terminal, like every other unacceptable-parameter case"
30280        );
30281
30282        // The point of the test: not one deposit instruction escaped for the valid first member.
30283        pin_mut!(pix_events);
30284        assert!(
30285            pix_events.next().now_or_never().flatten().is_none(),
30286            "no ReadyToDeposit may be emitted for a batch that is refused as a whole"
30287        );
30288
30289        Ok(())
30290    }

30292    /// The control lane must be sized for the worst-case commitment burst of a single SSA cycle.
30293    ///
30294    /// A dropped `SsaCommit` is unrecoverable — there is no retransmission — so the queue has to
30295    /// absorb the whole commitment set a cycle can deliver, capped by the polynomial ceiling
30296    /// `check_pix_params` enforces.
30297    #[test]
30298    fn start_control_lane_is_sized_for_the_worst_case_commitment_burst() {
30299        let cfg = SessionManagerConfig::default();
30300        let capacity = start_control_channel_capacity(&cfg);
30301
30302        // Number of commitments implied by the largest quota this node accepts, clamped by the
30303        // number of polynomials it would actually admit.
30304        let commitments = (*cfg.pix_config.quota_range.end() / PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE).min(MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64);
30305        let min_expected = commitments.div_ceil(MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG as u64) as usize;
30306
30307        assert_eq!(
30308            min_expected,
30309            capacity - START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
30310            "the PIX commitment burst must be the only variable component of the control lane"
30311        );
30312        assert!(
30313            min_expected > 0,
30314            "a non-zero accepted quota must imply commitment messages"
30315        );
30316
30317        // Guards against a units mistake (e.g. counting bytes rather than messages) turning this
30318        // into a multi-gigabyte ring allocation.
30319        assert!(capacity < 1_000_000, "capacity {capacity} is implausibly large");
30320    }
30321
30322    /// The session lane is sized from the handler pool, not from the session limit: a queued
30323    /// `StartSession` is drained only as fast as a handler frees up.
30324    #[test]
30325    fn start_session_lane_is_sized_from_the_handler_pool() {
30326        assert_eq!(
30327            start_session_channel_capacity(),
30328            MAX_CONCURRENT_START_SESSIONS * START_SESSION_LANE_DEPTH_FACTOR + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE
30329        );
30330        const _: () = assert!(
30331            MAX_CONCURRENT_START_SESSIONS > START_SESSION_ADMISSION_CONCURRENCY,
30332            "the lane must hold more handlers than may wait on the server, or the permit caps it"
30333        );
30334        // Well below the pre-allocation guard, whatever the operator configures elsewhere.
30335        assert!(start_session_channel_capacity() < 1_000_000);
30336    }
30337
30338    /// `quota_range` is operator-settable and the capacity it feeds is *reserved*, not merely
30339    /// enforced — `crossfire`'s array flavour pre-allocates every slot. So the derivation must be
30340    /// bounded independently of the configured quota.
30341    ///
30342    /// Regression test: an unclamped derivation asked for ~4.2e8 slots here (77 GB), which aborted
30343    /// the whole unit test binary with an allocation failure rather than failing one assertion. The
30344    /// sizing test above never caught it because it only exercises the default config.
30345    #[test]
30346    fn start_control_lane_capacity_is_bounded_for_any_quota_range() {
30347        // The commitment term saturates once the quota admits more commitments than there are
30348        // polynomials, so this is the largest value it can ever take.
30349        let saturated = (MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA as u64).div_ceil(MIN_COMMITMENTS_PER_SSA_COMMIT_MSG as u64) as usize;
30350
30351        for quota_end in [10_u64.pow(13), u64::MAX] {
30352            let cfg = SessionManagerConfig {
30353                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30354                    quota_range: 0..=quota_end,
30355                    ..Default::default()
30356                },
30357                ..Default::default()
30358            };
30359
30360            assert_eq!(
30361                start_control_channel_capacity(&cfg),
30362                saturated + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
30363                "quota_range end {quota_end} must not grow the commitment term past the polynomial ceiling"
30364            );
30365        }
30366
30367        // The batch factor is reserved too: a batch of N draws N cycles' commitment sets into this
30368        // one channel, and a dropped `SsaCommit` is unrecoverable. It must scale the commitment term
30369        // and nothing else, and must itself be bounded by `MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE` even when the config
30370        // was never clamped by `SessionManager::new`.
30371        let batched = |ssas_per_request| {
30372            start_control_channel_capacity(&SessionManagerConfig {
30373                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30374                    quota_range: 0..=u64::MAX,
30375                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
30376                        ssas_per_request,
30377                        ..Default::default()
30378                    },
30379                    ..Default::default()
30380                },
30381                ..Default::default()
30382            })
30383        };
30384        for ssas_per_request in [1, 2, MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE] {
30385            assert_eq!(
30386                batched(ssas_per_request),
30387                saturated * ssas_per_request + START_PROTOCOL_CHANNEL_RESERVE,
30388                "the commitment term must scale with ssas_per_request = {ssas_per_request}"
30389            );
30390        }
30391        assert_eq!(
30392            batched(MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE + 1),
30393            batched(MAX_SSA_BATCH_SIZE),
30394            "an unclamped ssas_per_request must not inflate the pre-allocated ring"
30395        );
30396        assert_eq!(
30397            batched(0),
30398            batched(1),
30399            "a zero ssas_per_request must not collapse the commitment term"
30400        );
30401    }
