30403    /// Verifies that once the exit/responder (Bob) has set up the SSA state, delivering coefficient
30404    /// commits for all polynomials causes the PIX event stream to emit `DepositNeeded`.
30405    ///
30406    /// ## Steps
30407    /// 1. Bob's manager is started with a `PixToolbox` configured for `polynomials_per_ssa=2, threshold=2,
30408    ///    surplus_shares=1`. Alice's session initiation is processed normally.
30409    /// 2. The exit has already registered an exit commitment from `handle_incoming_session_initiation`.
30410    /// 3. Coefficient 0 (constant terms across all polynomials) is delivered via `handle_ssa_commit` using identity
30411    ///    group elements as dummy commitments.
30412    /// 4. Coefficient 1 (linear terms) is delivered similarly.
30413    /// 5. After the second coefficient delivery, Bob's PIX event stream emits `DepositNeeded` with the correct `SsaId`
30414    ///    and `quota_per_ssa` matching `pix_params_to_quota(2, 2)`.
30415    /// 6. The event is received within a 2-second timeout.
30416    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
30417    async fn exit_receives_ssa_commits_and_emits_deposit_needed_event() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30418        use std::collections::HashMap;
30419
30420        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::{HoprPixCommitmentProof, HoprPixGroupElement};
30421        use hopr_protocol_pix::{
30422            Field, PixGroup, PixScalar, PolynomialIndex, SsaCommitmentProof, SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructor,
30423            SsaReconstructorConfig, SsaShareGenerator,
30424        };
30425        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30426
30427        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
30428            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
30429            threshold: 2,
30430            surplus_shares: 1,
30431        };
30432
30433        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events_rx) = PixToolbox::new(
30434            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
30435            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30436        );
30437        // This test reads the event stream itself, so the pool has to be played on the way through:
30438        // the Exit blocks its SSA request on the answer, and the request would otherwise be the
30439        // first event read here.
30440        let pix_events_rx =
30441            crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events_rx, |id| vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8; 3]);
30442
30443        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
30444            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30445                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
30446                ..Default::default()
30447            },
30448            ..Default::default()
30449        });
30450
30451        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
30452        bob_transport
30453            .expect_send_message()
30454            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
30455        // handle_incoming_session_initiation sends SessionEstablished + SsaRequest.
30456        bob_transport
30457            .expect_send_message()
30458            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
30459
30460        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
30461        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30462        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30463            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30464            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
30465        });
30466        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
30467
30468        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
30469
30470        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
30471            alice_pseudonym,
30472            StartInitiation {
30473                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
30474                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
30475                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
30476                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
30477            },
30478        )
30479        .await?;
30480
30481        // The exit commitment is registered by the supervisor's opening `RequestSsa`, which the
30482        // action driver carries out asynchronously — so wait for it rather than assume it.
30483        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::MIN);
30484        {
30485            let share_processor = pix_toolbox.share_processor.clone();
30486            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
30487                while !share_processor.contains_builder(&ssa_id) {
30488                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
30489                }
30490            })
30491            .await
30492            .context("the opening SSA request never registered an exit commitment")?;
30493        }
30494
30495        // Deliver coefficient 0 (constant terms across all polynomials).
30496        // Use the identity/infinity group element as a dummy commitment.
30497        // PixGroup<HoprPixSpec> = k256::ProjectivePoint, which has identity/infinity as all-zero bytes.
30498        let identity_element = {
30499            let g: PixGroup<HoprPixSpec> = Default::default();
30500            HoprPixGroupElement::try_from(g.to_bytes().as_ref()).expect("identity element must be valid")
30501        };
30502        let mut coeff_0_map = HashMap::new();
30503        for poly in 0..2 {
30504            coeff_0_map.insert(poly as PolynomialIndex, identity_element);
30505        }
30506        // The dummy constant terms sum to the identity, whose discrete logarithm is zero, so an
30507        // honest proof of knowledge over it is constructible — the Exit refuses the cycle without
30508        // one.
30509        let zero = <PixScalar<HoprPixSpec> as Field>::ZERO;
30510        let identity_proof = HoprPixCommitmentProof::from(
30511            SsaCommitmentProof::<HoprPixSpec>::prove(&ssa_id, &zero, &PixGroup::<HoprPixSpec>::default())
30512                .expect("identity proof must be constructible"),
30513        );
30514        mgr.handle_ssa_commit(
30515            alice_pseudonym,
30516            SsaClientCommitmentMessage {
30517                session_id: alice_pseudonym,
30518                ssa_index: SsaIndex::MIN,
30519                coefficient_index: 0,
30520                commitment_proof: Some(identity_proof),
30521                coefficient_commitments: coeff_0_map,
30522            },
30523        )
30524        .await?;
30525
30526        // Deliver coefficient 1 (linear terms across all polynomials).
30527        let mut coeff_1_map = HashMap::new();
30528        for poly in 0..2 {
30529            coeff_1_map.insert(poly as PolynomialIndex, identity_element);
30530        }
30531        mgr.handle_ssa_commit(
30532            alice_pseudonym,
30533            SsaClientCommitmentMessage {
30534                session_id: alice_pseudonym,
30535                ssa_index: SsaIndex::MIN,
30536                coefficient_index: 1,
30537                commitment_proof: None,
30538                coefficient_commitments: coeff_1_map,
30539            },
30540        )
30541        .await?;
30542
30543        // The first coefficient commitment should trigger DepositNeeded.
30544        pin_mut!(pix_events_rx);
30545        let event = tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2), pix_events_rx.next())
30546            .await
30547            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!("timeout waiting for pix event: {e}"))?
30548            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("pix_events_rx closed without emitting an event"))?;
30549
30550        assert!(matches!(
30551            event,
30552            HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(AgreedSsaQuota { ssa_id: ref received_ssa_id, .. }, _)
30553            if received_ssa_id == &ssa_id
30554        ));
30555
30556        let HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(quota, _) = event else {
30557            unreachable!();
30558        };
30559        assert_eq!(quota.quota_per_ssa, pix_params_to_quota(&small_pix_params()));
30560
30561        bob_sender.close_channel();
30562        bob_handle.await??;
30563
30564        Ok(())
30565    }
30566
30567    /// Ingesting one cycle's commitment burst must leave the shared CPU pool to packets (hoprnet#8765).
30568    ///
30569    /// The Exit takes the burst's ~45 `SsaCommit` messages at once. On the shared pool their jobs took
30570    /// every thread, and a packet decode queued behind them waited for the whole burst. The bound is
30571    /// relative to the burst's own length, so the verdict does not depend on machine speed.
30572    #[test_log::test(tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2))]
30573    async fn ssa_commit_burst_leaves_the_shared_pool_to_packets() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30574        use std::{
30575            sync::{
30576                Arc,
30577                atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering},
30578            },
30579            time::{Duration, Instant},
30580        };
30581
30582        use hopr_crypto_packet::prelude::{HoprPixCommitmentProof, HoprPixGroupElement};
30583        use hopr_protocol_pix::{EntryShareGenerator, SsaReconstructor, SsaShareGenerator};
30584        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30585        use hopr_utils::parallelize::cpu;
30586
30587        use crate::types::{DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA, DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY, DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES};
30588
30589        // The test sizes the shared pool, which takes a process of its own, so it runs itself again,
30590        // alone, in a child process. Under `cargo test` its siblings would share the pool.
30591        const ALONE: &str = "HOPR_TEST_SSA_COMMIT_BURST_ALONE";
30592        if std::env::var_os(ALONE).is_none() {
30593            let module = module_path!().split_once("::").map_or("", |(_, module)| module);
30594            let name = format!("{module}::ssa_commit_burst_leaves_the_shared_pool_to_packets");
30595            let run = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()?)
30596                .args(["--exact", name.as_str(), "--nocapture"])
30597                .env(ALONE, "1")
30598                .output()?;
30599            let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&run.stdout);
30600            print!("{stdout}{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&run.stderr));
30601            anyhow::ensure!(
30602                run.status.success() && stdout.contains("test result: ok. 1 passed;"),
30603                "the test failed, or did not run, in a process of its own"
30604            );
30605            return Ok(());
30606        }
30607
30608        // A shared pool smaller than the burst, as on any Exit.
30609        anyhow::ensure!(
30610            cpu::init_thread_pool(2).is_ok(),
30611            "the shared CPU pool was built before this test could size it"
30612        );
30613
30614        let dims = SsaGeneratorConfig {
30615            polynomials_per_ssa: DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA,
30616            threshold: DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY,
30617            surplus_shares: DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES,
30618        };
30619        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events_rx) = PixToolbox::new(
30620            SsaShareGenerator::new(dims).into(),
30621            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30622        );
30623        let mut pix_events_rx = Box::pin(crate::testing::answering_deposit_pool(pix_events_rx, |id| {
30624            vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8; 3]
30625        }));
30626
30627        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig::default());
30628        let mut transport = MockMsgSender::new();
30629        transport
30630            .expect_send_message()
30631            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
30632        let (sender, sender_handle) = mock_packet_planning(transport);
30633        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30634        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30635            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30636            while new_session_rx.next().await.is_some() {}
30637        });
30638        mgr.start(sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
30639
30640        let entry = HoprPseudonym::random();
30641        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
30642            entry,
30643            StartInitiation {
30644                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
30645                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
30646                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
30647                additional_data: pix_additional_data(
30648                    DEFAULT_PIX_POLYS_PER_SSA,
30649                    DEFAULT_PIX_SHARES_PER_POLY,
30650                    DEFAULT_PIX_SURPLUS_SHARES,
30651                ),
30652            },
30653        )
30654        .await?;
30655
30656        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(entry, SsaIndex::MIN);
30657        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
30658            while !pix_toolbox.share_processor.contains_builder(&ssa_id) {
30659                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
30660            }
30661        })
30662        .await
30663        .context("the opening SSA request never registered an exit commitment")?;
30664
30665        // The Entry's answer: one default cycle's commitment, chunked as it goes on the wire.
30666        let entry_generator = SsaShareGenerator::<HoprPixSpec>::new(dims);
30667        let burst: Vec<SsaClientCommitmentMessage<SessionId, HoprPixGroupElement, HoprPixCommitmentProof>> =
30668            SsaClientCommitmentMessage::new_multiple(
30669                entry,
30670                entry_generator.new_ssa_commitment(&entry, SsaIndex::MIN)?,
30671            )?;
30672        let burst_len = burst.len();
30673
30674        // Packet decodes, one every 2 ms, each waiting on the shared pool as the pipeline's do.
30675        let stop = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
30676        let prober = tokio::spawn({
30677            let stop = stop.clone();
30678            async move {
30679                let mut tick = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_millis(2));
30680                let mut probes = Vec::new();
30681                while !stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
30682                    tick.tick().await;
30683                    probes.push(tokio::spawn(async {
30684                        let sent = Instant::now();
30685                        let _ = cpu::spawn_decode_blocking(|| (), "packet_decode").await;
30686                        (sent, sent.elapsed())
30687                    }));
30688                }
30689                probes
30690            }
30691        });
30692
30693        // All at once, as the control lane hands them over.
30694        let started = Instant::now();
30695        for result in futures::future::join_all(burst.into_iter().map(|msg| mgr.handle_ssa_commit(entry, msg))).await {
30696            result?;
30697        }
30698        let burst_time = started.elapsed();
30699        stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
30700        // Every probe must come back: one still queued would leave its wait out of the verdict.
30701        let probes = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), futures::future::try_join_all(prober.await?))
30702            .await
30703            .context("a probed packet decode never finished")??;
30704
30705        let completed = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), async {
30706            while let Some(event) = pix_events_rx.next().await {
30707                if matches!(&event, HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositNeeded(quota, _) if quota.ssa_id == ssa_id) {
30708                    return true;
30709                }
30710            }
30711            false
30712        })
30713        .await?;
30714        assert!(completed, "the burst must complete the cycle's commitment");
30715
30716        let mut waits: Vec<Duration> = probes
30717            .into_iter()
30718            .filter(|(sent, _)| *sent >= started && *sent < started + burst_time)
30719            .map(|(_, wait)| wait)
30720            .collect();
30721        waits.sort_unstable();
30722        let worst = *waits.last().context("no packet decode was probed during the burst")?;
30723        let median = waits[waits.len() / 2];
30724        tracing::info!(
30725            ?burst_time,
30726            ?median,
30727            ?worst,
30728            probes = waits.len(),
30729            burst_len,
30730            "packet decode waits during the commitment burst"
30731        );
30732        assert!(
30733            worst * 4 < burst_time,
30734            "a packet decode waited {worst:?} during a {burst_time:?} commitment burst (median {median:?}): the burst \
30735             held every shared pool thread"
30736        );
30737
30738        sender.close_channel();
30739        sender_handle.await??;
30740        Ok(())
30741    }
30742
30743    /// A PIX Session whose Entry never answers the `SsaRequest` has the request re-sent once, byte for
30744    /// byte, and is then closed once the commitment deadline expires.
30745    ///
30746    /// The deposit pool answers and the Session holds SURBs, so the request goes out and its re-send is
30747    /// not skipped. With a 500 ms deadline and a 200 ms interval the first re-send is due at about 200 ms
30748    /// and the second, at 600 ms, would fall past the deadline, so it is not sent. `max_deposit_wait` is
30749    /// far out of reach: arming it needs a `CommitmentVerified`, which a mock transport cannot send.
30750    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
30751    async fn session_is_closed_when_the_entry_never_commits() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30752        use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
30753
30754        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
30755        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30756
30757        const DELIVERY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
30758
30759        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
30760            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
30761            threshold: 2,
30762            surplus_shares: 1,
30763        };
30764
30765        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
30766            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
30767            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30768        );
30769
30770        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
30771            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30772                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
30773                supervision: SupervisorConfig {
30774                    max_ssa_delivery_time: DELIVERY,
30775                    // Nothing arms it: the Entry sends no commitment, so there is nothing to re-request.
30776                    commitment_recommit_interval: Duration::from_millis(100),
30777                    ssa_request_resend_interval: Duration::from_millis(200),
30778                    // Far out of reach, so it cannot be what closes the Session.
30779                    max_deposit_wait: Duration::from_secs(3600),
30780                    ..Default::default()
30781                },
30782                ..Default::default()
30783            },
30784            ..Default::default()
30785        });
30786
30787        let (bob_sender, mut sent) = futures::channel::mpsc::unbounded();
30788        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30789        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30790            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30791            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
30792        });
30793        mgr.start(bob_sender, new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
30794
30795        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
30796        // Taken before the deadline can be armed, so the lower bound below holds whatever the scheduling.
30797        let started = Instant::now();
30798        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
30799            alice_pseudonym,
30800            StartInitiation {
30801                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
30802                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
30803                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
30804                additional_data: small_pix_additional_data(),
30805            },
30806        )
30807        .await?;
30808        assert_eq!(vec![alice_pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions());
30809
30810        // Stock the Session with SURBs, or the driver skips the re-send for lack of one to send it over.
30811        {
30812            let slot = mgr
30813                .sessions
30814                .get(&alice_pseudonym)
30815                .context("the session slot must exist")?;
30816            slot.surb_estimator
30817                .produced
30818                .fetch_add(1_000, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
30819        }
30820
30821        let mut next_message = async || {
30822            tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), sent.next())
30823                .await
30824                .context("timed out waiting for a message from Bob")?
30825                .context("Bob's sender closed")
30826                .map(|(_, data)| data)
30827        };
30828
30829        let established = next_message().await?;
30830        assert!(
30831            msg_type(&established, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SessionEstablished),
30832            "the first message is SessionEstablished"
30833        );
30834        let request = next_message().await?;
30835        assert!(
30836            msg_type(&request, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaRequest),
30837            "the second message is the opening SsaRequest"
30838        );
30839        let resend = next_message().await?;
30840        assert!(
30841            msg_type(&resend, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaRequest),
30842            "the third message is a re-send of the request"
30843        );
30844        assert_eq!(
30845            (request.data.application_tag, &request.data.plain_text),
30846            (resend.data.application_tag, &resend.data.plain_text),
30847            "the re-send is the request byte for byte"
30848        );
30849
30850        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
30851            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
30852                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
30853            }
30854        })
30855        .await
30856        .context("session should be closed once the commitment deadline expires")?;
30857        assert!(
30858            started.elapsed() >= DELIVERY,
30859            "the Session closed after {:?}, earlier than the {DELIVERY:?} deadline counted from before the initiation",
30860            started.elapsed()
30861        );
30862
30863        // The Session is already closed, so nothing more is sent. The deadline guard itself is covered by the
30864        // supervisor tests.
30865        while let Ok((_, data)) = sent.try_recv() {
30866            assert!(
30867                !msg_type(&data, StartProtocolDiscriminants::SsaRequest),
30868                "no second re-send may follow"
30869            );
30870        }
30871
30872        Ok(())
30873    }
30874

30950    /// The surplus an Entry offers must survive the round trip: stored by the Exit, then echoed
30951    /// back in the `SsaRequest` it sends.
30952    ///
30953    /// It is the one negotiated value with no other consumer — it is not part of the priced quota,
30954    /// so no quota check would notice it going missing, and the Exit does not act on it yet. Every
30955    /// other dimension is pinned several times over by the checks around it.
30956    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
30957    async fn exit_stores_and_echoes_the_offered_surplus() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
30958        use hopr_protocol_pix::SsaReconstructorConfig;
30959        use hopr_protocol_start::StartInitiation;
30960
30961        // Distinct from every default, so a value read from local config instead of the wire is
30962        // visibly wrong rather than accidentally right.
30963        const OFFERED_SURPLUS: u8 = 37;
30964
30965        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
30966            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
30967                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
30968                threshold: 2,
30969                surplus_shares: TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES,
30970            })
30971            .into(),
30972            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
30973        );
30974
30975        let mgr = SessionManager::new(SessionManagerConfig {
30976            pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
30977                quota_range: 0..=1024 * 1024 * 1024,
30978                ..Default::default()
30979            },
30980            ..Default::default()
30981        });
30982
30983        let echoed: Arc<std::sync::Mutex<Vec<PixParams>>> = Arc::new(std::sync::Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
30984        let echoed_clone = echoed.clone();
30985        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
30986        bob_transport.expect_send_message().returning(move |_, data| {
30987            if let Ok(HoprStartProtocol::SsaRequest(req)) = HoprStartProtocol::try_from(data.data)
30988                && let Ok(params) = req.dimensions()
30989            {
30990                echoed_clone.lock().unwrap().push(params);
30991            }
30992            Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })
30993        });
30994
30995        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
30996        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
30997        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
30998            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
30999            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
31000        });
31001        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox), None)?;
31002
31003        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
31004        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
31005            alice_pseudonym,
31006            StartInitiation {
31007                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
31008                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
31009                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31010                additional_data: pix_additional_data(2, 2, OFFERED_SURPLUS),
31011            },
31012        )
31013        .await?;
31014
31015        let expected = PixParams::try_new(2, 2, OFFERED_SURPLUS, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
31016
31017        let slot = mgr.sessions.get(&alice_pseudonym).context("session must exist")?;
31018        let ssa_state = slot.current_ssa_state.get().context("pix state must be set")?;
31019        assert_eq!(
31020            expected, ssa_state.params,
31021            "the Exit must keep the surplus the Entry offered, not its own"
31022        );
31023
31024        // The echo does not go out inline: the supervisor's opening `RequestSsa` is carried out by
31025        // the action driver spawned once the Session is published, which is what keeps
31026        // `SessionEstablished` ahead of `SsaRequest` on the wire.
31027        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
31028            while echoed.lock().unwrap().is_empty() {
31029                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
31030            }
31031        })
31032        .await
31033        .context("the supervisor's opening SsaRequest never reached the wire")?;
31034
31035        bob_sender.close_channel();
31036        bob_handle.await??;
31037
31038        let echoed = echoed.lock().unwrap().clone();
31039        assert_eq!(
31040            vec![expected],
31041            echoed,
31042            "the SsaRequest must echo back exactly what was offered"
31043        );
31044
31045        Ok(())
31046    }

31048    /// Verifies that `check_pix_params` rejects out-of-bounds parameters that pass the
31049    /// quota-range check but exceed the protocol limits.
31050    ///
31051    /// This is a regression test for the incentive-bypass fix (round-1 finding #1).
31052    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31053    async fn check_pix_params_must_reject_invalid_bounds() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31054        let mgr =
31055            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
31056                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
31057                    quota_range: 0..=10_000_000_000_000,
31058                    ..Default::default()
31059                },
31060                ..Default::default()
31061            });
31062
31063        let offer = |additional_data: u64| StartInitiation {
31064            challenge: 0,
31065            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
31066            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31067            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(additional_data, Duration::ZERO),
31068        };
31069        // Packed by hand rather than through `pix_additional_data`, because that helper refuses to
31070        // build the very values under test. The layout it mirrors is pinned in `PixParams`' own
31071        // tests. The suite is this build's, so that the dimension cases below fail on their
31072        // dimensions rather than on a curve mismatch — that rejection has its own test.
31073        let packed = |polys: u16, shares: u8, surplus: u8| {
31074            ((LOCAL_PIX_SUITE as u64) << 62)
31075                | ((polys as u64) << 48)
31076                | ((shares as u64) << 40)
31077                | ((surplus as u64) << 32)
31078        };
31079
31080        // polys_per_ssa > MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA (16192), and zero, with a valid quota -> should reject
31081        for polys in [0, MAX_POLYS_PER_SSA + 1, u16::MAX] {
31082            assert!(
31083                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(polys, 128, 0))).is_none(),
31084                "should reject polys_per_ssa {polys}"
31085            );
31086        }
31087
31088        // shares_per_poly < MIN_POLY_THRESHOLD with a valid quota -> should reject. There is no
31089        // matching upper-bound case: the threshold is a byte on the wire, so `MAX_POLY_THRESHOLD`
31090        // cannot be exceeded by anything a peer is able to send.
31091        for shares in [0, 1] {
31092            assert!(
31093                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, shares, 0))).is_none(),
31094                "should reject shares_per_poly {shares}"
31095            );
31096        }
31097
31098        // Valid params should still be accepted, and arrive intact — including the surplus, which
31099        // no other check looks at and which would therefore be free to go missing.
31100        let (accepted, batch_size) =
31101            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, 128, 37))).context("should accept valid params")?;
31102        assert_eq!(PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, 37, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?, accepted);
31103        assert_eq!(1, batch_size);
31104
31105        // Every surplus a byte can hold is legal.
31106        for surplus in [0, 1, u8::MAX] {
31107            assert_eq!(
31108                Some((PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?, 1)),
31109                decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(packed(8192, 128, surplus)))
31110            );
31111        }
31112
31113        Ok(())
31114    }
31115
31116    /// The Exit refuses a client whose PIX curve suite is not the one this node was built for.
31117    ///
31118    /// The curve is a build-time property on both sides and is not negotiated, so the only two
31119    /// outcomes are "same suite" and "refused". This matters because it happens *before* the Exit
31120    /// commits: every later PIX field — each coefficient commitment, the proof of knowledge — is
31121    /// sized by the curve, so a mismatch that got past here would surface as undecodable Start
31122    /// traffic on a Session both sides believed they had established.
31123    ///
31124    /// The quota range is wide open, so nothing but the suite can be doing the rejecting.
31125    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31126    async fn check_pix_params_must_refuse_a_foreign_curve_suite() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31127        let mgr =
31128            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
31129                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
31130                    quota_range: 0..=10_000_000_000_000,
31131                    ..Default::default()
31132                },
31133                ..Default::default()
31134            });
31135
31136        let offer = |suite: hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite| StartInitiation {
31137            challenge: 0,
31138            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
31139            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31140            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
31141                PixParams::try_new(8192, 128, 37, suite)
31142                    .expect("test dimensions must be valid")
31143                    .into_additional_data(0),
31144                Duration::ZERO,
31145            ),
31146        };
31147
31148        let foreign = match LOCAL_PIX_SUITE {
31149            hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::BabyJubJub => hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::Secp256k1,
31150            hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::Secp256k1 => hopr_protocol_pix::PixSuite::BabyJubJub,
31151        };
31152
31153        assert!(
31154            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(foreign)).is_none(),
31155            "a client offering {foreign} must be refused by a {LOCAL_PIX_SUITE} Exit"
31156        );
31157        assert!(
31158            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)).is_some(),
31159            "and the same dimensions on this build's own curve must still be accepted"
31160        );
31161
31162        // A suite identifier no curve claims is refused as well, rather than read as a third curve.
31163        let unknown = StartInitiation {
31164            challenge: 0,
31165            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
31166            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31167            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(
31168                (0b11u64 << 62) | (8192u64 << 48) | (128u64 << 40) | (37u64 << 32),
31169                Duration::ZERO,
31170            ),
31171        };
31172        assert!(
31173            decode_and_check(&mgr, &unknown).is_none(),
31174            "an unknown suite identifier must be refused"
31175        );
31176
31177        Ok(())
31178    }
31179
31180    /// The Exit judges an offer by its quota alone; the split is the Entry's choice.
31181    ///
31182    /// The surplus is insurance against the return relayers the *Entry* picks for its SURBs, and only
31183    /// the Entry knows how far it trusts them: one expecting most of them to fail may buy
31184    /// `4096 × (2 + 102)`, which carries ~86 % share loss where the deployed split carries ~50 %. What
31185    /// the Exit has a stake in is how much it serves for one deposit, which is the quota —
31186    /// `polys × (threshold + surplus)` shares — so every split whose quota fits `quota_range` is
31187    /// accepted, whatever its ratio of surplus to threshold, and the Entry's successor gate then
31188    /// follows the tolerance it bought.
31189    ///
31190    /// Reconstructor memory is also reserved from the offered dimensions, at admission against
31191    /// `max_live_cycle_bytes`. That is a capacity check, and one the configuration validator holds to
31192    /// admitting a Session at any split of the advertised quota — not a policy on the split.
31193    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31194    async fn the_exit_judges_an_offer_by_its_quota_alone() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31195        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31196        let offer = |params: PixParams| StartInitiation {
31197            challenge: 0,
31198            target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse().unwrap())),
31199            capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31200            additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0), Duration::ZERO),
31201        };
31202
31203        // The default range, in shares, is a quarter of the deployed cycle up to the whole of it:
31204        // 113 664 ..= 454 656.
31205        for (polys, threshold, surplus, quota_shares) in [
31206            (4096u16, 2u8, 102u8, 425_984u64),
31207            (1024, 2, 255, 263_168),
31208            (16192, 2, 26, 453_376),
31209            (4096, 32, 79, 454_656),
31210        ] {
31211            let params = PixParams::try_new(polys, threshold, surplus, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
31212            assert_eq!(quota_shares * PIX_QUOTA_BYTES_PER_SHARE, pix_params_to_quota(&params));
31213
31214            let (accepted, _) = decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(params)).with_context(|| {
31215                format!("{polys} x ({threshold} + {surplus}) fits the default quota range and must be accepted")
31216            })?;
31217            assert_eq!(params, accepted, "the split must arrive as offered");
31218        }
31219
31220        // The same threshold and the most surplus the byte carries, at a polynomial count whose quota
31221        // — 1 052 672 shares — is past the top of the range. Refused, and by the quota alone.
31222        let over = PixParams::try_new(4096, 2, u8::MAX, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?;
31223        assert!(pix_params_to_quota(&over) > *IncomingSessionPixConfig::default().quota_range.end());
31224        assert!(
31225            decode_and_check(&mgr, &offer(over)).is_none(),
31226            "an offer whose quota exceeds the range must be refused"
31227        );
31228
31229        Ok(())
31230    }
31231
31232    /// Verifies that dispatching too many `UnverifiableShare` events closes the session.
31233    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31234    async fn too_many_unverifiable_shares_closes_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31235        let params = small_pix_params();
31236        let quota = pix_params_to_quota(&params);
31237        let ssa_gen_config = SsaGeneratorConfig {
31238            polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
31239            threshold: 2,
31240            surplus_shares: 1,
31241        };
31242
31243        let pix_toolbox = pix_toolbox_with_pool(
31244            SsaShareGenerator::new(ssa_gen_config).into(),
31245            SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default()).into(),
31246        );
31247
31248        let mgr =
31249            SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(SessionManagerConfig {
31250                pix_config: IncomingSessionPixConfig {
31251                    quota_range: quota..=quota,
31252                    max_live_cycle_bytes: max_cycle_budget_for_quota(quota, 1),
31253                    supervision: SupervisorConfig {
31254                        max_deposit_wait: Duration::from_secs(1),
31255                        ..Default::default()
31256                    },
31257                    ..Default::default()
31258                },
31259                ..Default::default()
31260            });
31261
31262        let mut bob_transport = MockMsgSender::new();
31263        bob_transport
31264            .expect_send_message()
31265            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
31266        bob_transport
31267            .expect_send_message()
31268            .returning(|_, _| Box::pin(async { Ok(()) }));
31269
31270        let (bob_sender, bob_handle) = mock_packet_planning(bob_transport);
31271        let (new_session_tx, new_session_rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
31272        let _notifications = tokio::spawn(async move {
31273            pin_mut!(new_session_rx);
31274            while let Some(_session) = new_session_rx.next().await {}
31275        });
31276        mgr.start(bob_sender.clone(), new_session_tx, Some(pix_toolbox.clone()), None)?;
31277
31278        let alice_pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
31279
31280        mgr.handle_incoming_session_initiation(
31281            alice_pseudonym,
31282            StartInitiation {
31283                challenge: MIN_CHALLENGE,
31284                target: SessionTarget::TcpStream(SealedHost::Plain("127.0.0.1:80".parse()?)),
31285                capabilities: HoprSessionCapabilities(Capability::UsePIX.into()),
31286                additional_data: into_initiation_additional_data(params.into_additional_data(0), Duration::ZERO),
31287            },
31288        )
31289        .await?;
31290
31291        // Session is active
31292        assert_eq!(vec![alice_pseudonym], mgr.active_sessions());
31293
31294        let ssa_id = SsaId::new(alice_pseudonym, SsaIndex::new(1).expect("non-zero"));
31295
31296        // Exactly one event, reporting the absolute total the reconstructor would carry for a single
31297        // failed polynomial. There is no tolerance to exhaust first.
31298        let result = mgr
31299            .dispatch_pix_event(HoprSessionInPixEvent::UnverifiableShares {
31300                ssa_id,
31301                observed_total: 1,
31302                peer: crate::supervision::test_peer(),
31303            })
31304            .await;
31305        // Forwarding succeeds even for the event that closes: the supervisor decides, and it does so
31306        // after the send has been accepted.
31307        assert!(result.is_ok(), "dispatch_pix_event should not return an error");
31308
31309        // The supervisor's `Close` reaches the driver asynchronously, so the teardown it triggers
31310        // is observed rather than assumed.
31311        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), async {
31312            while mgr.num_active_sessions() > 0 {
31313                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10)).await;
31314            }
31315        })
31316        .await
31317        .context("session was not closed after too many unverifiable shares")?;
31318
31319        assert!(mgr.active_sessions().is_empty());
31320
31321        bob_sender.close_channel();
31322        bob_handle.await??;
31323
31324        Ok(())
31325    }
31326
31327    /// Verifies that `allocate_session_slot` signals waiters via `.send(())` rather than
31328    /// dropping the senders. The `Ok(Ok(()))` path in `handle_ssa_request` must be live.
31329    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31330    async fn allocate_session_slot_must_signal_waiters_not_cancel_them() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31331        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
31332        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31333
31334        // Register a waiter before the slot is allocated
31335        let (tx, mut rx) = oneshot::channel::<()>();
31336        mgr.slot_allocated
31337            .lock()
31338            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
31339            .entry(session_id)
31340            .or_default()
31341            .push(tx);
31342
31343        let (session_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
31344
31345        // Allocate the slot — this should signal the waiter. The slot is inserted here so that the
31346        // `commit` below can find it: that is where the token `admit` returns lands.
31347        let slot = SessionSlot {
31348            session_tx,
31349            routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(session_id)),
31350            abort_handles: Default::default(),
31351            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(SurbBalancerConfig::default())),
31352            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
31353            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
31354            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
31355            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
31356            pix_fill: Default::default(),
31357            exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
31358            returned_packets: Default::default(),
31359            cycle_budget: None,
31360            admission_token: Default::default(),
31361            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
31362            forward_receipts: None,
31363            exit_resume: Default::default(),
31364            instance: SlotInstance::new(0),
31365            opening: None,
31366        };
31367        let guard = mgr.allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone());
31368        assert!(guard.is_some(), "slot allocation must succeed");
31369
31370        // The waiter should receive Some(()) — the direct signal, not Canceled
31371        assert!(
31372            matches!(rx.try_recv(), Ok(Some(()))),
31373            "waiter must be signaled with Ok(()), not canceled"
31374        );
31375
31376        guard.unwrap().commit(Some(&slot), None, 0);
31377
31378        Ok(())
31379    }
31380
31381    /// Builds a slot for `session_id` that is not yet in any cache, for the guard tests below.
31382    fn unregistered_slot(session_id: SessionId) -> SessionSlot {
31383        let (session_tx, _) = crossfire::mpsc::bounded_blocking_async::<ApplicationDataIn>(SESSION_FORWARD_CAPACITY);
31384        SessionSlot {
31385            session_tx,
31386            routing_opts: DestinationRouting::Return(SurbMatcher::Pseudonym(session_id)),
31387            abort_handles: Default::default(),
31388            surb_mgmt: Arc::new(BalancerStateValues::from(SurbBalancerConfig::default())),
31389            surb_estimator: Default::default(),
31390            current_ssa_state: Default::default(),
31391            pix_supervisor: Default::default(),
31392            pix_egress_gate: Default::default(),
31393            pix_fill: Default::default(),
31394            exit_loss_signal: Default::default(),
31395            returned_packets: Default::default(),
31396            cycle_budget: None,
31397            admission_token: Default::default(),
31398            raised_surb_target: Default::default(),
31399            forward_receipts: None,
31400            exit_resume: Default::default(),
31401            instance: SlotInstance::new(0),
31402            opening: None,
31403        }
31404    }
31405
31406    /// A commit that finds its slot already gone must still commit the Session.
31407    ///
31408    /// The Session *was* established on this path — the Exit sends `SessionEstablished` before it
31409    /// commits, so an Entry can close or answer with a `SessionId`-scoped `SessionError` in that
31410    /// window — so the guard must be marked committed rather than rolled back. Only the admission is
31411    /// skipped: there is no slot left to carry its token. Skipping the commit instead would leave the
31412    /// teardown's "session closed" unpaired.
31413    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31414    async fn a_commit_without_a_slot_still_commits_the_session() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31415        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
31416        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
31417        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31418
31419        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
31420        let mut guard = mgr
31421            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
31422            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
31423
31424        // The teardown wins the race and removes the slot before the commit runs.
31425        assert!(
31426            mgr.sessions.remove(&session_id).is_some(),
31427            "the slot must have been registered"
31428        );
31429
31430        guard.commit(None, Some(&admission), 0);
31431
31432        assert!(
31433            guard.committed,
31434            "a Session that was established must be committed, not rolled back, even with no slot left"
31435        );
31436        assert_eq!(
31437            admission.admitted(&session_id),
31438            0,
31439            "with no slot to carry the token, nothing may be admitted"
31440        );
31441        assert_eq!(
31442            admission.retired(&session_id),
31443            0,
31444            "a commit that admitted nothing must retire nothing"
31445        );
31446        Ok(())
31447    }
31448
31449    /// A teardown that claims the token cell before `commit` runs forces the commit to retire its own
31450    /// admission.
31451    ///
31452    /// The order is the Exit-side one: `SessionEstablished` goes out before the commit, so a peer can
31453    /// close in that window. The teardown claims the cell and reads `NONE` (a no-op retire), and the
31454    /// commit then finds its `set` rejected — so it retires the admission it just made, or the ring
31455    /// would leak with no teardown ever removing it.
31456    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31457    async fn a_teardown_claiming_the_cell_first_forces_the_commit_to_retire_its_admission() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31458        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
31459        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
31460        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31461
31462        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
31463        let mut guard = mgr
31464            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
31465            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
31466
31467        // The teardown gets there first: it claims the cell and reads `NONE`, so its scheduled retire
31468        // is a no-op.
31469        assert_eq!(
31470            slot.claim_admission_token(),
31471            AdmissionToken::NONE,
31472            "an uncommitted slot's claimed token must be NONE"
31473        );
31474
31475        // The commit still runs and admits, but cannot record the token — so it must retire it.
31476        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 100);
31477
31478        let minted = admission.minted_tokens();
31479        assert_eq!(
31480            minted.len(),
31481            1,
31482            "the commit must still admit the Session it was told to commit"
31483        );
31484        assert_eq!(
31485            admission.retire_tokens(),
31486            vec![minted[0]],
31487            "the admission the commit could not record must be retired by the commit itself"
31488        );
31489        Ok(())
31490    }
31491
31492    /// A commit must size the ring from a target the Entry announced before it.
31493    ///
31494    /// The Exit answers `SessionEstablished` before it commits, so a `BalancerTarget` keep-alive can
31495    /// be processed while the ring does not exist yet. Its raise has no admission to widen; it records
31496    /// the figure on the slot, and the commit has to start from the larger of it and the target
31497    /// announced at establishment — otherwise an Entry that announces its main tier early gets a
31498    /// ping-tier ring and evicts everything minted past it (gnosis/gnosis_vpn#739, one interleaving
31499    /// earlier).
31500    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31501    async fn a_commit_must_size_the_ring_from_a_target_announced_before_it() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31502        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
31503        let session_id = HoprPseudonym::random();
31504        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31505
31506        let slot = unregistered_slot(session_id);
31507        let mut guard = mgr
31508            .allocate_session_slot(session_id, slot.clone())
31509            .context("slot allocation must succeed")?;
31510
31511        // The Entry's main tier, announced while the Session is established but not yet committed.
31512        slot.note_raised_surb_target(6_887);
31513        guard.commit(Some(&slot), Some(&admission), 688);
31514
31515        assert_eq!(
31516            vec![6_887],
31517            admission.admitted_targets(),
31518            "the commit must admit at the largest target already announced, not the ping tier"
31519        );
31520        Ok(())
31521    }
31522
31523    /// A commit whose re-read finds a *successor's* slot on the same pseudonym must not admit into it.
31524    ///
31525    /// The pseudonym is client-chosen and reusable, so a slot can be torn down and reallocated under
31526    /// the same key between a Session's `SessionEstablished` send and its parked commit. That commit
31527    /// re-reads the cache by key to land its token in the cached copy, and the copy it finds is then
31528    /// the successor's — admitting into it would stamp the successor's ring with this Session's token,
31529    /// and the successor's own commit would find the cell occupied and retire the successor's live
31530    /// admission, dropping a running Session to the quarantine. This is the commit-vs-commit arm the
31531    /// teardown-vs-commit test above does not reach: the slot is *present*, just not this one's, so the
31532    /// ownership marker — not absence — has to reject it.
31533    ///
31534    /// A true concurrent commit is not drivable from a test without instrumenting the manager, so the
31535    /// interleaving is built explicitly: A allocates and is torn down (freeing the key), B is allocated
31536    /// under the same key, and only then does A's parked commit run through `commit_slot_guard`.
31537    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31538    async fn a_commit_must_not_admit_into_a_successors_slot_on_the_same_pseudonym() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31539        let admission = RecordingAdmission::default();
31540        let pseudonym = HoprPseudonym::random();
31541        let mgr = SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::new(Default::default());
31542        mgr.set_surb_admission(Arc::new(admission.clone()));
31543
31544        // A allocates and then loses its slot to a teardown, which also claims the cell.
31545        let mut guard_a = mgr
31546            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, unregistered_slot(pseudonym))
31547            .context("A's slot allocation must succeed")?;
31548        let slot_a = mgr
31549            .sessions
31550            .remove(&pseudonym)
31551            .context("the teardown must have found A's slot")?;
31552        assert_eq!(
31553            slot_a.claim_admission_token(),
31554            AdmissionToken::NONE,
31555            "A's teardown must claim the cell and read nothing, so its scheduled retire is a no-op"
31556        );
31557
31558        // B is allocated under the same key before A's commit resumes. B's slot is the one the cache
31559        // now hands back for that pseudonym.
31560        let guard_b = mgr
31561            .allocate_session_slot(pseudonym, unregistered_slot(pseudonym))
31562            .context("B's slot allocation must succeed under the freed pseudonym")?;
31563
31564        // A's commit re-reads the key and finds B's slot, which it must refuse as not its own.
31565        commit_slot_guard(&mut guard_a, &mgr.sessions, pseudonym, mgr.surb_admission.clone(), 100);
31566
31567        assert!(
31568            guard_a.committed,
31569            "A was established, so its commit must still mark it committed"
31570        );
31571        assert_eq!(
31572            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
31573            0,
31574            "A must not admit into B's slot — a foreign slot is no more A's to admit into than an absent one"
31575        );
31576        assert_eq!(
31577            admission.retired(&pseudonym),
31578            0,
31579            "A must not retire anything either: it admitted nothing"
31580        );
31581
31582        // B's own commit is the one that admits, and it must land on B's untouched cell.
31583        let mut guard_b = guard_b;
31584        commit_slot_guard(&mut guard_b, &mgr.sessions, pseudonym, mgr.surb_admission.clone(), 100);
31585        assert_eq!(
31586            admission.admitted(&pseudonym),
31587            1,
31588            "B's commit is the only admission on this pseudonym and must still happen"
31589        );
31590        assert!(
31591            admission.retire_tokens().is_empty(),
31592            "B's live admission must not be retired by A's commit — the successor ring is not A's to release"
31593        );
31594        Ok(())
31595    }
31596
31597    /// What the Exit reports back to its pool must be what the Exit sent.
31598    ///
31599    /// The pool answers over a channel and nothing stops it answering for an SSA that is not in the
31600    /// batch, or for another Session entirely. Those replies are dropped from the wire; they must be
31601    /// dropped from the Exit's own memory of the batch too. Keying whole replies by `id.ssa_index()`
31602    /// did not do that: a foreign reply naming an in-batch index displaced the good entry, and
31603    /// `DepositNeeded` then handed the pool back deposit data belonging to another Session.
31604    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31605    async fn a_foreign_deposit_reply_must_not_displace_what_the_exit_sent() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31606        use hopr_protocol_pix::{SsaGeneratorConfig, SsaReconstructorConfig};
31607
31608        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31609        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31610        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN];
31611
31612        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
31613            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
31614                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
31615                threshold: 2,
31616                surplus_shares: 1,
31617            })
31618            .into(),
31619            Arc::new(SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default())),
31620        );
31621        drop(pix_events);
31622        let _ = pix_toolbox;
31623
31624        let ssa_state = SessionSsaState::new(PixParams::try_new(2, 2, TEST_SURPLUS_SHARES, LOCAL_PIX_SUITE)?);
31625
31626        // What the pool sent: the right entry, then a same-index entry belonging to another Session.
31627        let replies = vec![
31628            PixDepositData {
31629                id: PixAddressId::new(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN),
31630                data: b"mine".as_slice().into(),
31631            },
31632            PixDepositData {
31633                id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, SsaIndex::MIN),
31634                data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
31635            },
31636        ];
31637
31638        // Only the validated map is remembered, which is the whole point.
31639        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, replies)?;
31640        ssa_state.remember_sent_deposit_data(&validated);
31641
31642        let recalled = ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN);
31643        assert_eq!(
31644            b"mine".as_slice(),
31645            recalled.data.as_ref(),
31646            "the Exit must recall the payload it actually sent"
31647        );
31648        assert_eq!(
31649            PixAddressId::new(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN),
31650            recalled.id,
31651            "the id must name this Session and this index"
31652        );
31653
31654        // Consumed exactly once; a second cycle would see empty rather than a stale entry.
31655        assert!(
31656            ssa_state.take_sent_deposit_data(&session_id, SsaIndex::MIN).is_empty(),
31657            "taking must remove the entry"
31658        );
31659
31660        Ok(())
31661    }
31662
31663    /// Runs [`request_deposit_data`](SessionManager::request_deposit_data) against a pool that answers
31664    /// with exactly what `script` returns, in that order.
31665    ///
31666    /// `script` is handed the ids the Exit asked for and returns the replies the pool will send, one
31667    /// at a time — which is what makes reply *ordering* expressible, and ordering is the only thing
31668    /// the tests below differ on from a run that never had a problem.
31669    ///
31670    /// The pool holds its sender open after the script runs out, rather than dropping it and ending
31671    /// the stream. A pool that closes the channel ends the read all by itself, which would let a test
31672    /// pass on that alone — the reason the collection stopped is exactly what these tests are about,
31673    /// so the only things left to stop it are the ones under test.
31674    async fn request_deposit_data_answered_with(
31675        session_id: SessionId,
31676        batch: &[SsaIndex],
31677        script: impl FnOnce(Vec<PixAddressId>) -> Vec<PixDepositData> + Send + 'static,
31678    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
31679        request_deposit_data_pool(session_id, batch, DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, false, script).await
31680    }
31681
31682    /// [`request_deposit_data_answered_with`] with the deadline, and with the choice of whether the pool
31683    /// closes its reply channel once the script has run out instead of holding it open.
31684    async fn request_deposit_data_pool(
31685        session_id: SessionId,
31686        batch: &[SsaIndex],
31687        deadline: Duration,
31688        close_when_done: bool,
31689        script: impl FnOnce(Vec<PixAddressId>) -> Vec<PixDepositData> + Send + 'static,
31690    ) -> errors::Result<HoprPixDepositData> {
31691        let (pix_toolbox, pix_events) = PixToolbox::new(
31692            SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
31693                polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
31694                threshold: 2,
31695                surplus_shares: 1,
31696            })
31697            .into(),
31698            Arc::new(SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default())),
31699        );
31700
31701        tokio::task::spawn(async move {
31702            let mut events = Box::pin(pix_events);
31703            if let Some(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest(request)) = events.next().await {
31704                let mut created = request.deposit_data_created;
31705                for reply in script(request.deposit_ids) {
31706                    if created.send(reply).await.is_err() {
31707                        return;
31708                    }
31709                }
31710                if close_when_done {
31711                    return;
31712                }
31713                // Held open, not dropped — see above. The task is torn down with the test's runtime.
31714                std::future::pending::<()>().await;
31715            }
31716        });
31717
31718        SessionManager::<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>::request_deposit_data_within(
31719            &pix_toolbox,
31720            session_id,
31721            batch,
31722            deadline,
31723        )
31724        .await
31725    }
31726
31727    /// A reply the batch has no place for must not cost a reply that was asked for.
31728    ///
31729    /// The pool answers over one channel, and nothing about that channel separates a reply for this
31730    /// batch from another Session's. Reading a fixed number of *items* — one per requested SSA — let
31731    /// the first kind spend a slot belonging to the second, so a pool that answered every SSA and
31732    /// merely spoke out of turn lost the Session on the answer that got truncated.
31733    ///
31734    /// Ordering is the whole test: the same foreign reply arriving *after* the batch was complete
31735    /// never cost anything, because the collection had already stopped.
31736    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31737    async fn a_foreign_reply_before_a_valid_one_must_not_truncate_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31738        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31739        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31740        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
31741
31742        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, move |ids| {
31743            std::iter::once(PixDepositData {
31744                id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, SsaIndex::MIN),
31745                data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
31746            })
31747            .chain(ids.into_iter().map(|id| PixDepositData {
31748                id,
31749                data: b"mine".as_slice().into(),
31750            }))
31751            .collect()
31752        })
31753        .await
31754        .context("a pool that answered every requested SSA must not fail the request")?;
31755
31756        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
31757            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
31758
31759        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
31760        for index in batch {
31761            assert_eq!(
31762                b"mine".as_slice(),
31763                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
31764                "index {index} must carry this Session's payload"
31765            );
31766        }
31767
31768        Ok(())
31769    }
31770
31771    /// A second answer for an SSA already answered must not cost an SSA still outstanding.
31772    ///
31773    /// Same failure as the foreign reply above, from the other direction: the repeat is a reply the
31774    /// batch has no place for, and counting items charged it against the one SSA that had not been
31775    /// answered yet. Which copy of the repeat wins is not what is under test here — that
31776    /// [`deposit_data_for_batch`] takes the later one is incidental — only that the reply after it
31777    /// still arrives.
31778    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31779    async fn a_duplicate_reply_before_a_valid_one_must_not_truncate_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31780        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31781        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
31782
31783        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, |ids| {
31784            let mut replies = ids
31785                .iter()
31786                .map(|id| PixDepositData {
31787                    id: *id,
31788                    data: vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8].into_boxed_slice(),
31789                })
31790                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
31791            // The repeat of the first answer is inserted before the last one, so counting items
31792            // would have stopped on it and never read the SSA it was hiding.
31793            replies.insert(1, replies[0].clone());
31794            replies
31795        })
31796        .await
31797        .context("a pool that repeated itself but answered every SSA must not fail the request")?;
31798
31799        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
31800            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
31801
31802        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
31803        for index in batch {
31804            assert_eq!(
31805                &[index.get() as u8],
31806                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
31807                "index {index} must carry its own payload"
31808            );
31809        }
31810
31811        Ok(())
31812    }
31813
31814    /// Tolerating replies the batch has no place for must not become waiting for the deadline.
31815    ///
31816    /// Reading until every requested id is answered has no natural end when the pool never answers
31817    /// one, so the read is capped at twice the requested count. A pool that talks without ever
31818    /// closing the gap is cut off there and the request fails on the gap — which is the same
31819    /// verdict the deadline would reach, minus the [`DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`] spent reaching
31820    /// it, with the Session held open throughout.
31821    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31822    async fn a_pool_answering_only_noise_must_fail_on_the_cap_not_the_deadline() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31823        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31824        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31825        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
31826
31827        // Exactly the cap, and not one of them is for this Session.
31828        let noise = move |ids: Vec<PixAddressId>| {
31829            ids.iter()
31830                .flat_map(|id| {
31831                    std::iter::repeat_n(
31832                        PixDepositData {
31833                            id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, id.ssa_index()),
31834                            data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
31835                        },
31836                        2,
31837                    )
31838                })
31839                .collect()
31840        };
31841
31842        // Well under the deadline: the point is that the cap ends the read, not the clock.
31843        let result = timeout(
31844            Duration::from_secs(1),
31845            request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, noise),
31846        )
31847        .await
31848        .context("the cap must end the read long before DEPOSIT_DATA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT")?;
31849
31850        assert!(
31851            matches!(
31852                result,
31853                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(
31854                    _
31855                )))
31856            ),
31857            "a pool that answered none of the requested SSAs must fail the request, got {result:?}"
31858        );
31859
31860        Ok(())
31861    }
31862
31863    /// The reply that lands exactly on the cap still counts.
31864    ///
31865    /// One reply earlier and the batch would be complete without the cap ever mattering, so this is
31866    /// the only arrangement that tells `take(2 * requested)` apart from `take(2 * requested - 1)`:
31867    /// every requested SSA is answered, but the last answer is the last reply the read will accept.
31868    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31869    async fn the_last_reply_the_cap_allows_must_still_complete_the_batch() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31870        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31871        let other_session: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31872        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN, SsaIndex::new(2).expect("non-zero")];
31873
31874        let collected = request_deposit_data_answered_with(session_id, &batch, move |ids| {
31875            // One unusable reply per requested id, then the answers themselves — `2 * requested`
31876            // replies in total, with the one that closes the gap sitting on the boundary.
31877            ids.iter()
31878                .map(|id| PixDepositData {
31879                    id: PixAddressId::new(&other_session, id.ssa_index()),
31880                    data: b"someone else's".as_slice().into(),
31881                })
31882                .chain(ids.iter().map(|id| PixDepositData {
31883                    id: *id,
31884                    data: vec![id.ssa_index().get() as u8].into_boxed_slice(),
31885                }))
31886                .collect()
31887        })
31888        .await
31889        .context("the answer landing on the cap must be read, not cut off by it")?;
31890
31891        let validated = deposit_data_for_batch(&session_id, &batch, collected)
31892            .context("every SSA in the batch must come out with an entry")?;
31893
31894        assert_eq!(batch.len(), validated.len(), "the whole batch must be covered");
31895        for index in batch {
31896            assert_eq!(
31897                &[index.get() as u8],
31898                validated[&index].0.as_ref(),
31899                "index {index} must carry its own payload"
31900            );
31901        }
31902
31903        Ok(())
31904    }

31990    /// A full request queue is the pool being too slow; a closed one means nothing listens.
31991    #[test_log::test(tokio::test)]
31992    async fn a_full_request_queue_is_too_slow_and_a_closed_one_is_missing_data() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
31993        let session_id: SessionId = HoprPseudonym::random();
31994        let batch = [SsaIndex::MIN];
31995        let new_toolbox = || {
31996            PixToolbox::new(
31997                SsaShareGenerator::new(SsaGeneratorConfig {
31998                    polynomials_per_ssa: 2,
31999                    threshold: 2,
32000                    surplus_shares: 1,
32001                })
32002                .into(),
32003                Arc::new(SsaReconstructor::new(SsaReconstructorConfig::default())),
32004            )
32005        };
32006        type Mgr = SessionManager<UnboundedSender<(DestinationRouting, ApplicationDataOut)>>;
32007
32008        // Nobody reads the events, so filling the queue leaves the next request nowhere to go.
32009        let (full, _events) = new_toolbox();
32010        loop {
32011            let (deposit_data_created, _rx) = futures::channel::mpsc::channel(1);
32012            if full
32013                .pix_events
32014                .try_send(HoprSessionOutPixEvent::DepositDataRequest(PixDepositDataRequest {
32015                    deposit_ids: Vec::new(),
32016                    deposit_data_created,
32017                }))
32018                .is_err()
32019            {
32020                break;
32021            }
32022        }
32023        let result = Mgr::request_deposit_data(&full, session_id, &batch).await;
32024        assert!(
32025            matches!(
32026                result,
32027                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::DepositPoolTooSlow(
32028                    _
32029                )))
32030            ),
32031            "got {result:?}"
32032        );
32033
32034        let (closed, events) = new_toolbox();
32035        drop(events);
32036        let result = Mgr::request_deposit_data(&closed, session_id, &batch).await;
32037        assert!(
32038            matches!(
32039                result,
32040                Err(TransportSessionError::Manager(SessionManagerError::MissingDepositData(
32041                    _
32042                )))
32043            ),
32044            "got {result:?}"
32045        );
32046        Ok(())
32047    }

32049    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
32050    // PIX egress gate pressure
32051    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
32052
32053    /// The egress path opens exactly one block episode per park, and closes it when the park ends.
32054    ///
32055    /// Asserted here rather than in the gate's own tests because the wiring is what can be wrong:
32056    /// the gate reports a verdict, and this is the only place that turns the verdict into an
32057    /// episode. A permit path that forgot to would leave `hopr_pix_gate_blocks_total` silent while
32058    /// egress was stalled -- exactly the fault the metric exists to surface.
32059    #[tokio::test]
32060    async fn a_parked_egress_packet_opens_and_closes_one_block_episode() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
32061        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
32062
32063        probe::reset();
32064        // Strict prepay: the first packet is refused before anything is served.
32065        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
32066
32067        let permit = acquire_egress_permit(
32068            Some(gate.clone()),
32069            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
32070            ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(
32071                SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG,
32072                b"payload".as_slice(),
32073            )?),
32074        );
32075
32076        assert_eq!(
32077            1,
32078            probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"),
32079            "the refusal must be counted as one episode beginning"
32080        );
32081        assert_eq!(
32082            0,
32083            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
32084            "and must stay open while the packet is still parked"
32085        );
32086
32087        // Funding wakes the parked writer, which ends the episode.
32088        gate.release_service();
32089        timeout(Duration::from_secs(5), permit)
32090            .await
32091            .context("funding must wake the parked packet")?
32092            .context("a funded gate must admit it")?;
32093
32094        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"), "still one episode");
32095        assert_eq!(
32096            1,
32097            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
32098            "resuming must close the episode exactly once"
32099        );
32100        Ok(())
32101    }
32102
32103    /// Cancelling a parked packet closes its episode too.
32104    ///
32105    /// The case `Drop` exists for: a Session torn down while a writer is parked drops the permit
32106    /// future without ever resolving it, and a timer that only closed on the resume path would be
32107    /// left open for every Session that died blocked.
32108    #[tokio::test]
32109    async fn dropping_a_parked_egress_packet_closes_its_episode() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
32110        use crate::supervision::telemetry::probe;
32111
32112        probe::reset();
32113        let gate = ServiceGate::new(0, 10);
32114
32115        let permit = acquire_egress_permit(
32116            Some(gate.clone()),
32117            DestinationRouting::Return(HoprPseudonym::random().into()),
32118            ApplicationDataOut::with_no_packet_info(ApplicationData::new(
32119                SESSION_APPLICATION_TAG,
32120                b"payload".as_slice(),
32121            )?),
32122        );
32123        // Poll it once so the episode is actually begun inside the future.
32124        assert!(
32125            timeout(Duration::from_millis(50), permit).await.is_err(),
32126            "the packet must park rather than resolve"
32127        );
32128
32129        assert_eq!(1, probe::get("gate_blocks/predeposit_exhausted"));
32130        assert_eq!(
32131            1,
32132            probe::get("gate_block_observations/predeposit_exhausted"),
32133            "a cancelled park must still close its episode"
32134        );
32135        Ok(())
32136    }

32204    /// A counted packet the gate fails never reaches routing resolution, so it gives its SURB back,
32205    /// whether the gate was closed before it came or was poisoned while it was parked.
32206    #[tokio::test]
32207    async fn a_counted_packet_the_gate_fails_should_give_its_surb_back() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
32208        use crate::balancer::SurbFlowEstimator;
32209
